{أولئك لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ} kavli: «لهم»ün ism-i işaretin haberi, «عذابٌ»ün de onunla (merfû) fâil olması caizdir; haberi olan bir şeye (mübtedâya) dayandığı için amel etmiştir; yani: «Onlar için azap sabit olmuştur.» «لهم»ün mukaddem haber, «عذاب»ın muahhar mübtedâ, cümlenin de ism-i işaretin haberi olması da caizdir. Birincisi daha güzeldir; çünkü müfred ile haber vermek cümle ile haber vermekten daha yakındır; birincisi de müfred ile haber verme kabîlindendir.
{وَمَا لَهُمْ مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ} kavli: «من ناصرين»in fâil olması caizdir; câr (ve mecrûr), nefy harfine dayandığı için amel etmesi caiz olmuştur; yani: «Onlar için hiçbir yardımcı sabit olmamıştır.» İkincisi: (لهم) mukaddem haber, «من ناصرين» muahhar mübtedâdır. Her iki i'raba göre de «مِنْ» zâidedir; çünkü onun ziyadesinin iki şartı mevcuttur. «ناصرين» fâsılalara uygun düşmesi için cemi olarak getirilmiştir.

His saying, the Exalted: {كُفْراً}: a tamyīz (specification) transferred from agency; the original is: "then their disbelief increased". The first dāl is a substitute for the tāʾ of the pattern «افتعال» (iftiʿāl), because it occurs after the zāy. Thus the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) gave its i'rab, but there is some doubt in it, since the meaning is that it is a direct object. That is because a verb transitive to two objects, when made to express reflexive effect (muṭāwiʿ), loses one object; and this is of that kind, because the original is: زِدْتُ زيداً خيراً فازداده, and likewise the original of the noble verse is: زادهم الله كفراً فازدادوه.
The فاء was not brought here entering upon «لن», but was brought with the second «لن». It was said: because the فاء announces entitlement by the preceding description, for he explicitly stated the qualification of their dying in disbelief, unlike the first «لن», with which he did not state it explicitly; so for that reason the فاء was not brought.
ʿIkrima read: «لن نقبل» with the nūn of magnificence, «توبتَهم» in the accusative, and therefore he read: «فلن نقبل مِنْ أحدِهم ملء» in the accusative.
His saying: {وأولئك هُمُ الضآلون}: in this clause there are three views. First: that it is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, that is: "Those who disbelieved, their repentance will not be accepted, and they, those are the astray". Second: that it be made conjoined to the clause emphasized by إنّ, and then it has no grammatical position, because it is conjoined to what has no position. Third, and it is the strangest of them: that the wāw is a wāw of ḥāl, so the clause after it is accusative as a ḥāl, and the meaning is: their repentance from sins will not be accepted, the situation being that they are astray; repentance and misguidance are mutually contradictory and do not combine. Al-Rāghib said this, and it is remote in construction, even if it is close in meaning. The Shaykh said: "This construction rejects this meaning, for had this meaning been intended, the demonstrative noun would not have been brought."
His saying: {فَلَن يُقْبَلَ}: it has already preceded that ʿIkrima [read] «نقبل» with nūn and «ملءَ» in the accusative as a direct object; and some of them read: فلن يَقبل with the third-person yāʾ, in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and «ملءَ» in the accusative as preceded. Abū Jaʿfar and Abū l-Sammāl read: «مِل الأرض» with the hamza of «ملء» dropped, its vowel transferred to the sākin before it; and some of them assimilate the like of this, that is, the lām of «ملء» into the lām of «الأرض», because of the incidental meeting of the two.
المِلْء is the measure of what fills a vessel, and المَلْء with fatḥa on the mīm is the maṣdar (verbal noun). One says: «مَلأتُ القِرْبة أملؤها مَلْئاً» (I filled the waterskin, I fill it, a filling); and المُلاءة is the wrap, with ḍamma on the mīm and lengthening.
And «ذَهَبا»: the majority read it in the accusative as tamyīz; al-Kisāʾī said: "by removal of the preposition". This is like the first, because the tamyīz is implied with «مِنْ», and «ملء» needed an explanation because of its vagueness, since it denotes a measure, like القَفِيز and الصَّاع. Al-Aʿmash read «ذهبٌ» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "as a replacement for «مِلْءُ»", as one says: "عندي عشرون نفساً رجالٌ" (I have twenty persons, men); by "replacement" he means badal (substitute), and it would be the badal of an indefinite from a definite. The Shaykh said: "For that reason the masters fixed the saying «لك الحمدُ ملءُّ السماوات» with the nominative, as an adjective of «الحمد», and they considered its accusative as a ḥāl weak because it is definite." I say: its accusative as a ḥāl is not necessary so as to require the weakness he mentioned; rather, it is accusative as an adverbial, that is: the praise takes place as a filling of the heavens and the earth.
His saying: {وَلَوِ افتدى}: the majority retain the wāw, and it is the wāw of ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the place of His saying {وَلَوِ افتدى بِهِ}? I say: it is speech construed on the meaning, as though it had been said: 'No ransom will be accepted from any of them, even if he ransomed himself with the earth's fill.'" End. What should be understood is that Allah the Exalted informed that whoever dies a disbeliever will not have accepted from him what fills the earth of gold, in every circumstance he may intend, even in the state of ransoming himself from the punishment; that is because the state of ransoming is a state in which the ransomer cannot claim a favour over the one he ransoms from, for it is a state of subjugation by the one ransomed from over the ransomer.
The Shaykh said: "We have established regarding the like of this construction that «لو» comes alerting that what precedes it came by way of comprehensiveness, and what follows it came as a specific statement of the state that is thought not to fall within what precedes it, as in his saying, peace be upon him: 'Give the beggar, even if he comes on a horse' and 'Turn the beggar back, even with a burnt hoof', as though these things were such that they should not be brought, because the beggar's being on a horse indicates his wealth and so it is not fitting to give him, and likewise the burnt hoof has no use, so it would be fitting not to turn the beggar back with it."
It was said: the wāw here is redundant, and this may be supported by the reading of Ibn Abī ʿAbla «لو افتدى به» without wāw; its meaning is that the ransoming is made a condition in the non-acceptance, so the negation of the existence of acceptance is not generalized. And «لو» is said to be conditional here with the meaning of إنْ, not the one whose meaning is "because of the occurrence of something because of the occurrence of something else", since it is attached to the future, which is His saying {فَلَن يُقْبَلَ}, while that one is attached to the past.
And افتدى is of the pattern «افْتَعَلَ» from the word الفِدْيَة, and it is transitive to one object because it has the meaning of فَدَى, so افتعل in it and فعل have the same meaning, like شَوَى and اشتوى; and its object is omitted, its implied form being: افتدى نفسَه (he ransomed himself).
And the hāʾ in «به» has several views; the most apparent is its referring back to «ملء», because it is the measure of what fills it, that is: "even if he ransomed himself with the earth's fill". The second: that it refers back to «ذهبا»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. The Shaykh said: "It is found in some commentaries that it refers back to the fill or to the gold; and the saying «or to the gold» is an error." I say: the aspect of the error in it seems to be that it is not what is being spoken of; it was brought only as an explanation and clarification of something else, as an extra. The third: that it refers back to an omitted «مثل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that what is meant is «ولو افتدى بمثله» (even if he ransomed himself with its like), as in His saying: {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ} [المائدة: 36]. And «مِثل» is often omitted in their speech, as in your saying «ضَرَبْتُ ضربَ زيدٍ» (I struck the striking of Zayd), meaning the like of his striking; 'Abū Yūsuf or Abū Ḥanīfa', that is, the like of him; and:
1356 - لا هيثمَ الليلةَ للمَطيّ
(There is no Haytham tonight for the mounts)
and 'قضية ولا أبا حسنٍ لها' (A case, and no Abū Ḥasan for it), meaning: no one like Haytham and no one like Abū Ḥasan, just as it is added in their saying 'مثلُك لا يفعل كذا' (the like of you does not do such), they mean: 'you do not do', because of the two likes, one fills the place of the other, so they are in the ruling of one thing." The Shaykh said: "There is no need to imply «مثل» in His saying {وَلَوِ افتدى بِهِ}. It is as though al-Zamakhsharī imagined that what is denied acceptance cannot be ransomed with, so he needed to supply «مثل» in order to distinguish between what is denied acceptance and what is ransomed with. But it is not so, because that is, as we mentioned, by way of supposition and estimation, since customarily it is not possible that anyone possesses the earth's fill of gold such that if he spent it, in whatever manner he spent it, it would not be accepted from him; rather, had that been possible, there would be no need to imply «مثل», because acceptance is denied even in the state of ransoming. What he implied in the verse is not the like of what he illustrated with, because this implication is not needed and has no meaning, and nothing in the wording or the meaning indicates it, so it is not implied. As for what he illustrated with, such as 'I struck the striking of Zayd', and 'Abū Yūsuf and Abū Ḥanīfa', we know by the necessity of reason that «مثل» must be implied, for your striking cannot be the striking of Zayd, and the person of Abū Yūsuf cannot be the person of Abū Ḥanīfa. As for 'لا هيثم الليلة للمطي', what indicates the omission of «مثل» is what is established in the Arabic language, that the «لا» of generic negation does not enter proper names and take effect on them, so «مثل» had to be implied in order for it to remain as established for it, since it is established that it operates only on a genus, because proper-nameness contradicts the generality of the genus. As for his saying 'as it is added in the like of: مثلُك لا يفعل, meaning you', this is a statement that has been made, but the choice with the master grammarians is that nouns are not added." I say: the answer to this objection, despite its length, is what Abū l-Qāsim said in the preface of his Kashshāf: "The lexicographer, even if he chews the language with his two jaws, and the grammarian, even if he is more of a grammarian than Sībawayh," to the end.
His saying: {أولئك لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ}: it is permissible that «لهم» be the khabar of the demonstrative and «عذابٌ» its agent (fāʿil), and it operated because it relies on an owner of a predicate, that is: "those, there is settled for them a punishment"; and that «لهم» be a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of the demonstrative. The first is better, because informing by a single word is closer than informing by a clause, and the first is of the kind of informing by a single word.
His saying: {وَمَا لَهُمْ مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ}: it is permissible that «من ناصرين» be an agent, and the operation of the preposition-and-noun phrase is permissible because it relies on a negative particle, that is: "and nothing has settled for them of helpers". The second: that it is a fronted khabar and «من ناصرين» a postponed mubtadaʾ; and «مِنْ» is redundant on both i'rabs, because the two conditions for its redundancy are present. He used «ناصرين» in the plural to agree with the verse-endings.

His saying, the Exalted: {وَلْتَكُن مِّنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ}: «تكن» may be the complete verb, i.e. "let there be found among you a community", in which case «أمة» is the fāʿil (agent), and «يَدْعُون» is a clause in the position of nominative as an adjective of «أمة»; «منكم» is attached to «تكن» as partitive. «منكم» may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أمة», since it could have been made its adjective had it come after it. «مِنْ» may also be explicative (bayān), because the thing explained, although it comes later in wording, is earlier in rank. It may also be the incomplete verb, in which case «أمة» is its subject and «يَدْعُون» its predicate, and «منكم» is attached either to the being, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «أمة». It is also possible that «منكم» is the predicate and «يَدْعُون» an adjective of «أمة», though this is remote. The majority read «ولتكن»; al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī and al-Sulamī read it with kasra [on the lām], which is the original.

His saying: {وَيَأْمُرُونَ بالمعروف وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المنكر} is a case of mentioning the specific after the general out of concern for it [Translator's note: the source reads «بعد العلم»; «بعد العام» (after the general) is evidently meant], like His saying {وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98], because the name "good" applies to both, and indeed they are the greatest of goods. His saying {جَآءَهُمُ البينات}: He did not make the verb feminine, because of the separation and because it is non-literally feminine, meaning "the proofs".

His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الله}: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «نَتْلوها» is a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause. It is also said: {آيَاتُ الله} is a badal (substitute) from «تلك», and «نتلوها» is a clause serving as khabar of the mubtadaʾ. «بالحق» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «نَتْلوها» or its object, and it is a confirmatory ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because the Exalted sends them down only in this manner [Translator's note: the source reads «يُنَزِّلها إلا على هذه الصفة» ("sends them down except in this manner"), with the negation particle evidently dropped; the sense is given accordingly].

al-Zajjāj said: "There is an omission in the speech, the implied form being: these are the verses of the Qur'an, the arguments of Allah and His proofs." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "According to what he implied, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is omitted, because in his view the meaning of the verse is completed by this implication; but this implication is not needed, since the meaning is complete without it." The indication by «تلك» is to the preceding verses that include the punishment of the disbelievers and the bliss of the righteous.

The majority read «نَتْلوها» with the nūn of majesty, and in it is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the first. Abū Nuhayk read «يتلوها» with yāʾ, and it has two possibilities: one, that the fāʿil is the pronoun for the Creator, the Exalted, because He was mentioned earlier in His saying {آيَاتُ الله}; there is no iltifāt on this implication, unlike the reading of the majority. The second: that the fāʿil is the pronoun for Jibrīl.

His saying: {لِّلْعَالَمِينَ}: the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and is not attached to anything; it was added to the object of the maṣdar, which is ظلم. The fāʿil is omitted, and in the implied form it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted; the implied form being: "and Allah does not wish to wrong the worlds", so the lām was added to strengthen the governing element because it is derivative, as in His saying, the Exalted: {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]. It is also said: the meaning of the speech is "and Allah does not wish wrongdoing of the worlds, some of them against others". This was rejected on the ground that, had this been meant, the construction with «مِنْ» would have been preferable to the lām, so that it would have been said «ظُلماً من العالمين»; so this is a meaning the wording rejects. He made «ظلماً» indefinite because it is in a context of negation, so it covers every kind of wrongdoing.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ} sözü: Bu «كان» hakkında altı görüş vardır: Birincisi: Kendi babı üzere nâkıstır. Böyle olunca geçmişe ve kesintiye delâlet etmez; aksine kesintiye de elverişlidir, «كان زيد قائماً» (Zeyd ayakta idi) gibi; devamlılığa da elverişlidir, {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} [Nisâ: 16] ve {وَلاَ تَقْرَبُواْ الزنى إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً} [İsrâ: 32] gibi. Burada o, «لم يَزَلْ» (hep … olageldi) mertebesindedir; bu da karinelere göredir.
Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: «"كان", bir şeyin geçmiş bir zamanda mübhem bir şekilde var olmasından ibarettir; onda önceki bir yokluğa da sonradan ârız olan bir kesintiye de delil yoktur. Allah Teâlâ'nın {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} sözü ve {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ} sözü bu kabildendir; sanki "وُجِدْتُم خيرَ أمة" (en hayırlı ümmet olarak var oldunuz) denmiştir.» Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «Onun "önceki bir yokluğa delâlet etmez" sözü, "صار" manasında olmadığı zaman içindir. "صار" manasında olduğunda önceki bir yokluğa delâlet eder. "صار زيد عالماً" manasında "كان زيد عالماً" dediğinde, onun cehalet hâlinden ilim hâline geçtiğine delâlet eder. "Sonradan ârız olan bir kesintiye de (delâlet etmez)" sözüne gelince, daha önce zikrettik ki sahih olan, onun diğer fiiller gibi olduğu, mâzî lafzının kesintiye delâlet ettiği, sonra bazen kesinti olmayan yerde kullanıldığıdır. Delâlet ile kullanım arasında fark vardır. Görmez misin ki "Bu lafız umuma delâlet eder" dersin, sonra bazen umumun kastedilmediği, aksine hususun kastedildiği yerde kullanılır. "Sanki وُجِدْتُم خيرَ أمة denmiştir" sözü ise onun "Bu, {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} sözü gibidir" sözüyle çelişir; çünkü "وُجِدتم خير أمة" takdiri onun tâm olduğuna ve "خير أمة"nin hâl olduğuna delâlet eder. {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} sözünde ise şüphesiz o nâkıstır; böylece ikisi çelişmiştir.» Ben derim ki: Çelişki yoktur; çünkü bu, i'rab tefsiri değil mana tefsiridir.
İkincisi: «صِرْتُم» (oldunuz) manasındadır. «كان» çokça «صار» manasında gelir; şu söz gibi:
1385 - بتيهاءَ قَفْرٍ والمَطِيُّ كأنها ... قَطَا الحَزْنِ قد كانَتْ فِراخا بيوضُها
(Issız, kıraç bir çölde; binekler, yumurtaları yavru olmuş sert arazi bağırtlak kuşları gibi idi.)
Yani: Yavrular hâline geldi (صارَتْ).
Üçüncüsü: «وُجِدْتُم» manasında tâmdır; buna göre «خيرَ أمة» hâl olarak mansûbdur; yani: Bu hâlde var oldunuz.
Dördüncüsü: zâidedir; takdir: «أنتم خيرُ أمةٍ». Bu, iki sebeple mercûh bir görüş ya da yanlıştır: Birincisi: (كان) baş tarafta zâide yapılmaz; İbn Mâlik bu konuda ittifak nakletmiştir. İkincisi: Zâide olmasıyla birlikte «خير»e amel etmez. İkincisinde itiraz vardır; zira zâide olmak amel etmeye aykırı değildir; buna dair deliller Bakara sûresinde {أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ الله} [Bakara: 246] sözü yanında geçmişti.
Beşincisi: Kendi babı üzeredir; kastedilen: Allah'ın ilminde veya Levh-i Mahfûz'da (öyle) idiniz.
Altıncısı: Bu cümle {فَفِي رَحْمَةِ الله} sözüne bağlıdır; yani: Kıyamette onlara {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ} denir. Bu ise çok uzaktır.
{أُخْرِجَتْ} sözü: Bu cümlenin, «أمة»nin sıfatı olarak cer mahallinde olması caizdir ve zâhir olan budur. «خير»in sıfatı olarak nasb mahallinde olması da caizdir; bu durumda hitap zamirinden sonra gelmesine rağmen zâhir ismin lafzı gözetilmiş olur. Hitap zamiri gözetilseydi bu da caiz olurdu. Şöyle ki: Mütekellim veya gâib olsun, hazır bir zamir önce gelir, sonra ondan sonra haberi zâhir bir isim olarak gelir, sonra o zâhir isimden sonra ona sıfat olmaya elverişli bir şey gelirse, Arapların bunda iki yolu vardır: Birincisi: O önceki zamiri gözetmektir; böylece zâhir isme sıfat olarak vâki olan cümledeki (zamir) ona uygun kılınır. İkincisi: O zâhir ismi gözetmektir; böylece zamir, (sıfat cümlesinden) ona gâib olarak döndürülür. Bu, [şu örnekte olduğu gibidir:] «أنتَ رجلٌ تأمرُ بمعروفٍ» sözünde «أنت»i gözeterek hitapla (تأمر), «رجل»i gözeterek gâible «يأمر»; «وأنا امرؤ أقولُ الحق» sözünde «أنا»yı gözeterek mütekellimle, «امرىء»i gözeterek «يقولُ الحقَّ». Zamiri gözetmeye örnek Allah Teâlâ'nın {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ} [Neml: 55], {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ} [Neml: 47] sözleri, «وإنك امرؤٌ فيك جاهلية» (Sen kendisinde cahiliye bulunan bir kişisin) sözü ve şâirin şu sözüdür:
1386 - وأنت امرؤٌ قد كَثَّأَتْ لك لِحْيَةٌ ... كأنك منها قاعدٌ في جُوالِقِ
(Sen öyle bir adamsın ki sakalın gürleşmiş; sanki ondan dolayı bir çuvalın içinde oturuyorsun.)
Ayet-i kerimede «كنتم»i gözeterek «أُخْرِجْتُم» denseydi lafız bakımından caiz olurdu; ancak onunla okunması caiz değildir; çünkü kıraat, uyulan bir sünnettir. Daha evlâ olan, cümlenin «خير»in değil «أمة»nin sıfatı yapılmasıdır ki «تأمرون» sözündeki hitapla uyum sağlansın.
«للناس» sözü hakkında birkaç vecih vardır: Birincisi: «أُخْرجت»e müteallik olması. İkincisi: «خير»e müteallik olması. İkisi arasındaki mana farkı şudur: İkinci vecihte onların ümmetlerin en faziletlisi olmaları bu lafızdan lazım gelmez, başka bir yerden lazım gelir. Üçüncüsü: İ'rab bakımından değil mana bakımından «تأمرون»a mütealliktir; mecrûru mef'ûlün bihtir; öne alınınca âmil zayıfladı ve lâmın ilavesiyle güçlendirildi; {إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ} [Yûsuf: 43] sözünde olduğu gibi; yani: «تَعْبُرون الرويا» (rüyayı yorumluyorsanız). [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «للناسٍ» şeklinde tenvinli yazılmıştır.]
«تأمرون» sözü: Bu cümle hakkında birkaç vecih vardır: Birincisi: «كنتم»in ikinci haberidir; «كنتم»deki önceki zamiri gözetmiştir; haberi gözetseydi gâible «يأمرون» derdi; bunun tahkiki önce geçti. İkincisi: Hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir; bunu Râgıb ve İbn Atıyye söylemiştir. Üçüncüsü: «خير أمة»nin sıfatı olarak nasb mahallindedir; önce geçen sebepten dolayı hitapla getirmiştir; bunu Havfî söylemiştir. Dördüncüsü: İsti'nâfiyyedir; onunla onların en hayırlı ümmet oluşlarını açıklamıştır; sanki «Sizin ümmetlerin en hayırlısı olmanızın sebebi bu övülmüş hasletlerdir» denmiştir. Bu, vecihlerin en garibidir.
{لَكَانَ خَيْراً} sözü: «كان»ın ismi, fiilinin delâlet ettiği masdara dönen bir zamirdir; takdir: «İman (onlar için) hayırlı olurdu.» Onların «مَنْ كَذَبَ كان شراً له» (Yalan söyleyen için o kötü olur) sözleri gibi; yani: Yalan onun için kötü olur. Bunun benzeri: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [Mâide: 8] ve [şu söz]:
1387 - إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جَرَى إليه ... وخالفَ والسَّفِيهُ إلى خلافِ
(Beyinsiz nehyedildiğinde ona [beyinsizliğe] koşar ve muhalefet eder; beyinsiz zaten muhalefete meyleder.)
Yani: Beyinsizlik (السَّفَهُ) ona koştu.
Kendisine tafdîl edilen (mufaddal aleyh) mahzûftur; yani: Onlar için küfürlerinden ve cehaletleri üzere kalmalarından daha hayırlı. Hayırlılıktan kasıt, onların zannına göre: [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta cümle bu şekilde yarım kalmıştır; devamında bir şey yoktur.] İbn Atıyye şöyle demiştir: «"خير" lafzı tafdîl sîgasıdır; hâlbuki onların küfrü ile imanı arasında hayırda bir ortaklık yoktur. Bu ancak "خير" lafzındaki yaygınlık ve vecihlerin çeşitliliği sebebiyle caiz olmuştur; "أفضل" ve "أحب" lafızları ve bunların yerine geçenler de böyledir.» Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «Mümkün olduğunda onu asıl vaz'ı üzere bırakmak daha evlâdır; burada bu mümkündür; zira hayırlılık mutlaktır, en küçük bir ortaklıkla hâsıl olur.»
{مِّنْهُمُ المؤمنون} sözü sonuna kadar: Bunu haber vermek için sevk edilmiş isti'nâfiyye (cümle) kılınmıştır.

His saying, the Exalted: {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ}: concerning this «كان» there are six views. First: that it is the incomplete verb (nāqiṣa) on its usual footing. If so, it does not indicate pastness and cessation; rather it can be used for cessation, as in «كان زيد قائماً», and for permanence, as in {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 16] and {وَلاَ تَقْرَبُواْ الزنى إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً} [al-Isrāʾ: 32]. Here it is equivalent to «لم يَزَلْ» (has never ceased), and this is according to the contextual indications.

al-Zamakhsharī said: «كان» is an expression for the existence of a thing in a past time, in an indefinite manner, and it contains no indication of a prior non-existence nor of a subsequent cessation. Of this is His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً}, and His saying {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ}, as if it were said «وُجِدْتُم خيرَ أمة» ("you were found the best community"). The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: His saying "it does not indicate prior non-existence" holds when it does not mean «صار» (became); when it means «صار» it does indicate prior non-existence. If you say «كان زيد عالماً» in the sense of «صار زيد عالماً», it indicates that he moved from the state of ignorance to the state of knowledge. As for his saying "nor a subsequent cessation", we mentioned before that the sound view is that it is like the other verbs: the past wording of it indicates cessation, and then it may be used where there is no cessation, and there is a difference between indication and usage. Do you not see that you say "this word indicates generality", and then it may be used where generality is not meant but rather specificity? And his saying "as if it were said: you were found the best community" conflicts with his saying that it is like {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً}, because his implied form "you were found the best community" indicates that it is the complete verb and that «خير أمة» is a ḥāl, whereas in {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً} it is without doubt the incomplete verb; so the two conflict. I say: there is no conflict, because this is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of i'rab.

Second: that it means «صِرْتُم» (you became); and «كان» often comes in the sense of «صار», as in his saying:
1385 - بتيهاءَ قَفْرٍ والمَطِيُّ كأنها ... قَطَا الحَزْنِ قد كانَتْ فِراخا بيوضُها
(In a barren trackless desert, the riding camels like sandgrouse of the rough ground, whose eggs have become chicks.)
that is: they became chicks.
Third: that it is complete, meaning «وُجِدْتُم» (you were found), and «خيرَ أمة» on this basis is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "you were found in this state".
Fourth: that it is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being "you are the best community". This is a weak view, or a mistake, for two reasons. One: it is not added at the beginning, and Ibn Mālik transmitted agreement on that. The second: it does not govern «خير» while redundant; and in the second there is room for objection, since redundancy does not negate governing, and evidence for this was given earlier in al-Baqara at His saying {أَلاَّ نُقَاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ الله} [al-Baqara: 246].
Fifth: that it is on its usual footing, and what is meant is "you were, in Allah's knowledge", or "in the Preserved Tablet".
Sixth: that this sentence is connected to His saying {فَفِي رَحْمَةِ الله}, i.e. it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection {كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ}; and this is very remote.

His saying: {أُخْرِجَتْ}: this sentence may be in the position of genitive as an adjective of «أمة», which is the apparent view, or in the position of accusative as an adjective of «خير». In that case the wording of the overt noun is observed after it occurs following the second-person pronoun; and had the second-person pronoun been observed, that too would be permissible. That is: when a present pronoun (speaker or addressee) comes first, then its predicate comes as an overt noun, and after that overt noun comes something that can serve as a description of it, the Arabs have two ways. One: observing that preceding pronoun, so that the sentence serving as description of the overt noun / agrees with it; the other: observing that overt noun, so that the pronoun returning to it from the sentence is in the third person. For example, your saying «أنتَ رجلٌ تأمرُ بمعروفٍ» with address observing «أنت», and «يأمر» in the third person observing «رجل»; «وأنا امرؤ أقولُ الحق» in the first person observing «أنا», and «يقولُ الحقَّ» observing «امرؤ». Of observing the pronoun is His saying, the Exalted: {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ} [al-Naml: 55], {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ} [al-Naml: 47], and his saying «وإنك امرؤٌ فيك جاهلية» ("You are a man in whom there is jāhiliyya"), and the poet's saying:
1386 - وأنت امرؤٌ قد كَثَّأَتْ لك لِحْيَةٌ ... كأنك منها قاعدٌ في جُوالِقِ
(You are a man whose beard has grown thick, as if you were sitting in a sack because of it.)
Had it been said in the noble verse «أُخْرِجْتُم», observing «كنتم», it would have been permissible in wording, but it cannot be recited so, because recitation is a followed sunna. It is therefore preferable to make the sentence an adjective of «أمة», not of «خير», so that the address in «تأمرون» is in harmony.

His saying «للناسِ»: there are several aspects. One: that it is attached to «أُخْرجت». Second: that it is attached to «خير»; the difference between them in meaning is that on the second aspect it does not follow from this wording that they are the best of communities, but rather from another place. Third: that it is attached, in meaning but not in i'rab, to «تأمرون», its genitive being a direct object; when it was put first, the governing verb weakened and was strengthened by the added lām, as in {إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ} [Yūsuf: 43], i.e. "you interpret the dream".

His saying «تأمرون»: in this sentence there are several aspects. One: that it is a second khabar of «كنتم», observing the earlier pronoun in «كنتم»; had it observed the khabar it would have said «يأمرون» in the third person, and this was verified earlier. Second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; said by al-Rāghib and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. Third: that it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «خير أمة», and address was used for the reason given; said by al-Ḥawfī. Fourth: that it is resumptive, explaining by it their being the best community, as if it were said: the cause of your being the best of communities is these praiseworthy qualities; and this is the strangest of the aspects.

His saying: {لَكَانَ خَيْراً}: the subject of «كان» is a pronoun returning to the verbal noun indicated by its verb; the implied form being "belief would have been better", as they say «مَنْ كَذَبَ كان شراً له», i.e. lying would have been evil for him; and like it {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8], [and his saying]:
1387 - إذا نُهِي السَّفيهُ جَرَى إليه ... وخالفَ والسَّفِيهُ إلى خلافِ
(When the fool is forbidden, he runs toward it and defies; and the fool runs to opposition.)
that is: folly ran toward it.
That which is surpassed (al-mufaḍḍal ʿalayhi) is omitted, i.e. "better for them than their disbelief and their persisting in their ignorance". [Translator's note: the source then has an incomplete sentence: "And what is meant by betterness in their claim:" with nothing following.] Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The word «خير» is a comparative form, and there is no sharing of goodness between their disbelief and their belief; it is permissible only because of the wide extension and many branches of the word «خير», and likewise are the words «أفضل» and «أحب» and what follows their course." The Shaykh said: "Keeping it on its original sense is preferable when that is possible, and it is possible here, since betterness is unrestricted, and so it is obtained by the least sharing."

His saying: {مِّنْهُمُ المؤمنون} to its end: He made it resumptive, brought to report that.

His saying, the Exalted: {أَيْنَ مَا ثقفوا}: «أينما» is a conditional; it is an adverb of place, and «ما» is added to it; so «ثُقفوا» is in the position of jussive by it. The apodosis of the condition is either omitted, i.e. "wherever they are found they are overcome and humiliated", indicated by His saying {ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذلة}; or it is «ضُرِبَتْ» itself, according to those who permit the apodosis to precede the condition. {ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذلة} has no grammatical position on the first view, and its position is jussive on the second.

His saying: {إِلاَّ بِحَبْلٍ}: this prepositional phrase is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, and it is an unrestricted exception (mufarragh) from the general states. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is an exception from the most general of the general states, and the meaning is: 'Humiliation is struck upon them in all states except the state of their holding fast to a rope from Allah and a rope from the people.'" On this basis it is a connected exception. al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a disconnected exception." al-Farrāʾ implied: «إلاَّ أَنْ يَعْتصموا بحبل من الله», omitting what the prepositional phrase attaches to, as Ḥumayd ibn Thawr al-Hilālī said:
1388 - رَأَتْني بِحَبْلَيْها فَصَدَّتْ مخافةً ... وفي الحبلِ رَوْعاءُ الفؤادِ فَروقُ
(She saw me with her two ropes and turned away in fear; and in the rope there was a startled, fearful heart.)
He meant: «أقلبت بحبليها», omitting the verb because of the indication of it. [Translator's note: the source has «أقلبت»; by sense «أقبلت» ("she approached with her two ropes") is meant.] Ibn ʿAṭiyya gave as a parallel His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَن يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً إِلاَّ خَطَأً} [al-Nisāʾ: 92]. He said: "Because the first impression gives that he may kill by mistake, and that the rope from Allah and from the people removes the striking of humiliation; but it is not so. Rather there is an omission in the speech / that the understanding of the listener who considers the matter grasps, and its implied form in our verse is: «فلا نجاة من الموت إلا بحبلٍ» ('there is no escape from death except by a rope')." The Shaykh said: "On what he implied it is not a disconnected exception, because it is an exception from an implied sentence, which is «فلا نجاة من الموت», and it is connected on this implication; so it cannot be disconnected from the first, since one exception cannot be both disconnected and connected. The disconnected exception, as established in the science of grammar, is of two kinds: one to which the governing element can be applied, and one to which it cannot. This verse is of the latter on the supposition of disconnection, as the implied form is: 'but their holding fast to a rope from Allah and a rope from the people saves them from killing, captivity, the enslavement of their offspring, and the extermination of their wealth.' What shows that it is disconnected is the report of this in His saying, the Exalted, in Sūrat al-Baqara: {وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذلة والمسكنة وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ الله} [al-Baqara: 61], where He made no exception there." What follows this verse has been parsed earlier.

The majority read {إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ} with the feminine form, observing the wording of «حسنة». Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read it with yāʾ, because its femininity is figurative; its analogy is that «وإنْ يصبكم سيئة» also be read in the masculine, but I do not remember anything from him on it.

His saying: {إِنَّ الله عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصدور}: this sentence may be resumptive, the Exalted reporting it because they used to conceal their rage as far as they could, so He mentioned this to them by way of threat. It may also be a sentence of what is said, i.e. "Say to them such and such", in which case it is in the position of accusative by "say". The meaning of His saying «بذات» is "the hidden things that are possessors of the breasts"; so «ذات» here is the feminine of «ذي» meaning "possessor", the qualified noun being omitted and its adjective standing in its place, i.e. "Knowing of the hidden things that are companions of the breasts"; they were made companions of the breasts because of their constant attachment to them and non-separation from them, like "companions of Paradise" and "companions of the Fire".

They disagreed about stopping on this word: is it stopped at with tāʾ or with hāʾ? al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ and Ibn Kaysān said: "Stopping is with tāʾ, following the Mushaf's script." al-Kisāʾī and al-Jarmī said: "It is stopped at with hāʾ, because it is the tāʾ of femininity, as in «صاحبه»." Agreement with the script is preferable, since stopping at the explicit feminine tāʾ with tāʾ is established for us, so if we stop here with tāʾ we agree with that dialect and with the script, unlike the reverse.

His saying: {لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يَضِرْكم» with kasra on the ḍād and jussive rāʾ, as the apodosis of the condition, from ḍārahu yaḍīruhu; one also says ḍārahu yaḍūruhu, so there are two dialectal forms in the middle letter. One says ḍārahu yaḍīruhu ḍayran, so he is ḍāʾir and he is maḍīr; and ḍārahu yaḍūruhu ḍawran, so he is ḍāʾir and he is maḍūr, like qultuhu aqūluhu, so I am qāʾil and he is maqūl.

The others read «يَضُرُّكم» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with ḍamma. In this reading there are several aspects. One: that the verb is nominative and is not the apodosis of the condition, but only indicates the apodosis. That is because it is intended to be put first, the implied form being: "It will not harm you if you are patient and fear Allah; it will not harm you", and the «فلا يضركم», which is the apodosis, was omitted because what precedes indicates it, then what indicates the apodosis was put later. What I have mentioned is the explanation of Sībawayh and his followers. They had to commit this strain only because they saw the lack of jussive in an / imperfect verb where nothing prevents the jussive particle from acting on it. Like it is the saying of another:
1413 - يا أقرعُ بنَ حابسٍ يا أقرعُ ... إنَّك إنْ يَصْرَعْ أخوكَ تُصْرعُ
(O Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis, O Aqraʿ, if your brother is thrown, you will be thrown.)
with the last «تُصْرع» in the nominative, and likewise his saying:
1414 - وإنْ أتاهُ خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(If a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: "My wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.")
with «يقول» in the nominative. However this type is regular, unlike the former, I mean the condition and the response both being imperfect; for what is reported from Sībawayh and his followers is that the jussive is obligatory except in necessity, like «إنْ يُصْرعَ أخوك تُصْرعُ». His explanation of this verse as I have related from him shows that this is not restricted to necessity; so know that.

The second aspect: that the verb is nominative because it occurs after an implied fāʾ, and that and what follows it is in truth the apodosis; whenever a verb occurs after the fāʾ it is nominative, nothing else, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَنْ عَادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ الله مِنْهُ} [al-Māʾida: 95], the implied form being «فلا يَضُرُّكم». The fāʾ is omitted in a place other than the disputed one, as in the saying:
1415 - مَنْ يَفعلِ الحسناتِ اللهُ يشكُرها ... والشرُّ بالشر عند الله سِيَّانِ
(Whoever does good deeds, Allah thanks them; and evil by evil is the same with Allah.)
that is «فالله يشكرها». I have seen some report this aspect from al-Mubarrad, and there is room for objection in it, since when they recited the verse mentioned they reported from al-Mubarrad that he does not permit the omission of this fāʾ at all, neither in necessity nor otherwise, and they report that he used to say: "The transmission in this verse is rather:
مَنْ يفعلِ الخيرَ فالرحمنُ يَشْكُرُه ...
(Whoever does good, the Merciful thanks him …)"
and they replied to him that when a transmission is sound, another does not impugn it. I have seen some report it from al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī, and this is nearer.

The third aspect: that the vowel is a vowel of assimilation (ḥarakat ittibāʿ). The original is «لا يَضْرِرْكم» with unmerging, because of the sukūn of the second letter by jussive; and it will be mentioned that when two identical letters meet at the end of a verb with the second made sākin by jussive or by «وفقاً» [Translator's note: the source has «وفقاً»; «وقفاً» (pause) is evidently meant], the Arabs have two ways: merging (idghām), which is the dialect of Tamīm, and unmerging (fakk), which is the dialect of the Hijaz. But there is no way to merge except with a vowelled letter, so we were forced to vowel the second identical letter, and we vowelled it with the vowel nearest to it, namely the ḍamma on the letter before it, and merged what precedes into it; so it is jussive in implied form, and this vowel is in truth a vowel of assimilation and not a vowel of i'rab, unlike the two earlier aspects, in which it is a vowel of i'rab.

Know that whenever this type is merged, its first letter is either ḍamma-vowelled, fatḥa-vowelled or kasra-vowelled. If ḍamma-vowelled, like the noble verse and their saying «مُدَّ», there are three aspects in the state of merging: ḍamma for assimilation, fatḥa for lightness, and kasra on the basis of the meeting of two sākin letters; so you say muddu, mudda and muddi, ruddu, rudda and ruddi. They recite for this Jarīr's saying:
1416 - فَغُضِّ الطرفَ إنَّك من نُمَيْرٍ ... فلا كعباً بَلَغْتَ ولا كِلابا
(Lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.)
with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the ḍād as I have told you; and it will be mentioned that the verse was recited with the three aspects. If fatḥa-vowelled like ʿaḍḍa, or kasra-vowelled like firra, the final letter has two aspects: fatḥa and kasra, since there is no way for ḍamma; but with something like «فِرَّ» you may say kasra for two reasons, either assimilation or the meeting of two sākin letters, and likewise with fatḥa like «عَضَّ» you have two reasons also, either assimilation or lightness. All this holds when no third-person pronoun is attached to the verb; when a third-person pronoun is attached, like «رُدَّه», there are details and dialectal forms that are long to discuss and it is not fitting to go into them in this kind of work.

ʿĀṣim, in what al-Mufaḍḍal related from him, read with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with fatḥa, on the lightness I mentioned to you, / and it is, in their view, a better aspect than ḍamma on the rāʾ.
al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim read «لا يَضُرِّكم» with ḍamma on the ḍād and a doubled rāʾ with kasra, on the meeting of two sākin letters I mentioned to you. It seems that Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not know it as a reading, for he said: "As for the kasra, I do not know it as a reading." al-Zajjāj's expression on that is loose, since it appears from the flow of his speech that it is a reading. I say: I have shown that it is a reading as al-Zajjāj said, and praise be to Allah.

al-Kayd is scheming and guile. al-Rāghib said: "It is a kind of guile, and may be praised or blamed, though it is used more in the blameworthy." Ibn Qutayba said: "Its origin is from hardship, from their saying «فلان يكيدُ بنفسِه», meaning he passes through the pangs of death, and its derivatives." One says kidtu fulānan akīduhu like bʿtuhu abīʿuhu. He said:
1417 - مَنْ يَكِدْني بسيِّءٍ كنتُ منه ... كالشَّجا بين حَلْقِه والوَرِيد
(Whoever schemes against me with evil, I shall be to him like a bone stuck between his throat and his jugular vein.)
Ubayy read «لا يَضْرِرْكم» with unmerging, which is the Hijazi dialect, and on it is His saying, the Exalted: {إِن تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ}.
His saying «شيئاً» is accusative like the maṣdars, i.e. "any harm"; a parallel has been given. The majority read «بما يعملون محيطٌ» in the third person, which is clear. al-Ḥasan read it in the second person, either on iltifāt, or on the implication «قل لهم يا محمد» ("Say to them, O Muḥammad").

Allah Teâlâ'nın {وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ} sözü: «إذ»deki âmil gizlidir; takdiri: «واذكر إذ غدوت» (sabah erkenden çıktığın zamanı an). Böylece zarf olarak değil, mef'ûlün bih olarak mansûb olur. Bazıları onun, {قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ} [Âl-i İmrân: 13] sözündeki «فئتين»e ma'tûf olmasını caiz görmüştür; yani: «İki toplulukta ve sabah erkenden çıktığın zamanda sizin için bir ayet vardı.» Buna hiç uğranmamalıdır (iltifat edilmemelidir).
الغدوُّ: günün başında çıkmaktır. غَدا يَغْدُو denir, yani: sabah erkenden (غُدْوَةً) çıktı. Bazılarına göre «صار» manasında da kullanılır; bu durumda ismi ref', haberi nasbeden nâkıs bir fiil olur. Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.v.) şu sözü buna göredir: «Allah'a hakkıyla tevekkül etseydiniz, kuşları rızıklandırdığı gibi sizi de rızıklandırırdı; sabah aç karınla gider (تَغْدُو خِماصاً), akşam tok karınla döner.»
{مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} sözü «غَدَوْتَ»e mütealliktir. «من» hakkında iki vecih vardır: Daha zâhir olanı ibtidâ-i gâye için olmasıdır; yani: ailenin arasından. Ebü'l-Bekâ şöyle demiştir: «Mahalli nasbdır; takdiri: ailenden ayrıldın.» Onun bu söylediği ne bir i'rab tefsiridir ne de bir mana tefsiri; zira mana onun zikrettiğinden başkadır. İkincisi: «مع» manasında olmasıdır; yani: ailenle birlikte. Buna ne lafız ne de mana yardımcı olur.
{تُبَوِّىءُ} sözü: Cümlenin «غدوت»un fâilinden hâl olması caizdir; bu, mukadder (takdir edilmiş, gelecekteki) bir hâldir; yani: mü'minleri yerleştirmeyi kastederek; çünkü sabah çıkış vakti yerleştirme vakti değildir. Zaman geniş olduğu için mukârin (eşzamanlı) olması da muhtemeldir.
تُبَوِّىءُ yani yerleştirirsin; bu (fiil) iki mef'ûle müteaddî olur: birine bizzat, diğerine cer harfiyle. Bu (cer harfi) bazen hazfedilir; bu ayette olduğu gibi. Hazfedilmemesine örnek Allah Teâlâ'nın {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ البيت} [Hac: 26] sözüdür. Aslı المَبَاءة'dendir; o da dönülen yerdir. (Şâir) şöyle demiştir:
1418 - وما بَوَّأ الرحمنُ بَيْتَك منزلاً ... بشرقيِّ أجيادِ الصَّفا والمُحَرَّمِ
(Rahmân, senin evini Safâ'nın ve Harem'in Ecyâd'ının doğusunda bir konağa yerleştirmedi.)
Bir başkası şöyle demiştir:
1419 - كم مِن أخٍ لي صَالحٍ ... بَوَّأْتُه بيدَيَّ لَحْدا
(Nice salih kardeşim var ki onu kendi ellerimle bir lahde yerleştirdim.)
Bu lafzın iştikakı önce geçmişti. Şöyle de denmiştir: «"لإِبراهيم" sözündeki lâm zâidedir; buna göre (fiil) bizzat iki mef'ûle müteaddî olur.»
مقاعد, «مَقْعَد»ın çoğuludur; burada bununla oturma yeri kastedilmiştir. قعد, sadece mesel (atasözü)de «صار» manasında olabilir. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: «قعد ve قام'da genişlik yapılmış, nihayet "صار" yerine kullanılmışlardır.» Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «"قَعَد"ın "صار" yerine kullanılmasına gelince, arkadaşlarımızdan biri şöyle demiştir: Bu ancak mesel içinde tek bir şâz lafızda gelmiştir; onların "شَحَذَ شَفْرَته حتى قَعَدَتْ كأنها حَرْبة" (bıçağını biledi, nihayet bir mızrak gibi oldu) sözlerinde. Aynı şekilde Zemahşerî'nin Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُوماً} [İsrâ: 22] sözünü "فتصيرَ" manasında izah etmesini de eleştirmiştir; çünkü قَعَد'ın صار yerine kullanılması muttarid değildir.» Ben derim ki: Zemahşerî'nin zikrettiği, yani «قعد»ın bu sözü söyleyenin işaret ettiğinin dışında da «صار» manasında olması sahihtir. Ebû Ömer ez-Zâhid, İbnü'l-A'râbî'den, Arapların «قَعد فلان أميراً بعد أن كان مأموراً» (Falan, emir altındayken emir oldu) dediklerini, yani «صار» (oldu) manasında, nakletmiştir.
Sonra Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «"قام"ın "صار" yerine kullanılmasına gelince, onu "كان"ın kardeşleri arasında sayan ve "صار" manasında kılan kimseyi bilmiyorum; ancak İbn Hişâm el-Hadrâvî müstesna; o, şâirin şu sözünde:
1420 - على ما قام يَشْتِمُني لئيمٌ ... كخِنْزيرٍ تَمَرَّغَ في رماد
(Küle bulanmış bir domuz gibi alçak biri ne diye kalkıp bana sövüyor?)
onun mukârebe fiillerinden olduğunu zikretmiştir.» Ben derim ki: Diğer nahivciler onu zâide sayarlar; bu da şâzdır.
Kurrânın geneli «تُبَوِّىءُ» okumuş; onu tad'îf (şedde) ile müteaddî kılmışlardır. Abdullah (b. Mes'ûd) «تُبْوِىءُ» şeklinde bânın sükûnuyla okumuş; onu hemze ile müteaddî kılmıştır; bu, أكرم gibi أَبْوأَ'nın muzârisidir. Yahyâ b. Vessâb, Abdullah'ın kıraati gibi «تُبْوي» okumuştur; ancak o hemzeyi yâya ibdâl ederek teshil etmiş; böylece lafzı «تُحْيي»nin lafzı gibi olmuştur; onların «تُقْرىء» yerine «تُقْري» demeleri gibi. Abdullah «للمؤمنين» şeklinde cer lâmıyla okumuştur; {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ} [Hac: 26] sözü gibi. Bu lâm hakkında iki görüş olduğu önce geçti. Zâhir olan, onun ta'diye (müteaddî kılma) lâmı olmasıdır; çünkü (fiil) tad'îf ve hemzeden önce bizzat müteaddî değildir. Burada «تُهَيِّىء» (hazırlarsın) ve «ترتِّب» (düzenlersin) manasını tazammun etmiş olması da muhtemeldir.
Eşheb «مقاعدَ القتالِ» şeklinde onu «القتال»e izâfe ederek okumuştur. Cumhurun kıraatinde «للقتال»deki lâm hakkında iki vecih vardır: Daha zâhir olanı, illet lâmı olmak üzere «تُبَوِّىء»ye müteallik olmasıdır. İkincisi: «مقاعد»ın sıfatı olduğu için mahzûfa müteallik olmasıdır; yani: savaş için var olan ve hazırlanmış yerler. Müştak olsa bile «مقاعد»a müteallik olması caiz değildir; çünkü o mekândır, mekânlar (ism-i mekânlar) ise amel etmez.

His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ}: the governing element of «إذ» is implied, its implied form being «واذكر إذ غدوت» ("and remember when you set out in the morning"), so it is accusative as a direct object, not as an adverbial. Some allowed it to be conjoined to «فئتين» in His saying {قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ فِي فِئَتَيْنِ} [Āl ʿImrān: 13], i.e. "there was for you a sign in two groups and in when you set out in the morning"; but this should not be dwelt on.

al-Ghudūw is going out at the beginning of the day. One says ghadā yaghdū, i.e. he went out in the morning (ghudwa). Some use it in the sense of ṣāra (became), in which case it is incomplete, raising the subject and making the predicate accusative, and on this is his saying, peace be upon him: «لو توكلتم على الله حَقَّ توكُّلهِ لرزقكم كما يَرزق الطيرَ تَغْدُو خِماصاً وتروُح بِطاناً» ("If you relied on Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full").

His saying {مِنْ أَهْلِكَ} is attached to «غَدَوْتَ», and for «من» there are two aspects. The clearer is that it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. "from among your family". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Its position is accusative; the implied form is «فارقْتَ أهلك» (you left your family)." What he said is neither an explanation of i'rab nor of meaning, for the meaning is other than he mentioned. The second: that it means "with", i.e. "with your family"; neither wording nor meaning supports this.

His saying: {تُبَوِّىءُ}: the sentence may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «غدوت», and it is a prospective ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), i.e. "intending to settle the believers", because the time of setting out is not the time of settling. It may also be a concurrent one, since the time is wide.
Tubawwiʾu means "to lodge", and it takes two objects, one directly and the other by a preposition, which may be omitted, as in this verse. An example of its not being omitted is His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ البيت} [al-Ḥajj: 26]. Its origin is from al-mabāʾa, which is the place of return. He said:
1418 - وما بَوَّأ الرحمنُ بَيْتَك منزلاً ... بشرقيِّ أجيادِ الصَّفا والمُحَرَّمِ
(The Merciful has not lodged your house in a dwelling to the east of Ajyād of al-Ṣafā and al-Muḥarram.)
and another said:
1419 - كم مِن أخٍ لي صَالحٍ ... بَوَّأْتُه بيدَيَّ لَحْدا
(How many a righteous brother of mine have I lodged with my own hands in a grave.)
The derivation of this word was given earlier. It is also said: "The lām in his saying «لإبراهيم» is redundant, and on this it takes two objects by itself."
Maqāʿid is the plural of maqʿad, and what is meant here is the place of sitting. Qaʿada can mean ṣāra in proverbs especially. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Qaʿada and qāma have been broadened until they were made to function as ṣāra." The Shaykh said: "As for making qaʿada function as ṣāra, some of our colleagues said that this occurred only in a single irregular expression in a proverb, in their saying «شَحَذَ شَفْرَته حتى قَعَدَتْ كأنها حَرْبة» ('He sharpened his blade until it became like a spear'); and likewise he criticised al-Zamakhsharī for explaining His saying, the Exalted, {فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُوماً} [al-Isrāʾ: 22] in the sense of «فتصيرَ», because making qaʿada function as ṣāra is not regular." I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is correct, that qaʿada can mean ṣāra beyond what this critic indicated; Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid related from Ibn al-Aʿrābī that the Arabs say «قَعد فلان أميراً بعد أن كان مأموراً», i.e. he became.
Then the Shaykh said: "As for making qāma function as ṣāra, I know of no one who counted it among the sisters of kāna, or made it mean ṣāra, except Ibn Hishām al-Khaḍrāwī, who mentioned, regarding the poet's saying: /
1420 - على ما قام يَشْتِمُني لئيمٌ ... كخِنْزيرٍ تَمَرَّغَ في رماد
(Upon what ground does a base fellow begin to revile me, like a pig wallowing in ashes?)
that it is among the verbs of approximation." I say: other grammarians make it redundant, and that too is irregular.
The majority read «تُبَوِّىءُ», making it transitive by doubling. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «تُبْوِىءُ» with sukūn on the bāʾ, making it transitive by hamza, so it is the imperfect of abwaʾa like akrama. Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read «تُبْوي» like ʿAbd Allāh's reading, except that he eased the hamza by turning it into yāʾ, so its wording became like that of «تُحْيي», as they say «تُقْري» for «تُقْرىء». ʿAbd Allāh read «للمؤمنين» with the genitive lām, like {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Ḥajj: 26]. It was mentioned that there are two views about this lām. The apparent is that it makes the verb transitive, because before doubling and hamza it is not transitive by itself. It may be that he made it include here the meaning of «تُهَيِّىء» (to prepare) and «ترتِّب» (to arrange).
al-Ashhab read «مقاعدَ القتالِ» annexing it to «القتال». As for the lām in «للقتال» in the reading of the majority, there are two aspects. The clearer: that it is attached to «تُبَوِّىء» as the lām of cause. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «مقاعد», i.e. "seats that are present and prepared for fighting". It cannot be attached to «مقاعد», though it is a derived noun, since it is a noun of place, and nouns of place do not govern.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {إِذْ تَقُولُ} sözü: Bunda üç vecih vardır. Birincisi: Bu zarf, «إذ هَمَّتْ» sözünden bedeldir. İkincisi: «نصركم» ile mansûbtur. Üçüncüsü: Takdir edilen «اذكر» (hatırla) fiiliyle mansûbtur. Bu cümle Bedir kıssasının tamamlayıcısı mıdır —ki bu cumhurun görüşüdür ve buna göre bu sözde i'tirâz (ara cümle) yoktur— yoksa Uhud'un tamamlayıcısı mıdır ki bu durumda {وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ الله} sözü iki söz arasında i'tirâziyye cümle olur? Bu meşhur bir ihtilaftır.
{أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ} sözü: «ألن يكفيكم»in fâilidir; yani «Rabbinizin size yardım (imdâd) etmesi size yetmez mi?» Hemze nefy üzerine girince onu inkâr yoluyla takrir etmiştir (sabitleştirmiştir). «لا» yerine «لن» getirilmiştir, çünkü o nefyde daha beliğdir. Übey'in mushafında ise «لن» yerine «لا» ile «ألا» şeklindedir; sanki o, mânâyı tefsir etmeyi kastetmiştir.
«بثلاثة» sözü «يُمِدَّكم»e mütealliktir. Hasan-ı Basrî vasıl hâlinde sâkin bir hâ ile «ثلاثَهْ آلاف» diye okumuştur; «بخسمهْ آلاف» [Mütercim notu: kaynakta böyle yazılmıştır; doğrusu «بخمسهْ» olmalıdır] de böyledir. Sanki vaslı vakıf yerine koymuştur. Bu kıraat zayıftır, çünkü bitişikliği gerektiren iki muzâf-muzâfun ileyh arasındadır. İbn Atıyye şöyle demiştir: «Bu kıraatin vechi zayıftır; çünkü muzâf ve muzâfun ileyh tek bir şey gibidir, bitişikliği gerektirirler ve ikincisi birincinin tamamlayıcısıdır. Hâ ise ancak vakıf alâmetidir; dolayısıyla bitişiklik yeri olan bir mahalde vakıf yadırganır. Ancak Araplardan bazı yerlerde bunun benzeri gelmiştir. Bunlardan biri, Ferrâ'nın onların "أكلت لحما شاة" sözlerinden naklettiğidir; "لحمَ شاة"yı kastediyorlar, fethayı uzattılar da ondan bir elif meydana geldi; tıpkı vakıfta "قالَ"yi kastederek "قالا" dedikleri gibi. Sonra kafiyelerde ve benzeri düşünüp teenni etme yerlerinde fethayı uzatırlar. Şiirde de bundan şairin şu sözü vardır:
1422 - يَنْباع من ذِفْرى غضوبٍ جَسْرَةٍ ... زَيَّافَةٍ مثلِ الفنيق المُكْدَمِ
(Ter, öfkeli, cüsseli, salınarak yürüyen, ısırık izli damızlık deve gibi bir dişi devenin kulak arkasından sızar.)
"يَنْبَع"i kastetmiş ve uzatmıştır. Bunun benzeri diğer şairin şu sözüdür:
1423 - أقول إذ خَرَّتْ على الكَلْكال ... يا ناقتي ما جُلْت مِنْ مَجَال
(Göğsünün üzerine çöktüğünde derim ki: Ey devem, hiçbir alanda dolaşmadın!)
"الكلكل"i kastetmiş ve uzatmıştır. Bunun benzeri de diğer şairin şu sözüdür:
1424 - فأنتَ من الغوائلِ حين تُرْمَى ... ومن ذمِّ الرجال بمُنْتزاحِ
(Sen, belalar atıldığında onlardan ve adamların yermesinden uzak bir yerdesin.)
"بمنتزَح"i kastetmiştir. Ebü'l-Feth [İbn Cinnî] şöyle demiştir: "Bu uzatmanın tek bir kelimenin arasına girmesi caiz olunca, muzâf ile muzâfun ileyh arasında uzatma haydi haydi caizdir; çünkü onlar iki şeydir."» eş-Şeyh [Ebû Hayyân], İbn Atıyye'nin sözünden sonra şöyle demiştir: «Bu, uygun olmayan şeylerle çoğaltma ve benzetme yapmaktır. Bu şâz kıraatin tevcihine uygun olan, onun vaslı vakıf yerine koyma kabilinden olmasıdır; vakıfta [tâyı] hâya çevirdikleri gibi vasılda da onu [hâya] çevirmiştir. Onların sözlerinde vaslı vakıf yerine, vakfı da vasıl yerine koymak mevcuttur. "Ancak Araplardan bazı yerlerde bunun benzeri gelmiştir" sözüne gelince: Zikrettiği şeylerin hepsi harekeyi işbâ (doyurma/uzatma) babındandır; harekeyi işbâ ise vasılda tâyı hâya çevirmek gibi değildir. Bunun benzeri ancak onların "ثلثهَ اربعة" sözleridir: Tâyı hâya çevirmiş, "أربعة"nın hemzesinin harekesini ona nakletmiş ve hemzeyi hazfetmiştir. Böylece ibdâlde vaslı vakıf yerine koymuş ve [nakilde de] vaslı vakıf yerine koymuştur [Mütercim notu: kaynakta böyledir; ikinci ifadenin "vakfı vasıl yerine koymuştur" olması beklenir], zira nakil ancak vasılda olur.»
Şâz olarak sâkin bir tâ ile «بثلاثةْ» diye de okunmuştur; bu da sükûn bakımından vaslı vakıf yerine koyma kabilindendir. Şimdi üzerinde vakfedilen bu tâ hakkında ihtilaf edilmiştir: Bu, var olan te'nîs tâsı olup sadece sükûn mu bulmuştur, yoksa tâdan çevrilmiş te'nîs hâsından bedel midir? Bu, altında fayda olmayan bir ihtilaftır.
{مِّنَ الملائكة} sözü: «مِنْ»in beyân için olması caizdir; «مِنْ» ile mecrûrunun «ثلاثة»ya veya «آلاف»a sıfat olarak cer mahallinde olması da caizdir.
{مُنزَلِينَ} sözü: «ثلاثة آلاف»ın sıfatıdır; «الملائكة»den hâl olması da caizdir; birincisi daha açıktır. İbn Âmir teşdîd ile «مُنَزَّلين» diye okumuştur; Ankebût sûresindeki {إِنَّا مُنزِلُونَ على أَهْلِ هذه القرية} [âyet: 34] sözünü de şeddeli okumuştur; ancak burada ism-i mef'ûl, orada ism-i fâildir. Diğerleri ikisini de şeddesiz okumuştur. İbn Ebî Able burada zâ kesreli, şeddeli ve fâile mebnî olarak «مُنَزِّلين» diye okumuştur. Bazıları da aynı şekilde, ancak zâyı şeddesiz okumuştur; onu «أكرم» gibi «أنزل»den yapmıştır. Teşdîd de hemze de ikisi de ta'diye (fiili geçişli kılma) içindir; dolayısıyla «فَعَّل» ve «أَفْعل» aynı mânâdadır. Zemahşerî'nin teşdîdi tencîm (parça parça indirme) üzerine delâlet eder saydığı ve bu konudaki tartışmanın onunla yapıldığı daha önce geçmişti. Son iki kıraatte mef'ûl mahzûf olur, yani «müminlere zaferi, kâfirlere azabı indirenler olarak».
«بلى» sözü: Cevap harfidir; Allah Teâlâ'nın {أَلَنْ يَكْفِيكُمْ} sözündeki nefyi icaba (olumluya) çevirir. Bu konudaki söz daha önce doyurucu şekilde geçmişti. Şartın cevabı «يُمْدِدْكُم» sözüdür.
«الفَوْر»: acele ve süratdir. «فارَت القِدْر» (tencere kaynadı) da bundandır; yani kaynaması şiddetlendi ve içindekiler dışarı çıkmaya koştu. «فارَ يفُور فَوْراً» denir. Bununla öfke ve hiddet de ifade edilir; çünkü öfkeli kimse öfkelendiği kişiyi yakalamaya koşar. Dolayısıyla «الفور» aslında masdardır; sonra onunla, içinde gecikme olmayan ve başka bir şeye sapma bulunmayan hâl ifade edilir.

His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ تَقُولُ}: There are three views on it. The first: that this adverb is a badal (substitute) for his saying «إذ هَمَّتْ». The second: that it is accusative by «نصركم». The third: that it is accusative by an implied "remember" (اذكر). And is this sentence part of the completion of the story of Badr, which is the view of the majority, so that there is no parenthetical interruption in this discourse; or part of the completion of Uḥud, so that his saying {وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ الله} would be a parenthetical clause between the two discourses? It is a well-known disagreement.

His saying: {أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ}: the fāʿil (agent) of «ألن يكفيكم», i.e. "will the supplying of reinforcements by your Lord not suffice you?" When the hamza entered upon the negation, it made it affirmative in the manner of rebuke (inkār). «لن» was used rather than «لا» because it is stronger in negation. In the codex of Ubayy it is «ألا», with «لا» rather than «لن», as if he intended to explain the meaning.

And «بثلاثة» is attached to «يُمِدَّكم». Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «ثلاثَهْ آلاف» with a quiescent hāʾ in continuous speech (waṣl), and likewise «بخمسهْ آلاف», as if he made waṣl follow the course of pause (waqf). It is weak, because it occurs in two terms of a genitive construct that require connection. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The aspect of this reading is weak, because the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi are like one thing and require connection, the second being the completion of the first, whereas the hāʾ is only a sign of pause, so a pause is awkward in a place that is meant for connection. But something like this has occurred in places in the speech of the Arabs. Among that is what al-Farrāʾ related of their saying "akaltu laḥman shāh" (I ate the meat of a sheep), meaning "laḥma shāh": they stretched the fatḥa until an alif arose from it, as they say in pause "qālā", meaning "qāla". Then they stretch the fatḥa in rhyme-words and similar places of deliberation and steadiness. And among that in poetry is his saying:

1422 - يَنْباع من ذِفْرى غضوبٍ جَسْرَةٍ ... زَيَّافَةٍ مثلِ الفنيق المُكْدَمِ
(It gushes from behind the ear of an ill-tempered, bold she-camel, swaggering in her gait, like the bitten stud-camel.)

He means "yanbaʿu", and stretched it. And similar is the saying of another:

1423 - أقول إذ خَرَّتْ على الكَلْكال ... يا ناقتي ما جُلْت مِنْ مَجَال
(I say, when she fell upon her chest: O my she-camel, you did not roam from any field.)

He means "al-kalkal(i)", and stretched it. And similar is the saying of another:

1424 - فأنتَ من الغوائلِ حين تُرْمَى ... ومن ذمِّ الرجال بمُنْتزاحِ
(You, when shot at, are far from calamities and from the blame of men.)

He means "bi-muntazaḥ". Abū al-Fatḥ said: "If it is permissible for this prolongation to intervene within a single word, then prolongation is permissible between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi, since they are two." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said after Ibn ʿAṭiyya's words: "It is piling up and drawing parallels with what is not appropriate. What is appropriate for the justification of this irregular reading is that it is from making waṣl follow the course of waqf: he substituted [hāʾ] for it in waṣl as they substitute it in waqf, and it is found in their speech to make waṣl follow waqf and waqf follow waṣl. As for his saying 'but something like this has occurred in places in the speech of the Arabs', everything he mentioned is only from the category of the prolongation (ishbāʿ) of the vowel, and prolongation of the vowel is not like substituting hāʾ for tāʾ in waṣl. The parallel of this is only their saying "thalathah arbaʿa": he substituted hāʾ for the tāʾ, transferred the vowel of the hamza of "arbaʿa" to it, and dropped the hamza. So he made waṣl follow waqf in the substitution, and made waṣl follow waqf [Translator's note: the source repeats the same phrase here; the second occurrence is probably meant to read "made waqf follow waṣl"], since the transfer occurs only in waṣl."

It was also read irregularly «بثلاثةْ» with a quiescent tāʾ, which is likewise from making waṣl follow waqf as regards the quiescence. There is disagreement about this tāʾ upon which one now pauses: is it the tāʾ of the feminine which was there and has merely become quiescent, or is it a substitute for the feminine hāʾ which itself was substituted for the tāʾ? This is a disagreement with nothing of benefit beneath it.

And his saying {مِّنَ الملائكة}: it is possible that «مِنْ» is explanatory (lil-bayān), and possible that «من» and its genitive noun are in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «ثلاثة» or of «آلاف».

His saying: {مُنزَلِينَ}: an adjective of «ثلاثة آلاف», and it may be a ḥāl from «الملائكة», but the first is more evident. Ibn ʿĀmir read «مُنَزَّلين» with doubling (tashdīd), and likewise he doubled his saying in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, {إِنَّا مُنزِلُونَ على أَهْلِ هذه القرية} [verse 34], except that here it is a passive participle and there an active participle. The others lightened both. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read here «مُنَزِّلين» with doubling and kasra on the زاي, as an active voice. And some read it likewise but lightened the زاي, making it from anzala like akrama. The doubling and the hamza both serve for transitivity, so faʿʿala and afʿala are of the same meaning; and it has already been mentioned that al-Zamakhsharī makes the doubling indicate gradual (successive) sending down (tanjīm), and the discussion with him on that has gone before. In the last two readings the object is omitted, i.e. "sending down victory upon the believers and punishment upon the disbelievers".

His saying: «بلى»: a particle of response (ḥarf jawāb), and it is an affirmation of the negation in his saying, the Exalted, {أَلَنْ يَكْفِيكُمْ}; its discussion has already been given at length. And the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is his saying «يُمْدِدْكُم».

And al-fawr is haste and speed; from it: "fārat al-qidr" (the pot boiled over), when its boiling intensified and what was in it hurried to come out. One says: fāra yafūru fawran. It is used to express anger and fierceness, because the angry man hurries to strike at the one with whom he is angry. So al-fawr is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and then it is used to express the state in which there is no delay and no turning aside to anything else.

His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بشرى}: There are three views on it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and this is an emptied (unspecified-subject) exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), since the estimate is: "and He did not make it for anything of things except for the glad tidings". The conditions for its being accusative are present, namely unity of agent and of time, and its being a maṣdar brought for the cause. The second: that it is a second object of «جَعَل», taking it as a verb of transformation (taṣyīriyya). The third: that it is a badal from the هاء in «جَعَله»; this was said by al-Ḥawfī, who made the هاء refer back to the promise of reinforcement. And al-bushrā is a maṣdar of the pattern fuʿlā, like al-ruj ʿā.

His saying: {وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ}: There are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «بشرى». This is if we make it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. It is genitive with the lām only because one of the conditions of the accusative is deficient, namely the unity of agent: the agent of the making is Allah the Exalted, while the agent of the reassurance is the hearts. Therefore what is conjoined to is accusative, its conditions being complete, and the conjoined is genitive with the lām, its condition being deficient, as has gone before. The estimate: "and He did not make it except for the glad tidings and for the reassurance". The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and that your hearts may be reassured He did that", or "it was such and such".

The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "«وتطمئنَّ» is accusative by an implied «أنْ» after the lām of purpose (lām kay), so it is a conjunction of a noun upon the supposed position of another noun." Then he reported from Ibn ʿAṭiyya that he said: "The lām in «ولتطمئن» is attached to an implied verb indicated by «جعله», and the meaning of the verse is: 'This reinforcement was only so that you might rejoice at it and your hearts be reassured by it.'" The Shaykh said: "It is as if he saw that it is not possible, in his view, for «ولتطمئن» to be conjoined to «بشرى» by position, because it is a condition of conjunction by position, according to our colleagues, that there be a preserver of the position (muḥriz), and there is no preserver here, because the genitive-governing agent is missing. Whoever does not make the muḥriz a condition permits that, and it would be of the category of conjunction by supposition (ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum)." I say: Some have made the واو in «ولتطمئن» redundant (zāʾida), which suits the school of al-Akhfash; on this the lām is attached to «البشرى», i.e. the glad tidings are the reason for the making, and the reassurance is the reason for the glad tidings, so it is the reason of the reason.

Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī said: "In the mention of the reinforcement there are two aims. One: the entry of joy into their hearts, which is what is meant by {إِلاَّ بشرى}; and the second: the attainment of reassurance through victory so that they do not become cowardly, and this is the original purpose. So he distinguished between these two expressions as a warning of the difference between the two matters, conjoining the verb to the noun, and since the stronger is the attainment of reassurance, he introduced the particle of causation." The Shaykh said: "His words 'conjoining the verb to the noun' are open to dispute, since it is not a conjunction of a verb to a noun, and also his words 'he introduced the particle of causation', for it is not as he said." End of quotation. I say: If the Shaykh means that he did not introduce the particle of causation at all, that is not accepted and cannot be denied; but if he means that he did not introduce it in the sense the Imām intended, then it is easy.

Al-Jurjānī said in his Naẓm: "This is on the interpretation: 'and Allah did not make it except to give you glad tidings and that your hearts be reassured'. And whoever permits the insertion of the واو, which is the school of the Kufans, makes it inserted in «ولتطمئنَّ», so the estimate is: 'and Allah did not make it except glad tidings for you so that your hearts be reassured by it.'"

And the two pronouns in his saying «وما» «جعله» and «به» refer back to the reinforcement understood from the preceding verb, which is his saying «يُمْدِدْكم». It is also said that they refer to the victory; and it is said, to the marking (al-taswīm); and it is said, to the sending down; and it is said, to the number; and it is said, to the promise.

In this verse He said «لكم» and omitted it in Sūrat al-Anfāl, because that one is an abridgement of this one, and it seems that elaboration is more fitting here, because the story is complete here, so it suited the putting of them at ease by direct address. And he placed «به» later here and earlier in Sūrat al-Anfāl, because the address is present here in «لكم», so he made address follow address. And here he brought the two attributes as followers in his saying {العزيز الحكيم}, while he brought them in a resumptive sentence in al-Anfāl in his saying {إِنَّ الله عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ} [verse 10], because when he addressed them here, it was fitting to hasten their glad tidings that He is Mighty and Wise, i.e. that He is not overcome and that all His deeds are perfectly made, wisdom and rightness.

His saying, the Exalted: {أَوْ يَتُوبَ}: There are several views on its being accusative. The first: that it is conjoined to the accusative verbs before it, its estimate being: "that He may cut off, or abase them, or turn to them in forgiveness, or punish them". On this, his saying «ليس لك من الأمرِ شيءٌ» is a parenthetical sentence between the two conjoined elements. The meaning: Allah the Exalted is the Owner of their affair; if He wills, He cuts off a part of them or defeats them, or turns to them in forgiveness if they submit and return, or punishes them if they persist in their disbelief. A group of grammarians, such as al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj, took this analysis.

The second: that «أو» here is in the sense of «إلاَّ أَنْ» (unless), as in their saying "I will surely cling to you or you pay me my due" (لألزَمَنَّك أو تقضِيَني حقي), i.e. "unless you pay me".

The third: that «أو» is in the sense of «حتى» (until), i.e. "you have no part in the matter until He turns in forgiveness". On these two views the speech is connected with his saying «ليس لك من الأمر شيء», and the meaning is: you have no part in the matter, except that He turns to them in forgiveness through Islam, whereupon joy comes to you through their guidance to it, or He punishes them by killing or by fire in the Hereafter, so that He heals (the hearts) through them. Among those who held this are al-Farrāʾ and Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Like this speech is: 'I will surely blame you or you give me', in the sense of 'unless you give me' and 'until you give me'." And Ibn al-Anbārī recited in that regard the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

1425 - فقلتُ له لاَ تبْكِ عينُك إنَّما ... تحاولُ مُلْكَاً أو تموتَ فَتُعْذَرا
(I said to him: Let not your eye weep; you are only seeking a kingdom, or [else] you die and are excused.)

He meant: "until you die", or "unless you die." I say: In his estimating the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays with «حتى» there is something to consider, since the meaning does not accord with it, because he did not do that for the sake of this goal; and the grammarians did not estimate it except in the sense of «إلاَّ».

[Translator's note: the source numbers this view "the third" a second time; it is the fourth in order.] The third: that it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ», conjoined to his saying «الأمر», as if it were said: "You have nothing of the matter, or of His turning to them in forgiveness, or of His punishing them." Since it is in the interpretation of a noun, it is conjoined to the noun before it. It is of the category of his saying:

1426 - ولولا رجالٌ من رِزامٍ أعِزَّةً ... وآلُ سُبَيْعٍ أو أَسُوْءَكَ علقما
(Were it not for men of Rizām, mighty, and the family of Subayʿ, or I would grieve you, O ʿAlqama.)

and her saying:

1427 - لَلُبْسُ عباءةٍ وتقرَّ عيني ... أَحَبُّ إليَّ مِنْ لُبْسِ الشُّفوف
(To wear a cloak and have my eye be cooled is dearer to me than wearing fine garments.)

The fourth: that it is conjoined, by the interpretation mentioned, to «شيء», the estimate being: "You have nothing of the matter, nor Allah's turning to them in forgiveness, nor their punishment", i.e. you have no part either in their repentance or in their punishment; that returns only to Allah the Exalted.

Ubayy read: «أو يتوبُ، أو يعذِّبُهم» with both in the nominative, as a resumption in a nominal sentence whose mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "or He turns in forgiveness and punishes them".

Allah Teâlâ'nın {الذين يُنفِقُونَ} sözü: Mahallinde üç i'rab da caizdir: Cer, na't (sıfat), bedel veya beyân (atf-ı beyân) olarak; nasb ve ref' ise medhe (övgüye) işaret eden kat' (öncekinden koparma) üzerine.
{والكاظمين} sözü: Bunda, kendisinden öncekinde geçtiği üzere cer ve nasb caizdir. «الكَظْم»: hapsetmek (tutmak)tır. «كَظَمَ غيظَه» yani öfkesini tuttu. «كَظَم القِرْبة والسِّقاء»: tulumun ve su kabının ağzını, içindekinin çıkmasına engel olacak şekilde bağladığında söylenir. Tulumun ve su kabının bu şekilde bağlandığı kayış için kullanılan «الكِظام» de bundandır. «الكَظْم» aslında nefesin çıkış yeridir; «أخَذَ بَكَظْمِه» denir, yani nefesinin çıkış yerinden yakaladı. «الكُظُوم»: nefesin tutulmasıdır; bununla sükûnet de ifade edilir, «فلان لا يتنفَّس» (falan nefes almıyor) sözleri gibi. «المَكْظُوم»: öfkeyle dolu olandır; sanki öfkesinden konuşamaz ve nefesini çıkaramaz. «الكَظِيم»: üzüntüyle dolu olandır. Ebû Tâlib şöyle demiştir:
1428 - فَحَضَضْتُ قومي واحتَسَبْتُ قتالَهم ... والقومُ من خوفِ المَنايا كُظَّمُ
(Kavmimi teşvik ettim ve onlarla savaşmayı Allah'tan umdum; kavim ise ölüm korkusundan nefeslerini tutmuş (susmuş) hâldeydi.)
«كَظَم البعيرُ»: deve bundan dolayı geviş getirmeyi bıraktığında söylenir. Râî'nin şu sözü de bundandır:
1429 - وأفَضْنَ بعدَ كُظومِهِنَّ بِجِرَّةٍ ... مِنْ ذي الأباطِحِ إذ رَعَيْنَ حَقِيلا
(Develer, Hakîl'de otladıklarında, geviş getirmeyi kestikten sonra Zü'l-Ebâtıh [otundan] geviş getirmeye koyuldular.)
«الحقيل» bir bitkidir; bir yer olduğu da söylenmiştir. Birinciye göre mef'ûlün bihtir, ikinciye göre zarftır; bu durumda, muayyen bir mekân zarfı olduğu için «في» ile mecrûr olmaması şâz olur ve mef'ûl mahzûf olur, yani «Hakîl'de otu otladıklarında». Develer gevişlerini ancak korku anında keserler. Develeri çokça kesen bir adamı vasfeden A'şâ Bâhile'nin şu sözü de bundandır:
1430 - قد تَكْظِمُ البُزْلُ منه حين تُبْصِرُه ... حتى تَقَطَّع في أَجْوافِها الجِرَرُ
(Yaşlı güçlü develer onu gördüklerinde ondan [korkup] gevişlerini tutarlar; öyle ki karınlarındaki gevişleri kesilir.)
«الجِرَر», «جِرَّة»nın çoğuludur. «الكِظامَة»: terazinin ucunda bulunan ve iplerinin içinde toplandığı demir halkadır; yayın kirişine bağlanan kayış da odur. «الكَظَائِم»: iki el (iki taraf) arasında, suyun birinden diğerine aktığı oyuklardır. Bütün bunlar nefesin akış yerine benzetilerek söylenmiştir.

His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يُنفِقُونَ}: the three cases are possible for its position: the genitive, as a naʿt or badal or explicative apposition (bayān); and the accusative and nominative by severance (qaṭʿ) which signals praise.

His saying: {والكاظمين}: the genitive and accusative are possible for it, as has gone before regarding what precedes it. Al-kaẓm: restraining. Kaẓama ghayẓahu means he restrained it; and kaẓama al-qirba wa-l-siqāʾ (the water-skin and the milk-skin) when he tied their two mouths, preventing what is in them from coming out; from it comes al-kiẓām, the thong with which the skin and the water-skin are tied. Originally al-kaẓm is the outlet of the breath; one says "he took him by his kaẓm", i.e. the outlet of his breath. Al-kuẓūm: the holding back of the breath, by which stillness is expressed, as in their saying "so-and-so does not breathe". And al-makẓūm: one filled with rage, as if because of his rage he cannot speak or let out his breath; and al-kaẓīm: one filled with grief. Abū Ṭālib said:

1428 - فَحَضَضْتُ قومي واحتَسَبْتُ قتالَهم ... والقومُ من خوفِ المَنايا كُظَّمُ
(I urged on my people and counted their fighting a reward with Allah, while the people, out of fear of death, were holding their breath.)

And kaẓama al-baʿīr: when the camel stops chewing the cud because of that; from it is the saying of al-Rāʿī:

1429 - وأفَضْنَ بعدَ كُظومِهِنَّ بِجِرَّةٍ ... مِنْ ذي الأباطِحِ إذ رَعَيْنَ حَقِيلا
(And they poured forth, after their holding back, a cud from [the pasture of] Dhū al-Abāṭiḥ when they grazed ḥaqīl.)

And al-ḥaqīl is a plant; it is also said to be a place. On the first view it is a mafʿūl bihi, and on the second it is an adverb, and it would be irregular that it is not governed by «في», because it is a specific adverb of place, and the object would be omitted, i.e. "when they grazed the pasture in Ḥaqīl". Camels cut off their cud only at fright. From it is the saying of Aʿshā Bāhila describing a man who slaughters camels abundantly:

1430 - قد تَكْظِمُ البُزْلُ منه حين تُبْصِرُه ... حتى تَقَطَّع في أَجْوافِها الجِرَرُ
(The mature camels hold back [their cud] at him when they see him, until the cuds are cut off in their bellies.)

Al-jirar is the plural of jirra (cud). Al-kiẓāma: an iron ring at the end of the balance in which its cords are gathered; it is also the thong joined to the bowstring. And al-kaẓāʾim: openings between two hands (channels) from which water flows to the other; all of that by analogy with the passage of the breath.

His saying, the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: it may be attached to «خَلَتْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «سنن», because originally it could be an adjective, and when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl.

And al-sunan is the plural of «سُنَّة», which is the way that a person follows and keeps to; from it comes "the sunna of the prophets", peace be upon them. Khālid al-Hudhalī said to his maternal uncle Abū Dhuʾayb:

1433 - فلا تَجْزَعَنْ مِنْ سُنَّةٍ أنت سِرْتَها ... فَأَوَّلُ راضٍ سُنَّةً مَنْ يَسيرُها
(So do not be distressed at a custom you yourself set; the first to be content with a custom is the one who sets it.)

And another said:

1434 - وإنَّ الأُلَى بالطَّفِّ مِنْ آلِ هاشمٍ ... تَأَسَّوا فَسَنُّوا للكرامِ التآسِيا
(Those at al-Ṭaff of the family of Hāshim followed one another's example, and so set for the noble the custom of mutual emulation.)

And Labīd said:

1435 - مِنْ أمةٍ سَنَّتْ لهم آباؤُهم ... ولكلِّ قومٍ سُنَّةٌ وإمامُها
(From a community whose forefathers set a custom for them; every people has a custom and its leader.)
