Bu şahitlerde delil yoktur. «في الدنيا حسنةً وفي الآخرةِ حسنةً» ve «وجَعَلْنَا من بينِ أيديهم» kavline gelince: Çünkü iki şeyi iki şeye atfetmiştir: Hâfıdı tekrar ederek «الآخرة»yi «الدنيا»ya, ikinci «حسنةً»yi birinci «حسنةً»ye atfetmiştir. Aynı şekilde «مِنْ خلفهم»i «من بين»e, «سداً»yı «سداً»ya atfetmiştir. Beyitte de böyledir; orada «أَدِيمَها»yı «تَراها»nın birinci mef'ûlüne, «نَغِلا»yı ikinci mef'ûl olan «كشِبْه»e, ikinci «يوماً»yı da birinci «يوماً»ya atfetmiştir; bu durumda onda ayırma yoktur. O zaman denir ki: Ebû Ali'nin bunu mutlak olarak men etmesi ve zarureti istisnâ etmemesi gerekirdi; çünkü şahit getirdiği şey, zikrettiğim şekilde te'vil edilmiştir. Eğer "Ebû Ali onu ancak şu sebeple bundan (iki şeyi iki şeye atıf babından) kılmamıştır: Bu, ikinci zarfın birincide vaki olanla tahsis edilmesine götürür; yani onu birinci ve ikinci günde çizgili (Yemen) cübbeler gibi görmesine; çünkü ma'tûfun hükmü ma'tûfun aleyhin hükmüdür; bu, senin «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة ويوم السبت» (Zeyd'i cuma günü ve cumartesi günü dövdüm) demenin benzeridir; «يومَ السبت», cuma gününün Zeyd'i dövmekle kayıtlandığı gibi onunla kayıtlıdır; hâlbuki maksat, beyitteki ikinci günün başka bir kayıtla, yani yüzeyini bozulmuş görmekle kayıtlanmasıdır" denirse, cevap şudur: Eğer ikinci zarfı başka bir anlamla kayıtlamaksızın zâhirle baş başa bırakılsaydık, hüküm senin zikrettiğin gibi olurdu; çünkü «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة ويوم السبت» örneğinde zikrettiğin gibi zâhir odur. Ama onu başka bir şeyle kayıtladığında, bu nass sebebiyle o zâhir terk edilmiş olur. Görmez misin ki «ضربت زيداً يوم الجمعة وعمراً يوم السبت» (Zeyd'i cuma günü, Amr'ı da cumartesi günü dövdüm) dersin; bu da böyledir. Bu, tefekküre muhtaç bir yerdir.
«فبشَّرناها بإسحاق»a gelince: «يعقوب», «إسحاق»a atfen mecrûr değil, bilakis gizli bir fiille mansûbdur; yani: "Ona Ya'kûb'u da bağışladık." Buna ref' kıraati delâlet eder; çünkü o, onun müjdeden kopuk olduğunu haber verir. Nasıl olur ki, bu görüşü söyleyenin "Ma'tûfun aleyh mecrûr olduğunda câr ma'tûfla birlikte tekrar edilir" dediği geçti? [Mütercim notu: Metinde «ووهبا لها» yazılmıştır; «ووهبنا لها» olmalıdır.] {أَن تُؤدُّواْ الأمانات}e gelince: Bunda da delâlet yoktur; çünkü «إذا» bir zarftır ve mutlaka bir âmili olmalıdır. [Mütercim notu: Metinde «لا بدل له من عامل» yazılmıştır; «لا بُدَّ له من عامل» olmalıdır; buna göre çevrilmiştir.] Onun âmili ya «أَنْ تَحْكُموا»dır —ki anlam cihetinden açık olan budur— [Mütercim notu: Metindeki «/» işareti kaynak baskıda sayfa geçişini gösterir.] ya da «يأمُركم»dır. Birincisi, anlam ona göre olsa bile, mümtenidir; çünkü Basralılara göre mevsûlün etki alanındaki şey ona takdim edilmez. Kûfeliler ise bunu caiz görürler; onlara göre bu ayet de buradandır. Şu sözle istidlal etmişlerdir:
4596 - كان جَزائي بالعصا أَنْ أُجْلَدا
(Benim cezam sopayla dövülmek oldu.)
[Mütercim notu: Beyit numarası metinde «4596» olarak yazılmıştır; sıralamaya göre «1596» olmalıdır.]
Bu, sarih mef'ûlde de şu sözde gelmiştir:
1597 -. . . . . . . . . . . . ... وشفاءُ غَيِّك خابراً أَنْ تَسْألي
(…Bilgisizliğinin şifası, bilen birine sormandır.)
Zarf ve benzerinde nasıl olmaz? İkincisi de mümtenidir; çünkü emir, hüküm vaktinde vaki değildir. Şeyh (Ebû Hayyân) böyle söylemiştir; bunda nazar vardır. Bu ikisi bâtıl olunca, ondaki âmil, sonrasının tefsir ettiği takdir edilmiş bir şeydir; takdiri: "Hükmettiğinizde hükmetmenizi…"dir. Son «أن تحكموا» birinciye delâlet eder.
{بالعدل} kavli: Bunda iki vecih caizdir. Birincisi: «تحكموا»ya mütealliktir; bu durumda bâ ta'diye içindir. İkincisi: «تَحْكُموا»nın fâilinden hâl olmak üzere mahzûfa mütealliktir; bu durumda bâ musâhabet içindir; yani: "Adaletle iç içe ve onunla beraber olarak." İki anlam birbirini gerektirir.
{إِنَّ الله نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ} kavli: «نعم» ve «بئس»e bitişik «ما» hakkındaki söz ve insanların onun hakkında zikrettikleri geçmişti; ona müracaat etmelisin. Ancak İbn Atıyye burada vehimden uzak olmayan bir nakil yapmıştır; onu zikretmek gerekir. O şöyle demiştir: «"نِعْم"e eklenen "ما", "ربما"da olduğu gibi ve "Rasûlullah (s.a.v.) dudaklarını kıpırdatanlardandı (مِمَّا يحرِّك شفتيه)" sözündeki "مِمَّا"da olduğu gibi, fiilin ona bitişmesi için hazırlayıcı (müheyyie) olan "ما"dır. Şu söz gibi:
1598 - وإنَّا لَمِمَّا نضربُ الكبشَ ضربةً ... على رأسِه تُلْقي اللسانَ من الفم
(Biz, (ordunun) koçuna (komutanına) başına öyle bir darbe vuranlardanız ki dili ağızdan düşürür.)
Bunda o, "ربما" mesabesindedir; ancak anlamda ona muhaliftir; çünkü "ربما" azlık, "مِمَّا" çokluk içindir. "ما" muvattıe (zemin hazırlayıcı) olmakla birlikte "الذي" anlamındadır; ancak isim olarak zemin hazırlamıştır; fakat kasıt, fiilde bulunan ve ona bitişen anlamadır.» Şeyh (Ebû Hayyân) şöyle demiştir: «Bu tutarsızdır; çünkü onu muvattıe ve müheyyie kıldığı cihetle isim olmaz; "الذي" anlamında kıldığı cihetle ise isim olması gerekir; böylece ikisi birbirini iter.»

Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَكَيْفَ} kavli: «كيف»de iki vecih caizdir. Birincisi: Nasb mahallindedir; bu Zeccâc'ın görüşüdür; o şöyle demiştir: «Takdiri: "Onları nasıl görürsün?"dür.» İkincisi: Mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir; yani: "Musibet onlara isabet ettiği vakit onların yaptıkları nasıl olur?" «إذا», «كيف»ten sonra takdir edilen o şeyin ma'mûlüdür. «بما»daki bâ sebebiyyet içindir. «ما»nın masdariyye de ismiyye (ism-i mevsûl) de olması caizdir; (ismiyye ise) âid mahzûftur. {يَحْلِفُونَ} kavli: «جاؤوك»in fâilinden hâldir. «إنْ» nâfiyedir; yani: «ما أردنا» ("istemedik"). «إحساناً», meseledeki iki görüşe göre ya mef'ûlün bihtir ya da müstesnâdır.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {في أَنْفُسِهِمْ}: there are several views on it. The most sound: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قل», and there are two meanings in it. The first: "speak to them in private, with no one else with them", because that is more conducive to the acceptance of advice. The second: "speak to them concerning their souls that harbour hypocrisy, words that reach in them what will restrain them from returning to hypocrisy". The second view: it is attached to «بليغاً», i.e. "words that affect their hearts, by which they are greatly distressed and which they deeply feel"; al-Zamakhsharī stated its meaning. Al-Shaykh rebutted him on the ground that this is the doctrine of the Kufans, since it involves placing the dependent of an adjective before the qualified noun: if you said «جاء زيداً رجلٌ يضربُ» (a man came striking Zayd), it would not be allowed according to the Basrans, because the dependent precedes only where the governor may precede, and here the governor may not precede, because the adjective does not precede the qualified noun; while the Kufans allow the dependent of the adjective to precede the qualified noun. As for the Basrans' saying that the dependent precedes only where the governor precedes, it is open to discussion: we have found this rule broken in His words {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السآئل فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9-10], for «اليتيم» is governed by «تقهر» and «السائل» by «تنهر», and they precede the prohibitive «لا», while their governor may not be placed before it, since the jussive verb does not precede what makes it jussive; so the dependent has preceded where the governor does not precede. Likewise what they said about his words:
1602 - قنافِذُ هَدَّاجون حولَ بيوتِهم ... بما كان إيَّاها عطيَّةُ عَوَّدا
(Hedgehogs creeping about their houses [at night], because of what ʿAṭiyya accustomed them to.)
They explained this verse on the basis that in «كان» there is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), «عَطِيَّةُ» being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «عَوَّدَ» its khabar (predicate), so that the dependent of its khabar — which is neither an adverbial nor the like — does not follow «كان» directly. This obliged them to place the dependent, which is «إياهم» [Translator's note: so here; the verse has «إيَّاها»], before where the governor does not precede, because when the khabar is a verb governing a latent pronoun in the nominative, its placement before the mubtadaʾ is disallowed lest it be confused with the agent, as in «زيد ضرب عمراً». The original source of this discussion is the placing of the khabar of «ليس» before it, which the majority allowed because of the words of Allah the Exalted {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ} [Hūd: 8]; the point of evidence is that «يوم» is governed by «مصروفاً» and has preceded «ليس», and the precedence of the dependent signals the precedence of the governor. They were then countered with what I have mentioned to you. There is scope for examination in this discussion that this is not the place for; I have treated it thoroughly in my book «al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr: Sharḥ Tashīl al-Fawāʾid», so refer to it. The third: it has been transmitted from Mujāhid — and I do not think it is authentic from him — that it is attached to «مصيبة», so it is a case of advancing and postponing [word order]; the Qur'an is to be kept free of that, and I have only mentioned it to point out its weakness.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ} kavli: Bu meselede dört görüş vardır. Birincisi —ki İbn Cerîr'in görüşüdür—: Birinci «لا», kendinden önce geçen bir söze reddir; takdiri: "Hayır, akıl erdirmiyorsunuz" ya da: "Durum, sana indirilene iman ettiklerine dair iddia ettikleri gibi değildir." Sonra bundan sonra yeni bir yemine başlamıştır. Buna göre «لا» üzerinde vakf tâmdır. İkincisi: Birinci «لا», nefye önem verildiği için yemine takdim edilmiş, sonra te'kîd için tekrar edilmiştir. Birincinin düşürülmesi sahih olurdu ve nefiy anlamı kalırdı; ancak zikredilen önem verme delâleti kaybolurdu. İkincinin düşürülmesi de sahih olurdu ve önem verme anlamı kalırdı; ancak nefiy delâleti kaybolurdu. Bu yüzden ikisi bir araya getirilmiştir. Üçüncüsü: İkincisi zâidedir; yemin nefiy harfi ile menfî arasında i'tirâziyyedir; sanki takdir: "Rabbine yemin olsun ki iman etmezler"dir. Dördüncüsü: Birincisi zâide, ikincisi zâide değildir. Bu Zemahşerî'nin tercihidir; o şöyle demiştir: «"لا", {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [Hadîd: 29] kavlinde bilmenin vücubunu te'kîd için ziyade edildiği gibi, yemin anlamını te'kîd için ziyade edilmiştir. "لا يؤمنون" yeminin cevabıdır. Eğer "Bunun, "لا يؤمنون"deki "لا"yı desteklemek için ziyade edildiğini neden ileri sürmedin?" dersen, derim ki: Bunda nefiy ile isbatın eşit olması buna engeldir; bu da şu kavlidir: {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ وَمَا لاَ تُبْصِرُونَ إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ} [Hâkka: 38].» Yani: Cevapta «لا» bulunmadığı yerde de yeminden önce «لا» gelmiştir. Zemahşerî, Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُون} [Hâkka: 38] kavlindeki «لا»nın da yemin anlamını te'kîd için zâide olduğu görüşündedir; bu iki görüşten biridir; diğer görüş de Taberî'nin geçen görüşü gibidir. Zikredilen izahlarda ayetin benzeri, diğerinin şu sözüdür:
1603 - فلا واللَّهِ لا يُلْفَى لِما بي ... ولا لَلِما بهم أبداً دواءُ
(Hayır, Allah'a yemin olsun ki ne bendeki derde ne de onlardaki derde ebediyen bir deva bulunmaz.)
{حتى يُحَكِّمُوكَ} kavli: «حتى», «لا يؤمنون» kavline müteallik bir gâyedir; yani: "İman onlardan bu gâyeye kadar nefyedilir"; bu da seni hakem kılmaları, sıkıntı duymamaları ve emrine teslim olmalarıdır. «ربِّك» kavlinde, {واستغفر لَهُمُ الرسول} kavlindeki gaiblikten, «ثم جاؤوك» kavline dönerek iltifat yapmıştır. Ebü's-Semmâl «شَجْر» şeklinde, harekelerin art arda gelmesinden kaçarak cîmin sükûnuyla okumuştur; bu zayıftır; çünkü fetha sükûnun kardeşidir. «بينهم», «شجر» ile mansûb bir zarftır; sahih olan budur. Ebü'l-Bekā onun hâl olmasını caiz görmüş ve bu hâlin sâhibi hakkında iki ihtimal zikretmiştir. Birincisi: İsm-i mevsûl olan «ما»dan hâl olmasıdır. İkincisi: «شجر»in fâilinden hâl olmasıdır; o da anlamca yine ism-i mevsûlün kendisidir. Buna göre mahzûfa mütealliktir. «ثم لا يجدوا», «حتى»den sonrakine ma'tûftur. «ويَجِدُوا»nın iki mef'ûle müteaddî olan (fiil) olması muhtemeldir; bu durumda birincisi «حرجاً», ikincisi ondan önceki câr ve mecrûr olur ve mahzûfa müteallik olur. Tek mef'ûle müteaddî olan olması da muhtemeldir; bu durumda «في أنفسهم»de iki vecih caizdir. Birincisi: Fazlaların (tamamlayıcı unsurların) taalluku şeklinde «يجدوا»ya mütealliktir.
İkincisi: «حَرَجاً»dan hâl olmak üzere mahzûfa mütealliktir; çünkü nekirenin sıfatı ona takdim edildiğinde hâl olarak mansûb olur.
{مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ} kavlinde iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: Bizzat «حرجاً»ya mütealliktir; çünkü «خَرَجْتُ من كذا» dersin. [Mütercim notu: Metinde «خَرَجْتُ» yazılmıştır; bağlam «حَرِجْتُ من كذا» (falan şeyden sıkıntı duydum) olmasını gerektirir.] İkincisi: Mahzûfa mütealliktir; «حرجاً»nın sıfatı olduğu için nasb mahallindedir. «ما»nın masdariyye olması da, «الذي» anlamında olması da caizdir; yani: "Senin hükmünden" ya da "Senin hükmettiğin şeyden bir sıkıntı"; mevsûf bir nekire olması da caizdir; bu son iki görüşe göre âid mahzûftur.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: there are four views on this question. The first, which is the view of Ibn Jarīr: the first «لا» is a rejection of speech that preceded it, its implied form being: "No, you do not understand", or: "the matter is not as they claim, that they believe in what was sent down to you"; then He began an oath after that. On this view the pause on «لا» is complete. The second: the first «لا» was placed before the oath out of concern for the negation, then repeated for emphasis. It would have been valid to drop the first and the [meaning of] negation would remain, but the indication of the said concern would be lost; and it would have been valid to drop the second and the meaning of concern would remain, but the indication of negation would be lost; so both were combined for that reason. The third: the second is redundant (zāʾida), and the oath is parenthetical between the particle of negation and what is negated, as though the implied form were: "So they do not believe, by your Lord". The fourth: the first is redundant and the second is not redundant; this is the choice of al-Zamakhsharī, for he said: "«لا» is added to emphasise the meaning of the oath, as it was added in {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ} [al-Ḥadīd: 29] to emphasise the necessity of knowing; and «لا يؤمنون» is the answer to the oath. If you say: why did you not claim that it was added to support the «لا» in «لا يؤمنون»? I say: that is rejected by the equal status of negation and affirmation in it; that is His words {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ وَمَا لاَ تُبْصِرُونَ إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 38]" — meaning that «لا» has come before the oath where there is no «لا» in the answer. So al-Zamakhsharī holds that the «لا» in the words of Allah the Exalted {فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُون} [al-Ḥāqqa: 38] is also redundant, to emphasise the meaning of the oath; this is one of two views, the other being like the view of al-Ṭabarī already mentioned. Like the verse, according to the explanations mentioned, are the words of another:
1603 - فلا واللَّهِ لا يُلْفَى لِما بي ... ولا لَلِما بهم أبداً دواءُ
(No, by Allah, no remedy is ever found for what afflicts me, nor for what afflicts them.)
His words {حتى يُحَكِّمُوكَ}: «حتى» is [a particle of] limit attached to His words «لا يؤمنون», i.e. faith is negated of them up to this limit, which is their making you judge, their not finding distress, and their submitting to your command. There is a shift (iltifāt) in His word «ربِّك» from the third person in His words {واستغفر لَهُمُ الرسول}, returning to His words «ثم جاؤوك». Abū al-Sammāl read «شَجْر» with sukūn on the jīm, to escape the succession of vowels; this is weak, because fatḥa is the sister of sukūn. «بينهم» is an adverbial made accusative by «شجر»; this is the correct view. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and gave two possibilities for the one qualified by this ḥāl. The first: it is a ḥāl from the relative «ما». The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «شجر», which is also the relative noun itself in meaning; on this view it is attached to an omitted element. «ثم لا يجدوا» is conjoined to what follows «حتى». «يَجِدُوا» may be the one transitive to two objects, the first being «حرجاً» and the second the preposition-phrase before it, which is then attached to an omitted element; or it may be the one transitive to one object, in which case two views are possible on «في أنفسهم». The first: it is attached to «يجدوا», in the way supplementary elements (faḍalāt) are attached.
The second: it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «حَرَجاً», because the adjective of an indefinite noun, when placed before it, becomes accusative as a ḥāl.
On {مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ} there are two views. The first: it is attached to «حرجاً» itself, because you say «حَرِجْتُ من كذا» [Translator's note: printed «خَرَجْتُ» (I went out); the context requires «حَرِجْتُ» (I felt distress)]. The second: it is attached to an omitted element, so it is in the position of accusative because it is an adjective of «حرجاً». «ما» may be maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), or in the sense of «الذي», i.e. "distress from your judgement" or "from that which you judged"; or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective; on these two [latter] views the referent pronoun is omitted.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {مِّنَ النبيين}: there are four views on it. The most apparent: it is an explication of «الذين أَنْعَم الله عليهم» (those whom Allah has favoured). The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «عليهم». The third: it is a ḥāl from the relative noun, which is in meaning like the first; on these two views it is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "being among the prophets". The fourth: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُطِعِ». Al-Rāghib said: "I.e. whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, among the prophets and those after them; and His words {فأولئك مَعَ الذين أَنْعَمَ الله عَلَيْهِم} are an allusion to the Highest Assembly; then He said {وَحَسُنَ أولئك رَفِيقاً}; this is made clear by his words, peace be upon him, at death: 'O Allah, join me to the Highest Companion.' This is apparent." End of quotation. Al-Shaykh showed it to be unsound in terms of meaning and in terms of grammatical technique. In terms of meaning: the Messenger here is Muhammad ﷺ, and Allah the Exalted has informed that whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be with those mentioned; if «مِن النبيين» were made attached to «يُطِع», «من النبيين» would be an explanation of the conditional «مَنْ», which would entail that in his time, peace be upon him, or after him, there are prophets who obey him; and this is not possible because of the words of Allah the Exalted {وَخَاتَمَ النبيين} [al-Aḥzāb: 30] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Aḥzāb: 40] and his words, peace be upon him: "There is no prophet after me." In terms of technique: what precedes the fāʾ occurring as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) does not govern what follows it; if you said «إنْ تضرب يقم عمروٌ زيداً», it would not be allowed. Are these four descriptions for one class of people or for different classes? There are two views.
His words: {وَحَسُنَ أولئك رَفِيقاً}: on the accusative of «رفيقاً» there are two views. The first: it is a tamyīz (specification). The second: it is a ḥāl. On the assumption that it is a tamyīz, there are two possibilities [Translator's note: printed «في احتمالان»; read «ففيه احتمالان»]. The first: it is transferred from the agent position, its implied form being «وحَسُنَ رفيقُ أولئك» (and excellent is the companion of those); on this view the companion is other than the thing specified, and «مِنْ» may not enter on it.
The second: it is not transferred, so it is the specified thing itself, and «مِنْ» may enter on it. It was brought here in the singular for one of two reasons: either because «الرفيق» is like «الخليط» (associate) and «الصديق» (friend) in applying to singular, dual and plural with one form; or by sufficing with the singular in place of the plural because the meaning is understood — and its being a verse-ending (fāṣila) made that good. «أولئك» may point to the prophets and those after them, or to whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, being made plural only according to its meaning. On this view it may be said that He observed the wording of «مَنْ», so made it singular in His word «رفيقاً», and its meaning, so made it plural in His word «أولئك»; except that beginning with construal according to the wording is better in that. On this view He would have combined in it construal according to the wording in «يُطِعْ», then according to the meaning in «أولئك», then according to the wording in «رفيقاً».
The majority read with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn of «حَسُن». Abū al-Sammāl read with fatḥa on it and sukūn on the sīn, for lightness, like «عَضْد» for «عَضُد»; this is the dialect of Tamīm. «وحُسْن» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the sīn is also permissible, as though they transferred the vowel of the ʿayn to the fāʾ after stripping it of its vowel; this is the dialect of some of Qays.
Al-Zamakhsharī made this of the type of exclamation (taʿajjub), for he said: "In it is the meaning of exclamation, as though it were said: how excellent are those as companions! Because of its independence in the meaning of exclamation, «وحَسْنَ» has been read with sukūn on the sīn; one who exclaims says «حَسُنَ الوجهُ وجهُك» and «حَسْن الوجهُ وجهك» (how fine a face is your face!), with fatḥa and ḍamma along with the sukūn." Al-Shaykh said: "This is confusion and the grafting of one doctrine onto another. We say: they disagreed about «فَعُل» intended for praise. Al-Fārisī and most grammarians held that it may be attached only to the category of «نعم» and «بئس», so its agent can only be what can be an agent for them. Al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad held that it may be attached to the category of «نعم» and «بئس», its agent being treated like theirs — that is when the meaning of exclamation does not enter it — and that it may be attached to the verb of exclamation, in which case it is not treated like «نعم» and «بئس» either in the agent or in the rest of their rules; so you say «لَضَرُبَتْ يَدُكَ» (how [skilled] your hand is at striking!) and «لَضَرُبَتِ اليدُ». He took the exclamation from the doctrine of al-Akhfash and the example from the doctrine of al-Fārisī, so he followed neither of the two doctrines. As for his making the sukūn and the transfer [of the vowel] evidence of its being independent in exclamation, that is not granted, because al-Farrāʾ reported that as a dialectal form in what is not intended for exclamation."

The words of Allah the Exalted: {الذين يَشْرُونَ الحياة}: the fāʿil (agent) of His words {فَلْيُقَاتِلْ}. «يَشْرون» admits two views. The first: it is in the sense of «يشترون» (they buy). If it is said: you have established that the bāʾ enters only on what is given up, and the apparent case here is that it has entered on what is taken — the answer is that what is meant by those who buy is the hypocrites who lag behind from jihad; they were commanded to change the hypocrisy in them, make their faith in Allah and His Messenger sincere, and fight in the way of Allah; so it has entered only on what is given up, because the hypocrites give up the Hereafter and take this world. The second: «يشرون» is in the sense of «يَبيعون» (they sell), and what is meant by those who sell is the believers who stay behind from jihad [Translator's note: so in the source], preferring the deferred to the immediate. The counterpart of this verse, in that «شرى» can bear buying and selling according to two perspectives, is the words of Allah the Exalted {وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ} [Yūsuf: 20], which will come. Something of this has preceded for you at the beginning of al-Baqara.
The majority read the lām of «فَلْيقاتل» with sukūn, because it occurs after the fāʾ, so that the word resembles «كتف». It has been read with kasra, which is the original. The majority read «فيُقْتل» as passive, and Muḥārib ibn Dithār as active; the first is more apparent, because of His words «أو يَغْلِب». «يُقْتَلْ» and «يُغْلِب» are conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʾ in «فسوف» is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); it may not be omitted. The well-known [reading] is to pronounce this bāʾ distinctly before the fāʾ; Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, Hishām and Khallād — with a variant from him — assimilated it. The majority read «نُؤْتيه» with the nūn of majesty, and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Aʿmash with the yāʾ of the third person; both are clear.
He put His words {فَيُقْتَلْ} first because it is the rank of martyrdom, which is greater than any other; and He put second the overcoming, which comprises two kinds: killing the enemies of Allah and gaining the spoils, the first being greater than the second.

His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا فَرِيقٌ}: «إذا» here is the "sudden" (fujāʾiyya) particle. It has already been stated that there are three views about it: the first, and the soundest, is that it is an adverb of place; the second, that it is an adverb of time; the third, that it is a particle. These views have a place other than this one. It has also been said of this «إذا» that it is a sudden, locative one and that it is the answer to «لَمَّا» in His saying {فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ}. On that basis there are two possibilities. The first: it is a fronted khabar (predicate), «فريق» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), «منهم» is an adjective (naʿt) of «فريق», and likewise «يَخْشَون»; and it is permissible that «يخشون» be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «فريق» because of its being qualified. The implied form is: "so in the presence there is a group, being among them, fearing (khāshūn or khāshīn)". The second: «فريقٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» is its adjective, and that is what justifies beginning with it (an indefinite noun), and «يَخْشَوْن» is a predicative clause, and it is what governs «إذا». On the first view, what governs it is omitted, according to the rule for adverbs that occur as a khabar. It has been said that here it is an adverb of time, but this is invalid, because in that case it must have a governor, and its governor is either what precedes it or what follows it. It cannot be what precedes it, because what precedes it, namely «كُتب», is past in form and meaning whereas «إذا» is for the future, so that is impossible. If it is said: it is made here to refer to the past, in the sense of «إذ»; it is answered: that is not permissible, because the implied form would then become: "when fighting was prescribed for them, at the time of a group of them fearing", and this requires an answer to «لَمَّا» and it has no answer. Nor can it be what follows it, because if its governor comes after it, it is its answer, and it has no answer here. It was stated at the beginning of al-Baqara that there are two views on «لَمَّا»: the view of Sībawayh, that it is a particle of "occurrence due to occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), and the view of al-Fārisī, that it is an adverb of time in the sense of «حين». The refutation of him was given there: that it is answered by the negative «ما» and by the sudden «إذا», and that what follows it does not govern what precedes it, which makes repeating it unnecessary; and what immediately follows it cannot govern it, because on his claim it is in the position of the genitive by annexation, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf. Some have replied that what governs it here is the meaning of «يَخْشَوْن», as if it were said: "they became anxious"; he said: "and «جزعوا» (they became anxious) is what governs «إذا»; and this verse is problematic, because it contains two adverbs, one for what is past and the other for what is future." End of quotation.

His saying: {كَخَشْيَةِ الله}: it has three possibilities. The first, which is the well-known one among the i'rab scholars: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a fear like the fear of Allah". The second, which is the established view of Sībawayh, repeatedly: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the omitted pronoun of the fear, i.e. "they fear it, the people", that is, "they fear the fear the people, likening it to the fear of Allah".
The third: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يَخْشَوْن», i.e. "they fear the people like the people of the fear of Allah", that is, "resembling the people of the fear of Allah, or with a greater fear", i.e. a fear greater than that of the people who fear Allah. And «اشدَّ» is conjoined to the ḥāl. So said al-Zamakhsharī. Then he said: "If you ask: why did you depart from the obvious, which is that it be an adjective of the maṣdar, and did not take the implied form to be: 'they fear with a fear [like the fear of] Allah', meaning: like what Allah is feared? I say: His saying {أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً} refuses that, because it and what is conjoined to it are of one ruling; and if you said «يخشون الناسَ أشدَّ خشيةً» it could only be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the group, and it would not be accusative as a maṣdar is, because you do not say «خَشِي فلانٌ أشدَّ خشيةً» putting «خشية» in the accusative while intending the maṣdar; you only say «أشدَّ خشيةٍ», putting it in the genitive. And if you put it in the accusative, «أشدَّ خشيةً» can only be an expression for the agent, as a ḥāl from him — unless you make the fear itself 'fearing', along the lines of their saying «جَدَّ جَدُّه», and claim that its meaning is: 'they fear the people with a fear like a fear that is greater in fearing than the fear of Allah'; on this basis it is also permissible that the position of «أشدُّ» be genitive, conjoined to «خشية الله», meaning 'like the fear of Allah or like a fear greater than it'." End of quotation.

It is permissible to put «خشيةً» in the accusative in another way, namely by conjoining it to the position of the kāf, and «أشدَّ» is then accusative as a ḥāl from «خشية», because it is originally an adjective of an indefinite noun that has been put before it; the original is: "they fear the people like the fear of Allah or a fear greater than it". So «خشية» is not accusative as a tamyīz (specification), so that what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned follows from it and has to be excused. Something similar was given earlier at His saying {أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً} [al-Baqara: 200]. The maṣdar is annexed to its object and the agent is omitted, i.e. "like their fear of Allah". And «أو» admits the possibilities mentioned in His saying: {أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً} [al-Baqara: 74]; it may also be for classification (tanwīʿ): meaning that some of them fear them like the fear of Allah, and some of them fear them with a fear greater than the fear of Allah. And «لولا أخَّرْتَنا»: «لولا» is the particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Ibn Kathīr and the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «لا يُظْلَمون» in the third person, following the absent persons before it, while the rest read it in the second person, as a shift of address (iltifāt). And «فَتيلاً»: its i'rab has already been given.

His saying, the Exalted: {لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ}: in «ليس» there is a pronoun which is its subject, and there is disagreement about it: it was said that it refers to something expressed; it was said that it refers to what the wording indicates of the verb; and it was said that the cause of the verse indicates it. As for its referring to something expressed, it was said that it is the promise given earlier in His saying {وَعْدَ الله}, and this is what al-Zamakhsharī chose; he said: "In «ليس» is the pronoun of the promise of Allah, i.e. what Allah promised of reward is not attained by your wishes nor by the wishes of the People of the Book. The address is to the Muslims, because none believes in the promise of Allah except one who believes in Him." And this is a good possibility. As for its referring to what the wording indicates, it was said that it is the faith understood from His saying «والذين آمنوا», and this is the view of al-Ḥasan, who said: "Faith is not by wishing." As for its referring to what the cause indicates, it was said that it refers to the neighbouring (mujāwara) of the Muslims with the People of the Book [Translator's note: the source has «مجاورة»; the context suggests «محاورة», i.e. dialogue or dispute], in that some of them said: "Our religion is before your religion, and our prophet is before your prophet, so we are better"; and the Muslims said: "Our Book judges over your Book, and our Prophet is the seal of the prophets"; so it was revealed. It was also said: it refers to the reward and punishment, i.e. neither reward for good deeds nor punishment for bad deeds is by your wishes. It was also said: the Jews said "We are the prophets of Allah and His beloved ones, and we are the people of Paradise", and likewise the Christians; and the disbelievers of Quraysh said "We shall not be resurrected", so it was revealed, i.e. what you claimed, O disbelievers of Quraysh, is not by your wishes.
Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba ibn Niṣāḥ, al-Ḥakam and al-Aʿraj read «أمانِيكم» and «ولا أمانِي» with lightening (a single yāʾ), as though they pluralised it on faʿālil rather than faʿālīl, as they said «قَرْقور» with plural «قراقير» and «قراقِر»; and the Arabs reduce the yāʾ from faʿālīl, just as they add it to faʿālil, as in the saying:
165 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . تَنْقادَ الصياريفِ
(... as the money-changers examine [coins].)
[Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the source only in part.] And His saying: {مَن يَعْمَلْ}: a resumptive clause that corroborates the ruling of the preceding clause. The majority read «ولا يَجِدْ» jussive, conjoined to the apodosis of the condition; it is narrated from Ibn ʿĀmir that it is nominative, which is by cutting off from the sequence. It may then be resumptive and it may be a ḥāl, so it was said, and there is a consideration in this, in that an imperfect negated by «لا» is not accompanied by the wāw when it occurs as a ḥāl.
His saying: {مِنَ الصالحات مِن ذَكَرٍ}: the first «من» is partitive, because the one under obligation cannot bear the doing of all righteous deeds. Al-Ṭabarī said: "It is redundant according to some", and there is weakness in this for the absence of the two conditions. And the second «مِنْ» is explicative. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl, and as to its owner there are two possibilities: the first, that it is the nominative pronoun of «يعمل»; the second, that it is «الصالحات», i.e. "righteous deeds, from male or female"; the clarification of this has already been given at His saying: {لاَ أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أنثى} [Āl ʿImrān: 195], and the discussion on «أو» too. And His saying «وهو مؤمن» is a circumstantial clause from the agent of «يعمل». Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «يُدْخَلون» here, in Maryam and at the beginning of Ghāfir, with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix and fatḥa on the khāʾ, passive; Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr alone for the second in Ghāfir, and Abū ʿAmr alone for the one in Fāṭir; the rest read it with fatḥa on the imperfect prefix and ḍamma on the khāʾ, active, and that is for variety in eloquence, and differences may be apparent that this book cannot accommodate.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِيَّاكُمْ} is conjoined to «الذين أُوتوا», and here it must be separate because attachment is impossible. Some argued from this verse that when the attached pronoun is possible, one may turn to the detached pronoun, because it would have been possible to say «ولقد وَصَّيْناكم والذين أوتوا». Likewise they argued from the words of Allah the Exalted: {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1], since one could say «يخرجونكم والرسولَ». This does not prove it. As for the first verse, because the speech in it came in the order of actual occurrence, for the injunction to those before us preceded the injunction to us; since this meaning was intended, it was impossible — this being so — for it to be rendered with the attached pronoun. As for the second verse, because in it the prior mention of the Messenger was intended, to honour him and to censure those who dared such a heinous act; so it was impossible — in this case — to bring it as attached. «ومِنْ قبلكم» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أوتوا», and may be attached to «وَصَّيْنا»; the first is more apparent.
His words: {أَنِ اتقوا} — two views are possible regarding «أن». The first: that it is maṣdariyya (infinitival), with omission of the preposition, its implied form being «بأن اتَّقوا»; when the preposition was omitted, the well-known disagreement applied to it. The second: that it is the explicative [«أن»], because it comes after something that has the meaning of speech but not its letters, namely "injunction". The apparent view is that His words {وَإِن تَكْفُرُواْ} are a resumptive clause informing of this state, not included in what the injunction governs. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وإنْ تكفروا فإن لله» is conjoined to «اتقوا», because the meaning is: We commanded them and commanded you with piety, and We said to them and to you: if you disbelieve." There is an objection to his words, because his positing "saying" negates the conditional clause's being included within the scope of the injunction with respect to grammatical craft, and he did not intend only an explanation of meaning; rather he intended that and an explanation of the i'rab, as shown by his saying: "conjoined to «اتقوا»", and «اتقوا» is within the scope of the injunction, whether you make «أن» maṣdariyya or explicative.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {لاَّ يُحِبُّ الله الجهر بالسواء} kavli: [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «بالسواء» yazılıdır; ayetteki ve hemen ardından geçen lafız «بالسوء»dur.] «بالسوء», «الجهر»e mütealliktir; o (الجهر) «أل» ile marife kılınmış bir masdardır. Fârisî bununla, «أل» ile marife kılınmış masdarın amel etmesinin caiz olduğuna istidlal etmiştir. Bunda delil olmadığı söylenmiştir; çünkü zarf ve câr (mecrûr)da fiillerin kokuları (fiil anlamı taşıyan şeyler) amel eder. Bu masdarın fâili mahzûftur, yani: «الجهر أحد» (birinin açıkça söylemesi). Fâilin hazfinin bazı durumlarda kıyasi olarak yapıldığı ve bunlardan birinin masdar olduğu daha önce geçmişti. — bu konudaki ihtilafla birlikte — «الجهر»in meçhul bir fiilden alınmış olması da caizdir; bu durumda ondan sonraki câr, fâilin yerine geçtiği için ref' mahallinde olur; çünkü «لا يحب الله أن يُجهر بالسوء» (Allah kötülüğün açıkça söylenmesini sevmez) deseydin, «بالسوء» fâilin yerine geçmiş olurdu ve o zaman onun (masdara) bir taalluku olmazdı. «من القول», «السوء»dan hâldir.

{إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ} kavli: Bu istisnâda iki görüş vardır. Birincisi: Muttasıl olmasıdır. İkincisi: Munkatı' olmasıdır. Muttasıl olduğu söylendiğinde, (bir görüşe göre) masdarın fâili olan takdîrî «أحد»den müstesnâdır; bu durumda «مَن»ın istisnânın aslı üzere nasb mahallinde ya da «أحد»den bedel olarak ref' mahallinde olması caizdir ki tercih edilen budur. Açıkça söylenseydi: «لا يحبُّ الله أن يَجْهَر أحدٌ بالسوء إلا المظلومُ» ya da «المظلومَ» şeklinde ref' ve nasb ile denirdi. Bunu Mekkî, Ebü'l-Bekā ve başkaları zikretmiştir. Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «Bu Ferrâ'nın mezhebidir; o, 'ما قام إلا زيدٌ'de 'زيد'in 'أحد'den bedel olmasını caiz görmüştür. Cumhurun mezhebine göre ise o, âmilin kendisi için boşaltıldığı (müferrağ) müstesnâdan olur; dolayısıyla masdarla fâil olarak merfû olur. Cehrin nefyin kapsamında bulunması bunu güzelleştirmiştir; sanki 'Sözden kötülüğü ancak mazlum açıkça söyler' denmiştir.» (Söz) bitti. Ferrâ'nın mezhebi ile bu ayet arasındaki fark açıktır; çünkü nahivciler Ferrâ'nın mezhebini benimsememelerinin sebebini şöyle söylemişlerdir: Çünkü mahzûf tamamen unutulmuş bir şey haline gelmiştir. Buradaki masdarın fâili ise telaffuz edilmiş gibidir, unutulmuş değildir. Dolayısıyla onların bu takdîrî fâilden istisnâyı caiz görmelerinden, ortaya çıkan fark sebebiyle Ferrâ'nın mezhebine tâbi oldukları sonucu çıkmaz. (Bir görüşe göre de) müferrağ müstesnâdır; bu durumda Şeyh'in sözünde açıklandığı gibi «مَنْ» fâil olarak ref' mahallinde olur. Tefrîğ (boşaltma) ancak nefy veya benzerinde olur; ancak cehr, nefyin kapsamında yer alan sevginin müteallakı olunca bu caiz olmuştur. (Bir görüşe göre de) bir muzâfın hazfi üzere «الجَهْر»den müstesnâdır; takdiri: «إلا جَهْرَ مَنْ ظُلِم» (zulme uğrayanın açıkça söylemesi hariç). Böylece muttasıl olması takdirine göre bunlar üç vecihtir; bunlardan «مَنْ»ın mahalli hakkında dört vecih hâsıl olur: İki vecihten ref' — ki bunlar takdîrî «أحد»den bedel olması ya da müferrağ olması üzere fâil olmasıdır —; nasb da takdîrî «أحد»den ya da bir muzâfın hazfi üzere «الجهر»den istisnânın aslı üzeredir.

İkinci (görüş): Munkatı' istisnâ olmasıdır; takdiri: «Fakat zulme uğrayan kimse, uğradığı zulme denk olan şeyle zalimden hakkını alabilir.» Bu durumda «مَنْ» yalnızca munkatı' istisnâ üzere nasb mahallinde olur.

Cumhur «إلاَّ مَنْ ظُلِمَ»i meçhul olarak okumuştur. Aralarında İbn Abbâs, İbn Ömer, İbn Cübeyr ve Hasan'ın da bulunduğu kalabalık bir grup ise ma'lûm olarak «ظَلَم» okumuştur; bu munkatı' istisnâdır; dolayısıyla munkatı' istisnânın aslı üzere nasb mahallindedir. Âlimlerin bu istisnânın takdiri hakkındaki ifadeleri farklı olmuştur; bunun özeti üç takdirden birine döner: Ya birinci cümleye dönüktür; sanki şöyle denmiştir: «Allah kötülüğün açıkça söylenmesini sevmez; fakat zalim onu sever ve yapar.» Ya cehrin fâiline dönüktür, yani: «Allah birinin kötülüğü açıkça söylemesini sevmez; fakat zalim onu açıkça söyler.» Ya da cehrin müteallakına, yani «kendisine kötülük açıkça söylenen ve yüzüne karşı kötülükle karşılanan kimse»ye dönüktür, yani: «Allah biri hakkında kötülüğün açıkça söylenmesini sevmez; fakat zalime karşı kötülük açıkça söylenir», yani belki vazgeçer diye onda bulunan kötülükler yüzüne karşı zikredilir. Bu kıraatte bu müstesnânın munkatı' olarak mahallen mansûb olması sahih olandır. İbn Atıyye ve Zemahşerî onun bedel olarak ref' mahallinde olmasını caiz görmüşlerdir; ancak ikisinin dayanağı farklıdır. İbn Atıyye şöyle demiştir: «'مَنْ'ın i'rabı bu te'villerin bazısında nasbı ihtimal dahilinde tutar; takdîrî 'أحد'den bedel olarak ref'i de ihtimal dahilinde tutar»; yani, tahkiki geçtiği üzere masdarda takdir edilen «أحد»den. Zemahşerî de şöyle demiştir: «'مَنْ'ın merfû olması da caizdir; sanki 'Allah kötülüğün açıkça söylenmesini sevmez, ancak zalim (sever)' denmiştir; 'ما جاءني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ' (bana Zeyd gelmedi, ancak Amr) — 'Bana ancak Amr geldi' manasında — diyenlerin lügatine göre. {لاَّ يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي السماوات والأرض الغيب إِلاَّ الله} [Neml: 65] da bundandır.» Şeyh ikisine reddiye yaparak şöyle demiştir: «Onun — yani İbn Atıyye'nin — zikrettiği bedel olarak ref'in caiz olması sahih değildir. Şöyle ki munkatı' (istisnâ) iki kısımdır: Bir kısmına âmil yönelebilir; 'ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمار' (orada kimse yok, ancak bir eşek var) gibi; bunda iki lügat vardır: Hicaz lügatinde nasb vâciptir, Temîm lügatinde ise bedel caizdir. Eğer âmil ona yönelmezse herkese göre nasbı vâciptir; 'المالُ ما زاد إلا النقصَ' (mal artmadı, ancak eksildi), yani 'fakat ona eksiklik geldi' gibi; bunda bedel caiz değildir, çünkü âmili ona yöneltsen sahih olmaz.» (Şeyh) şöyle demiştir: «Ayet bu kısımdandır; çünkü 'لا يحبُّ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بالسوءِ إلا الظالمُ' deyip 'يجهر'i 'الظالم'e yöneltsen sahih olmaz.» Ve şöyle demiştir: «Onun — yani Zemahşerî'nin — caiz gördüğü bu şey caiz değildir; çünkü fâilin hükümsüz (lağv) olması mümkün değildir; 'الظالم'in 'الله'tan bedel olması da, 'عمرو'nun 'زيد'den bedel olması da mümkün değildir. Çünkü bu babdaki bedel, hakikaten bedel-i ba'z min küll'e döner — 'ما قام القومُ إلا زيدٌ' (kavim kalkmadı, ancak Zeyd) gibi — ya da mecazen döner — 'ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمارٌ' gibi. Ayette ise ne hakikaten ne de mecazen bedel caizdir; zikredilen misal de öyledir; çünkü 'الله' Teâlâ bir alemdir (özel isimdir), 'زيد' de öyledir; dolayısıyla ikisinde, içlerine bir şeyin girdiği vehmedilip de istisnâ edilecek bir umum yoktur. Munkatı' istisnâdan bedelin caiz olduğu yerlere gelince, bunun sebebi kendinden öncekinin (müstesnânın) içine girdiği vehmedilen umumi bir şey olmasıdır; böylece mecazen kendinden öncekinden bedel yapılır. Onun 'ما جاءني زيد إلا عمروٌ' diyenlerin lügatine göre sözüne gelince, bunun bir lügat olduğunu ancak Sîbeveyh'in Kitâb'ında biliyoruz; (orada Sîbeveyh) munkatı' istisnâ hakkında sonuncusu şu olan beyitleri okuduktan sonra:

167 - 2- عَشِيَّةَ ما تُغْني الرماحُ مكانَها ... ولا النبلُ إلا المشرفيُّ المُصَمَّمُ
(O akşam ki, ne mızraklar yerini tutar ne oklar; ancak kemiğe işleyen Meşrefî kılıç [işe yarar].)

aynen şöyle demiştir: 'Bu, «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلاَّ عمروٌ» (bana Zeyd gelmedi ancak Amr) ve «ما أعانَه إخوانُكم إلا إخوانُه» (ona sizin kardeşleriniz yardım etmedi, ancak kendi kardeşleri) (sözlerini) güçlendirir; çünkü bunlar marifelerdir; sonraki isimler onların aynısı da değildir, bir kısmı da değildir.' 'ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو'nun Arapların sözünden olduğunu ne açıkça söylemiş ne de ima etmiştir. Sîbeveyh'in sözünü şerh eden şöyle demiştir: 'Bu, «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو»yu güçlendirir', yani bunun Arapların sözünden sabit olması gerekir; çünkü 'النبل' (oklar), Meşrefî (kılıç) olmayan bir marifedir; tıpkı Zeyd'in Amr olmaması ve Zeyd'in kardeşlerinin senin kardeşlerin olmaması gibi.» Şeyh şöyle demiştir: «'ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو' beytin benzeri değildir; çünkü beyitte bir umum tasavvur edilebilir; zira mana: 'Silah işe yaramaz'dır. 'زيد'de ise umum vehmedilmez. Bununla birlikte, onların sözünden 'ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو' varid olsaydı, 'ما أتاني زيد ولا غيره إلا عمروٌ' (bana ne Zeyd ne de başkası geldi, ancak Amr) üzere sahih olması mümkün olurdu; istisnâ ona delâlet ettiği için ma'tûf hazfedilmiş olurdu. Fâilin hükümsüz kılınması ya da 'عمرو'nun 'زيد'den bedel olması üzere olmasına gelince, bu caiz değildir. Ayete gelince, o da zikrettiği şeyden değildir; çünkü 'مَنْ'ın mef'ûlün bih, 'الغَيبَ'in de ondan bedel-i iştimâl olması muhtemeldir; takdir: 'Göklerde ve yerde olanların gaybini ancak Allah bilir', yani onların gizlisini ve açığını ancak Allah bilir. 'مَنْ'ın mahallen merfû olduğu kabul edilse bile, onda bir umum tasavvur edilir ve mecazen 'الله' ondan bedel yapılır; sanki 'Var olanlar gaybı bilmez, ancak Allah bilir' denmiştir. Ya da Allah Teâlâ'ya nispetle zarfiyette mecaz yoluyla olur; zira bu, Kur'an ve Sünnette ondan (bu şekilde) gelmiştir: {وَهُوَ الله فِي السماوات وَفِي الأرض} [En'âm: 3], {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله وَفِي الأرض إله} [Zuhruf: 84]; 'Allah nerede?' demiş, 'Gökte' demiştir. Arapların sözünden de: 'لاوذو في السماءِ بيتُه' (Hayır, evi gökte olana yemin olsun) — Allah'ı kastederler. Ayet bu vecihleri ihtimal dahilinde tuttuğuna göre, onun zikrettiğine hamledilmesi zorunlu olmaz.» Onun ikisine yaptığı reddiye (burada) bitti.

İbn Atıyye'ye reddiyesi açıktır. Zemahşerî'ye reddiyesinin ise bir kısmında itiraz payı vardır. «Bunun bir lügat olduğunu ancak Sîbeveyh'in Kitâb'ında biliyoruz» sözüne gelince, benzerinin kullanımının sıhhatine delil olarak bu yeter. Bu yüzden Sîbeveyh'in Kitâb'ının şârihleri, okuduğu beyitler sebebiyle bu sözü Arapların sözünün kıyası olduğu şeklinde şerh etmişlerdir. «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ»yu «ما أتاني زيد ولا غيرُه» ile te'vil etmesine gelince, onun dediği zorunlu değildir. Buradaki istisnânın sıhhati şudur: Söyleyenin «ما أتاني زيد» sözü, Amr'ın da kendisine gelmediği vehmini doğurabilir; o da bu vehmi nefyetmiştir; bu kadarı munkatı' istisnâda yeterlidir. Eğer «ما أتاني زيد إلا عمروٌ»nun te'vili onun dediği gibi olsaydı, munkatı' istisnâ olmaz, muttasıl olurdu; hâlbuki nahivciler bunun munkatı' istisnâdan olduğunda ittifak etmişlerdir. Ayeti zikrettiği şeyle te'vil etmesine gelince, bunda mecaz yapmak tehlikeli bir iştir; böylesine girişilmemesi gerekir.

The words of Allah the Exalted: {لاَّ يُحِبُّ الله الجهر بالسواء}: [Translator's note: the source prints «بالسواء» here; the verse and the following discussion have «بالسوء».] «بالسوء» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الجهر», which is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made definite by «أل»; al-Fārisī used it as evidence that a maṣdar made definite by «أل» may govern. It was said: there is no proof in it, because an adverbial and a preposition [with its noun] are governed even by the faint scent of verbs. The fāʿil (agent) of this maṣdar is omitted, i.e. "someone's speaking openly"; it has preceded that the omission of the fāʿil is regular in certain forms, among them the maṣdar. «الجهر» may also be taken from a passive verb — with disagreement over that — so the preposition with its noun after it would be in the position of the nominative, standing in place of the fāʿil, because if you said "Allah does not love that evil be spoken openly", «بالسوء» would stand in place of the fāʿil and would not then be attached to it. And «من القول» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السوء».
His words: {إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ} — there are two opinions about this exception. The first: that it is connected (muttaṣil). The second: that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). If it is said to be connected, it was said: it is excepted from the implied «أحد» which is the fāʿil of the maṣdar, so «مَن» may be in the position of the accusative on the basic rule of exception, or of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «أحد» — and this is the preferred view. If it were made explicit, it would be said: "Allah does not love that anyone speak evil openly except the wronged", with «المظلوم» nominative or accusative. Makkī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others mentioned this. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is the position of al-Farrāʾ, who permitted in «ما قام إلا زيدٌ» that «زيد» be a badal from «أحد». On the position of the majority, it is of the excepted for which the governing element is left free (mufarragh), so it is nominative as the fāʿil of the maṣdar; this is made good by «الجهر» being within the scope of negation, as though it were said: no one speaks evil words openly except the wronged." End of quotation. The difference between the position of al-Farrāʾ and this verse is clear, for the grammarians did not accept the position of al-Farrāʾ, they said, because the omitted element has become utterly forgotten; whereas the fāʿil of the maṣdar here is like something pronounced, not forgotten. So their permitting exception from this implied fāʿil does not entail their following the position of al-Farrāʾ, given the evident difference. It was also said: it is an unfilled (mufarragh) exception, so «مَنْ» is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil, as set out in the Shaykh's words; the unfilled exception occurs only in a negation or what resembles it, but since «الجهر» is the object of the love that falls within the scope of negation, that became acceptable. It was also said: it is excepted from «الجهر» with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "except the speaking openly of one who was wronged". These are three views on the assumption that it is connected, from which four views on the position of «مَنْ» are obtained: the nominative from two views, namely as a badal from the implied «أحد», or as fāʿil on its being unfilled; and the accusative on the basic rule of exception from the implied «أحد», or from «الجهر» with the omission of a muḍāf.
The second: that it is a disconnected exception, its implied form being: "but one who has been wronged may obtain redress from his wrongdoer with what equals his grievance"; so «مَنْ» is in the position of the accusative only, as a disconnected exception.
The majority read «إلاَّ مَنْ ظُلِمَ» in the passive; a large group, among them Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan, read «ظَلَم» in the active, and it is a disconnected exception, so it is in the position of the accusative on the basic rule of the disconnected exception. The scholars' expressions differed in positing this exception, and the upshot comes back to one of three implied forms: either it refers back to the first clause, as though it were said: "Allah does not love speaking evil openly, but the wrongdoer loves it, so he does it"; or it refers back to the fāʿil of «الجهر», i.e. "Allah does not love that anyone speak evil openly, but the wrongdoer speaks it openly"; or it refers back to the object of «الجهر», namely "the one to whom evil is spoken openly and to whose face it is said", i.e. "Allah does not love that evil be spoken openly to anyone, but evil is spoken openly to the wrongdoer", i.e. his evil traits are mentioned to his face, that perhaps he may desist. That this excepted element in this reading is in the position of the accusative as disconnected is the correct view. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be in the position of the nominative as a badal, but their reasoning differed. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The i'rab of «مَنْ» in some of these interpretations may be the accusative, and it may be the nominative as a badal from the implied «أحد»" — meaning the «أحد» implied in the maṣdar, as its examination preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مَنْ» may be nominative, as though it were said: Allah does not love speaking evil openly except the wrongdoer, according to the dialect of those who say «ما جاءني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ» ('Zayd did not come to me, except ʿAmr'), meaning: none came to me but ʿAmr; and from it is {لاَّ يَعْلَمُ مَن فِي السماوات والأرض الغيب إِلاَّ الله} [al-Naml: 65]." The Shaykh rebutted them both, saying: "What he — meaning Ibn ʿAṭiyya — mentioned of the permissibility of the nominative as a badal is not correct, because the disconnected [exception] is of two kinds. One kind is that to which the governing element can be directed, as in «ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمار» ('there is no one in it except a donkey'); in this there are two dialects: the dialect of the Ḥijāz requires the accusative, and the dialect of Tamīm permits the badal. If the governing element cannot be directed to it, its accusative is obligatory for all, as in «المالُ ما زاد إلا النقصَ» ('the wealth did not increase, except decrease'), i.e. but decrease befell it; the badal is not permissible in it, because if you directed the governing element to it, it would not be valid." He said: "The verse is of this kind, because if you said «لا يحبُّ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بالسوءِ إلا الظالمُ», making «يجهر» govern «الظالم», it would not be valid." And he said: "What he — meaning al-Zamakhsharī — permitted is not permissible, because the fāʿil cannot be void (laghw), and «الظالم» cannot be a badal from «الله», nor «عمرو» a badal from «زيد», because the badal in this chapter comes back to a badal of part from whole, either in reality, as in «ما قام القومُ إلا زيدٌ», or figuratively, as in «ما فيها أحدٌ إلا حمارٌ»; and in the verse the badal is permissible neither in reality nor figuratively, and likewise the example mentioned, because "Allah the Exalted" is a proper name, and likewise "Zayd", so there is no generality in them such that something could be imagined to be included in them and then be excepted. As for the disconnected exception in which the badal is permissible, that is because what precedes it is general, and [the excepted] is imagined to be included in it, so it is substituted for what precedes figuratively. As for his saying 'according to the dialect of those who say «ما جاءني زيد إلا عمروٌ»', we do not know this as a dialect except in the Book of Sībawayh, after he recited verses on the disconnected exception, the last of which is:
1672 - عَشِيَّةَ ما تُغْني الرماحُ مكانَها ... ولا النبلُ إلا المشرفيُّ المُصَمَّمُ
(On the evening when neither the spears availed in their place, nor the arrows — only the Mashrafī sword that cuts through the bone.)
Its text is: 'This strengthens «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلاَّ عمروٌ» and «ما أعانَه إخوانُكم إلا إخوانُه», because they are definites, the latter nouns being neither them nor part of them.' He neither stated nor hinted that «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» is from the speech of the Arabs. One who commented on Sībawayh's words said: 'So this strengthens «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو»', i.e. this ought to be established as the speech of the Arabs, because «النبل» is a definite that is not the Mashrafī, just as Zayd is not ʿAmr, and just as Zayd's brothers are not your brothers." The Shaykh said: "«ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» is not analogous to the verse, because a generality may be imagined in the verse, since the meaning is: weapons did not avail; whereas no generality is imagined in «زيد». Moreover, if «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمرو» did occur in their speech, it could be valid as «ما أتاني زيد ولا غيره إلا عمروٌ» ('neither Zayd nor anyone else came to me except ʿAmr'), the conjoined element having been omitted because the exception indicates it. As for its being on the voiding of the fāʿil, or on «عمرو» being a badal from «زيد», that is not permissible. As for the verse, it is not of what he mentioned, because «مَنْ» may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «الغَيبَ» a badal from it, a badal of inclusion, the implied form being: 'none knows the unseen of those in the heavens and the earth except Allah', i.e. their secret and their open affairs none knows except Allah. And if it is granted that «مَنْ» is in a nominative position, a generality may be imagined in it, so «الله» is substituted for it figuratively, as though it were said: 'none of the existing beings knows the unseen except Allah'; or it is by way of figurative locative sense in relation to Allah the Exalted, since that has come concerning Him in the Quran and the Sunna, as in {وَهُوَ الله فِي السماوات وَفِي الأرض} [al-Anʿām: 3] and {وَهُوَ الذي فِي السمآء إله وَفِي الأرض إله} [al-Zukhruf: 84]; [and] he said: 'Where is Allah?' She said: 'In the heaven.' And from the speech of the Arabs: «لا وذو في السماءِ بيتُه» ('No, by the One whose house is in the heaven'), meaning Allah. Since the verse admits these views, interpreting it as he mentioned is not determined." End of his rebuttal of them both.
His rebuttal of Ibn ʿAṭiyya is clear; as for his rebuttal of al-Zamakhsharī, some of it is open to objection. As for his saying "we do not know it as a dialect except in the Book of Sībawayh", that suffices as proof of the validity of using its like; that is why the commentators on the Book of Sībawayh explained these words as being the analogy of the speech of the Arabs, because of the verses he recited. As for his interpreting «ما أتاني زيدٌ إلا عمروٌ» as «ما أتاني زيد ولا غيرُه», what he said is not the only possibility; the validity of the exception in it is that the speaker's saying «ما أتاني زيد» might suggest that ʿAmr also did not come to him, so he negated this suggestion, and this much suffices in a disconnected exception. If the interpretation of «ما أتاني زيد إلا عمروٌ» were as he said, it would not be a disconnected exception but a connected one, whereas the grammarians agreed that it is disconnected. As for interpreting the verse with what he mentioned, figurative usage in that is a perilous matter, and one should not venture upon its like.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ} kavlinde iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ} kavlindeki «ما»ya ma'tûf olmasıdır; bu durumda birincinin müteallik olduğu şeye müteallik olur. İkincisi: «طبع»den sonra gelen «بكفرهم»e atıf olmasıdır. Zemahşerî bunu son derece açık bir şekilde açıklamış, itiraz getirmiş ve en güzel cevapla cevap vermiştir. Şöyle demiştir: «Eğer: '«وبكفرهم» kavlini neye atfetti?' dersen, derim ki: Doğru vecih, onun 'فبما نقضِهم'e atfedilmesi ve {بَلْ طَبَعَ الله عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ} kavlinin, istitrad (söz arasında başka bir konuya değinme) yoluyla {وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ} kavline tâbi olan bir söz kılınmasıdır. Onu kendisine bitişik olan 'بكفرِهم' kavline atfetmek de caizdir. Eğer: 'İster idrâbdan öncekine — ki o {وَكُفْرِهِم بَآيَاتِ الله} kavlidir — ister ondan sonrakine — ki o 'بكفرهم' kavlidir — atfedilsin, küfrü, kendisinde onun zikri bulunan şeye ma'tûf olarak getirmenin manası nedir?' dersen, derim ki: Onlardan küfür tekrar tekrar sadır olmuştur; çünkü önce Mûsâ'yı, sonra Îsâ'yı, sonra Muhammed'i inkâr ettiler; böylece küfürlerinin bir kısmını diğerine atfetmiştir. Ya da ma'tûfların toplamını ma'tûfun aleyhin toplamına atfetmiştir; sanki şöyle denmiştir: Misakı bozmayı, Allah'ın ayetlerini inkâr etmeyi, peygamberleri öldürmeyi ve 'Kalplerimiz perdelidir' sözlerini bir araya getirmeleri ve küfürleriyle Meryem'e iftira etmelerini ve Îsâ'yı öldürmekle övünmelerini bir araya getirmeleri sebebiyle onları cezalandırdık; ya da: Bilakis Allah, küfürleri ve küfürleriyle şunu ve şunu bir araya getirmeleri sebebiyle onları mühürledi.» [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «المطعوف» yazılıdır; «المعطوف» olarak çevrilmiştir.]

{بُهْتَاناً} kavlinin nasbında beş vecih vardır. En zâhiri: Mef'ûlün bih olmasıdır; çünkü «كلام» (söz) manasını tazammun etmiştir; «قلت خطبة وشعراً» (bir hutbe ve şiir söyledim) gibi. İkincisi: Masdarın türü üzere mansûb olmasıdır; «قَعَد القرفصاء» (çömelme oturuşuyla oturdu) demeleri gibi; yani söz bazen iftira olur, bazen iftira olmaz. Üçüncüsü: Mahzûf bir masdarın sıfatı olarak mansûb olmasıdır, yani: «قولاً بُهتاناً» (iftira olan bir söz); bu, birincinin manasına yakındır. Dördüncüsü: Kendi lafzından takdir edilen bir fiille mansûb olmasıdır, yani: «بَهَتوا بُهْتاناً» (bir iftira ile iftira ettiler). Beşincisi: «قولهم»deki mecrûr zamirden hâl olmasıdır, yani: «iftira ederek»; muzâfun ileyhten hâl gelmesi caiz olmuştur, çünkü o mana bakımından fâildir; takdir: «Bunu iftira ederek söylemeleri sebebiyle».

The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ} — there are two views on it. The first: that it is conjoined to «ما» in His words {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ}, so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what the first is attached to. The second: that it is conjoined to «بكفرهم», which comes after «طبع». Al-Zamakhsharī clarified this with the utmost clarity, raised an objection and answered it in the best way; he said: "If you ask: to what is His saying «وبكفرهم» conjoined? I say: the proper view is that it is conjoined to «فبما نقضِهم», and His saying {بَلْ طَبَعَ الله عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ} is made speech following His saying {وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ} by way of digression (istiṭrād). It may also be conjoined to what immediately precedes it, namely His saying «بكفرِهم». If you ask: what then is the meaning of bringing disbelief conjoined to something in which it has already been mentioned — whether it is conjoined to what precedes the iḍrāb or to what follows it — namely His saying {وَكُفْرِهِم بَآيَاتِ الله} and His saying «بكفرهم»? I say: disbelief recurred from them, because they disbelieved in Moses, then in Jesus, then in Muḥammad, so He conjoined some of their disbelief to some; or He conjoined the whole of the conjoined elements to the whole of what they are conjoined to [Translator's note: the source prints «المطعوف», evidently a slip for «المعطوف» ("the conjoined")], as though it were said: so for their combining the breaking of the covenant, disbelief in the signs of Allah, killing the prophets and their saying 'our hearts are covered', and for their combining their disbelief with their slander of Mary and their boasting of killing Jesus, We punished them; or: rather Allah sealed them for their disbelief and their combining their disbelief with such and such."
His words: {بُهْتَاناً} — there are five views on its accusative. The most apparent of them: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), for it [the verb of saying] is made to include the meaning of «كلام» ('speech'), as in «قلت خطبة وشعراً» ('I said a sermon and poetry'). The second: that it is accusative as the type of the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in their saying «قَعَد القرفصاء» ('he sat in the squatting posture'), meaning that the saying may be a slander or not a slander. The third: that it is accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a slanderous saying", and this is close in meaning to the first. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb from its own root, i.e. "they slandered a slander". The fifth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «قولهم», i.e. "slandering"; a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is permissible because it is the fāʿil (agent) in meaning; the implied form is: "and for their saying that, slandering".

And the words of Allah the Exalted: {وَقَوْلِهِمْ} are conjoined to «وكفرهم». «عيسى» is a badal (substitute) from «المسيح», or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and likewise «ابن مريم», which may also be an adjective. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted these three views in «رسول الله», except that the badal with derived words is rare; it may be said that «رسول الله» has been treated like non-derived nouns. He also permitted it to be accusative by an implied «أعني» ('I mean'), and there is no need for that. His words «شُبِّه لهم»: «شُبِّه» is passive, and there are two views on it. The first: that it is predicated of the preposition [with its noun] after it, as in your saying «حِيل إليه» and «لُبس عليه». The second: that it is predicated of the pronoun of the one killed, indicated by their saying «إنَّا قتلْنا», i.e. "but the one they killed was made to resemble [him] to them". If it is asked: why may it not refer to the Messiah? The answer is that the Messiah is the one resembled, not the one made to resemble.
[His words]: «لفي شك منه»: «منه» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «شك», attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted element; it is not permissible for it to be attached to «شك» itself, because «الشك» takes its complement only with «في», not with «من»; and it should not be said that «مِنْ» has the meaning of «في», for that is a weaker opinion, and we have no need of it here.
And His words: {مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ} — two views are possible regarding «علم». The first: that it is nominative as fāʿil (agent), the governing element being one of the two prepositional phrases, either «لهم» or «به»; when one of them is made what puts it in the nominative, the other is attached to what the nominative-governing one is attached to, namely the implied "being settled". «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), since both conditions for redundancy are met. The second view: that «من علم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «من» also redundant in it, and there are two possibilities for the khabar (predicate). The first: that it is «لهم»; then «به» is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the khabar, governed by the implied "being settled", or a ḥāl from «عِلْم», even though it is indefinite, because it precedes it and because it relies on a negation. If it is said: this entails placing the ḥāl of a noun made genitive by a preposition before it, which is a poetic necessity not permissible in ordinary speech — the answer is that we do not grant that; rather, Abū al-Baqāʾ and others transmitted that the position of most of the Basrans is that it is permissible; and even if we granted that it is permissible only in necessity, the genitive here is made genitive by a redundant preposition, and the redundant [preposition] is treated as discarded. Or it is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification, i.e. "I mean by it"; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this, and there is no need for it. It may not be attached to «علم» itself, because what a maṣdar (verbal noun) governs does not precede it. The second possibility: that «به» is the khabar, and «لهم» is attached to the "being settled" as preceded; the lām may also be clarifying and specifying, like the one in His words: {وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَّهُ كُفُواً أَحَدٌ} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 4]. This negative clause admits three views. [The first:] the genitive, as a second adjective of «شك», i.e. "not known". The second: the accusative as a ḥāl from «شك»; this is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it is specified by the description in His words «منه». The third: resumption; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is far-fetched.
His words: {إِلاَّ اتباع الظن} — there are two opinions about this exception. The first — and it is the correct one, the majority mentioning no other — is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because following conjecture is not of the genus of knowledge. To my knowledge it was read only with «اتِّباع» in the accusative, on the basic rule of the disconnected exception, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz; in [the dialect of] Tamīm it may be a badal from «علم» according to its wording, and so genitive, or according to its position, and so nominative, because it is in a nominative position, as I set out for you before, «من» being redundant in it. [Translator's note: the source prints «المضع», evidently a slip for «الموضع» ("the position").] The second — Ibn ʿAṭiyya said — is that it is connected (muttaṣil); he said: "since knowledge and conjecture are joined by the genus of being among the beliefs of certainty; the one who conjectures says by way of figurative usage 'my knowledge in this matter is such-and-such', meaning only his conjecture." End of quotation. This is not agreed upon, because conjecture is that in which one of the two sides is preponderant, and certainty is that in which one of them is decisively affirmed; and even granting it, following conjecture is not of the genus of knowledge but other than it, so it too is disconnected, i.e. "but following conjecture is what they have".
His words: {وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً} — there are several opinions on the pronoun in «قتلوه». The most apparent of them is that it refers to Jesus, and the majority of exegetes hold this. The second — held by Ibn Qutayba and al-Farrāʾ — is that it refers to knowledge, i.e. "they did not kill the knowledge with certainty", in the manner of their saying «قتلت العلم والرأي يقيناً» ('I killed the knowledge and the opinion with certainty') and «قتلته علماً» ('I killed it in knowledge', i.e. mastered it). The aspect of figurative usage in it is that killing a thing comes about through subduing and mastering it, as though it were said: their knowledge was not a knowledge comprehended; it was only from conjecture and guesswork. The third — held by Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī and a large group — is that it refers to the conjecture; you say «قتلت هذا الأمر علماً ويقيناً», i.e. I verified it; so it is as though it were said: their conjecture was not validated for them, they did not verify it with certainty, and they did not settle the conjecture with certainty.
His words: {يقيناً} — there are five views on it. The first: that it is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a certain killing". The second: that it is a maṣdar from the meaning of the governing element before it, as its figurative sense preceded, because it is in its meaning, i.e. "they did not become certain of it with certainty". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «قتلوه», i.e. "they did not kill him being certain of his killing". [Translator's note: the source prints «أيك», evidently a slip for «أي» ("i.e.").] The fourth: that it is accusative by a verb from its own root, omitted because it is indicated, i.e. "they were not certain of it with certainty", and it emphasises the content of the negative clause before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ posited the governing element on this view as affirmative, saying: "its implied form is: they were certain of that, with certainty", and there is an objection to this. The fifth — transmitted from Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī — is that it is accusative governed by what comes after «بل», in His words {رَّفَعَهُ الله}, and that there is a transposition in the speech, i.e. "rather Allah raised him to Himself with certainty". Al-Khalīl and those after him explicitly stated that this is prohibited, i.e. that what comes after «بل» does not govern what is before it; so it should not be held authentic from him. And His words {بَل رَّفَعَهُ الله إِلَيْهِ} are a refutation of what they claimed about killing and crucifying him. The pronoun in «إليه» refers to «الله», with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "to His heaven and the place of His command and prohibition".

His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: «إنْ» here is negating, in the sense of «ما», and «من أهل» admits two analyses. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the omitted oath clause together with its response; the implied form is: "And there is no one of the People of the Book but — by Allah — he will surely believe in him." So it is like His saying: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ [مَّعْلُومٌ]} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164], i.e. "there is no one of us", and like His saying: {وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا} [Maryam: 71], i.e. "there is no one of you but he will come to it". This is the apparent analysis. The second — held by al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ — is that it is in the position of the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The clause «ليؤمِنَنَّ به» is an oath clause standing as the adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being: 'And there is not, of the People of the Book, anyone but he will surely believe in him'; and similar to it are: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164] and {وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا} [Maryam: 71]; and the meaning is: there is not, of the Jews, anyone but he will surely believe."

Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is a gross error, since he claimed that «ليؤمنن به» is an oath clause [قسيمة] standing as the adjective of an omitted qualified noun, and so on; whereas the adjective of the omitted «أحد» is only the preposition and its genitive noun, as we have construed it. As for his saying «ليؤمنن به», it is neither an adjective of a qualified noun nor an oath clause [قسيمة]; it is only the clause of the response to the oath, the oath being omitted, and the oath together with its response is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, since no predication (isnād) can be formed from «أحد» and the genitive phrase, because that would convey no information; the predication is formed only by the oath clause and its response, and that is where the information lies. Likewise the khabar is «إلاَّ له مقام», and likewise «إلا واردها», since no predicative construction can be formed from what precedes «إلا»." «[Translator's note: the text reads «قسيمة» in both places in this quotation, apparently for «قسمية» "oath clause"; translated as written in sense.]»

This man — as you see — has spoken ill of al-Zamakhsharī in claiming that it is an error, whereas it is sound and correct. Would that I knew how a predication cannot be formed from «أحد», qualified by the clause after it, and the preposition-phrase before it! Its parallel is your saying: «ما في الدار رجلٌ إلا صالحٌ» ("There is not in the house a man but a righteous one"): just as «في الدار» is a fronted khabar, «رجل» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and «إلا صالحٌ» its adjective — and it is meaningful, sound speech — so it is here; the most that can be said is that «إلا» has entered upon the adjective to convey restriction (ḥaṣr). As for his objection to him for saying "an oath clause" when it is only the response to the oath, he need not be excused for that, and such objections suffice him. [Translator's note: the source reads «ويكفيه مثلُ هذه الاعتراضات»; the sense is obscure, so it is rendered literally.]

The lām in «ليؤمِنَنَّ» is the response to an omitted oath, as has preceded. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ليؤمِنَنَّ» is the response to an omitted oath; and it is said: he emphasized with it outside the oath, as it occurs in negation and interrogation." His saying "and it is said …" is only sound if we refer the disagreement to the nūn of emphasis, because emphasis with the nūn of emphasis is known to occur regularly in interrogation, and in negation with disagreement over it; but emphasis with the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) in negation and interrogation is not known at all.

He also said before that: "[The implied form is] 'and there is not, of the People of the Book, anyone (أحد)'; and it is said that the omitted word is «مَنْ», and its parallel has passed, except that construing «مَنْ» here is far-fetched, because the exception comes after the noun is complete, and «مَنْ», whether relative or indefinite-qualified, is not complete." He means that some made the omitted word the word «مَنْ», construing: "وإنْ مِنْ أهل مَنْ إلا ليؤمِنَنَّ", putting the word «مَنْ» in place of «أحد». His saying "and its parallel has passed" refers to His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب لَمَن يُؤْمِنُ بالله} [Āl ʿImrān: 199]; the point of the parallel is that there the «مَنْ» that is implied here is stated explicitly.

Ubayy read: {ليؤمِنُنَ به قبل موتهم} with ḍamma on the first nūn, out of regard for the meaning of the omitted «أحد», for although its wording is singular its meaning is plural. The pronoun in «به» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is said: to Allah the Exalted; and it is said: to Muḥammad, upon him be peace. The pronoun in «موته» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is related in the exegesis that when he descends to earth everyone will believe in him, until the whole religion becomes Islamic. And it is said: it refers back to the implied «أحد», i.e. no scripturist dies until he believes in ʿĪsā; this is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, whereupon ʿIkrima said to him: "What do you think if he falls from a house, or is burned, or a wild beast eats him?" He said: "He does not die until he moves his lips with it", i.e. with belief in ʿĪsā. Al-Fayyāḍ ibn Ghazwān read: «وإنَّ من أهل الكتاب» with «إنَّ» doubled; and it is a rejected reading because of its difficulty.

His saying: {وَيَوْمَ القيامة}: what governs it is «شيهداً» «[Translator's note: so in the text, for «شهيداً».]». In it is evidence for the permissibility of fronting the khabar of «كان» before it, because fronting the governed word signals [the permissibility of] fronting the governing word. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that it be in the accusative by «يكون»; this is according to the view of those who allow «كان» to govern the adverb and what resembles it. The pronoun in «يكون» refers to ʿĪsā; and it is said: to Muḥammad, upon him be peace.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَبِظُلْمٍ} kavli: Bu câr ve mecrûr «حَرَّمنا»ya müteallik (bağlı) olup ba sebebiyyedir. Ancak tahrimin sebebinin çirkinliğine dikkat çekmek için âmilinin önüne alınmıştır. «فبظلمِ» kavlinin {فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مَّيثَاقَهُمْ} kavlinden bedel olduğu daha önce geçmiş, bunu söyleyene yapılan reddiye de geçmiştir; bu sebeple tekrarına gerek kalmamıştır. «من الذين», «ظلم»in sıfatıdır, yani: Yahudi olanlardan sâdır olan bir zulüm. Orada, zulmün, kendisiyle amel edilmek üzere hazfedilmiş bir sıfatı olduğu da söylenmiştir, yani: «hangi zulümle (ne büyük bir zulümle)» ya da «büyük bir zulümle»; şairin şu sözünde olduğu gibi:
167 - 3- فلا وأبى الطيرِ المُرِبَّةِ بالضحى ... على خالدٍ لقد وقَعْتِ على لَحْمِ
(Hayır! Kuşluk vakti Hâlid'in üzerinde dönüp duran kuşların babası hakkı için, sen mutlaka bir ete konmuşsun!)
yani: büyük bir et. [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «للعمل بها» yazılıdır; muhtemelen «للعلم بها» (bilindiği için) kastedilmiştir; yazıldığı gibi çevrilmiştir.]

{أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ} kavli: Bu cümle «طيبات»ın sıfatıdır, dolayısıyla mahalli nasbtır. Onu bu şekilde nitelemenin anlamı, yani: onların helal olma hâli üzere bulunduklarıdır; bunu İbn Abbâs'ın {كانت أُحِلَّتْ لهم} kıraati açıklar.

«كثيراً» kavli: Bunda üç vecih vardır. En zâhiri: Mef'ûlün bih olmasıdır, yani: «insanları ya da bir fırkayı ya da bir topluluğu çok engellemeleri sebebiyle». Nasbının masdar olması dolayısıyla olduğu da söylenmiştir, yani: «çok engelleme». Zaman zarfı olması dolayısıyla olduğu da söylenmiştir, yani: «uzun bir zaman». Birincisi evlâdır; çünkü bunun ardından gelen masdarlar mef'ûllerini nasbetmektedir, böylece bab tek bir yol üzerine yürümüş olur.

Ba, {وَبِصَدِّهِمْ} kavlinde tekrarlanmış, «وأَخْذِهم» kavlinde ve sonrasında tekrarlanmamıştır; çünkü ma'tûf ile ma'tûfun aleyh arasında, ma'tûfun aleyhin ma'mûlü olmayan bir şeyle, bilakis onun âmili olan «حَرَّمْنا» ve ona müteallik olan şeyle fasıla girmiştir. Ma'tûf, ma'tûfun aleyhten, ma'tûfun aleyhin ma'mûlü olmayan bir şeyle fasıla edilerek uzaklaşınca, bu sebeple ba tekrarlanmıştır.
