The pronoun in «بينهم» may refer to the Jews alone because they are diverse sects and branching factions, and it may refer to the Jews and the Christians because their mention has preceded in His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ اليهود والنصارى} [al-Māʾida: 51], and because the two classes are included in His saying: {قُلْ ياأهل الكتاب} [al-Māʾida: 59]. The alif and lām in «الأرض» may be for the genus and may be for a known referent.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {والصابئون} kavli: Cumhur onu vav ile okumuştur; şehirlerin mushaflarında da böyledir. Onun ref'inde dokuz vech vardır. Birincisi —Basra ehlinin çoğunluğunun, yani Halîl, Sîbeveyh ve onlara tâbi olanların görüşü—: İbtidâ ile merfûdur; haberi, birincinin haberinin ona delâlet etmesi sebebiyle mahzûftur ve onda te'hîr niyeti vardır. Takdir: «إنَّ الذين آمنوا والذين هادُوا مَنْ آمنَ بهم...» (sonuna kadar) «والصابئون كذلك». Bunun benzeri «إن زيداً وعمروٌ قائمٌ»dur; yani «إنَّ زيداً قائم وعمرو قائم». Bunu yaptığımızda hazf birinciden midir —yani ikincinin haberi zikredilmiş olur; takdir: «إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ وعمروٌ قائم» olup birinci «قائم» hazfedilmiştir— yoksa tersi midir? İki meşhur görüş vardır; her ikisi de [kelamda] varid olmuştur. [Şair] şöyle der:

176 - 9- نحنُ بما عِنْدنا وأنت بما ... عندك راضٍ والرأيُ مختلفُ
(Biz kendi yanımızdakine, sen de kendi yanındakine razısın; görüş ise farklıdır.)

yani «نحن رضوان» [Mütercim notu: Metinde «رضوان» yazılı; «راضون» olmalıdır]. Bunun tersi de şu sözüdür:

177 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإني وقَيَّار بها لَغَريبُ
(…şüphesiz ben ve Kayyâr orada gerçekten garibiz.)

Takdir: «وقيارٌ بها كذلك». Eğer "Hazfin [burada] de birinciden olması neden caiz değildir?" denirse, cevap şudur: Bundan, lâmın «إنَّ» ile nesh edilmemiş mübtedânın haberine girmesi lâzım gelir; bu ise azdır ve ancak şiir zaruretinde vaki olur. Âyette ise tahric üzere bu iki takdir de caizdir. Zemahşerî şöyle der: "«والصابئون» ibtidâ üzere merfûdur; haberi mahzûftur ve onda, «إنَّ»nin etki alanındaki ismi ve haberinden te'hîr niyeti vardır; sanki şöyle denmiştir: «إنَّ الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والنصارى حكمُهم كذلك والصابئون كذلك». Sîbeveyh buna şahit olarak şu beyti inşad etmiştir:

177 - 1- وإلاَّ فاعلَمُوا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... بُغاةٌ ما بَقِينا في شِقاقِ
(Yoksa bilin ki biz ve siz, ayrılık içinde kaldığımız sürece azgınlarız.)

yani: «فاعلموا أنَّا بُغاةٌ وأنتم كذلك»." Sonra bir sözden sonra şöyle der: "Eğer '«والصابئون» kavli ma'tûftur; onun için mutlaka bir ma'tûfun aleyh gerekir; o nedir?' dersen, derim ki [Mütercim notu: Metinde «قتل» yazılı; «قلت» olmalıdır]: O, mahzûf haberiyle birlikte, {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ} (sonuna kadar) kavlinin cümlesine ma'tûf bir cümledir; kendisine atfedildiği cümlenin mahalli olmadığı gibi onun da mahalli yoktur. Eğer 'Takdim ve te'hîr ancak bir fayda için olur; o nedir?' dersen, derim ki: Faydası, sâbiîlerin, kendilerinden iman ve salih amel sahih olursa tövbelerinin kabul edileceğine dikkat çekmektir; o hâlde başkaları hakkında ne düşünülür! Şöyle ki: Sâbiîler bu sayılanların sapıklık bakımından en açık olanı ve azgınlık bakımından en şiddetlisidir. Onlara ancak bütün dinlerden çıktıkları (صَبَؤوا) için sâbiî denmiştir; tıpkı şairin, muhatapların azgınlık vasfında kendi kavminden daha ileri olduklarına dikkat çekmek için «وأنتم» sözünü öne alması gibi; zira onu «بُغاةٌ» olan haberden önce çabucak getirmiştir; ta ki kavmi —onlar bunda daha ileri ve daha köklü oldukları hâlde— azgınlığa onlardan önce girmesin. Eğer '«والصابئين وإياكم» denseydi takdim hâsıl olurdu' dersen, derim ki: Böyle denseydi hiçbir şekilde takdim olmazdı; çünkü onda [kelimeyi] yerinden giderme yoktur. Mukaddem ve muahhar, yerinde duran için değil, yerinden giderilen için söylenir. Bu cümle i'tirâz (ara söz) mecrasında cereyan eder."

İkinci vech: «إنَّ», «نعم» (evet) manasındadır; dolayısıyla bir cevap harfidir ve o takdirde mahalli yoktur. Buna göre ondan sonraki ibtidâ ile mahallen merfû, ondan sonraki de ona ref' ile ma'tûftur; hepsinin haberi ise {مَنْ آمَنَ} (sonuna kadar) kavlidir. Onun «نعم» manasında olması mercûh bir görüştür; bazı nahivciler bunu söylemiş ve Allah Teâlâ'nın {إِنْ هذان لَسَاحِرَانِ} [Tâhâ: 63] kavlini, onu elif ile okuyanın kıraatinde, bundan saymıştır; o âyette uzun bir söz vardır, inşallah yerinde gelecektir. Abdullah b. ez-Zübeyr'in, kendisine "Beni sana taşıyan deveye Allah lanet etsin" diyen birine cevap olarak «إنَّ وصاحبُها» (evet, sahibine de) demesini de bundan saymıştır; yani "evet, sahibine de". Başka birinin şu sözünü de bundan saymıştır:

177 - 2- بَرَزَ الغواني في الشبا ... بِ يَلُمْنَني وألومُهُنَّهْ
ويَقُلْنَ شَيْبٌ قد عَلا ... كَ وقد كَبِرْتَ فقلتُ إنَّهْ
(Güzel kadınlar gençlikte ortaya çıktılar; beni kınıyorlar, ben de onları kınıyorum. "Seni ak saç kapladı, yaşlandın" diyorlar; ben de "Evet" dedim.)

yani "evet"; hâ ise sekt hâsıdır. Şöyle cevap verilmiştir: İbn ez-Zübeyr'in sözünde isim ve haber mahzûftur; isme ma'tûf olan ise ona delil olarak kalmıştır; takdir: «إنها وصاحبها معلونان» [Mütercim notu: «ملعونان» olmalıdır] (o deve ve sahibi lanetlenmiştir). Beytin takdiri ise: «إنه كذلك» (o öyledir). «نعم» manasında olduğu takdir edilse bile burada onu o manada kabul etmek sahih değildir; çünkü ondan önce, kendisine cevap olacağı bir şey geçmemiştir; «نعم» ise söz başında gelmez, ancak bir soruya cevap olarak gelir ve onu tasdik eder. Şöyle diyen de olabilir: Orada takdîrî bir soru olması caizdir; bunu birçok yerde zikretmişlerdir; bunlardan biri Allah Teâlâ'nın {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} [Kıyâme: 1] ve {لاَ جَرَمَ} [Hûd: 22] kavlidir; şöyle demişlerdir: Şöyle şöyle diyen birine reddiye olması muhtemeldir.

Üçüncü vech: «هادوا»daki müstetir zamire ma'tûf olmasıdır; yani «هادوا هم والصابئون» (onlar ve sâbiîler yahudi oldular). Bu, Kisâî'nin görüşüdür. Talebesi Ferrâ ve Zeccâc bunu reddetmiştir. Zeccâc şöyle der: "Bu iki yönden hatadır. Birincisi: Bu görüşte sâbiî yahudilikte yahudiye ortak olur; oysa öyle değildir; zira sâbiî yahudiden başkasıdır. Eğer «هادوا», yahudilikten değil de Allah Teâlâ'nın {إِنَّا هُدْنَآ إِلَيْكَ} [A'râf: 156] kavlinden 'tövbe ettiler' manasında kabul edilir ve mana 'onlar ve sâbiîler tövbe ettiler' olursa, tefsir bunun dışında bir şeyle gelmiştir; çünkü bu âyette «الذين آمنوا»nın manası ancak ağızlarıyla imandır; zira bununla münafıkları kastetmektedir; çünkü o, ağızlarıyla iman edip kalpleri iman etmeyenlerin vasfıdır. Sonra yahudileri ve hıristiyanları zikretmiş ve 'Onlardan Allah'a iman edene şu vardır' demiştir; onları yahudi ve hıristiyan kılmıştır. Eğer mü'min olsalardı «مَنْ آمنَ فلهم أجرهم» denmesine ihtiyaç olmazdı." Derim ki: Bu, iki görüşten birine, yani «الذين آمنوا»nın nifak yoluyla mü'min olanlar olduğu görüşüne göredir. Ebü'l-Bekā ve Mekkî b. Ebî Tâlib bunu başka bir vechle reddetmişlerdir; o da kendisine atfedilen zamirin te'kîd edilmemesidir. Derim ki: Bu Kisâî'yi bağlamaz; çünkü sahih olan şart koşmak olsa da onun mezhebi bunu şart koşmamaktır. Evet, sahih delillerin reddettiği bir görüşü söylemesi bakımından Kisâî'yi bağlar; Allah daha iyi bilir.

Bu görüşü, başkası Kisâî'den naklettiği gibi Mekkî de Ferrâ'dan nakletmiş ve ona geçen şeyle reddetmiştir. Ferrâ'nın Kisâî'ye muvafakat edip sonra döndüğü de, ona muhalif olup sonra ona döndüğü de muhtemeldir. Özetle meselede iki görüş olması caizdir.

Dördüncü vech: «إنَّ»nin isminin mahalline atfen merfûdur; çünkü o, «إنَّ» girmeden önce ibtidâ ile merfûdur; «إنَّ» ona girince manasını değiştirmemiş, aksine te'kîd etmiştir; işin sonu, onda lafzen amel etmiş olmasıdır. Bu yüzden o ve «أنّ» —bir görüşe göre— diğer kardeşleri değil, fetha ile [Mütercim notu: Metinde «بالتفح» yazılı; «بالفتح» olmalıdır] buna ihtisas etmiştir; çünkü onlarda ibtidâ manası bakidir; ليت، لعل ve كأن ise böyle değildir; zira onlar temenni, terecci ve teşbihe çıkmıştır. Ferrâ babı tek bir mecrada yürütmüş ve bunu ليت ve لعل'de de caiz görmüştür. Şu beyti inşad etmiştir:

177 - 3- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ ... في بلدٍ بها أنيسُ
(Keşke ben ve sen, ey Lemîs, insanların bulunduğu bir beldede olsaydık.)

Burada «ليتني»deki yâya atfen bir ref' zamiri olan «أنت»i getirmiştir. Atıf dışındaki tâbiler de bu hususta onun mecrasında cereyan eder mi? Ferrâ ve Yûnus bunun caiz olduğu görüşüne gitmiş ve Allah Teâlâ'nın {قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بالحق عَلاَّمُ الغيوب} [Sebe': 48] kavlini bundan saymışlardır; onlara göre «عَلاَّم»ın ref'i, mahalle göre «ربي»nin sıfatı olarak olmasındandır. «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون» sözünü de hikâye etmişlerdir. Sîbeveyh ise Araplardan «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون» diyeni hatalı saymış ve şöyle demiştir: "Bil ki Araplardan bir kavim hata eder ve «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون» derler." İnsanlar bu hususta ona itiraz etmişlerdir; çünkü o, dil ehlini —ki onlar dili vaz' edenler veya vâzıdan alanlardır— hatalı saymıştır. Şöyle cevap verilmiştir: Onlar Arapların geneline nispetle hata etmektedirler. Özetle insanlar bu mezhebi, yani «إنَّ»nin isminin mahalline atfen ref'in mutlak olarak —yani haberden önce de sonra da, ismin i'rabı gizli de olsa açık da olsa— caiz olmasını reddetmişlerdir. Bazıları haberden sonra mahalle göre ref'in caiz olduğuna dair icmâ nakletmiştir; bu bir şey değildir. Özetle meselede dört mezhep vardır: Muhakkiklerin mezhebi: mutlak olarak men. Bazılarının mezhebi tafsildir: haberden önce memnû, sonra caizdir. Ferrâ'nın mezhebi: İsmin i'rabı gizli ise lafzî çirkinlik kalktığı için caizdir; onların sözünden «إنك وزيد ذاهبان» hikâye edilmiştir. Dördüncüsü Kisâî'nin mezhebidir: mutlak olarak cevaz. Allah Teâlâ'nın {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ والذين هَادُواْ} âyetinin zâhirleriyle ve şairin —o da Dâbi' el-Bürcümî'dir— şu sözüyle istidlal eder:

177 - 4- فَمَنْ يَكُ أمسى بالمدينةِ رحلُه ... فإني وقَيَّارٌ بها لغريبُ
(Kimin yükü [konağı] Medine'de ise [iyi]; ben ve Kayyâr ise orada gerçekten garibiz.)

Ve şu sözüyle:

177 - 5- يا ليتنا وهما نَخْلُو بمنزلةٍ ... حتى يَرى بعضُنا بعضاً ونَأْتَلِفُ
(Keşke biz ve onlar bir konakta baş başa kalsak da birbirimizi görsek ve kaynaşsak.)

Ve şu sözüyle:

177 - 6- وإلاَّ فاعلموا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Yoksa bilin ki biz ve siz…)

beyit; ve şu sözüyle:

177 - 7- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ
(Keşke ben ve sen, ey Lemîs…)

Ve onların «إنك وزيدٌ ذاهبان» sözüyle. Bunların hepsi hem Kisâî hem de Ferrâ için delil olmaya elverişlidir. Kisâî'nin, ismin i'rabı açık olduğu hâlde bunun caiz olduğuna dair bir delil getirmesi gerekir; «إنَّ زيداً وعمروٌ قائمان» gibi. Zemahşerî mahalle göre ref'i reddetmiş ve şöyle demiştir: "Eğer 'Onun ref'inin «إنَّ» ve isminin mahalline atıf için olduğunu neden iddia etmedin?' dersen, derim ki: Bu, haberden fâriğ olmadan önce sahih değildir; «إنَّ زيداً وعمرو منطلقان» denmez. Eğer 'Te'hîr niyeti varken neden sahih olmasın; sanki «إنَّ زيداً منطلق وعمرو» demişsin gibi?' dersen, derim ki: Çünkü onu ref' ettiğimde «إنَّ» ve isminin mahalline göre ref' etmiş olurum; ikisinin mahallindeki âmil ibtidâdır; dolayısıyla haberde de âmilin o olması gerekir; zira ibtidâ, «إنَّ»nin amelinde iki cüzü kapsaması gibi amelinde iki cüzü kapsar. Eğer te'hîr niyet edilen «الصابئون»u ibtidâ ile ref' etsen, haberi de «إنَّ» ile ref' etmiş olsan, ikisinde iki farklı ref' edici âmil çalıştırmış olurdun." Reddettiği şeyde bu açıktır; ancak onun sözü, haber tamamlandıktan sonra bunu caiz gördüğünü anlatır. Bazılarının bunun cevazında icmâ naklettiği daha önce geçti.

Beşincisi: Vâhidî şöyle der: "Âyette Hişâm b. Muâviye'nin dördüncü bir görüşü vardır: O da «إنَّ»nin haberini gizlemen ve «الصابئون» ile söze başlamandır. Takdir: Onların Müslüman olduğunu söyleyenin görüşüne göre «إنَّ الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا يُرْحَمُون» (rahmet olunurlar), kâfir olduklarını söyleyenin görüşüne göre «يُعَذَّبون» (azap olunurlar). Yeri bilindiği için haber hazfedilir; tıpkı {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بالذكر} [Fussılet: 41] kavlinden, yani «يُعاقَبون»un hazfedilmesi gibi." Sonra Vâhidî şöyle der: "Bu görüş Basralıların görüşüne yakındır; ancak onlar ibtidânın haberini gizler ve «مَنْ آمن»i «إن»nin haberi kılarlar; bu ise onun tersidir; çünkü «مَنْ آمَن»i ibtidânın haberi kılmış ve «إنَّ»nin haberini hazfetmiştir." Derim ki: Durum onun dediği gibidir; ben de buna başta şu sözümle dikkat çekmiştim: Onlardan kimi hazfi birinciden takdir eder, kimi de tersini yapar. [Mütercim notu: Vâhidî bunu "dördüncü görüş" diye anarken müellif "beşinci vech" olarak sıralıyor.]

Altıncısı: «الصابئون», Sîbeveyh ve Halîl'in mezhebinde olduğu gibi ibtidâ ile merfûdur ve haberi mahzûftur; ancak bu mübtedâda te'hîr niyet edilmez. Onunla Sîbeveyh'in mezhebi arasındaki fark, te'hîr niyetinin olup olmamasıdır. Ebü'l-Bekā şöyle der: "Bu da zayıftır; çünkü onda hazf ve faslın lüzumu vardır"; yani hazf ile faslın bir araya gelmesinin lâzım gelmesinden dolayı. Bununla mekânın lâzımî hazf yerlerinden olduğunu kastetmiyor; çünkü Kur'an'ın indirildiği gibi okunması lâzımdır; o mekân başka bir [kelamda] zikre de hazfe de elverişli olsa bile.

Yedincisi: «الصابئون» mansûbdur; ancak tesniyeyi her hâlde elif ile yapan Hâris oğulları ve başkalarının lügati üzere gelmiştir; «رأيت الزيدان ومررت بالزيدان» gibi. Bunu Mekkî b. Ebî Tâlib ve Ebü'l-Bekā nakletmiştir. Bu görüşü söyleyenin —zayıflığına rağmen— şüphesi şudur sanki: Elifin tesniyenin ref' alâmeti olduğunu, bu lügatte ise ref', nasb ve cerde [hepsine] nâib kılındığını görmüştür; aynı şekilde vav da cemi müzekker sâlimin ref' alâmetidir; elifin kaldığı gibi nasb ve cer hâlinde de kalır. Bu zayıftır, hatta fâsittir.

Sekizincisi: «الصابئون»daki nasb alâmeti nûnun fethasıdır; nûn, «الزيتون» ve «عربون»daki gibi i'rab harfidir. Ebü'l-Bekā şöyle der: "Eğer 'Ebû Alî bunu vav ile değil ancak yâ ile caiz görmüştür' denirse, şöyle denir: Ondan başkası bunu caiz görmüştür; kıyas da bunu reddetmez." Derim ki: Bir meseleye işaret ediyor; o da şudur: Fârisî, cemi teksîr mecrasında cereyan eden bazı cemi sâlimlerde —بنين ve سنين gibi— i'rabın nûnda olmasını, bunun yalnızca yâ ile olup vav ile olmaması şartıyla caiz görmüştür; «جاء البنينُ» denir. [Şair] şöyle der:

177 - 8- وكان لنا أبو حسن عليٌّ ... أباً بَرّاً ونحنُ له بنينُ
(Ebü'l-Hasan Ali bize iyiliksever bir baba idi; biz de onun oğullarıydık.)

Hadiste de: «اللهم اجْعَلْها عليهم سنيناً كسنينِ يوسف» (Allah'ım, onu onların üzerine Yûsuf'un yılları gibi [kıtlık] yılları kıl) vardır. [Şair] şöyle der:

177 - 9- دعانيَ مِنْ نجدٍ فإنَّ سنينَه ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيباً وشَيَّبْنَنا مُرْدَا
(Beni Necd'den bırakın; çünkü onun yılları biz ak saçlıyken bizimle oynadı ve biz tüysüz gençken bizi ağarttı.)

Burada izafede nûnu sabit tutmuştur. Bu kıraat gelip nasb alâmetinin nûnun fethası olduğu şeklinde tevcîh edilince ve bu görüşle meşhur olan Fârisî olunca, Ebü'l-Bekā bu soruyu sormuş ve ondan başkasının bunu vav ile bile caiz gördüğü cevabını vermiş ve kıyasın bunu reddetmediğini söylemiştir. Derim ki: Kıyas bunu reddeder; yâ ile olması ile vav ile olması arasındaki fark açıktır; bunu «Şerhu't-Teshîl»de tahkik ettim. Evet, bir şeye cemi müzekker sâlim ile isim verildiğinde onda beş vech caizdir; bunlardan biri: Vav ile birlikte harekelerle i'rab edilmesi ve «الَّذُوْن»un benzeri olmasıdır; «جاء الذون ورأيت الذون ومررت بالذون» gibi «جاء الزيدون ورأيت الزيدون ومررت بالزيدون» denir. Bu, onunla isim verildiğinde [böyledir]; cemi olduğu sürece ise onda Ebü'l-Bekā'nın zikrettiği şeyi bilmiyorum. Bununla birlikte isbat eden, nefyeden aleyhine delildir; özellikle ilimde ve zamanda [benden] önde olduğu hâlde.

Dokuzuncusu: Mekkî şöyle der: "«الصابئون» ancak şu sebeple ref' edilmiştir: «إنَّ»nin «الذين»de bir ameli görünmemiştir; dolayısıyla ma'tûf, «إنَّ» cümleye girmeden önceki asıl ref'i üzere kalmıştır." Derim ki: Bu aynen Ferrâ'nın mezhebidir; yani «إنَّ»nin isminde i'rab görünmediğinde onun mahalline atfı caiz görmesi; ancak Mekkî'nin ibaresi zâhiren buna uymaz.

Übey b. Ka'b, Osman b. Affân, Âişe, Cahderî, Saîd b. Cübeyr ve bir cemaat yâ ile «والصابئين» okumuştur. el-Keşşâf sahibi bunu İbn Kesîr'den nakletmiştir; bu ondan meşhur değildir. Bu kıraatin tahrici açıktır: «إنَّ»nin isminin lafzına atıftır. Onda mushaf hattına bir muhalefet olsa da bu küçük bir muhalefettir ve benzerleri vardır: Kunbül'ün İbn Kesîr'den {سراط} ve babını sîn ile okuması, Hamza'nın bir rivayette onu zâ ile okuması gibi; oysa o bütün mushaflarda sâd ile yazılmıştır. Ve herkesin {إيلافهم}i yâ ile okuması gibi; oysa hepsinde hat yâsızdır.

Hasan-ı Basrî ve Zührî, bânın kesresi ve ondan sonra hâlis bir yâ ile {والصابِيُون} okumuşlardır; bu, hemzenin tahfifidir; {يَسْتهزِيُون}u hâlis yâ ile okuyanın kıraati gibi. Nâfi'in kıraati Bakara'da geçmiştir. «النصارى»ya gelince, «إنَّ»nin isminin lafzına atfen mansûbdur; külfetli olduğu için onun da «الصابئون»u ref' eden şeyle merfû olduğunu iddia etmeye gerek yoktur.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {مَنْ آمَنَ} kavli: «مَنْ»de iki vech caizdir. Birincisi: Şartiyyedir; «فلا خوفٌ» (sonuna kadar) kavli de şartın cevabıdır. Buna göre «آمن» şart sebebiyle cezm mahallinde, «فلا خوف» de onun cevabı olması sebebiyle cezm mahallindedir; fâ ise lâzımdır. İkincisi: İsm-i mevsûldür; haber «فلا خوف»tur; mübtedâ şarta benzediği için fâ girmiştir. Buna göre «آمَنَ» sıla olarak geldiği için i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; «فلا خوفٌ» haber olarak geldiği için mahalli ref'dir; fânın girmesi, Kur'an dışında olsaydı caiz [ama zorunlu olmayan] olurdu. Bu iki vechte «مَنْ»in mahalli ibtidâ ile ref'dir. İsm-i mevsûl olması durumunda [Mütercim notu: Metinde «مصولة» yazılı; «موصولة» olmalıdır] «إنَّ»nin isminden ve ona atfedilenlerden bedel olarak nasb mahallinde olması da, yalnızca ma'tûftan bedel olması da caizdir. Bu, «الذين آمنوا» hakkındaki ihtilaftır: Bunlarla hakiki mü'minler mi kastedilmiştir, yoksa nifakla mü'min olanlar mı? Önceki takdirlerin her birine göre, bu cümleden «مَنْ»e dönen zamir mahzûftur; takdiri: «مَنْ آمَنَ منهم» (onlardan iman eden); başka bir yerde bunu açıkça söylemiştir. Cümlenin geri kalanının i'rabı daha önce geçmiştir.

His saying, the Exalted: {والصابئون}: the majority read it with the wāw, and so it is in the codices of the cities. For its nominative there are nine possibilities. The first, which is the view of the majority of the people of Basra, al-Khalīl and Sībawayh and their followers: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, because the khabar of the first indicates it, the intention being to postpone it; and the implied form is: "Indeed those who believed and those who were Jews – whoever believes in them... to its end – and the Sabians likewise"; and like it: «إن زيداً وعمروٌ قائمٌ», i.e. «إنَّ زيداً قائم وعمرو قائم». If we do that, is the omission from the first, i.e. the khabar of the second is the one retained, the implied form being «إنَّ زيداً قائمٌ وعمروٌ قائم», with the first «قائم» omitted, or the reverse? Two well-known views; each of them has occurred. He said:
176 - 9- نحنُ بما عِنْدنا وأنت بما ... عندك راضٍ والرأيُ مختلفُ
(We, with what we have, and you, with what you have, are content, and opinion differs.)
i.e. «نحن رضوان» [Translator's note: the source reads «رضوان»; «راضون» is presumably meant]; and the reverse is his saying:
177 - 0- ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... فإني وقَيَّار بها لَغَريبُ
(... for I and Qayyār here are strangers.)
The implied form being «وقيارٌ بها كذلك». If it is said: why is it not permissible that the omission be from the first here too? The answer is that this would entail the lām entering the khabar of a mubtadaʾ not abrogated by «إنَّ», which is rare and occurs only in the necessity of poetry; so in the verse these two implications are permissible on this derivation. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«والصابئون» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted, the intention being to postpone it from what is within the scope of «إنَّ» of its noun and khabar, as if it were said: 'indeed those who believed, those who were Jews and the Christians – their ruling is thus – and the Sabians likewise.'" And Sībawayh cited as evidence for that:
177 - 1- وإلاَّ فاعلَمُوا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... بُغاةٌ ما بَقِينا في شِقاقِ
(Otherwise know that we and you are rebels so long as we remain in dissension.)
i.e. "know that we are rebels and you likewise." Then he said after some discussion: "If you say: His saying «والصابئون» is a conjoined word that must have something it is conjoined to, so what is it? I say: it, together with its omitted khabar, is a clause conjoined to the clause of His saying {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ} to its end, and it has no position, just as the one it is conjoined to has no position. If you say: advancing and postponing are only for a benefit, so what is it? I say: its benefit is the alert that the Sabians are accepted in repentance if faith and righteous action are sound from them; so what is the supposition about others? That is because the Sabians are the clearest of these enumerated in error and the most severe in rebelliousness; and they were called Sabians only because they 'inclined away' (ṣaba'ū) from all religions, i.e. went out; just as the poet advanced his saying «وأنتم» as an alert that those addressed are deeper in the description of rebellion than his own people, where he hastened with it before the khabar which is «بُغاةٌ», lest his people enter into rebellion before them though they are deeper in it than they and firmer of foot. If you say: if it had been said «والصابئين وإياكم», the advancing would have been achieved? I say: if it were said so, it would not be advancing in any respect, because there is no displacement from its place in it; one says 'advanced' and 'postponed' of what is displaced, not of what stays in its place; and this clause runs in the manner of a parenthetical clause."
The second possibility: that «إنَّ» is in the sense of «نعم» and so is a particle of response, and in that case it has no position; and on this what follows it is nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, and what follows that is conjoined to it in the nominative, and the khabar of all of it is His saying {مَنْ آمَنَ} to its end. That it is in the sense of «نعم» is a weaker view, which some grammarians held, and they made of it His saying, the Exalted: {إِنْ هذان لَسَاحِرَانِ} [Ṭāhā: 63] in the reading of those who read it with the alif; there is a long discussion about the verse which will come in its place, God willing. They also made of it the saying of ʿAbdullāh b. al-Zubayr: «إنَّ وصاحبُها», in answer to one who said to him "may Allah curse the she-camel that carried me to you", i.e. «نعم وصاحبُها» ("yes, and her owner"); and they made of it the saying of another:
177 - 2- بَرَزَ الغواني في الشبا ... بِ يَلُمْنَني وألومُهُنَّهْ
ويَقُلْنَ شَيْبٌ قد عَلا ... كَ وقد كَبِرْتَ فقلتُ إنَّهْ
(The beauties came forth in youth, they blame me and I blame them; and they say: 'Grey hair has come upon you, and you have grown old'; so I said: «إنَّهْ».)
i.e. «نعم», the hāʾ being for pausing. It was answered that the noun and the khabar are omitted in the saying of Ibn al-Zubayr, and the word conjoined to the noun remains as an indication of it, the implied form being «إنها وصاحبها معلونان» ("she and her owner are cursed"), and the implied form of the verse «إنه كذلك»; and on the supposition that it is in the sense of «نعم», it is not valid to make it that here, because nothing preceded it for it to be an answer to, and «نعم» does not occur as the beginning of speech, but only as an answer to a question, so that it is an affirmation of it. One might say: "It is possible that there is an implied question there, and they have mentioned that in many places, among them His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ أُقْسِمُ} [al-Qiyāma: 1] and {لاَ جَرَمَ} [Hūd: 22]; they said: it may be a rebuttal to one who says such-and-such."
The third possibility: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «هادوا», i.e. "they were Jews, they and the Sabians"; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī, and his pupils al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj rejected it. al-Zajjāj said: "It is an error from two angles. One of them: that the Sabian, in this view, shares with the Jew in Judaism, and that is not so, for the Sabian is other than the Jew; and if «هادوا» is made in the sense of 'they repented', from His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّا هُدْنَآ إِلَيْكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 156], not from Judaism, so that the meaning is 'they repented, they and the Sabians', then the exegesis has come otherwise, because the meaning of «الذين آمنوا» in this verse is only belief with their mouths, since He means the hypocrites, for it is a description of those who believed with their mouths while their hearts did not believe; then He mentioned the Jews and the Christians and said: whoever of them believes in Allah has such-and-such, making them Jews and Christians; and had they been believers, it would not have been necessary to say «مَنْ آمنَ فلهم أجرهم»." I say: this is according to one of the two views, I mean that «الذين آمنوا» are believers in hypocrisy. Abū l-Baqāʾ and Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib rejected it by another point, namely the absence of emphasis on the pronoun that is conjoined-to. I say: this does not bind al-Kisāʾī, because his school does not make that a condition, though the sound view is the condition; yes, it binds al-Kisāʾī in that he held a view that the sound proofs reject, and Allah knows best.
This view was reported by Makkī from al-Farrāʾ, as others reported it from al-Kisāʾī, and he rejected it by what has preceded; so it may be that al-Farrāʾ used to agree with al-Kisāʾī and then withdrew, or that he disagreed with him and then returned to him; and in sum two views are possible in the question.
The fourth possibility: that it is nominative by coordination to the position of the noun of «إنَّ», because before its entry it was nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and when it entered upon it, it did not change its meaning but emphasised it; the most that can be said is that it acted in it verbally, and for that reason it and «أنَّ» were singled out for the fatḥa [Translator's note: the source text reads «بالتفح», which appears corrupt; «بالفتح» is presumed], "but according to a view, with that and not with the rest of its sisters" [Translator's note: the sentence is garbled in the source], because the meaning of inceptiveness remains in it, unlike layta, laʿalla and kaʾanna, for these passed to wishing, hoping and comparison. al-Farrāʾ ran the chapter as one, and permitted that in layta and laʿalla, and cited:
177 - 3- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ ... في بلدٍ بها أنيسُ
(O would that I and you, Lumays, were in a land where there is company.)
He brought «أنت», a nominative pronoun, in coordination to the yāʾ in «ليتني». Do appositives other than conjunction run in the same course in that? al-Farrāʾ and Yūnus held that it is permissible, and made of it His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقْذِفُ بالحق عَلاَّمُ الغيوب} [Sabaʾ: 48], where the nominative of «عَلاَّم» in their view is as an adjective of «ربي» by position; and they reported «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون». Sībawayh declared mistaken whoever of the Arabs said «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون», for he said: "Know that some of the Arabs err, saying «إنهم أجمعون ذاهبون»". People took him to task for that, in that he declared mistaken the people of the language, who are the originators or the receivers from the originator; and it was answered that they are mistaken in relation to the generality of the Arabs. In sum, people have rejected this school, I mean the permissibility of the nominative by conjunction to the position of the noun of «إنَّ» absolutely, I mean before the khabar and after it, whether the case-ending of the noun is hidden or apparent. Some reported consensus on the permissibility of the nominative by position after the khabar, and it is nothing. In sum there are four schools in the question: the school of the verifiers: prohibition absolutely; the school of some: a distinction, so that before the khabar it is barred and after it is permissible; the school of al-Farrāʾ: if the case-ending of the noun is hidden, that is permissible because of the removal of the verbal dislike, and it was reported from their speech: «إنك وزيد ذاهبان»; the fourth, the school of al-Kisāʾī: permissibility absolutely, and he cites the apparent senses of His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ والذين هَادُواْ} the verse, and the saying of Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
177 - 4- فَمَنْ يَكُ أمسى بالمدينةِ رحلُه ... فإني وقَيَّارٌ بها لغريبُ
(Whoever's baggage has come to rest in Medina, I and Qayyār here are strangers.)
and his saying:
177 - 5- يا ليتنا وهما نَخْلُو بمنزلةٍ ... حتى يَرى بعضُنا بعضاً ونَأْتَلِفُ
(O would that we and they two were alone at a station, until some of us saw others and we became reconciled.)
and his saying:
177 - 6- وإلاَّ فاعلموا أنَّا وأنتمْ ... ... ... ...
(Otherwise know that we and you ...)
the verse, and his saying:
177 - 7- يا ليتني وأنتِ يا لميسُ
(O would that I and you, Lumays...)
and their saying «إنك وزيدٌ ذاهبان». All of these may serve as evidence for al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ together; and al-Kisāʾī should adduce evidence for the permissibility of that with the case-ending of the noun apparent, such as «إنَّ زيداً وعمروٌ قائمان». al-Zamakhsharī rejected the nominative by position, saying: "If you say: why do you not claim that its nominative is by conjunction to the position of «إنَّ» and its noun? I say: that is not valid before the khabar is completed; you do not say «إنَّ زيداً وعمرو منطلقان». If you say: why is it not valid, when the intention is to postpone it, as if you said «إنَّ زيداً منطلق وعمرو»? I say: because when I make it nominative I make it nominative on the position of «إنَّ» and its noun, and the governor in their position is inceptiveness, so it must be the governor in the khabar, since inceptiveness comprises the two parts in its operation, just as «إنَّ» comprises them in its operation; so if you made «الصابئون», with the intention of postponement, nominative by inceptiveness while you had made the khabar nominative by «إنَّ», you would have applied two different nominative-governors to them." What he rejected with is clear, except that his speech suggests that he permits that after the khabar is completed, and it has preceded that some reported consensus on its permissibility.
The fifth: al-Wāḥidī said: "In the verse there is a fourth view, of Hishām b. Muʿāwiya: that the khabar of «إنَّ» is implied and «الصابئون» is begun anew, the implied form being «إنَّ الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا يُرْحَمُون» ('will be shown mercy') on the view of those who say they are Muslims, and «يُعَذَّبون» ('will be punished') on the view of those who say they are disbelievers; so the khabar is omitted since its place is known, as it is omitted from His saying: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بالذكر} [Fuṣṣilat: 41], i.e. «يُعاقَبون» ('will be punished')." Then al-Wāḥidī said: "This view is close to the view of the Basrans, except that they imply the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and make «مَنْ آمن» the khabar of «إنَّ», whereas this is the reverse of that, for he made «مَنْ آمَن» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ and omitted the khabar of «إنَّ»." I say: it is as he said, and I drew attention to that in my first statement that some of them imply the omission from the first and some reverse it.
The sixth: that «الصابئون» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, like the school of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, except that postponement is not intended for this mubtadaʾ; so the difference between it and the school of Sībawayh is the intention of postponement and its absence. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also weak, because of the necessity of omission and separation in it", i.e. because of what is entailed in combining omission and separation; and he does not mean by that that the place is among the places of necessary omission, since the Qurʾān must be recited as it was sent down, even if that place in other than it permits mention and omission.
The seventh: that «الصابئون» is accusative, and it came only in the dialect of Banū l-Ḥārith and others who make the dual with alif in every case, as in «رأيت الزيدان ومررت بالزيدان»; Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib and Abū l-Baqāʾ reported that. It is as if the doubt of this speaker, weak as it is, is that he saw the alif as the sign of the nominative of the dual, and in this dialect it is made to serve for nominative, accusative and genitive; and likewise the wāw is the sign of the nominative of the sound plural, so it remains in the accusative and genitive as the alif remained; and this is weak, indeed corrupt.
The eighth: that the sign of the accusative in «الصابئون» is the fatḥa of the nūn, the nūn being the letter of declension, as it is in «الزيتون» and «عربون». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it is said: Abū ʿAlī permitted that only with the yāʾ and not with the wāw, it is said: others have permitted it, and analogy does not repel it." I say: he alludes to a question, namely that al-Fārisī permitted, in some sound plurals, which are those that run in the course of broken plurals, like banīn and sinīn, that the case-ending alight on their nūn, on the condition that that be with the yāʾ specifically and not the wāw, so that «جاء البنينُ» is said. He said:
177 - 8- وكان لنا أبو حسن عليٌّ ... أباً بَرّاً ونحنُ له بنينُ
(And Abū Ḥasan ʿAlī was for us a dutiful father, and we are his sons.)
and in the ḥadīth: «اللهم اجْعَلْها عليهم سنيناً كسنينِ يوسف» ("O Allah, make them years like the years of Yūsuf"). And he said:
177 - 9- دعانيَ مِنْ نجدٍ فإنَّ سنينَه ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيباً وشَيَّبْنَنا مُرْدَا
(Leave me alone from Najd, for its years played with us when grey and turned us grey when beardless.)
So he retained the nūn in annexation. When this reading came and was explained by the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa of the nūn, and the one famous for this view is only al-Fārisī, Abū l-Baqāʾ asked this question and answered that others permit it even with the wāw, and made out that analogy does not refuse it. I say: analogy does refuse it, and the difference between it when it is with the yāʾ and when it is with the wāw is evident, which I have verified in my Sharḥ al-Tashīl. Yes, if it is used as a name, being a sound masculine plural, five possibilities are permitted in it, the first of which is that it be declined by vowels with the wāw and become the like of «الَّذُوْن», so that it is said «جاء الزيدون ورأيت الزيدون ومررت بالزيدون», like «جاء الذون ورأيت الذون ومررت بالذون»; this is when it is used as a name; but as long as it is a plural I do not know of what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned; and whoever affirms is a proof against whoever denies, especially with his precedence in knowledge and time.
The ninth: Makkī said: "«الصابئون» was made nominative only because «إنَّ» showed no effect in «الذين», so the conjoined word remained in its original nominative before the entry of «إنَّ» upon the sentence." I say: this is exactly the school of al-Farrāʾ, I mean that he permits conjunction to the position of the noun of «إنَّ» when no case-ending shows in it, except that the wording of Makkī does not apparently agree with this.
Ubayy b. Kaʿb, ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān, ʿĀʾisha, al-Jaḥdarī, Saʿīd b. Jubayr and a group read «والصابئين» with the yāʾ, and the author of al-Kashshāf reported it from Ibn Kathīr, but that is not well known from him. This reading is clear in derivation, by conjunction to the form of the noun of «إنَّ», and although it contradicts the script of the codex, it is a slight contradiction and has parallels, such as the reading of Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr of {سراط} and its kind with sīn, and like the reading of Ḥamza in one transmission of it with zāy, while it is written with ṣād in the rest of the codices, and like the reading of all of {إيلافهم} with yāʾ, while the writing is without it in all of them.
al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Zuhrī read {والصابِيُون} with kasra on the bāʾ followed by a pure yāʾ, which is a lightening of the hamza, like the reading of those who read {يَسْتهزِيُون} with a pure yāʾ, and Nāfiʿ's reading has preceded in al-Baqara. As for «النصارى», it is accusative by conjunction to the form of the noun of «إنَّ», and there is no need to claim that it is nominative by what made «الصابئون» nominative, because of the difficulty of that.
His saying, the Exalted: {مَنْ آمَنَ}: two possibilities for «مَنْ». One: that it is conditional, and His saying «فلا خوفٌ» to its end is the apodosis, and on this «آمن» is in the position of the jussive by the condition and «فلا خوف» in the position of the jussive as its apodosis, the fāʾ being necessary. The second: that it is a relative and the khabar is «فلا خوف», the fāʾ having entered because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to the condition; «آمَنَ» on this has no position because it occurs as ṣila, and «فلا خوفٌ» is in the position of the nominative because it occurs as khabar, and the entry of the fāʾ would be permissible if it were in other than the Qurʾān. On these two possibilities the position of «مَنْ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; and on its being a relative it may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal from the noun of «إنَّ» and what is conjoined to it, or a badal from the conjoined word only; and this depends on the disagreement about «الذين آمنوا»: are the real believers meant by them, or believers in hypocrisy? On each of the preceding suppositions the returning element from this clause to «مَنْ» is omitted, its implied form being «مَنْ آمَنَ منهم», as He stated explicitly in another place; and the i'rab of the rest of the clause has already preceded.

His saying, the Exalted: {أَلاَّ تَكُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr (al-Baṣrī) and the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it with ḍamma on the nūn (تَكُونُ), and the rest read it with fatḥa. As for the one who read it with ḍamma, for him «أَنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy «أَنَّ», and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), omitted, its implied form being «أنه» (that it); «لا» is a negator, «تكون» is a complete verb (tāmma), «فتنةٌ» is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; and it explains the pronoun of the matter and affair. On this reading «حَسِب» here is for certainty, not doubt. Among its uses for certainty is the poet's saying:
178 - 0- حَسِبْتُ التقى والجودَ خيرَ تجارةٍ ... رَباحاً إذا ما المرءُ أصبحَ ثاقِلاً
(I reckoned piety and generosity the best of merchandise, in profit, when a man becomes weighed down [by age or burdens].)
That is: I was certain, because doubt is not fitting there. We were compelled to make it mean certainty in the noble verse only because the lightened «أَنْ» occurs only after certainty. As for his saying:
178 - 1- أرجو وآمُل أَنْ تدنُو مودتُها ... وما إخالُ لدينا منكِ تنويلُ
(I hope and aspire that her affection will draw near, though I do not think there will be any bestowal from you with us.)
its apparent sense is that it [the «أن»] is the lightened one, since it does not govern, and yet it occurs after «أرجو» and «آمل», which are not certainty. The answer is in two ways. The first: «أَنْ» is the subjunctive (nāṣiba) one, and it was merely left without effect (uhmilat) by analogy with the maṣdar «ما». The proof of this is that, had it been the lightened one, it would have been separated from the verbal clause by what we shall mention. This would then be like the saying of Allah the Exalted: {لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ الرضاعة} [al-Baqara: 233], and like his saying:
178 - 2- يا صاحبيَّ فَدَتْ نفسي نفوسَكما ... وحيثما كنتما لُقِّيتُما رَشَدا
(O my two companions, may my soul ransom your souls, and wherever you may be, may you meet with right guidance.)
أَنْ تَحْمِلا حاجةً لي خَفَّ مَحْمَلُها ... تستوجبا نعمةً عندي بها ويَدا
(That you carry a need of mine, light to carry, you will earn thereby a favour and a kindness from me.)
أَنْ تقرآنِ على أسماءَ ويحكما ... مني السلامَ وألاَّ تُشْعِرا أحدا
(That you two recite to Asmāʾ, woe to you both, my greetings, and that you let no one know.)
His saying «أَنْ تقرآن» is a badal (substitute) for «حاجة», and he left «أن» without effect. Similar is his saying:
178 - 3- إني زعيمٌ يا نُوَيْ ... قَةُ إن نجوْتِ من الرَّزاحِ
(I am guarantor, O little she-camel, if you escape from exhaustion,)
ونجوتِ من وَصَبِ العدو ... و [من الغدو] إلى الرَّواحِ
(and escape the fatigue of running, and [the morning journey] to the evening journey,)
أَنْ تهبطين بلادَ قَوْ ... مٍ يَرْتَعُون من الطِّلاحِ
(that you will descend upon the land of a people who graze on the ṭilāḥ trees.)
However it is construed in the verses I have mentioned, one of two irregularities (shudhūdhayn) necessarily follows, each of which has been said to be possible: either leaving «أَنْ» without effect, or the lightened one occurring after something other than knowledge, with no separation between it and the verbal clause.
The second of the two answers: his hope and aspiration were so strong that they came close to certainty, so he treated them as certainty in this respect. As for the poet's saying:
178 - 4- عَلِموا أَنْ يُؤَمَّلون فجادُوا ... قبلَ أَنْ يُسْألوا بأعظمِ سُؤْلِ
(They knew that they were being hoped for, so they gave generously, before being asked, in answer to the greatest of requests.)
the apparent sense is that it is the lightened one, and the absence of separation is irregular; it is also possible that it is the subjunctive one, in which case its occurrence after knowledge is irregular and its being left without effect is irregular. So in the first there is one irregularity, namely the absence of separation, and in the second there are two: the occurrence of the subjunctive one after knowledge, and leaving it without effect by analogy with its sister «ما».
Here (in the verse) it came with what is obligatory according to some, or the better course according to others, namely the separation between the lightened «أَنْ» and its khabar when it is a verbal clause with a fully conjugating verb that is not an invocation. The separator is either a negation, as in this verse, or a particle of futurity (ḥarf tanfīs), as in His saying, the Exalted:
{عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُمْ مرضى} [al-Muzzammil: 20], and similar: «عَلِمْت أن سوف تقومُ» (I knew that you would stand); or «قد», as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَنَعْلَمَ أَن قَدْ صَدَقْتَنَا} [al-Māʾida: 113]; or «لو», which is rare, as in His saying: {وَأَلَّوِ استقاموا} [al-Jinn: 16] and {أَن لَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ الغيب} [Sabaʾ: 14]. I specified "verbal" to exclude the nominal clause, which needs no separator, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ الحمد للَّهِ رَبِّ العالمين} [Yūnus: 10] and as in his saying:
178 - 5- في فتيةٍ كسيوفِ الهندِ قد عَلِموا ... أَنْ هالِكٌ كلُّ مَنْ يَخْفَى ويَنْتَعِلُ
(Among youths like Indian swords, who knew that everyone who goes barefoot or wears sandals is perishing.)
And I specified "fully conjugating" to exclude the non-conjugating verb, which needs no separator, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سعى} [al-Najm: 39] and {وَأَنْ عسى أَن يَكُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 185]; and "not an invocation" to exclude the one that occurs as an invocation, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَّ غَضَبَ الله} [al-Nūr: 9] in the reading of Nāfiʿ.
As for the one who put «تكونَ» in the accusative, for him «أَنْ» is the one that puts the imperfect in the subjunctive, entering upon a verb negated with «لا»; and «لا» does not prevent what follows it from being governed by what precedes it, whether a subjunctive particle, a jussive particle or a preposition. The subjunctive is like this verse; the jussive is like His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ} [al-Anfāl: 73] and {إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ الله} [al-Tawba: 40]; and the preposition is like: «جئت بلا زادٍ» (I came without provisions).
And «حَسِب» here is in its usual sense of supposition (ẓann). For the subjunctive «أن» does not occur after knowledge, just as the lightened one does not occur after anything else; and the occurrence of the subjunctive one after certainty is irregular, though that is explicit about it, as in his saying:
178 - 6- نَرْضَى عن الناسِ إنَّ الناسَ قد عَلِموا ... أَنْ لا يدانِيَنا من خَلْقِه بشرُ
(We are content with people; indeed people have known that no human of His creation comes near us.)
Nobody may say that "knowledge" here means supposition, since no necessity calls for that. The most frequent case after verbs of doubt is the subjunctive with «أَنْ», and for that reason there is consensus on the accusative in His saying, the Exalted: {أَحَسِبَ الناس أَن يتركوا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]. As for His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِمْ} [Ṭā Hā: 89], the majority are for the nominative, because seeing applies to knowledge.
The upshot is that whenever it occurs after knowledge it must be the lightened one; when it occurs after what is neither knowledge nor doubt it must be the subjunctive one; and if it occurs after a verb that admits both certainty and doubt, two forms are allowed in respect of two considerations: if we take it as certainty we make it the lightened one and put what follows it in the nominative, and if we take it as doubt we make it the subjunctive one and put what follows it in the accusative. The noble verse is of this category, as is His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَلاَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِم} [Ṭā Hā: 89] and His saying: {أَحَسِبَ الناس أَن يتركوا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]; but in the first it was read only with the nominative, and in the second only with the accusative, because the reading is a followed sunna. This is the precise formulation of the matter. I say it because some say that after verbs of doubt two forms are allowed, which gives the impression that it may be the lightened one while the verb before it remains in its meaning of doubt; but what he means is what I have told you, the formal possibility under the two considerations mentioned. Hence al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did the verb of supposition enter upon «أَنْ», which is for affirmation? I say: He placed their supposition, because of its strength in their breasts, in the position of knowledge." The reason requiring the lightened one after certainty, the subjunctive after other than it, and the two forms where there is hesitation is what they have mentioned: the lightened «أَنْ» indicates the firmness and settledness of the matter because it is for emphasis like the heavy one, and knowledge and its category are likewise, so it is fitting to place it after certainty because of the affinity between them. The proof of this is that it occurs in its heavy form after certainty, as in His saying, the Exalted:
{وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ الله هُوَ الحق المبين} [al-Nūr: 25], {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ الله على كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ} [al-Baqara: 106], {أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ الله لَهُ مُلْكُ السموات والأرض} [al-Baqara: 107], and so on. And the kind that does not indicate firmness and settledness is followed by the subjunctive one, as in His saying, the Exalted: {والذي أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِي} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 82], {نخشى أَن تُصِيبَنَا دَآئِرَةٌ} [al-Māʾida: 52], {فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 80], {أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ أَن تُقَدِّمُواْ} [al-Mujādila: 13], and so on. And the kind that admits both is followed sometimes by the lightened one and sometimes by the subjunctive one, as mentioned under the two considerations. On either assumption, I mean its being the lightened or the subjunctive one, it fills the place of the two objects according to the majority of the Basrans, and of the first object, with the second omitted, according to Abū l-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash), that is: "they supposed the absence of trial to be existent or occurring." Some grammarians reported that whoever reads the nominative should separate «أن» from «لا» in writing, because the implied pronoun «ه» (the pronoun of the matter) intervenes in meaning, while whoever reads the accusative should not separate them, there being no intervener between them. Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: "This may be admissible outside the muṣḥaf; as for the muṣḥaf, it was written only joined." End of quotation. I say: this expression contains looseness, since the word "joined" suggests that it is written «أنلا», with «أن» joined to «لا» in writing; it ought rather to be said: no form is written for it [the nūn], or a separate form is written for it. [Translator's note: the Arabic text of this last sentence is as printed; the intended sense is as rendered.]
His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ}: in this book there are five aspects. The first: the wāw is a sign of the plural of the agent, just as the feminine tāʾ is attached to the verb to indicate the feminine of the agent, as in «قامت هند»; and this dialect also applies to the dual and the feminine plural, so one says «قاما أخواك، وقمن أخواتك», as in his saying:
178 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وقد أَسْلَماه مُبْعَدٌ وحَميمٌ
(... and they both abandoned him, a distant one and a close kinsman.)
and his saying:
178 - 8- ولكنْ دِيافِيٌّ أبوه وأمُّه ... بِحَوْرانَ يَعْصِرنَ السَّليطَ أقاربُهْ
(But his father and mother are of Diyāf, in Ḥawrān; his relatives press the oil.)
Some argued from his saying, peace be upon him: "Angels succeed one another among you" («يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة»). The grammarians call this dialect the dialect of «أكلوني البراغيث» (the fleas ate me). But the more eloquent usage is that no sign be attached to the verb. The grammarians distinguished between the attachment of the feminine sign and that of the dual and plural signs in that the feminine sign is more obligatory, because femininity is in the very essence of the agent, unlike duality and plurality, which are not inherent.
The second aspect: the wāw is a pronoun referring to those mentioned, to whom the wāw of «حسبوا» refers, and «كثير» is a badal (substitute) for this pronoun, as you say: «إخوتك قاموا كبيرُهم وصغيرُهم» (your brothers stood, the elder of them and the younger) and the like.
The third aspect: the wāw is also a pronoun and «كثيرٌ» is a badal for it. The difference between this aspect and the previous one is that the pronoun in the first aspect is explained by what precedes it, namely the Children of Israel, whereas in this aspect it is explained by what follows it. This is one of the places where a pronoun is explained by what follows it, namely when the thing explaining it is made a badal of it; it is a disputed question, whose treatment has already been given. The fourth aspect: the pronoun refers to those mentioned earlier, and «كثير» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Makkī gave two implied forms: one, "the blind and deaf are many of them"; the other, "the blindness and the deafness are many of them", the indication being His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ}. On his first implied form «كثير» applies to them, and «منهم» is an adjective of «كثير»; on the second «كثير» applies to the blindness and the deafness, not to them, and «منهم» is an adjective of it in the sense that it issued from them; and this second is not apparent. Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as: "those are many of them". The fifth aspect: «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ and the verbal clause before it is the khabar. It is not said that a verb, whenever it occurs as a khabar, must be placed later, for that is conditional on the agent being latent, as in «زيدٌ قام»; for if it were put first, «قام زيدٌ», it would be confused with the agent. If it is said: this too would be confused with the agent in the dialect of «أكلوني البراغيث», the answer is that it is a weak dialect to which we pay no heed. Abū l-Baqāʾ weakened this aspect for another reason, saying: "because the verb has occurred in its proper position, so nothing else is intended for it." There is room for objection in this, since we do not concede that it occurred in its proper position; it would have occurred in its proper position only if it were bare of a sign. Like this verse also is His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3].
The majority read «عَمُوا وَصمُّوا» with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the ṣād; the original is «عَمِيُوا» and «صَمِمُوا» like «شَرِبُوا», so the first was altered by elision and the second by assimilation (idghām). Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read «عُمُوا» and «صُمُّوا» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and ṣād, and with the mīm of «عَمُوا» lightened. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "on the implication of «عَماهُم الله وصَمَّهم», that is: He struck them and hit them with blindness and deafness, as one says «نَزَكْتُه» when you strike him with the spear (nayzak), and «رَكَبْتُه» when you strike him with your knee." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) did not object to him, although before that, after reporting the reading, he had said: "It follows the course of «زُكِم الرجلُ» (the man was afflicted with a cold) and «أَزْكَمَه الله», and «حُمَّ» (he was feverish) and «أَحَمَّه الله»; one does not say «زَكَمه الله» nor «حمَّه», just as one does not say «عَمَيْتُه» nor «صَمَمْته»; these are verbs that came in the passive, whose agent is not named, and they are transitive triliteral; when they are built in the active they become intransitive, and if you want to build them in the active as transitive you introduce the hamza of transitivization, which is a strange type among verbs." End of quotation. His saying "just as one does not say «عَمَيْتُه» nor «صَمَمْته»" implies that the triliteral of these is not transitive, yet al-Zamakhsharī said, on the implication, «عَماهُم الله وصَمَّهم», thus using the triliteral as transitive. If what the Shaykh said is correct, then Abū l-Qāsim's words must be invalid, or vice versa.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «كثيراً» in the accusative, as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, though it has been mentioned more than once that for Sībawayh it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Makkī said: "Were you to put «كثيراً» in the accusative in ordinary speech, it would be permissible to make it an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: much blindness and deafness." I say: it is as though he had not come across it as a reading, or it was not sound in his view because of its irregularity.
As for His saying {فَعَمُواْ}, He joined it with «ف», and His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ}, He joined it with «ثم»; and this is a fine meaning: immediately after the supposition, blindness and deafness befell them without delay, and He attributed both verbs to them, in contrast to His saying {فَأَصَمَّهُمْ وأعمى أَبْصَارَهُمْ} [Muḥammad: 23], because that concerns someone who had no prior guidance. And He attributed the good action to Himself in His saying {ثُمَّ تَابَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}, and joined His saying {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ} with the particle of delay as an indication that they persisted in error until the time of repentance.

His saying, the Exalted: {ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ}: its meaning is "one of the three", and for that reason the majority forbade putting what follows it in the accusative; you do not say «ثالثٌ ثلاثةً» nor «رابعٌ أربعةً». They said: because it is an active participle and works like its verb, and here no verb can stand in its place, since one does not say «ربَّعْتُ الأربعة» nor «ثلَّثْتُ الثلاثة»; and also because it is one of the three, so it would have to govern itself. Thaʿlab permitted the accusative in such a case, and the majority rejected him with what I have told you. But when it is not of the same wording as what follows it, both forms are permitted: the accusative and the genitive construct, such as «رابعٌ ثلاثةَ» and, if you wish, «ثلاثةٍ». Know that from one to ten an active-participle form may be derived, such as «واحد», and it may be formed before that, so one says «حادي وثاني وثالث» up to «عاشر». It may then be used on its own, so one says «ثالث» and «رابع», just as one says «ثلاثة» and «أربعة» without mentioning the thing counted; or it may be used in the manner of active participles if something different in wording follows it, and that is only what is one rank below it, such as «عاشرُ تسعةٍ» and «تاسعُ ثمانيةٍ»; it is not combined with what is two ranks below, such as «عاشرُ ثمانيةٍ» or «ثامنُ أربعةٍ», and it is not combined at all with what is above it, so one does not say «تاسعُ عشرةٍ» nor «رابعُ ستةٍ». Once this is established, it is given the ruling of the active participle, so it governs only under its conditions. But when it is combined with a term agreeing with it in wording, its genitive construct is obligatory, as in «ثالثُ ثلاثةٍ» and «ثاني اثنين», and Thaʿlab's disagreement has been mentioned. It may also be built from eleven to nineteen, so one says «حادي عشر» and «ثالث عشر»; it may be used on its own as I mentioned to you; and it may be used together with another term, which must be only an agreeing one, so one says «حادي عشر أحد عشرَ» and «ثالثَ عشرَ ثلاثَة عشرَ», and one does not say «ثالثَ عشرَ اثني عشرَ», although some disagreed. The ruling for the feminine is like its ruling in the explicit adjectives, so one says «ثالثة» and «رابعة», «حاديةَ عشرةَ», and «ثالثةَ عشرةَ ثلاثَ عشرةَ». It has many rulings which I treated fully in «شرح التسهيل».
His saying: {وَمَا مِنْ إله}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) in the mubtadaʾ because of the presence of the two conditions, namely that the discourse is not affirmative and that what it governs is indefinite. «إلهٌ» is a badal (substitute) for the position of «إلهٍ» governed in the genitive by the all-inclusive «مِنْ», because its position is nominative, as mentioned before. The implied meaning: "there is no deity in existence except a deity characterized by oneness". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «مِنْ» in His saying «مِنْ إله» is for all-inclusiveness, and it is the one implied with the «لا» of generic negation in your saying «لا إلهَ إلا اللَّهُ»; the meaning is: "there is no deity at all in existence except a deity characterized by oneness, and He is Allah the Exalted." From this it follows that «مِنْ إله» is the mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, and «إلا إلهٌ» is a badal on the position. Makkī said: "In ordinary speech the accusative is permissible: «إلا إلهاً», as an exception." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been read in the genitive as a badal for the word «إله», it would have been permissible in Arabic." I say [Translator's note: printed «قتل», evidently for «قلت»]: it is not as he said, because it would require «مِنْ» to be redundant in an affirmative context, since the negation is broken by «إلاَّ»; if you said «ما قامَ إلا من رجلٍ» it would not be allowed, and so too here. That is allowed only on the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash, for the Kufans stipulate only the indefiniteness of what it governs, and al-Akhfash stipulates nothing.
Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī preferred the genitive as a badal for the word «إله», but it is remote because «مِنْ» is not made redundant in an affirmative context." I say: if someone held that His saying «إلا إلهٌ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the matter being one of the emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), as if it were said «ما إلهٌ إلا إلهٌ متصفٌ بالواحدِ» (there is no deity except a deity characterized by the One), no objection would appear to him; but I have not seen them say it. There is room for consideration in it.
His saying: {لَيَمَسَّنَّ} is the answer to an omitted oath, and the answer to the condition is omitted because this indicates it. The implied form: "By Allah, if they do not desist, there will surely touch ...". This came according to the rule I established: when a condition and an oath come together, the answer is given to whichever of the two comes first, unless something with a khabar precedes them; the condition is sometimes answered regardless; and it was also mentioned earlier that the verb of the condition in that case is only past in form, or in meaning and not form, as in this verse. If it is asked: the one that comes first here is the condition, since the oath is implied and so its implied position is later; the answer is that had the oath been intended to be later in implication, the condition would have been answered; when the oath was answered it was known that it is implied as being first. Some expressed this by saying: "The preparatory lām of the oath is sometimes omitted while its ruling is observed, as in this verse, for the implied form is «ولئن لم»", as is explicitly stated in other places, such as His saying: {لَّئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ المنافقون} [al-Aḥzāb: 60]. Parallel to this verse is His saying: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ} [al-Aʿrāf: 23] and {وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 121]. It was mentioned earlier that this type of oath-answer must be met with the lām and one of the two nūns according to the Basrans, except for what I excepted for you. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «لَيَمسُّهُم عذاب»? I say: putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun has a benefit, namely repeating the testimony against them of disbelief."
His saying: {مِنْهُمْ} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Either from «الذين» or from the pronoun of the agent in «كفروا»." I say: the ruling does not change in meaning, because the pronoun of the agent is the relative itself, and the difference is verbal only. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «مِنْ» in His saying {لَيَمَسَّنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ مِنْهُمْ} is explicative, like the one in His saying {فاجتنبوا الرجس مِنَ الأوثان} [al-Ḥajj: 30]. I say: on this view «منهم» is attached to an omitted element. If you say: on making it a ḥāl it is also attached to an omitted element, I say: the difference between them is that on making it a ḥāl it is attached to an omitted element which is in reality the ḥāl, whereas on this view it is attached to a verb explaining the first relative, as if it were said «أعني منهم» (I mean from among them), and «أعني» has no grammatical position because it is an explicative clause. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "«مِنْ» in «منهم» is partitive, that is: being of them, and the link is achieved by the pronoun, as if it were said: their disbeliever; not all of them remained in disbelief." End of quotation. He means: this is an implication on its being partitive, and it amounts to its being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

Allah Teâlâ'nın {أَفَلاَ يَتُوبُونَ} sözü: Benzeri birçok kez geçmiştir; bunda iki görüş vardır: Cumhurun görüşü, atıf harfinin takdiren hemzeden önce olduğudur; Ebü'l-Kâsım'ın [Zemahşerî] görüşü ise atıf harfinin yerinde kaldığı ve [hemzeden sonra] kendisine atfedilen bir cümlenin hazfedildiğidir; takdir: "Küfürlerinde sebat mı ediyorlar da tevbe etmiyorlar?" İstifhâm hakkında iki görüş vardır. / Bunların daha zâhir olanı: Onların hâline taaccüp (hayret) ettirmek içindir: Bu çirkin sözden nasıl tevbe etmez ve istiğfar etmezler? İkincisi: Emir anlamındadır; bu, İbn Ziyâd el-Ferrâ'nın görüşüdür; sanki "Bu iki sözden tevbe edin ve istiğfar edin" demiş gibidir; {فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُّنتَهُونَ} [Mâide: 91] sözü gibi. İbn Atıyye'nin sözü onun tahdîz (teşvik) için olduğunu anlatır. Şöyle demiştir: "Celle ve alâ, onları tevbeye ve mağfiret dilemeye teşvik etmekle onlara şefkat göstermiştir." Bununla mânâ bakımından kastetmiştir; yoksa bu lafızdan tahdîz anlamak kabul edilmiş değildir. Atıf harfinin, hemze ile tahdîz anlamı veren «لا» arasını ayırması nasıl akla uygun olur? Eğer "Bu ancak tahdîz bildiren «ألا»nın basit olup mürekkep olmadığı görüşümüze göre müşkil olur; bu durumda onda atıf harfiyle fasıl iddia edilmez. Ama onun nefy bildiren «لا»nın başına gelmiş istifhâm hemzesi olduğunu ve ikisinin anlamının tahdîz hâline geldiğini söylersek, atıf harfiyle fasıl zarar vermez; çünkü bu, başına istifhâm hemzesi giren nefy bildiren «لا»da bilinen bir şeydir" dersen, cevap şudur: Bu mutlak olarak caiz değildir; çünkü o [asıl] anlam sıyrılmış ve başka bir anlam, yani tahdîz meydana gelmiştir. Asılda caiz olmasından, yeni bir anlam meydana geldikten sonra da caiz olması lazım gelmez.

His saying, the Exalted: {مَّا المسيح ابن مَرْيَمَ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ}: like His saying: {وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلاَّ رَسُولٌ} [Āl ʿImrān: 144]. And «قد خَلَتْ» is an adjective of it, as in the other verse. The meaning of restriction (ḥaṣr) has been mentioned. His saying: {وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ} is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and this clause has no grammatical position. «صِدِّيقَةٌ» is the feminine of «صِدِّيق», which is a form of intensification like «فَعّال» and «فَعُول», except that it does not work as the forms of intensification work, so one does not say «زيدٌ شِرِّيبٌ العسلَ» as one says «شَرَّابٌ العسلَ», though analogy requires that it work. Is it from the triliteral «صَدَق» or from the doubled «صَدَّق»? Analogy requires the first, because forms of intensification are regular from the triliteral and not from the quadriliteral, from which only few came. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from «التصديق» (affirming as true)", and so did Ibn ʿAṭiyya, except that he made it a possibility; and this is clear from His saying: {وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَاتِ رَبَّهَا}, where He made explicit the doubled verb attributed to her.
His saying: {كَانَا يَأْكُلاَنِ الطعام} has no position, because it is resumptive and an explanation that the two of them are like the rest of humanity in needing what every generated body needs, whereas the true God is exalted above that. Some [Translator's note: printed «بضعهم», evidently for «بعضهم»] said: "It is a metonymy for their need to relieve themselves", and there is no need for that. His saying «كيف» is accusative by «نُبَيِّن» after it, and what is in it was mentioned at His saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28] and elsewhere; it cannot be governed by what precedes it, because it has the head of the sentence. This interrogative clause is in the position of accusative because it suspends (muʿallaqa) the verb before it. His saying: {ثُمَّ انظر أنى يُؤْفَكُونَ} is like the clause before it; «أَنَّى» means "how", «يُؤْفكون» governs «أنَّى», and «يُؤْفكون» means "are turned away".

His saying, the Exalted: {مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ}: «ما» may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which), or an indefinite noun that is described; the clause after it is then either a ṣila (relative clause), having no grammatical position, or an adjective, whose position is accusative. As for «ما» being applied to rational beings here, because Jesus and his mother are meant, there are several explanations. One: «ما» was used with a rational being intended because it is vague and applies to everything; so said Sībawayh. Or the kind was intended, as in His saying {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ النسآء} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], that is: the good kind. Or the rational together with the non-rational was intended, because most of what was worshipped besides [Allah] is non-rational, such as idols, statues, stars and trees; or [it applies to him because] he resembles it in his first state, since in his first state he is not described as having intellect, so how [Translator's note: printed «فيكف», evidently for «فكيف»] could he be taken as a god to be worshipped? In the repetition of the command in His saying «انظُرْ» ... «ثم انظر» there is an indication of the importance of looking; moreover the objects of the two lookings differ: the first is a command to look at how Allah the Exalted clarified and explained the signs to them so that there is no doubt or suspicion in them, and the second command is to look at how they were turned away from reflecting on them and believing in them, or at their being overturned from what was intended for them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say [Translator's note: printed «قتل», evidently for «قلت»]: what is the meaning of the delay (tarākhī) in His saying «ثم انظر»? I say: its meaning is what lies between the two wonders; he means that He explained the signs to them in a wondrous way, and that their turning away from them is more wondrous than that." End of quotation. He means that it is a matter of delay in rank, not in time, and similar is {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 1], which will come.
His saying: {والله هُوَ السميع العليم}: «هو» may be a second mubtadaʾ, with «السميعُ» its khabar and «العليمُ» a second khabar or an adjective, the clause being the khabar of the first; it may be a separating pronoun (faṣl), the details of which are known; and it may be a badal. The apparent view about this clause is that it has no grammatical position, but it is possible that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَعْبُدون», that is: "Do you worship other than Allah, when Allah is the one who deserves worship because He hears everything and knows it?" Al-Zamakhsharī's words tend to this, for he said [Translator's note: printed «فإن قال», evidently for «فإنه قال»]: {والله هُوَ السميع العليم} is attached to «أتعبدون», that is: "Do you associate partners with Allah and not fear Him, when He is the one who hears what you say and knows what you believe? Do you worship the helpless when Allah is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing?" End of quotation. The link between the ḥāl and its owner is the wāw. The coming of these two attributes after this statement is perfectly fitting, for the All-Hearing hears what is complained to Him of harm and the request for benefit, and knows where both fall and how they come about.

His saying, the Exalted: {غَيْرَ الحق}: there are five aspects in it. The first: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "do not exceed bounds in your religion with an excess other than the truth", that is, a false excess; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the agent in «تَغْلُوا», that is: "do not exceed bounds, transgressing the truth"; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The third: it is a ḥāl from «دينكم», that is: "do not exceed bounds in it while it is false, but do exceed bounds in it while it is true"; this is supported by what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "Because excess in religion is of two kinds: a true one, which is to investigate its realities, to search into its remotest meanings, and to strive to attain its proofs; and a false excess, which is to overstep the truth and pass beyond it by turning away from the evidence." The fourth: it is accusative as a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil). The fifth: as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) reported these two aspects from others and considered them remote, saying: "Furthest is the one who held that it is a connected exception, and the one who held that it is a disconnected exception and implies it as «لكن الحقَّ فاتبعوه» (but the truth, so follow it)." I say: the excepted-from is hard to specify; what appears is that it is His saying {فِي دِينِكُمْ}, as though it were said: "do not exceed bounds in your religion, except the true religion, for excess in it is permitted to you", and the meaning of excess in it is what was given in al-Zamakhsharī's explanation.
Al-Wāḥidī mentioned for it the ḥāl and the exception, saying: "The accusative of «غيرَ الحق» is in two ways. One: ḥāl and cutting off (qaṭʿ) from «الدين», as if it were said: 'do not exceed bounds in your religion, being in opposition to the truth', because they opposed the truth in their religion and then exceeded bounds in it by insisting upon it. The second: that it be accusative as an exception, so «الحق» is excepted from what is forbidden to be exceeded in, such that excess in what is true is permitted, in the sense of following it and holding firm to it." This is explicit in what I told you, that the excepted is «دينُكم» [Translator's note: so printed; by the analysis above «دينكم» is the excepted-from (mustathnā minhu), not the exception].
The meaning of excess (ghuluww) was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. The apparent sense of these earlier analyses is that «تَغْلُوا» is an intransitive verb, and Abū l-Baqāʾ stated so explicitly; however the lexicographers explain it with a transitive meaning, for they said: its meaning is "do not exceed the limit". Al-Rāghib said: "«الغلو» is exceeding the limit. It is said when it concerns price: «غلاء»; when it concerns measure and rank: «غُلُوّ»; and of an arrow: «غَلْو»; and their verbs are all «غلا يغلو»." On this basis «غير الحق» may be accusative as a direct object, that is: "do not exceed in your religion anything other than the truth" [Translator's note: printed «تتجازوا», evidently for «تتجاوزوا»]. If we explain «تغلوا» as meaning "go far", from their saying «غلا السهمُ» (the arrow went far), it would be intransitive; so the one who said it is intransitive may have taken it from this and not from the first.
His saying: {كَثِيراً}: there are two aspects for its accusative. One: it is a direct object, and this is the view of most of the interpreters, who explain it as: "and they led many of them astray", or of the hypocrites. The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar, that is, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "leading astray much"; and on this the object is omitted, that is: "they led others astray with much leading astray."

His saying, the Exalted: {مِن بني إِسْرَائِيلَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; its owner is either «الذين» or the wāw of «كفروا», and they are one in meaning. His saying: {على لِسَانِ دَاوُودَ وَعِيسَى}: what is meant by "tongue" is the organ, not the language; so said the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), meaning that the one pronouncing the cursing of these people is the tongue of these two prophets. The phrase «على لِسَانِ» came in the singular rather than the dual or plural, and he did not say «على لسانَيْ» nor «على ألسنةِ», because of a general rule, which is: whenever two parts, each single in its owner, are annexed to both of the owners without distinction, three forms are allowed for them: the plural wording, which is the preferred, followed by the dual according to some; and according to others the singular takes precedence over the dual. So one says «قَطَعْتُ رؤوسَ الكبشين» and, if you wish, «رأسَي الكبشين», and, if you wish, «رأسَ الكبشين»; and from this is {فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا} [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. My saying "two parts" excludes two things that are not parts, like «درهميكما»; yet it has occurred: «من بيوتِكما وعمائمكما وأسيافمكا» [Translator's note: printed «أسيافمكا», evidently for «أسيافكما»] because there is no risk of confusion. My saying "single" excludes such as «العينين واليدين» (the two eyes and the two hands); as for His saying {فاقطعوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا} [al-Māʾida: 38], it is understood by consensus. And my saying "without distinction" excludes such as «قَطَعْتُ رأسي الكبشين: السمينِ والكبشِ الهزيل» (I cut the heads of the two rams, the fat one and the lean ram), and this verse is of that kind, so only the singular is permissible. Some said: "and it is the preferred", that is, another is permissible. The verification of this rule was given in Sūrat al-Māʾida at length [Translator's note: printed «طويٍ», evidently for «طويل»], so refer to it.
In my mind there is something about the organ being what is meant by "tongue", and this is supported by what al-Zamakhsharī said: "Allah sent down their cursing in the Zabūr on the tongue of Dāwūd and in the Injīl on the tongue of ʿĪsā", and the force of this refuses its being the organ. Then I saw that al-Wāḥidī mentioned two views from the commentators and preferred what I said. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means in the Zabūr and in the Injīl; the meaning is that Allah the Exalted cursed in the Zabūr whoever disbelieves among the Children of Israel, and likewise in the Injīl. It was also said: «on the tongue of Dāwūd and ʿĪsā» because the Zabūr is the tongue of Dāwūd and the Injīl is the tongue of ʿĪsā." This is explicit that what is meant by "tongue" is other than the organ. Then he said: "Al-Zajjāj said: it is possible that Dāwūd and ʿĪsā knew that Muḥammad is a prophet sent, and that they cursed whoever disbelieves in him." The view is the first; so al-Zajjāj's allowing that makes apparent that the organ is meant by "tongue", but this is not a view of the commentators. «على لسانِ» is attached to «لعن». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "as one says: «جاء زيدٌ على فرس»." There is room for consideration in it, since the apparent sense is that it is a ḥāl. His saying «ذلك بما عَصَوْا» has had its parallel mentioned before. His saying {وَّكَانُواْ يَعْتَدُونَ}: in this defective clause there are two aspects, the more apparent being that it is joined to the ṣila of «ما», namely «عَصَوْا», that is [Translator's note: printed «بسب», evidently for «بسبب»]: "that is because of their disobedience and their being transgressors". The second: it is resumptive, that is: Allah the Exalted informed about them of that. The Shaykh said: "What supports this is what comes after it as an elaboration of it, namely His saying {كَانُواْ لاَ يَتَنَاهَوْنَ}."

And His saying, the Exalted: {عَن مُّنكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ}: attached to «يَتَناهَوْن», and «فعلوه» is an adjective of «منكر». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is the meaning of describing the wrongdoing with «they did it», when prohibition does not come after the deed? I say: its meaning is that they did not forbid one another repeating a wrongdoing they had done, or a wrongdoing like one they had done, or a wrongdoing they intended to do, as you see the signs of plunging into immorality and its instruments being levelled and prepared. It is also possible that the meaning is: they do not desist and do not refrain from a wrongdoing they have done, but persist in it and continue. One says: «تناهى عن الأمر» and «انتهى عنه» when he refrained from it."

Allah Teâlâ'nın {لَبِئْسَ مَا} sözü: «بئسما قَدَّمَتْ»: Bunun benzerinin i'rabı geçmiştir; tekrarına gerek yoktur. Burada bu terkibe özgü başka bir ilave vardır; onu öğreneceksin. {أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ} sözü: Mahalli hakkında birkaç vecih vardır. Birincisi: Zem ile tahsis edilen (mahsûs bi'z-zem) şeyden bedel olarak merfûdur. Mahsûs hazfedilmiş ve sıfatı onun yerine konmuştur. Zira «ما»yı, zem fiilinin fâili olarak ref' mahallinde marife tâm bir isim olarak i'rab edersin; mahsûs bi'z-zem mahzûftur; «قَدَّمت لهم انفُسُهم» da onun sıfatı olarak ref' mahallinde bir cümledir. Takdir: "Nefislerinin onlar için önceden gönderdiği bir şey ne kötü şeydir!" «أَنْ سَخِط اللهُ عليهم» de mahzûf «شيء»den bedeldir. Bu, daha önce tespiti geçtiği üzere Sîbeveyh'in mezhebidir. İkincisi: O, mahsûs bi'z-zemdir; bu durumda onda meşhur üç vecih vardır. Birincisi: Mübtedâdır, önündeki cümle onun haberidir; buna göre rabıt, bunu [rabıt] kabul edenlere göre umumdur; ya da cümle mübtedânın aynı olduğundan rabıta ihtiyaç yoktur. İkincisi: Mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberidir; çünkü «بِئْسَ الرجل» dediğinde sana "O kim?" denir, sen de "Falan" dersin; yani "O, falandır." Üçüncüsü: Haberi mahzûf bir mübtedâdır. Bunun tahriri geçmiştir. Onun mahsûs bi'z-zem olduğu görüşüne Zemahşerî gibi bir topluluk gitmiştir; [Zemahşerî] başkasını zikretmemiştir. Şöyle demiştir: "{أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ} mahsûs bi'z-zemdir; sanki 'Onların âhirete azıkları ne kötüdür: Allah'ın onlara gazabı!' denmiştir. Anlam: Allah'ın gazabını gerektiren şey." Derim ki: Bu muzâfın takdirinde, üzerinde düşünen kimseye gizli kalmayacak güzellikler vardır; çünkü Bârî Teâlâ'ya izâfe edilen gazabın kendisi için "mahsûs bi'z-zemdir" denmez; mahsûs bi'z-zem ancak onun sebepleridir. Vâhidî, Mekkî ve Ebü'l-Bekâ da bu görüşe gitmiştir. Ancak Şeyh [Ebû Hayyân], bu vechi Ebü'l-Kâsım ez-Zemahşerî'den naklettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: "Bu i'rab ancak Ferrâ ve Fârisî'nin / «ما»yı mevsûl kabul eden mezhebine göre, ya da «ما»yı temyîz, «قَدَّمَتْ لهم»ü de onun sıfatı kabul edenlerin mezhebine göre sahih olur. Sîbeveyh'in mezhebine göre ise bu mümkün olmaz." Sonra Sîbeveyh'in mezhebini zikretmiştir.
«أَنْ سَخِطَ»in vecihlerinden üçüncüsü: «ما»dan bedel olarak ref' mahallindedir. Mekkî ve İbn Atıyye bu görüşe gitmiştir; ancak Mekkî bunu başkasından nakletmiştir; şöyle demiştir: "Denildi ki: «لبئس»deki «ما»nın marife olması üzere ondan bedel olarak ref' mahallindedir."
