Şeyh, bu vechi İbn Atıyye'den naklettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: "«ما» ister tâm ister mevsûl olsun bu sahih olmaz; çünkü bedel, mübdelün minhin yerine geçer; «أَنْ سَخِطَ»in ise «بِئْسَ»in fâili olması caiz değildir; çünkü «بِئْس»in fâili «أَنْ» ve fiil olmaz." Bu, onun dediği gibi açık bir itirazdır.
Dördüncü vecih: «ما»nın temyîz olduğu söylendiğinde, «ما»dan bedel olarak nasb mahallindedir. Bunu Mekkî ve Ebü'l-Bekâ zikretmiştir. Bu asla caiz değildir. Çünkü Basralılara göre temyîzin şartı nekre olmasıdır; «أَنْ» ve onun etki alanındaki şey ise onlara göre, zamire benzediği için marifelerin en marifesi kabîlindendir. Bunun tespiti geçmiştir. O hâlde — bedel mübdelün minhin yerine geçtiğine göre — nasıl temyîz olur? [Mütercim notu: metinde «فيكف» yazılmıştır; «فكيف» olduğu açıktır.] Kûfelilere göre de bu caiz değildir; çünkü onlar her marife ile, özellikle «أَنْ» ve fiil ile temyîzi caiz görmezler. Beşincisi: «قَدَّمَتْ» ile mansûb olup, önceki açıklamaya göre mevsûl veya mevsûf «ما»ya râci olan zamirden bedel olarak nasb mahallindedir. Takdir: "Onu, [yani] Allah'ın gazabını önceden gönderdi." «الذي رأيت زيداً أخوك» (gördüğüm, [yani] Zeyd, kardeşindir) demen gibi. Bunda kendi yerinde bir tartışma vardır. Altıncısı: Hâfıdın düşürülmesi (nez'u'l-hâfıd) ile nasb mahallindedir; zira takdir «لأَنْ سَخِط»tir (gazap ettiği için). Bu, Sîbeveyh'in ve Ferrâ'nın mezhebine göre cârîdir; çünkü onlar hâfıd hazfedildikten sonra «أَنْ»in mahallinin nasb olduğunu ileri sürerler. [Mütercim notu: metinde «مذهبه سيبويه» yazılmıştır; «مذهب سيبويه» olduğu açıktır.] Yedincisi: O takdir edilen hâfıd ile cer mahallindedir; bu, Halîl'in ve Kisâî'nin mezhebine göre cârîdir; çünkü onlar ikisinin [«أَنْ» ve fiilin] cer mahallinde olduğunu ileri sürerler. Bunun tahkiki birçok kez geçmiştir. Buna göre mahsûs bi'z-zem mahzûftur; yani: "Nefislerinin onlar için önceden gönderdiği şey, [yani] amelleri veya yaptıkları ne kötüdür!" Takdir edilen illet lâmı ise ya zem cümlesine mütealliktir — yani: "Onların zemmedilmesinin sebebi Allah'ın onlara gazabıdır" —, ya da kendisinden sonraki mahzûf bir şeye; yani: "Allah onlara gazap ettiği için şöyle şöyle oldu."

And His saying, the Exalted: {لَبِئْسَ مَا}: and «بئسما قَدَّمَتْ»: the i'rab of its parallel has been given before, so there is no need to repeat it; here there is something further, because of the particularity of the construction, and you will learn it. His saying: {أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}: there are several aspects for its position. The first: it is nominative as a badal (substitute) for the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), the makhṣūṣ having been omitted and its adjective set in its place; for «ما» is parsed as a complete, definite noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of the verb of blame, the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm being omitted, and «قَدَّمت لهم انفُسُهم» is a clause in the position of nominative as an adjective of it. The implied form: "How evil is the thing, a thing their souls have sent forward for them"; so «أَنْ سَخِط اللهُ عليهم» is a badal for the omitted «شيء». This is the school of Sībawayh, as its explanation preceded. The second: it is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, and then the three well-known aspects apply. One: it is a mubtadaʾ and the clause before it is its khabar, the link on this view being generality according to those who make it so, or no link being needed because the clause is identical with the mubtadaʾ. Two: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, because when you say «بِئْسَ الرجل» you are asked: who is he? and you say: so-and-so, that is: he is so-and-so. Three: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the treatment of that has already been given. A group, such as al-Zamakhsharī, held that it is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, and he mentioned nothing else; he said: {أَن سَخِطَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ} is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm, as if it were said: "How evil is their provision for the Hereafter: Allah's wrath against them", the meaning being: "what causes Allah's wrath". I say: in implying this muḍāf there are merits that are not hidden from one who reflects on it, for the very wrath attributed to the Creator, the Exalted, is not said to be the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm; rather what is the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is its causes. Al-Wāḥidī, Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ also held this, except that the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), after reporting this aspect from Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī, said: "This i'rab is sound only on the school of al-Farrāʾ and al-Fārisī in making «ما» a relative, or on the school of one who makes «ما» a tamyīz (specification) with «قَدَّمَتْ لهم» as its adjective; as for the school of Sībawayh, it cannot work." Then he mentioned Sībawayh's school.
The third aspect of «أَنْ سَخِطَ»: it is in the position of nominative as a badal for «ما», and Makkī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this, except that Makkī reported it from others, saying: "It was said: in the position of nominative as a badal for «ما» in «لبئس», on the view that it is definite." The Shaykh said, after reporting this aspect from Ibn ʿAṭiyya: "This is not sound, whether «ما» is complete or relative, because the badal takes the place of what it substitutes, and «أَنْ سَخِطَ» cannot be the fāʿil of «بِئْسَ», since the fāʿil of «بِئْس» is not «أَنْ» plus the verb." It is a clear objection as he said.
The fourth aspect: it is in the position of accusative as a badal for «ما» when it is said to be a tamyīz; Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is not permissible at all, because the condition of tamyīz according to the Basrans is that it be indefinite, and «أَنْ» with what is in its scope is, for them, among the most definite of definites because it resembles the pronoun, as its explanation has preceded; how [Translator's note: printed «فيكف», evidently for «فكيف»], then, can it be a tamyīz, since the badal takes the place of what it substitutes? For the Kufans too this is not permissible, because they do not permit tamyīz with any definite, especially «أَنْ» plus the verb. The fifth: it is in the position of accusative as a badal for the pronoun governed in the accusative by «قَدَّمَتْ», which refers to «ما», whether relative or described, according to what has preceded; the implied form: «قَدَّمَتْه سُخْط الله», like your saying «الذي رأيت زيداً أخوك» (the one I saw, Zayd, is your brother); there is a discussion of this in its place. The sixth: it is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, as the implied form is «لأَنْ سَخِط»; this follows the school of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ [Translator's note: printed «مذهبه سيبويه», evidently for «مذهب سيبويه»], because both claim that the position of «أَنْ» after the removal of the preposition is accusative. The seventh: it is in the position of genitive by that implied preposition; this follows the school of al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī, because both claim that the two are in the position of genitive, and this has been verified more than once. On this, the makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm is omitted, that is: "How evil is what their souls have sent forward for them, their deed or their doing"; and the implied lām of cause is attached either to the clause of blame, that is: "the cause of their blame is Allah's wrath against them", or to an omitted element after it, that is: "because Allah's wrath came upon them, it was such-and-such («كيتَ وكيتَ»)".

His saying, the Exalted: {لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ الناس}: the i'rab of this was given before, in such as His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ الناس على حياوة} [al-Baqara: 96], which makes repetition unnecessary. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement)", but that is nothing; rather it is the lām with which an oath is met. «أشدَّ الناس» is the first object, and «عداوةً» is accusative as tamyīz (specification). «للذين» is attached to it [to «عداوةً»], strengthened by the lām since it is secondary in governing to the verb; and its being feminine with tāʾ does no harm, because it is built upon it, so it is like his saying:
179 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . .
ورهبةٌ ... عقابَك. . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(... and fear of your punishment ...) [Translator's note: only this fragment of the verse is given in the source.]
«للذين» may also be an adjective of «عداوة», attached to an omitted element, with «اليهودَ» as the second object. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is possible that «اليهود» is the first and «أشدَّ» the second, and this is the apparent view, since the aim is that Allah the Exalted informs about the Jews and the polytheists that they are the most intense of people in enmity to the believers, and about the Christians that they are the nearest of people in affection to them; the aim is not to inform about the most intense and nearest of people as being of the Jews and Christians. If it is said: whenever the two are equal in definiteness and indefiniteness, the first object must come first and the second last, as is obligatory in the mubtadaʾ and khabar, and this is of that kind; the answer is: that is obligatory only where there is confusion; but when evidence indicates it, advancing and postponing are permitted, and from it is his saying:
179 - 1- بَنُونا بنو أبنائِنا، وبناتُنا ... بنوهُنَّ أبناءُ الرجالِ الأباعدِ
(Our sons are the sons of our sons, but our daughters' sons are the sons of distant men.)
Here «بنو أبنائنا» [Translator's note: printed «بنوا أبناء», evidently for «بنو أبنائنا»] is the mubtadaʾ and «بَنُونا» is its khabar, because the meaning rests on likening the children of the sons to sons; and similar is the saying of the other:
179 - 2- قبيلةٌ ألأَمُ الأحياءِ أكرمُها ... وأَغْدُر الناسِ بالجيرانِ وافِيها
(A tribe: the most ignoble of the living is its noblest, and the most treacherous of people to neighbours is its most faithful.)
«أكرمُها» is the mubtadaʾ and «ألأمُ الأحياءِ» is its khabar; likewise «وافيها» is a mubtadaʾ and «أغدرُ الناس» its khabar, and the meaning rests on this; and the verse is of this kind in what I have told you."
His saying: {والذين أَشْرَكُواْ} is conjoined to «اليهود», and what is said of the second clause is as what is said of the one before it. «ذلك بأنَّ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and its explanation has preceded; «منهم» is the khabar of «أنَّ» and «قسيسين» is its noun; «أن» with its noun and khabar is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the bāʾ with its genitive noun here is the khabar of «ذلك». «القسيسين» is the plural of «قِسِّيس» on the pattern «فِعِّيل», which is a form of intensification like «صِدِّيق», as already mentioned; here it means the chief and worshipper of the Christians. Its origin is from «تَقَسَّسَ الشيءَ» when one follows it and seeks it by night; one says «تقسَّسْتُ أصواتَهم», that is, I followed them by night. The chief of the Christians is called «قِسّ» and «قِسِّيس», and the guide by night «قَسْقَاس» and «قَسْقَس»; so said al-Rāghib. Another said: «القَسّ», with fatḥa on the qāf, is following a thing, and from it the scholar of the Christians was named, for his pursuit of knowledge. Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj said:
179 - 3- أَصْبَحْنَ عن قَسِّ الأذى غَوافِلا ... يَمْشِين هَوْناً خُرُداً بَهالِلا
(They became heedless of the pursuit of harm, walking gently, bashful, noble.)
One says «قَسَّ الأثرَ» and «قَصَّه» also with ṣād; and one says «قَسّ» and «قِسّ», with fatḥa and kasra on the qāf, and «قِسِّيس». Ibn ʿAṭiyya claimed that it is non-Arabic, an Arabized loanword. Al-Wāḥidī said: "The Arabs have spoken of «القَسّ» and «القِسّيس»," and al-Māzinī recited:
179 - 4- لو عَرَضَتْ لأيْبُلِيٍّ قَسِّ ... اشعثَ في هيكلهِ مُنْدَسِّ
(Had she appeared before an ʾAybulī [monk], a priest, disheveled, hidden in his temple,)
حَنَّ إليها كحنينِ الطَسِّ ...
(he would have yearned for her as the cup yearns ...)
and he recited from Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt:
179 - 5- لو كان مُنْفَلَتٌ كانت قساوسةٌ ... يُحْيِيهم الَّهُ في أَيْديهم الزُّبُرُ
(Had there been any escape, there would be priests whom Allah gives life, with the scriptures in their hands.)
This is the lexicographers' discussion of «القِسّيس». Then he said: "ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: "The Christians lost the Injīl and what is in it, and there remained of them a man called «قسيساً»", meaning that he remained on his religion and did not change it; so whoever remained on His guidance and religion was called «قِسِّيس». Quṭrub said: «القَسّ» and «القِسّيس» is the scholar in the language of the Romans. Waraqa said:
179 - 6- لما خَبَّرْتَنا مِنْ قولِ قَسٍّ ... من الرهبانِ أكرُه أَنْ يَبُوحا
(When you told us of the words of a priest among the monks, which I dislike to be divulged.)
On this, «القَسّ» and «القِسّيس» are among the words in which the two languages coincide." I say: this strengthens Ibn ʿAṭiyya's view. The lexicographers did not report for this word «القُس», with ḍamma on the qāf, either as a maṣdar or as an adjective. As for Quss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, it is a proper name, so it may be among what is changed by way of becoming a proper name, its origin being «قَسّ» or «قِسّ» with fatḥa or kasra as Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported; Quss ibn Sāʿida was the most learned of the people of his time, and he is the one of whom he, peace be upon him, said: "He will be raised as a community by himself." As for the plural of «قِسِّيس», it is a sound plural, as in the noble verse. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Had it been pluralized as «قَسُوساً», it would have been right, because the two are of one meaning", meaning «قِسّ» and «قِسِّيس». He said: "«القِسّيس» is also pluralized as «قساوِسَة»; they pluralized it on the pattern of «المَهالِبَة», the original being «قساسِسَة»; the sīns multiplied, so one of them was replaced by a wāw", and they recited Umayya's «لو كان مُنْفَلَتٌ كانت قساوسةٌ» (the verse). Al-Wāḥidī said: "«القُسوسة» is the maṣdar of «القِسّ» and «القِسّيس»." I say: it is as though he made this maṣdar derived from this noun, like «الأبوّة», «الأخوّة» and «الفتوّة» from the words «أب», «أخ» and «فتى»; I had earlier mentioned that «القَسّ» with fatḥa is originally the maṣdar and that the scholar was named by it for intensification; and I do not know what led the one who said it is Arabized to do so, given the existence of its meaning in the Arabs' language as you have learned from what preceded.
«الرُّهْبان» is the plural of «راهب», like «راكب» and «رُكْبان», «فارِس» and «فُرْسان». Abū l-Haytham said: "«الرُّهبان» may be singular and may be plural", and he recited, for its being singular, the poet's saying:
179 - 7- لو عايَنَتْ رهبانَ دَيْرٍ في القُلَلْ ... لأَقْبَلَ الرُّهبانُ يَعُدُوا ونَزَلْ
(Had she seen the monk of a monastery on the peaks, the monk would have come running and descended.)
Had it been a plural he would have said «يَعُدُون» and «نَزَلُوا», with the plural pronoun. But there is no proof in this, because a singular pronoun may return to an explicit plural when it is interpreted as one, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنعام لَعِبْرَةً نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ} [al-Naḥl: 66], where the hāʾ in «بطونه» refers to «الأنعام»; and he said:
179 - 8- وطابَ البانُ اللِّقاحِ وبَرَدْ
(And the milk of the milch camels became sweet and cold.)
where in «بَرَدْ» there is a pronoun that refers to «أَلْبان»; and they said: «هو أحسنُ الفتيانِ وأجملُه» (He is the best of the youths and the most beautiful of him). And the other said:
179 - 9- لو أنَّ قوميَ حين أَدْعُوهمْ حَمَلْ ... على الجبالِ الشُّمِّ لانهدَّ الجَبَلْ
(Had my people, when I call them, been loaded onto the lofty mountains, the mountain would have collapsed.)
and other examples that would take long to mention. Among the instances of its coming as a plural is the verse, and in the noble Qurʾān it occurs only as a plural. Kuthayyir said:
180 - 0- رُهْبانُ مَدْيَنَ والذين عَهِدْتُهُمْ ... يبكون من حَذَرِ العقابِ قُعودا
(The monks of Madyan and those I knew, weeping, seated, from fear of punishment,)
لو يَسْمعون كما سَمِعْتُ كلامَها ... خَرُّوا لِعَزَّةَ رُكَّعاً وسُجودا
(had they heard her speech as I heard it, they would have fallen down for ʿAzza in bowing and prostration.)
It was said: there is no proof in this because he said «والذين», so it is possible that the pronoun was pluralized because of this plural and not because «رهبان» is a plural. More explicit than this is Jarīr's saying:
180 - 1- رُهبانُ مَدْيَنَ لو رَأَوْكِ تَنَزَّلُوا ... والعُصْمُ مِنْ شَعَفِ العَقُولِ الفادِرِ
(The monks of Madyan, had they seen you, would have come down, and the mountain goats from the peak of the high refuge.)
Ibn al-Haytham [Translator's note: earlier cited as Abū l-Haytham; the source's text varies] said: "If the singular «رهبان» is pluralized as «رَهابين» and «رهابِنَة», it is permissible, and if you say «رهبانيون» it is right, as if you attributed it to monasticism (rahbāniyya); and «الرهبانية» is from «الرَّهْبَة», which is fear." Al-Rāghib said: "«الرُّهبان» may be singular or plural; whoever makes it singular pluralizes it as «رَهابين», and «رهابِنَة» as a plural is more fitting", meaning that this pattern predominates in the plural, like «الفرازِنَة», «الموازِجَة» and «الكيالِجة». Al-Layth said: "«الرهبانيِّة» is the maṣdar of «الراهب», and «الترهُّب» is devotion in a hermitage." This resembles the earlier discussion that «القَسْوَسة» is a maṣdar of «القَسّ» and «القِسّيس», and there is no need for this, since «الرهبانية» is a maṣdar in itself, from «الترهُّب», which is devotion, or from «الرَّهَب», which is fear; hence al-Rāghib said: "«الرهبانيِّة» is the excess of one who undertakes devotion out of extreme fear." The derivation of this root was given at His saying {وَإِيَّايَ فارهبون} [al-Baqara: 40].
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ} is conjoined to the «أنَّ» governed in the genitive by the bāʾ, that is: "that is because of what preceded and because they are not arrogant."

Allah Teâlâ'nın {لاَ يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ} sözü sonuna kadar: Bunun i'rabı ve kelimelerin iştikakı Bakara sûresinde geçmiştir. Hamza, Kisâî ve Âsım'dan Ebû Bekir [Şu'be], «عَقَدْتُمْ» şeklinde kâfı şeddesiz ve aynden sonra elif olmaksızın; İbn Âmir'den İbn Zekvân «فاعلتم» vezninde «عاقدتم»; diğerleri ise kâfı şeddeli olarak «عَقَّدتم» okumuştur. Şeddesiz okuyuş asıldır. Şeddeli okuyuşa gelince birkaç vechi muhtemeldir. Birincisi: Teksîr (çokluk) içindir; çünkü kendisine hitap edilen bir topluluktur. İkincisi: Mücerred anlamındadır; böylece birinci kıraate uygun olur; «قَدَّر» ve «قَدَر» gibi. Üçüncüsü: «واللهِ الذي لا إله إلا هو» (Kendisinden başka ilâh olmayan Allah'a yemin olsun ki) gibi yeminin te'kîdine delâlet eder. Dördüncüsü: Bağlanma (iltizam) ile azmin te'kîdine delâlet eder. Beşincisi: Diğer kıraatteki elifin bedelidir; bunun anlamının ne olduğunu bilmiyorum. Yeminin tekrarı için olması caiz değildir; çünkü keffâret bir kere [yemin etmekle] de vâcip olur.
Ebû Ubeyd bu kıraate cüret etmiş ve onu zayıf göstermiştir; şöyle demiştir: "Şedde, birbiri ardınca tekrar içindir. Bu kıraatin, tekrarlanmadığı için tek yeminde keffâretin düşmesini gerektirmesinden emin değilim." İnsanlar bu hususta onu yanılmış saymış ve önceki anlamları zikretmişlerdir; böylece kıraat tilâvet ve anlam bakımından selâmette kalmıştır; hamd Allah'adır.
«عاقدت»e gelince, «جاوزت الشيء» ve «جُزْتُه» (şeyi geçtim) gibi mücerred anlamında olması muhtemeldir. Fârisî şöyle demiştir: "«عاقَدْتم» iki şeye ihtimallidir. Birincisi: «طارقت النَّعْل» (nalını yamadım) ve «عاقبتُ اللص» (hırsızı cezalandırdım) gibi «فَعَل» anlamında olması. Diğeri: İki fâil gerektiren «فاعَلْتُ»ın kastedilmesi; sanki anlam şudur: 'Üzerine yeminleri akdettiğiniz şey sebebiyle.' Onu «عاهد» (ahitleşti) anlamında olduğu için «على» ile müteaddî kılmıştır; [Allah Teâlâ] {بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهِ الله} [Fetih: 10] buyurmuştur. Nitekim {نَادَيْتُمْ إِلَى الصلاة} [Mâide: 58] sözünü de «إلى» ile müteaddî kılmıştır; oysa bâbı «ناديت زيداً» demendir; {وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ الطور} [Meryem: 52] gibi. Çünkü o, 'şuna çağırdım' anlamındaydı; [Allah Teâlâ] {مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى الله} [Fussılet: 33] buyurmuştur. Sonra genişletilmiş, câr hazfedilmiş ve fiil mef'ûle nakledilmiştir; sonra sıladan mevsûla râci zamir hazfedilmiş, böylece {بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ الأيمان} olmuştur; tıpkı {فاصدع بِمَا تُؤْمَرُ} [Hicr: 94] sözünden hazfedildiği gibi." Derim ki: —Allah ona rahmet etsin— müfâale anlamını açıklamak istemiş, tazmîn ve râci zamirin kademeli olarak hazfi için bu benzerleri getirmiştir. Anlam: "Üzerine yeminleri akdettiğiniz ve yeminlerin üzerine sizinle akitleştiği şey sebebiyle"; böylece akitleşmeyi mecazen yeminlere nispet etmiştir. Birisi şöyle diyebilir: Bu kadar çok zorlamaya ihtiyaç duyacak şekilde bir râci zamire ihtiyacımız olmayabilir. Bu da «ما»yı masdariyye yapıp mef'ûlü mahzûf kabul etmemizle olur; takdiri: "Başkalarıyla yeminleri akitleşmeniz sebebiyle", yani "Başkalarıyla yeminler üzerine akitleşmenizden dolayı." [Mütercim notu: metinde «قد لانحتاج» bitişik yazılmıştır.] Böylece başka bir mecazdan, yani akitleşmenin yeminlere nispet edilmesinden de kurtuluruz; çünkü bu vecihte akitleşme başkasına nispet edilir ki bu hakiki bir nispettir. Bir topluluk bunu — yani bu vechi — açıkça belirtmiştir.
Şeyh [Ebû Hayyân], Ebû Ali'nin sözünü tenkit ederek / şöyle demiştir: "Onun «طارَقْتُ النعل» ve «عاقبت اللص» gibidir sözü [doğru değildir]; o, onun gibi değildir; çünkü sen «طَرَقْتُ» ve «عَقَبْتُ» demezsin; ama «عاقَدْت اليمين» ve «عَقَدْتُها» dersin." Bu Ebû Ali'ye lazım gelmez; çünkü onun kastı, iki kişiden ortaklık anlamındaki müfâalenin ondan nefyedilmiş olması bakımından onun gibi olduğudur; nitekim «عاقَبْتُ» ve «طارَقْتُ»ten de nefyedilmiştir. Onda ayrıca şöyle de deniyor olması teşbihe zarar vermez.
Şöyle de demiştir: "Câr harfinin, sonra zamirin kademeli olarak hazfedildiğini takdir etmesi uzaktır. «فاصدَعْ بما تؤمر» da bunun benzeri değildir; çünkü «أمر» bazen kendiliğinden, bazen de câr harfiyle müteaddî olur; asıl harf ile olsa da. Ayrıca «فاصدَعْ بما» sözündeki «ما»nın «الذي» anlamında olması zorunlu değildir; bilakis zâhir olan masdariyye olmasıdır. Burada da en güzeli masdariyye olmasıdır; çünkü bir masdar olan «اللَّغْو» ile karşılaştırılmıştır."
Nisâ sûresinde Allah Teâlâ'nın {والذين عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ} [âyet: 33] sözü ve «عَاقَدْت» geçmiş, bu ikisindeki tartışmayı sana zikretmiştim. Böylece burada meşhur [kıraatlerde] üç kıraat, orada ise iki kıraat olmuştur. [Mütercim notu: metinde «فصار في ثلاث قراءات» geçmektedir; «فصار في هذه ثلاث قراءات» kastedildiği anlaşılmaktadır.] Hamza'dan Nisâ sûresinde şeddeli olarak «عَقَّدت» rivayet edildiğini zikretmiştim; buna göre orada da üç kıraat olur. Ancak bu garip bir tesadüftür; çünkü Hamza bu sûrede şeddesiz okuyanlardandır, Nisâ'da ise ondan şeddeli okuyuş rivayet edilmiştir.
Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعَامُ} sözü: Mübtedâ ve haberdir. «فكفارته»deki zamirde dört vecih vardır. Birincisi: Kendisinden söz edilmemiş olsa da sözün siyakının delâlet ettiği hinse (yemini bozmaya) râcidir; yani "yemini bozmanın keffâreti." İkincisi: «ما»yı mevsûl isim yaparsak ona râcidir; bu, bir muzâfın hazfı üzeredir; yani "onu bozmanın keffâreti." Zemahşerî böyle takdir etmiştir. Üçüncüsü: Kendisine delâlet eden fiil önce geçtiği için akde râcidir. Dördüncüsü: Müennes olsa da, "hilf" (yemin etme) anlamında olduğu için yemine râcidir. Bu ikisini Ebü'l-Bekâ söylemiştir; ikisi de zâhir değildir. [Mütercim notu: metinde «بظارهرين» yazılmıştır; «بظاهرين» olduğu açıktır.] «إطعامُ», mef'ûlüne muzâf bir masdardır; bir harf ve mâlum bir fiille takdir edilir; yani: "Onun keffâreti, yeminini bozanın on [yoksulu] doyurmasıdır." Masdarın fâili çoğu kez hazfedilir. Onu meçhul bir fiille, yani "on [yoksulun] doyurulması" şeklinde takdir etmeye zorlayan bir zaruret yoktur; çünkü bunda, daha önce dikkat çekilen bir ihtilaf vardır. Birincisine göre «عشرة»nın mahalli nasb, ikincisine göre ise nâib-i fâil olarak ref' olur. Bunun tâbide ortaya çıkan bir faydası vardır: «يعجبني أكلُ الخبزِ» (ekmeğin yenmesi hoşuma gider) dediğinde, onu mâlum takdir edersen «الخبز»e tâbi olanı lafız üzere cer, mahal üzere nasb ile getirirsin; meçhul takdir edersen onu cer ve ref' ile getirirsin. «يعجبني أكلُ الخبزِ والسمنِ / والسمنَ / والسمنُ» dersin. Hadiste: «نَهَى عن قتلِ الأبتر وذو الطُّفْيَتَيْنِ» (Kuyruksuz yılanı ve sırtında iki çizgi olanı öldürmeyi yasakladı) şeklinde, "kuyruksuz yılanın öldürülmesi" anlamı üzere «ذو» ref' ile [gelmiştir]. Ebü'l-Bekâ şöyle demiştir: "İyisi, onu — yani masdarı — fâili zikredilmiş bir fiille takdir etmesidir; çünkü öncesi ve sonrası hitaptır." Derim ki: Bu, bunu güçlendiren bir karinedir; çünkü anlam: "Onun keffâreti, siz yemin edenlerin doyurmanızdır." Sana daha önce, karine bulunmasa bile, asıl olduğu için onu mâlum fiille takdir etmenin râcih olduğunu söylemiştim.
{مِنْ أَوْسَطِ} sözü: Bunda iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: Öncesinin açıkladığı mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir; takdiri: "Onların yiyeceği, ortalamasından olur." Söz {مساكين} sözünde tamamlanmış olur. Bunun daha fazla açıklaması inşallah yakında gelecektir. İkincisi: İkinci mef'ûlün sıfatı olduğu için nasb mahallindedir; takdir: "Ortalamasından olan bir azık veya yiyecek." Birinci mef'ûl ise masdarın kendisine izâfe edildiği «عشرة»dır. «ما» mevsûl isimdir; râci zamir mahzûftur; yani "yedirdiğiniz şeyin ortalamasından." Ebü'l-Bekâ onu «مِنْ» ile mecrûr olarak takdir etmiş ve "kendisinden yedirdiğiniz şey" demiştir. Bunda nazar vardır; çünkü mecrûr râci zamirin hazfedilmesinin şartı, iki harfin ve iki müteallikin aynı olmasıdır. Burada iki harf — «مِنْ» ve «مِنْ» — aynı olsa da âmil farklıdır; çünkü ikinci «مِنْ» «تُطْعِمُون»a mütealliktir, birincisi ise mahzûf mef'ûlün sıfatı olarak geldiği için mahzûfa, yani mutlak kevne mütealliktir. Şöyle denebilir: Fiil {مِنْ أَوْسَطِ} sözüne yöneldiği için sanki onda amel eden odur; biz ancak sanat (nahiv kuralları) zarureti için bir mef'ûl takdir ettik. Eğer "Mevsûl «مِنْ» ile mecrûr olmamıştır; o ancak izâfetle mecrûr olmuştur" dersen, cevap şudur: Mevsûla muzâf olan şey bu hususta mevsûl gibidir; «مُرَّ بغلام الذي مررت» (Yanından geçtiğim kimsenin kölesinin yanından geç) gibi.
«أهليكم», «تُطْعِمُون»un birinci mef'ûlüdür; ikincisi, geçtiği üzere mahzûftur; yani "onu ailelerinize yedirirsiniz." «وأهليكم» sâlim çoğuldur; alem ve sıfat olmaması şartlarından eksiktir. [Mütercim notu: metinde «ونقصه من الشروط» geçmektedir; yani bu kelimede sâlim çoğul şartlarından alem veya sıfat olma şartı eksiktir.] Bunu güzelleştiren şey, «هو أهلُ لكذا» (O, şuna ehildir) sözlerinde olduğu gibi çoğu kez "şuna layık" anlamında kullanılmasıdır; dolayısıyla sıfatlara benzemiş ve onların çoğulu gibi çoğul yapılmıştır. Allah Teâlâ {شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا} [Fetih: 11] ve {قوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَاراً} [Tahrîm: 6] buyurmuştur. Hadiste de şöyle gelmiştir: "Allah'ın ehilleri (أهلين) vardır." "Ey Allah'ın Resûlü, onlar kimlerdir?" denildi. "Kur'ân okuyucuları; onlar Allah'ın ehli ve has kullarıdır" buyurdu. «أهلُوا الله» sözü, izâfet sebebiyle nûnu hazfedilmiş bir çoğuldur; tekil olması da muhtemeldir; bu durumda «أهلُ الله» diye yazılır; lafızda o tektir.
Ca'fer es-Sâdık «أهالِيكم» şeklinde yâyı sükûnla okumuştur. Bunda iki tahrîc vardır. / Birincisi: «أهالي», «أَهْلَة»nın kırık çoğuludur; dolayısıyla «لَيْلة – لَيال» gibi kıyasa göre şâzdır. İbn Cinnî şöyle demiştir: "«أَهال», «ليَال» mesabesindedir; tekilleri «أَهْلاة» ve «لَيْلاة»dır. Araplar «أهلٌ» ve «أَهْلَة» derler. Şâir şöyle demiştir:
180 - 6- وأَهْلَةُ وُدٍّ قد سُرِرْتُ بوُدِّهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Sevgileriyle sevindiğim nice dostluk ehli …)"
Ebû Zeyd'in sözünün kıyası, onu «أحاديث» ve «أعاريض» gibi takdir edilen bir tekilin çoğulu yapmandır. İbn Cinnî'nin "«أهال», «ليال» mesabesindedir; tekilleri «أَهْلاة» ve «لَيْلاة»dır" sözü de buna işaret eder. Bunun semâ' yoluyla olması da, Ebû Zeyd'in dediği gibi kıyas yoluyla olması da muhtemeldir.
İkincisi: Bu, «أَهْل» için bir ism-i cemidir. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: "«ليلة»nin çoğulunda «الليالي» ve «أرض»ın çoğulunda «الأراضي» gibi." [Mütercim notu: metinde «كاليالي» yazılmıştır; «كالليالي» olduğu açıktır.] Onun "«ليلة»nin çoğulunda ve «أرض»ın çoğulunda" sözüyle lügavî çoğulu kastetmiştir; çünkü ism-i cemi anlamca çoğuldur. Bunun ıstılah bakımından «ليلة» ve «أرض»ın çoğulu olduğunu kastetmez; zira onu ism-i cemi olarak kabul etmiştir; o hâlde onu ıstılahî olarak nasıl çoğul yapar? [Mütercim notu: metinde «يجلعه» yazılmıştır; «يجعله» olduğu açıktır.]
Ca'fer'in kıraatinin kıyası, hafifliği sebebiyle yâyı fetha ile harekelemekti; fakat o, yâyı elife benzetmiş ve harekeyi onda takdîrî kılmıştır. Bu, nazımda çoktur; Nâbiğa'nın şu sözü gibi:
180 - 7- رَدَّتْ عليه أقاصِيه ولَبَّده ... ضَرْبُ الوليدةِ بالمِسْحاةِ في الثَّأَدِ
(Cariyenin ıslak toprakta kürekle vurması, onun uç kısımlarını üzerine geri çevirdi ve onu sıkıştırdı.)
Diğerinin şu sözü:
180 - 8- كأنَّ أيدِيهنَّ بالقاعِ القَرِقْ ... أيدي جوارٍ يتعاطَيْنَ الوَرِقْ
(Düz ve sert ovadaki [develerin] ayakları, sanki gümüş paraları birbirine veren cariyelerin elleridir.)
Bu, bundan daha doyurucu biçimde geçmiştir.
Allah Teâlâ'nın {أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ} sözü: Bunda iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: «إطعام»a ma'tûftur; yani: "Onun keffâreti on [yoksulu] doyurmak veya o on [yoksulu] giydirmektir." İkincisi: «من أوسط»ın mahalline ma'tûftur; Zemahşerî böyle demiştir. Onun söylediği, «من أوسط» hakkında sana geçen bir vecihte yürür; o da «من أوسط»ın, öncesinin delâlet ettiği mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olmasıdır; takdiri: "Onların yiyeceği ortalamasındandır." Ona göre söz {عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ} sözünde tamamdır; sonra yiyeceğin şunun ortalamasından olacağına dair başka bir habere başlamıştır. Ama «مِنْ أوسط»ın ikinci mef'ûl olduğunu söylersek, i'rabca farklı oldukları için «كسوتهم»ün ona atfı imkânsızdır.
Cumhur «كِسوتهم»i kâfın kesresiyle okumuştur. İbrâhîm en-Nehaî, Ebû Abdurrahmân es-Sülemî ve Saîd b. el-Müseyyeb ise dammesiyle okumuştur. Bakara'da bunların hem masdarda hem de giydirilen şeyde iki lügat olduğu geçmiştir. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: "«القُدوة»deki «القِدوة» ve «الأُسوة»deki «الإِسوة» gibi." Ancak Bakara'da dammesiyle okuyan Talha'dır; onu burada zikretmemişler, bunları da orada zikretmemişlerdir. [Mütercim notu: metinde «إلا أن قرأ» geçmektedir; «إلا أن مَن قرأ» kastedildiği anlaşılmaktadır.]
Saîd b. Cübeyr ve İbnü's-Semeyfa' «أو كأُسْوَتِهم» şeklinde, «أُسْوة»nin başına giren cer kâfı ile okumuştur. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: "Anlamı: Ya da israf olsun cimrilik olsun ailelerinize yedirdiğiniz şeyin benzeri; onları nafakalarının miktarından eksik bırakmazsınız, aksine onları eşit tutarsınız. Eğer 'Kâfın mahalli nedir?' dersen, derim ki: Ref'dir; takdiri: 'Ya da onların yiyeceği, kendilerininki gibidir'; yani: Onlara ortalamayı yedirmezlerse, kendi yiyeceklerinin benzeri gibi." [Alıntı burada] bitti. Daha önce onun «من أوسط»ı mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olarak ref' mahallinde kabul ettiği geçmişti; dolayısıyla ona göre kâf «مِنْ أوسطِ»a ma'tûf olarak merfû olur. Ebü'l-Bekâ da buna yakın bir şey söylemiştir; şöyle demiştir: "Kâf ref' mevziindedir; yani: Ya da ailelerinizin örneğinin benzeri." Şeyh ise şöyle demiştir: "O, «مِنْ أوسط»ın mahalline ma'tûf olarak nasb mevziindedir"; çünkü ona göre o ikinci mef'ûldür.
Ancak bu kıraat, giydirmeyi keffâretten nefyetmektedir; oysa insanlar onun üç hasletten biri olduğunda icmâ etmiştir. Fakat bu kıraatin sahibi "Giydirme sünnetten çıkarılmıştır" diyebilir. Ama keffârette giydirmenin dayanağının bu âyet olduğu üzerinde icmâ bulunsaydı, bu okuyucuya reddiye vermek sahih olurdu.
{أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ} sözü: «إطعامُ»a ma'tûftur. Mef'ûlüne muzâf bir masdardır. Bununla ilgili söz, «إطعامُ عشرة» hakkındaki söz gibidir: Onu mâlum veya meçhul bir fiille takdir etmenin cevazı ve bu hususta söylenenler. {فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ} sözü, Nisâ'daki {فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ} [âyet: 92] sözü gibidir; bu, tahrir edilmiş olarak geçmiştir.
{إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ} sözü: Ebü'l-Bekâ şöyle demiştir: "Zarf olarak mansûbdur; onu nasb eden «كفارة»dır; yani: O doyurma, / ya da ona ma'tûf olan şey, yemin ettiğiniz vakitte yemini bozmanızı sizden örter." Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: "Zikredilen o şey keffârettir. «تلك كفارةُ» denseydi de sahih olurdu; 'o şeyler' anlamında, ya da te'nîs keffâret için olurdu. Anlam: 'Yemin edip de bozduğunuzda.' Keffâretin, yemin etmenin kendisiyle değil, yemini bozmakla vâcip olduğu bilindiği için bozmanın zikri terk edilmiştir." Zemahşerî'nin zikrettiği bu şey, yani bozmanın takdiri zorunludur. Bu yüzden Ebü'l-Bekâ'nın "«إذا»da amel eden «كفارةُ أَيْمانكم»dür; çünkü anlam: O, yemin ettiğiniz vakitte yeminlerinizi örter" sözü ayıplanmıştır. Ona şöyle denmiştir: Keffâret yemin etme vaktinde vâki değildir; içinde vâki olmayan bir şey zarfta nasıl amel eder? Âyetin zâhiri, «إذا»nın salt zarf olduğu ve onda şart anlamının bulunmadığıdır; bu ise onda galip olanın dışındadır. [Mütercim notu: metinde «ممتحِّضة» yazılmıştır; «متمحِّضة» olduğu açıktır.] Şart olması da caizdir; Basralıların kaidesine göre cevabı, öncekinin delâlet ettiği mahzûf bir şey olur; Ebû Zeyd'e ve Kûfelilere göre ise öncekinin kendisidir. Takdir: "Yemin edip de bozduğunuzda, işte bu yeminlerinizin günahının keffâretidir"; «أنتَ ظالمٌ إنْ فَعَلْتَ» (Yaparsan zalimsin) sözleri gibi. {كذلك يُبَيِّنُ} sözündeki kâf, i'rabcıların cumhuruna göre mahzûf bir masdarın sıfatıdır; yani: "Allah âyetlerini o açıklamanın benzeri bir açıklamayla açıklar." Sîbeveyh'e göre ise, birçok kez bilindiği üzere o masdarın zamirinden hâldir.

His saying, Exalted is He: {عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تَسْألوا». The grammarians disagreed about «أشياء» in five schools.

The first — the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Māzinī and the majority of the Basrans —: it is an ism jamʿ (collective noun) from the wording of «شيء», singular in form and plural in meaning, like «طَرْفاء» and «قَصْباء». Its original form is «شَيْئاء», with two hamzas with an alif between them, on the pattern «فَعْلاء» like «طَرْفاء». They found the meeting of two hamzas with an alif between them heavy, especially as it was preceded by a weak letter, namely the yāʾ; and this word circulated very frequently on their tongues, so they transposed the word by placing its lām (third radical) — namely the first hamza — before its fāʾ (first radical) — namely the shīn — and said «أَشْياء», so its pattern became «لَفْعاء»; and it was made a diptote because of the extended alif of femininity. This school was preferred on the grounds that nothing follows from it except transposition (qalb), and transposition is frequent in their language, as in «الجاه», «الحادي», «القِسِيّ», «ناءَ», «آدُر», «آرام», «ضِئاء» in the reading of Qunbul, and «أَيِس»; the originals being «وجه», «واحد», «قُووس», «نَأَى», «أَدْوُر», «أَرْآم», «ضياء» and «يَئِس». Some objected to this that transposition is contrary to the base rule, and that it has occurred only out of poetic necessity or in a small portion of speech; but this is refuted by the examples I have given. We do not deny that transposition is not regular; as for the anomalous and rare, it is like their saying «رَعَمْلي» for «لَعَمْري» and «شَواعي» for «شوايع». [The poet] said:
181 - 3- وكان أَوْلاها كِعابُ مُقامِرٍ ... ضُرِبَتْ على شَزَنٍ فهنَّ شَواعِي
(The first of them were like a gambler's dice, cast on a rough edge, so they scattered in all directions.)
He means «شوائع».
As for the schools that follow, difficulties are raised against them from which this school is free; for that reason the majority adopted it rather than any other.

The second school — held by al-Farrāʾ —: «أشياء» is the plural of «شيء», and the original of «شيء» is «شَيِّئ» on the pattern «فَيْعِل», like «لَيِّن»; then it was lightened to «شيء», just as they lightened «لَيِّن», «هَيِّن» and «مَيِّت» to «لَيْن», «هَيْن» and «مَيْت». Then he pluralized it after its lightening; its original is «أَشْيِئاء», with two hamzas with an alif between them, after a yāʾ, on the pattern «أَفْعِلاء». So two hamzas met — the lām of the word and the one of femininity — and the alif resembles the hamza, and the plural is heavy; so they lightened the word by changing the first hamza into a yāʾ because of the kasra before it, so two yāʾs met, the first of them with kasra; then they deleted the yāʾ that is the ʿayn (second radical) of the word for lightness, so it became «أَشْياء», and its pattern now, after the deletion, is «أَفْلاء»; and its being a diptote is because of the alif of femininity. [Translator's note: the source has «بعد الخلاف» ("after the disagreement"), apparently a slip for «بعد الحذف» ("after the deletion"); rendered by the latter sense.] This is the method of some, such as Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, in the morphological analysis of this school. Others, such as Abū al-Baqāʾ, said: when it became «أَشْيئاء», the second hamza, which is the lām of the word, was deleted, since it was through it that the heaviness arose, and the yāʾ with kasra was given fatḥa so that the alif of the plural would remain sound; so its pattern became «أَفْعاء».

The third school — held by al-Akhfash —: «أَشْياء» is the plural of «شَيْء» on the pattern of «فَلْس», i.e. not lightened from «شَيِّئ» as al-Farrāʾ says, but the plural of «شيء». He said that «فَعْل» is pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء», so it became «أَشْيِئاء» with two hamzas with an alif between them, after a yāʾ; then what was done in the school of al-Farrāʾ was done to it. [Translator's note: the source has «مذهب الفقراء», an evident misprint for «مذهب الفراء»; rendered accordingly.] The two methods mentioned from Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ in the morphological analysis of this school apply here too. Most authors report the school of al-Farrāʾ as being his and al-Akhfash's. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ, al-Akhfash and al-Ziyādī said: the pattern of «أَشْياء» is «أَفْعِلاء», and its original is «أَشْيِئاء», like «هيِّن» and «أَهْوِناء», but it was lightened," then he gave the morphological analysis of the word to the end. And Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: the original of the word is «شَيِّئ» like «هَيِّن», then it was lightened by deletion," and he gave the analysis to the end. So these transmitted their two schools as a single thing, and the truth is what I have reported from them. What I have said is indicated by what al-Wāḥidī said, for he said: "Al-Farrāʾ in this word followed the school of al-Akhfash," except that he confused matters when he claimed that it is like «هَيْن» and «لَيْن», which were pluralized on «أَهْوناء» and «أَلْيِناء»; for «هَيْن» is a lightening of «هيِّن», and for that reason its pluralization on «أَفْعِلاء» was permissible, whereas «شَيء» is not lightened from «شَيِّئ» so as to be pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء».

These two schools — I mean the school of al-Farrāʾ and of al-Akhfash — although they are free from [positing] diptote status without a cause, have been rejected by people. Al-Zajjāj said: "This view is a mistake, because «شَيْء» is «فَعْل», and «فَعْل» is not pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء». As for «هَيِّن» and «لَيِّن», their original is «هَيين» and «لَيين», so they were pluralized [on] «أَفْعِلاء», just as «فعيل» is pluralized on «أَفْعِلاء», like «نصيب» and «أَنْصباء»." I say: this is very strange — I mean his making the original of «هيّن» to be «هَيين» on the pattern «فَعِيل», and likewise «لَيّن» and «لَيِين»; that is why he explicitly likened them to «نصيب». People say that the original of «هَيِّن» is «هَيْوِن», as the original of «ميِّت» is «مَيْوِت», then it underwent the well-known weakening; and the original of «لَيّن» is «لَيْيِن» with two yāʾs, the first with sukūn and the second with kasra, and the first was assimilated. Derivation supports them, for «الهيِّن» is from «هانَ يهون», and because when they pluralized it on «أَفْعلاء» they made the wāw appear, saying «أَهْوِناء».

Al-Zajjāj said: "Al-Māzinī debated al-Akhfash on this question, and said to him: 'How do you form the diminutive of «أشياء»?' He said: 'I say «أُشَيَّاء».' Al-Māzinī said: 'If it were «أَفْعال» [i.e. a broken plural], it would be returned in the diminutive to its singular, and one would say «شُيَيْئات», like «شُعَيْعات». And the consensus of the Basrans is that the diminutive of «أصدقاء», if it is for feminines, is «صُدَيِّقات», and if for masculines, «صُدَيِّقون».' And al-Akhfash was silenced." [Translator's note: the source reads «لو كانت أَفْعالاً» ("if it were afʿāl"), although al-Akhfash's claimed pattern is «أَفْعِلاء»; the forms «شُيَئْات» and «صُدّيَّقات» are spelled thus in the source and are rendered by the evident forms.]

I say: the elaboration of this is that when a broken plural is put into the diminutive, it is either one of the plurals of paucity — which are four on the correct view: «أَفْعِلة», «أَفْعُل», «أَفْعال» and «فِعْلة» — in which case it is put into the diminutive on its own form; or it is one of the plurals of multitude, in which case it is not put into the diminutive on its own form, on the correct view — and if anything of that occurs it is counted anomalous, like «أُصَيْلان», the diminutive of «أُصْلان», the plural of «أَصيل» — but rather it is returned to its singular. Then, if it denotes non-rational beings, it is put into the diminutive and pluralized with alif and tāʾ, so you say in the diminutive of «حُمُر», the plural of «حمار»: «حُمَيْرات»; and if it denotes rational beings, it is put into the diminutive and pluralized with wāw and nūn, so you say in the diminutive of «رجال»: «رُجَيْلون». And if it is an ism jamʿ (collective noun) like «قوم» and «رهط», or an ism jins (generic noun) like «قمر» and «شجر», it is put into the diminutive on its own form like all other singulars.

Returning to «أشياء»: their forming its diminutive on its own form indicates that it is an ism jamʿ, because the ism jamʿ is put into the diminutive on its own form, as in «رُهَيْط» and «قُوَيْم»; and it is not a broken plural, since it would be one of the plurals of multitude and it was not returned to its singular. This binds al-Akhfash because he is a Basran, and a Basran must do that; and «أُصَيْلان» is anomalous with him, so no analogy is drawn from it. In Makkī's wording he said: "Moreover, it binds them to form the diminutive of «أشياء» as «شُوَيَّات» or as «شُيَيْئات», and no one has said that." I say: his saying «شُوَيَّات» is not good, for this is not a place for changing yāʾ into wāw; do you not see that when you form the diminutive of «بيت» you say «بُيَيْت», not «بُوَيْت»? Except that the Kufans permit that, so he may hold their view.

Makkī also rejected the school of al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash by two things. The first: it entails the absence of a parallel, since «أَفْعِلاء» has not occurred as the plural of «فَيْعِل» such that this would be its parallel; and «هَيّن» with «أهْوناء» is anomalous, and no analogy is drawn from it. The second: that its deletion and weakening are carried out not according to rule. "So this view goes outside both analogy and transmitted usage in its pluralization and its weakening."

The fourth school — the view of al-Kisāʾī and Abū Ḥātim —: it is the plural of «شيء» on «أَفْعال», like «بَيْت» and «أبيات», and «ضيف» and «أضياف». People objected to this view that it entails diptote status without its cause, since if it were on «أَفْعال» it would be fully declinable like «أبيات». Al-Zajjāj said: "The Basrans and most of the Kufans agreed that al-Kisāʾī's view is wrong, and they bound him to make «أنباء» and «أسماء» diptotes." I say: al-Kisāʾī sensed this rebuttal and excused himself from it, but with what is not acceptable. Al-Kisāʾī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "It — i.e. «أَشْياء» — is on the pattern «أَفْعال», but it became frequent in speech and so resembled «فَعْلاء», and was made a diptote just as «حَمْراء» is a diptote." He said: "And they pluralized it as «أَشاوَى», just as they pluralized «عَذْراء» as «عذارى» and «صَحْراء» as «صحارى»; and as «أَشْياوات», just as «حَمْراوات» is said." He means that they treated «أَشْياء», although it is on «أفعال», in the manner of «حَمْراء» and «عَذْراء» in both the broken and the sound plurals.

However, al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj objected to this excuse. Al-Farrāʾ said: "If it were as he said, the more fitting of the two options would be that it be declined (tujrā), because when a word becomes frequent in speech it becomes light and may be declined, just as naming with «يزيد» became frequent and they declined it when indefinite, though it has an augment yāʾ that prevents declension." I say: by «الإجراء» he means full declension (al-ṣarf). And al-Zajjāj said: "The Basrans and most of the Kufans agreed…", which was given just above. Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd said: it — i.e. «أشياء» — is a diptote because it resembled «حمراء», since the Arabs say «أَشْياوات» just as they say «حَمْراوات»." He said: "And it binds them both not to decline, in the plural, «أسماء» and «أبناء», given the Arabs' saying of them: «أسماوات» and «أبناوات»." I say: the explanation of this has been given. Then Makkī, after mentioning from al-Kisāʾī what I have given, and transmitting the school of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ, said: "Abū Ḥātim said: «أَشْياء» is «أَفْعال», the plural of «شيء», like «أبيات»." This gives the impression that the school of al-Kisāʾī given earlier is other than this school; but it is not so — rather it is the very same.

I say: some answered on behalf of al-Kisāʾī that the grammarians, in the chapter of diptotes, took into account formal resemblance rather than resemblance in meaning. This is indicated by the question of «سراويل» in the dialect of those who make it a diptote, for there are two interpretations of it, one of them being that it is a foreign singular treated like its counterpart in pattern in Arabic, i.e. the form «مصابيح», for example. It is also indicated by their treating the shortened alif of ilḥāq (assimilation to a pattern) like the shortened alif of femininity, but together with proper-name status; so they took into account mere outward form. Were it not for fear of prolixity, I would mention many parallels to it.

The fifth school: its pattern is also «أَفْعِلاء», as the plural of «شَيِيء» on the pattern of «ظريف»; and «فَعيل» is pluralized on «أَفعلاء», like «نَصيب» and «أنْصِباء», and «صَدِيق» and «أَصْدقاء». Then the first hamza, which is the lām of the word, was deleted, and the yāʾ was given fatḥa so that the alif of the plural would remain sound, so it became «أَشْياء», and its pattern after the deletion is «أَفْعاء». Makkī made it, in morphology, like the morphological analysis of the school of al-Akhfash, inasmuch as the hamza is changed into a yāʾ and then one of the two yāʾs is deleted. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: "The deletion in the plural was made acceptable by its deletion in the singular; and it was deleted from the singular only for lightness, because of frequency of use, since «شيء» applies to every named thing, whether accident, substance or body; so it was made a diptote in the plural because of the hamza of femininity." [Translator's note: the source reads «فلم ينصرف همزةِ التأنيث», evidently missing «لـ» ("because of"); rendered by the evident sense.] He said: "And this is a good view, consistent in the plural, and its being a diptote is according to rule — were it not that the diminutive objects to it, as it objected to al-Akhfash." I say: his saying "this is a good view" is open to question, because of the many objections raised against it, which is evident from what has preceded.

When the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] mentioned this school, he said in its morphological analysis: "Then the first hamza was deleted and the yāʾ of prolongation was given fatḥa because what follows it is an alif." He said: "Its pattern on this view became «أفياء», and on the view before it «أَفْلاء»." So I saw it written «أفياء» with a yāʾ, and this is a gross mistake; then I allowed that this may be a mistake made against him by the copyist, and that it was originally «أَفْعاء» with ʿayn, which the copyist misspelled as «أَفْياء». [Translator's note: the quoted words «ألى أفياء» and «إلا أَفْلاء» in the source evidently stand for «إلى أفياء» and «إلى أَفْلاء» ("became …"); rendered accordingly.]

People rejected this view on the grounds that [the claim] that the original of «شيء» is «شَيِيء» on the pattern of «صديق» is a claim without proof, and that [on it] it ought not to be put into the diminutive on its own form but returned to its singular, as was set out above.

The upshot of the discussion of «أشياء»: is it an ism jamʿ, whose original is «شَيْئاء» like «طَرْفاء», then its lām was transposed before its fāʾ so that its pattern became «لَفْعاء»; or is it an explicit plural? And if it is said to be an explicit plural, is its original «أَفْعِلاء», which then undergoes deletion and becomes «أَفْعاء» or «أَفْلاء»; or is its pattern «أفعال» like «أبيات»? Were it not for fear of departing from the purpose, I would have mentioned the question with all its aspects in full; but in this there is a sufficiency befitting this place. [Translator's note: the source has «خلف» and «متسوفاة», evidently for «خوف» and «مستوفاة».]

His saying, Exalted is He: {إِن تُبْدَ}: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «تَسُؤكم». This conditional clause is in the position of a genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «أشياء», and likewise the conjoined conditional clause too. Ibn ʿAbbās read «إن تَبْدُ لكم تَسُؤْكم» with both verbs in the active, the imperfect prefix being tāʾ, with the fāʿil (agent) being the pronoun of «أشياء». [Translator's note: the source has the garbled spelling «تَبءدُ»; rendered as «تَبْدُ».] Al-Shaʿbī read — according to what Abū Muḥammad ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted from him — {إنْ يَبْدُ} with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the dāl, and «يَسُؤْكم» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the fāʿil being a pronoun referring back to whatever is fitting to supply according to the meaning, i.e. "if your asking, or what you ask for, appears to you, it will grieve you." It cannot refer back to «أشياء», because that is treated as a metaphorical feminine, and whenever a verb is attributed to a feminine pronoun of any kind, the attachment of the [feminine] marker is obligatory on the correct view, and no attention is paid to poetic necessity. Others transmitted from al-Shaʿbī that he read {يُبْدَ لكم يَسُؤْكم} with yāʾ in both, except that he gave ḍamma to the first yāʾ and fatḥa to the second; the meaning being: "if the asking about them is made manifest (يُبْدَ), i.e. appears, that asking will grieve you," i.e. its answer, or the asking itself, because it is a cause of that; and the one who makes manifest is Allah the Exalted. [Translator's note: the source has «سببٌ في لك», evidently for «سبب في ذلك».]

The pronoun in «عنها» may refer back to the kind of things that were forbidden, not to those very things; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and al-Wāḥidī transmitted it from the author of "al-Naẓm", who gave as a parallel His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان مِن سُلاَلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ} [al-Muʾminūn: 12], meaning Ādam, "then We made him" — he said: meaning the son of Ādam; so the pronoun referred back to what the first indicated. And it may refer back to those very things; al-Zamakhsharī said something to that effect.

His saying: {حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ القرآن}: there are two possibilities for this adverb. The first — which is the apparent one, and al-Zamakhsharī said nothing else —: it is accusative by «تسألوا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "'And if you ask about them' — about these hard obligations — 'when the Quran is being sent down' — in the time of revelation, which is as long as the Messenger is among you receiving revelation — 'they will be shown to you,' those obligations which grieve you and which you are commanded to bear, and so you expose yourselves to Allah's anger through your neglect of them." From here I said to you that the pronoun in «عنها» refers back to the first «أشياء», not to their kind. The second: the adverb is accusative by «تُبْدَ لكم», i.e. "those things will appear to you at the time of the Quran's descent." [Translator's note: the source has «لتك», evidently for «تلك» ("those").]

Some said: "There is fronting and postponement in the speech, because the implied order is: about things which, if you ask about them, will be shown to you at the time of the Quran's descent, and if they are shown to you, will grieve you." There is no doubt that the meaning is according to this order; except that this is not to be called fronting and postponement, for the wāw does not entail sequence, so there is no difference. Rather, this was only placed first before His saying {وَإِن تَسْأَلُواْ} for a benefit, namely deterrence from asking: He first told them that their asking about things which, whenever they appear, would grieve them, before informing them that if they asked about them they would be shown to them, so that they would be deterred; and that is a fitting meaning.

His saying: {عَفَا الله عَنْهَا}: there are two views on it. The first: it is in the position of a genitive, because it is another naʿt of «أشياء»; on this view the pronoun in «عنها» refers back to «أشياء». There is no need to claim fronting and postponement here, as some did, who said: "Its implied form is: do not ask about things which Allah has pardoned, which if they are shown to you… to the end of the verse"; for each of the two conditional clauses, and this clause, is a naʿt of «أشياء», so from where [does it follow] that this clause deserves to be placed before what precedes it? It is as though this speaker only supposed it to be fronted in order to make clear that it is a naʿt and not resumptive. The second: it has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive; on this view the pronoun in «عنها» refers back to the question indicated by «لا تَسْألوا», and it may refer back to «أشياء» — whereas on the first view this is required, by the necessity of a link between the naʿt and what it qualifies.

His saying, Exalted is He: {قَدْ سَأَلَهَا}: the pronoun in «سألها» apparently refers back to «أشياء». But al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did He say 'do not ask about things' and then say «قد سَألَها» and not 'asked about them' (سألَ عنها)? I say: [the pronoun in «سألها»] does not refer back to «أشياء» such that it would be made transitive to it by «عن»; rather it refers back to the question (المسألة) indicated by His saying «لا تَسْألوا», i.e. a people asked the question, then became disbelievers by it — i.e. by what it led to." Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed his approach. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Their statement is only tenable with the omission of a muḍāf, and some exegetes stated it explicitly, i.e. 'asked the like of it,' i.e. the like of this question, or the like of these questions." [Translator's note: the source has «ولا يتجه قولُهما إلى حذف مضاف» ("…is not directed to the omission of a muḍāf"), apparently «إلا على حذف مضاف»; and «أي: قال سأل أمثالَها» has a superfluous «قال»; rendered by the evident sense.]

And al-Ḥawfī said about «سألها»: "The apparent sense is that the pronoun refers back to «أشياء», but taking it according to its apparent sense is untenable, neither from the side of Arabic wording nor from the side of meaning. As for the side of wording: it ought to have been made transitive by «عن», as it was made transitive in the first instance. As for the side of meaning: the thing asked about is decisively different, for their asking is other than the asking of those before them. The asking of these people was like one who asked: 'Where is my she-camel?', 'What is in my she-camel's belly?', 'Where is my father?' and 'Where will I enter?' And the asking of those [earlier people] was other than this, such as: {أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً} [al-Māʾida: 114], {أَرِنَا الله جَهْرَةً} [al-Nisāʾ: 153], {اجعل لَّنَآ إلها} [al-Aʿrāf: 138] and the like."
[Translator's note: the source reads «وأين أبي» ("where is my father"); in the well-known reports the question was "who is my father?".]

And al-Wāḥidī said, transmitting from al-Jurjānī: "This asking in the verses differs from the meaning of asking in His saying {لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ} {وَإِن تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْهَا}. Do you not see that the asking in the first verse was made transitive by the preposition, while here it was not made transitive by the preposition? That is because the asking here is a request for the thing itself, as in «سَأَلْتُك درهماً» ('I asked you for a dirham'), i.e. I requested it from you; whereas the asking in the first verse is an asking about the state of the thing and its manner. He only conjoined His saying {قَدْ سَأَلَهَا قَوْمٌ} to what precedes it, although it is not like it in interpretation, because He was forbidding them from burdening themselves with what they had not been charged with, and which had been lifted from them."

I say: it may refer back to «أشياء» in wording, not in meaning, just as the grammarians said in the case of «عندي درهمٌ ونصفُه» ("I have a dirham and half of it"), i.e. and half of another dirham. And of this kind is:
181 - 4- وكلُّ أُناسٍ قاربوا قَيْدَ فَحْلِهِمْ ... ونحنُ خَلَعْنا قيدَه فَهْوَ سارِبُ
(Every people kept their stallion's tether short, but we cast off its tether, so it roams free.)

His saying: {مِّن قَبْلِكُم} is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying {سَأَلَهَا}. If it is said: may it be a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم»? I say: a group prohibited that, giving as their reason that an adverb of time does not occur as a khabar (predicate), a naʿt or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of a concrete entity (al-jutha). Something like this was given to you earlier at the beginning of al-Baqara, at His saying {والذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} [verse 21], for the ṣila (relative clause) is like the naʿt. And «بها» is attached to «كافرين»; it was only placed first for the sake of the verse-endings (al-fawāṣil).

And al-Nakhaʿī read «سالها» with imāla (inclination of the vowel) and without hamza; these are two dialects, and from this is «يَتَساولان». His applying imāla to «سأل» is like Ḥamza's imāla of «خاف». The verification of that was given earlier in al-Baqara at {فَإِنَّ لَكُمْ مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ} [verse 61] and {سَلْ بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} [verse 211].

His saying, Exalted is He: {مِن بَحِيرَةٍ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), because the two well-known conditions are present. And «جَعَلَ» may be in the sense of «سَمَّى» (to name), transitive to two objects, one of them omitted, the implied form being: "Allah did not make — i.e. did not name — any animal a baḥīra." Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is in the sense of «شَرَعَ» (to legislate) and «وضع» (to lay down), i.e. Allah did not legislate it nor command it." Al-Wāḥidī said, after a long discussion: "So the meaning of 'Allah did not make any baḥīra' is: He did not make it obligatory nor command it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«جَعَلَ» in this verse cannot be in the sense of «خلق» (to create), because Allah created all of these things; nor in the sense of «صَيَّر» (to make into), because making-into requires a second object. So its meaning is: Allah did not institute nor legislate." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected all these transmitted views, on the grounds that the lexicographers did not count «شرع» among the meanings of «جَعَل»; he explained the verse as making-into (taṣyīr), with the second object omitted, i.e. "Allah did not make a baḥīra something legislated."

And «البَحيرة» is on the pattern «فَعِيلة» in the sense of «مَفْعولة» (passive), so the entry of the tāʾ of femininity on it is not according to rule; but since it came to be treated like non-derived nouns, it was made feminine. I have clarified this at His saying {والنطيحة} [al-Māʾida: 3]. Its derivation is from «البَحْر», and «البَحْر» is breadth (السَّعَة); from it is «بَحْرُ الماءِ» (the sea), because of its breadth.

The lexicographers disagreed greatly about what the baḥīra was among the Arabs. Abū ʿUbayd said: "It is the she-camel that has borne five litters, the last of them a male; then her ear is slit and she is left alone, so she is not ridden, not milked, and not driven away from pasture or water; and if an exhausted traveller met her he would not ride her." This was related from Ibn ʿAbbās, except that he did not mention a male at the end. Some said: "When the she-camel had borne five litters, they looked at the fifth: if it was a male they slaughtered it and ate it; and if it was a female they slit her ear and left her to graze and come to water, not ridden and not milked; this is the baḥīra." This was related from Qatāda. Some said: "The baḥīra is the female that is the fifth litter, as explained above, except that its flesh and its milk are not lawful for women; if she dies, she becomes lawful for them." Some said: "The baḥīra is the daughter of the sāʾiba" — the explanation of the sāʾiba will come — "so when the sāʾiba bore a female, they slit her ear and left her with her mother to graze and come to water, not ridden even by an exhausted traveller." This is the view of Mujāhid ibn Jabr. [Translator's note: the source has «ولا تكرب» for «ولا تُركب», and «وسأتي» for «وسيأتي»; rendered by the evident sense.] Some said: "It is the one whose flow — i.e. its milk — was withheld for the sake of the false gods (al-ṭawāghīt), so no one milks her." Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab held this. It was said: it is the one left in the pasture without a herdsman; Ibn Sīda said this. It was said: when she bore five females, they slit her ear and left her. Some said — and it is attributed to Masrūq —: "When she bore five or seven, they slit her ear." And it was said: "It is the she-camel that bears ten litters; then her ear is slit lengthwise into two halves, and she is left, not ridden, not milked, and not driven away from pasture or water; and when she dies her flesh is lawful for men but not for women." Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted this, and Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāghib said the same.

And it was said: the baḥīra is the male calf (السِّقْب): when it was born they slit its ear and said: "O Allah, if it lives then it is one kept as property (قَنِيّ), and if it dies then it is slaughtered (ذَكِيّ)"; and when it died they ate it. [Translator's note: the source reads «نحروا أذنه» ("they slaughtered its ear"), apparently a slip for «بحروا أذنه» ("they slit its ear"); rendered by the latter sense.] The way to reconcile these many views is that the Arabs differed in their practices regarding the baḥīra.

As for the sāʾiba, it was said: when a man returned from a journey, or [wished to] give thanks for a blessing, he set a camel loose (سَيَّب), so it was not ridden, and what was mentioned for the baḥīra was done with it; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd. It was said: it is the she-camel that bears ten females, so she is not ridden and none drinks her milk except a guest or a child; al-Farrāʾ said this. It was said: it is what was left for their gods; a man would bring his livestock to the custodians (al-sadana) and leave it with them, and its milk would flow. It was said: it is the she-camel left so that a pilgrimage might be made on her; that was transmitted from al-Shāfiʿī. And it was said: it is the slave who is freed on condition that there be no walāʾ (clientage), no ʿaql (blood-money liability) and no inheritance attaching to him.

And «السائِبَة» here admits two views. The first: it is an active participle in its proper sense, from «ساب يَسِيب», i.e. to roam freely, like the flowing of water; and it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «سِبْتُه»; one says «سَيَّبْتُه فساب وانساب» ("I set it loose, so it went loose and roamed"). The second: it is in the sense of a passive participle, as in «عيشةٌ راضية» ("a pleasing life," lit. "a pleased life"); but the occurrence of «فاعِل» in the sense of «مَفْعول» is very rare, as in «ماء دافق» ("gushing water"). What ought to be said is that it is «فاعل» in the sense of "possessor of such-and-such," i.e. in the sense of relation (nasab), as in their saying «لابن», i.e. "possessor of milk"; and from it, on one of the two views, are «عيشةٌ راضية» and «ماء دافق», i.e. "possessing contentment" and "possessing gushing"; and likewise this one, i.e. "possessing roaming (سَيْب)."

And «الوصيلة» here is on the pattern «فَعِيلة» in the sense of «فاعِلة» (active), according to the explanation that will come, so the entry of the tāʾ is according to rule. The lexicographers disagreed about it: is it of the kind of sheep and goats, or of the kind of camels? Then they also disagreed after that. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the ewe that bears seven litters, two female kids at a time; and when at the last of them she bore a female kid and a male kid, it was said: 'she has joined her brother (وصلت أخاها),' so she was treated like the sāʾiba." Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the ewe: when she bore a male it was for their gods, and when she bore a female it was for them." Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It is the ewe that bears seven litters; if the seventh was a female, the women derived no benefit from it at all, unless it died, in which case the men and the women ate it; if it was a male they slaughtered it and all ate it; and if it was a male and a female, they said: 'she has joined her brother,' so they left her with him, not slaughtered, and none but the men, not the women, benefited from her; if she died, the women shared in her with the men." Ibn Qutayba said: "If the seventh was a male it was slaughtered and the men, not the women, ate it, and they said: 'Exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives'; if it was a female she was left among the flock; and if it was a male and a female, then it is as in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās." And it was said: "It is the ewe that bears ten females in succession in five litters; then whatever she bore after that was for the males, not the females." Abū Isḥāq and Abū ʿUbayda held this, except that Abū ʿUbayda said: "And when she bore a male and a female together, they said: 'she has joined her brother,' so they did not slaughter him because of her."

And it was said: it is the ewe that bears five litters, or three; if it was a male kid they slaughtered it, if it was a female they kept her, and if it was a male and a female they said: "she has joined her brother." All of this is according to those who restrict it to the kind of sheep and goats. As for those who said it is of camels, they said: "It is the she-camel that bears a female as her first offspring, then follows it with the birth of another female with no male between them, so they leave her for their gods, and say: 'she has joined a female to a female with no male between them.'" [Translator's note: the source has «أنهى», an evident misprint for «أنثى» ("a female"); rendered accordingly.]

And «الحامي» is an active participle from «حَمَى يَحْمي», i.e. to protect/withhold. The lexicographers' explanation of it differs. From al-Farrāʾ: "It is the stallion to whose offspring's offspring a foal is born; then they say: 'he has protected his back,' so he is not ridden, not used, and not driven away from water or trees." Some said: "It is the stallion from whose offspring, males and females, ten females are produced"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya related that. [Translator's note: the source has «من يبن», an evident misprint for «من بين» ("from among").] Some said: "It is the stallion from whose loins ten litters are born; then they say: 'he has protected his back,' and they leave him like the sāʾiba as described above." This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd, and Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj inclined to it. It was related from al-Shāfiʿī that it is the stallion that covers in its owner's herd for ten years. And Ibn Zayd said: "It is the stallion for which seven females are produced in succession; then he protects his back and what was described above is done with him."

You have now learned the origin of the lexicographers' disagreement about these things: it is due to the differences among the practices of the Arabs and their corrupt opinions concerning them.

They recited concerning the baḥīra the saying [of the poet]:
184 - 5- مُحَرَّمَةٌ لا يَطْعَمُ الناسُ لحمَها ... ولا نحن في شيءٍ كذاك البحائرُ
(Made inviolable — people do not taste their flesh, nor do we in any way; such are the baḥāʾir.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed «184» in the source, while the neighbouring verses are numbered «181»; it is kept as written.]

And he recited concerning the sāʾiba the saying [of the poet]:
181 - 6- وسائبةٍ لله مالي تشكُّرا ... إنِ اللهُ عافَى عامراً أو مجاشعا
(My property shall be a sāʾiba for Allah, in thanksgiving, if Allah grants well-being to ʿĀmir or Mujāshiʿ.)

They recited concerning the waṣīla [a verse] of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
181 - 7- أجِدَّك أمَّا كنت في الناسِ ناعقاً ... تراعي بأَعْلى ذي المجازِ الوَصايلا
(By your earnestness! Were you not among people one who shouts at the flock, tending the waṣāʾil on the heights of Dhū al-Majāz?)

And they recited concerning the ḥāmī the saying [of the poet]:
181 - 8- حَماها أبو قابوسَ في عِزِّ ملكِه ... كما قد حَمَى أولادَ أولادهِ الفحلُ
(Abū Qābūs protected it in the might of his kingship, as the stallion has protected the offspring of his offspring.)

His saying, Exalted is He: {عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ}: the majority read «أنفسكم» in the accusative, and it is accusative by way of ighrāʾ (incitement) through «عليكم», because «عليكم» here is an ism fiʿl (verbal noun of command), the implied form being "keep to yourselves," i.e. to their guidance and their protection from what harms them. So «عليكم» here governs a fāʿil (agent) in the nominative, its implied form being "عليكم أنتم"; for that reason a nominative may be conjoined to it, as in «عليكم أنتم وزيدٌ الخيرَ» ("keep, you and Zayd, to the good"), as though you said: "keep, you and Zayd, to the good." [Translator's note: the source has «الزموا أنتم زيدٌ الخيرَ» without the conjunctive wāw; rendered as «وزيدٌ».]

The grammarians disagreed about the pronoun attached to it and its sisters, such as «إليك», «لديك» and «مكانك». The correct view is that it is in the position of a genitive (majrūr), as it was before the word was transferred to ighrāʾ; this is the school of Sībawayh. Al-Akhfash argued for it by what he related from the Arabs: «على عبدِ الله» with «عبد الله» in the genitive, and that is decisive on the question. Al-Kisāʾī held that it is in the position of an accusative, and this is far-fetched because of the accusative of what comes after the two of them — I mean «على» and what follows it — as in this verse. Al-Farrāʾ held that it is in the position of a nominative. I have verified these schools with their proofs at length in "Sharḥ al-Tashīl".

Abū al-Baqāʾ said — after making «كم» in the position of a genitive governed by «على» —: "unlike «رُوَيدَكم», for the kāf there is for address and has no position, since «رويد» has been used for the imperative addressed to someone present without the kāf of address; and likewise His saying, Exalted is He, {مَكَانَكُمْ} [Yūnus: 28]: «كم» is in the position of a genitive." I say: there is long discussion on this question; the correct view is that «رويد» sometimes has what follows it in the position of a genitive and sometimes in the position of an accusative, and this is not its place. I have presented earlier, in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, the disagreement over the permissibility of placing the governed word of this category before it.

Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym read «أنفسُكم» in the nominative, according to what the author of "al-Kashshāf" related from him. It is problematic, and it is explained on one of two views. Either as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «عليكم» as its khabar (predicate) placed before it, the meaning still being that of ighrāʾ, since ighrāʾ has come in the form of a nominal clause; of this kind is the reading of some {ناقةُ الله وسُقْياها} [al-Shams: 13], and this is a warning (taḥdhīr), which is the counterpart of ighrāʾ. The second of the two views: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «عليكم», because, as stated earlier, it stands in the place of the verb; except that emphasizing it with «النفس» without emphasizing it with a detached pronoun is anomalous. On this view the object is omitted, its implied form being "keep, you yourselves, to the soundness of your state and your guidance."

His saying: {لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the doubled rāʾ. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read {لا يَضُرْكم} with ḍamma on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read {لا يَضِرْكم} with kasra on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ; and Abū Ḥaywa read {لا يَضْرُرُكم} with sukūn on the ḍād and ḍamma on the first and second rāʾ.

As for the reading of the majority, it admits two views. The first: that the verb in it is jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the command in «عليكم», and the rāʾ was given ḍamma only in harmony with the ḍamma of the ḍād; and the ḍamma of the ḍād is the vowel of the first rāʾ, transferred to the ḍād for the sake of assimilating it into the rāʾ after it, the original being {لا يَضْرُرْكم}. And the jussive may be not by way of being the answer to the command, but by way of being a resumptive prohibition, the working of it being as stated. Supporting the permissibility of the jussive here, in both senses mentioned — answer and prohibition — are the readings of al-Ḥasan and al-Nakhaʿī, for both are explicit in the jussive, though they admit the jussive either as answer or as prohibition.

The second view: that the verb is indicative (marfūʿ), being neither an answer nor a prohibition, but resumptive, brought to give information of that; it is supported by the reading of Abū Ḥaywa mentioned above.

As for the reading of al-Ḥasan, it is from {ضارَه يَضُوره}, like «صانَه يصونه»; and the reading of al-Nakhaʿī is from {ضاره يضيره}, like «باعه يَبيعه» [Translator's note: the source has «كباعة»]; and the jussive in both is according to the two views stated for the reading of the generality. Abū al-Baqāʾ related «لا يَضُرَّكم» with fatḥa on the rāʾ; its explanation is as a jussive, the fatḥa being for lightness, and that is clear, the jussive likewise being according to the two views stated. All of these are dialects to which attention was drawn earlier in Āl ʿImrān.

And {مَّن ضَلَّ} is the fāʿil (agent). And «إذا» is an adverb governed in the accusative by «يَضُرُّكم», i.e. "the one who has gone astray does not harm you at the time of your being guided." It may also be conditional, its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being omitted because the speech indicates it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is unlikely that it is an adverb of «ضَلَّ», because the meaning is not sound with it." I say: because the meaning would become a negation of the harm coming from one who goes astray at the time of their being guided, and it might then be imagined that it does not negate for them the harm of one who went astray at a time other than that of their being guided; but this does not negate the soundness of the meaning altogether, as he stated.

His saying, Exalted is He: {شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ}: this verse and those after it are among the most difficult in the Quran in ruling, i'rab and exegesis. Scholars have never ceased to find them difficult and to shrink back from them, so much so that Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book called al-Kashf: "This verse, in its reading, its i'rab, its exegesis, its meanings and its rulings, is among the hardest and most difficult verses in the Quran." He said: "What it contains of the sciences could be expounded in thirty leaves or more." He said: "We have mentioned it with commentary in a separate book." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is the speech of one who did not attain certainty (lit. 'the coolness') in its exegesis, and that is evident from his book." Al-Sakhāwī said: "I have not seen any of the scholars whose discussion of it came out clear from its beginning to its end." Al-Wāḥidī said: "This verse and those after it are among the most abstruse things in the Quran in meaning and i'rab." I say: I seek the help of Allah the Exalted in explaining its i'rab, the derivation of its individual words, the morphology of its words, its readings and the understanding of its composition — what pertains particularly to this work. As for the rest of its sciences, we ask Allah for help in refining them in my book "Tafsīr al-Qurʾān al-ʿAzīz", if Allah wills; and with Him is all power and strength.

The majority read {شهادةُ بينكم} with «شهادة» nominative, annexed to «بينكم». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and al-Shaʿbī read it nominative with tanwīn, and «بينَكم» accusative. Al-Sulamī, and al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj in one transmission from them, read «شهادةً» with tanwīn in the accusative, and «بينَكم» accusative.

As for the reading of the majority, there are five views in explaining it. [Translator's note: the source has «تخريجهما» ("the explanation of the two of them") with a dual pronoun; rendered as "it".] The first: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is «اثنان». On this view the omission of a muḍāf is unavoidable, either from the first or from the second. Its implied form with [omission] from the first is: "the possessors of the testimony among you are two," i.e. the two holders of the testimony among you are two; and its implied form with [omission] from the second is: "the testimony among you is the testimony of two." We were only compelled to [posit] an omission from the first or the second so that mubtadaʾ and khabar would be true of one and the same thing, because testimony is an abstract notion while the two are concrete persons. The two analyses mentioned for the likes of «زيدٌ عدلٌ» ("Zayd is justice") — namely making him the very maṣdar for emphasis, or its standing for an active participle — do not apply here, because the meaning rejects them here. However, al-Wāḥidī transmitted from the author of "al-Naẓm" that he said: "«شهادة» is a maṣdar put in the place of nouns," meaning by the testimony the witnesses, just as one says «رجلٌ عَدْلٌ ورِضا» and «رجالٌ عدلٌ ورِضا وزَوْر»; "and if you take it in the sense of witnesses, it is on the omission of a muḍāf, and the meaning would be: the number of witnesses among you is two." He cited as evidence His saying {الحج أَشْهُرٌ} [al-Baqara: 197], i.e. the time of the Ḥajj: "were it not for that, «أشهر» would be accusative on the interpretation 'the Ḥajj is in months'." I say: on its apparent sense, he made the maṣdar the very witnesses for emphasis, and for that reason he illustrated it with «رجال عدل»; and this is open to question. [Translator's note: the source has «فعلى ظاهر»; probably «فالظاهر».]

The second: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ too, and its khabar is omitted, indicated by the context of the speech; on this view «اثنان» is nominative through the maṣdar, which is «شهادة», the implied form being: "among what has been prescribed for you is that two shall testify." Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it thus, and it is one of the two views of al-Zajjāj, and it is very apparent. On these two views «إذا» is an adverb of «شهادة», i.e. "that there be testimony at the time death — i.e. its causes — is present." And on these views «حين الوصية» admits three views. The most acceptable of them: it is a badal (substitute) from «إذا»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. He said: "In its substitution for it there is a proof that the bequest is obligatory." The second: it is accusative by «الموت» itself, i.e. death occurs at the time of the bequest; and it must be interpreted as the causes of death, because at the time of actual death there is no bequest. The third: it is accusative by «حَضَر», i.e. the causes of death are present at the time of the bequest.

The third [of the five views]: «شهادةُ» is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «إذا حضر», i.e. "the occurrence of the testimony is at the time of death's being present"; and «حين» is according to the three views just given concerning it.
