Bir görüşe göre ماد يميد yani 'hareket etti'den türemiştir; bu durumda kıyasa uygun ism-i fâildir ...» denilmektedir. (Alıntı bitti.)

* Fevâid:
1- «يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ» ...
Münâdâ «عيسى»nın i'rab harekesi nedir? Cevap: Nahivciler bu tür münâdâda iki vechi caiz görmüş ve şöyle demişlerdir:
Münâdâ müfred alem olur, arada bir ayırıcı olmaksızın ardından «ابن» gelir, sonra ابن de âyette olduğu gibi bir aleme muzâf olursa, onu «müfred alem» münâdâda olduğu gibi damme üzere mebnî kılabiliriz; nasb olan «ابن»in harekesine tâbi de kılabiliriz. Bunun örneği Amr b. Külsûm'un şu sözüdür:
بأي مشيئة عمرو بن هند ... تطيع بنا الوشاة وتزدرينا
(Ey Amr b. Hind, hangi irade iledir ki bizim hakkımızda koğucuları dinliyor ve bizi hor görüyorsun?)
Buna göre «عمرو» damme üzere mebnî sayılabileceği gibi, «ابن»in harekesi olan nasba tâbi olarak mansûb da sayılabilir: Düşün ... !

* Vocabulary:
(وفى) with a promise: wafāʾ; and أوفى به, īfāʾ: that is, he brought it complete, with nothing lacking. The poet combined the two:
أما ابن طوف فقد أوفى بذمته ... كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها
(As for Ibn Ṭawf, he has fulfilled his pledge, as the driver of the she-camels of the star fulfilled [his duty] toward them.)
Of one who does not give full measure it is said: أخسر الكيل ("he shorted the measure"); and of one who does not fulfil the covenant: غدر ("he betrayed") and نقض ("he broke"). And نقض the covenant and the promise are one and the same thing.
(العقود): the plural of عقد (with fatḥa on the first letter), a verbal noun used as a noun and then pluralised. It is the firmly bound covenant, likened to the tying (ʿaqd) of horses and the like. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم ... شدّوا العناج وشدّوا فوقها الكربا
(A people who, when they make a pact for their neighbour, tighten the cord and tighten the knots above it.)
In origin it is applied to solid bodies, such as the knot of a rope and the bonding of a building, and then it is borrowed for abstract things, such as the contract of sale, the covenant and the like. The ʿaqd is therefore more specific than the ʿahd (covenant); and what is meant by العقود is what they bind themselves to by contract.
(البهيمة): every four-legged creature on land and sea; and it was said: whatever has no speech, because of the indistinctness (ibhām) in its voice. But by common usage it is restricted to what is other than beasts of prey and birds. So said al-Rāghib. It is reported from al-Zajjāj that the bahīma, among animals, is whatever has no intellect at all. In al-Qāmūs: the bahīma is every creature with four legs even in water, or every living thing that does not discriminate; its plural is bahāʾim.
(الْأَنْعامِ): these are camels, cattle, sheep and goats, and buffaloes. The annexation of بهيمة to الأنعام is for clarification (li-l-bayān), like "the arāk tree" (شجر الأراك); that is: "the eating of the bahīma that is of the livestock has been made lawful for you". Some held that the annexation is in the sense of comparison, that is: "the bahīma that resembles the livestock has been made lawful for you"; it was said: in chewing the cud and in lacking fangs. It is better to say that the point of resemblance that necessitates lawfulness is that they are among the good things (ṭayyibāt), which are the basis of lawfulness. Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: "Among that is that they suppose الأنعام to mean النَّعَم; yet the Arabs distinguished between them, making النعم a name for camels specifically, or for the herd in which camels are, and making الأنعام a name for the kinds of livestock, so that some even included in it gazelles and wild asses, clinging to the saying of the Exalted: «أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام»." Al-Rāghib said: النعم is specific to camels, and its plural is أنعام. They were so named because they are among the greatest blessings (niʿam) in their eyes. But الأنعام is said of camels, cattle and sheep and goats, and it is not called أنعام unless camels are among its number." Ibn Barrī said: it is a case of predominance (taghlīb), since they gave النعم predominance over the rest; and there is in reality no difference between them, and it is all-inclusive.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to call for fulfilment of what the contract requires. The i'rab of the vocative has already been given. أوفوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; بالعقود is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا.
(أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ) The sentence is explicative, because it is a detailing after a general statement, on the basis that العقود includes all the rulings that Allah the Exalted has legislated and commanded those under obligation to fulfil. أحلت is a passive past verb; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحلت; وبهيمة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and الأنعام is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ) إلا is a particle of exception, and ما is the excepted. It was said: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), because the expression is not of the genus of the bahīma, and the prohibition is due to something that supervenes, such as death and the like. The sentence يتلى عليكم is the ṣila of the relative. غير is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم»; ومحلي is a muḍāf to «غير», and الصيد is a muḍāf ilayhi to «محلي». The sentence وأنتم حرم, of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl from «محلي الصيد», as if it were said: "We have made lawful for you some of the livestock while you refrain from game, being in iḥrām, so that there be no hardship upon you."
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ ما يُرِيدُ) The sentence gives the reason for the ruling. إن and its ism; the sentence يحكم is its khabar. ما may be a maṣdar particle or a relative, and in either case it is accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that is: "He rules by His will," or "by that which He wills"; and there is no frivolity in His rulings, nor any defect, nor any injustice.

* Benefits:
The scholars and exegetes expounded at length on what is meant by العقود. In our view it is general, comprising all the covenants of Allah that He entrusted to His servants, of acts of worship and dealings, by which the affairs of this world and the next are together ordered. Fine is the saying of al-Rāghib:
"Contracts, with regard to the thing contracted and the contracting party, are of three kinds: a contract between Allah the Exalted and the servant, a contract between the servant and himself, and a contract between the servant and others among mankind."
The jurists and the scholars of legislation have gone into it extensively, composing long works on it and treating the legal rulings relating to it, which are easy to consult in their proper places.

An eloquent sentence:
The foundation on which contracts rest in Islam is this eloquent, concise and meaningful sentence, «أوفوا بالعقود». It indicates, with force and grace, that every believer must fulfil what he has contracted and bound himself to, and that no one may restrict what the Lawgiver has left unrestricted except by a text from Him. Every saying or deed that people count as a contract is a contract that they must fulfil, as Allah the Exalted commanded, provided it does not involve forbidding what is lawful or permitting what is forbidden, of what is established in the Sharia, such as a contract under compulsion, or to burn someone's house or a tree in an orchard, or for an indecency, or to consume some of people's property wrongfully, such as usury, gambling and bribery [Translator's note: the source reads «والمسير»; «والميسر» (gambling) is meant].

Custom and mutual consent:
All worldly matters are ordered under this, such as sale, hire, partnerships and other worldly dealings. The basis in them is people's custom and their mutual consent, so long as it does not contradict a ruling of the Sharia. This is perfectly clear and firm. Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyya composed a book called «Madārik al-Qiyās» on the subject of contracts, in which he covered this subject exhaustively, supported by evidence from the Book, the Sunna and the reports of the righteous predecessors; let whoever wishes consult it.

A report on the philosopher al-Kindī:
They mention that the philosopher al-Kindī was told by his companions: "O sage, make for us the like of this Qur'an." He said: "Yes, I shall make the like of part of it." Then he withdrew for many days, and came out and said: "By Allah, I cannot, and no one can bear it. I opened the Mushaf and Sūrat al-Māʾida came out. I looked, and behold, it speaks of fulfilment, forbids breach of faith, makes lawful with a general permission, then makes an exception, then tells of His power and wisdom, in two lines. No one can produce the like of this except in volumes (ajlād)."
That is, in many large volumes.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ): resumptive speech introduced to set out what they did and what issued from some of them after the covenant was taken. (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted «اذكر» (remember); the address is to the Prophet, so that what issued from them may be recounted to him. The clause (قال موسى), of verb and fāʿil (agent), is in the position of genitive by annexation; (لقومه) is attached to (قال).
(يا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (يا) is a vocative particle; (قوم) is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (عليكم) is attached to (نعمة).
(إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِياءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكاً): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to «النعمة»; the clause (جعل) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (فيكم) is attached to (جعل) as being its first object «[Translator's note: so in the text; i.e. the prepositional phrase (فيكم) occupies the place of the first object]», and (أنبياء) is its second object; (وجعلكم ملوكا) is conjoined to what precedes, and (ملوكا) is a second object.
(وَآتاكُمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (آتاكم) is a verb and its first object, the agent being «هو»; (ما) is a relative noun, the second object; the clause (لم يؤت أحدا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (من العالمين) is attached to an omitted ṣila «[Translator's note: so in the text; it is more naturally an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحدا)]». What is meant by "the worlds" is the nations that had passed up to their time and the world of their time: [the favours] such as the creation of the sea «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «خلق البحر»; probably «فلق البحر» (the parting of the sea) is meant]», the shading by clouds, the manna and the quails, and other great matters.
(يا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ): the clause is resumptive; (ادخلوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (الأرض) is a direct object by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (ادخلوا); and (المقدسة) is a naʿt of (الأرض).
(الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): (التي) is a second adjective of (الأرض); the clause (كتب الله) is the ṣila; and (لكم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (كتب).
(وَلا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلى أَدْبارِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (ترتدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), the wāw being the agent; and (على أدباركم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (ترتدوا).
(فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تنقلبوا) is conjoined to (ترتدوا), so it is jussive like it. The fāʾ may also be the causative fāʾ (al-sababiyya), since a prohibition precedes it, so that [the verb] is accusative by an implied «أن» after it. (خاسرين) is a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
The vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker is of four kinds:
1- That which has one dialectal form: it is the word ending in a weak letter, yāʾ or alif; its yāʾ to which it is annexed must be retained and given fatḥa, e.g. «يا قاضيّ» and «يا فتايَ».
2- That which has two forms: it is the adjective resembling the imperfect verb, by which we mean the active and passive participles and the intensive forms of the active participle; its yāʾ is always retained, either with fatḥa or with kasra «[Translator's note: the standard rule is fatḥa or sukūn for this yāʾ; the text reads «مكسورة» as translated]», e.g. «يا مكرمي» and «يا ضاربي».
3- That which has six forms: it is everything other than that, which is neither «أب» nor «أم», e.g. «يا غلامي». The most common is to drop the yāʾ and make do with the kasra, e.g.:
«يا غلامِ»; then retaining it with sukūn as in the original, e.g. «يا غلامِيْ»; or with fatḥa, e.g. «يا غلامِيَ». Then turning the kasra into fatḥa and the yāʾ into alif, e.g. «يا حسرتا».
Then dropping the converted alif and making do with the fatḥa, so you say «يا حسرةَ»; then dropping the yāʾ, relying on its being intended, and giving ḍamma to the noun annexed to the yāʾ, as in «يا غلامُ».
4- That which has ten forms: it is «الأب» and «الأم». In them, in addition to the six forms mentioned, there are four other forms: that you substitute the tāʾ of the feminine for the yāʾ of the speaker and give it kasra, which is the most common; or give it fatḥa; or give it ḍamma, which is rare; and sometimes the tāʾ and the alif are combined, so that it is said: «يا أبتا» and «يا أمتا».

* Vocabulary:
(قُرْباناً): «القربان», with ḍamma on the qāf; there are two views on it:
1- It is a noun for that by which one draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whether charity, a sacrifice or other than that; like «الحلوان», also with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ: the name of what is given (yuḥlā, i.e. given).
One says: «قرّب صدقة» and «تقرّب بها», because «تقرّب» is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «قرّب».
2- That it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was then applied to the thing by which one draws near, as in their saying «نسج اليمن» (the weave of Yemen, i.e. what is woven). Evidence for this is that it was not put in the dual, though the place calls for the dual, because each of Qābīl and Hābīl had his own offering, and the base form would be to say «قربانين». The holders of the first view said: there is no proof in this, because the meaning is: when each one of them offered an offering, as in the saying of the Exalted: «فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة» (then flog them eighty lashes), i.e. each one of them eighty lashes.
(تَبُوءَ): you return [bearing].

* I'rab:
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ): the clause is conjoined to the implied verb in His saying «وإذ قال موسى لقومه», meaning: "mention, O Muḥammad, to your people and tell them the account of the two sons of Ādam," namely Hābīl and Qābīl, and the story of the offering and its cause. The story of Qābīl's killing of Hābīl fills the lengthy works of exegesis.
(اتل) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; (عليهم) is attached to «اتل»; (نبأ) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ابني) is annexed to «نبأ», the nūn having been dropped because of annexation; (آدم) is annexed to «ابني»; (بالحق) is attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a recitation bound up with the truth"; or [it is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), so the implied form is: "while you are bound up with the truth," i.e. with truthfulness; or from the direct object, i.e. "recite their account as bound up with truth and truthfulness."
(إِذْ قَرَّبا قُرْباناً فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِما وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (نبأ), i.e. "recite their story and their account that took place at that time"; or it is a badal (substitute) from it, i.e. "and recite to them the account, the account of that time," supposing the omission of the muḍāf. The clause (قربا) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (قربا) is a verb and its agent, and (قربانا) is the direct object. In (فتقبل): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تقبل) is a past verb in the passive; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as «هو», referring to «قربانا»; (من أحدهما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (تقبل); and (ولم يتقبل من الآخر) is conjoined to (تقبل).
(قالَ: لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ قالَ: إِنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the clause (لأقتلنك) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (أقتلنك) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it must be emphasised with the heavy nūn; the kāf is the direct object. (إنما) is [inna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); and the clause (إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين) is the object of saying.
(لَئِنْ بَسَطْتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي ما أَنَا بِباسِطٍ يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ): the lām prepares for the oath; (إن) is conditional; (بسطت) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ being the agent; (إلي) is attached to (بسطت); (يدك) is the direct object; and the clause is resumptive, explaining what he meant to say. In (لتقتلني), the lām is the causal lām; (تقتلني) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ the direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بسطت). (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative, operating like «ليس»; (أنا) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (باسط) is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar (predicate); (يدي) is the direct object of (باسط), because it is an active participle; (إليك) is attached to (باسط). In (لأقتلك), the lām is the causal lām, and (أقتلك) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām. The clause is the answer to the oath because [the oath] precedes the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it.
(إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); (إن) with its noun, and the clause (أخاف الله) its khabar; and (رب العالمين) is a badal from (الله) or an adjective.
(إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ): the clause is a second reason for his refraining from fighting, after the first reason. (إن) with its noun; the clause (أريد) is its khabar, the agent being latent, implied as «أنا»; (أن تبوء) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative as the direct object of (أريد); (بإثمي), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted [element] in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (تبوء), i.e. "you return carrying it," or "bound up with it." In (فتكون), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb conjoined to (تبوء), following it in the accusative; its noun is «أنت»; and (من أصحاب النار) is attached to the omitted khabar of (تكون).
(وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (جزاء الظالمين) is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين» there is comprehensive, all-encompassing speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): this clause gathers many meanings in brief words, for it contains the gist of the story from beginning to end, and the story is long; the reader will find it in the lengthy works. The gist of the meaning is that Allah the Exalted accepts obedience only from a God-fearing believer. It is reported of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh that he wept when death came to him, and it was said to him:
"What makes you weep? You were such-and-such and such-and-such." He said: "I hear Allah saying: «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»."
2- In His saying «إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك» there is the device of ittisāʿ (amplitude).
It is that the speaker brings speech in which interpretation is wide, according to what its words can bear, so that its interpretation widens according to people's intellects and the differences in their understanding. In the verse it lies in his wanting his brother's sin, because its meaning is: "I do not want to kill you and be punished."
Since one of two things had to be wanted — either his own sin, supposing that he defended himself and killed his brother, or his brother's sin, supposing that he surrendered — and he did not want the first, he was compelled to the second. So he did not then want his brother's sin for its own sake; rather he meant that sin lies in defending oneself in a way that leads to killing, which was not lawful at that time, and from that it followed that he wanted his brother's sin. This is like a person's wishing for martyrdom.
Its meaning is that the unbeliever returns bearing his killing and the sin he incurs thereby; but [the martyr] did not intend the unbeliever's sin for its own sake; he only wanted to give himself in the way of Allah, hoping [for that], the unbeliever's sin in killing coming implicitly and consequentially. What indicates this is that there is no difference in attaining the rank of martyrdom and its merit between the killer dying in unbelief and his life being sealed with faith, so that the sin of the killing, through which the martyr became a martyr, is annulled for him — I mean, whether the sin remains on his killer or is annulled for him, that neither diminishes nor increases the merit of his martyrdom. If the unbeliever's sin in killing were intended, the wish would differ according to its remaining or being annulled. So this shows that it is a necessary, consequential matter, not an intended one.

Views of the scholars:
The scholars of exegesis, grammar and rhetoric have spoken at length «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أقاض», a misprint for «أفاض»]» on this verse. What they have presented comes down to three interpretations:
a- That it is with the omission of the interrogative hamza, i.e. «إني أريد أأن تبوء؟» (do I want that you should return…?); and it is a disapproving question, because wanting disobedience is disobedience.
b- That «لا» is omitted, the implied form being «إني أريد أن لا تبوء بإثمي» (I want that you not return with my sin), like the saying of the Exalted: «يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا» (Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray), i.e. that you not go astray.
c- That the wanting is as it stands, being either figurative or real wanting; wanting that was permissible for him for reasons the exegetes mentioned, among them that indications appeared to him showing that his death was near, that his brother was an unbeliever, and that wanting punishment for an unbeliever is good.
3- The condition came in the form of a verb, namely His saying «بسطت», and the answer in the form of an active participle, namely His saying «ما أنا بباسط», to convey that he does not do what would earn this abominable deed; therefore He emphasised it with the redundant bāʾ that emphasises the negation.
Al-Mutanabbī and ittisāʿ:
In any case, this verse and the ittisāʿ in it appear to be among the things subtle for the understanding; but it is a necessary subtlety, containing many meanings drawn out from the speech. Al-Mutanabbī gazed toward its heaven, and he very often inclined to this kind of eloquence, so that his speech became subtle. Among his ittisāʿ is his saying:
لولا مفارقة الأحباب ما وجدت ... لها المنايا إلى أرواحنا سبلا
(Were it not for parting from loved ones, the fates would not have found for themselves paths to our souls.)
The outward form of the speech suggests at first glance that «لها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «وجدت»; but that would involve the verb of an overt [agent] passing to that agent's own attached pronoun, which is not allowed. So it must be taken as originally an adjective of «سبلا», which became a ḥāl when it was placed before it; and His saying «إلى أرواحنا» is likewise, since the meaning is: "paths travelled to our souls." You also have a strange view on «لها»: that you take «لها» as the plural of «لهاة» (uvula), like «حصى» and «حصاة», with «المنايا» annexed to it; ascribing uvulas to the fates is then a metaphor, likening them to something that swallows people; and he put «اللها» in place of mouths because the uvulas are adjacent to the «نعم» «[Translator's note: the text reads «للنعم» (to the blessings/favours); perhaps a misprint for «للطعم» (taste) or «للفم» (the mouth)]». «اللهاة», with fatḥa, is the piece of flesh overhanging the throat at the far end of the roof of the mouth.
Of this kind is his saying in love poetry:
كشفت ثلاث ذوائب من شعرها ... في ليلة فأرت ليالي أربعا
واستقبلت قمر السماء بوجهها ... فأرتني القمرين في وقت معا
(She uncovered three locks of her hair in one night, and showed four nights; and she faced the moon of the sky with her face, and showed me the two moons at one time together.)
The meaning is not as people think, that he saw two moons at one time, the moon and her face; rather, the accurate view is that when she faced the moon of the sky, its image was imprinted on her face, so he saw both at one time, just as shapes face a mirror and the image is imprinted in it, so you see the mirror and the shapes imprinted in it at one time together.
Al-Tibrīzī erred when he explained the verse, saying: it is possible that he meant a moon and a moon, because two real moons do not come together in one night, just as the sun and moon do not come together. One of the poets clung to the fringes of al-Mutanabbī and composed two verses most like sleight-of-hand and tricks:
رأت قمر السماء فذكرتني ... ليالي وصلها بالرقمتين
كلانا ناظر قمرا ولكن ... رأيت بعينها ورأت بعيني
(She saw the moon of the sky and reminded me of the nights of her union at al-Raqmatayn; each of us gazes at a moon, but I saw with her eye and she saw with mine.)
The best that can be said about them is that "two moons" means a real moon, which is the moon of the sky, and a figurative moon, which is the face of the beloved. So he says: she saw the figurative moon, which is the moon of the sky, and I saw her face, which is the real moon; because she looked at the moon of the sky and he looked at her face, so it holds true that he saw with her eye and she saw with his. This is hyperbole and excess in description; but the poets have customarily made the beloved the real moon and the one in the sky the figurative moon. Others said in explaining them:
This poet alludes «[Translator's note: the printed text has «يتسير», apparently a misprint for «يشير»]» to the moon of the sky being one of his beloved's lovers, and that his beloved saw it one night and, by her seeing it, clothed it with the light of her beauty and the charms of her qualities, cast her likeness upon it, and lent it her name. So she reminded this lover of those nights of union at al-Raqmatayn, and that by her union with him she annihilated him and overcame him with her qualities, until she became with him like a single moon, and both look at it. Hence he said "each of us gazes at a moon," i.e. a single moon whose manifestation became multiple; but she looks at it with his eye, which is the eye of love, because the lover has become beloved; and he looks with her eye, because she lent him an eye with which he saw her, so it is as though the one who sees her is she herself. The discussion of ittisāʿ is long; we content ourselves here with what has been said.

* Vocabulary:
(طوّعت): widened and adorned (made attractive); from «طاع المرعى له», when the pasture became ample for him.
(سَوْأَةَ): «السوءة», with fatḥa on the sīn: the private parts, and what of the body may not be uncovered. «السوءة» is also disgrace. The «سوءة» was singled out for mention because concern for covering it is greater.

* I'rab:
(فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (طوعت) is a past verb; (له) is attached to (طوعت); (نفسه) is the fāʿil (agent); (قتل أخيه) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فقتله) is also conjoined, and (فأصبح) is also conjoined, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «هو»; and (من الخاسرين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate).
(فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُراباً يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (بعث) is a past verb, (الله) the agent and (غرابا) the direct object; the clause (يبحث في الأرض) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «غرابا»; and (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يبحث).
(لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوارِي سَوْأَةَ أَخِيهِ): the lām is causal; (يريه) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بعث), so the latent pronoun in the verb refers to Allah; they may also be attached to (يبحث), i.e. it digs and stirs up the earth in order to show, so the latent pronoun refers to the raven. The interrogative clause suspends (muʿalliqa) the visual seeing, so it is in the position of accusative as a second object, standing in its place; because «رأى» of sight, before being made transitive by the hamza, takes one object, and by the hamza it acquired another object, which is the first object. Its like has come before in the saying of the Exalted:
«رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى» (My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead).
(قالَ يا وَيْلَتى أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هذَا الْغُرابِ): the clause is resumptive, as though said as an answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: what did he say when he saw the raven doing that? (يا) is a vocative particle; (ويلتا) is a word of anguish and sorrow. He called it as though woe were not present with him, so he called it to come: "O woe, come, for this is the time for your coming."
You may also take the one addressed as omitted and make «الويل» accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb which the Arabs let fall out of use; the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ of the speaker; and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The hamza is for interrogation and wonder, as though he wondered at himself:
how was he not guided to what the raven was guided to? (عجزت) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is included in the object of saying. (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (أكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by (أن); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (عجزت), i.e. «أعجزت [عن]»; the noun of (أكون) is a latent pronoun implied as «أنا»; (مثل) is the khabar of (أكون); (هذا) is a demonstrative, the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (الغراب) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative.
(فَأُوارِيَ سَوْأَةَ أَخِي فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ النَّادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (أواري) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (أن أكون). This is preferable to making it causative (sababiyya) because it is preceded by an interrogative, [in which case] (أواري) would be an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causative fāʾ; for the fāʾ that occurs as the answer to an interrogative forms, from the interrogative clause and the answer, a condition and its consequence, and here that is not formed. You say: «أتزورني فأكرمك» (will you visit me so that I honour you?), meaning: «إن تزرني أكرمك» (if you visit me I will honour you). But if you said here: «إن أعجز عن أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب أوار سوءة أخي» (if I am unable to be like this raven, I will cover my brother's corpse), it would not be correct, because the covering does not result from his inability to be like the raven. For this reason we have considered the conjunction preferable. (سوءة أخي) is the direct object. In (فأصبح) the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصبح) is a defective past verb, its noun a latent pronoun implied as «هو», and (من النادمين) its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz) in His saying «يا ويلتا», because he called upon something that does not reason, whereas the basis of the vocative is that it be addressed to one who reasons.

* Benefits:
This story which the Qur'an has presented is fit to be the kernel of a great story; it needs a creative pen to make of it a splendid work of art. It is reported that Ādam remained for a hundred years after the killing of Hābīl without laughing, and that he lamented him in poetry; this is a falsely attributed lie, for it is established that the prophets do not compose poetry. Maymūn ibn Mihrān reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: whoever says that Ādam composed poetry has lied; rather he would mourn over him and describe his grief in prose speech resembling an elegy; then the centuries handed it down, and when it reached Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān, who was the first to write in Arabic, he put it into verse and said:
تغيّرت البلاد ومن عليها ... فوجه الأرض مغير قبيح
(The lands and those upon them have changed; the face of the earth is dust-covered and ugly.)
They mentioned six verses after this one; and not content with that, they fabricated a report whose content is that Iblīs answered him in the same metre and rhyme with five verses. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «All of that is sheer lies, and the poetry is nothing but falsely attributed and full of grammatical errors.» Al-Zamakhsharī is pointing to the second verse, which is:
تغيّر كل ذي لون وطعم ... وقل بشاشة الوجه المليح
(Everything of colour and taste has changed, and the cheerfulness of the comely face has diminished.)
They transmitted it with iqwāʾ (a vowel fault in the rhyme), i.e. with «المليح» in the genitive. Some transmit it with «بشاشة» in the accusative without nunation and «الوجه المليح» in the nominative, and then it is not an error; they explained it as the dropping of the nunation from «بشاشة» and its being accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Our philosopher-poet Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī alluded to this story in Risālat al-Ghufrān; refer to it if you wish — and may Allah protect you. He singled out the Children of Israel with this story, as will come, because killing was their habit, even reaching the prophets.

* Vocabulary:
(أَجْلِ): «الأجل», with sukūn on the jīm, is a maṣdar (verbal noun). One says «أجل عليهم شرا», i.e. he committed evil against them and stirred it up; then it came to be used for crimes, as in their saying «من جراك فعلته» (I did it on your account), i.e. "from the fact that you committed it," i.e. you perpetrated it; then its use was broadened, and it came to be used for every [expression of] cause.

* I'rab:
(مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ كَتَبْنا عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (كتبنا), and (على بني إسرائيل), a preposition and its genitive noun, is also attached to (كتبنا); i.e. We legislated retaliation (qiṣāṣ) upon the killer, so that the legitimacy of retaliation would be a fixed ruling in all nations. He singled out the Children of Israel only — as we mentioned just now — because killing was the habit and custom of the Children of Israel, to the point that they ventured to kill prophets and messengers; because the purpose is to console the Prophet ﷺ and comfort him on account of their attempts to assassinate him and his Companions.
(أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ): (أن) and what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (كتبنا). The hāʾ is the noun of (أنّ), and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (نفسا) is the direct object; (بغير نفس), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (قتل), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «قتل», i.e. "he killed it wrongfully"; (أو) is a conjunction; (فساد) is conjoined to (نفس), which is genitive by the annexation of (غير) to it; and (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فساد).
(فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كأنما) is [kaʾanna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (قتل الناس) is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and the direct object; (جميعا) is a ḥāl; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar (predicate) of «من»; and the conditional clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «أنه».
(وَمَنْ أَحْياها فَكَأَنَّما أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the parsing of its like has been given.
(وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); the clause (قد جاءتهم):
has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; (رسلنا) is the fāʿil (agent); and (بالبينات) is attached to (جاءتهم).
(ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إن) with its noun; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of «كثيرا»; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by annexation; (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to «مسرفون»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (مسرفون) is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): the basis of the simile is that the two acts of killing share in violating the sanctity of blood, in audacity against Allah, and in encouraging people to kill. The point of the simile is to make the matter of killing appear dreadful and to magnify the matter of saving life, by depicting each of them in an image befitting it.

* Lügat:
(الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ): Kıyasa aykırı olarak «الرب»e nisbettir. Ayrıca şöyle de denir:
ربّيّ (râ'nın kesrasıyla) ve ربوبيّ (râ'nın fethasıyla). Kıyasa aykırı olarak nisbet edilmiş en meşhur isimleri Fevâid bölümünde aktaracağız. الرّبانيّ: kendini ilâhî olana adamış, ibadete düşkün kimsedir.
(الْأَحْبارُ): Fakihler (âlimler); tekili fetha ve kesra ile حبر'dir. Ferrâ şöyle demiştir:
Kesra daha fasihtir. Bu kelime التحبير ve التحسين'den (süslemek, güzelleştirmekten) alınmıştır; çünkü onlar onu (ilmi/sözü) süsler ve güzelleştirirler. Hristiyanlara göre الحبر الأعظم (Papa), Seyyid Mesîh'in yeryüzündeki halefidir; Yahudilere göre ise kâhinlerin reisidir.

* İ'rab:
(وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْراةُ): İsti'nâfiyye bir sözdür; onların, iman etmedikleri kişiyi ve kitabını hakem kılmalarına hayret etmek için sevk edilmiştir; oysa o, iman ettiklerini iddia ettikleri kendi kitaplarının açıkça belirttiği gibi haktır. «كيف» taaccüp bildiren istifhâm olup hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. «يحكمونك» merfû muzâri fiildir; vâv fâil, kâf mef'ûlün bihtir. Vâv hâl içindir; «عندهم» mekân zarfı olup öne alınmış mahzûf habere mütealliktir; «التوراة» sona bırakılmış mübtedâdır. Cümle «يحكمونك»deki vâvdan hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir.
(فِيها حُكْمُ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ وَما أُولئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ): «فيها» câr ve mecrûr olup öne alınmış mahzûf habere mütealliktir; «حكم الله» sona bırakılmış mübtedâdır; cümle «التوراة»dan hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. «ثم» tertip ve terâhî bildiren atıf harfidir; «يتولون», «يحكمونك» üzerine atıftır. Terâhîye delâlet eden «ثم» ile atfın faydası, uzun düşünmeden ve hakem kılmanın doğruluğunu gösteren ayetlerin ortaya çıkmasından sonra, onların yüz çevirmelerinin, i'râzlarının ve uzun hükümden [Mütercim notu: Metinde «عن الحكم الطويل» şeklindedir.] yüz çevirmekte ısrarlarının köklü olduğuna delâlet etmektir. «من بعد ذلك» câr ve mecrûr olup «يتولون»a mütealliktir veya hâldir. Vâv âtıfe veya isti'nâfiyyedir; «ما» Hicâziyye nefy «ما»sıdır; ism-i işaret kesra üzere mebnî olup onun ismi olarak ref' mahallindedir. Bâ zâid cer harfidir; «المؤمنين» lafzen mecrûr, «ما»nın haberi olarak mahallen mansûbdur.
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْراةَ): İsti'nâfiyye bir sözdür; Tevrat'ın yüceliğini, mertebesinin yüksekliğini ve hükümlerine riayetin vâcip olduğunu beyan etmek için sevk edilmiştir. «إن» ve ismi; «أنزلنا» cümlesi onun haberidir; «التوراة» mef'ûlün bihtir.
(فِيها هُدىً وَنُورٌ يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا): Cümle «التوراة»dan hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. «فيها» öne alınmış mahzûf habere mütealliktir; «هدى» sona bırakılmış mübtedâdır; «نور», «هدى» üzerine atıftır. «يحكم بها النبيون» cümlesi isti'nâfiyyedir ve Tevrat'ın şanının yüceliğini açıklamaktadır; onu «التوراة»dan ikinci hâl de kılabilirsin. «بها», «يحكم»e mütealliktir; «النبيون», «يحكم»in fâilidir; «الذين» sıfattır; «أسلموا» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılasıdır.
(لِلَّذِينَ هادُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتابِ اللَّهِ): Câr ve mecrûr «يحكم»e mütealliktir; «هادوا» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılasıdır. Anlam: Kendi aralarında onunla hükmederler. «أنزلنا»ya veya «هدى» ve «نور»un mahzûf sıfatına müteallik olmaları da caizdir. «الربانيون» ve «الأحبار», «النبيون» üzerine ma'tûftur. «بما استحفظوا», «يحكم»e mütealliktir; «من كتاب الله», «استحفظوا»ya mütealliktir. «استحفظوا» meçhul mâzî fiildir; vâv nâib-i fâildir. «ما»nın masdariyye veya mevsûl olması caizdir. «من كتاب الله» sözünün mahzûf bir hâle müteallik olması da caizdir.
(وَكانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَداءَ): «استحفظوا» üzerine atıftır. Vâv «كان»ın ismidir; «عليه», «شهداء»ya mütealliktir; «شهداء», «كانوا»nın haberidir.
(فَلا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ وَاخْشَوْنِ): Fâ, fasîha fâsıdır; yani: Bunu öğrendiyseniz insanlardan korkmayın. «لا» nehiy edatıdır; «تخشوا», nehiy «لا»sı ile meczûm muzâri fiildir; vâv fâil, «الناس» mef'ûlün bihtir. «واخشون»: vâv atıf harfidir; «اخشون» nûnun hazfı üzere mebnî emir fiildir; vâv fâildir; nûn vikâye nûnudur; hazfedilmiş mütekellim yâsı mef'ûlün bihtir.
(وَلا تَشْتَرُوا بِآياتِي ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا): Öncekilere atıftır. «لا» nehiy edatıdır; «تشتروا», «لا» ile meczûm muzâri fiildir. «بآياتي», «تشتروا»ya mütealliktir; bâ, yerleşik kaide olduğu üzere terk edilen (verilen) şeye girmiştir. «ثمنا» mef'ûlün bih, «قليلا» sıfattır.
(وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْكافِرُونَ): Vâv, hüküm genel olsun diye isti'nâfiyyedir; rüşvet alıp Allah'ın hükmünden başkasıyla hükmeden herkes küfre girmiştir. «من» cezmeden şart ismi olup mübtedâ olarak ref' mahallindedir. «لم» nefy, kalb ve cezm harfidir; «يحكم», «لم» ile meczûm muzâri fiildir ve fiilü'ş-şarttır. «بما», «يحكم»e mütealliktir; «أنزل الله» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılasıdır. «فأولئك»: fâ cevâbü'ş-şart için râbıtadır; ism-i işaret mübtedâ, «هم» ikinci mübtedâ, «الكافرون» haberdir; isim cümlesi ism-i işaretin haberidir. Fâ ile birleşen cümle cevâbü'ş-şart olarak cezm mahallindedir; fiilü'ş-şart ve cevabı «من»in haberidir.

* Belâgat:
Bu ayette, yolu ince olan bir belâğat sanatı vardır; buna dikkat eden azdır, çünkü delâleti derindir; onun derinliğini ancak nefisleri yakîn ve ilham ışığıyla aydınlanmış ilham sahipleri yoklayabilir. Belâğat âlimlerinden hiçbiri daha önce bunun için bir bâb açmamıştır; fakat o, meânî ilmindeki ıtnâb silsilesine dahildir. Bu, peygamberlerin sıfatı hakkında «الذين أسلموا» sözünün siyakındadır. Bilindiği gibi İslam, peygamberlerde bulunduğu baştan kabul edilen apaçık şeylerdendir [Mütercim notu: Metinde «البداءة» yazılıdır; muhtemelen «البداهة» kastedilmiştir.]; onlar bu hususta en sıradan bireyler olan ümmetleriyle eşittir. Fakat nasıl ki mevsûfun büyük bir sıfatla yüceltilmesi kastedilirse, sıfatın da büyük mevsûfuyla yüceltilmesi kastedilir. «Şair Mütenebbî'nin bir kasidesini okudum» dediğinde, Mütenebbî'yi şairlikle övmek kastedilmez; çünkü bu sıfat, büyüklüğüne rağmen, onu (diğerlerinden) ayırmaz; en sıradan şair de onunla vasıflanır. Fakat sen, bu büyük şairin onunla vasıflananlar arasında yer almasıyla şairliği övmüş olursun. Bu yüzden Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.v.) methinde şunu söyleyen kimse son derece güzel yapmıştır:
فلئن مدحت محمدا بقصيدتي ... فلقد مدحت قصيدتي بمحمد
(Kasidemle Muhammed'i övdümse, aslında Muhammed ile kasidemi övmüş oldum.)
Aksi hâlde, Zemahşerî ve başkalarının belirlediği gibi onu (sıfatı) yalnızca (mevsûfun) övgüsüne hasretseydik, belâğatin alışılmış kanununun —ki o, aşağıdan yukarıya yükselmektir (terakkî)— dışına çıkmış olurduk.
Eğer maksat sıfatı mevsûfla övmek olmasaydı, bu, Kur'an'da gelenle nasıl bağdaşırdı? Görmüyor musun ki Ebu't-Tayyib el-Mütenebbî'nin kendisi şu sözünde belâğatin en yüksek makamından kaymıştır:
شمس ضحاها هلال ليلتها ... درّ تقاصيرها زبرجدها
(Kuşluk vaktinin güneşi, gecesinin hilâli; gerdanlığının incisi, zebercedi.)
Burada güneşten hilâle, inciden zebercede inmiştir; bu yüzden eski tenkitçiler ona bu küçük kusuru yöneltmişlerdir.

* Fevâid:
Nisbet kaideleri nahiv kitaplarında geniş olarak anlatılmıştır; ancak nisbet kaidelerine aykırı düşen çok kullanılan isimler vardır. Edibin ezberlemesi için bunların en çok kullanılanlarını aktarmak istedik ve bu isimlerin bir kısmı için harf sırasına göre düzenlenmiş bir liste hazırladık:
أنافي: büyük burunluya nisbet.
أموي: أمية'ye nisbet.
بهرانيّ: بهراء'ya nisbet; Kudâa oğullarından bir kabile olup yurtları Humus ovasındaydı; komşuları Tenûh ve Tağlib gibi Hristiyanlığa inanırdı.
بدوي: بادية'ye (çöl) nisbet.
بحراني: البحرين'e nisbet.
تهامي ve تهام: تهامة'ya nisbet.
ثقفي: ثقيف'e nisbet.
جذميّ: جذيمة'ye nisbet.
جلولي: جلولاء'ya nisbet; Irak'ta Horasan yolu üzerinde bir şehirdir; Araplar Sâsânî hükümdarının ordusunu yendiğinde.
حروري: حروراء'ya nisbet; Irak'ta Kûfe'den pek uzak olmayan bir yerdir; ilk Hâricîler Ali b. Ebî Tâlib'e karşı ayaklandıklarını açıkça ilan ettiklerinde orada toplanmışlardır; o da Nehrevân vakasında onlarla savaşıp onları yok etmiştir.
حرميّ: hânın kesrasıyla, الحرمين'e, yani Mekke ve Medine mescitlerine nisbet.
حضرميّ: حضرموت'a nisbet.
دهريّ (dâlin dammesiyle): دهر'e nisbet.
ديرانيّ: دير'e (manastır) nisbet.
روحانيّ: روح'a nisbet.
رباني: رب'e nisbet.
رقباني: kalın boyunluya nisbet.
رديني: ردينة'ye nisbet; mızraktır. Rudeyne, mızrak düzeltmekle meşhur olmuş bir kadındır.
سليقي: سليقة'ye nisbet.
شآم: الشام'a nisbet.
شعراني: çok kıllıya nisbet.
صدراني: geniş göğüslüye nisbet.
صنعاني: صنعاء'ya nisbet.
طائيّ: طيّء'e nisbet.
عبديّ: بني عبيدة'ye nisbet.
عبشمي: عبد شمس'e nisbet.
عبدريّ: عبد الدار'a nisbet.
يمان: اليمن'e nisbet.
عبدلي: عبد الله'a nisbet.
فرهوديّ: فراهيد'e nisbet.
قرشي: قريش'e nisbet.
كنتي: كنت'e nisbet.
لحياني: büyük sakallıya nisbet.
مروزي: مرو'a nisbet.
نباطي: الأنباط'a nisbet.
ناصري: الناصرة'ye nisbet.

* I'rab:
(أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ): the speech is conjoined to what preceded, brought to show one pattern of their obstinacy and their following the path of falsehood. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Do they turn away from your judgement and seek the judgement of the Jāhiliyya?" حكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His saying «يبغون»; الجاهلية is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يبغون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أحسن is its khabar (predicate); من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحسن; حكما is a tamyīz (specification); and لقوم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Jalāl and others said: the lām means عند ("in the view of"), attached to أحسن, i.e. "in the view of a people who are certain". The clause يوقنون is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصارى أَوْلِياءَ): the i'rab of the vocative has preceded. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا», and the wāw is the fāʿil; اليهود is a mafʿūl bihi, النصارى is conjoined to اليهود, and أولياء is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. (بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ and أولياء بعض the khabar; the nominal clause is a naʿt of أولياء, or inceptive, mentioned as a reason for the prohibition. (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. فإنه: the fāʾ is linking, إنّ and its noun, and منهم its khabar; the nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): inna and its noun; لا is negative; يهدي is an imperfect verb; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين a naʿt; the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون» there is a delightful art, the art of īghāl (penetration): the speaker completes his speech before bringing its close, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something that conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of that speech. It is of two kinds:
1- Īghāl of choice (īghāl takhyīr): as in this verse, for the meaning was complete with His saying: «ومن أحسن من الله حكما». When the speech needed a verse-ending (fāṣila) suited to what is before and after it, it came conveying an additional meaning which would not have been obtained without it. That is because none knows that Allah's judgement is better than every judgement except one who is certain that He is One, Wise and Just — so that His oneness negates any partner in the judgement in which He alone is unique, there being no rival to Him in it and none to contradict Him; and from His wisdom follows putting each thing in its place, so that putting the right out of its place is safe from Him; and justice negates from Him injustice in judgement. Then He turned away from saying «يعلمون» ("who know") to saying «يوقنون» ("who are certain"), so that their knowledge of their Lord would be knowledge of conclusiveness and certainty.

Precautionary īghāl in poetry:
As for precautionary īghāl in poetry, it occurs specifically in the rhymes and does not go beyond them; some call it al-tablīgh. Al-Ḥātimī related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [Translator's note: the source prints «يريد»; the name is «يزيد»] al-Mubarrad, who said: al-Tawwazī told me: I said to al-Aṣmaʿī: "Who is the greatest of poets?" He said: "The one who makes a mean meaning great by its wording, or comes to a great meaning and makes it mean, or completes his speech before the rhyme and, when he needs the rhyme, conveys a meaning by it." I said: "Such as whom?" He said: "Such as al-Aʿshā, when he says:
كناطح صخرة يوما ليوهنها ... فلم يضرها وأوهى قرنه الوعل
(Like one butting a rock one day to weaken it; it did not harm it, and the mountain goat weakened its own horn.)
The comparison was complete with his saying: وأوهى قرنه ('and weakened its horn'); then, when he needed the rhyme, he said: «الوعل» ('the mountain goat')." I said: "And how did the mountain goat come to be preferred over everything that butts?" He said: "Because it hurls itself down from the mountain peak onto its horn and is not harmed." I said: "Then such as whom?" He said: "Such as Dhū al-Rumma in his saying:
قف العيس في أطلال ميّة واسأل ... رسوما كأخلاق الرّداء المسلسل
(Halt the camels at the ruins of Mayya and question traces like the worn-out rags of a threadbare cloak.)
His speech was complete; then he needed the rhyme and said: المسلسل ('threadbare'), and so added something. And his saying:
أظن الذي يجدي عليك سؤالها ... دموعا كتبديد الجمان المفصّل
(I think that what questioning them will bring you is tears like the scattering of pearls from a strung necklace separated by beads.)
He completed his speech; then he needed the rhyme and said «المفصل» ('separated by beads'), and also added something." There is no disagreement among people that Imruʾ al-Qays was the first to originate this idea, in his saying describing the horse:
إذا ماجرى شأوين وابتل عطفه ... تقول: هزيز الريح مرت بأثأب
(When he has run two heats and his flank is wet, you would say: the roar of the wind passing through the athʾab trees.)
He went to the utmost in describing it, presenting it in this state after it has run two heats and its flank has become wet with sweat; then he added «الأثأب» as a penetration in its description: it is a tree in whose folded branches the wind makes a great rustling and a loud sound. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā followed him and said:
كأن فتات العهن في كل منزل ... نزلن به حبّ الفنا لم يحطّم
(As though the shreds of dyed wool at every halt where they alighted were fanā berries not yet crushed.)
So he penetrated deeply in the simile by likening the scattered shreds of purple wool to fanā berries not yet crushed, because it is red outside and white inside; if it is not crushed, no white at all appears in it, and it is pure red. Al-Aʿshā followed them both and said, describing a woman:
غرّاء فرعاء مصقول عوارضها ... تمشي الهوينى كما يمشي الوجي الوحل
(Radiant, long-haired, her side-teeth polished; she walks slowly, as one with sore hooves walks stuck in mud.)
He penetrated with his saying «الوحل» ("stuck in mud") after having said «الوجي» ("sore-footed"). Al-Rashīd greatly admired the saying of Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
إذا ما علت منّا ذؤابة شارب ... تمشّت به مشي المقيّد في الوحل
(When it rises to the forelock of a drinker among us, it makes him walk like a fettered man in mud.)
And he would say: "May Allah fight him! It was not enough for him to make him fettered until he put him in mud."
2- Precautionary īghāl (īghāl iḥtiyāṭ):
It is that the speaker completes the meaning of his speech before ending it, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something conveying an additional meaning to complete the hyperbole, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء» ("nor can you make the deaf hear the call"); then He, Mighty and Majestic, knew that the speech needed a verse-ending matching the endings of what is before and after it, so He brought it conveying a meaning additional to the meaning of the speech, where He said: «إذا ولّوا مدبرين» ("when they turn their backs, retreating"). If it is said: what is the meaning of مدبرين, when the mention of turning away has made it unnecessary? We say: that does not make it unnecessary, since turning away may be with one side rather than another, as aversion may be. More of it will come when discussing Sūrat al-Naml, if Allah the Exalted wills.

* Vocabulary:
(دائِرَةٌ): الدائرة is one of the predominant attributes with which the thing described is not mentioned. Al-Rāghib in his Mufradāt distinguished between الدائرة and الدولة: الدائرة is the encircling line; then it was used to express an event, and it is said only of what is disliked, whereas الدولة is said of what is liked. It is reported that ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I have allies among the Jews, many in number, and I declare myself free before Allah and His Messenger of their alliance, and I take Allah and His Messenger as allies." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears turns of fortune (الدوائر); I will not declare myself free of the alliance of my allies." They were the Jews of Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
(حَبِطَتْ): i.e. the works which they used to affect in people's view became void.

* I'rab:
(فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ): the fāʾ may be resumptive, with the speech resumptive, brought to show the manner of their alliance, its cause, and what their affair and their destiny would come to. It may also be conjunctive, with the speech conjoined to His saying: «إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين». In either case it has no grammatical position. ترى is an imperfect verb, and the seeing is either visual or cognitive; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and مرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause). The clause يسارعون is either a ḥāl (circumstantial), if the seeing is visual, or a second mafʿūl bihi, if the seeing is cognitive; and فيهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يسارعون. (يَقُولُونَ نَخْشى أَنْ تُصِيبَنا دائِرَةٌ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun of «يسارعون»; the clause نخشى is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what is in its scope is the object of نخشى; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; and دائرة is the fāʿil (agent). (فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; عسى is one of the verbs of hope and operates like «كان»; الله is its noun, and أن يأتي is an interpreted maṣdar as its khabar. It has preceded that the khabar of عسى is most commonly an imperfect verb joined with أن. بالفتح is attached to يأتي; أو أمر is conjoined to الفتح; and من عنده is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمر. (فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ نادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive or causative; يصبحوا is conjoined to يأتي, or accusative by an implied أن after the causative fāʾ, because it is preceded by عسى, which is for hope. يصبحوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and the wāw is its noun; على ما is attached to نادمين; the clause أسروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; في أنفسهم is attached to أسروا; and نادمين is the khabar of «أصبح». (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: أَهؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to state what the believers say.
يقول الذين is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. It has been read with يقول in the accusative, conjoined to «أن يأتي», and it has been read without the wāw, so it is also resumptive. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الذين the khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying; the clause أقسموا is the ṣila; بالله is attached to أقسموا; and جهد أيمانهم is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl. (إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and معكم is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of إنّ. (حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ): a resumptive clause. It has been said that it is the speech of Allah, and most analysts hold this; it has also been said that it is the speech of the believers, and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān hold this. أعمالهم is the fāʿil of حبطت; the fāʾ is conjunctive; أصبحوا is a defective past verb, the wāw is its noun, and خاسرين its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted: «حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين» there is an art which Qudāma called al-ighrāb wa-l-ṭurfa (the rare and the novel). It is of three kinds:
1- A kind in which the rarity lies in the wording, and it is plentiful.
2- A kind in which the rarity lies in the meaning, as in the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
يطمّع الطير فيهم طول أكلهم ... حتى تكاد على أحيائهم تقع
(Their long feeding on them makes the birds covet them, until they almost alight upon their living.)
He took the well-known idea that birds alight only on the slain and follow armies, trusting they will be sated, and went beyond it, by an increase of hyperbole made pleasing by its being joined with «تكاد» ("almost"), to what he said; so his verse attained a rarity and novelty that no other attains.
3- And a kind in which the rarity is neither in its meaning nor in the outward form of its wording, but in its interpretation: it is that which, if taken in its outward sense, would make the speech faulty, but if interpreted, the interpretation returns it to a pattern of eloquent speech and removes the fault from its outward form.
The noble verse is of this kind, for one might say: the word «أصبحوا» ("they became by morning") is outwardly padding with no benefit, for these who are reported to be losers were in the evening in the same state as in the morning; and if you said: "the honey became sweet by morning" (أصبح العسل حلوا), the word «أصبح» would be redundant padding with no benefit, because it was likewise in the evening.
Al-Rummānī devised for this word an interpretation by which the great benefit is obtained [Translator's note: the source has «لجليلة»; «الجليلة» is meant], which would not be obtained without its coming. It is that, when he said: since the sick man who has spent the night suffering severe pains has his condition assessed in the morning — if by morning he is recovering and relieved of those pains, good is hoped for him, and his cure and recovery from that illness are thought most likely; and if by morning he is as he was in the evening, his perishing is certain, by the established pattern that illnesses flare up at night and subside in the morning [Translator's note: the sentence in the source, beginning «وهي أنه لما قال», has no main clause for لما; it is translated as it stands]. The state of the wretched has been likened to the sick man who by morning is in the same pain as in the evening, so he is one whose amendment is despaired of. On this basis the word «فأصبحوا» conveys a fine and beautiful meaning and ceases to be useless padding. And when Allah, glorified is He, reported that their works had become void, it was known conclusively that they had become losers; so no other word is fit in the place of «أصبحوا», and the meaning is not complete without it. As for the example given by al-Rummānī, «أصبح العسل حلوا وقد أمسى كذلك» ("the honey became sweet by morning, having been so in the evening") [Translator's note: in the source this example was earlier attributed to an objector, not to al-Rummānī], this is said only of matters occurring in the abode of this world, because its time has morning and evening; when a thing is in the morning in the state in which it is in the evening, mentioning morning and evening in it is padding with no benefit. But as for the Day of Resurrection, in which there is no evening, likening it to what is in the morning in a time accompanied by an evening is a likening that does not correspond to it.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ): resumptive speech, brought to show the state of apostates in general. The i'rab of the vocative has preceded many times. من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يرتد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, and it was given the fatḥa because of its lightness, as has preceded under the rule of the doubled verb. منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been read «يرتدد», with the assimilation undone. عن دينه is attached to يرتد; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause سوف يأتي الله is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of «من». يأتي الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بقوم is attached to يأتي; the clause يحبهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; and the clause يحبونه is conjoined to the clause يحبهم. On Allah's love for the servant and the servant's love for Allah [Translator's note: the source has «وجب العبد لله»; «وحبّ العبد لله» is meant] there are engaging discussions about which disagreement has raged; this is not the place to examine them, so let the reader refer to them in the long works. (أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): أذلة is a second naʿt of قوم; على المؤمنين is attached to أذلة, which is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); أعزة is a third naʿt; and على الكافرين is attached to أعزّة. (يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ): the clause يجاهدون is a fourth naʿt of قوم, and the clause ولا يخافون is conjoined to the clause يجاهدون, so it is in effect a fifth naʿt. (ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and فضل الله its khabar. «ذلك» may be used to point to the singular, the dual and the plural, and here it points to the qualities of which the first is: يحبهم ويحبونه. The clause يؤتيه is a second khabar, or you may make it resumptive; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of يؤتيه. The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, واسع a first khabar, and عليم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The servant's love for Allah is by his obedience to Him; this is the kind of majāz (figurative usage) in which the effect is named by the cause.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between أذلة and أعزّة.

* İ'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): «و» isti'nâfiyye; «أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل»: i'rabı az önce geçti. «ما» «التوراة» ve «الإنجيل»e atıf; «أنزل» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılası. Mevsûl ile bu ikisinden başka kitaplar kastedilmiştir; İşaya'nın kitabı, Daniel'in kitabı ve Davud'un Zebur'u gibi. «إليهم» «أنزل»e müteallik; «من ربهم» mahzûf bir hâle müteallik.
(لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ): Lâm «لو»nun cevabında vâki olan lâmdır; «أكلوا» cümlesi cezmetmeyen şartın cevabı olduğu için i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «من فوقهم» «أكلوا»ya müteallik; «من تحت أرجلهم» «من فوقهم»e atıf. Mef'ûlün hazfedilmesinin sırrı Belâgat bölümünde gelecektir.
(مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ ساءَ ما يَعْمَلُونَ): Cümle hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. «منهم» öne alınmış mahzûf habere müteallik; «أمة» sona bırakılmış mübtedâ; «مقتصدة» sıfat. «كثير»: «و» atıf harfi. «كثير» mübtedâdır; câr ve mecrûrla nitelendiği için onunla başlamak caiz olmuştur. «ساء ما يعملون» cümlesi «كثير»in haberi; «يعملون» cümlesi «ما»nın sılasıdır.

* Belâgat:
Bu ayette, belâgatin unsuru ve iksiri olan mecaz alanına giren iki beliğ hazf vardır:
1- «أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل» sözünde muzâfın hazfi. Kastedilen, Tevrat ve İncil'in hükümleri ve hadleri ile onların altında yer alan derin hükümler ve yaygın ibretlerdir.
2- Mef'ûlün bihin hazfi; bundaki incelikler daima yenilenir. Allah Teâlâ'nın «لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم» sözü belâgatin en uzak sınırlarına ulaşmıştır. «أكلوا»nın mef'ûlü, umumu kastetmek için ya da bizzat fiili kastetmek için hazfedilmiştir; «Falan kişi çözer ve bağlar, sağlamlaştırır ve bozar, zarar verir ve fayda verir» sözlerinde olduğu gibi. Bütün bunlarda asıl olan, zihnindeki kastedilen manayı bir şey için mutlak olarak isbat etmektir. Söz konusu hazifte üç vecih vardır:
a- Onlara göğün bereketlerini ve yerin bereketlerini yağdırması.
b- Meyveli ağaçları ve verimli ekinleri çoğaltması.
c- Onları meyveleri olgunlaşmış bahçelerle rızıklandırması; ağaçların tepelerinden sarkanları koparırlar, ayaklarının altından yere düşenleri toplarlar.

* İ'rab:
(وَإِذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ): «و» isti'nâfiyyedir; atıf harfi olması da caizdir, bu durumda cümle «لا يستكبرون» sözüne ma'tûf olur. «إذا» şart manasını içeren gelecek zaman zarfı; «سمعوا» cümlesi zarfın ona izâfesi sebebiyle cer mahallinde; «و» fâil; «ما» mef'ûlün bih olarak nasb mahallinde ism-i mevsûl; «أنزل» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılası olduğu için i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; «إلى الرسول» «أنزل»e müteallik.
(تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): Cümle cezmetmeyen şartın cevabı olduğu için i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «ترى» muzâri fiil; fâili takdiri «أنت» olan müstetir zamir; «أعينهم» basarî «ترى»nin mef'ûlü; «تفيض» cümlesi hâliyye. «من الدمع» câr ve mecrûr olup temyîz olarak nasb mahallindedir; bu i'rabın daha fazla açıklaması Belâgat bölümünde gelecektir.
(مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): Câr ve mecrûr «تفيض»e müteallik; «عرفوا» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılası; «من الحق» câr ve mecrûr olup mahzûf bir hâle müteallik.
(يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنا آمَنَّا فَاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): «يقولون» cümlesi, «عرفوا»daki zamir olan «و»dan ya da «أعينهم»deki mecrûr zamirden hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. Muzâfun ileyhten hâl gelmesi caiz olmuştur, çünkü muzâf onun bir cüzüdür. Takdir edilmiş bir soruya cevap olarak sevk edilmiş isti'nâfiyye cümle olması da caizdir; sanki «Kur'an'ı dinlediklerinde hâlleri nedir?» denmiştir. «ربنا» muzâf münâdâ; «آمنا» fiil ve fâil; cümle mekûlü'l-kavl olarak nasb mahallinde. «فاكتبنا»: «ف» isti'nâfiyye; «اكتبنا» emir fiil ve mef'ûlün bih; fâil müstetir; «مع الشاهدين» zarf olup «اكتبنا»ya müteallik.
(وَما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَما جاءَنا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): «و» isti'nâfiyye; «ما» ref' mahallinde mübtedâ olan istifhâm ismi; «لنا» mahzûf bir habere müteallik; «لا نؤمن بالله» cümlesi hâl olarak nasb mahallinde; «بالله» «نؤمن»e müteallik; «ما» «الله»a atıf; «جاءنا» cümlesi sıla olduğu için i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; «من الحق» mahzûf bir hâle müteallik.
(وَنَطْمَعُ أَنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الصَّالِحِينَ): «و» atıf harfi; «نطمع» muzâri fiil, fâili «نحن»; «أن» ve sonrası nez'u'l-hâfıd ile mansûb masdar te'vilindedir; (takdir edilen) câr ve mecrûr «نطمع»a müteallik. «ربنا» fâil; «مع القوم الصالحين»: zarf «يدخلنا»ya müteallik. Cümlenin tamamı «نؤمن» cümlesine ma'tûftur. «و»nun hâliyye ve cümlenin hâl olarak nasb (mahallinde) olması da caizdir.

* Belâgat:
1- Gözlerin taşmasında mecaz vardır; alâka dolmaktır.
2- Temyîzde mübalağa; bu en beliğ terkiplerdendir. Çünkü yükselme onda üç mertebe yükselir: Birincisi «فاض دمع عينه» (gözünün yaşı taştı); ikincisi fâilin temyîze dönüştürülmesi; üçüncüsü temyîzin ta'lîl (sebep bildirme) sûretinde ortaya konması. Böylece temyîzin yanında ta'lîli de ifade etmiştir. Sözün ta'lîl ile birlikte olması, aslından temyîzle birlikte olmasından daha uzaktır; çünkü bu, şundandır: Bunun benzerinde temyîzin aslında fâil olduğu yerleşmiştir; «طاب محمد نفسا» (Muhammed'in gönlü hoş oldu) ve «اشتعل الرأس شيبا» (baş ağarıklıkla tutuştu) gibi. «فاضت عينه دمعا» (gözü yaşça taştı) dediğinde, benzerlerindeki âdetle birlikte bu asıl anlaşılır; ta'lîlde ise böyle bir şey bilinmemektedir.

﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ i'rabı daha önce geçti. ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾: «تحلوا» meczûm muzâri fiil, fâili ve mef'ûlü; «الله» lafzatullah muzâfun ileyhtir. ﴿وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ﴾ «شعائر»e ma'tûftur; «الحرام» sıfattır. ﴿وَلَا الْقَلائِدَ﴾ aynı şekilde öncesine ma'tûftur; ﴿وَلَا الْهَدْيَ﴾ (de öyle). ﴿وَلَا آمِّينَ﴾ mahzûf bir mevsûfun sıfatıdır, yani: «ولا تحلوا قتال قوم آمّين». ﴿الْبَيْتَ﴾ «آمين»in mef'ûlün bihidir. ﴿الْحَرامَ﴾ sıfattır. ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: muzâri fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih; «من ربهم» «فضل»e müteallik; cümle hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir, yani: «حال كونهم مبتغين من ربهم». ﴿وَرِضْواناً﴾ «فضلا»ya ma'tûftur. ﴿وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا﴾: «إذا» gelecek zaman için zarftır; «حللتم» mâzî fiil ve fâil; cümle izâfetle cer mahallindedir; ﴿اصطادوا﴾ cümlesi cezmetmeyen şartın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. ﴿وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾: te'kîd nûnu bitiştiği için fetha üzere mebnî muzâri fiil olup «لا» ile cezm mahallindedir. ﴿شَنَآنُ﴾ fâildir; «ك» birinci mef'ûldür. ﴿قَوْمٍ﴾ muzâfun ileyhtir. ﴿أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ﴾: mâzî fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih; fiil «أن» ile nasb mahallindedir; müevvel masdar cer harfiyle cer mahallindedir; takdir: «لصدهم لكم»; (câr ve mecrûr) «شنآن»a müteallik. ﴿عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ﴾ kendilerinden önceki fiile müteallik. ﴿الْحَرامَ﴾ sıfattır. ﴿أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا﴾: müevvel masdar ikinci mef'ûlün bih olarak nasb mahallindedir, yani: «لا يكسبنكم الاعتداء».
﴿وَتَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ﴾: câr ve mecrûr kendilerinden önceki emir fiile müteallik; «و» onun fâili; cümle öncesine ma'tûftur. ﴿وَالتَّقْوى﴾ «البر»e ma'tûftur. ﴿وَلا تَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ﴾: «ولا تعاونوا» nehiy «لا»sı ile meczûm muzâri; cezm alâmeti «ن»un hazfi; «و» fâilidir. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾: emir fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih; cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ﴾: «إن», lafzatullah onun ismi, «شديد» haberi; cümle ta'lîliyyedir.

﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ i'rabı geçti. ﴿اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ i'rabı 8 numaralı ayette geçti [Mütercim notu: Bu ifadenin i'rabı 8. ayette değil 7. ayette geçmiştir.]. ﴿إِذْ﴾ geçmiş zaman için zarf olup «نعمة»ye müteallik. ﴿هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾: «همّ» mâzî fiil, «قوم» fâil; «يبسط» fiili ile «أن»den oluşan müevvel masdar cer harfiyle cer mahallindedir; câr ve mecrûr «همّ»e müteallik. ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ kendilerinden önceki fiile müteallik. ﴿أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ mef'ûlün bihtir; ﴿هَمَّ﴾ cümlesi izâfetle cer mahallindedir. ﴿فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ﴾: mâzî fiil ve mef'ûlü; cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾: cümle isti'nâfiyyedir. ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: lafzatullah «على» ile mecrûr olup (câr ve mecrûr) kendilerinden sonraki fiile müteallik; «و» atıf harfidir. ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: «ف» isti'nâfiyye; «يتوكل» emir lâmı ile meczûm muzâri; «المؤمنون» fâilidir.

﴿وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصارى﴾: mâzî fiil ve fâil; cümle isti'nâfiyyedir. ﴿نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ﴾: mübtedâ ve haber; lafzatullah muzâfun ileyh; cümle mekûlü'l-kavldir. ﴿وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ﴾ «أبناء»ya ma'tûftur. ﴿قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾: «ما» sükûn üzere mebnî istifhâm ismi olup «ل» ile cer mahallindedir; câr ve mecrûr «يعذبكم»e müteallik; cer harfi girdiği için «ما»nın elifi hazfedilmiştir; «ف» fasîha fâsıdır, yani: «إذا كنتم كذلك فلم يعذبكم؟»; cümle takdir edilen bir şartın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; fiilü'ş-şart ve cevabı mekûlü'l-kavldir; ﴿قُلْ﴾ cümlesi isti'nâfiyyedir. ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ﴾: mübtedâ ve haber; «بل» idrâb harfi; cümle isti'nâfiyyedir. ﴿مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ﴾: «ممن» câr ve mecrûru mahzûf olup «بشر»in sıfatı olan bir şeye müteallik; «خلق» cümlesi «من»in sılasıdır. ﴿يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾: «لمن» «يغفر»e müteallik; cümle isti'nâfiyyedir; «يشاء» cümlesi sıladır. ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ «يغفر»e ma'tûftur. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ i'rabı önceki ayette geçti. ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ﴾: câr ve mecrûr «المصير» mübtedâsının mahzûf haberine müteallik; cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ﴾ 15. ayette geçti. ﴿عَلى فَتْرَةٍ﴾ «جاءكم»e müteallik. ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ mahzûf olup «فترة»nin sıfatı olan bir şeye müteallik. ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: «أن» ve fiilden oluşan müevvel masdar, muzâfun ileyhin hazfi takdiriyle [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «حذف المضاف إليه» yazılıdır; açıklamadaki «كراهة» ifadesine göre hazfedilen muzâftır.] mef'ûlün lieclihtir, yani: «كراهة قولكم»; ya da cer harfiyle cer mahallindedir: «لئلا تقولوا». ﴿ما جاءَنا مِنْ بَشِيرٍ﴾: «جاء» mâzî fiil, «نا» mef'ûlü; «ما» nefy harfi; «من» zâid cer harfi; «بشير» lafzen mecrûr, mahallen fâil olarak merfû isimdir; cümle mekûlü'l-kavldir. ﴿وَلا نَذِيرٍ﴾ ma'tûftur. ﴿فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ﴾: mâzî fiil, mef'ûlün bih ve fâil; cümle takdir edilen cezmetmeyen bir şartın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur, yani: «إذا ادعيتم ذلك فقد جاءكم بشير». «ف» fasîha fâsıdır. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾: câr ve mecrûr «قدير» haberine müteallik; cümle isti'nâfiyyedir.

﴿وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصارى﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the Name of Majesty is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the speech). ﴿وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ﴾ conjoined to أبناء. ﴿قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ ما is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعذبكم; the alif of ما is dropped because the preposition has entered upon it; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted condition), i.e. "if you are so, then why does He punish you?"; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition with no grammatical position, and the protasis and its apodosis are the maqūl al-qawl; the clause ﴿قُلْ﴾ is resumptive. ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and khabar; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun ممن are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بشر, and the clause خلق is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ لمن: the two are attached to يغفر; the clause is resumptive, and the clause يشاء is the ṣila. ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ conjoined to يغفر. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse. ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ المصير, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ﴾ it has preceded in verse 15. ﴿عَلى فَتْرَةٍ﴾ the two are attached to جاءكم. ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of فترة. ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from أن and the verb is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), on the assumption that the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted [Translator's note: so in the source; going by the gloss كراهة, it is the muḍāf that is omitted], i.e. "out of dislike of your saying" (كراهة قولكم); or it is in the position of the genitive by a preposition: "lest you say" (لئلا تقولوا). ﴿ما جاءَنا مِنْ بَشِيرٍ﴾ جاء is a past verb and نا its object; ما is negative; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and بشير is a noun genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَلا نَذِيرٍ﴾ conjoined. ﴿فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ﴾ a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied non-jussivizing condition, i.e. "if you claim that, then a bringer of good tidings has come to you". The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar قدير, and the clause is resumptive.

﴿وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ﴾: mâzî fiil, câr ve mecrûr ona müteallik; «نا» fâili, «الكتاب» mef'ûlü. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ mahzûf olup «الكتاب»tan hâl olan bir şeye müteallik. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ ikinci hâldir. ﴿لِما﴾ «مصدقا»ya müteallik. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ zarf olup «ما»nın mahzûf sılasına müteallik. ﴿مِنَ الْكِتابِ﴾ mahzûf bir hâle müteallik. ﴿وَمُهَيْمِناً﴾ ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ya ma'tûftur. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ kendilerinden öncekine müteallik. ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: emir fiil, ondan sonraki zarf ona müteallik; «ف» fasîha fâsıdır; cümle takdir edilen bir şartın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. ﴿بِما﴾ «أنزل الله»e müteallik [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta böyledir; bir kelime düşmüş gibi görünmektedir, kastedilen muhtemelen «بما, احكم fiiline müteallik; أنزل الله cümlesi ما'nın sılasıdır» olmalıdır.]; cümle «ما»nın sılasıdır. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾: «لا» ile meczûm muzâri ve mef'ûlü; fâili «أنت»; cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿عَمَّا جاءَكَ﴾: «عما» mahzûf bir hâle müteallik, takdiri «مائلا عما جاءك»; cümle sıladır. ﴿مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ mahzûf olup «جاءك»in müstetir fâilinden hâl olan bir şeye müteallik. ﴿لِكُلٍّ﴾ kendilerinden sonraki «جعلنا»ya müteallik veya «جعلنا»nın birinci mef'ûlüdür. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ mahzûf olup, «كل»deki ivaz tenvîninin yerini tuttuğu mahzûf ismin sıfatı olan bir şeye müteallik;
