الرهن is well known, and the taking of the pledge: الرّهن, الرّهون, الرّهان. واسترهنني فرهنته ضيعتي. Figuratively: جاءا فرسي رهان, two horses of a race, that is, equal; وإني لك رهن بكذا, that is, I am a guarantor for it; ورجلي رهينة, that is, shackled. al-Samhariyy ibn Asad al-ʿUklī said:
لقد طرقت ليلي ورجلي رهينة ... فما راعني في السجن إلا سلامها
(Laylā came by night while my foot was in fetters; in the prison nothing startled me but her greeting.)
وفلان رهن بكذا ورهين ورهينة ومرتهن به: he is held to account for it. The Exalted said «كل امرئ بما كسب رهين» and «كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة». الرهو is stillness. The Exalted said «واترك البحر رهوا», that is, still; and عيش راه is a tranquil life. Someone passed by a bedouin who was «فالج» [Translator's note: «فالج» means both "paralysed" and "a two-humped camel"; the wording of the source is ambiguous] and said: "Glory to Allah, stillness between two humps!" One says طلع رهوا ورهوة, which is like a hill. Dhū al-Rumma said:
يجلّي كما جلّى على رأس رهوة ... من الطير أقنى ينفض الطلّ أزرق
(He clears away as a blue, hook-nosed bird clears away, shaking off the dew, on the top of a hillock.)
وجاءت الخيل رهوا means in succession; وأتاه بالشيء رهوا سهوا means easily, without any hindrance. He said:
يمشين رهوا فلا الأعجاز خاذلة ... ولا الصدور على الاعجاز تتكل
(They walk gently, so neither do the rumps fail nor do the chests rely on the rumps.)
This is among the wonders of this noble language.
(القتر): and القترة is dust with blackness in it; one says قتر (as in فرح, نصر and ضرب), and from it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
متوح برداء الملك يتبعه ... موج ترى فوقه الرايات والقترا
(Clothed in the mantle of kingship, followed by a wave above which you see banners and dust.)
It was also said: القتر is smoke, and from it comes the dust of the cooking pot. It was said: القتر is the small amount, and الاقتار in livelihood is straitness; one says قترت الشيء and اقترته, that is, I reduced it, and from it «وعلى المقتر قدره».
(القطع): the plural of قطعة, of the night, in which there is darkness; and القِطع, with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ, is the part of the night in which there is darkness. Both were read.

* I'rab:
(لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى وَزِيادَةٌ): للذين is a fronted khabar; the clause أحسنوا is a ṣila; الحسنى is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and زيادة is conjoined to الحسنى, meaning what exceeds the reward. (وَلا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلا ذِلَّةٌ): It is permissible for the wāw to be resumptive, because of the multiplicity of favours to the doers of good, and it is permissible for it to be a conjunction, with the clause يرهق وجوههم conjoined to الحسنى, and then the implying of أن is necessary; so if you wish you put it in the accusative and if you wish you put it in the nominative, in the manner of Maysūn's saying:
ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني ... أحب إليّ من لبس الشفوف
(To wear a cloak and have my eye cooled is dearer to me than wearing fine robes.)
لا is negative; يرهق وجوههم is an imperfect verb and a direct object; قتر is the agent; and ولا ذلة is conjoined to قتر. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; أصحاب is the khabar; الجنة is a muḍāf ilayhi; هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيها is attached to خالدون; and خالدون is the khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. (وَالَّذِينَ كَسَبُوا السَّيِّئاتِ جَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِها): It is permissible for the wāw to be a conjunction, with الذين conjoined by sequence to the first الذين, that is, "for those who did good is the best, and for those who earned evil deeds the recompense of an evil deed is the like of it", so that the division is balanced; and this is the easiest of the aspects mentioned by the i'rab-writers and grammarians. It is also permissible for the wāw to be resumptive and الذين a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is جزاء سيئة بمثلها, and this too is an easy view without strain; and there are other views we have set aside because they are strained and there is no need of them. The clause كسبوا السيئات, made of verb, agent and direct object, is the ṣila of the relative; جزاء is a second mubtadaʾ; سيئة is a muḍāf ilayhi; and بمثلها is the khabar of جزاء, that is, an omitted one, "by the like of it". (وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ): It was said that this clause is conjoined to كسبوا, and there is weakness in that on two counts: first, that the future is not conjoined to the past; second, that a long clause intervenes between them. It was said that the wāw is ḥāl and the clause ترهقهم ذلة is a ḥāl, and what is strained in that is not hidden. It was said that the wāw is parenthetical and the clause parenthetical, but a parenthesis is not apt here, because He is enumerating the states of their punishment. We see that the wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive, as if He were enumerating the kinds of punishment for them to terrify, and likewise His saying: (ما لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عاصِمٍ): ما is negative or Ḥijāzī; لهم is a fronted khabar; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عاصم; من is redundant; and عاصم is a delayed mubtadaʾ, or the delayed noun of ما according to those who allow the fronting of its khabar. (كَأَنَّما أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً): This is a resumptive clause that completes the three fates of theirs, namely the equal recompense, the abasement that overtakes them, and the covering of their faces with pieces of the night. كأنما is kāffa and makfūfa; أغشيت is a passive past verb; وجوههم is the nāʾib fāʿil; قطعا is a second direct object; من الليل is an adjective of قطع; and مظلما is a second adjective of قطعا, read with kasra on the qāf and sukūn on the ṭāʾ. On the reading قَطَعاً it is problematic for مظلما to be an adjective, so it is parsed as a ḥāl from الليل, the operator in it being either أغشيت, on the ground that الليل is an adjective of قطعا so that its reaching the described is like its reaching the adjective, or else the sense of the verb in «من الليل». (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): This is a fourth resumptive clause in which their inevitable fates are completed; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, أصحاب النار the khabar, and هم فيها خالدون a nominal clause, a ḥāl from them.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām's statement on «والذين كسبوا»:
Ibn Hishām said regarding this verse: The clause «وترهقهم ذلة» is conjoined to «كسبوا السيئات», so it is part of the ṣila, and what lies between them is a parenthesis by which the measure of their recompense is made clear, and the clause «ما لهم من الله من عاصم» is the khabar; so said Ibn ʿUṣfūr, and it is far-fetched, because the apparent sense is that «ترهقهم» was not brought in to define «الذين» so as to be conjoined to its ṣila, but was brought to announce what befalls them as recompense for their earning evil deeds. Further, it is not determinate, since it is possible that the khabar is «جزاء سيئة بمثلها», in which case there is no parenthesis in the verse; and it is possible that the khabar is the negative clause as mentioned, with the two clauses before it parenthetical; or that the khabar is «كأنما أغشيت», so that the parenthesis is of three clauses; or «أولئك أصحاب النار», so that the parenthesis is of four clauses. It is also possible, and this is the most apparent, that «الذين» is not a mubtadaʾ but is conjoined to the first «الذين», that is, «للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة» and for those who earned evil deeds the recompense of an evil deed is the like of it; so "its like" here is set against "the increase" there. Its parallel in meaning is the saying of the Exalted «من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون», and in wording their saying "In the house is Zayd and in the room ʿAmr", which is conjoining upon the two governed items of two different operators according to al-Akhfash, and upon the implying of the preposition according to Sībawayh and the verifiers. Among the things that favour this aspect is that the apparent sense is that the bāʾ in «بمثلها» is attached to الجزاء; so if «جزاء سيئة» is a mubtadaʾ, a khabar has to be implied, that is "occurring", as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, or «لهم», as al-Ḥūfī said, and that is better because it dispenses with implying a link between this clause and its mubtadaʾ, which is الذين. According to what we have chosen, «جزاء» is conjoined to «الحسنى», so no other implication is needed. As for the saying of Abū al-Ḥasan and Kaysān that «بمثلها» is the khabar and that the bāʾ was added in the khabar as it is added in the mubtadaʾ in «بحسبك درهم», it is rejected by the majority; yet their view may be supported by His saying «وجزاء سيئة سيئة».

* I'rab:
(قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ): هل is a particle of interrogation; من شركائهم is a fronted khabar; من is a relative, a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause يبدأ الخلق is a ṣila; and ثم is a particle conjoining to يبدأ. [Translator's note: the source writes «شركائهم» (their partners) here, while the verse reads «شركائكم»; translated as written.] (قُلِ اللَّهُ يَبْدَؤُا الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ): الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يبدأ الخلق is its khabar; the nominal clause is the content of the saying; ثم يعيده is conjoined to يبدأ; the فاء is a conjunction; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; and تؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. (قُلْ هَلْ مِنْ شُرَكائِكُمْ مَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ): another argument against what was mentioned; من شركائكم is a fronted khabar; من is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and يهدي is an imperfect verb that takes two objects, the second being introduced either by the lām or by إلى, and the preposition is sometimes omitted for lightness. In this verse the two modes of transitivity by a preposition are combined: the first and the third are made transitive by إلى and the second by the lām, and the first direct object of the three verbs is omitted. The implied form is: "Is there among your partners one who guides another to the truth? Say: Allah guides whom He wills to the truth. Is then he who guides another to the truth...?" The secret in the variation of the prepositions will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(قُلِ اللَّهُ يَهْدِي لِلْحَقِّ): the i'rab of its like has gone before. (أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُتَّبَعَ): The hamza is for denying interrogation, and it is the eighth question whose answer is not mentioned, and the answer here is "Allah"; من is a mubtadaʾ and أحق its khabar; أن is a maṣdar and accusative-governing particle; يتبع is passive; and the interpreted maṣdar is a muḍāf ilayhi of أحق after being put in the accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "more deserving of being followed". (أَمَّنْ لا يَهِدِّي إِلَّا أَنْ يُهْدى): أم is a conjunction; من is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يهدي is a ṣila; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, so the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) of the most general of states, that is, "he does not guide or become guided in any state except the state of his being guided", i.e. of others guiding him; and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "more deserving". You may also make من conjoined to the first من, in which case you do not need the khabar. (فَما لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ): The فاء is resumptive; ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ; and لكم is its khabar, that is, "what thing is established for you in taking these, who are unable to guide themselves, so how do you judge with falsehood and set up rivals and partners to Allah?" (وَما يَتَّبِعُ أَكْثَرُهُمْ إِلَّا ظَنًّا): a resumptive speech conveyed to explain the secret of their not grasping the truth and not understanding the content of the proof; ما is negative; يتبع أكثرهم is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; and ظنا is a direct object. (إِنَّ الظَّنَّ لا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئاً): a resumptive speech conveyed to explain the reason for their failing to understand and not grasping it; إن and its noun, with the clause لا يغني as its khabar; من الحق is a fronted ḥāl; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "any bit of avail", or a direct object by including in يغني the sense of "repels". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ): إن with its noun and khabar; بما is attached to عليم; and the clause يفعلون has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of ما, whether it be relative or maṣdar.

* Rhetoric:
The variation of prepositions:
This is a topic to which reference was made earlier in al-Anfāl, and it contains the secret of the variation of prepositions. Most people put these particles in the wrong places and are ignorant of the subtleties hidden in their placement where they are placed. Here the verb هدى is made transitive to «الحق» by إلى twice, and in the three [«وفي الثلاثة»] by the lām. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse itself uses the lām only in the second occurrence (يهدي للحق), as the author says in the i'rab section.] The grammarians are heedless of this secret and say that whatever may be governed by إلى may be governed by the lām, which gives the sense of limit as it does, but not conversely; so one does not say, for "I said to him" (قلت له), "قلت اليه"; and they say "the water is in the cup" because في is for containment, and they allow transitivity by الباء because it takes its place in containment, and it is not permitted to say, for "I passed by him" (مررت به), "مررت فيه". Once this is established we say, and Allah knows best, that there is a secret behind the form. When guidance is attributed to them, it must be made transitive by إلى, which conveys distance, as though it were by implication far from them; but when it is attributed to Allah the Exalted, it must be made transitive by the lām, which conveys nearness, as though it were among His exclusive attributes and the possession of His right hand, He alone having it in a manner of permanence and perfection. Lofty examples of this variation will come.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ لِي عَمَلِي وَلَكُمْ عَمَلُكُمْ): The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كذبوك is a verb, agent and direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; فقل: the فاء is the linking one, because what follows it is a clause of request; قل is an imperative verb; لي is a fronted khabar; عملي is a delayed mubtadaʾ; ولكم عملكم is conjoined; and the clause لي عملي is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. (أَنْتُمْ بَرِيئُونَ مِمَّا أَعْمَلُ): أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; بريئون is the khabar; مما is attached to بريئون; and the clause أعمل is the ṣila of the relative. (وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): conjoined to what has gone before, and the i'rab is plain. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ): The wāw is a conjunction; منهم is a fronted khabar; من is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and يستمعون is an adjective of من if it is an indefinite described noun, that is, "people who listen", and a ṣila if it is a relative; and he returned the pronoun in the plural, regarding the meaning of من, though more often its wording is regarded, as in His saying «ومنهم من ينظر إليك»; reference to this has been made many times. إليك is attached to يسمعون. [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is يستمعون.] (أَفَأَنْتَ تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَعْقِلُونَ): The hamza is for denying interrogation; the فاء is a conjunction of immediate sequence, and in it are the two well-known aspects, of regarding an omission of the one conjoined to, or regarding fronting and delaying, both of which have been indicated before; the wāw is a conjunction; لو and what attaches to it; كانوا is kāna and its noun; and the clause لا يعقلون is its khabar. al-Zajjāj said: its meaning is "even if they were ignorant", in addition to deafness; when the removal of hearing and the removal of intellect come together, the matter is complete and the human being has lost all human characteristics. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْكَ): conjoined to the preceding one and its like, but here he carried the pronoun on the wording of من; and the difference between the two places is that the listeners are mostly a group, while the one looking is mostly a single person. (أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي الْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كانُوا لا يُبْصِرُونَ): conjoined to what has gone before, and the meaning is "even if to lack of sight were added lack of insight". The apodosis of لو in the two clauses is omitted, on the indication of His saying أفأنت تسمع الصم and His saying أفأنت تهدي العمي; and each of them is conjoined to an implied clause opposed to it, and both are in the position of the ḥāl from the object of the preceding verb, that is: "Will you make the deaf hear, if they were to use reason, and if they were not to use reason? Will you guide the blind, if they were to see and if they were not to see?", that is, you do not make them hear and you do not guide them in any case. More on this simile will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ النَّاسَ شَيْئاً): إن is a particle resembling the verb; الله is its noun; the clause لا يظلم is its khabar; الناس is a direct object; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "any bit of wrong", and it is possible that it be a second object of يظلم, in the sense "He does not diminish anything of people's deeds".
(وَلكِنَّ النَّاسَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): The wāw is ḥāl; لكن is a particle of istidrāk and of governing the accusative; الناس is its noun; أنفسهم is a fronted direct object of يظلمون; and the clause يظلمون is the khabar of لكن.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya):
In His saying the Exalted «ومنهم من يستمعون إليك» to the end of the verse there is a representational metaphor, and it has already been said that the representational metaphor is a composition used for other than what it was set for, on account of a relation of resemblance. He likened them, in their not being guided, to the deaf and the blind; indeed they are worse, for «it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts»; and because the deaf who has intellect may sometimes use physiognomy to draw inference, and the blind who has insight in his heart may guess and surmise. The thing likened to has come composite because the thing likened is also composite; and had he resorted to simile, the artistic effect would have dwindled and would not have had that value we notice in the metaphor, because the metaphor, though built on observation, yet its composition induces us to forget the simile and calls us to imagine a new image; and in terms of wording, as you see in the verse, it leaves the dual expression, that is, the likened and the likened to, and uses the single expression, which claims that there is only one thing we are speaking of; and invention keeps its effect in tying a successful metaphor, and in this field the genius of artists and creators shines forth.
Moreover, Abū al-Ṭayyib looked up to the sky of this eloquence with his saying:
وإذا خفيت على الغبي فعاذر ... أن لا تراني مقلة عمياء
(If I am hidden from the dullard, he is excused that a blind eyeball does not see me.)
He means that if his place is hidden from the dullard, that is, the ignorant who knows nothing and did not know my worth and did not acknowledge my merit, I excuse him, because the ignorant is like the blind, and the blind eyeball, if it does not see, has its excuse in its blindness; likewise the ignorant who is ignorant of me and of my worth. And before al-Mutanabbī it was said:
وقد بهرت فما أخفى على أحد ... إلا على أكمه لا يعرف القمرا
(I have dazzled, so I am hidden from no one, except from one born blind who does not know the moon.)

2- Refinement (al-tahdhīb):
In these preceding verses there is a badīʿ art called the art of refinement, on which the scholars of this art have dwelt at length, and it can be summarised as a description that covers every chosen speech, namely the repeated looking into speech after composing it, and the close thought in refining and polishing it, whether verse or prose, and uncovering what is difficult of its abstruse meanings and rare of its i'rab, and casting off what distances itself from places of delicacy, of harsh wording and a coarse, jarring word. Abū Tammām expressed it in his testament to al-Buḥturī. It is reported from Abū ʿUbāda [Translator's note: al-Buḥturī is elsewhere known as Abū ʿUbāda; the text then has Abū Tammām address him as "Abū ʿUbayda", as written] that he said: "In my youth I sought poetry and went back in it to a sound nature, and I had not yet found for it an easy approach and ways of improvisation, until I went to Abū Tammām and attached myself to him. The first thing he said to me was: O Abū ʿUbayda, choose your times when you are of few cares and empty of griefs, and know that the custom regarding times, when a person sets out to compose something or memorise it, is that he choose the hour before dawn; and do not make verse or prose in a state of weariness, for much of it is little. Thoughts are springs: if you are gentle with them they gather, and if you are rough with them they run dry. Hum the poetry at the time of making it, for it helps. A poet may imagine excellent poetry and manage it one time and not another. Beware of obscuring the meanings, and place the noble meaning in a gentle wording so that neither spoils the other. Whenever poetry disobeys you, leave it, and whenever it obeys you, return to it. Give your mind rest when it is tired, and work on the meanings you love most and on all that suits your nature, for souls give out of desire and do not give out of compulsion. Make the verses scattered, as the mind provides, then string them together at the end, and secure the opening, the transition and the close, for that is the hardest part of the poem. And distinguish with your thought the landing-place of the message and the pouring-point of the poem, for it will be easier for you. Compose it first and refine it last."

Refinement in the verse:
As for the verse we are examining, it is His saying the Exalted «ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون، ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون». One might say: what is the benefit of the two closing clauses, when what precedes them has made them unnecessary? It is answered that in the speech there is fronting and delaying, knowledge of which removes the question, namely that it be said «ومنهم من ينظر إليك ولو كانوا لا يبصرون أفأنت تهدي العمي», and the other likewise. Against this comes the saying of one who says: what calls for setting the speech on fronting and delaying, which is one of the causes of obscurity? I say: what calls for it is aiming to bring the clause-endings alike with what comes before and after them of the rhymed endings. For before it is: «وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون», and after it: «إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم كانوا يظلمون». [Translator's note: the source quotes the last verse with «كانوا يظلمون», while the Qur'an reads «يظلمون»; translated as written.] Most of the rhymed endings of the sūra are of this measure and rhyme.

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ كَأَنْ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا ساعَةً مِنَ النَّهارِ): The adverb is attached to يتعارفون according to the soundest views; the clause يحشرهم is a genitive complement of it; كأن is the lightened form of the heavy, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter; the clause لم يلبثوا is the khabar of كأن; the clause كأن لم يلبثوا is a ḥāl from the هاء in يحشرهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; ساعة is an adverb attached to يلبثوا; and من النهار is an adjective of ساعة. (يَتَعارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ): The clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in يلبثوا, so it is an interwoven ḥāl, or from the pronoun in يحشرهم, so it is a successive ḥāl; بينهم is an adverb attached to يتعارفون. The meaning after this i'rab is that the creatures will know one another at that time as they were in the world, as if they had stayed in the world only an hour of the day; then recognition will be cut off when they behold the punishment and disown one another. There are other analyses that the space is too narrow to take in, and what we have given is the closest of them. (قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ وَما كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ): قد is a particle of affirmation; خسر الذين is a verb and agent; the clause كذبوا is a ṣila; بلقاء الله, a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to كذبوا; the clause قد خسر is resumptive; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان with its noun; and مهتدين is its khabar; and it is conjoined to قد خسر or to the ṣila of الذين, because whoever denies Allah is not guided. (وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ): إن is conditional and ما redundant; نرينك is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the kāf is a direct object; بعض is a second object; الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause نعدهم is a ṣila; أو is a particle of conjunction; and نتوفينك is conjoined to نرينك. (فَإِلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهُمْ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ): The فاء is the linking one; إلينا is a fronted khabar; مرجعهم is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the apodosis; ثم is a conjunction, not of temporal order but of the order of reports; الله is a mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar; على ما يفعلون is attached to شهيد; and the clause يفعلون is a ṣila. (وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولٌ): لكل is a fronted khabar; أمة is a muḍāf ilayhi of كل; and رسول is a delayed mubtadaʾ. (فَإِذا جاءَ رَسُولُهُمْ قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ): The فاء is conjoined to the description of رسول, that is, "he is sent to them, and when..."; إذا is an adverb of the future; the clause جاء رسولهم is a genitive complement of it; the clause قضي has no grammatical position; بينهم is an adverb attached to قضي; بالقسط is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of قضى [Translator's note: so in the source; since the verb is passive, the nāʾib fāʿil is evidently meant]; the wāw in وهم is a conjunction or ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ; and the clause لا يظلمون is the khabar.

* Vocabulary:
(الولي) is the opposite of the enemy; so he is the one who loves. The servants' love of Allah is their obedience to Him, and His love of them is His honouring them. On the first sense, فعيل has the meaning of fāʿil (active); on the second, the meaning of mafʿūl (passive); so it is shared between the two. Now we have investigated all the compounds in the words whose fāʾ, ʿayn and lām (first, middle and last radicals) are wāw, lām and yāʾ, and we found that they come down to a meaning of nearness and proximity. One says: وليه وليا: he came near to him; and أوليته إياه: I brought him near to it; "eat of what is next to you" (كل مما يليك) and "I sat next to him" (جلست مما يليه); and سقط الوليّ, which is the rain that follows the first spring rain (al-wasmī); وليت الأرض, and it is مولّية (the land received the walī rain); ولي الأمر and تولاه, and he is its guardian (waliyyuhu) and master (mawlāhu); he is the guardian of the orphan and the guardian of the slain man, and they are his guardians (awliyāʾuhu); ولي ولاية; and he is the governor (wālī) of the town and they are its governors (wulāt); "may Allah have mercy on the just governors"; واستولى عليه; and "this is my mawlā": my cousin, and "they are my mawālī"; and "my mawlā": my master and my slave; and a mawlā of clear authority is a master and helper, and he is more entitled to it (awlā bihi); ووالاه موالاة; and ووالى between two things, and they are in succession (walāʾ). The Arabs say: "separate your sheep from my sheep" (wāli ghanamaka min ghanamī), i.e. set them apart and distinguish them; and if the sheep are both ewes and goats it is said "separate them". Dhū al-Rumma said:
يوالي إذا اصطكّ الخصوم أمامه ... وجوه القضايا من وجوه المظالم
(He distinguishes, when the litigants clash before him, the aspects of the cases from the aspects of wrongs.)
وولاه ركنه: he turned his side to him. «فولّ وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام» (so turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque); and توليته: I made him a guardian: «ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم» (and whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is of them); and تولاك الله بحفظه (may Allah take you under His protection); and he put the wilīya on the riding-beast, which is the packsaddle. Abū Zubayd said: كالبلايا رؤسها في الولايا ... ما نحات السّموم حرّ الخدود (like the camels left to die at graves, their heads on the saddle-cloths, whom the hot winds have stripped of the heat of their cheeks). And ولّى عني and تولى, and «أولى لك» (woe to you), meaning ويل لك; and استولى على الغاية. This is from the rare in the highest degree.
[Translator's note: the second verse by Abū Zubayd is given in the source without a verse break and the gloss is tentative; I translated the text as printed.]

* I'rab:
(أَلا إِنَّ أَوْلِياءَ اللَّهِ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) ألا is a particle of alerting (tanbīh) with which speech is opened, composed of the hamza and the negative لا, changed from its first meaning to alerting. وإن أولياء الله: inna and its noun; لا is negative; خوف is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it was permissible to begin with it because of its negation; عليهم is the khabar (predicate); ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحزنون is its khabar.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَكانُوا يَتَّقُونَ) The position of الذين آمنوا admits three equally preferable possibilities. First, the accusative, as an adjective of أولياء الله. Second, the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هم الذين آمنوا. Third, the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the khabar being the following clause لهم البشرى. The clause آمنوا is a ṣila (relative clause); وكانوا يتقون is conjoined to the ṣila; and the clause يتقون is the khabar of كانوا.
َهُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا)
[Translator's note: the opening of this Qur'anic quotation is truncated in the source, which reads «َهُمُ الْبُشْرى»; the verse is لَهُمُ الْبُشْرى فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا.]
لهم is a fronted khabar and البشرى a delayed mubtadaʾ; في الحياة is attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of البشرى, the operator in the ḥāl being the settling (istiqrār) implied in لهم; and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. The clause لهم البشرى is either resumptive; and if الذين is made a mubtadaʾ, it is in the position of the nominative as khabar.
َ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ)
[Translator's note: the opening of the quotation is truncated in the source; the text is وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ.]
وفي الآخرة is conjoined to في الحياة الدنيا; لا is the lā of generic negation, تبديل is its noun, and لكلمات الله is the khabar of لا.
لِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ)
[Translator's note: the opening is truncated in the source; the text is ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ.]
ذلك is a mubtadaʾ; هو is a second mubtadaʾ; الفوز is the khabar of هو, and the clause is the khabar of ذلك; العظيم is an adjective of الفوز; and the two clauses are parenthetical (muʿtariḍatān). (وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهُمْ إِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعاً هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; يحزنك is an imperfect verb jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the kāf is a direct object; قولهم is the agent; and إن and its noun. Its hamza takes kasra because the sentence is resumptive in the sense of giving a reason for the might of Allah; and it is not permissible that it takes kasra because it occurs after قول, because it would then become a quotation from them, and the Prophet ﷺ would have been grieved by that, which would be disbelief. ولله is the khabar of إن; جميعا is a ḥāl of العزة, and it may be an emphasis (tawkīd); it is not feminized with tāʾ because فعيل is the same for masculine and feminine. هو is a mubtadaʾ; السميع is its first khabar and العليم its second khabar.

* Vocabulary:
(يَخْرُصُونَ) The original sense of الخرص is estimation (ḥazr), i.e. conjecture and assessment, and it is used for lying because that is how it is predominantly used. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "خرصت النخل خرصا, of the pattern قتل: I estimated its fruit, and the noun is الخرص with kasra. And خرص الكافر خرصا: the unbeliever lied; so he is a خارص and a خرّاص."

* I'rab:
(أَلا إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ) ألا is a particle of alerting, which has been mentioned; إن is a particle resembling the verb; ولله is its fronted khabar (predicate); and من is its delayed noun. He singled out those with intellect for mention in order to magnify: for if they belong to Him and are included in His dominion, then what lies beyond them, that which has no intellect, is all the more not to have any peer or partner. في السموات is the ṣila (relative clause) of من, and ومن في الأرض is conjoined to من في السموات.
(وَما يَتَّبِعُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ شُرَكاءَ) ما is negative; يتبع الذين is an imperfect verb and an agent; the clause يدعون is a ṣila; and من دون الله is a ḥāl of شركاء because it precedes it; شركاء is the direct object of يتبع, and the object of يدعون is omitted because the meaning is understood. The implied form is: "those who invoke other than Allah, gods as partners, do not follow", i.e. they do not follow in reality the partners, even if they call them partners, because partnership with Allah in lordship is impossible: ﴿إن يتبعون إلا ظنهم﴾ that they are partners. It is also possible that ما is interrogative, and is then accusative by what follows it, i.e. "what do they follow?"; Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to this i'rab. It is also possible that ما is a relative noun conjoined to من, as though He says: «والله ما يتبعه الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء» [Translator's note: so in the source; the conjunction to من requires «ولله», i.e. "and to Allah belongs what those who invoke partners besides Allah follow"], i.e. "and His are their partners". It is also possible that this relative ما is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, its implied form being: "and that which the polytheists follow is falsehood". These are four possibilities which we have given because they are close in preference, though the first is the easiest of them.
(إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ) إن is negative; يتبعون is a verb and an agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; الظن is a direct object; and إن is also negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the clause يخرصون is their khabar.
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهارَ مُبْصِراً) هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي is the khabar; the clause جعل is the ṣila of the relative. Then, if الجعل means origination and creation, it takes one object; if it means making into (taṣyīr), it takes two objects. In either case لكم is attached to جعل and الليل is a direct object. لتسكنوا: the lām is for reason, and تسكنوا is accusative by an implied أن; the preposition and its genitive noun is either an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi) or a second direct object; فيه is attached to تسكنوا; النهار is conjoined to الليل; and مبصرا is either a ḥāl or a second direct object, as already stated. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ) إن is a particle resembling the verb; وفي ذلك is the fronted khabar of إن; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is the delayed noun of إن; لقوم is an adjective of آيات; and the clause يسمعون is an adjective of القوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «والنهار مبصرا» there is a rational figurative expression (majāz ʿaqlī), for the attribution of seeing to the day is not literal. It has already been said that the rational figure is the attribution of an action or its like to something other than that to which it belongs, as in the saying of Abū Tammām:
تكاد عطاياه يجنّ جنونها ... إذا لم يعوذها بنغمة طالب
(His gifts are almost driven mad, if he does not shield them with the plea of a petitioner.)
It may also be treated as an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) if comparison is intended. Of this is the saying of Jarīr:
لقد لمتنا يا أم غالب في السّرى ... ونمت وما ليل المطيّ بنائم
(You blamed us, Umm Ghālib, for the night journey, and you slept, while the night of the riding-beasts does not sleep.)

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ بَعَثْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ رُسُلًا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ) It is conjoined to the story of Nūḥ. بعثنا is a verb and an agent; من بعده is a ḥāl; رسلا is a direct object; and إلى قومهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective. (فَجاؤُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا بِما كَذَّبُوا بِهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; جاءوهم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بالبينات is attached to جاءوهم; the fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يؤمنوا is accusative by an implied أن after it; the lām and what it governs are the khabar of كان; بما is attached to يؤمنوا; the clause كذبوا is a ṣila; به is attached to كذبوا; and من قبل is a ḥāl, with قبل built on ḍamma because it is cut off from the genitive construct in form but not in meaning. (كَذلِكَ نَطْبَعُ عَلى قُلُوبِ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) The kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "we seal with a sealing like that sealing"; and على قلوب المعتدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نطبع. (ثُمَّ بَعَثْنا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ مُوسى وَهارُونَ إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ بِآياتِنا) This too joins a story to a story, as a case of conjoining the specific to the general. من بعدهم is a ḥāl; موسى is the direct object of بعثنا; هارون is conjoined to موسى; إلى فرعون is attached to بعثنا; وملئه is conjoined to فرعون; and بآياتنا is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bearing our nine signs", which will be stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ, namely His saying the Exalted: «ولقد آتينا موسى تسع آيات بينات» (and We gave Mūsā nine clear signs). Eight of them have already been mentioned in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: two in His saying «فألقى موسى عصاه» (so Mūsā cast down his staff) and His saying «ونزع يده» (and he drew out his hand); one in His saying «ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين» (and We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought); and five in His saying «فأرسلنا عليهم الطوفان» (so We sent upon them the flood). The ninth will come in this sūra in His saying «ربنا اطمس على أموالهم» (our Lord, obliterate their wealth), i.e. transform it into stones, as will come in its place.
(فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا وَكانُوا قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; استكبروا is a verb and an agent; كانوا: kāna and its noun; قوما is its khabar; and مجرمين is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal or a connector; the clause جاءهم is added (muḍāf) [to it], or has no position; الحق is the agent; and من عندنا is attached to جاءهم. (قالُوا: إِنَّ هذا لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) The clause قالوا has no position; inna and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); سحر is the khabar of إن; and مبين is an adjective. (قالَ مُوسى: أَتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَكُمْ أَسِحْرٌ هذا وَلا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُونَ) قال موسى is a verb and an agent; the hamza is interrogative; تقولون is an imperfect verb and an agent; للحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقولون; لما is temporal and the clause جاءكم is added to it; أسحر: the hamza is for denunciatory, reproachful interrogation; سحر is a fronted khabar and هذا a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the sentence is the content of the saying; ولا: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and لا is negative; يفلح الساحرون is an imperfect verb and an agent, and the clause is circumstantial. (قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا لِتَلْفِتَنا عَمَّا وَجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا) قالوا is a verb and an agent; the hamza is for explanatory interrogation (istifhām bayānī) in which the stubborn obstinate person exhausts his collapsing arguments in order to justify his persistence in contentiousness, dissimulation and obstinacy; the clause أجئتنا is the content of the saying, a verb, an agent and a direct object; لتلفتنا: the lām is for reason, and تلفت is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after the lām of reason; عما is attached to تلفتنا; the clause وجدنا is a ṣila; عليه is attached to an omitted ḥāl, its implied form being "devoted"; and آباءنا is a direct object. (وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; تكون is an imperfect defective verb; ولكما is its fronted khabar; الكبرياء is its delayed noun; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "extending". الكبرياء is a maṣdar on the pattern فعلياء, and its meaning is greatness; it was also said to mean kingship, because kings are described by pride, and hence the king is called a tyrant (jabbār). Bashshār ibn Burd said:
إذا الملك الجبار صعّر خده ... مشينا إليه بالسيوف نعاتبه
(When the tyrant king turns his cheek away in pride, we walk to him with swords to reproach him.)
They also described them with «الصيد» (arrogance, holding the head high) and «الشوس» (looking askance in pride), and for that reason Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt described Muṣʿab in his saying:
ملكه ملك رأفة ليس فيه ... جبروت منه ولا كبرياء
(His kingship is a kingship of compassion; in it is no tyranny from him, nor pride.)
negating what kings are upon of that.
(وَما نَحْنُ لَكُما بِمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is Hijāzī (operating like ليس) and نحن is its noun; بمؤمنين: the bāʾ is redundant and مؤمنين is the khabar of ما in position.
[Translator's note: "Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt" is my expansion of the source's "ابن الرقيات"; the text gives only the shortened name.]

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām said, in the course of his discussion of the omission of the object: "Among its rare cases is the omission of the thing said while the saying remains, as in: قال موسى: أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم, i.e. 'it is magic', by the evidence of أسحر هذا."
There is a good deal of obscurity in this statement, and al-Dasūqī followed it up, saying: "What the author mentioned is one of the possibilities mentioned in al-Kashshāf, and its wording is: 'If you say: they were certain, by their saying «إن هذا لسحر مبين», that it was magic; so how was it said to them "Do you say: is this magic?" I say: there are several possibilities. That the meaning of His saying «أتقولون للحق» is: do you find fault with it and slander it, when you ought to submit to it and magnify it, from their saying "so-and-so fears the slander (al-qāla)", and "the people were disputing (tqāwul)" when some say to others what harms them; and like the saying here is the mention (dhikr) in his saying 'we heard a young man mention them', then he said 'is this magic?', so he denied what they said in finding fault with it and slandering it. And that the object of أتقولون is omitted, namely what is indicated by their saying «إن هذا لسحر مبين», as though it was said: "Do you say what you say?", meaning their saying 'this is clear magic'; then it was said 'is this magic?' And that the clause 'is this magic? and the magicians do not prosper' is a quotation of their speech, as though they said: "Have you two come with magic by which you seek success?"' End of what al-Zamakhsharī said." Al-Dasūqī handled it in a way that spoiled it, and so we preferred to quote what al-Zamakhsharī said verbatim from al-Kashshāf; even so it is not free of obscurity. Its clarification: the saying in the first view is a metonymy for fault-finding and so does not require an object; in the second it requires an object. What we hold is that Ibn Hishām's question is not valid, and that al-Zamakhsharī's objection and his effort to answer it are not valid either, and for that reason we passed over all of this in the i'rab. Better than all of it is the wording of Abū al-Suʿūd, which is: "Mūsā said, that is, he said three sentences. The first: «أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم»; the second: «أسحر هذا»; the third: «ولا يفلح الساحرون». His saying «للحق» means concerning it and for its sake; and his saying «لما جاءكم» means at the time of its coming to you from the very beginning, without reflection or consideration, which is contrary to the said saying. And «إنه لسحر» is the content of the saying, omitted because what precedes it indicates it, and as an indication that he does not utter it. And «أسحر هذا» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar and is a denunciatory interrogation, resumptive, from his side (peace be upon him), as a denial of their saying, and a reproach after reproach and a charge of ignorance after ignorance. And «ولا يفلح الساحرون» is a circumstantial clause from the pronoun of those addressed, and the connector is the wāw without a pronoun, as in the saying of one who said: 'The winter came and I own no provision', i.e. 'Do you say of the truth that it is magic, when its doer does not prosper', that is, he neither attains what he seeks nor escapes what he dislikes; so how could it issue from one like me, among those supported by the Almighty, the Wise?'"
[Translator's note: some of the quoted Kashshāf passage is obscure in the source (the clause "من قولهم فلان يخاف القالة" and the verse «سمعنا فتى يذكرهم»); I have translated it as printed. The words "Ibn Hishām's" statement is quoted from Mughnī al-Labīb.]

* Lügat:
(تَبَوَّءا): «تبوّأ المكان»: Orayı mesken (مباءة) edindi; «توطنه» demen gibi, yani orayı vatan edindiğinde. «بوأت له بيتا», yani onu (ona) edindim. Ebû Ali şöyle demiştir: «تبوأ» iki mef'ûle geçişli bir fiildir.
(اطْمِسْ): «الطمس», bir şeyin izini silerek gidermektir. «طمست الريح آثار الديار»: Rüzgâr yurtların izlerini sildi. Tams, yok olmaya ve silinmeye doğru değişmektir. Ka'b b. Züheyr şöyle demiştir:
من كل نضّاخة الذّفرى إذا عرقت ... عرضتها طامس الأعلام مجهول
(Kulak arkası terledikçe ter fışkıran her deveden; hedefi, işaretleri silinmiş, bilinmeyen bir yoldur.)

* İ'rab:
(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى وَأَخِيهِ أَنْ تَبَوَّءا لِقَوْمِكُما بِمِصْرَ بُيُوتاً): Vâv isti'nâfiyyedir; «أوحينا» fiil ve fâildir; «إلى موسى» câr ve mecrûr olup «أوحينا»ya müteallik; «أخيه» «موسى»ya atıftır. «أن»in müfessire olması câizdir; çünkü öncesinde, harfleri olmaksızın kavil anlamında olan bir şey, yani vahyetme geçmiştir. Kendi bâbı üzere masdariyye olması da câizdir; bu durumda girdiği kelimeyle birlikte «أوحينا»nın mef'ûlü olarak nasb mevziindedir, yani «İkisine (yer) edinmeyi vahyettik». «لقومكما» «تبوءا»ya müteallik ve ikinci mef'ûl itibarıyla [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «وباعتبارها مفعولا ثانيا» şeklinde kesik bir ibare vardır; kastedilen, ikinci mef'ûl yerinde olması olabilir.]; «بمصر» hâldir; «بيوتا» «تبوأا»nın mef'ûlüdür. Ebu'l-Bekâ onun «تبوءا»ya müteallik olmasını câiz görmüştür. (وَاجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): «واجعلوا» «تبوأا»ya atıftır; «بيوتكم» «اجعلوا»nın birinci mef'ûlü, «قبلة» ikinci mef'ûlüdür; «أقيموا الصلاة» atıftır, emir fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; «بشر المؤمنين» de atıftır. Hitabın çeşitlendirilmesinin sırrı Belâgat bahsinde gelecektir. (وَقالَ مُوسى رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوالًا فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): «قال موسى» fiil ve fâildir; «ربنا» nidâ harfi hazfedilmiş muzâf münâdâdır; «إن» ve ismi; «آتيت» cümlesi «إنّ»nin haberidir; «فرعون» mef'ûlün bihtir; «ملأه» «فرعون»a atıftır; «زينة» ikinci mef'ûlün bihtir; «أموالا» «زينة»ye atıftır; «في الحياة الدنيا» «زينة»nin sıfatıdır. (رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ): «ربنا» muzâf münâdâdır, te'kîd için tekrarlanmıştır. Lâm sayrûret ve âkıbet lâmıdır; yani: Onlara zikredilen nimetleri, şükretsinler ve senin yoluna uysunlar diye verdin; ama işlerinin sonu, onlara nankörlük etmeleri ve senin yolundan sapmaları oldu. İllet lâmı olması da câizdir; mânâ şudur: Onlara verdiğini istidrâc yoluyla verdin; dolayısıyla verme bu illet içindi. Hasan-ı Basrî şöyle demiştir: Bu, içinde bulundukları sapıklık üzere kalmaları için onların aleyhine dua lâmıdır. «عن سبيلك» câr ve mecrûr olup «يضلوا»ya müteallik. (رَبَّنَا اطْمِسْ عَلى أَمْوالِهِمْ وَاشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ): «اطمس» emir fiildir, fâili «أنت»tir; «على قلوبهم» câr ve mecrûr olup «اطمس»e müteallik [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta böyledir; «اطمس»e müteallik olan «على أموالهم»dir.]; «واشدد على قلوبهم» «اطمس على أموالهم»e atıftır. (فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتَّى يَرَوُا الْعَذابَ الْأَلِيمَ): «يؤمنوا» nasb ve cezm ihtimali taşır. Nasb, âtıfe olan sebebiyet fâsından sonra gizli «أن» iledir ya da «ليضلوا فلا يؤمنوا» kavline atıf yoluyladır; Müberred bunu tercih etmiştir; buna göre «ربنا اطمس على أموالهم واشدد على قلوبهم» kavli i'tirâz olur. Cezm ise, onların aleyhine dua vechi üzeredir; nahivcilerin nehiy adını verdiği «لا»nın, Allah Teâlâ'ya nispetle dua lâmı [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «لام الدعاء» yazılıdır; kastedilen dua «لا»sıdır.] olması esasına göre. Benzeri A'şâ'nın şu beytidir:
فلا ينبسط من بين عينيك ما انزوى ... ولا تلقني إلا وأنفك راغم
(İki gözünün arasında büzülen şey (kaşlarının çatıklığı) açılmasın; beni ancak burnun yere sürtülmüş olarak karşıla.)
«حتى» gâye ve cer harfidir; «يروا» «حتى»dan sonra gizli «أن» ile mansûb muzâri fiildir; vâv fâildir; «العذاب» mef'ûlün bih, «الأليم» sıfattır. (قالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما): «قد أجيبت» cümlesi mekûlü'l-kavldir; «دعوتكما» nâib-i fâildir.
(فَاسْتَقِيما وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): Fâ fasîhadır; «استقيما» emir fiildir, elif fâildir. «ولا تتبعان»: Vâv âtıfedir; «لا» nehiy edatıdır; «تتبعان» «لا» ile meczûm muzâri fiildir; cezm alâmeti nûnun hazfıdır; tesniye elifi fâildir; şeddeli nûn, sakîl te'kîd nûnudur ve tesniye elifinden sonra geldiği için kesreli olmuştur. Hafs, tâ şeddeli olarak, nûnu hafif ve kesreli «تتبعان» okumuştur [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta bu kıraat Hafs'a nispet edilmiştir; meşhur rivayette Hafs nûnu şeddeli okur, nûnu hafif okuyan İbn Zekvân'dır (İbn Âmir'in râvisi).]. Bu durumda «لا»nın hem nefiy hem nehiy için olması ihtimali vardır. Nefiy için olursa nûn ref' nûnu olur ve cümle isim cümlesi olur, yani «وأنتما لا تتبعان» (Siz ikiniz uymazsınız); ya da sonrasıyla ilgisi olmayan, müstenef salt bir haber olur. Nehiy için olursa nûn te'kîd içindir ve hafif olanıdır. «سبيل» mef'ûlün bih, «الذين» muzâfun ileyhtir; «لا يعلمون» cümlesi sıladır.

* Belâgat:
Hitapta çeşitlendirme: Allah Sübhânehû onlara hitabını çeşitlendirmiştir; önce tesniye, sonra cemi, en sonunda da tekil getirmiştir. Bunun sırrı şudur: Mûsâ ve Hârûn'a, kavimleri için evler edinmeleri ve onları ibadet için seçmeleri hitap edilmiştir; sonra hitap, içinde namaz kılmak üzere mescitler edinmeleri hususunda onlara ve kavimlerine umumî olarak yöneltilmiştir; çünkü bu, cumhura (herkese) vâciptir. Sonra en sonunda, en yüce maksat olan müjde, hem ona hem de müjdelenene tazim için Mûsâ'ya tahsis edilmiştir.

﴿وَ﴾: vâv isti'nâfiyyedir.
﴿أَنْ﴾: tefsîriyyedir.
﴿أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ﴾: emir fiil ve mef'ûlü; fâili mahzûftur.
﴿لِلدِّينِ﴾: (câr ve mecrûr) «أقم» fiiline müteallik.
﴿حَنِيفاً﴾: mansûb hâl.
﴿وَلا تَكُونَنَّ﴾: vâv atıf harfidir.
﴿لا﴾: cezmeden nehy harfi; «تكونن» nâkıs muzâri fiildir, ağır te'kîd nûnuna bitiştiği için fetha üzere mebnîdir ve cezm mahallindedir; ismi mahzûftur.
﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: (câr ve mecrûr) mahzûf habere müteallik. Cümle ma'tûftur.

﴿فَإلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكم فاعْلَمُوا أنَّما أُنْـزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ﴾: «أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ»nin mânası: yani «Allah onun indirilişini bildiği hâlde indirildi»; ve onun kendi katından bir hak olduğunu bilendir. —Allah daha iyi bilir— «بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ»nin, «Allah'ın onda gaybdan haber verdiği ve olacak ile geçmiş şeylere —ki Hz. Peygamber (s.a.v.) bunlar hakkında bir kitap okumamıştı— delâlet ettiği şeyle» [mânasında] olması da caizdir. Bu, onun Allah katından olduğuna delildir.

Allah Teâlâ'nın ﴿واصْنَعِ الفُلْكَ بِأعْيُنِنا﴾ sözü: «اَلْفُلْكُ» gemi demektir. «اَلْفَلَكُ» hem tekil hem çoğul olur [Mütercim notu: kaynakta kelime böyle harekelenmiştir; tartışılan kelime «اَلْفُلْكُ»tür]; nitekim «أسَدٌ» ve «أُسْدٌ» dedikleri gibi tekilde «فَلَكٌ», çoğulda «فُلْكٌ» demişlerdir; çünkü «فُعْلٌ» ve «فَعَلٌ» vezinlerinin çoğulu birdir ve çoğu zaman aynı anlamda gelirler. «اَلْعُجْمُ» ve «اَلْعَجَمُ», «اَلْعُرْبُ» ve «اَلْعَرَبُ», «اَلْفُلْكُ» ve «اَلْفَلَكُ» denir. «اَلْفَلْكَةُ» ise yuvarlak olan veya yuvarlaklık taşıyan her şey için söylenir. ﴿بِأعْيُنِنا ووَحْيِنا﴾'nın anlamı: Sana bakmamızla, seni korumamızla ve sana vahyettiğimizle (demektir). ﴿وَلا تُخاطِبْنِي في الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إنَّهم مُغْرَقُونَ﴾: Anlamı: “Kâfirlerin mühlet verilmesi hususunda bana hitap etme (dil açma); onlar boğulacaklardır.”

Allah Teâlâ'nın ﴿وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ في مَوْجٍ كالجِبالِ﴾ sözü: Göğün ve yerin sularının birleştiği, ikisinin arasını kapladığı ve geminin bu suda aktığı söylenmiştir.
﴿وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ في مَوْجٍ كالجِبالِ﴾ sözü: Dalga ancak suyun üstünde olur. Tefsirde, suyun her şeyi on beş zirâ aştığı gelmiştir.
Allah —azze ve celle— şöyle buyurmuştur: ﴿فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ [Kamer: 12]. Göğün suyu ile yerin suyunun birleşmesi ve aralarının kaplanmaması caizdir; aralarının kaplanması da caizdir. «اَلْمَوْجُ» suyun dalgalanmasıdır; oluşumu en çok suyun üst kısmında bilinir.
Suyun içinde dalgalanması da caizdir. Gemi hakkındaki rivayete gelince, uzunluğu hakkında söylenenlerin en çoğu bin iki yüz zirâ olduğudur; “altı yüz zirâ” da denmiştir. Nûh'un kırk yaşında peygamber olarak gönderildiği, Allah'ın —senâsı yüce olsun— buyurduğu gibi kavmi arasında ﴿ألْفَ سَنَةٍ إلا خَمْسِينَ عامًا﴾ [Ankebût: 14] kaldığı, gemiyi elli yılda yaptığı ve tufandan sonra altmış yıl yaşadığı da söylenmiştir.
﴿وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وكانَ في مَعْزِلٍ﴾: Onun kendi dininden, yani babasının dininden ayrı bir yerde (مَعْزِل) olması caizdir; —ki daha uygun olanı budur— gemiden ayrı bir yerde olması da caizdir. ﴿يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا﴾: Kıraatin en iyisi kesradır, yani yânın kesrası [Mütercim notu: metinde böyle; kastedilen «يا بُنَيِّ» şeklinde son harfin kesrasıdır]. Kesrası da fethası da iki yönden caizdir. (Kesranın) birinci (yönü): Aslı «يا بُنَيِّي»dir; nidâda izâfet yâsı hazfedilir ve kesra ona delâlet etmek üzere kalır.
(İkinci yönü): Yânın «اِرْكَبْ»deki râ'nın sükûnu sebebiyle hazfedilmesi ve yazıda telaffuzdaki hâliyle bırakılması da caizdir. Fetha da iki yöndendir: (Birincisi) aslı «يا بُنَيّا»dır; izâfet yâsından elif bedel yapılır —Araplar “يا غُلامًا أقْبِلْ” (Ey oğlancığım, gel) derler—; sonra elif, kendi sükûnu ve râ'nın sükûnu sebebiyle hazfedilir ve yazıda telaffuzdaki hazfine göre bırakılır.
(İkincisi): Nidâ elifinin de, izâfet yâsının hazfedildiği gibi hazfedilmesi caizdir. İzâfet yâsı ve izâfet elifi nidâda, tıpkı tenvînin hazfedilmesi gibi hazfedilmiştir; çünkü izâfet yâsı, tenvînin isme bir ziyade olması gibi isimde bir ziyadedir. Okunmamış başka bir vecih daha caizdir: O da yânın ispatıdır: «يا بُنَيِّي». Bu, yâların bir araya gelmesi sebebiyle ağır olur.

﴿قالَتْ يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾: Mushafta «يا ويْلَتى» yâ ile (yazılmış)tır; kıraat ise eliflidir; istersen tefhîm (kalın okuma) ile, istersen imâle ile. Aslı «يا ويْلَتِي»dir; yâ ve kesradan elif bedel yapılmıştır, çünkü fetha ve elif, yâ ve kesradan daha hafiftir. Üzerinde hâ'sız vakıf yapmak caizdir; tercih edilen ise hâ ile vakıf yapılmasıdır: «يا ويْلَتاهُ».
Mushafa gelince, ona muhalefet edilmez; üzerinde hâ'sız vakıf yapılmaz [Mütercim notu: kaynakta «ولا يُوقَفُ عَلَيْهِ بِغَيْرِ الهاءِ» yazılıdır; devamdaki «zorda kalan hâ'sız vakfeder» ifadesi bağlamla uyumlu görünmemektedir, kaynaktaki gibi çevrilmiştir]. Vakfeden kimse zorda kalırsa hâ'sız vakfeder. «يا ويْلَتى»dan sonraki iki hemzeye gelince, bunlarda üç vecih vardır.
İstersen birincisini tahkîk eder (açık okur), ikincisini tahfîf edersin ve «يا ويْلَتى أالِدُ» dersin. İstersen —ki tercih edilen budur— birincisini tahfîf eder, ikincisini de tahfîf eder ve «يا ويْلَتى آلِدُ» dersin. İstersen ikisini birden tahkîk eder ve «أألِدُ» dersin.
İki hemzenin tahkîki İbn Ebî İshak'ın mezhebidir. ﴿وَهَذا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا﴾: Kıraat nasb iledir; üzerinde icmâ edilen mushafta da böyledir. Hâl üzere mansûbdur. Buradaki hâlin nasbı, nahvin ince ve kapalı konularındandır. Şöyle ki: “هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا” dediğinde, eğer Zeyd'i tanımayan birine onun Zeyd olduğunu haber vermeyi kastediyorsan “هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا” demen caiz olmaz; çünkü (o takdirde) ayakta durduğu müddetçe Zeyd olur.
Ayakta durmaktan ayrılınca da Zeyd olmaz. Bunu ancak Zeyd'i tanıyan kimseye “هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا” diye söylersin; hâlde tenbih (dikkat çekme) amel eder. Anlam: “Ayakta durduğu hâlde Zeyd'e dikkat et”; sana ayakta durduğu hâlde Zeyd'e işaret edilmiştir; çünkü «هَذا» hazır olana işarettir. Dolayısıyla, zikrettiğimiz gibi, doğru vecih nasbdır.
Ref' de caizdir. Sîbeveyh ve Halîl, ref'in dört vecihten olduğunu söylemişlerdir: Bunlardan bir vecih şudur: “هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ” dersin; «زَيْد»i «هَذا» ile merfû yaparsın, «قائِمٌ»u da ikinci haber olarak merfû yaparsın; sanki “هُوَ قائِمٌ” ya da “هَذا قائِمٌ” demiş olursun. «زَيْد» ve «قائِم»in ikisini birden «هَذا»nın iki haberi kılıp ikisini de «هَذا» ile haber olarak merfû yapman da caizdir; tıpkı iki tadı birleştirdiğini kastederek “هَذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ” (Bu mayhoştur) demen gibi. «زَيْد»i «هَذا»dan bedel kılman da caizdir; sanki “زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ” demiş olursun. «زَيْد»i «هَذا»yı açıklayan (atf-ı beyân) kılman da caizdir; sanki “هَذا قائِمٌ”u kastetmişsin, sonra “زَيْدٌ” sözünle onun kim olduğunu açıklamışsındır. İşte bunlar dört vecihtir.

Allah Teâlâ'nın ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بِٱلْبُـشْرَىٰ﴾ kavli.
Yani çocuk müjdesiyle.
* Sonra Allah Teâlâ şöyle buyurdu: ﴿قَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ﴾ [âyet 69].
﴿قَال سِلْمٌ﴾ şeklinde de okunur.
Ferrâ dedi ki: سِلْم ve سَلاَم birdir; nitekim حِلّ ve حَلاَل denir.
* Sonra Allah Teâlâ şöyle buyurdu: ﴿فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ﴾.
İbn Ebî Talha, İbn Abbâs'tan şöyle dediğini rivayet etti: O, iyice pişmiş olandır. Katâde de böyle dedi.
Dahhâk dedi ki: Pişinceye kadar altında ateş yakılan şeydir.
Ebû Ubeyde'nin sözü: ﴿حَنِيذٍ﴾ "محنوذ" anlamındadır, yani kızartılmış. "حَنَذْتُ فرسي" denir; yani atımı terlettim.
Anlam şudur: Onlar ona misafir olduklarında, onlara bir buzağı getirmekte gecikmedi; sonra "أنْ"den (önceki) bâ hazfedilmiştir.
Şöyle de denildi: Elçiler "Cebrâil, Mîkâil ve İsrâfil"dir (a.s.). ﴿بِٱلْبُـشْرَىٰ﴾ İshâk'ın müjdesidir.
Şöyle de denildi: Müjde, Lût kavminin helâkiyle (ilgili) idi.
[Mütercim notu: Metinde «وقول أبو عبيدة» yazılıdır; dil kuralına göre «وقول أبي عبيدة» olmalıdır.]

His saying, the Exalted: {كِتَابٌ}: It is permissible that it be the khabar (predicate) of «ألر», He reporting of these letters that they are a book described by such-and-such; and that it be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "that is a book", which is indicated by its appearing overtly in His saying, the Exalted: {ذَلِكَ الكتاب} [al-Baqara: 2]; and what suffices you on that was given at the beginning of this work.
His saying: {أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ}: It is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «كتاب». The hamza in «أُحْكِمَتْ» may be for transfer (naql) from «حَكُمَ» with ḍamma on the kāf, that is: "became wise", in the sense "were made wise", as in His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الكتاب الحكيم} [Luqmān: 2]. It may be from their saying «أَحْكَمْتُ الدابة» when you put the ḥakama (bridle-bit) on it to prevent it from bolting, as in the saying of Jarīr:
2633 - أبني حَنِيْفَةَ أَحْكِموا سُفَهاءَكمْ ... إني أخاف عليكمُ أَنْ أَغْضبا (O sons of Ḥanīfa, restrain your fools; I fear for you that I may grow angry)
so the meaning is that they were prevented from corruption. It may also be not for transfer, from iḥkām, which is perfecting, like a well-built, well-ordered structure; the meaning is: that they were composed in a firm, perfected composition.
His saying: {ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ}: «ثم» is in its usual sense of delay, because they were first made firm and then set out in detail, according to the occasions of revelation. ʿIkrima, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Jaḥdarī, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «فَصَلَتْ» with two fatḥas and a light ʿayn. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning is: separated, as in His saying {فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ} [al-Baqara: 249], that is: departed." Others explained it here as "distinguished between the one in the right and the one in the wrong", which is better. Al-Zamakhsharī made «ثم» for ordering in reporting and not for ordering of occurrence in time, and said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «ثم»? I say: its meaning is not delay in time but in rank, as you say: it is perfectly firm, then perfectly detailed; and so-and-so is noble in origin, then noble in action." It was also read: «أحْكَمْتُ آياتِه ثم فَصَّلْتُ» with both verbs ascribed to the tāʾ of the first person and «آياته» accusative as direct object, that is: "I made its verses firm, then I set them out in detail"; al-Zamakhsharī reported this reading.
His saying: {مِن لَّدُنْ}: It is permissible that it be a second adjective of «كتاب», and that it be a second khabar according to those who permit that; and it is permissible that it be governed by one of the two preceding verbs, I mean «أُحْكِمَتْ» or «فُصِّلَتْ», this being of the chapter of conflict (tanāzuʿ), with the second verb taking effect, since had the first been given effect, a pronoun would have been implied in the second. Al-Zamakhsharī leaned to this in his saying: "and that it be connected with «أُحْكِمت» and «فُصِّلَتْ», that is: from the presence of ... their making firm and their setting out in detail [Translator's note: the source reads «من عندِ أحكامُها وتفصيلُها», where a word appears to be missing], and there is a fine antithesis in it, because the meaning is: a Wise One made them firm, and a Well-Informed One of the manners of things set them out in detail, that is, explained and clarified them." The Shaykh said: "He does not mean that «مِنْ لدن» is attached to both verbs together from the point of view of the craft of i'rab, but means that it is of the chapter of effect (iʿmāl), so it is attached to them both by meaning." And that is also the meaning of the saying of Abū l-Baqāʾ: "and it is permissible that it be an object, the operator in it being «فُصِّلَتْ»."

His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنِ استغفروا}: There are two aspects regarding it. One: that it is conjoined to the first «أنْ», whether the «لا» after it is negation or prohibition, so the aspects reported regarding it return to this «أَنْ». The second: that it is accusative as an incitement (ighrāʾ). Al-Zamakhsharī said on this aspect: "It may be a fresh speech, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as an incitement from him to confine worship to Allah the Exalted; and what indicates it is His saying «إني لكم منه نذيرٌ وبشير», as if he said: 'Abandon the worship of any but Allah! I am to you a warner from Him', like His saying, the Exalted: {فَضَرْبَ الرقاب} [Muḥammad: 4]."
His saying: {ثُمَّ توبوا}: It is conjoined to the preceding command to seek forgiveness, and «ثم» is in its usual sense of delay, because one first seeks forgiveness, then repents and strips oneself of that sin for which forgiveness was sought. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «ثم» in {ثُمَّ توبوا إِلَيْهِ}? I say: its meaning is: seek forgiveness from polytheism, then return to Him in obedience; or: seek forgiveness, and seeking forgiveness is repentance, then make the repentance sincere and be steadfast in it, as in His saying, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ استقاموا} [al-Aḥqāf: 13]." I say: his saying "or seek forgiveness" to the end means that some made seeking forgiveness and repentance one meaning, so he needed to interpret «توبوا» as «أَخْلِصوا التوبة» (make repentance sincere).
His saying: {يُمَتِّعْكُمْ}: It is the response to the command (jawāb al-amr). The disagreement about what makes it jussive has already been given: whether it is the request clause itself or an implied conditional particle. Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd b. ʿAlī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «يُمْتِعْكم» in the light form, from amtaʿa; and it has already been mentioned that Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read {فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلاً} [al-Baqara: 126] in al-Baqara in the light form like this reading.
His saying: {مَّتَاعاً}: There are two aspects for its accusative. One: that it is accusative as a maṣdar by dropping the additional letters, as the implied form is: "tamtīʿan"; so it is like His saying: {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. The second: that it is accusative as a direct object, "matāʿ" meaning the name of what is enjoyed, so it is like your saying: «متَّعْتُ زيداً أثواباً» ("I gave Zayd garments to enjoy").
His saying: {كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ}: «كلَّ» is the first object and «فضلَه» the second object; al-Suhaylī's disagreement on this has already been given. The pronoun in «فضله» may refer back to Allah the Exalted, that is: "He gives every possessor of merit his merit", that is, his reward; or refer back to the word «كل», that is: "He gives every possessor of merit the requital of his merit, not diminishing anything of it", that is, the requital of his deeds.
His saying: {وَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: The majority read «تَوَلَّوا» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the wāw and a doubled lām, and there are two possibilities in it. One: that the verb is the imperfect of tawallā, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped for lightness, like tanazzalu — which of the two was dropped has already been given — and this is the apparent one, and for that reason the address came in His saying «عليكم». The second: that it is a past verb ascribed to the pronoun of the absent plural, and the address came on the implication of saying, that is: "so say to them: I fear for you", and were it not for that, the construction would have been: «فإني أخاف عليهم».
Al-Yamānī and ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar read «تُوَلُّوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the wāw and ḍamma on the lām, which is the imperfect of wallā, like your saying zakkā yuzakkī. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» reported from al-Yamānī and ʿĪsā: «وإن تُوُلُّوا» with three ḍammas, passive. I say: he did not make clear what it is or its morphology. It is a past verb; when it was made passive its first letter was given ḍamma for the passive, and its second letter too, because it begins with a tāʾ of muṭāwaʿa (the reflexive, "compliance" tāʾ), and every verb that begins with a tāʾ of muṭāwaʿa has its first and second letters given ḍamma; and the lām was given ḍamma too, although its origin is kasra, because of the wāw of the pronoun; the origin is «تُوُلِّيُوا», like tudūḥirajū; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was dropped and two sukūns met, so the yāʾ was dropped because it was the first of them, leaving what precedes the wāw of the pronoun with kasra, which was given ḍamma to match the pronoun; its pattern thus became «تُفُعُّوا» with its lām dropped, and the wāw standing in place of the agent.
Al-Aʿraj read «تُوْلُوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, sukūn on the wāw and ḍamma on the lām, the imperfect of awlā; no weighty meaning appears for this reading here, and the object is omitted, to be implied in a way fitting the meaning.
And «كبير» is an adjective of «يوم», as an exaggeration of the terrors that occur in it. It was also said: rather «كبير» is an adjective of «عذاب», and it is accusative but was put in the genitive by proximity (jiwār), like their saying «هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» with «خَرِبٍ» in the genitive though it is an adjective of «جُحر», and the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2634 - كأن ثَبِيراً في عَرانين وَبْلِه ... كبيرُ أناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّل (As if Thabīr, amid the first drops of its downpour, were a great man of the people wrapped in a striped cloak)
with «مُزَمّل» in the genitive, though it is an adjective of «كبيرُ». The discussion of this has already been given at length in Sūrat al-Māʾida.

[Translator's note: In the source, the last paragraph («و "كبير" صفةٌ ل "يوم" …») appears without a heading and belongs to the commentary on {عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ}; also the source's sentence on «تُوْلُوا» and the omitted object ends without a full stop.]

His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَعَلَّكَ}: The best is that it be in its usual sense of hope (tarajjī) in relation to the one addressed. It was said: it is for the interrogative, as in his saying, peace be upon him: «لعلنا أعجلناك» ("Perhaps we have hurried you").
His saying: {وَضَآئِقٌ}: a conjunction on «تارك». He turned away from «ضيّق», although it is more frequent than «ضائق». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "to show that it is a passing straitness, not a lasting one; and the like of it are sayyid and jawād, so when you want occurrence you say sāʾid and jāʾid." The Shaykh said: "This ruling is not specific to these words; rather everything built from the triliteral for permanence and settledness on a pattern other than fāʿil is returned to it when the meaning of occurrence is wanted; you say ḥāsin, thāqil and sāmin for ḥasuna, thaqula and samuna", and he cited:
2638 - بمنزلةٍ أمَا اللئيمُ فسامِنٌ ... بها وكرامُ الناسِ بادٍ شُحوبُها (In a position where the mean one grows fat in it, while the noble among people show pallor)
It was also said: he turned from «ضيِّق» to «ضائق» only to match the pattern of «تارك».
The hāʾ in «به» refers back to «بعض»; it was said: to «ما»; it was said: to the denial. And «صدرُك» is the agent of «ضائق». It is also permissible that «ضائقٌ» be a fronted khabar and «صدرك» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a khabar for the kāf in «لعلك», so that it reports with two khabars, one a single word and the other a clause conjoined to a single word, since it is in its meaning; so it is like «إنَّ زيداً قائم وأبوه منطلق», that is: «إن زيداً أبوه منطلق» ("Zayd, his father is departing").
His saying: {أَن يَقُولُواْ}: It is in the position of accusative or genitive according to the well-known disagreement about «أنْ» after the dropping of the preposition or the muḍāf, its implied form being: "out of dislike or fear that they say", or "so that they do not say", or "by their saying". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لأن يقولوا», that is, «لأَنْ قالوا», so it is in the sense of the past"; there is no need for this, and how can this be claimed for it when with it is that which is explicit for the future, namely the accusative-governing particle? And «لولا» is exhortative, and the exhortative clause is accusative as the object of saying.

His saying, the Exalted: {أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلِ}: «ما» may be a restrictive particle that prepares (kāffa muhayyiʾa). In «أُنْزِل» there is a pronoun referring to what is revealed to you; «بعلمٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "connected with His knowledge". It is also permissible that «ما» be a relative, either a noun or a particle, being the ism of «إنَّ», the khabar being the preposition and its noun, the implied form being: "so know that its sending down", or "that what was sent down is connected with knowledge".
Zayd b. ʿAlī read «نَزَّل» with fatḥa on the nūn and a doubled zāy, the agent of «نَزَّل» being a pronoun of Allah the Exalted; and {وَأَن لاَّ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} is a conjunction on the preceding «أنَّ», but this one is lightened, so its ism is omitted and the negative clause is its khabar.
His saying: {نُوَفِّ}: The majority read «نُوَفِّ» with the nūn of majesty and a doubled fāʾ, from waffā yuwaffī; Ṭalḥa and Maymūn read it with the yāʾ of the third person, and Zayd b. ʿAlī likewise, except that he lightened the fāʾ, from awfā yūfī; the agent in these two readings is a pronoun of Allah the Exalted. «تُوَفَّ» was also read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled fatḥa on the fāʾ, from wafā yuwaffā, passive, with «أعمالُهم» nominative standing in place of the agent. «نُوَفِّ» is jussive on these readings because it is the apodosis of the condition, as in His saying, the Exalted: {مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الآخرة نَزِدْ لَهُ [فِي حَرْثِهِ] وَمَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدنيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنهَا} [al-Shūrā: 20].
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that «كان» is redundant, and said: "for that reason he made its apodosis jussive". Perhaps this is not sound, since if it were redundant, «يريد» would be the condition, and if it were the condition it would be jussive, and one would say «مَنْ كان يُرِدْ».
Some claimed that the verb of the condition is not put in the past with the apodosis in the imperfect except with «كان» in particular, and for this reason it has come in the Qurʾān only so. This is not correct, for it occurs with other than «كان». Zuhayr said:
2639 - ومَنْ هاب أسبابَ المنايا يَنَلْنَه ... ولو رام أسبابَ السماء بسُلَّمِ (Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he were to seek the causes of heaven by a ladder)
As for the Qurʾān, it came about by coincidence that it is so.
Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «نوفِي» with a light fāʾ and the yāʾ retained, from awfā. This reading admits that the verb is jussive, its jussive being implied by the dropping of an implied vowel, as in the saying:
2640 - ألم يَأْتيك والأنباءُ تُنمي ... بما لاقَتْ لَبُونُ بني زياد (Has it not come to you — and news spreads — what the milch-camel of Banū Ziyād met with?)
considering that this can occur in ordinary speech, like {إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقِ} [Yūsuf: 90], which will come with full treatment in its sūra; and it admits that the verb is nominative, because the condition occurs in the past, as in the saying:
2641 - وإنْ شُلَّ رَيْعانُ الجميعِ مخافةً ... نقولُ جِهاراً ويَلْكُمْ لا تُنَفِّروا (And if the front of the whole company is scattered in fear, we say openly: Woe to you, do not cause stampede)
and as in the saying of Zuhayr:
2642 - وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مَسْألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ (And if a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden)
Is the nominative because it is on the intention of fronting, which is the view of Sībawayh, or on the intention of the fāʾ, as is the view of al-Mubarrad? A well-known disagreement.

His saying, the Exalted: {وَحَبِطَ مَا صَنَعُواْ فِيهَا}: It is permissible that «فيها» be attached to «حَبِط», and the pronoun on this refers to the Hereafter, that is: "and the nullity of what they did became manifest in the Hereafter". It is permissible that it be attached to «صنعوا», in which case the pronoun refers to the life of this world, as it referred to it in His saying {نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فِيهَا}. And «ما» in «ما صنعوا» may be in the sense of «الذي» with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "what they did"; or a maṣdar particle: "and their doing became void".
His saying: {وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُواْ}: The majority read it with «الباطل» nominative, and there are three aspects. One: that «باطل» is a fronted khabar and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} a postponed mubtadaʾ; and «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, that is: "and their having been doers is void", or in the sense of «الذي» with the returning pronoun omitted, that is: "what they used to do"; this on the basis that the speech is of the conjunction of clauses, this clause being conjoined to what precedes it. Second: that «باطل» is a mubtadaʾ and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} its khabar; so said Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib, and it is not far from a mistake, and the wonder is that he mentioned nothing else. Third: that «باطل» is conjoined to the khabars before it, that is: "those: void is what they used to do", and {مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ} is the agent of «باطل»; this is supported by what Zayd b. ʿAlī read: {وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}, making it a past verb conjoined to «حَبِط».
Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read, Makkī said "and it is so in their codex", and al-Zamakhsharī reported it from ʿĀṣim, «وباطلاً» in the accusative, and there are three aspects. One: that it is accusative by «يعملون» with «ما» redundant; to this Makkī, Abū l-Baqāʾ and the author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» leaned; and it involves putting the governed word of the khabar of «كان» before «كان», a matter of disagreement, the correct view being that it is permissible, as in His saying, the Exalted: {أهؤلاء إِيَّاكُمْ كَانُواْ يَعْبُدُونَ} [Sabaʾ: 40], where the apparent sense is that «إياكم» is accusative by «يعبدون». The second: that «ما» is indefinite-intensifying (mubhama) and is accusative by «يعملون», its meaning being: "a falsehood, what a falsehood they used to do". The third: that «باطلاً» is in the sense of a maṣdar, "what they used to do became void, a voiding". Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these two aspects. The meaning of his saying that «ما» is mubhama is that here it is an adjective of the indefinite noun before it, and for that reason he implied it as «باطلاً أيَّ باطل»; it is therefore like the saying:
2643 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وحديثٌ ما على قِصَرِهْ (… and a tale, such a tale, for all its brevity)
and «لأمرٍ ما جَدَعَ قصيرٌ أَنْفَه» ("It was for some matter that Qaṣīr cut off his nose"), and he has already given that in His saying, the Exalted: {مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً} [al-Zumar: 9].

[Translator's note: the source cites {مَثَلاً مَّا بَعُوضَةً} as al-Zumar: 9, which is probably an error for al-Baqara: 26; translated as written.]

Allah Teâlâ'nın şu sözü: {مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: Buradaki «ما» için üç vecih câizdir. Birincisi: nefy (olumsuzluk) «ما»sı olmasıdır. Bu, onlar işitme ve görme sahibi olsalar da, bunlardan fayda görmedikleri için bunu onlardan nefyetmiş olur; yahut işitme ve görmenin müteallik olduğu (konusu) belirli bir şeydir. İkincisi: masdariyye «ما»sı olmasıdır. Bu durumda iki te'vîl vardır. Biri: «ما»nın zarfın yerine geçmesidir; yani «istitâatleri müddetince». Bu takdirde «ما», «يُضاعف» ile mansûbdur; yani «işitmeye ve görmeye güçleri yettiği müddetçe kendilerine azap katlanır». İkinci te'vîl: «ما»nın, câr harfinin düşürülmesiyle mahallen mansûb olmasıdır; nitekim «أنْ» ve «أنَّ» ile (bu ikisi birbirinin kardeşidir) câr harfi hazfedilir. Ferrâ bu görüşe gitmiştir. Bu câr da yine «يُضاعَف»e müteallik olur; yani «işitip görmeleri, fakat yararlanmamaları sebebiyle kendilerine azap katlanır». Üçüncüsü: «ما»nın «الذي» (ism-i mevsûl) anlamında olması ve yine câr harfinin hazfi üzerine olmasıdır; yani «بالذي كانوا». Bunda uzaklık vardır, çünkü harfin hazfi kıyasa uygun (düzenli) değildir.
«يُضاعف» sözündeki cümle isti'nâfiyyedir. Şöyle de denmiştir: «ما كانوا» sözündeki zamir «أولياء»ya döner; bunlar da onların ilâhlarıdır; yani «gerçekte onların hiçbir veli (dost, koruyucu) yoktu; her ne kadar onların veli olduklarına inansalar da». Buna göre {يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ العذاب} cümlesi i'tirâziyyedir (araya girmiş cümle).

His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا نَرَاكَ}: It may be of the heart (qalbiyya, "we think") or of the eye (baṣariyya, "we see"). On the first, the clause of His saying «اتَّبعك» is in the position of accusative as a second object; on the second, it is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, with «قد» implied according to those who stipulate that.
Al-arādhil: there are two aspects. One: that it is a plural of a plural; the second: only a plural. Those who say the first differed: it was said that it is a plural of «أَرْذُل», and «أَرْذُل» is a plural of «رَذْل», like kalb, aklub and akālib. It was said: rather it is a plural of «أَرْذال», and «أَرْذال» is also a plural of «رَذْل». Those who say that it is not a plural of a plural, but only a plural, said: it is a plural of «أَرْذُل», and it is permissible that it be a plural of «أَرْذُل» only because it is treated like nouns, in that what it qualifies has been abandoned, like al-abṭaḥ and al-abraq. Some of them said: it is the plural of the comparative «أَرْذَل», and it came as a plural as {أَكَابِرَ مُجَرِمِيهَا} [al-Anʿām: 123] and {أحاسِنُكم أخلاقاً} [al-Anʿām: 123] came. One says: a man is radhl and rudhāl, like rakhl and rukhāl, meaning one who is turned away from because of his inferiority.
His saying: {بَادِيَ الرأي}: Abū ʿAmr, of the seven, and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «بادِئَ» with hamza, and the rest with a clear yāʾ in place of the hamza.
