Buradaki «كان»ın nâkıse olması zayıftır; çünkü mana buna uzaktır. Nâkıse olduğu takdir edilirse, «من القرون»un mahzûfa hâl olarak müteallik olması zorunlu olur; çünkü nahivcilerin çoğuna göre nâkıse «kâne» amel etmez ve «يَنْهَوْن» «كان»ın haberi olarak nasb mahallinde olur.

Âmme «بَقِيَّة»yi «bâ» fethalı ve «yâ» şeddeli okumuştur. Bunda iki vecih vardır: Birincisi: mübalağa için «fe'île» vezninde, fâil manasında bir sıfattır; bu yüzden ona «te» girmiştir. O zaman kastedilen, bir şeyin ordusu (cündü) ve seçkinidir. Bir şeyin ordusuna ve seçkinine «bakıyye» denmesi, «Filan insanların bakıyyesidir, cömertlerin bakıyyesidir» sözlerindendir; çünkü kişi, çıkardığı şeyden en iyisini ve en faziletlisini alıkoyar. Hamâse beyti de buna yorumlanmıştır:
2730 - إنْ تُذْنِبُوا ثم تَأْتِيني بقيَّتُكم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Beyit anlamı: Günah işleyip sonra bana, aranızdan geriye kalan seçkinlerinizle gelirseniz…) [Mütercim notu: Beyit kaynakta yarım bırakılmıştır.]
Atasözü: «Köşelerde gizli şeyler, insanlar arasında geriye kalanlar vardır.»

İkincisi: «el-bakvâ» manasında bir masdardır. Zemahşerî der ki: «Bakıyye, “et-takıyye”nin “et-takvâ” manasına olduğu gibi “el-bakvâ” manasına olabilir; yani: Neden onlardan, kendilerini esirgeyen, kendilerini Allah'ın gazabından ve azabından koruyan sahipler bulunmadı?»

Bir grup, «yâ»yı hafif okuyarak «بَقِيَة» diye okumuştur; bu, «şeciye»nin «şeciye»den gelmesi gibi «bakıye»den ism-i fâildir. Takdir: «أولو طائفةٍ بَقِيةٍ», yani kalan bir topluluğun sahipleri. Ebû Ca'fer ve Şeybe «بُقْية» diye, «fâ» zammeli ve «ayn» sakin olarak okumuştur. «بَقْيَة» diye de okunmuştur; masdarın bir kez olması (merre) üzere. «في الأرض», «الفساد»a mütealliktir; «el» ile birlikte gelen masdar sarih mef'ûllerde amel ediyorsa zarflarda nasıl amel etmesin? Mahzûfa, «الفساد»dan hâl olarak müteallik olması da caizdir.

Onun sözü: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}: Bunda iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: munkatı' istisnâ olmasıdır. Bu, tahdîzin hakikî manasına hamledilmesiyle olur; hakikatine hamledilince, mananın bozulmaması için istisnânın munkatı' olması zorunlu hâle gelir.

Zemahşerî [kaynakta “Zemşahrî” yazılıdır] der ki: «Manası: “Ancak nesillerden kurtardıklarımızdan az bir kısmı fesattan nehyedildi; geri kalanlar nehyi terk edenlerdi.”» Sonra şöyle der: «Bu istisnânın muttasıl olmasına yüklenebilecek bir vecih var mıdır dersen? Derim ki: Onu kelamın zâhirine göre muttasıl yaparsan mana bozulur; çünkü bu, “bakıyye” sahiplerinin fesattan nehyetmeye teşvik edilmeleri olur, ancak onlardan kurtulanların az bir kısmı hariç. Tıpkı “Kavmin Kur'an'ı okusaydı, ancak içlerindeki salihler hariç” demen gibi; Kur'an okumaya teşvik edilenlerden salihleri istisna etmeyi kastedersin.» Ben derim ki: Çünkü söz, kurtulanların fesattan nehyetmeye teşvik edilmemiş olmalarına varır ki bu bozuk bir manadır.

İkincisi: muttasıl olmasıdır. Bu, tahdîzin nefiy manasına te'vil edilmesiyle olur ve böylece sahih olur; ancak bu, mûcib olmayan (olumlu olmayan) bir yerde nasbe götürür, ancak nasbten başkası evlâdır. Zemahşerî der ki: «Onları fesattan nehyetmeye teşvik etmede, onlardan bunun nefyi manası vardır; sanki şöyle denmiştir: “Nesillerden bakıyye sahibi, az bir kısmı dışında, bulunmadı.” Böylece istisnâ muttasıl ve mana sahih olur, nasbı istisnânın aslına göre olur; ancak en fasih olan, bedel olarak ref' edilmesidir.» Ben derim ki: Buradaki tahdîzin nefiy manasında olduğunu destekleyen şey, Zeyd b. Ali'nin «إلا قليلٌ» şeklinde ref'li okumasıdır; nefiy manasını gözetmiş ve en fasih olan şekilde bedel yapmıştır, {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [النساء: 66] sözü gibi. Ferrâ da demiştir ki: «Mana: “Olmadı” şeklindedir; çünkü istifhamda bir tür inkâr vardır.» Tahdîzi istifham diye adlandırmıştır. Ahfeş'ten, bu istisnânın muttasıl olmasının zorunlu olduğunu düşündüğü nakledilmiştir; sanki nefiy manasını gözetmiştir.

«مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنا»daki «مِن» tebʻîz (kısmilik) içindir. Zemahşerî onun tebʻîz için olmasını reddetmiş, bilakis beyân için olduğunu söylemiştir: «Hakkı beyân için olmaktır, tebʻîz için değil; çünkü kurtuluş yalnızca nehyedenlere aittir; Azîz ve Celîl olan Allah'ın şu sözü buna delildir: {أَنجَيْنَا الذين يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ السواء وَأَخَذْنَا الذين ظَلَمُواْ بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ} [الأعراف: 165].» Ben derim ki: Birinciye göre, «قليلاً»in sıfatı olarak mahzûfa mütealliktir; ikinciye göre ise beyân yoluyla mahzûfa müteallik olur, yani «أعني».

Onun sözü: {واتبع}: Âmme «أتَّبع» diye, vasl hemzesi, şeddeli «te» ve fethalı «bâ» ile okumuştur; malum meçhul değil, fâili belli mâzî fiildir. Bunda iki vecih vardır: Birincisi: gizli bir zamire atfedilmiştir; ikincisi: «vav» atıf için değil hâl içindir. Bu, Zemahşerî'nin şu sözüyle açıklık kazanır: «{واتبع الذين ظَلَمُواْ} sözü neye atfedilmiştir dersen? Derim ki: Manası “şehvetlere uydular” ise gizli bir şeye atıf olur; çünkü mana şöyledir: “Ancak kurtardıklarımızdan az bir kısmı fesattan nehyedildi ve zulmedenler şehvetlerine uydular”; o hâlde «نُهوا»ya atıftır. Manası “nimete boğulmanın karşılığına uydular” ise «vav» hâl içindir; sanki şöyle denmiştir: “Azını kurtardık, oysa zulmedenler karşılıklarına uymuşlardı.”»

Ben derim ki: «ما أُتْرفوا» sözünde iki vecih caiz görmüştür: Birincisi: muzâf hazfedilmeksizin mef'ûldür; «ما» şehvetlere ve sebebiyle şımardıkları nimetlere delâlet eder. İkincisi: muzâfın hazfi üzeredir, yani «جزاء ما أترفوا»; ve «واتَّبع» hakkındaki sözü bu iki vecih üzerine kurmuştur, bildiğin gibi.

«el-İtrâf»: «terf»den «if'âl» vezninde olup nimettir; «sabiyyün mutrefün», yani bedeni nimetlendirilmiş çocuk denir. «أُتْرفوا»: nimetlendiler. Şöyle de denmiştir: «et-turfe» nimette genişliktir.

Ebû Amr, Cu'fî ve Ca'fer rivayetinde «وأُتبع» diye, kat' hemzesi zammeli, «te» sakin, «bâ» kesreli ve meçhul olarak okumuştur; o zaman muzâfın hazfi zorunludur, yani «أُتْبِعوا جزاء ما أُتْرفوا فيه». «ما»nın «الذي» manasında olması caizdir ve zâhir olan budur, çünkü «فيه»deki zamir ona dönmektedir; masdariyye olması da caizdir, yani «onların nimete boğulmalarının karşılığı».

Onun sözü: {وَكَانُواْ مُجْرِمِينَ}: Bunda üç vecih vardır. Birincisi: «ما»yı masdariyye kılarsak «أُتْرِفُوا»ya atıftır, yani: «Şımarmalarına ve suçlu olmalarına uydular.» İkincisi: «اتَّبع»a atıftır, yani: «Şehvetlerine uydular ve bu sebeple suçlu oldular; çünkü şehvetlere uyan günahlara gömülmüştür.» Üçüncüsü: i'tirâz ve onlar hakkında «onlar suçlu bir kavimdir» hükmüdür; bunu Zemahşerî zikretmiştir. Şeyh der ki: «Buna nahiv ıstılahında i'tirâz denmez; çünkü bu, âyetin sonudur ve birbirine muhtaç iki şey arasında değildir.»

* İ'rab:
(قال) mâzî fiil, fâili «هو» (إنّما) kâffe ve mekfûfe (يأتي) merfû muzâri, ref' alâmeti yâ üzerinde takdîrî damme; (كم) mef'ûlün bih zamiri (الباء) cer harfi (الهاء) cer mahallinde zamir, (يأتي)'ye müteallik, (الله) lafzatullah, merfû fâil (إن) şart harfi (شاء) mâzî fiil, fiilü'ş-şart olarak cezm mahallinde, fâili «هو»; mef'ûlü mahzûftur, yani «شاء تعجيله لكم» (الواو) hâl vâvı (ما) «ليس» amelini yapan nefy «ما»sı (أنتم) ayrı zamir, ref' mahallinde «ما»nın ismi (الباء) habere ziyade edilmiş zâide cer harfi (معجزين) mahallen mansûb, lafzen mecrûr; cer alâmeti yâ.
«قال ...» cümlesi beyânî isti'nâf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«يأتيكم به الله» cümlesi mekûlü'l-kavl olup nasb mahallindedir.
«إن شاء ...» cümlesi i'tirâziyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; cevâbü'ş-şart mahzûftur, yani «فإنّ أمره إلى الله».
«ما أنتم بمعجزين» cümlesi «يأتيكم»deki hitap zamirinden hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir.
(الواو) atıf harfi (لا) nefy harfi (ينفع) merfû muzâri; (كم) mef'ûlün bih zamiri (نصحي) merfû fâil, ref' alâmeti yâdan önceki harf üzerinde takdîrî damme.. (الياء) muzâfun ileyh (إن أردت) «إن شاء» gibidir.. (التاء) fâil (أن) masdar ve nasb harfi (أنصح) mansûb muzâri, fâili «أنا» (اللام) cer harfi; (كم) cer mahallinde zamir, (أنصح)'a müteallik, (إن كان) «كنت» gibidir [Dipnot: Önceki (32). âyette.], (الله) lafzatullah, kâne'nin merfû ismi (يريد) «ينفع» gibidir, fâili «هو» (أن يغوي) «أن أنصح» gibidir; (كم) mef'ûlün bih (هو) ayrı zamir, mebnî olup ref' mahallinde mübtedâ (ربّكم) merfû haber ve muzâfun ileyh (الواو) atıf harfi (إلى) cer harfi; (الهاء) cer mahallinde zamir, (ترجعون)'a müteallik; o da meçhul merfû muzâridir.. (الواو) nâib-i fâil.
(أن أنصح) müevvel masdarı mef'ûlün bih olarak nasb mahallindedir; âmili «أردت»tir.
(أن يغويكم) müevvel masdarı mef'ûlün bih olarak nasb mahallindedir; âmili «يريد»dir.
«لا ينفعكم نصحي» cümlesi «يأتيكم به الله» cümlesine ma'tûf olup nasb mahallindedir.
«أردت ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.. Cevâbü'ş-şart mahzûftur; öncesi ona delâlet etmektedir; yani: «فلا ينفعكم نصحي».
«إن كان الله ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.. Cevâbü'ş-şart mahzûftur; birinci şart ve cevabı ona delâlet etmektedir; yani: «إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي» [Dipnot: Hâşiyetü'l-Cemel'de şöyle gelmiştir: «İkinci şartın cevabı, birinci şart ve cevabıdır. Takdir: وإن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي. Bunun sebebi şudur: Sözde iki şart ve bir cevap bir araya gelirse, ikinci şart birincide şart kılınır; dolayısıyla cevap ancak ikinci şart gerçekleşip dış dünyada birinciden önce var olursa vuku bulur; çünkü şart dış dünyada meşrûttan öncedir. Eğer iş tersine dönüp önce birincisi var olursa, ona bağlanan şey vuku bulmaz. Bir kimse kölesine "أنت حرّ إن كلّمت زيدا إن دخلت داره" (Zeyd'le konuşursan, evine girersen hürsün) dese, ancak Zeyd'le konuşmadan önce eve girme gerçekleşirse azat olur.. Beyzâvî'nin ibaresi şöyledir: Sözün takriri: إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم فإن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي.» (Nakil burada biter.) Yani Resûl'ün istemesi hâlinde nasihatin fayda vermesi ancak Allah'ın iradesi şartıyla tamam olur.].
«أنصح ...» cümlesi harfî mevsûl (أن)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«أن يغويكم» cümlesi ikinci harfî mevsûl (أن)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«هو ربّكم» cümlesi ta'lîliyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«ترجعون» cümlesi ta'lîliyye cümleye ma'tûf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* Sarf:
(نصح): «نصح ينصح» (fe-te-ha bâbı) fiilinin semâî masdarı, vezni fâsı ötreli فعل. Başka masdarlar da vardır: nûnu fethalı «نصح», nûnu fethalı ve kesralı «نصاحة» ve nûnu fethalı «نصاحية».

* Fevâid:
- Bir şartın diğerine itirazı (araya girmesi):
Bu âyet-i kerîmede iki şart gelmiştir; o da Allah Teâlâ'nın وَلا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ هُوَ رَبُّكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ kavlidir. İbn Hişâm şöyle demiştir: Bu âyette tartışma vardır; zira şairin şu sözünde olduğu gibi iki şart art arda gelip ardından bir cevap gelmemiştir:
إن تستغيثوا بنا إن تذعروا تجدوا ... منا معاقيل عزّ زانها كرم
(Korkutulur da bizden yardım dilerseniz, bizde cömertliğin süslediği izzet kaleleri bulursunuz.)
Zira âyet-i kerîmede cevap zikredilmemiştir; ancak iki şarttan önce, mânâ bakımından birinci şartın cevabı olan şey gelmiştir; dolayısıyla onun yanında takdir edilmesi gerekir. Asıl şöyledir: «إن أردت أن أنصح لكم فلا ينفعكم نصحي إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم». Fakihler buna bir hüküm bina etmişlerdir: Biri «إن أكلت إن شربت فأنت طالق» (Yersen, içersen boşsun) derse, kadın sonrakini öne almadıkça ve öncekini sona bırakmadıkça boş olmaz; çünkü bu durumda takdir şöyledir: «إن شربت فإن أكلت فأنت طالق»; cevap da ikisinden önce gelene aittir.

* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قيل) past verb, passive (يا) vocative particle (أرض) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative (ابلعي) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الياء) an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent) (ماءك) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الواو) conjunction (يا سماء أقلعي) like يا أرض ابلعي (الواو) conjunction (غيض) like قيل, (الماء) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) (الواو) conjunction (قضي الأمر) like غيض الماء (الواو) conjunction (استوت) past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.. and the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is "it", i.e. the Ark (على الجوديّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استوت), (الواو) conjunction (قيل) like the first (بعدا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. ابعدوا or بعدوا, by way of imprecation (للقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the maṣdar (بعدا) [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: The lām in (للقوم) belongs to the complement of the maṣdar; a group disallowed attaching it to the maṣdar and said it is attached to His saying (قيل), the implied meaning being: and it was said for the sake of the wrongdoers, since one who has perished cannot be addressed except figuratively. Someone else said: it is for specification and clarification, attached to (قيل).. And it was said: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being "the imprecation", i.e. the imprecation is against the wrongdoing people.. so there are two clauses in the construction..
(2, 3) Because it is originally the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).. The majority make the nāʾib fāʿil omitted, its implied form being (القول), and the clause explicative.], (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا أرض ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «2».
The clause «ابلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «يا سماء ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يا أرض.
The clause «أقلعي ...» has no grammatical position; the reply to the second vocative.
The clause «غيض الماء ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قضي الأمر ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «استوت على الجوديّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «قيل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «(بعد) بعدا..» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil «3».

* Morphology:
(غيض): in it the alif reverts to yāʾ and the first radical (fāʾ) of the word takes kasra
to suit the yāʾ.
(استوت): in it there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by dropping because of the meeting of two quiescents: the alif came quiescent before the tāʾ of the feminine and was dropped; its pattern is افتعت.
(الجوديّ): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for a specific mountain; and it is said: every mountain is called a jūdī.
(بعدا): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb بعد يبعد, of the كرم class, its pattern being فُعْل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- This noble āya is examined from four angles: from the angle of the science of bayān and from the angle of the science of maʿānī – these two being the foundations of rhetoric – and from the angle of eloquence of meaning and the angle of eloquence of wording. As for examining it from the angle of the science of bayān, which is examining the majāz (figurative usage), the istiʿāra (metaphor) and the kināya (metonymy) in it, and what is connected with that of the qarīna (contextual indicator), the tarshīḥ (reinforcement of the metaphor) and the taʿrīḍ (allusion): when He, mighty is His dominion, wanted to build the meaning: "We wanted to return what had burst forth from the earth to its belly, so it returned; and to cut off the deluge of the sky, so it was cut off; and to make the water that came down from the sky abate, so it abated; and to accomplish the affair of Nūḥ, peace be upon him – which is fulfilling what We had promised him of drowning his people – so it was accomplished; and to settle the Ark on al-Jūdī, so it settled; and We left the wrongdoers drowned," He, glory be to Him, built the speech on likening the thing intended with this to one commanded, from whom disobedience is impossible – because of the perfect awe in which he holds the commander – and on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive command, effective in bringing about what is sought, as a depiction of His immense power, glory be to Him, and that these immense bodies of the heavens and the earth follow His will, the Exalted, in bringing into existence and annihilating, and follow His wish concerning them in alteration and change, as if they were rational, discerning beings. Then upon the combination of the two similes He built the composition of the speech, and He, majestic and exalted, said: «قيل ...» as a majāz for will, of the type of mentioning the effect and intending the cause, because will is a cause of the occurrence of speech in general; and He made the qarīna of this majāz the addressing of inanimate things, namely «يا أرض ...» «ويا سماء ...»; and this address to the earth and the sky is by way of istiʿāra, because of the mentioned resemblance. What appears is that he [Translator's note: the author being drawn upon, unnamed here] meant there is an istiʿāra bi-l-kināya (implicit metaphor) here, since the thing likened is mentioned (I mean the sky and the earth, from which the occurrence of a matter is intended) and what it is likened to is intended (I mean the one commanded who is described as being incapable of disobedience, by way of claim), with the qarīna being the attribution of the address to it and the entry of the vocative particle upon it – both of these being properties of the obedient one commanded – and this would be a takhyīl (imaginative attribution). Then for the sinking of water into the earth He borrowed "swallowing", which is the action of drawing food in, because of the resemblance between them, namely going to a hidden resting place.
In al-Kashshāf: "swallowing" is made a metaphor for the earth's soaking up of the water, and this is better, because soaking up indicates a drawing by the parts of the earth of what is on it, like swallowing in relation to an animal, and because soaking up is the action of the earth while sinking is the action of the water, together with the correspondence (ṭibāq) between the two verbs in transitivity. Then He borrowed "water" for food by way of istiʿāra bi-l-kināya, likening it to food, because the earth gains strength through water in growing crops and trees as the eater gains strength through food; and He made the qarīna of the metaphor the word «ابلعي ...», because it is coined for use with food and not with water.
Then He, majestic and exalted, said: «ماءك ...», annexing the water to the earth, by way of majāz, likening the connection of the water with the earth to the connection of property with the owner; and He chose the pronoun of address for the sake of tarshīḥ. Its upshot is that there is a linguistic majāz in the annexation form that indicates possessive specification, and for this reason the address was made a tarshīḥ for this metaphor, in that the address indicates the earth's fitness for ownership.
Then for the withholding of the rain He chose "desisting" (iqlāʿ), which is an agent's leaving off an action, because of the resemblance between them in the cessation of what there was of rain or action; so in «أقلعي ...» there is an istiʿāra with respect to its substance, and likewise with respect to its form as well. It is built on likening the bringing into being of what is intended to a decisive, effective command, and the address in it is also a tarshīḥ of the metaphor of the vocative.
Then He, glory be to Him, said «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْداً ...»
So He, majestic and exalted, did not state explicitly who made the water abate, nor who accomplished the affair, settled the Ark and said "away with". Likewise He, glory be to Him, did not state explicitly the one who said «يا أَرْضُ ...» «وَيا سَماءُ ...» at the beginning of the āya, following in each of these the path of kināya, because those immense matters issue only from One possessed of power whose essence cannot be fathomed, an Overpowering One who cannot be overcome; so there is no room for the imagination to go to someone other than Him, majestic is His greatness, being the one saying «يا أَرْضُ ...» and «يا سَماءُ ...», nor the one making abate what abated, nor the one accomplishing such a dreadful affair, nor that the settling and fixing of the Ark could be by the settling of anyone else.
Then He, the Exalted, sealed the speech with taʿrīḍ, as a warning to those who tread the path of those people in denying the messengers, peace be upon them, wronging only themselves and nothing else; and as a display of the place of displeasure and of the respect in which they deserved it, and that the rising of the deluge and that dreadful scene were only because of their wrongdoing, as the imprecation of destruction after their destruction announces, and the description with wrongdoing together with the ruling being tied to it.
As for examining it from the angle of the science of maʿānī, which is examining the benefit of each word in it and the reason for each fronting and postponing among its clauses: «يا ...» was chosen rather than the rest of its sisters because it is more frequent in use, and because it indicates the distance of the one addressed, which the situation of displaying greatness and showing the dignity of might and omnipotence calls for. As for looking at the order of the clauses: the vocative was put before the command, so it was said: «يا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي ...» «وَيا سَماءُ أَقْلِعِي ...»
rather than saying: "Swallow, O earth, and desist, O sky", following what is required – in the case of one who is truly commanded – of putting the alerting first, so that the command coming after it may settle firmly in the soul of the one addressed, intending thereby the meaning of tarshīḥ for the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in the earth and the sky. Then He put the command to the earth before the command to the sky, because it is the origin, given that the deluge began from it, as its oven gushed forth first.
All this is examining the āya from the two sides of rhetoric. Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ mentioned that it contains twenty kinds of badīʿ (embellishment), although it is seventeen words, namely: complete correspondence (munāsaba tāmma) in «ابلعي ...» and «اقلعي ...»; the istiʿāra in them; the ṭibāq (antithesis) between the earth and the sky; the majāz in «يا سَماءُ ...», for the literal is "O rain of the sky"; ishāra (allusion) in «وَغِيضَ الْماءُ ...», for many meanings are expressed by it, because the water does not abate until the rain of the sky desists and the earth swallows what comes out of it, so what is on the face of the earth decreases; irdāf (expressing by a consequent) in «وَاسْتَوَتْ ...»; tamthīl (representation) in «وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ ...»; taʿlīl (causation), for the abating of the water is the cause of the settling; ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm (sound division), for it covers the divisions of the water in the state of its decrease; iḥtirās (precaution) in the imprecation, lest it be imagined that the drowning, because of its generality, included those who did not deserve destruction, for His justice, the Exalted, prevents Him from invoking against one who does not deserve it; ḥusn al-nasaq (fine sequence); iʾtilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā (harmony of wording with meaning); ījāz (concision), for He, glory be to Him, told the story comprehensively in the briefest expression; tashīm (foreshadowing), because the beginning of the āya indicates its end; tahdhīb (refinement), because its individual words are described with attributes of beauty; ḥusn al-bayān (clarity of exposition), in that the listener does not hesitate in understanding the meaning of the speech and nothing of it is obscure to him; tamkīn (settledness), because the fāṣila (verse-ending) is settled in its place, at rest in its position; and insijām (flow). Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī added iʿtirāḍ (parenthesis).
[Translator's note: the list as given in the source names fewer than twenty kinds; it is translated as written.]

* Benefits:
1- Rhetorical inimitability in the Qur'an:
This āya comprises arts of rhetoric exceeding twenty-five arts, which the scholars of rhetoric have mentioned in detail and there is no room to set them out; one can only fall prostrate before the greatness of Allah, mighty and majestic, and bow before His inimitable expression, acknowledging that falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, a revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy. It is related that a great scholar tried to criticize the Noble Qur'an by discovering a simple flaw in it, and the attempt went on for months; he had a group who kept coming to him and asking him what he had done. But in the end he broke the pen and the inkwell and said: This is the speech of Allah; it is not to be disputed. Then he passed by a mosque and heard a boy reciting this āya, and he said: It is not for a human being to say speech like this.
2- Imām al-Nasafī's comment on this āya:
And from the angle of eloquence of meaning: it is, as you see, a subtle arrangement of the meanings, and a conveying of them summarized and made clear; no complexity besets the mind in seeking what is intended, and no twisting makes the road to the seeker doubtful. And from the angle of eloquence of wording: its words, as you see, are Arabic and in use, free from dissonance, far from ugliness, sweet on the tongue-tips, smooth on the tongue-edges; each of them is like water in smoothness, like honey in sweetness, and like the breeze in gentleness. Hence the obstinate opponents agreed that human capacity falls short of producing the like of this āya. How excellent is the status of the Revelation! A scholar does not contemplate one of its āyas without perceiving subtleties beyond counting; and do not think the āya is restricted to what has been mentioned, for perhaps what has been left out is more than what has been written.

* I'rab:
(قال يا نوح) its i'rab has been given [Note: In āya (32) of this sūra.], (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna (ليس) defective, non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (من أهلك) like من أهلي, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of laysa [Note: In the previous āya (45).] (إنّه) like the first (عمل) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessor of a deed" (ذو عمل) (غير) naʿt (adjective) of عمل, nominative (صالح) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (لا) prohibitive, putting into the jussive [Translator's note: the source has حازمة, evidently for جازمة] (تسألن) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm).. and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء), dropped for lightness, is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (ما) relative noun [Note: Or it is an indefinite noun qualified by what follows, meaning "a thing".. and the clause after it is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of it.], indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a second mafʿūl bihi (ليس) like the first (اللام) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the fronted khabar (به) like لك, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (علم), which is the postponed noun of laysa, nominative [Translator's note: the source has لبس, evidently for ليس] (إنّي) like إنّه (أعظ) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil (agent) is "I", and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (أن) maṣdar particle (تكون) defective imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, implied as "you" (من الجاهلين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of تكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being من, attached to (أعظك) in the sense of "I forbid you" [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: I admonish you out of dislike that you be among the ignorant.].
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يا نوح ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: Or it is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the clause after it is the object of the saying.].
The clause «إنّه ليس من أهلك» has no grammatical position; the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ليس من أهلك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «إنّه عمل ...» has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا تسألن ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: i.e. if knowledge of this has come to you, then do not ask Me ...
The clause «ليس لك به علم» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «إنّي أعظك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أعظك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).

* Benefits:
1- The infallibility (ʿiṣma) of the prophets:
Those who do not hold the infallibility of the prophets have taken these āyas as evidence, saying that what is meant by His saying, the Exalted, إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ is the asking, and it is forbidden; therefore He forbade him from it by His saying فَلا تَسْئَلْنِ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ; and His saying, glory be to Him and exalted, إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ indicates that that asking was ignorance, so it contains rebuke and threat; and seeking forgiveness and mercy for it indicates that a sin was committed. The answer is that Allah, mighty and majestic, had promised Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, that He would save him and his family; so Nūḥ took the apparent sense of the wording and followed the interpretation according to the apparent sense, not knowing what was hidden from him, and without doubting the promise of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted; so he ventured this question for this reason. Allah, mighty and majestic, then reproached him for asking about what he had no knowledge of, and made clear to him that he was not of his family whose rescue He had promised him, because of his disbelief and his deed, which is not righteous; and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, informed him that He would drown him with those who did wrong, and forbade him from addressing Him concerning them. So Nūḥ became fearful about his having ventured to ask his Lord about something he had not been permitted, and feared destruction from that; so he took refuge in his Lord, mighty and majestic, humbled himself before Him, sought refuge with Him, and asked Him for forgiveness and mercy, because the good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near. There is nothing in the āya that requires the commission of a sin or act of disobedience by Nūḥ, upon him be blessings and peace, other than his interpretation and his venturing to ask about what he had not been permitted, and this is neither a sin nor an act of disobedience. And in this incident there is said what was said concerning the Prophet's ﷺ ransoming of the captives of Badr; and Allah knows best.
2- Dropping the yāʾ for lightness:
In the Noble Qur'an the yāʾ is dropped from some nouns and verbs without a grammatical reason requiring it, and the grammarians said that the reason for its dropping is lightness; in parsing we consider it present and parse it. It occurs in this āya in His saying, the Exalted: فلا تسألن, originally فلا تسألني; the yāʾ was dropped for lightness, and it is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. In Sūrat al-Kahf there is His saying, the Exalted, ذلِكَ ما كُنَّا نَبْغِ, i.e. نبغي; and it also occurs in another place in the Noble Qur'an: وَإِذا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ; and in the previous āya there occurs رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي, i.e. (ربي). This is a feature of the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic, that distinguishes it from the speech of human beings; the dropping of the yāʾ has a purpose and wisdom, and harmony and accord with the concordant musical cadence of the Noble Qur'an, and in it there is a pointer to some subtle meanings. For example, in His saying, the Exalted, رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ there is a pointer to the nearness of Allah, mighty and majestic, to the servant and His answering him before he has completed the word (ربي). And Allah knows best.

* İ'rab:
(الواو) atıf harfi (إلى عاد) câr ve mecrûr, takdiri «أرسلنا» olan mahzûfa müteallik [Dipnot: Mecrûrun, «أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه» —25. âyet— sözündeki mecrûra ma'tûf olması caizdir; (أخاهم) de (نوحا)'ya ma'tûf olur; bu durumda atıf, müfredlerin atfı olur; tıpkı «ضرب زيد عمرا وبكر خالدا» dememiz gibi.. Ancak yukarıdaki i'rab, araya giren uzunluk sebebiyle daha yakındır; onda atıf, aşağıda geleceği üzere cümlelerin atfıdır.], (أخاهم) mahzûfun mansûb mef'ûlün bih'i, nasb alâmeti elif.. (وهم) [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «وهم» şeklindedir; kastedilen muhtemelen «هم»dir.] muzâfun ileyh zamir (هودا) (أخاهم)'dan mansûb bedel (قال) mâzî fiil (يا) nidâ harfi (قوم) mansûb muzâf münâdâ, nasb alâmeti, tahfif için hazfedilmiş yâdan önceki harf üzerinde takdîrî fetha; hazfedilmiş (الياء) muzâfun ileyh (اعبدوا) nûnun hazfi üzere mebnî emir fiil.. (الواو) fâil (الله) lafzatullah, mef'ûlün bih (ما) nefy harfi (اللام) cer harfi; (كم) cer mahallinde zamir, mukaddem habere müteallik (من) zâid cer harfi (إله) lafzen mecrûr, mahallen merfû muahhar mübtedâ (غير) «إله»in merfû sıfatı, mahallen ona tâbi'dir; (الهاء) muzâfun ileyh (إن) nefy harfi (أنتم) mebnî olup ref' mahallinde mübtedâ olan ayrı zamir (إلّا) hasr edatı (مفترون) merfû haber, ref' alâmeti vâv.
«(أرسلنا) إلى عاد ...» cümlesi kasem cevabı olan «أرسلنا نوحا» cümlesine ma'tûf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur [Dipnot: Bu sûrenin (25.) âyetinde.].
«قال ...» cümlesi beyânî isti'nâf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur [Dipnot: Veya «قد» takdiriyle (أخاهم)'dan hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir.].
«يا قوم ...» cümlesi mekûlü'l-kavl olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«اعبدوا ...» cümlesi nidânın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«ما لكم من إله غيره» cümlesi ta'lîliyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«إن أنتم إلّا مفترون» cümlesi söz kapsamındaki isti'nâf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* İ'rab:
(إن) nefy harfi (نقول) merfû muzâri; fâil «نحن» (إلّا) hasr edatı (اعترى) elif üzerinde takdîrî fetha üzere mebnî mâzî fiil; (الكاف) mef'ûlün bih zamir (بعض) merfû fâil (آلهتنا) bir öncekinin gibi [Dipnot: Bir önceki (53.) âyette.], (بسوء) câr ve mecrûr, (اعتراك)'e müteallik, (قال) mâzî fiil; fâil «هو» (إنّي أشهد) «إنّي أعوذ» gibi [Dipnot: Bu sûrenin (47.) âyetinde.], (الله) lafzatullah mansûb mef'ûlün bih; üzerine şahit tutulan şey mahzûftur, sonra gelen ona delâlet eder (الواو) atıf harfi (اشهدوا) «استغفروا» gibi bir fiil [Dipnot: Bu sûrenin (52.) âyetinde.], (أنّ) fiile benzeyen harf —nâsih—; (الياء) nasb mahallinde enne'nin ismi olan zamir (بريء) merfû haber (من) cer harfi (ما) masdar harfi (تشركون) merfû muzâri.. vâv fâil.
«إن نقول ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«اعتراك» cümlesi mekûlü'l-kavl olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«قال ...» cümlesi beyânî isti'nâf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«إنّي أشهد ...» cümlesi ikinci mekûlü'l-kavl olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«أشهد الله» cümlesi inne'nin haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«اشهدوا ...» cümlesi «إنّي أشهد..» cümlesine ma'tûf olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«تشركون» cümlesi harfî mevsûl (ما)'nın sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
(أنّي بريء..) müevvel masdarı mahzûf bir cer harfiyle cer mahallindedir, yani «بأنّي بريء..»; (اشهدوا)'ya müteallik.
(ما تشركون) müevvel masdarı «من» cer harfiyle cer mahallindedir; «بريء»e müteallik.
(من دون) câr ve mecrûr, «تشركون»un mahzûf mef'ûlünün sıfatı olan mahzûfa müteallik; yani «تشركون آلهة من دونه» (O'ndan başka ilâhları ortak koşuyorsunuz); (الهاء) muzâfun ileyh zamir (الفاء) mukadder bir şartın cevabını bağlayan rabıta harfi (كيدوا) «استغفروا» gibi «1», (النون) vikâye için; (الياء) mef'ûlün bih zamir (جميعا) «كيدوا»nın fâilinden mansûb hâl (ثمّ) atıf harfi (لا تنظروا) «لا تتولّوا» gibi «2», (النون) vikâye için; tahfif için hazfedilmiş (الياء) mef'ûlün bih zamir.
«كيدوني ...» cümlesi mukadder bir şartın cevabı olarak cezm mahallindedir; yani «إن استطعتم أن تكيدوني فكيدوني» (bana tuzak kurmaya gücünüz yetiyorsa kurun).
«لا تنظرون» cümlesi «كيدوني» cümlesine ma'tûftur.
(إنّي) birincisi gibi (توكّلت) mâzî fiil ve fâili (على الله) câr ve mecrûr, (توكّلت)'e müteallik, (ربّ) lafzatullahtan mecrûr bedel, cer alâmeti sonundaki takdîrî kesre; (الياء) muzâfun ileyh zamir (الواو) atıf harfi (ربّكم) birinci «ربّ»e ma'tûf, mecrûr.. (كم) muzâfun ileyh (ما) nefy harfi (من) zâid cer harfi (دابّة) lafzen mecrûr, mahallen merfû mübtedâ (إلّا) hasr edatı (هو) mübtedâ olan ayrı zamir (آخذ) «هو»nun merfû haberi (بناصيتها) câr ve mecrûr, «آخذ»a müteallik.. (ها) muzâfun ileyh (إنّ ربّي) i'rabı geçti [Dipnot: Bu sûrenin (41.) âyetinde.] (على صراط) câr ve mecrûr, inne'nin haberi olan mahzûfa müteallik (مستقيم) «صراط»ın mecrûr sıfatı.
«إنّي توكّلت ...» cümlesi öncekinin ta'lîli olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«توكّلت ...» cümlesi inne'nin haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«ما من دابة إلّا هو آخذ ...» cümlesi başka bir ta'lîl olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«هو آخذ ...» cümlesi «دابّة»nın haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«إنّ ربّي على صراط ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* Sarf:
(اعتراك): Bunda kalb yoluyla i'lâl vardır. Aslı «اعتري»dir; yâ fethadan sonra harekeli olarak gelince elife kalbedilmiş ve —sonunda elif ile— «اعترى» olmuştur. Vezni افتعل'dir. Kelimenin lâmı olan yâ, mücerredi «عرا يعرو» olan vâvdan dönüşmüştür; masdarı «عروة»dir.
(ناصية): Başın ön kısmının veya ön kısımda biten saçın adıdır. Kelimede kalb yoluyla i'lâl vardır: «نصوت الرجل» deriz, yani adamın perçeminden tuttum. Aslı —sadın kesresi ve vâvın fethasıyla— «ناصوة»dir; vâv harekeli olup öncesi meksûr olunca yâya kalbedilmiş ve «ناصية» olmuştur. Vezni فاعلة'dir. Perçemden tutmak, galebe ve kahırdan kinâyedir.

* Belâgat:
1- Teâlâ'nın «قالَ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ» kavlinde:
O, «أشهد الله واشهدوا» demiş, ona denk ve aynı mânâda olsun diye «وأشهدكم» dememiştir. Çünkü onun şirkten berî olduğuna Allah'ı şahit tutması sahih ve sâbittir; onları şahit tutması ise dinlerini hafife almaktan ve onlara pek aldırış etmediğini göstermekten başka bir şey değildir. Bu yüzden ikisi arasındaki farklılık sebebiyle birincinin lafzından udûl etmiş ve onu emir lafzıyla getirmiştir; tıpkı bir adamın, aralarındaki bağ kopmuş olan kimseye onunla alay ederek ve hâlini hafife alarak «اشهد عليّ أني لا أحبك» (seni sevmediğime şahit ol) demesi gibi. Bu bir cihettir. İkinci cihetten ise haber sîgası, ondan şahit tutmanın vuku bulduğunu haber vermekten başka bir ihtimal taşımaz; Allah'ı şahit tutması vâki ve muhakkak olduğundan, bu sahih ve sâbit bir şahit tutma olduğu için onu haber sîgasıyla ifade etmiştir; onlar tarafında ise dinlerini hafife almayı içeren emir sîgasıyla ifade etmiştir ki bu makamda murad ettiği de budur. Üçüncü cihetten ise, Allah Teâlâ'ya hitabı ile onlara hitabını birbirinden ayırmak için haber sîgasından emir sîgasına udûl etmiştir; Allah Teâlâ'ya hitabı, emir sîgasından daha yüce, daha şerefli ve muhatap için daha zengin/kapsamlı olan haber sîgasıyla ifade etmiştir.
2- Mecaz: Teâlâ'nın «ما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِناصِيَتِها» kavlinde; yani: O ancak onun mâliki, ona kâdir olandır; onu dilediği gibi tasarruf eder; o, Sübhânehû'ya karşı direnemez. Perçemden tutmanın kudret ve tasallut için kullanılması mecaz veya kinâyedir.
3- Temsîl: Teâlâ'nın «إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ» kavlinde; bu, burhânın içine dâhildir ve bir temsîl ve istiâredir. Çünkü Teâlâ kulların işlerine muttalidir, onlara sevap ve ikab ile karşılık verendir, kendisine sığınana kâfidir; tıpkı ana yol üzerinde durup onu muhafaza eden kimse gibi. Bu, Sübhânehû ve Teâlâ'nın «إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ» kavli gibidir.

* I'rab:
(إن) negative particle (نقول) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "we" (إلّا) particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (اعترى) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (بعض) fāʿil, nominative (آلهتنا) like the previous one [Note: In the previous āya (53).], (بسوء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اعتراك), (قال) past verb, and the fāʿil is "he" (إنّي أشهد) like إنّي أعوذ [Note: In āya (47) of this sūra.], (الله) the Word of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); the thing attested is omitted, indicated by what comes next (الواو) conjunction (اشهدوا) a verb like استغفروا [Note: In āya (52) of this sūra.], (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of anna (بريء) khabar (predicate), nominative (من) a preposition (ما) maṣdar particle (تشركون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «إن نقول ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «اعتراك» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّي أشهد ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the second saying.
The clause «أشهد الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «اشهدوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause إنّي أشهد..
The clause «تشركون» has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي بريء..) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. بأنّي بريء.., attached to (اشهدوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تشركون) is in the position of genitive by the preposition من, attached to بريء.
(من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted object of تشركون, i.e. "you associate gods besides Him", and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الفاء) linking to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition (كيدوا) like استغفروا «1», and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya) and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (جميعا) ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of كيدوا, accusative (ثمّ) conjunction (لا تنظروا) like لا تتولّوا «2», and (النون) is for protection and (الياء), dropped for lightness, is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «كيدوني ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you are able to plot against me, then plot against me.
The clause «لا تنظرون» is conjoined to the clause كيدوني.
(إنّي) like the first (توكّلت) past verb and its agent (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (توكّلت), (ربّ) badal (substitute) of the Word of Majesty, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on its end, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) conjunction (ربّكم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first ربّ, genitive.. and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi (ما) negative particle (من) redundant (zāʾida) preposition (دابّة) genitive in form, nominative in position, mubtadaʾ (subject) (إلّا) particle of restriction (هو) detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (آخذ) khabar of هو, nominative (بناصيتها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to آخذ.. and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi (إنّ ربّي) its i'rab has been given [Note: In āya (41) of this sūra.] (على صراط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna (مستقيم) naʿt of صراط, genitive.
The clause «إنّي توكّلت ...» has no grammatical position; a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of what preceded.
The clause «توكّلت ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «ما من دابة إلّا هو آخذ ...» has no grammatical position; another causal explanation.
The clause «هو آخذ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of دابّة.
The clause «إنّ ربّي على صراط ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(اعتراك): in it there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion (qalb); its origin is اعتري: the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa and was converted to alif, so it became اعترى – with a final alif – its pattern being افتعل; the yāʾ, which is the lām of the word, is converted from a wāw: its bare form is عرا يعرو, and the maṣdar is عروة.
(ناصية): a noun for the front of the head, or the hair growing at the front; in the word there is iʿlāl by conversion: we say نصوت الرجل, i.e. I seized him by his forelock; the origin is ناصوة – with kasra on the ṣād and fatḥa on the wāw – and when the wāw was voweled and what preceded it had kasra, it was converted to yāʾ, so it became ناصية, its pattern being فاعلة. Seizing by the forelock is a kināya (metonymy) for domination and subjugation.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying, the Exalted, «قالَ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ».
He said only "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness", and did not say "and I call you to witness", so as to be parallel to it and of its meaning, because his calling Allah to witness to his disavowal of shirk is valid and established, whereas calling them to witness is nothing but contempt for their religion and an indication of little regard for them; for that reason he turned away from the wording of the first, because of the difference between them, and it was brought in the form of a command, as a man says to someone with whom all ties have dried up: "Bear witness against me that I do not love you", in mockery of him and in contempt of his state. This is from one angle. From a second angle, the declarative form admits nothing but reporting the occurrence of calling to witness from him; so since his calling Allah to witness was actual and realized, it was expressed in the declarative form, because it is a valid and established calling to witness; and on their side it was expressed in the imperative form, which includes contempt for their religion, and that is what he intends in this situation. From a third angle, he turned to the imperative form from the declarative form only to distinguish between his address to Allah the Exalted and his address to them, by expressing the address to Allah the Exalted in the declarative form, which is more exalted, more noble and more ample for the one addressed than the imperative form.
2- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «ما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِناصِيَتِها», i.e. except that He is its owner, having power over it, directing it as He wills, it not being resistant to Him, glory be to Him. Using "seizing by the forelock" for power and dominion is a majāz or a kināya.
3- Tamthīl (representation): in His saying, the Exalted, «إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ», included in the proof; it is a tamthīl and an istiʿāra (metaphor), because He, the Exalted, is aware of the affairs of the servants, requiting them with reward and punishment, sufficient for whoever holds fast to Him, like one who stands on the highway and guards it; and it is like His saying, glory be to Him and exalted: «إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ».

* Vocabulary:
(أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ): arranged in a firm, solid arrangement, beset by no breach or defect, as though it were a solidly built, well-laid structure. It may also be a transfer by the hamza from حكُم (with ḍamma on the kāf), i.e. "it became wise". It is also said that its meaning is "it was protected from corruption", from their saying أحكمت الدابة, when you put the ḥakama (bit-piece) on the animal to restrain it from mating [Translator's note: so the source; the ḥakama is usually described as restraining the animal from running wild]. Jarīr said:
أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم ... إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا
(O sons of Ḥanīfa, restrain your fools; I fear for you that I may become angry.)
A lengthy discussion of wisdom (ḥikma) in the Qur'an has preceded, and more of it will come as well.

* I'rab:
(الر، كِتابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ): الر — what is said about it has preceded. كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a Book", the clause أحكمت آياته is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, and آياته is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; فصلت is a passive past verb [Translator's note: the source misprints it as «فصت»]; من is a preposition and لدن is an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive; both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) فصلت, or to an omitted naʿt of كتاب — and this is preferable, because it was first described by the firmness of its verses and their detailing, both indicating the loftiness of its rank in itself, and then it was described by this attribute, indicating the loftiness of its standing in terms of its relation. حكيم is in genitive construct to لدن, and خبير is a naʿt of حكيم. (أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنَّنِي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ): أن may be lightened from the heavy [أنّ], its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with لا prohibitive and تعبدوا jussive by لا, the clause being the khabar of the lightened أن. Or أن may be a maṣdar-forming particle that puts in the accusative, with لا negating and the verb after it accusative by أن, and أن with what is in its domain is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) by implying the lām, in the sense of "so that you do not worship". Or it may be explicative (tafsīriyya), because the detailing of the verses carries the sense of speech, as though it were said: "He said: do not worship anyone but Allah," or "He commanded you not to worship anyone but Allah." Perhaps this is easier than the two preceding views, even though the three views are equal in weight. إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إنّ and its noun, with the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) between them; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نذير and بشير; منه is a ḥāl (circumstantial); نذير is the khabar of إنّ and بشير is conjoined to نذير. (وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ): the wāw is a conjunction and أن is conjoined to the first أن, conjoining one reason to another, and it follows the same course in parsing; ربكم is the object of استغفروا, ثم is a conjunction, and توبوا is conjoined to أن استغفروا, so it is a third reason. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «وأن استغفروا» and what follows may be a fresh statement, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, urging people to devote worship exclusively to Allah; this is indicated by his saying: إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير. (يُمَتِّعْكُمْ مَتاعاً حَسَناً إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى): يمتعكم is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request, namely His saying أن استغفروا ربكم; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi, متاعا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), حسنا is a naʿt, إلى أجل is attached to يمتعكم, and مسمى is a naʿt of أجل. (وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ): the wāw is a conjunction and يؤت is conjoined to يمتعكم, jussive like it, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is "He", i.e. Allah; كل is a first object, ذي فضل is a muḍāf ilayhi, and فضله is a second object. (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, إن is conditional, تولوا is an imperfect verb whose original form is تتولوا, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), إنّ and its noun, the clause أخاف عليكم is the khabar of إنّ, and the clause فإني أخاف عليكم is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذاب is a mafʿūl bihi, يوم is a muḍāf ilayhi, and كبير is a naʿt of يوم. The Day of Resurrection is described by greatness just as it is described by magnitude and heaviness. (إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): إلى الله is a fronted khabar and مرجعكم a postponed mubtadaʾ; هو is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدير, and قدير is the khabar of هو.

* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً): what is said about لئن has preceded. أذقنا is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), نا is the fāʿil (agent), الإنسان is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), منّا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of رحمة and was placed before it, and رحمة is a second object.
(ثُمَّ نَزَعْناها مِنْهُ إِنَّهُ لَيَؤُسٌ كَفُورٌ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نزعناها is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزعناها; إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), يئوس is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ and كفور is a second khabar of إنّ.
(وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْناهُ نَعْماءَ بَعْدَ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ): the parsing of its like has preceded. بعد is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted naʿt of نعماء; ضراء is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), a diptote because it ends in the extended alif of the feminine; and the clause مسته is a naʿt. (لَيَقُولَنَّ ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئاتُ عَنِّي): the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the clause ذهب السيئات is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl), and عني is attached to ذهب. (إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ): إنّ and its noun, the shifted lām; فرح is a first khabar and فخور a second khabar of إنّ. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ): إلا is a particle of exception and الذين is excepted from الإنسان, because the lām in it is generic, so the exception is connected; it may also be a disconnected exception, since what is meant is a particular person. In either case it is in the position of the accusative. The clause صبروا is the ṣila (relative clause), and عملوا الصالحات is conjoined. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لهم is a fronted khabar and مغفرة a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

* Rhetoric:
1- In "making taste" there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), because it is originally taking a thing in the mouth to perceive food, and it was then borrowed for pleasure [Translator's note: the source prints «للذات»; «اللذة» (pleasure) is evidently intended], likening it to what is tasted and then quickly vanishes, as flavours vanish.
2- Between النعماء and الضراء there is antithesis (ṭibāq). All of these topics have been discussed before.

* Benefits:
السراء, النعماء and الضراء: it is said that they are maṣdars (verbal nouns) meaning المسرة (gladness), النعمة (favour) and المضرة (harm). The correct view is that they are nouns of maṣdars (asmāʾ al-maṣādir), not the maṣdars themselves: السراء is ease, النعماء is favour, and الضراء is hardship; they are names for these meanings. If we say they are maṣdars, they denote the act itself, which is the meaning; and if they are names for them, they denote what brings about these meanings.

* Vocabulary:
(وَزِينَتَها): الزينة is enhancing a thing by something else, such as clothing, ornament or appearance. One says زانه يزينه زينة and زيّنه يزينه تزيينا. [Translator's note: the source prints the imperfect of the second verb as «يزينه»; «يزيّنه» is evidently intended.]
(نُوَفِّ): التوفية is rendering what is due in full.
(يُبْخَسُونَ): البخس is diminishing what is due, and every wrongdoer is باخس. In the proverb: «تحسبها حمقاء وهي باخس» ("you think her a fool, yet she is a cheat").

* I'rab:
(مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وَزِينَتَها نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ فِيها وَهُمْ فِيها لا يُبْخَسُونَ): من is a conditional noun putting in the jussive, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the noun of كان is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من, and the clause يريد الحياة الدنيا is the khabar (predicate) of كان; كان is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive in position; زينتها is conjoined to الحياة; نوفّ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive by the dropping of the weak letter; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نوفّ, أعمالهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and فيها is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). وهم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), هم is a mubtadaʾ, فيها is attached to يبخسون, and the clause لا يبخسون is the khabar of هم. Al-Farrāʾ said:
كان here is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being من يرد الحياة الدنيا. This is a fine and elegant view [Translator's note: the source has «ضريف», a misspelling of «ظريف»], were it not that it is not regular, and it is not permissible to interpret the Qur'an by it. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الذين its khabar; the clause ليس is the ṣila (relative clause); لهم is the fronted khabar of ليس, في الآخرة is a ḥāl, إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and النار is the postponed noun of ليس. (وَحَبِطَ ما صَنَعُوا فِيها وَباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, حبط is a past verb, ما is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause صنعوا is the ṣila. ما may also be maṣdar-forming, so that together with what it enters on it is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), the fāʿil of حبط. فيها is attached to صنعوا or to حبط. وباطل: the wāw is a conjunction, باطل is a fronted khabar and ما is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; ما may also be maṣdar-forming, so that together with what it enters on it is in the sense of a maṣdar, a postponed mubtadaʾ. كانوا is كان and its noun, and the clause يعملون is its khabar.

* Vocabulary:
(أَراذِلُنا): our lowest ones. There are two views about it. The first is that it is a plural of a plural: it is the plural of أرذُل (with ḍamma on the dhāl), the plural of رذْل (with sukūn), like كلب, أكلب and أكالب. The second is that it is the plural of a singular, namely أرذل, like أكبر and أكابر, أبطح and أباطح, أبرق and أبارق; الأرذل is that which is shunned for its poor quality. Al-Zamakhsharī chose the second view, and the author of al-Qāmūs preferred it.
(بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ): the outward [first] opinion. It may be pronounced with a hamza, giving بادئ الرأي. Whoever does not use the hamza meant: "you, in what appears of opinion"; and whoever uses the hamza meant:
"you, at the first of opinion and its beginning". Abū ʿAlī has a fine discussion of this expression, which we quote in full for its benefit:
"The meaning for whoever said بادي الرأي without hamza, making it from بدا in the sense of 'appeared', is: none followed you but the lowest, in what appeared to them of opinion, without following it up with examination of it and deliberation. These two words are close in meaning, because [a root whose] lām (third radical) is a hamza means the beginning of a thing and its first, and when the lām is a wāw the meaning is appearing; and the beginning of a thing is an appearing, so each of them is used in place of the other. It is permissible for the active participle to be an adverb (ẓarf), just as it is permissible for faʿīl, e.g. قريب and مليء, because fāʿil and faʿīl alternate in meaning, e.g. عالم and عليم, شاهد and شهيد. What made that good is its being in genitive construct with الرأي. They have also treated the maṣdar (verbal noun) in this way in being put in construct with it, in their saying اما جهد رأيي فإني منطلق ('as for the utmost of my opinion, I am departing'), and this can only be an adverb" — to the end of this delightful discussion. More will come in the I'rab.
(الرَّأْيِ): maṣdar of رأى رأيا; its plural is آراء. Opinion is reflecting on the beginnings of matters, considering their consequences, and knowing what they lead to of error and correctness. The "people of opinion" (aṣḥāb al-raʾy) according to the jurists are the people of analogy (qiyās) and interpretation. The poets have agreed in praising opinion. Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī said:
ولا أرضى الفتى ما لم يكمل ... برأي الكهل أقدام الغلام
(I am not satisfied with a young man unless he completes the boldness of youth with the judgement of a mature man.)
And Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said:
الرأي قبل شجاعة الشجعان ... هو أول وهي المحل الثاني
فإذا هما اجتمعا لنفس حرة ... بلغت من العلياء كل مكان
(Judgement comes before the courage of the brave: it is first and courage holds second place; and when the two come together in a free soul, it reaches every summit of eminence.)

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ): a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause, brought to begin mentioning a number of stories as consolation for the Prophet ﷺ, as a lesson from them, and as a model in what their protagonists encountered. This sūra contains seven stories. The lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa), قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), نوحا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. إني is with kasra on the hamza on the intention of [an implied verb of] saying, which is often implied, needing no evidence. إنّ and its noun, لكم is attached to نذير, نذير is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ and مبين is its naʿt (adjective).
(أَنْ لا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ): أن is explicative (mufassira), لا is prohibitive, تعبدوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) and the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi; إنّ and its noun, the clause أخاف is its khabar, عليكم is attached to أخاف, عذاب يوم is the object of أخاف, and أليم is a naʿt of يوم. (فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ):
the fāʿ is a conjunction, قال الملأ is a verb and its fāʿil, الذين is a naʿt of الملأ, the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause), and من قومه is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَراذِلُنا بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ): the clause is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl). ما is negating, and نراك is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; إلا is a particle of restriction. The seeing may be mental or visual, so بشرا is a second object on the first view and a ḥāl on the second; مثلنا is a naʿt. وما نراك is conjoined to the first ما نراك, and it too may be mental or visual, so the clause اتبعك is either a second object or a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction, الذين is the fāʿil of اتبعك, هم أراذلنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and the clause is the ṣila. بادي الرأي is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "at the first of opinion", and what governs it is اتبعك; what is said about it has preceded at length. It is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of Nūḥ in اتبعك, i.e. "while you are of exposed opinion, with no sound judgement". (وَما نَرى لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا مِنْ فَضْلٍ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كاذِبِينَ): وما نرى is conjoined to what preceded, لكم is attached to نرى, علينا is attached to فضل, من is a redundant preposition, and فضل is genitive in form, a mafʿūl bihi accusative in position; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, نظنكم is conjoined to ما نرى, the kāf is a first object and كاذبين a second object. (قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَآتانِي رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to address them gently, and among it is calling them "[my] people" [Translator's note: the source's «ومنا صفتهم» appears corrupt; this rendering follows the evident intent]. يا قوم is the one addressed (munādā), in genitive construct to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker. أرأيتم has been discussed in detail before; رأيتم is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. "tell me". Here [أرأيتم] requires البينة as a mafʿūl bihi, and كنت requires البينة in the genitive with على; so the second was given governance and [a pronoun] was implied in the first. The implied form is: "Have you considered the clear proof from my Lord, if I am upon it — shall we compel you to it?" So the first object was omitted, the interrogative clause is the second object, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because it is indicated. إن is conditional, كنت is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, على بينة is the khabar of كنت, and من ربي is a naʿt. The meaning of على here is elevation, because the possessor of a clear proof is elevated above others; it is also said to be for accompaniment in the sense of مع, and that is not far-fetched. وآتاني: the wāw is a conjunction, and آتاني is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; رحمة is a second object and من عنده is a naʿt of رحمة. (فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوها وَأَنْتُمْ لَها كارِهُونَ): the fāʿ is a conjunction, عميت is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, implied as "it"; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عميت. The explanation of the reality of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. أنلزمكموها: the hamza is interrogative, i.e. "shall we force you to it?" In this verb there are three pronouns: the first is latent, implied as "we", and it is the fāʿil; the second is the pronoun of the one addressed, i.e. the kāf, and it is the first object; the third is the pronoun of the absent, i.e. the hāʾ, and it is the second object. The mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, and the wāw is for lengthening the ḍamma on the mīm and is not a pronoun. The order among them has been observed, because the speaker is the most specific to the verb, then the pronoun of the one addressed, then the pronoun of the absent. وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, لها is attached to كارهون, and كارهون is the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. What is said about the clause أنلزمكموها has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In attributing blindness to the clear proof there is a rational metonymic attribution (majāz ʿaqlī), treating it as a rational being. Its reality is that the argument and the clear proof, which were made a source of insight and enabling sight, were made blind, because the blind man is not guided and does not guide others. So the clear proof was made blind to you and did not guide you, just as if the scout of a people, who leads them through dark wildernesses and branching deserts, were struck blind to them, so that they remained bewildered, stumbling about and seeking deliverance from their bewilderment. Some of them made it a case of inversion (qalb), i.e. that it was they who were blinded, so that it is of the type "I put the ring into my finger" and "I put the cap into my head" [i.e. instead of "my finger into the ring"]. The poet said: ترى الشوك فيها مدخلا ظل رأسه ... وسائره باد إلى الشمس أجمع
(You see the thorns in it with the shade of its head made to enter [them], while all the rest of it is exposed to the sun.) [Translator's note: the source reads «الشوك»; the verse is usually cited as «ترى الثور فيها مدخل الظل رأسه».]
2- Allusion (taʿrīḍ) in His saying «قال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي». What is said about allusion has preceded. Their aim here was to allude that they were more entitled to prophethood than he, and that had Allah wished to place it in anyone He would have placed it in them. These people claimed to overcome Nūḥ in argument from two angles: first, that the followers are the lowest, neither an example nor a model; second, that they, besides that, did not deliberate in following him nor think deeply about the truth of what he brought, but rushed into it impromptu, without thought or deliberation.

* Vocabulary:
(الجدال) and المجادلة: confronting [the opponent] with what twists the opponent away from his position, by an argument or a specious doubt. It is الجدل, i.e. strong twisting. One says جدل الحبل: he twisted the rope; a twisted halter (زمام مجدول) is الجديل. They say: "as though in the halter", "one of the daughters of Jadīl" [a famous stallion]. طعنه فجدّله: he thrust at him and threw him down on الجدالة, which is the earth. [The poet] said:
قد أركب الآلة بعد الآله ... وأترك العاجز بالجداله
(I ride one hard state after another, and leave the feeble man lying on the ground.)
The falcon is called أجدل because it is among the strongest of the hunting birds. They say: "If they stand still, they are palaces (جوادل); and if they pass by, they are falcons (أجادل)", i.e. if they stand [Translator's note: the source prints «وفقن» for «وقفن»], they are palaces, and if they pass by, they are falcons. Al-Aʿshā said:
في مجدل شيّد بنيانه ... يزلّ عنه ظفر الطائر
(In a fortress whose structure is built high, from which the bird's talon slips.)
Among the figurative usages: امرأة مجدولة الخلق, a woman of slender build; درع مجدولة and جدلاء, i.e. a firmly made coat of mail; عمل على جديلته, he acted according to his nature on which he was "twisted"; استقام جدول القوم, when the people's affair became orderly, like a stream (جدول) when its flow is steady and continuous. A Bedouin looked at the pilgrims' caravan proceeding in succession and said: "As for the pilgrims, their stream has become straight." From following the derivation of this root it becomes clear that every word whose first and second radicals are jīm and dāl indicates strength, twisting and firmness. Thus جدب المكان جدوبة, and جدب and أجدب, the opposite of أخصب (to be fertile) — and it is not hidden what hardship and affliction there is in that for those whose land becomes barren. الجدث is the grave, and among their sayings: «شر الأحداث، نزول الأجداث» ("the worst of events is descending into graves"). جدح السويق واللبن بالمجدح: he stirred the gruel and milk with the مجدح, which is a stick with two crosspieces at its head with which it is stirred until mixed. أرسلت السماء مجاديح الغيث (the sky sent down the rain-stirrers); المجاديح is the plural of المجدح, i.e. al-Dabarān [the star], whose rain-season (nawʾ) is abundant. In the ḥadīth of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: "I have sought rain with the مجاديح of the sky," by which he meant seeking forgiveness. رجل مجدود: a fortunate man; and there is nothing in this world stronger than the workings of الجَدّ (with fatḥa on the jīm), i.e. fortune; and الجِدّ (with kasra) is effort and toil. مشى على الجادّة: he walked on the main road; امشوا على الجوادّ, which is the plural of الجادة. أجدّ المسير and جدّ: he hastened the journey. [The poet] said:
أشوقا ولما يمض لي غير ليلة ... فكيف إذا جدّ المطي بنا عشرا
(Longing already, when only one night has passed for me? Then how will it be when the mounts hasten with us for ten?)
جدره: he called him from behind the wall (الجدار). He is جدير بكذا, i.e. strong enough to undertake it. Zuhayr said:
بخيل عليها جنّة عبقرية ... جديرون يوما أن ينالوا فيستعلوا
(With horses ridden by men like jinn of ʿAbqar, worthy one day to attain and rise high.)
جُدر الصبي and جُدّر: the boy had smallpox; he is مجدور الوجه and مجدّر. Among the witty verses of Ibn al-Muʿtazz:
بي قمر جدّر لما استوى ... فزاده حسنا وزالت هموم
أظنه غنى لشمس الضحى ... فنقطته طربا بالنجوم
(I love a moon [a beauty] who caught smallpox when he reached his prime, which only increased his beauty and dispelled cares; I think he sang to the morning sun, and in delight she dotted him with stars.)
جدع أنفه وأذنه: he cut off his nose and his ear, so he is مجدوع; when it becomes a permanent quality, one says أجدع, feminine جدعاء. جادع صاحبه: he quarrelled with his companion and reviled him; جدّعه, when he said to him "جدعا لك" (may you be mutilated). جدف الملّاح السفينة: the sailor propelled the ship with the oar (المجداف). Aʿshā Hamdān said:
لمن الظّعائن سيرهنّ تزحّف ... عوم السفين إذا تقاعس تجدف
(Whose are the travelling women whose march creeps along, like the floating of ships, when they lag, propelled by oars?)
خفق الطائر بمجدافيه: the bird flapped its two "oars", i.e. its wings, which are its strength. الجدا and الجدوى are a gift — and how strong it is! استجديته: I asked him [for a gift]; جدوته and اجتديته are like it. [The poet] said: جدوت أناسا موسرين فما جدوا ... ألا الله أجدوه إذا كنت جاديا
(I asked wealthy people for gifts and they did not give; rather, ask Allah when you seek a gift.)
One of our early men of letters perceived this root and the secret of the conjunction of the jīm and the dāl, and enumerated it in verse, which we cite below:
عظمة والقطع حظ جدّ ... والاجتهاد ضد هزل جدّ
وجانب وجاء جمعا جدّ ... واسم لما بين الكلا من بئر
أمّ أب وأمّ أمّ جدّه ... ومصدر الشيء الجديد جدّه
مدينة أي بالحجاز جدّه ... والضمّ والكسر لشط النهر
للنبت والحائط قيل جدر ... وللنبات قيل أيضا جدر
وجمع جدر أي جدار جدر ... وآفة الأطفال داء الجدري
والسنة الشديدة الجداع ... أما الجدال فاسمه جداع
والكلأ الذّاوي هو الجداع ... كذا وضيم الكلم المضرّ
الفتل والصرع وعود جدل ... والصدر بالفتح وكسر جدل
جمع جديل أي زمام جدل ... وجمع جدلاء لدرع الكر
(Summary of the verses: جدّ means greatness, cutting, fortune, and — as the opposite of jest — earnestness/effort; it also means a side, and the plural of جادّ; and it is the name of a well among the pasture. جدّة is a paternal and a maternal grandmother; جدّة is the verbal noun of a thing being new; and Jidda is a city in the Ḥijāz; with ḍamma and kasra, جُدّ/جِدّ is a river bank. جدر is said of plants and of a wall; the plural of جدار is جدر; and the affliction of children is the disease الجدري (smallpox). جداع is a severe year, and also disputation (الجدال); withered pasture is also جداع, as is harmful, wounding speech. جدل is twisting, throwing down, and a stick; with fatḥa it is the chest, and with kasra, جِدل; it is the plural of جديل (a halter), and the plural of جدلاء, the coat of mail of battle.)
This is truly remarkable.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا يا نُوحُ قَدْ جادَلْتَنا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدالَنا): قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); يا is a vocative particle, and نوح is the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), جادلتنا is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فأكثرت is conjoined to جادلتنا, and جدالنا is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ): the fāʿ is the faṣīḥa fāʿ, i.e. "if you are truthful, then bring us". بما is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, the clause تعدنا is the ṣila (relative clause), and the returning pronoun is omitted. It is also correct for ما to be maṣdar-forming, i.e. "[bring] your promise to us". إن كنت من الصادقين is a condition whose apodosis is indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring us"; من الصادقين is the khabar (predicate) of كنت. (قالَ إِنَّما يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ إِنْ شاءَ وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ): إنما is the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), يأتيكم is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi, به is attached to يأتيكم, and الله is the fāʿil; إن شاء is a condition and its verb, and the apodosis is omitted. وما: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), ما is the Ḥijāzī ما, أنتم is its noun, and بمعجزين is its khabar, accusative in position, because of the redundant preposition. (وَلا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negating, and ينفعكم نصحي is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; إن أردت is a condition and its verb, أن with what is in its domain is the object of أردت, and لكم is attached to أنصح. إن كان is likewise a condition and its verb; الله is the noun of كان, the clause يريد is the khabar of كان, and أن يغويكم — أن with what is in its domain — is the object of يريد. The explanation of the succession of the two conditions is that the apodosis of the second condition, namely إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم, is what is indicated by His saying لا ينفعكم نصحي, and the second condition with its apodosis is the apodosis of the first. The detail of that and its meaning will come in the section of Benefits. (هُوَ رَبُّكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ربكم the khabar; إليه is attached to ترجعون; ترجعون is in the passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ): أم is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa); يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the clause افتراه is the speech reported by "say" (maqūl al-qawl). (قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرامِي وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُجْرِمُونَ): إن is conditional, and افتريته is a verb, a fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). The fāʿ is linking (rābiṭa), عليّ is a fronted khabar and إجرامي a postponed mubtadaʾ; أنا is a mubtadaʾ and بريء the khabar, مما is attached to بريء, and the clause تجرمون is the ṣila.

* Benefits:
When two conditions and one apodosis come together in speech, the second condition is made a condition within the first, so the apodosis does not take place unless the second condition is fulfilled and exists in reality before the first exists. The parallel to this verse among the questions of the jurists is the saying: "You are divorced if you drink if you eat." This is known as the question of one condition intervening upon another. What is transmitted is that if she drank and then ate, he does not break his oath [i.e. she is not divorced], and if she ate and then drank, he breaks it. The commentators have established concerning the verse that when one condition comes upon another, the second is prior to the first in meaning, even though it is later in wording; the implied form is: "My advice will not benefit you, if Allah intends to lead you astray, if I wish to advise you." Al-Bayḍāwī said: "Thus is the construction of the speech: if Allah intends to lead you astray, then if I wish to advise you, my advice will not benefit you for that reason. And if someone said: 'You are divorced if you enter the house if you speak to Zayd,' and she entered and then spoke to Zayd, she is not divorced."
Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī:
They mentioned that when one condition intervenes upon another, e.g. "if you eat, if you drink, you are divorced", the stated apodosis belongs to the earlier of them, and the apodosis of the second is omitted, indicated by the first condition and its apodosis (that is, the first condition and its apodosis are later in meaning, since it is the indication of the apodosis), as they said concerning the apodosis that comes after an oath and a condition. For this reason the precise jurists said of the example mentioned that she is not divorced until she does first what was mentioned later and later what was mentioned first, because the implied form then is "if you drink, if you eat, you are divorced". All of this is good, but they counted among it His saying, Exalted is He: ولا ينفعكم نصحي إن أردت أن أنصح لكم إن كان الله يريد أن يغويكم — and this is questionable, since two conditions do not follow in succession with an apodosis after them, as in the example and as in the poet's saying:
إن تستغيثوا بنا إن تذعروا تجدوا ... منّا معاقل عزّ زانها كرم
(If you seek our help, if you are frightened, you will find in us strongholds of might adorned by generosity.)
and the saying of Ibn Durayd:
فإن عثرت بعدها إن وألت ... نفسي من هاتا فقولا: لا لعا
(And if I stumble after this — if my soul escapes from this one — then say: may he not rise again.)
