And the clause: «لا تعثوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أوفوا ...
(184) (الواو) is a conjunction (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi (الجبلّة) is conjoined by the wāw to the pronoun of address, the accusative object, accusative, (الأولين) is a naʿt of الجبلّة, accusative like it, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to أوفوا ...
And the clause: «خلقكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).

* Morphology:
(المخسرين), plural of المخسر, an active participle from the quadriliteral أخسر; its pattern is مُفْعِل (with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).
(الجبلّة), a noun meaning the creatures and nations, taken from الجبل (the mountain) because of their strength; its pattern is فِعِلّة (with kasra on the fāʾ and the ʿayn and a shaddated fatḥa on the lām), and there are other dialectal forms of its pronunciation.

* Benefits:
الأيكة has two readings: a- الأيكة: which is the tangled trees or the thicket.
b- ليكة: which is the name of the village in which the people of Shuʿayb lived.
Accordingly, regarding الأيكة, which is the thicket or the trees tangled one with another, we mention some of what the poets said about the الأيك and its cooing dove on its branches. One of them said:
أيبكي حمام الأيك من فقد إلفه ... وأصبر عنها إنني لصبور
(Does the dove of the thicket weep at the loss of its mate while I endure without her? I am indeed enduring)
And al-Riyāshī recited for one of them:
دعوت فوق أفنان من الأيك موهنا ... مطوقة ورقاء في إثر آلف
(I called, above the branches of the thicket in the dead of night, a collared grey dove after a mate)
[Translator's note: the source reads «دعوت» ("I called") in the first line; metre and sense require «دعت» ("she called/cooed"); translated as written.]

فهاجت عقابيل الهوى إذ ترنمت ... وشبت ضرام الشوق تحت الشراسف
(She stirred the remnants of passion when she warbled, and kindled the blaze of longing beneath the rib-ends)

بكت بجفون دمعها غير ذارف ... وأغرت جفوني بالدموع الذوارف
(She wept with eyelids whose tears did not flow, and incited my eyelids to flowing tears)
And ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim said:
ألا يا حمام الأيك إلفك حاضر ... وغصنك ميّاد ففيم تنوح
(O dove of the thicket, your mate is present and your branch is swaying, so why do you lament?)

أفق لا تنح من غير شيء فإنني ... بكيت زمانا والفؤاد صحيح
(Wake up, do not lament for nothing, for I wept a time while the heart was sound)

ولوعا فشطت غربة دار زينب ... فها أنا أبكي والفؤاد جريح
(In passion, then the far exile of Zaynab's abode departed; so here I am weeping while the heart is wounded)

* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis ...
And the pronoun in (إنّه) refers to the Noble Qur'an.
The clause: «إنّه لتنزيل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(193) (به) is attached to a ḥāl from الروح, that is, "furnished with it", and the governing element in it is نزل ...
And the clause: «نزل به الروح ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of (إنّ) [Note: or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumptive clause.].
(194-195) (على قلبك) is attached to (نزل), (اللام) is causal (تكون) is a defective imperfect verb, a nāsikh, accusative through an implied أن after the lām (من المنذرين) is attached to the khabar of تكون (بلسان) is attached to (نزل) [Note: or attached to المنذرين ... and al-ʿUkbarī permitted making it a badal (substitute) of (به) by repeating the preposition, that is, "speaking in the Arabic language".], (مبين) is a second naʿt of لسان, genitive.
And the interpreted maṣdar أن تكون is in the position of genitive through the lām, attached to (نزل).
And the clause: «تكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied maṣdar particle (أن).
(196) (الواو) is a conjunction (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis (في زبر) is attached to the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause: «إنّه لفي زبر..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه لتنزيل ...
(197) (الهمزة) is for the interrogative of reproof and reproach (الواو) is a conjunction (لهم) is attached to a ḥāl from آية (آية) is the khabar of يكن, accusative (أن) is a maṣdar and subjunctive particle ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلمه علماء ... ) is in the position of nominative, the ism of يكن.
And the clause: «لم يكن ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إنّه لفي زبر.
And the clause: «يعلمه علماء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (أن).
(198) (الواو) is a conjunction (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle, "impossibility of the second because of impossibility of the first" (imtināʿ li-imtināʿ) (على بعض) is attached to (نزّلناه) ...
And the clause: «لو نزّلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لم يكن لهم آية.
(199) (الفاء) is a conjunction (عليهم) is attached to (قرأه), (ما) is a negative particle (به) is attached to مؤمنين, the khabar.
And the clause: «قرأه عليهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نزّلناه.
And the clause: «ما كانوا به مؤمنين» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the non-jussive conditional (لو).

* Morphology:
(192) تنزيل: a maṣdar with the meaning of the passive participle, that is, "that which is sent down"; its pattern is تفعيل.
(195) عربيّ: a relational noun (ism mansūb) ascribed to عرب, a collective generic noun (ism jins jamʿī); its pattern is فَعَلِيّ (with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn).
(198) الأعجمين: plural of الأعجم, which is a shortened form of الأعجميّ (with the yāʾ of relation), a noun for one who does not speak Arabic; it is an adjective of the pattern أفعل and its feminine is عجماء, and the regular plural of it would be عجم (with ḍamma then sukūn), but it was pluralized as a sound plural in view of its origin in the relational form; and it is from عجم يعجم of the chapter كرم, meaning that there was a thickness (lukna) in his tongue.

* İ'rab:
(قالَ: أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ): Mahzûf bir takdir yapmak gerekir; yani «İkisi Firavun'un kapısına gittiler; bir yıl boyunca kendilerine izin verilmedi. Sonunda kapıcı, 'Burada âlemlerin Rabbinin elçisi olduğunu iddia eden bir adam var' dedi. (Firavun) 'Ona izin ver, belki ona güleriz' dedi. İkisi ona risaleti tebliğ ettiler. Mûsâ'yı tanıdı, çünkü onun evinde yetişmişti; ona 'ألم نربك' dedi.» Hemze takrîrî istifhâm içindir; «لم» nefy, kalb ve cezm harfidir; «نربك» «لم» ile meczûm muzâri fiildir; cezm alâmeti illet harfinin hazfidir; fâil müstetir zamir olup takdiri «نحن»dir; kâf mef'ûlün bihtir; «فينا» «نربك»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «وليدا» hâldir. «لبثت» fiil ve fâildir; «فينا» «لبثت»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «من عمرك» hâldir, çünkü «سنين»in sıfatı idi; «سنين» de zarf olup yine «لبثت»e müteallikti.
(وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ): Vâv atıf harfidir; «فعلت» fiil ve fâildir; «فعلتك» mef'ûlün bih veya mef'ûl-i mutlaktır; «التي» sıfattır; «فعلت» cümlesi sıladır. Vâv hâliyyedir; «أنت» mübtedâdır; «من الكافرين» haberdir; yani nimetimi inkâr edenlerden. Mûsâ'nın yaptığı o iş, (Firavun'un) Kıptî ekmekçisini öldürmesidir. (قالَ فَعَلْتُها إِذاً وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ): «قال» mâzî fiildir, yani Mûsâ (dedi); «فعلتها» fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih veya mef'ûl-i mutlaktır, yani «o işi yaptım». «إذن», cevap mesabesinde bir cezâ harfidir; vâv hâl vâvıdır; «أنا» mübtedâdır; «من الضالين» haberdir; yani Allah'ın bundan sonra bana verdiği ilim ve risaletten habersiz olanlardan. Nübüvvet makamını, Firavun'un kendisine yakıştırdığı o sıfattan, yani ona «وأنت من الكافرين» sözünden yüce tuttu ve «من الضالين» dedi; yani öldürmeyi kastetmeden hataen öldüren kimse gibi hata edenlerden. [Mütercim notu: Metinde «فروعون» yazılıdır; «فرعون» olmalıdır.] (فَفَرَرْتُ مِنْكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ): Fâ atıf harfidir; «فررت» fiil ve fâildir; «منكم» «فررت»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «لما», Fârisî'nin dediğine göre «حين» anlamındadır, Sîbeveyh'in dediğine göre ise râbıtadır; «خفتكم» cümlesi zarfın kendisine izâfe edildiği cümledir. «فوهب» «ففررت»e ma'tûftur; «لي» «وهب»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «ربي» fâildir; «حكما» mef'ûlün bihtir; «وجعلني من المرسلين» öncekine ma'tûftur. Bu sözle onun nübüvvetine yönelttiği kusurlamayı defetti; yani hikmet ve nübüvvetin bağışlanması o hadiseden sonra olmuştu. Sonra da terbiye ile ona minnet etmesine yönelip şu sözüyle onu çürüttü, kökünden iptal etti ve temelinden söküp attı:
(وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): Firavun'un ona yönelttiği itham temelden yıkmak için sevk edilmiş isti'nâfiyye bir sözdür. «تلك» mübtedâ, «نعمة» haberdir; «تمنها» cümlesi «نعمة»nin sıfatıdır; «علي» «تمنها»ya müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur. «أن» ve onun etki alanındakiler «تلك»in atf-ı beyânıdır; çünkü işaret, hakikatinin künhüne ancak tefsiriyle varılabilecek çirkin bir plana ve kötü bir hasletedir; bu yüzden atf-ı beyân, müphem olanı tefsir eden ve kapalı olanı açan olarak gelmiştir. Müevvel masdarın «نعمة»den bedel olarak i'rab edilmesi ya da mef'ûlün lieclih olarak nasb mahallinde olması da caizdir. «تمنها» muzâri fiildir [Mütercim notu: Metinde «ونمنها» yazılıdır; «وتمنها» olmalıdır.]; fâili müstetir zamir olup takdiri «أنت»tir; hâ zamiri nez'u'l-hâfıd ile mansûbdur; çünkü «منّ» bâ ile geçişli olan lâzım bir fiildir; yani «تمن بها» (onu başa kakıyorsun).
Celâl, muhtasar tefsirinde, bazılarının sözün başında bir hemze takdir ettiğine, yani «وتلك»ten önce takdir ettiğine ve sözün aslının «أو تلك؟» olduğuna işaret etmiştir; yani «Bu, bana başa kakacağın bir nimet değildir.» Bunu takdir eden Ahfeş'tir. Bu hemze, açıkladığımız gibi nefy manasını içeren inkârî istifhâm içindir.

* Belâgat:
İbhâm:
«وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت» sözünde tefsirsiz ibhâm vardır. İbhâm iki kısımdır: tefsir edilmiş ibhâm ve tefsirsiz ibhâm. Zira «التي فعلت» sözünde zihin her yöne gider ve birçok manayı taşır. Bu, Kur'an-ı Kerim'de çok ve yaygındır.

* I'rab:
(قالَ: أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ فِينا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ) An omitted element must necessarily be implied here, namely: "So the two of them set off for Pharaoh's gate, and were not given leave to enter for a year, until the gatekeeper said: 'There is a man here who claims to be the messenger of the Lord of the worlds.' Pharaoh said: 'Let him in, perhaps we shall laugh at him.' So the two delivered the message to him, and he recognised Moses, because he had been raised in his house, and said to him: ألم نربك (Did we not raise you...)". The hamza is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; نربك is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; the kāf is the direct object; فينا is attached to نربك; وليدا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ولبثت is a verb and agent; فينا is attached to لبثت; ومن عمرك is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of سنين; and سنين is an adverbial attached also to لبثت.
(وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; فعلت is a verb and agent; فعلتك is a direct object or an absolute object; التي is an adjective; the clause فعلت is its ṣila (relative clause); the wāw is a ḥāl-wāw; أنت is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and من الكافرين its khabar (predicate), that is, those who deny my favour. The deed that Moses had done was the killing of his baker, the Copt. (قالَ فَعَلْتُها إِذاً وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ) قال is a past verb, that is, Moses; فعلتها is a verb, agent and direct object, or an absolute object, that is, "I did the deed"; إذن is a particle of requital, standing in the place of the answer; the wāw is the ḥāl-wāw; أنا is the mubtadaʾ and من الضالين its khabar, that is, [one of those who had gone astray] from what Allah gave me afterwards of knowledge and the message. He thereby held the station of prophethood above that attribute which Pharaoh had applied to him, namely his words to him وأنت من الكافرين, and so he said من الضالين, that is, those who err, like one who kills by mistake without intending to kill. (فَفَرَرْتُ مِنْكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْماً وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; فررت is a verb and agent; منكم is attached to فررت; لما is temporal, as al-Fārisī says, or a connective, as Sībawayh says, and the clause خفتكم is what the adverbial is annexed to; فوهب is conjoined to ففررت; لي is attached to وهب; ربي is the agent; حكما is the direct object; and وجعلني من المرسلين is conjoined to what precedes. By this statement he warded off the slur upon his prophethood, that is, the gift of judgement and prophethood came after that incident. Then he turned back on his reminder of the favour of rearing him, and refuted it, nullified it from its very root and tore it out from its foundation, with the words: (وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّها عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to demolish the accusation Pharaoh had directed at him. وتلك is a mubtadaʾ and نعمة its khabar; the clause تمنها is an adjective of نعمة; علي is attached to تمنها; and أن together with what is within its scope is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to تلك, because the demonstrative points to a hideous plan and an ugly trait whose reality cannot be grasped except through its explanation, so the explicative apposition came to explain what was left vague and to open what was closed. It is also permissible to parse the interpreted maṣdar as a badal (substitute) from نعمة, or as being in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). تمنها is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, because مَنَّ is an intransitive verb that is made transitive by the bāʾ, that is, "you bestow it upon me" (تمن بها).
Al-Jalāl pointed out in his abridged tafsir that some scholars implied a hamza at the beginning of the sentence, that is, before وتلك, so that the original sentence is "أو تلك؟", meaning: "This is not a favour for you to remind me of it." The one who implied it is al-Akhfash. This hamza is for rebuking interrogation (istifhām inkārī) containing the sense of negation, as we have explained.

* Rhetoric:
Ambiguity (al-ibhām):
In his words «وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت» there is an ambiguity with no explanation. It is of two kinds: an ambiguity that is explained, and an ambiguity without explanation. His words «التي فعلت» send the imagination in every direction and bear many meanings, and this is frequent and widespread in the Noble Qur'an.

* Lügat:
(ثُعْبانٌ): الثعبان yılandır; erkeğine de dişisine de denir; çoğulu ثعابين'dir. «الثعبان»ın iştikakı «ثعب الماء»dandır, yani suyu akıttı, o da fışkırıp aktı (فانثعب). Bu «sel gibi akıcılık» (ثعبانية) özelliği asâda, onu attığında ortaya çıkmıştır. Sâ'nın ayn ile birlikte (kökte) bulunmasının renkten renge girme, hile ve «الارهان» gibi bir hususiyeti vardır [Mütercim notu: «الارهان» kelimesi metinde bu şekildedir; anlamı belirsizdir, aynen bırakılmıştır.]. «ثعّ يثعّ» (ضرب babından) «ثعّا»: yediğini kustu, denir. «انثعّ الأكل من فمه» (yemek ağzından boşaldı), «الدم من أنفه أو جرحه» (kan burnundan veya yarasından), yani döküldü. Onların sözlerinden: «سالت الثّعبان كما انساب الثعبان» (sel yatakları, yılanın süzülüp aktığı gibi aktı); (buradaki ilk) «الثعبان», «ثعب»in çoğuludur; o da sel yatağıdır. (Şair) şöyle dedi:
وما ثعب باتت تطرّده الصبا ... بسرّاء واد منجد غير اتهما
(Necid'e yönelmiş, Tihâme'ye inmemiş bir vadinin en güzel yerinde, sabâ rüzgârının bütün gece önüne katıp sürdüğü bir sel yatağı (suyu) değildir ...)
Mecaz olarak: «صاح به فانثعب إليه»: ona seslendi, o da koşarak ona doğru fırladı. «شدّ أثعوب» (sel gibi akan koşu). (Şair) şöyle dedi:
لها إذا حرّ الحرار واللوب ... قوائم «عوج» وشدّ أثعوب
(Taşlık yerler ve kara taşlı arazi kızıştığında, onun «Avc» cinsi atınkiler gibi bacakları ve sel gibi akan bir koşusu vardır.)
Ebû Duâd şöyle dedi:
وكل قائمة تهوي لوجهتها ... لها أتي كفرغ الدلو أثعوب
(Yöneldiği yere doğru inen her bir bacağın, kovanın ağzından boşalan su gibi sel misali akan bir hamlesi vardır.)
Her ikisi de istiâre babındandır; ancak yol farklıdır. «ثعب عليهم الغارة»: onlara baskın düzenledi. «ثعب البعير شقشقته»: deve, şıkşıkasını (ağzından çıkan kızgınlık kesesini) çıkardı. «ثعلت أسنانه تثعل» (فتح babından) «ثعلا»: dişlerinden biri diğerinin üzerine bindi; o (kişi) «أثعل»dir. Bunda renkten renge girme ve hile manası vardır. «أثعل الأمر»: iş büyüdü ve vahim hâle geldi. «الثّعل» (şeddeli sâ'nın dammesiyle), kokusu bozulduğunda su tulumunda ortaya çıkan küçük bir böcektir. «ثعالة», dişi tilkinin özel adıdır; gayr-i munsariftir. «ثعلب» ve «تثعلب»: kurnazlıkla kaçtı ya da kurnazlığında tilkiye benzedi. «الثعلب», hilesi ve kurnazlığıyla meşhur, tüyleri her yıl dökülen bir hayvandır; «داء الثعلب» da bundandır ki saç dökülmesi olayıdır. Dişisine «ثعلبة», erkeğine «ثعلبان» denir; «ثعلب» kelimesi müzekkere de müennese de kullanılır; çoğulu «ثعالب» ve «ثعال»dir. «الثعلب» ayrıca mızrak demirinin yuvasına giren mızrak ucudur. Beşşâr şöyle dedi:
وجيش كجنح الليل يزحف بالحصى ... وبالشوك والخطي حصر ثعالبه
(Gecenin karanlığı gibi bir ordu ki çakıl taşları, dikenler ve uçları daralmış (حصر) Hattî mızraklarıyla ilerler.) [Mütercim notu: Metinde «حصر» yazılıdır; bu bağlamdaki anlamı belirsizdir, yazıldığı gibi çevrilmiştir.]
«الثعلبة» ayrıca kuyruk sokumu kemiği ve makattır. Kısacası bu kökün tilkilik (kurnazlık) ve yılanlık (akıcılık) özelliği açıktır.
(أَرْجِهْ): «أرجئه» de denir; hem hemze ile hem de (hemzesiz) tahfif ile okunmuştur; bunlar iki lügattir. Bir şeyi ertelediğinde «أرجأته» ve «أرجيته» denir. «المرجئة» (Mürcie) da bundandır.

* İ'rab:
(فَأَلْقى عَصاهُ فَإِذا هِيَ ثُعْبانٌ مُبِينٌ): Fâ atıf harfidir; «ألقى» mâzî fiildir; fâili müstetir olup takdiri «هو»dur; «عصاه» mef'ûlün bihtir. «فإذا»: fâ atıf harfidir; «إذا» fücâiyyedir (ani durum bildirir); zarf veya harftir; bunun bahsi daha önce ayrıntılı olarak geçmişti. «هي» mübtedâ, «ثعبان» haberdir; «مبين» sıfattır. Zünbûriyye meselesinin ve Sîbeveyh'in Yahyâ el-Bermekî'nin huzurunda bu mesele etrafında Kisâî ile ihtilafının bahsi daha önce geçmişti. (وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذا هِيَ بَيْضاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ): Cümle öncekine ma'tûftur ve i'rabında ona benzer.
(قالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هذا لَساحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ): Firavun dedi. «للملأ» «قال»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «حوله» zarf olup mahzûf bir hâle müteallikti. Zemahşerî'nin bunun i'rabında bir incelik gösterisi vardır; güzelliğinden dolayı onu naklediyoruz:
«Eğer 'حوله'de âmil nedir?' dersen, derim ki: O iki nasb ile mansûbdur: lafızda nasb ve mahalde nasb. Lafzî nasbda âmil, zarfta takdir edilen (fiil)dir; mahallî nasbda âmil ise hâl üzere nasbdır.»
«إنّ» fiile benzeyen harftir; «هذا» ismidir; lâm müzahlaka lâmıdır; «ساحر» haberdir; «عليم» ikinci haberdir. (يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ): Cümle «ساحر»in sıfatıdır. O, meczû recez bahrinden tam bir beyittir; ancak kasıt bulunmadığı için şiir değildir; bunun bahsi daha önce ayrıntılı olarak geçmişti. «أن» ve onun etki alanındakiler «يريد»in mef'ûlüdür; «من أرضكم» «يخرجكم»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «بسحره» de «يخرجكم»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur.
(فَماذا تَأْمُرُونَ): Fâ atıf harfidir; «ماذا» istifhâm ismi olup «تأمرون» sözünün mef'ûlün bihidir; ya da masdar manasında olduğu için mef'ûl-i mutlaktır; ya da «ما» istifhâm ismi, «ذا» haber olan ism-i mevsûldür ve «تأمرون» cümlesi sıladır. Bunu, gördüğü şey onu şaşkına çevirdikten ve dehşet ve hayret onu kapladıktan sonra söyledi. (قالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخاهُ وَابْعَثْ فِي الْمَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ): «قالوا» fiil ve fâildir; «أرجه» emir fiildir; hâ zamiri mef'ûlün bihtir; «أخاه» mef'ûlün maahtır ya da hâ zamirine ma'tûftur; «ابعث» «أرجه»ye ma'tûftur; «في المدائن» «ابعث»e müteallikti; «حاشرين», mahzûf bir mef'ûlün bihin sıfatıdır; yani «sihirbazları toplayıp bir araya getirecek zaptiyeler (şurta)». (يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ): «يأتوك» emrin cevabı olduğu için meczûm muzâri fiildir; «بكل سحار» «يأتوك»e müteallik câr ve mecrûrdur; «عليم» «سحار»ın sıfatıdır.

* Fevâid:
الشُّرَط: tekili «شرطي»dir; bunlar valilerin yardımcılarının seçkinlerinden olan bir gruptur; bizim günlerimizde ise zabıtanın amirleri ve adamlarıdır. Kendileriyle tanınacakları bir alâmet edindikleri için böyle adlandırılmışlardır. es-Sıhâh'ta şöyle denir: «الشرط (harekeli olarak): muhafızlardır; kendileriyle tanınacakları bir alâmet edindikleri için böyle adlandırılmışlardır.» «الشرط» ayrıca savaşa ilk katılan ve ölüme hazırlanan ilk birliktir.

* Vocabulary:
(لَشِرْذِمَةٌ): The shirdhima is a small group of people; its plural is sharādhim and sharādhīm. Thiyāb sharādhim means torn garments, and sharradha al-jamʿ (with doubling) means he scattered the gathering.
(حاذِرُونَ): Alert (mutayaqqiẓūn). It is an intensive form of the active participle, and it was also read ḥādhirūn. Abū ʿUbayda said: The two are of one meaning; one says rajul ḥadhir and ḥādhir with one meaning. It is also said that there is a difference between them: the ḥadhir is the alert one and the ḥādhir the fearful one; and it is said that the ḥadhir is one created and disposed to caution, and the ḥādhir is one in whom that has befallen. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
"Ḥadhira ḥadharan (of the pattern taʿiba), and iḥtadhara and iḥtaraza all have one meaning: he prepared and made ready, so he is ḥādhir and ḥadhir, and the noun from it is al-ḥadhar like ḥamal. Ḥadhira al-shayʾ means he feared it, so the thing is maḥdhūr, that is, feared; and ḥadhartuhu al-shayʾ, so he is wary of it." In another reading, ḥādirūn with the unpointed dāl; the ḥādir is the fat, strong one. He said:
أحب الصبي السوء من أجل أمه ... وأبغضه من بغضها وهو حادر
(Gloss: I love the bad boy for the sake of his mother, and I hate him out of hatred of her, though he is stout.)
That is, the basis of loving a child is love for his mother, not the goodness of his qualities. The pronoun in أبغضه refers to the boy without his description, but this is the disposition of one immersed in the love of women.
(مُشْرِقِينَ): Entering the time of sunrise (shurūq), from sharaqat al-shams shurūqan when it rose.
(فِرْقٍ): With a kasra on the fāʾ, that is, a piece.
(الطود): The mountain, or its great mass, as in al-Qāmūs; the plural is aṭwād, and ṭāda yaṭūdu means he was firm.
(وَأَزْلَفْنا): We brought near.

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبادِي إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ) The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, to begin the command directed to Moses to travel by night with his people toward the sea, which was thirty years after the events mentioned above. أوحينا is a verb and agent; إلى موسى is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أوحينا; أن is explicative, because in revelation there is the meaning of saying without its letters; أسر is an imperative from asrā, that is, he travelled by night. In another reading, with a kasra on the nūn and the hamza of أسر as a connecting hamza, from sarā, a dialect form of asrā. بعبادي is attached to أسر or is a ḥāl, that is, "accompanied by my servants"; the clause إنكم متبعون is a justification of the command to travel by night. (فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي الْمَدائِنِ حاشِرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, even though in time there was a gap, because, as is reported, they were occupied with burying their dead from the plague that swept Egypt; أرسل فرعون is a verb and agent; في المدائن is a ḥāl; and حاشرين is the direct object. (إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ) The clause is the content of an omitted saying, accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "saying"; إن with its noun, the shifted lām, and شرذمة its khabar; قليلون is an adjective, because they were a minority, small [Translator's note: the source prints «فسئيلة؟؟؟», an illegible word followed by three question marks] in relation to Pharaoh's people. The secret of the sound masculine plural for a small group will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنا لَغائِظُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction or ḥāl; إن with its noun; لنا is attached to غائظون; the shifted lām; and غائظون is the khabar of إن, that is, "doers of what angers us". (وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حاذِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction or ḥāl; إن with its noun; the shifted lām; جميع is a first khabar and حذرون [Translator's note: the source prints «حذرون» rather than «حاذرون»] a second khabar, that is, "we are a people whose habit is alertness, caution and the use of resolve in affairs". Pharaoh wanted to cover the breach that had struck his awe, so he described himself and his clan with the most emphatic descriptions indicating firmness of rank and strength of spirit. (فَأَخْرَجْناهُمْ مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive; أخرجناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; من جنات وعيون is attached to أخرجناهم. He meant the orchards that lay on both banks of the Nile and the small rivers branching from the Nile and distributed among the houses. A lengthy description of Egypt will come in the section of benefits. (وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ) Conjoined to جنات وعيون. By "treasures" he meant the wealth beneath the earth, and singled it out because what was above it had its landmarks effaced, or because they had not spent it on what ought to be spent on goodness.
(كَذلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْناها بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "We brought them out in the like of that bringing-out". It is permissible to parse the kāf as an adjective of مقام كريم, that is, "a station like that station which they had"; and it is permissible to parse the kāf as nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "the matter is thus". وأورثناها: the wāw is a conjunction or parenthetical, and the latter is perhaps preferable; أورثناها is a verb, agent and first direct object, and بني إسرائيل a second direct object, that is, after the drowning of Pharaoh and his people. (فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أتبعوهم is a past verb, agent and second direct object [Translator's note: the source says «مفعول به ثان», "second direct object", though only the pronoun object is given], that is, they caught up with them; and مشرقين is a ḥāl. (فَلَمَّا تَراءَا الْجَمْعانِ قالَ أَصْحابُ مُوسى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal, adverbial, or a connective; تراءى الجمعان is a past verb and agent, that is, they faced each other and each saw the other; the clause قال has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لما; أصحاب is the agent of قال; and the clause إنا لمدركون is the content of the saying. (قالَ كَلَّا إِنَّ مَعِي رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ) قال موسى; كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproach. Moses wished to cast blame upon them for the weakness of their nerves and the slackness of their resolve, that is, "they will never overtake us". Then إن معي is a justification for this rebuke; إن is a particle resembling the verb; the adverbial is attached to an omitted element which is a fronted khabar, and ربي is its postponed noun; the clause سيهدين is resumptive. He erred who parsed it as a ḥāl, and the detail will come in the section of benefits. (فَأَوْحَيْنا إِلى مُوسى أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصاكَ الْبَحْرَ فَانْفَلَقَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أوحينا is a verb and agent; إلى موسى is attached to أوحينا; أن is explicative; اضرب بعصاك البحر is an imperative, a latent agent and a direct object; بعصاك is attached to اضرب; and in فانفلق the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, which has often gone before, that is, "he struck, and so it split". (فَكانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيمِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; كان with its noun; the kāf is a noun in the sense of "like", its khabar, or it is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and العظيم is an adjective of الطود. (وَأَزْلَفْنا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أزلفنا is a verb and agent; ثم is an adverbial in the sense of "there"; and الآخرين is the direct object. By them he meant Pharaoh's people, that is, "We brought them near to Moses' people".
(وَأَنْجَيْنا مُوسى وَمَنْ مَعَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ) وأنجينا is conjoined to what precedes; it is a verb and agent; موسى is the direct object; من is conjoined to موسى; معه is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of من; and أجمعين is an emphasis of من. (ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) A justification of what went before, that is, "We made that and decreed it only that it should be a sign and an admonition for people, but most of them did not take heed of it". في ذلك is the fronted khabar of إن; the shifted lām; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان with its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition [Translator's note: the source says «والباء حرف جر زائد» although no bāʾ appears in this verse as printed; the reference is to the form in the surah's refrain, which has not occurred in the verse text here; translated as written] and مؤمنين is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of كان. The redundancy of the bāʾ in the khabar of كان will come in the section of benefits. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) Conjoined to what precedes; إن with its noun; the shifted lām; هو is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; and العزيز الرحيم are two khabars of إن, or of هو, the clause being the khabar of إن.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون»: the shirdhima is the small group or party, as we mentioned in the section on vocabulary, and it would have been possible to be content with it as an expression of fewness; but he described it with "the fewest of the few" to increase their contempt and belittle their standing; then he pluralised their description so that it be known that every class of them is few; and he chose the sound masculine plural, which is the plural of paucity. These are four aspects that support one another in making them few. There is also a fifth aspect, which is that pluralising the adjective while the described is singular may be an exaggeration in the adherence of that description to the described and its extremity in it in relation to other described things. Reflect on this, for it is among the finest subtleties.

* Benefits:
1- Conditions for a ḥāl to be a clause:
A ḥāl is a clause on three conditions:
1- The clause must be declarative (khabariyya), that is, one that admits truth and falsehood. This condition is agreed upon, because the ḥāl is like the adjective, and the adjective cannot be a performative (inshāʾī) clause. As for what occurs in the hadith: «Do not sell gold for gold except hāʾ wa-hāʾ ["take and give"]», it is based on an implied saying, that is, "except saying hāʾ and hāʾ", from the side of the seller and the buyer.
In al-Murādī's commentary on al-Tashīl, the declarative includes the conditional, and it is permissible for it to occur as a ḥāl; but the statement of al-Mughnī contradicts it. The verified view is that regarding the conditional clause, if the speech is the apodosis and the condition is a restriction upon it, then if the apodosis is a declarative, the conditional clause is declarative, and if performative, performative; and if the speech is the whole of the condition and apodosis, it is not declarative, because the particle has taken it out of that.
Moreover, he erred who said, regarding the verse of one of the later poets:
أطلب ولا تضجر من مطلب ... فآفة الطالب أن يضجرا
أما ترى الحبل بتكراره ... في الصخرة الصمّاء قد أثرا
(Gloss: Seek, and do not grow weary of seeking, for the bane of the seeker is to grow weary. Do you not see the rope, by its repetition, has left its mark in the solid rock?)
that لا is prohibitive and that the wāw is the ḥāl-wāw. Ibn Hishām says in al-Mughnī: This is an error, and the correct view regarding the wāw is that it is a conjunction, either [conjoining] a maṣdar made up from أن and the verb, onto a maṣdar imagined from the preceding command, that is, "let there be from you seeking and non-wearying", or a clause onto a clause. On the first, the fatḥa of تضجر is an inflectional sign and لا is negative; on the second, the fatḥa is indeclinable by reason of composition, the original being ولا تضجرن with the light nūn of emphasis, which was dropped out of necessity, and لا is prohibitive, the conjunction being like «واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا». Then Ibn Hishām resumed his statement in al-Mughnī in the eighth type of the sixth aspect and said: "The sounder view is that the fatḥa, meaning the fatḥa of تضجر, is inflectional, like that in لا تأكل السمك وتشرب اللبن, not indeclinable because of an omitted nūn of emphasis."
2- The clause must not be introduced by an indication of futurity, because the purpose of the ḥāl is to specify the occurrence of the content of its governor with the time of occurrence of the content of the ḥāl, and that contradicts futurity. He erred who parsed «سيهدين» in the words of the Exalted «إني ذاهب إلى ربي سيهدين» as a ḥāl. The error is evident from the technical side; and as for the side of meaning, he made the meaning of the verse "I shall go guided", thus diverting the extension of time to the going, whereas in the verse it belongs to the guidance. It was answered that "guided" occurs after the going, in which there is an extension, so it must also have an extension, like the restricted. As for their saying «لأضربنه إن ذهب وإن مكث», a conditional clause was permitted there as a ḥāl although introduced by an indication of futurity, namely إن, because the meaning is "I shall strike him in every case", since it is not valid to stipulate the existence and the non-existence of a thing for one and the same thing.
3- It must be linked either by the wāw and the pronoun together, to strengthen the link, as in «ألم تر إلى الذين خرجوا من ديارهم وهم ألوف حذر الموت»: the clause هم ألوف is a ḥāl from the wāw in خرجوا, linked by the wāw and the pronoun, which is هم; or by the pronoun alone without the wāw, as in «اهبطوا بعضكم لبعض عدو»: بعضكم is a mubtadaʾ and عدو its khabar, and لبعض is attached to عدو or is a ḥāl from it, and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in اهبطوا, that is, "enemies to each other, each misleading the other", and it is linked by the pronoun alone, which is the kāf and mīm; or linked by the wāw alone without the pronoun, as in «لئن أكله الذئب ونحن عصبة»: the clause ونحن عصبة is a ḥāl from الذئب, linked by the wāw only, and نحن has no part in the linking since it does not refer back to the owner of the ḥāl.
2- The description of Egypt to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:
When ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ became settled in the governorship of Egypt, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to him: "Describe Egypt to me." He wrote back to him: "The letter of the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah prolong his life, has come, asking me about Egypt. Know, Commander of the Faithful, that Egypt is a dusty village and a green tree, its length a month and its breadth ten [days]. A dusty mountain and a dune of sand flank it, and in its midst strides a Nile blessed in its mornings, auspicious in its evenings, in which increase and decrease run like the course of the sun and the moon. It has a season in which it yields its milk and its flies multiply; the springs and wells of the earth feed it, until, when its flood has swollen and its waves have grown mighty, it overflows both its banks, and no escape from one village to another is possible except in small boats, light craft and skiffs which in appearance are like the leaves of the evening. Then, when it has completed its rise, it turns back on its heels as it first appeared in its course, and swells in its flow. At that time a despised community and a guarded people go out, who plough the land and sow grain in it, hoping thereby for growth from the Lord; what they strive for by their toil is for others, who obtain it from them without their effort. When the crop surrounds and shines, the dew waters it and the soil beneath nourishes it. So while Egypt, Commander of the Faithful, is a white pearl, behold, it is black ambergris; then behold, it is a green emerald; then behold, it is a variegated brocade. Blessed be Allah, the Creator of what He wills." — to the end of that delightful letter.
In al-Maqrīzī's Khiṭaṭ there is what clears up the obscurities of this letter:
"Some of them described Egypt and said: Three months it is a white pearl, three months a black musk, three months a green emerald, and three months a red ingot of gold. As for the white pearl, in the months of Abīb, Masrā and Tūt the water mounts over it, and you see the world white, with its estates on rises and hillocks like stars encircled by water from every side, so there is no way to any of its villages except by skiffs. As for the black musk, in the months of Bāba, Hātūr and Kīhak the water uncovers from the land, which turns into black earth, and in these months the sowing takes place. As for the green emerald, in the months of Ṭūba, Amshīr and Baramhāt the plants of the land and its spring multiply, and it becomes green as though it were an emerald. As for the red ingot, in the months of Baramūda, Bashans and Baʾūna the herbage reddens and the crop reaches harvest, and it is like an ingot of gold in appearance and benefit."
3- The redundancy of the bāʾ in the khabar of كان:
Laysa and kāna are distinguished by the permissibility of a redundant bāʾ in their khabars. Its redundancy is frequent in the khabar of laysa and of the Ḥijāzī mā; as for kāna, it is not made redundant except when preceded by negation or prohibition, as in the verse and as in the words of al-Shanfarā:
وإن مدّت الأيدي إلى الزاد لم أكن ... بأعجلهم إذا أجشع القوم أعجل
(Gloss: If hands are stretched toward the provisions, I am not the hastiest of them, when the people are most greedy, the hastiest.)

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive statement, brought to begin the narration of the third story. «كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين»: verb, agent and direct object. The verb is feminine in view of the meaning of «القوم», which is the nation and the group. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«al-qawm» is used as masculine and feminine, so one says «qāma al-qawm» and «qāmat al-qawm»; likewise every collective noun that has no singular from its own wording, such as «rahṭ» and «nafar»." In al-Zamakhsharī and al-Bayḍāwī: "«al-qawm» is feminine, and therefore its diminutive is «quwayma»", and this is taken as referring to the most common usage. If you ask: how did He say "the people of Noah denied the messengers" when they denied only Noah alone? I say: it is like their saying "So-and-so rides the beasts and wears the cloaks" when he has only one beast and one cloak. (إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) The adverb is attached to «كذبت»; the clause «قال» is in the position of the genitive because the adverb is annexed to it; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قال»; «أخوهم» is the agent of «قال» and «نوح» is a badal (substitute). He called him their brother only following their manner of speech, as in their saying "O brother of the Arabs" and "O brother of Tamīm", meaning "O one of them". Of this is the verse in al-Ḥamāsa:
لا يسألون أخاهم حين يندبهم ... في النائبات على ما قال برهانا
(They do not ask their brother, when he summons them in calamities, for proof of what he said.)
«ألا» is a particle of offering; «تتقون» is an imperfect verb and agent. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ) A justification for his offering them the inclination towards piety. «إن» and its noun; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) or to «رسول»; «رسول» is the khabar and «أمين» is an adjective. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «اتقوا الله»: imperative verb, agent and direct object; «أطيعون»: the fāʾ is a conjunction [Translator's note: the source says «الفاء»; the conjunction here is the wāw], and «أطيعون» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent, the nūn is the protective nūn, and the omitted yāʾ, omitted to keep the verse endings, is the direct object.
(وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «أسألكم» is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and «أجر» is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is a direct object; «إن» is negative; «أجري» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «على رب العالمين» is the khabar. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) Its i'rab was given just above. The five stories were opened with the command to piety to indicate that the heavenly religions agree on the obligation of knowing the truth and following it, and the very same sentence was repeated as emphasis of this lofty aim. (قالُوا: أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ) The hamza is for an interrogative of denial; «نؤمن» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we"; «لك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نؤمن»; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; «اتبعك الأرذلون» is a verb, direct object and agent. The ḥāl wāw here ought to have «qad» implied after it. This is a kind of foolishness: they measure the worthiness of followers by the amount of wealth and goods they enjoy, or by the lineage and standing by which they are distinguished, but Islam made all Muslims equal. (قالَ وَما عِلْمِي بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; «ما» may be interrogative or negative. On the first, it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ and «علمي» is its khabar, and «بما» is attached to «علمي» in every case; on making it negative, the khabar is omitted so that the speech becomes a clause with it. The clause «كانوا» is the ṣila of «ما» and the clause «يعملون» is the khabar of «كانوا». (إِنْ حِسابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّي لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ) «إن» is negative; «حسابهم» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «على ربي» is the khabar of «حسابهم»; «لو» is a particle of prevention (imtināʿiyya); «تشعرون» is an imperfect nominative verb. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, just as the object of «تشعرون» is omitted, its implied form being "that"; the implied apodosis is "you would not have faulted them, nor ascribed any deficiency to them". (وَما أَنَا بِطارِدِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is the Ḥijāzī «mā»; «أنا» is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; «طارد» is genitive in form, and in position the khabar of «ما»; «المؤمنين» is muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) «إن» is negative; «أنا» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «نذير» is the khabar and «مبين» an adjective. (قالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يا نُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمَرْجُومِينَ) The lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; «إن» is conditional; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تنته» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لم», and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; in «لتكونن» the lām is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted according to the well-known rule:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(Omit, when a condition and an oath come together, the answer of whichever you put later; that is binding.)
«تكونن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the noun of «تكونن» is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and «من المرجومين» is the khabar.
(قالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي كَذَّبُونِ) «رب» is the one addressed (vocative), annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted; «إن» and its noun; the clause «كذبون» is its khabar, and «كذبون» is a past verb, agent and direct object; the first-person yāʾ was omitted to keep the verse endings. (فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحاً وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «افتح» is an imperative verb whose meaning is supplication, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; «بيني» is an adverb attached to «افتح»; «بينهم» is conjoined to «بيني»; «فتحا» may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and may be a direct object. «al-Fatḥ» here is from «al-fatāḥa» in the sense of judgment, and «al-fattāḥ» is the judge, so called for his opening the locks of affairs. In al-Qāmūs: "«al-fatāḥa», with ḍamma and kasra; it is said «baynahumā fatāḥāt», that is, disputes." The meaning is: "judge between us as each of us deserves"; what is meant is "send down punishment upon them", and therefore he said «ونجني». «ونجني»: the wāw is a conjunction and «نجني» is conjoined to «احكم»; «ومن»: the wāw is a conjunction or of accompaniment, and «من» is conjoined to the yāʾ or is an object of accompaniment; «معي» is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of «من»; «من المؤمنين» is a ḥāl. (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and this is of the speech of the Exalted; «أنجيناه» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «من» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the hāʾ; «معه» is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; «في الفلك» is attached to the "being-in-place" to which the adverb is attached; «المشحون» is an adjective of «الفلك», and «al-mashḥūn» means "filled".
(ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنا بَعْدُ الْباقِينَ) «ثم» is a conjunction of delay; «أغرقنا» is a verb and agent; «بعد» is an adverb of time, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, the meaning being "after their rescue"; «الباقين» is the direct object of «أغرقنا». (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive statement to show the lesson of this story. «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «في ذلك» is an advanced khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; «آية» is the delayed noun of «إن»; the wāw is a conjunction or a ḥāl wāw; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun; «مؤمنين» is its khabar. He means that their overwhelming majority did not believe, and therefore they were seized; had even half of them at least been believers, they would have been saved. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; «هو» is a separating pronoun or a mubtadaʾ; «العزيز» is the khabar of «إن» or of «هو»; «الرحيم» is a second khabar. The i'rab of its like has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
The repetition in His saying «فاتقوا الله وأطيعون» is for emphasis and for fixing the matter in the souls, even though each of the two was tied to a reason: the first to trustworthiness, the second to the cutting off of covetousness. Its like is your saying: "Do you not fear Allah in my disobedience, when I raised you as a small child? Do you not fear Allah in my disobedience, when I taught you as a grown one?"
In it there is also advancing (taqdīm): the command to fear Allah is put before the command to obey him, because fear of Allah is the reason for obeying him.

* Vocabulary:
(نَخْلٍ): «Al-nakhl» and «al-nakhīl» is the well-known date-bearing tree, with a straight, tall trunk with knots; the singular is «nakhla» and «nakhīla». In al-Miṣbāḥ, in summary: «al-nakhl» is a collective noun, the singular being «nakhla», and every collective noun of this sort is used as feminine and masculine; as for «al-nakhīl», with yāʾ, it is feminine by agreement.
(طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ): What comes out of it like the blade of a sword, in whose interior are the stalks of the date cluster; it is likened to a sword blade in form and shape. In al-Mukhtār: "The spathe (ṭalʿ) is called «haḍīm» as long as it has not come out, because parts of it are folded into others", from their saying «kashḥ haḍīm» (a slender flank). In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "«Al-ṭalʿ» is a measure; you say 'the army is a ṭalʿ of a thousand'; and from the palm, something that comes out like two sandals joined together, with the fruit set in rows between them and the tip pointed; or what appears of its fruit at the beginning of its emergence." «Al-haḍīm» is the ripe, soft, tender, delicate.
(فارِهِينَ): It was also read «farihīn»: exultant, skilled in work, from «al-farah», which is intense joy. He said in al-Kashshāf: "«Al-farāha» is cleverness and vigour; from it 'a spirited horse' (khayl farha)."
(شِرْبٌ): With kasra on the shīn, meaning a share.
(فَعَقَرُوها): That is, one of them struck her with the sword on her legs. His name was Qudār. We shall relate the story that was woven around this story, to be an incentive for pens to compose an artistic story from it.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive clause, brought to begin the fifth story; it is a verb, agent and direct object. «Thamūd» is the name of Ṣāliḥ's tribe, named after their father, Thamūd, the grandfather of Ṣāliḥ. As to the expression of Ṣāliḥ in the plural, what was said earlier applies.
(إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صالِحٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) The adverb is attached to «كذبت»; the i'rab of the clause has been given. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ) Its i'rab has also been given.
(فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) Its i'rab has also been given. (وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) Its i'rab has also been given. (أَتُتْرَكُونَ فِي ما هاهُنا آمِنِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke; «تتركون» is a passive imperfect verb; «فيما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تتركون»; «ها» is a particle of attention; «هنا» is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative; «آمنين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تتركون», that is, in that bliss which is settled in this place; then He explained it by His saying: (فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ وَزُرُوعٍ وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُها هَضِيمٌ) «في جنات» is a badal of His saying «فيما هاهنا», with the preposition repeated; what follows is conjoined to «جنات»; «طلعها» is mubtadaʾ and «هضيم» is khabar, and the clause is an adjective of «نخل».
(وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبالِ بُيُوتاً فارِهِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «تنحتون» is conjoined to «تتركون», so it is within the scope of the interrogative of denial and rebuke, and the position of the rebuking interrogative clause is accusative as a ḥāl; «من الجبال» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تنحتون»; «بيوتا» is the direct object; «فارهين» is a ḥāl. A similar clause has already passed, in which was the carving (naḥt), which is «al-naḥr» [Translator's note: so the source; «al-najr», carving, is meant] and shaping. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) Its i'rab has been given.
(وَلا تُطِيعُوا أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ) The wāw is for ḥāl, and «لا» is prohibitive; «تطيعوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive «لا», and the wāw is the agent; «أمر المسرفين» is the object. The meaning of obeying a command will come in the section of Rhetoric. (الَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا يُصْلِحُونَ) «الذين» is an adjective of «المسرفين»; the clause «يفسدون» is the ṣila; «في الأرض» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يفسدون»; «ولا يصلحون» is conjoined to His saying «يفسدون». The secret of the conjunction will come in the section of Rhetoric. (قالُوا: إِنَّما أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ) «إنما» is the restraining particle with the restrained; «أنت» is mubtadaʾ and «من المسحرين» is the khabar, that is, those who were bewitched so much that the sorcery overcame their minds; the clause is the content of the saying. It was also said that «al-musaḥḥar» is the one who is sustained by food and drink, so «al-musaḥḥar» is the one who has a «saḥr», which is the lung; so it is as though they said, "You are only a human like us, who eats and drinks."
(ما أَنْتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا فَأْتِ بِآيَةٍ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) «ما» is negative; «أنت» is mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «بشر» is the khabar and «مثلنا» an adjective. In «فأت» the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you are truthful as you claim, then bring"; «بآية» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to His saying «فأت»; «إن» is conditional; «كنت»: «kāna» and its noun, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; «من الصادقين» is the khabar of «كنت»; the apodosis of «إن» is omitted, indicated by what precedes, that is, "then bring a sign".
(قالَ هذِهِ ناقَةٌ لَها شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ) «هذه» is mubtadaʾ and «ناقة» is khabar, and the clause is the content of the saying; «لها» is an advanced khabar and «شرب» a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is an adjective of «ناقة»; «لكم» is an advanced khabar and «شرب يوم» a delayed mubtadaʾ; «معلوم» is an adjective of «يوم».
(وَلا تَمَسُّوها بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is prohibitive; «تمسوها» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لا», the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object; «بسوء» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تمسوها»; in «فيأخذكم» the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation and «يأخذكم» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ; the kāf is the direct object; «عذاب» is the agent, «يوم» is muḍāf ilayhi and «عظيم» is an adjective of «يوم». (فَعَقَرُوها فَأَصْبَحُوا نادِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «عقروها»: verb, agent and direct object; in «فأصبحوا» the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أصبحوا نادمين»: «aṣbaḥa» is a defective past verb, the wāw is its noun and «نادمين» its khabar. You may also make «أصبحوا» a complete verb, the wāw the agent and «نادمين» a ḥāl; in the story of Ṣāliḥ there will come what favours its being complete. (فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذابُ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «أخذهم» is a past verb with an advanced direct object, and «العذاب» is a delayed agent; the clause «إن في ذلك لآية» is a justification for the seizing; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw or a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun and khabar. (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) Its i'rab has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين» there is a mental figurative expression (majāz ʿaqlī), because a command is not obeyed; the one obeyed is the one who gives it, that is, "do not obey the transgressors in their command".
2- Al-irdāf (the follow-on):
It would have sufficed to say «الذين يفسدون في الأرض», but since His saying «يفسدون» does not negate their being at times righteous, He followed it with His saying «ولا يصلحون» to show the perfection of their corruption and of their transgression in it.

* Benefits:
The story of Ṣāliḥ:
In al-Qurṭubī: "Allah revealed to Ṣāliḥ that his people would hamstring his she-camel, so he told them that. They said, 'We would never do it.' Ṣāliḥ said to them, 'In this month of yours a boy will be born who will hamstring her, and your destruction will be at his hands.' They said, 'No male will be born this month but we will kill him.' Nine of them had sons born in that month and they slaughtered their sons; then to the tenth one, who refused to slaughter his son, a son was born, and none had been born to him before. The tenth man's son was blue-eyed and ruddy and grew up quickly. Whenever he passed the nine and they saw him, they said, 'If our sons were alive they would be like this.' The nine were angry with Ṣāliḥ because he had been the cause of their killing their sons, so they banded together and swore by Allah, 'We will attack him and his family by night.' They said, 'We will go out on a journey so that people see our journey, and we will be in a cave; when night comes and Ṣāliḥ goes out to his mosque, we will come to him and kill him. Then we will say: we did not witness the destruction of his family, and we are truthful. They will believe us and know that we had gone out on a journey.' Ṣāliḥ did not sleep with them in the village but slept in the mosque, and when morning came he went to them and admonished them. When they entered the cave and wished to come out, the cave fell upon them and killed them. People who had learned of this saw it and cried out in the village, 'O servants of Allah! Was Ṣāliḥ not satisfied to order them to kill their children until he killed them?' So the people of the village agreed on hamstringing the she-camel."
The account of the hamstringing of the she-camel:
It is related that Misṭaʿ [Translator's note: the source prints «مسطعا»; in other sources this name appears as «مصدع», Miṣdaʿ] drove the she-camel into a narrow place in a mountain path and shot her with an arrow, which hit her leg, and she fell; then Qudār struck her. It was also said that he said, "I will not hamstring her until all of you agree." They would go in to the woman in her curtained chamber and say, "Do you agree?" and she would say, "Yes", and likewise their children.
Qudār became a proverb for ill omen. Zuhayr alluded to him, but erred, making him the "red one of ʿĀd" when he is the red one of Thamūd, in verses of his in which he describes war and warns his people of its evil results. We give them here in full because of their importance:
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتم ... وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم
(War is nothing but what you know and have tasted; it is not a matter of conjecture and hearsay.)
متى تبعثوها تبعثوها ذميمة ... وتضر إذا ضرّيتموها فتضرم
(When you rouse it, you rouse it hateful; and it grows fierce when you make it fierce, and it blazes.)
فتعرككم عرك الرحى بثفالها ... وتلقح كشافا ثم تنتج فتئثم
(It will grind you as the millstone grinds with its padding; it conceives, being mounted again, then bears, and bears twins.)
فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم ... كأحمر عاد ثم ترضع فتفطم
(It will bear you boys, every one of them more ill-omened than the red one of ʿĀd; then it suckles, and weans.)
That is, it bears you sons, each of whom matches in ill omen the hamstringer of the she-camel, who is Qudār ibn Sālif.

* Vocabulary:
(الذُّكْرانَ): One of the plurals of «dhakar»; «al-dhakar» is the opposite of the female. In al-Mukhtār: "«Al-dhakar» is the opposite of the female, and its plural is «dhukūr», «dhukrān» and «dhakāra», like «ḥijāra»." In al-Qāmūs many plurals are given for it: "Its plural is «dhukūr», «dhukūra», «dhukrān», «dhikār», «dhikāra» and «dhikara»."
(الْقالِينَ): Those who hate. «Al-qilā» is intense hatred, as if it were a hatred that roasts the heart and the liver. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«Qalaytu al-rajul aqlīhi», of the pattern «ramā», with «qilā» with kasra and shortened, and sometimes lengthened, means I hated him; and in a dialect, of the pattern «taʿiba»." The wording of al-Qāmūs: "«Qalāhu», like «ramāhu» and «raḍiyahu», «qilan», «qilāʾan» and «maqliyya»: he hated him and disliked him with utmost dislike, and so left him; or «qalāhu» in forsaking and «qaliyahu» in hatred."
(الْغابِرِينَ): He said in al-Kashshāf: "The meaning of «al-ghābirīn» in the punishment and destruction: those who were not saved." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«Ghabara ghubūran», of the pattern «qaʿada», means he remained; it is sometimes used for what has passed also, and so is among the contronyms (aḍdād). Al-Zubaydī said: «ghabara ghubūran» means he stayed; and in one dialect it is with the unpointed letter (ʿ-b-r) for the past and with the pointed (gh-b-r) for what remains; and «ghubbar al-shayʾ», of the pattern «sukkar», is its remainder." In al-Qāmūs: "«Ghabara ghubūran» means he stayed and he went, a contronym; he is «ghābir», from «ghubbar», like «rukkaʿ»; and «ghubr al-shayʾ», with ḍamma, is its remainder."

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive clause, brought to begin the sixth story. (إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) Lot was not their brother by lineage; he called him their brother only following their manner of speech, as earlier, or in view of his dwelling beside them and neighbouring them in their town. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ، فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ، وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) He opened every story with these verses and their i'rab has been given, so this renews the covenant with it. (أَتَأْتُونَ الذُّكْرانَ مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of denial and rebuke; «تأتون الذكران»: imperfect verb, agent and direct object; the position of the rebuking interrogative clause is the accusative as a ḥāl; and «من العالمين» is a ḥāl. (وَتَذَرُونَ ما خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ عادُونَ) «وتذرون» is conjoined to «تأتون», within the scope of the rebuking interrogative; it is an imperfect verb and agent; «ما» is the direct object; the clause «خلق لكم ربكم» is the ṣila; «من أزواجكم» is a ḥāl, taking «من» as explanatory, and it may also be partitive; the detail of all this will come in the section of Rhetoric. «بل» is a particle of transitional turning away; «أنتم» is mubtadaʾ; «قوم» is the khabar and «عادون» an adjective, that is, those who overstep the lawful to the unlawful, because the meaning of «al-ʿādī» is the one who transgresses in his wrongdoing, exceeding the limit in it. (قالُوا: لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يا لُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُخْرَجِينَ) «قالوا» is a past verb and agent; «لئن»: the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath and «إن» is conditional; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تنته» is an imperfect verb, jussive by «لم»; «لتكونن»: the lām falls in the answer of the oath; «تكونن» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the (elided) wāw is the noun of «تكونن» (Translator's note: the source says «والواو اسم تكونن», though the verb is second person singular and its noun is a latent pronoun, "you"; it is translated as written); «من المخرجين» is the khabar, that is, "of the number of those whom we have expelled". A detailed discussion of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. (قالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقالِينَ) «إن» and its noun; «لعملكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «القالين»; «من القالين» is the khabar of «إن», and the clause is the content of the saying. Some were strict and said, in the glosses on al-Bayḍāwī, the following: "«من القالين» is attached to an omitted word, that is, «laqālin min al-qālīn», and that omitted word is the khabar of «إن», and «من القالين» is an adjective, and «لعملكم» is attached to the omitted khabar; for if «من القالين» were made the khabar of «إن», the «qālīn» would operate in «لعملكم», which leads to putting the object of the ṣila before the relative noun, which is «al», though that is not permissible." I say: this, for all its precision and suitability to the rules, involves great artificiality that takes it to the impossible, and there is no call for this strictness, given that the use of «al» as a relative is almost rare.
(رَبِّ نَجِّنِي وَأَهْلِي مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ) «رب» is the one addressed, annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted from it; «نجني» is an imperative verb of supplication and the yāʾ is the direct object; «أهلي» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the yāʾ; «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نجني», and the clause «يعملون» is the ṣila of «ما». (فَنَجَّيْناهُ وَأَهْلَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction on an implied omitted element so that the story is coherent; «نجيناه» is a past verb, agent and direct object; «أهله» is an object of accompaniment or conjoined to the hāʾ; «أجمعين» is emphasis. (إِلَّا عَجُوزاً فِي الْغابِرِينَ) «إلا» is a particle of exception; «عجوزا» is the excepted by «إلا», and she is his wife; «في الغابرين» is an adjective of «عجوزا», as if it were said "except an old woman who remained behind". (ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ) Conjoined to what precedes. (وَأَمْطَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَراً فَساءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ) «وأمطرنا» is conjoined to «دمرنا»; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أمطرنا»; «مطرا» is the direct object; in «فساء» the fāʾ is a conjunction and «ساء» is a verb of dispraise; «مطر المنذرين» is the agent of «ساء»; and the one specified for dispraise is omitted, being «their rain». What is meant by the rain is the stones that poured down upon them. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً وَما كانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) «إن», its advanced khabar and its delayed noun; the wāw is a ḥāl wāw; «ما» is negative; «كان» with its noun and khabar.
(وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ) Its i'rab has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying «وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم»: in this verse there is vagueness (ibhām) in His saying «ما خلق لكم», by which He intended «iqbāluhunna» [Translator's note: the source prints «إقبالهنّ»; «aqbāluhunna», their fronts, i.e. private parts, is meant], and in that there is regard for modesty and discretion. «من» may be explanatory and may be partitive.
2- Turning to the adjective (al-ʿudūl ilā al-ṣifa):
In His saying «لتكونن من المخرجين» and His saying «من القالين» there is a turning from the verbal clause to the adjective. Often in the Qur'an, especially in this form, there is a turning from expression by the verb to expression by the derived adjective, and then making the one described by it one of a group, as in Pharaoh's saying «لأجعلنك من المسجونين»; examples are many. The secret in this is that expression by the verb conveys only the occurrence, whereas expression by the adjective, and then making the one described by it one of a group, conveys something beyond the occurrence: that the mentioned adjective is like a mark of the one described, firmly attached to him, as if it were a title, and as if he belonged to a class that has become of this specific kind, famed for some bad marks. Listen to the saying of the Exalted «رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف», how He attached to them a bad title and made them of a base kind famed for the mark of lagging behind, until it became a title clinging to it. This is general in all that comes to you and in what has passed of such examples; so reflect on it and give it its due.

* Vocabulary:
(الْأَيْكَةِ): In the language, a dense tree; its plural is أيك. The Qāmūs says: "أيك يأيك (of the pattern تعب) أيكا, and استأيك الشجر: the trees became intertwined and formed an أيكة. The أيك is the dense, intertwined trees, the singular being أيكة." So الأيكة is applied to a single one of the أيك, and to a thicket of intertwined trees near Madyan. They said: their tree was the dūm (doum palm), and it was the village of Shuʿayb, named after its builder Madyan ibn Ibrāhīm, eight days' journey from Egypt. The Qur'an commentators and the lexicographers disagreed about it, and we shall quote some of what they said.
Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"أصحاب الأيكة was read with the hamza and without it (with the hamza dropped), and in the genitive as an annexation, which is the sound reading. As for whoever read it in the accusative and claimed that ليكة, on the pattern of ليلة, is the name of a town, that is a delusion to which the script of the muṣḥaf led him, since it is written in this sūra and in Sūrat (Ṣād) without an alif. There are things in the muṣḥaf written contrary to the analogy of the conventional orthography; it was written thus in these two sūras only according to the pronunciation of the speaker, just as the grammarians write لان and لولا in this form to show the pronunciation of the lightened form; and in the rest of the Qur'an it is written in the original way, and the story is one. Besides, ليكة is a name that is not known. It is reported that the أصحاب الأيكة were people of intertwined trees, and their tree was the dūm."
Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī said:
"In one reading, with the hamza dropped, its vowel cast onto the lām, and with fatḥa on the hāʾ (sic: the final letter); it is a thicket of trees near Madyan." This procedure implies that the existing lām is the lām of definiteness, and in that case his statement "and with fatḥa on the hāʾ" is not sound, since a noun joined with al, whether definite or otherwise, is put in the genitive with kasra, whether a transfer (of the vowel) has occurred in it or not. Some explained the fatḥa by saying that the noun is on the pattern of ليلة, so the lām is part of the structure of the word and there is no transfer, but rather the vowel of the lām is original; so putting it in the genitive with fatḥa is then clear.
Al-Shihāb al-Khafājī said:
"Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and others found this reading problematic, because there is no ground for the fatḥa, since the transfer of the vowel of the hamza does not require changing the case ending from kasra to fatḥa. The answer given is that ليكة in this reading is the name of the town, and it is not fully declined (ghayr muṣrafa) because of being a proper name and feminine; and the lām in it is part of the word, not the definite article, because that would require full declension. So the claim of the one who says it rests on a transfer is incorrect. With this, what the grammarians said is refuted, for they ascribed this reading to corruption."
Al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī went on at great length in justifying this reading, and his text is:
Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir read ليكة with a single lām and with fatḥa on the tāʾ (sic), making it a noun not defined by al, with أصحاب annexed to it, here and in (Ṣād) in particular; and the others read الأيكة, defined by al, in agreement with what is unanimously agreed in (al-Ḥijr) and in (Qāf). People's statements about the first reading are confused, and some of them were bold against its reciter, and I shall mention a portion of that for you. Its justification, according to what Abū ʿUbayda said, is that ليكة is the name of the village in which they lived, while الأيكة is the name of the whole country, so the difference between them is like the difference between Makka and Bakka.
The author of the Qāmūs said:
"Whoever reads الأيكة, it is the thicket; whoever reads ليكة, it is the name of the village, and its place is (under the letter) lām. In al-Bukhārī the form اللائكة, plural of أيكة, occurs, and it seems to be an error."
His commentator in al-Tāj said:
"His saying 'and it seems to be an error' is because it has no ground and none of the imams spoke it; but he (may Allah be pleased with him) is trustworthy in what he transmits, so one should think well of him, and his commentators answered for him and declared it sound."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said:
"أصحاب الأيكة is read with kasra on the tāʾ, with the hamza pronounced fully, or lightened by casting (its vowel), like الأنثى and الأنثى. ليكة has been read with a yāʾ after the lām and fatḥa on the tāʾ, but this does not hold, since ليكة does not exist in the language so as to be made a proper name; and if it is claimed that the hamza was turned into a lām, that is extremely far-fetched."
The أيك and the doves in poetry:
The أيك and its doves have captivated the poets, and their poems about it are many. Abū Ḥātim recited, from a man of Banū Nahshal:
ألام على فيض الدموع وإنني ... بفيض الدموع الجاريات جدير
أيبكي حمام الأيك من فقد إلفه ... وأصبر عنها إنني لصبور
(I am blamed for the overflowing of my tears, though I deserve the flowing tears. Shall the dove of the thicket weep for the loss of its mate, while I endure the loss of her? I am indeed patient.)
Al-Riyāshī recited from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: Muntajiʿ ibn Nabhān recited to me, from a man of Banū al-Ṣayyidāʾ:
دعت فوق أفنان من الأيك موهنا ... مطوقة ورقاء في إثر آلف
فهاجت عقابيل الهوى إذ ترنمت ... وشبت ضرام الشوق تحت الشراسف
بكت بجفون دمعها غير ذارف ... وأغرت جفوني بالدموع الذّوارف
(Late at night, above the branches of the thicket, a collared, ash-grey dove called out after a mate. When she trilled, she stirred the remnants of passion and kindled the blaze of longing beneath the ribs. She wept with eyelids whose tears did not fall, and she incited my eyelids to shed pouring tears.)
The curious thing in this chapter is the saying of ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim:
ألا يا حمام الأيك إلفك حاضر ... وغصنك ميّاد ففيم تنوح
أفق لا تنح من غير شيء فإنني ... بكيت زمانا والفؤاد صحيح
ولوعا فشطّت غربه دار زينب ... فها أنا أبكي والفؤاد جريح
(O dove of the thicket, your mate is present and your branch sways; so why do you mourn? Wake up, do not mourn for nothing, for I wept for a time while my heart was sound, in ardent love; then the abode of Zaynab grew distant, so now I weep while my heart is wounded.) [Translator's note: the third verse is garbled in the source (غربه, "its edge", seems out of place); translated as best it can be understood.]
(القسطاس): With kasra or ḍamma on the qāf, and it has been read with both: the straight balance. If it derives from القسط, which is justice, and the ʿayn is regarded as repeated [Translator's note: i.e. the sīn], then its pattern is فعلاس; otherwise it is quadriliteral. It is also said that it means "justice" in Greek (Rūmī).
(وَلا تَعْثَوْا): And do not spread corruption. One says عثا في الأرض and عثي, and that is like highway robbery, raiding and destroying crops. In al-Mukhtār: "عثا في الأرض: he corrupted; its pattern is that of سما; and عثي with kasra, عثوا also, and عثى with two fatḥas on the pattern of فتى. Allah the Exalted said: 'ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين'." I say: al-Azharī said: "The readers all agree on fatḥa of the thāʾ, which indicates that the Qur'an was revealed in the second dialect."
(وَالْجِبِلَّةَ): With kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ and with shadda on the vowelled lām: the unified, coarse creation. In the Qāmūs: "الجبلة, الجبلة, الجبلة and الجبلّة—and this last is the one read—: the face and what faces you of it, the build, the nature, the origin, strength, and hardness of the ground." الجبل with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the bāʾ is the verbal noun of جبله الله على كذا, i.e. He moulded and created him thus; and the name of the nature is جبلة. This word, in this sense, has many synonyms: الجبلة, الخيم, الطبع, النحيزة, الطبيعة, النبيتة, الضريبة, السجية, الشنشنة, الخليقة, السليقة, السليقة (sic), الشيمة, الغريزة, النجار. Some have versified the meanings of الجبل, saying:
قد جبل الله الطباع جبلا ... وسمي المال الكثير جبلا
وعدد الناس الكثير جبلا ... بالضم إن أردت أو بالكسر
وجه وقوة وغيث جبلة ... وامرأة غليظة والجبلة
جماعة أو كثرة كالجبله ... لقدح من خشب ذي كبر
(Allah has moulded natures, jabalan; abundant wealth is also called jabal; and a great number of people is jabal, with ḍamma if you wish, or with kasra; a face, strength and rain, jibla; a coarse woman, and the jibla; a group or a multitude like the jabla; for a large wooden cup.) [Translator's note: the verses are obscure and appear corrupt in the source; the gloss is approximate.]
(كِسَفاً): With kasra on the kāf and fatḥa on the sīn; it has also been read كسفا with sukūn on the sīn, and both are plurals of كسفة, like قطع and سدر. Abū ʿUbayda said: "الكسف is the plural of كسفة, like سدر and سدرة; al-Sulamī and Ḥafṣ read كسفا, also the plural of كسفة, which is the piece and the side, like كسرة and كسر." In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "الكسفة is a piece of a thing; one says 'give me a كسفة of your garment', i.e. a piece; and one says الكسف and الكسفة are the same." Al-Akhfash said: "Whoever read كسفا from the sky made it singular, and whoever read كسفا made it a plural."
(الظُّلَّةِ): The narrow shade, and what one takes shade under from heat or cold, and whatever shades you, such as a tree; the plural is ظلل and ظلال. The "Day of the Ẓulla" became famous through their punishment: a cloud hovered above them and shaded them after intense heat had struck them, and it rained fire upon them, so they were burned up.

* I'rab:
(كَذَّبَ أَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) A resumptive statement, uttered to mention the seventh and last story in this sūra. (إِذْ قالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلا تَتَّقُونَ) This verse and those after it have been covered in all seven stories, and the secret of that will come in the chapter on rhetoric. He did not say "their brother" as He said of the prophets before him, because he was not of the أصحاب الأيكة by lineage; when He mentioned Madyan, He said "their brother Shuʿayb" because he was of them. (إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ، فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ، وَما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلى رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) Verses covered in the seven stories. (أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَ) أوفوا is an imperative verb and fāʿil (agent), الكيل is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تكونوا is an imperfect defective verb jussive by لا, the wāw is its ism (subject), and من المخسرين is the khabar (predicate) of تكونوا. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Measuring is of three kinds: full, scanty, and excessive. He commanded the obligatory, which is giving full measure, and forbade the forbidden, which is giving scanty measure, and did not mention the excessive; it seems that leaving it out of both command and prohibition is evidence that if one does it, he has done well, and if he does not, there is no blame on him." (وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ) Its i'rab is clear. (وَلا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْياءَهُمْ وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, تبخسوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the wāw is fāʿil, الناس is the first mafʿūl bihi and أشياعهم is the second mafʿūl bihi. [Translator's note: the source writes أشياعهم; the Qur'anic word is أَشْياءَهُمْ.]
Among their sayings: "لا تبخس أخاك حقه" (Do not diminish your brother of his right). And ولا تعثوا is conjoined to ولا تبخسوا, في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعثوا, and مفسدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) confirming the meaning of its governing verb, although the two words differ in form. (وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالْجِبِلَّةَ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, اتقوا is an imperative verb and fāʿil, الذي is mafʿūl bihi, the clause خلقكم is the ṣila, الجبلة is conjoined to الذي, and الأولين is an adjective of الجبلة. (قالُوا إِنَّما أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ) إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (a restricting particle and the restricted), أنت is mubtadaʾ and من المسحرين is khabar; the sentence is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). (وَما أَنْتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنا وَإِنْ نَظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ الْكاذِبِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, أنت is mubtadaʾ, إلا is a particle of restriction, بشر is khabar, and مثلنا is an adjective of بشر; the wāw is a conjunction, إن is the lightened form of the heavy (إنّ) and its ism is omitted, نظنك is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن", and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and من الكاذبين is a khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
"If you say: the lightened إنّ and its lām—how did they come to be separated by the verb ظن and the second of its two objects? I say: the original is that they are separated by the mubtadaʾ and khabar, as in إن زيد لمنطلق. Since the two chapters—I mean the chapter of كان and the chapter of ظننت—are of the same kind as the chapter of mubtadaʾ and khabar, it was done in both chapters, so it was said إن كان زيد لمنطلقا and إن ظننته لمنطلقا." (فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنا كِسَفاً مِنَ السَّماءِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ), أسقط is an imperative verb, علينا is attached to أسقط, كسفا is mafʿūl bihi, and من السماء is an adjective of كسفا; إن is conditional, كنت is a past defective verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, the tāʾ is its ism, and من الصادقين is the khabar of كنت; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "فأسقط علينا".
