(Baht her uzak şeyi yaklaştırır, baht her kapalı kapıyı açar. Bahtlı birinin bir dal parçasını eline aldığını ve onun elinde yeşerdiğini işitirsen inan; mahrum birinin içmek için bir suya geldiğini ve suyun kuruduğunu işitirsen doğrula. Allah'ın yarattıkları içinde tasaya en layık olan, dar bir rızıkla imtihan edilen himmet sahibi kimsedir. Bazen nefsime bir düşünce gelir de onun yüzünden hiç yaratılmamış olmayı dilerim.)
Geçen istişhad bize yeter; çünkü bu bizi maksattan çıkarabilir.
Boileau'nun şaire nasihatleri:
Bahsi, Fransız yazar Boileau'nun şaire yönelik zikrettiği değerli nasihatlerle bitiriyoruz. Bunların özeti şudur: Şair ahlâksızlıktan uzak durmalıdır. Aşkı tasvir etmek mubahtır, doğru; ancak bu tasvirde herhangi bir bayağılık bulunmaması şartıyla. Kıskançlıktan da sıyrılmalıdır; o, edebiyatçıların afetlerinden bir afettir ve birinde bulunursa onun yeteneklerinin zayıflığına delalet eden bir rezilettir.
Sonra onun sohbeti hoş ve konuşması tatlı olmalıdır. Ayrıca bir şairi lekeleyen şeylerden biri de himmetini mal kazanmaya yöneltmesidir; buna karşılık şan ve şerefe ulaşmaya çalışması ona yaraşır. Geçmişte nefisleri terbiye etmiş, onlarda vatanseverliği alevlendirmiş, hikmeti ve fazileti öğretmiş olan o ilahî sanat olan şiirin değerini düşürmemelidir.
2- Kâhin Satîh kimdir:
Tarih şunu rivayet eder: Gassânî Satîh (سطحيا [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «سطحيا» yazılı; doğrusu «سطيحا»dır.]) insanların en kâhiniydi. Arim selini önceden haber vermişti. Kafatası hariç bedeni bir elbise gibi dürülürdü; kafatasına elle dokunulduğunda kemiğinin yumuşaklığından dolayı iz bırakırdı. Daima yere serili hâldeydi. Söylendiğine göre 150 yıl yaşamış ve Muhammed'in (s.a.v.) doğduğu gece ölmüştür.
Kâhinliğinden biri şudur: Resûlullah'ın (s.a.v.) doğduğu gece Kisrâ'nın eyvanı sarsıldı ve ondan on dört şerefe düştü. Memleket halkı bunu büyük bir olay saydı. Şam valisi Kisrâ'ya o gece Semâve vadisinin (suyunun) kesildiğini yazdı; Yemen valisi Sâve gölünün o gece çekildiğini yazdı; Taberiye valisi o gece Taberiye gölünde suyun akmadığını yazdı; Fars valisi de ateşin o gece söndüğünü yazdı. Mektuplar art arda gelince tahtını ortaya çıkardı, memleket halkının karşısına çıktı ve onlara haberi bildirdi. Mûbezân şöyle dedi: «Ey hükümdar! O gece beni dehşete düşüren bir rüya gördüm: Asil Arap atlarını yeden azılı develer gördüm; sonunda Dicle'ye daldılar ve ülkemize yayıldılar.» (Kisrâ) «Onun yorumu hakkında sende ne var?» dedi. O şöyle dedi:
«Bende bir şey yok; ama Hîre'deki valine haber gönder, onların âlimlerinden birini sana göndersin; çünkü onlar olayların (geleceğin) bilgisine sahip kimselerdir.» Vali ona Abdülmesîh b. Nufeyle el-Gassânî'yi gönderdi. Kisrâ ona haberi bildirdi. O da: «Ey hükümdar! Bende bu konuda bir şey yok; ama beni dayım Satîh'e gönder» dedi. Onu yolcu etti. Yanına vardığında onu can çekişir hâlde buldu; ona seslendi, ama cevap vermedi. Bunun üzerine şöyle dedi:
أصمّ أم يسمع غطريف اليمن ... أتاك شيخ الحيّ من آل سنن
أبيض فضفاض الرداء والرسن
(Yemen'in efendisi sağır mı, yoksa işitiyor mu? Sana Senen ailesinden kabilenin şeyhi geldi; ak yüzlü, geniş cüppeli ve geniş yularlı.)
Satîh başını ona kaldırdı ve şöyle dedi: «Abdülmesîh, hızlı bir deve üzerinde, Satîh'e doğru geldi; Satîh ise kabrin kenarına varmışken. Seni Sâsânoğullarının hükümdarı gönderdi; eyvanın sarsılması, ateşlerin sönmesi ve Mûbezân'ın rüyası sebebiyle. O, asil Arap atlarını yeden azılı develer gördü; sonunda vadiye daldılar ve ülkeye yayıldılar. Ey Abdülmesîh! Tilâvet ortaya çıktığında, Semâve vadisi taştığında ve asa sahibi zuhur ettiğinde, Şam Satîh için Şam olmaktan çıkar (orası artık bildiği yer olmaz). Onlardan, düşen şerefeler sayısınca kral ve kraliçe hükümdar olacaktır. Gelecek olan her şey gelecektir.» Sonra şöyle dedi:
إن كان ملك بني ساسان أفرطهم ... فإن ذا الدهر أطوار دهارير
منهم بنو الصرح بهرام وأخوته ... والهرمزان وسابور وسابور
فربما أصبحوا منهم بمنزلة ... يهاب صولهم الأسد المهاصير
حثوا المطي وجدوا في رحيلهم ... فما يقوم لهم سرج ولا كور والناس أبناء علات فمن علموا ... أن قد أقل فمحقور وم
هجور والخير والشر مقرونان في قرن ... والخير متبع والشر محذور
[Mütercim notu: Kaynakta satır düzeni bozuktur; «وم / هجور» = «ومهجور» mısra sınırında bölünmüştür.]
(Sâsânoğullarının hükümdarlığı onları terk ettiyse, bu zamanın hâlleri değişip durur. Onlardan Sarh oğulları Behrâm ve kardeşleri, Hürmüzân, Sâbûr ve Sâbûr vardır. Nice zaman onlar öyle bir mevkie ulaştılar ki saldırılarından kükreyen arslanlar bile çekinirdi. Binitlerini sürdüler ve yolculuklarında ciddiyetle ilerlediler; ne eyer ne de semer onlara dayanabildi. İnsanlar üvey kardeşler gibidir: Kimin yoksullaştığını bilirlerse o hor görülür ve terk edilir. Hayır ve şer bir ipe bağlıdır; hayrın peşinden gidilir, şerden sakınılır.)
Sonra (Abdülmesîh) Kisrâ'ya geldi ve ona haber verdi; bu onu kederlendirdi ve şöyle dedi: «Bizden on dört hükümdar saltanat sürene kadar zaman dönüp dolaşır.» Hâlbuki hepsi kırk yıl içinde hükümdar oldular.

* I'rab:
(هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ عَلى مَنْ تَنَزَّلُ الشَّياطِينُ): resumptive speech, brought to refute his being a soothsayer (kāhin) who receives from the devils. «هل» is an interrogative particle; «أنبئكم» is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). «على من» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تنزل»; it was put first to give it importance and because the interrogative has the front of the sentence. It suspends (taʿlīq) the verb of informing from governing, and the clause stands in place of the second and third objects. «تنزل» is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped, the original being «تتنزل»; «الشياطين» is the agent of «تنزل».
(تَنَزَّلُ عَلى كُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تنزل», and it is a badal (substitute) of the preposition and genitive noun before it. «أفاك» is the muḍāf ilayhi of «كل», and «أثيم» an adjective. They are the soothsayers and false claimants to prophecy, such as Shiqq, Saṭīḥ, Musaylima and Ṭalḥa [Translator's note: presumably Ṭulayḥa al-Asadī is meant].
(يُلْقُونَ السَّمْعَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ كاذِبُونَ): «يلقون» is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent. It refers to the devils, in which case the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it refers to «كل أفاك أثيم», inasmuch as that is plural in meaning, in which case the clause is resumptive or an adjective of «كل أفاك أثيم». The meaning of their "casting the hearing" is their listening intently to the Highest Assembly so as to steal something [Translator's note: the source prints «ليسترقو»], or casting the thing heard to the soothsayers. «السمع» is the direct object. The wāw is of ḥāl; «أكثرهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كاذبون» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.
(وَالشُّعَراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغاوُونَ): also resumptive speech, brought to refute his being a poet, as they claimed. An ample discussion of poetry, and of who the poets are whom the deviators follow, will come in the Benefits section. «الشعراء» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يتبعهم» its khabar; «يتبعهم» is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object, and «الغاوون» is the postponed agent.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي كُلِّ وادٍ يَهِيمُونَ): the clause is explicative (mufassira). The hamza is of the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "anta" (you). «أن» and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of «تر». «في كل واد» are attached to «يهيمون»; «يهيمون» is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is the khabar of «أنهم». It is also permissible to attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted word which is the khabar, the clause «يهيمون» being a ḥāl. The representation of their going into every path of speech by the image of a valley will be discussed in the Rhetoric section.
(وَأَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ ما لا يَفْعَلُونَ): a conjoined clause.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً): «إلا» is a particle of exception, and «الذين» is excepted (mustathnā) from the censured poets. The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause); «عملوا الصالحات» is conjoined to «آمنوا» and falls within the scope of the ṣila; «ذكروا الله» is also conjoined; «كثيرا» is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e., "they remembered Allah with much remembrance", or an adjective of an omitted adverb of time, i.e., "much time".
(وَانْتَصَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا): conjoined to what preceded. «ما» is maṣdariyya, i.e., "after their being wronged", an instance of annexing the maṣdar (verbal noun) to its object.
(وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, the sīn is a particle of futurity, «يعلم» is an imperfect verb and «الذين» its agent; the clause «ظلموا» is the ṣila. «أي منقلب» is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, because «أي» is parsed according to what it is annexed to; it has suspended «يعلم» from governing. Note that what governs «أي» is «ينقلبون», not «يعلم», because interrogative nouns are not governed by what precedes them. Al-Naḥḥās said: «The truth of the matter is that the interrogative is one meaning and what precedes it is another meaning; if it governed it, some meanings would enter into others.»

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون» there is a subtle istiʿāra tamthīliyya (representational metaphor): there is no valley, no ravines and no wandering; it is only penetration into the regions of speech, going astray in descriptions, amatory verse (taghazzul), tashbīb and nasīb, and little concern for the honour they violate and the rumours they spread. The details of that will come in the discussion of poetry in the Benefits section. It is related of al-Farazdaq that Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik heard his words:
فبتن بجانبي مصرعات ... وبت أفض إغلاق الختام
(They spent the night beside me, laid low, while I spent it breaking the locks of the seals.)
and said: "The prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is now due upon you." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has averted the ḥadd from me by His words «وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون»."

* Benefits:
1- The merit of poetry:
The exception of the righteous poets — those who defend their homelands, call to virtues and reform, and depict the faults and evils of society in order to mend its cracks — shows the lofty rank and high station poetry has. Al-Bukhārī related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Some poetry is wisdom." From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and began speaking in a certain way, and he said: 'Some eloquence is magic, and some poetry is wisdom.'" Abū Dāwūd transmitted it. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Poetry is speech; some of it is good and some of it is ugly, so take the good and leave the ugly." Al-Shaʿbī said: "Abū Bakr used to compose poetry, ʿUmar used to compose poetry, ʿUthmān used to compose poetry, and ʿAlī was a better poet than the three, may Allah be pleased with them all."
Between verse and prose:
The author of al-ʿUmda said: «The speech of the Arabs is of two kinds: versified and prose, and each of them has three grades: excellent, middling and poor. When the two grades agree in measure and are equal in value, and neither has any superiority over the other, the judgment goes to poetry, as is evident in the naming, because every versified piece is better than every prose piece of its kind by customary acknowledgement. Do you not see that pearls — which are the brother of speech and its kin, to which it is compared and by which it is likened — when they are scattered (manthūr), are not safe and are not used for the purpose for which they were acquired and selected, even though they are of higher worth and greater price; but when they are strung (manẓūm), that preserves them better from being cheapened and shows their beauty better despite much use. Likewise speech, when it is scattered, is dispersed in the ears and rolls away from natural dispositions.»
Lying is blameworthy except from poets:
Among its merits is that lying, whose ugliness people agree upon, is good in it; and it suffices you that it made lying good and forgave its ugliness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr when he had written to his brother Bujayr forbidding him from Islam and had mentioned the Prophet ﷺ in a way that angered him. His brother sent to him: "Woe to you! The Prophet has threatened you because of what reached him about you; he had threatened men in Mecca among those who satirized him and harmed him, and he killed them — meaning Ibn Khaṭal and Ibn Ḥubāba — and those who remain of the poets of Quraysh, such as Ibn al-Zibaʿrā and Hubayra ibn Abī Wahb, have fled in every direction. If you have any need for your life, fly to the Messenger of Allah, for he does not kill one who comes repenting; otherwise flee to your place of safety, for by Allah he will kill you." The earth became narrow for him, and he came to the Messenger of Allah in disguise. When the Prophet [Translator's note: the source prints «البني», a misprint for «النبي»] had prayed the dawn prayer, Kaʿb put his hand in the hand of the Messenger of Allah and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr has come seeking safe-conduct [Translator's note: the source prints «مسنأمنا», a misprint for «مستأمنا»], repenting; will you grant him safety, so that I bring him to you?" He said: "He is safe." Then Kaʿb uncovered his face and said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah; this is the place of one who seeks refuge with you. I am Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr." The Messenger of Allah granted him safety, and Kaʿb recited his ode whose beginning is:
بانت سعاد فقلبي اليوم متبول ... متيّم إثرها لم يفد مكبول
(Suʿād has departed, and my heart today is love-sick, enslaved in her wake, a captive unransomed.)
In it, after his amatory prelude and the mention of the intensity of his fear and dread, he says:
أنبئت أن رسول الله أوعدني ... والعفو عند رسول الله مأمول
(I was told that the Messenger of Allah threatened me, and pardon is hoped for from the Messenger of Allah.)
مهلا هداك الذي أعطاك نافلة الق ... سر آن فيها مواعيظ وتفصيل
(Gently! May He guide you who gave you the gift of the Qur'an, in which are admonitions and detailed exposition.) [Translator's note: «الق ... سر آن» is as printed in the source; the word is «القرآن», split across the hemistichs.]
لا تأخذنّي بأقوال الوشاة فلم ... أذنب وقد كثرت فيّ الأقاويل
(Do not seize me on the words of slanderers, for I have not sinned, though the rumours about me have multiplied.)
The Prophet did not reproach him for his words — and he would not have threatened him over a falsehood — rather he pardoned him and gave him his cloak (burda). Muʿāwiya bought it from him for thirty thousand dirhams — al-ʿUtbī said for twenty thousand — and it is the one the caliphs inherited, wearing it on Fridays and festivals.
It is related that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by Ḥassān while he was reciting poetry in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "A grumbling like the grumbling of a camel?" Ḥassān said: "Leave me alone, ʿUmar; by Allah, you know that I used to recite in this mosque before one who was better than you, and he did not object to it." ʿUmar said: "You have spoken the truth."
The author of al-ʿUmda said: «As for the argument of one who does not understand the drift of the speech from the words of the Exalted «والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون، ألم تر أنهم في كل واد يهيمون، وأنهم يقولون ما لا يفعلون», it is an error and a bad interpretation, because what is meant by this text is the poets of the polytheists who attacked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with satire and touched him with harm. As for the believers other than them, they are not included in any of that. Do you not hear how Allah the Mighty and Majestic excepted them and drew attention to them, saying: «إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وذكروا الله كثيرا وانتصروا من بعد ما ظلموا»? He means the Prophet's poets who defended him and answered the polytheists on his behalf, such as Ḥassān ibn Thābit, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa. The Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the source prints «صلى الله عليهم وسلم»] said of them: "These few are harder on Quraysh than the shower of arrows" [Translator's note: the source prints «نصح النبل»; the familiar wording is «نضح النبل»], and he said to Ḥassān ibn Thābit: "Satirize them — meaning Quraysh — and the Holy Spirit is with you; by Allah, your satire is harder on them than the fall of arrows in the darkness before dawn. And meet Abū Bakr, so that he teaches you those foibles [of theirs]." If poetry were forbidden or disliked, the Prophet would not have taken poets whom he rewarded for poetry, ordered to compose it and listened to it from them.
As for his words ﷺ: "That the belly of one of you be filled with pus until it corrupts it is better for him than that it be filled with poetry," this refers only to one in whose heart poetry has prevailed [Translator's note: the source prints «من غلب الشعراء على قلبه», "whose heart the poets prevailed over"; «الشعر» seems intended] and taken possession of him, until it distracts him from his religion and the performance of his obligations and prevents him from the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.»
Many of the rightly guided caliphs, the eminent Companions and Successors, and the famous jurists composed poetry.
Of that is the poetry of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. They said: his name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, and it is said that ʿAtīq was a nickname of his. He said, concerning the raid of ʿUbayda ibn al-Ḥārith [Translator's note: the poem's lines are broken across lines in the source; they are given here as whole verses, with the text unchanged]:
أمن طيف سلمى بالبطاح الدمائث ... أرقت أوامر في العشيرة حادث
(Was it from the phantom of Salmā in the soft valleys that I lay sleepless, or from something that has befallen the clan?)
ترى من لؤي فرقة لا يصدّها ... عن الكفر تذكير ولا بعث باعث
(You see a band of Luʾayy whom neither reminder nor any rousing turns back from disbelief.)
رسول أتاهم صادق فتكذّبوا ... عليه وقالوا: لست فينا بماكث
(A truthful Messenger came to them, and they belied him and said: "You shall not remain among us.")
إذا ما دعوناهم إلى الحق أدبروا ... وهرّوا هرير المجمرات اللواهث
(Whenever we called them to the truth they turned away and snarled like panting dogs.)
فكم قد متتنا فيهم بقرابة ... وترك التقى شيء لهم غير كارث
(How often we appealed to them by kinship! Yet abandoning piety is something that does not trouble them.)
فإن يرجعوا عن كفرهم وعقوقهم ... فما طيبات الحلّ مثل الخبائث
(If they turn back from their disbelief and undutifulness — the good lawful things are not like the foul ones.)
وإن يركبوا طغيانهم وضلالهم ... فليس عذاب الله عنهم بلابث
(And if they ride on in their transgression and error, Allah's punishment will not be slow to reach them.)
فأولى برب الراقصات عشية ... حراجيح تخدي في السريح الرثائث
(I swear by the Lord of the camels that trot at evening, lean ones pacing in worn-out sandals,)
كأدم ظباء حول مكة عكف ... يردن حياض البئر ذات النبائث
(like tawny gazelles staying about Mecca, coming down to the troughs of the well with its dug-up earth,)
لئن لم يفيقوا عاجلا من ضلالهم ... ولست إذا آليت قولا بحانث
(that if they do not soon wake from their error — and when I swear an oath I do not break it —)
لتبتدرنهم غارة ذات مصدق ... تحرم أطهار النساء الطوامث
(a raid of true valour will surely rush upon them, forbidding [to them] the pure and the menstruating women alike,)
تغادر قتلى تعصب الطير حولهم ... ولا يرأف الكفار رأف ابن حارث
(leaving slain men about whom the birds flock; and Ibn Ḥārith shows the disbelievers no pity.)
فأبلغ بني سهم لديك رسالة ... وكل كفور يبتغي الشر باحث
(So convey from me a message to Banū Sahm and to every ungrateful one who seeks out evil:)
فإن شتموا عرضي على سوء رأيهم ... فإني من أعراضهم غير شاعث
(if in their ill judgment they revile my honour, I shall not stain theirs.)
Here it must be pointed out that Ibn Hishām said in his Sīra: «Most of the people of knowledge deny that this ode is by Abū Bakr.»
Of the poetry of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him — who was among the most discerning critics of poetry in his time and the most penetrating in his knowledge of it:
هوّن عليك فإن الأمو ... ر بكف الإله مقاديرها
(Take it easy, for the measures of all affairs are in the hand of God;)
فليس يأتيك منهيها ... ولا قاصر عنك مأمورها
(what is forbidden of them will not come to you, nor will what is decreed fall short of you.)
Also of his poetry, when he had put on a new cloak and people looked at him:
لا شيء مما ترى تبقى بشاشته ... يبقى الإله ويفنى المال والولد
(Nothing you see keeps its brightness; God remains, while wealth and children perish.)
لم تغن عن هرمز يوما خزائنه ... والخلد قد حاولت عاد فما خلدوا
(His treasures did not avail Hurmuz one day; ʿĀd sought immortality, yet they did not endure.)
ولا سليمان إذ تجري الرياح له ... والجنّ والإنس فيما بينها ترد
(Nor Solomon, when the winds ran for him, and jinn and men came and went between them.)
حوض هنالك مورود بلا كذب ... لا بد من ورده يوما كما وردوا
(There is a watering-place there, truly to be reached; one day it must be reached, as they reached it.)
Of the poetry of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him:
غنى النفس يغني النفس حتى يكفّها ... وإن عضّها حتى يضر بها الفقر
(Richness of soul enriches the soul until it restrains it, even if poverty bites it until it harms it.)
وما عمرة- فاصبر لها إن لقيتها- بكائنة إلا سيتبعها يسر
(No hardship — so be patient with it if you meet it — comes to be but ease will follow it.) [Translator's note: the source prints «عمرة»; the sense requires «عسرة» (hardship).]
Of the poetry of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, what he said on the day of Ṣiffīn, mentioning Hamdān and their support of him:
ولما رأيت الخيل ترجم بالقنا ... نواصيّها حمر النحور دوامي
(When I saw the horses pelted with spears in their forelocks, their breasts red and bleeding,)
وأعرض نقع في السماء كأنه ... عجاجة دجن ملبس بقتام
(and dust spread broad in the sky like the cloud of a gloomy day clothed in murk,)
ونادى ابن هند في الكلاع وحمير ... وكندة في لخم وحيّ جذام
(and the son of Hind called out among al-Kalāʿ and Ḥimyar, Kinda, Lakhm and the tribe of Judhām,)
تيمّمت همدان الذين هم هم ... - إذا ناب دهر- جنتي وسهامي
(I made for Hamdān, who are — when fate strikes — my shield and my arrows.)
فجاوبني من خيل همدان عصبة ... فوارس من همدان غير لئام
(A band of Hamdān's horsemen answered me, knights of Hamdān, no base men.)
فخاضوا لظاها واستطاروا شرارها ... وكانوا لدى الهيجا كشرب مدام
(They plunged into its blaze and scattered its sparks, and in the fray they were like drinkers of wine.)
فلو كنت بوّابا على باب جنة ... لقلت لهمدان ادخلوا بسلام
(Were I a gatekeeper at the gate of Paradise, I would say to Hamdān: "Enter in peace.")
Of the poetry of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, when he came out to his companions dyed, related by al-Mubarrad:
تسوّد أعلاها وتأبى أصولها ... فليت الذي يسودّ منها هو الأصل
(Its tips turn black, but its roots refuse; would that what turns black were the root.)
Of the poetry of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, when his brother al-Ḥasan reproached him concerning his wife:
لعمرك انني لأحب دارا ... تحل بها سكينته والرباب
(By your life, I love a house in which Sukayna and al-Rabāb dwell;)
أحبهما وأبذل جلّ مالي ... وليس للائمي عندي عتاب
(I love them both and spend most of my wealth, and the one who blames me has no reproach from me.)
Many of the caliphs composed poetry. Of the poetry of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
أيقظان أنت اليوم أم أنت حالم ... وكيف يطيق النوم حيران هائم
(Are you awake today or dreaming? And how can one bewildered and distraught bear to sleep?)
فلو كنت يقظان الغداة لحرقت ... جفونا لعينيك الدموع السواجم
(Were you awake this morning, pouring tears would have burnt the lids of your eyes.)
نهارك يا مغرور سهو وغفلة ... وليلك نوم والردى لك لازم
(Your day, O deluded one, is distraction and heedlessness, your night is sleep, and death clings to you.)
وتشغل فيما سوف تكره غبّه ... كذلك في الدنيا تعيش البهائم
(You busy yourself with what you will hate the outcome of; thus do beasts live in this world.)
Among the jurists, Muḥammad ibn Idrīs al-Shāfiʿī was famous for poetry; he was among the most versatile of people in poetry, and he is the one who said:
ومتعب العيس مرتاحا إلى بلد ... والموت يطلبه في ذلك البلد
(Many a one wears out his camels, eager for a land, while death seeks him in that very land;)
وضاحك والمنايا فوق مفرقه ... لو كان يعلم غيبا مات من كمد
(and many a one laughs while death hovers over his head; if he knew the unseen he would die of grief.)
من كان لم يؤت علما في بقاء غد ... ماذا تفكره في رزق بعد غد
(One who has been given no knowledge that he will survive tomorrow — why does he think about provision for the day after?)
Among his famous masterpieces are his words on fortune:
الجدّ يدني كلّ شيء شاسع ... والجدّ يفتح كل باب مغلق
(Fortune brings near every distant thing, and fortune opens every closed door.)
فإذا سمعت بأن مجدورا حوى ... عودا فأورق في يديه فصدق
(If you hear that a fortunate man took hold of a dry stick and it put forth leaves in his hands, believe it.) [Translator's note: the source prints «مجدورا»; the sense requires «مجدودا» (fortunate).]
وإذا سمعت بأن محروما أتى ... ماء ليشربه فجفّ فحقق
(And if you hear that an unfortunate man came to water to drink it and it dried up, take it as true.)
وأحقّ خلق الله بالهم امرؤ ... ذو همة يبلى برزق ضيق
(The most deserving of God's creatures of worry is a man of high aspiration afflicted with narrow means.)
ولربّما عرضت لنفسي فكرة ... فأودّ منها أنني لم أخلق
(And sometimes a thought presents itself to me, so that because of it I wish I had not been created.)
[Translator's note: in the source the lines of this poem and of the preceding ones are broken across lines; they are given here as whole verses with the text unchanged.]
What we have cited as evidence suffices us, for more may take us away from our purpose.
Boileau's advice to the poet:
We close the discussion with the valuable advice that the French writer Boileau gave to the poet, which in summary is: the poet must keep himself clear of licentiousness; it is true that depicting love is permitted, but only so long as there is no kind of vulgarity in the depiction. He should strip himself of envy, for it is one of the banes of men of letters, a vice which, if found in one of them, indicates the weakness of his gifts.
Then he should be good company and pleasant in conversation. Further, among the things that disgrace a poet is directing his concern to earning money; on the contrary, it befits him to strive to attain glory. He must not lower the standing of poetry, that divine art which in times past refined souls, kindled patriotism in them and taught wisdom and virtue.
2- Who was Saṭīḥ the soothsayer:
History relates that Saṭīḥ [Translator's note: the source prints «سطحيا»] al-Ghassānī was the greatest soothsayer among people. He warned of the Flood of al-ʿArim. His body could be folded as a garment is folded, except for the skull of his head, and if it was touched with the hand it left an impression on it because of the softness of its bone. He always lay stretched flat on the ground. He lived 150 years, as it is said, and died on the night Muhammad ﷺ was born. Among his soothsaying is this: on the night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born, the hall (īwān) of Kisrā shook and fourteen of its battlements fell, and the people of the kingdom took that as a grave matter. The governor of Syria wrote to Kisrā that the valley of al-Samāwa had been cut off that night; the governor of Yemen wrote to him that the lake of Sāwa had sunk that night; the governor of Tiberias wrote to him that the water had not flowed that night in the lake of Tiberias; and the governor of Persia wrote to him that the fire had gone out that night. When the letters came to him one after another, he displayed his throne and came out to the people of his kingdom and told them the news. The Mōbadhān (chief priest) said: "O King, I saw a vision that night that terrified me: I saw unruly camels leading Arab horses until they plunged into the Tigris and spread through our lands." He said: "What do you have regarding its interpretation?" He said: "I have nothing, but send to your governor in al-Ḥīra to dispatch to you a man of their scholars, for they are people with knowledge of events." So he sent him ʿAbd al-Masīḥ ibn Nufayla al-Ghassānī, and Kisrā told him the news. He said: "O King, I have nothing about it, but equip me to go to my maternal uncle Saṭīḥ." So he equipped him, and when he came to him he found him at the point of death. He called to him, but he did not answer, so he said:
أصمّ أم يسمع غطريف اليمن ... أتاك شيخ الحيّ من آل سنن
أبيض فضفاض الرداء والرسن
(Is the chief of Yemen deaf, or does he hear? The elder of the tribe of the house of Sanan has come to you, fair, with ample cloak and halter.)
Saṭīḥ raised his head to him and said [Translator's note: the following speech is in rhymed prose]: "ʿAbd al-Masīḥ, on a swift camel, has come to Saṭīḥ, when he is at the edge of the grave. The king of the Banū Sāsān sent you, because of the shaking of the hall, the dying out of the fires, and the vision of the Mōbadhān: he saw unruly camels leading Arab horses until they plunged into the river and spread through the lands. O ʿAbd al-Masīḥ, when the recitation appears, the valley of al-Samāwa overflows, and the bearer of the staff appears, then Syria will not be Syria for Saṭīḥ. Of them there will reign kings and queens to the number of the battlements that fell, and all that is coming will come." Then he said:
إن كان ملك بني ساسان أفرطهم ... فإن ذا الدهر أطوار دهارير
(If the kingdom of the Banū Sāsān has passed them by, this fortune is phases of vicissitudes.)
منهم بنو الصرح بهرام وأخوته ... والهرمزان وسابور وسابور
(Among them were the lords of the palace, Bahrām and his brothers, al-Hurmuzān, Sābūr and Sābūr.)
فربما أصبحوا منهم بمنزلة ... يهاب صولهم الأسد المهاصير
(Often they stood in such a rank that the fierce lions feared their assault.)
حثوا المطي وجدوا في رحيلهم ... فما يقوم لهم سرج ولا كور
(They urged on their mounts and hurried in their departure, and neither saddle nor camel-saddle could hold them.)
والناس أبناء علات فمن علموا ... أن قد أقل فمحقور ومهجور
(People are sons of one father by different mothers: whomever they know to have become poor is despised and shunned.)
والخير والشر مقرونان في قرن ... والخير متبع والشر محذور
(Good and evil are tied together in one rope; good is followed and evil is guarded against.)
He went to Kisrā and told him, and that grieved him; he said: "Until fourteen kings of us reign, time will have turned." All of them reigned within forty years.

﴿إِلَّا﴾: istisnâ edatı. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: «إلا» ile müstesnâ olup nasb mahallinde. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: cümle sıladır. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mâzî fiil, fâil ve kesra ile mansûb mef'ûlün bih; cümle «آمنوا»ya ma'tûftur. ﴿وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾: mâzî fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾: mef'ûl-i mutlakın sıfatı, yani «ذكرا كثيرا» (çok anışla); cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿وَانْتَصَرُوا﴾: cümle ma'tûftur. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: câr ve mecrûr «انتصروا»ya müteallik. ﴿ما﴾: masdariyye. ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾: meçhul mâzî fiil ve nâib-i fâili; «ما» ve fiilden oluşan cümle, «بعد»in ona izâfetiyle cer mahallinde bir masdar te'vilindedir. ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ﴾: merfû muzâri fiil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: ism-i mevsûl, fâil; cümle isti'nâfiyyedir. ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾: mâzî fiil ve fâil; cümle sıladır [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta harekelenme ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾ şeklinde verilmiş; ayetteki kelime malum «ظَلَمُوا»dır, i'rabı da buna göredir]. ﴿أَيَّ﴾: istifhâm ismi, mef'ûl-i mutlak olarak nasb mahallinde. ﴿مُنْقَلَبٍ﴾: muzâfun ileyh. ﴿يَنْقَلِبُونَ﴾: nûnun sübûtuyla merfû muzâri fiil; vâv fâil; cümle «سيعلم»in iki mef'ûlünün yerini tutmuştur. Allah Teâlâ bu sûrede şairleri yermişti; bunun üzerine Hz. Peygamber'in (s.a.v.) şairleri Ka'b b. Mâlik, Abdullah b. Revâha ve Hassân b. Sâbit (Allah onlardan razı olsun) ağlayarak Resûlullah'a (s.a.v.) geldiler ve: «Ey Allah'ın Nebîsi! Allah bu ayeti, ﴿وَالشُّعَراءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغاوُونَ﴾ ayetini indirdi» dediler. O da onlara: «Ondan sonrasını okuyun: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا..﴾» buyurdu. Mü'minleri istisnâ eden bu ayetin inmesine sevindiler.

﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by إلا, in the position of accusative. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the kasra; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to آمنوا. ﴿وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ an adjective (naʿt) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "much remembrance"; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَانْتَصَرُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) انتصروا. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya). ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾ a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause, from ما and the verb, is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the annexation of بعد to it. ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿ظُلِمُوا﴾ here; the word in the verse is ظَلَمُوا (active), as the analysis "past verb and fāʿil" indicates.] ﴿أَيَّ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿مُنْقَلَبٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause stands in place of the two objects of سيعلم. Allah had censured the poets in this sura, so the poets of the Prophet ﷺ, Kaʿb ibn Mālik, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa and Ḥassān ibn Thābit, may Allah be pleased with them, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weeping, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, Allah has sent down this verse: والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون." He said to them: "Read what comes after it: إلا الذين آمنوا.."
And they rejoiced at the revelation of this verse, which excepted the believers.

﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾: «جَوابَ», «كانَ»nin haberidir; «أنْ قالُوا» ise isimdir. «فَما كانَ جَوابُ قَوْمِهِ إلّا أنْ قالُوا» (ref' ile) de caizdir.
Allah Teâlâ'nın ﴿إنَّهم أُناسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾ sözü: Lût kavmi bunu Lût'a ve onunla birlikte iman edenlere, onlarla alay etmek yoluyla söyledi; çünkü onlar erkeklerin arkalarından ve kadınların arkalarından (yaklaşmaktan) temiz kalmışlardı. İbn Ömer'den rivayet edilir ki ona: "Bu kadınlar hakkında caiz midir?" diye soruldu; ona: "Tahmîd hakkında ne dersin?" denildi; o da: "Müslümanlar bunu yapar mı?" dedi. Bu son derece büyük (bir günahtır); Allah'ın «فاحِشَة» (hayâsızlık) diye adlandırdığı şey budur.

Onun sözü: {تَخْرُجْ}: Zâhir olan, onun «أَدْخِلْ» sözünün cevâbı olmasıdır; yani «onu sokarsan bu sıfatla çıkar». Sözde bir hazif olduğu da söylenmiştir; takdiri: «وأَدْخِلْ يدَك تَدْخُلْ، وأَخْرِجْها تَخْرُجْ». Birincide ispat ettiğini ikincisinden, ikincide ispat ettiğini birincisinden hazfetmiştir. Bu, ihtiyaç olmayan bir takdirdir.
Onun sözü: {بَيْضَآءَ}: «تَخْرُجْ»un fâilinden hâldir. {مِنْ غَيْرِ سواء}nın başka bir hâl olması, «بَيْضاء»daki zamirden hâl olması veya «بَيْضاء»nın sıfatı olması câizdir.
Onun sözü: {فِي تِسْعِ}: Bunda birkaç vecih vardır: Birincisi: Üçüncü hâl olmasıdır; Ebü'l-Bekâ böyle demiştir, yani «يَخْرُجْ»un fâilinden; yani «dokuz âyet içinde bir âyet olarak». Bunu böyle takdir etmiştir. İkincisi: Mahzûf bir şeye müteallik olmasıdır; yani «dokuz âyet içinde git (اذهَبْ)». Zemahşerî'nin bunu tercih etmesi, bu konunun başında besmele zikredilirken geçmişti; onu şu söze benzetmişti:
3543 - وقُلْتُ إلى الطَعامِ فقالَ منهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Ben "yemeğe" dedim, onlardan biri dedi ki...)
ve «بالرَّفاهِ والبنين» (refah ve oğullarla!) sözlerine. Bu takdiri daha doğru ve daha güzel saymıştır. Üçüncüsü: «وأَلْقِ عَصاكَ وأَدْخِلْ» sözüne müteallik olmasıdır. Zemahşerî dedi ki: «Anlamın şu olması câizdir: "Asânı at ve elini dokuz âyet içine sok", yani dokuz âyetin toplamı içine. Bir diyen şöyle diyebilir: Âyetler on bir idi; bunlardan ikisi el ve asadır. Dokuz ise: Denizin yarılması (el-felk), tûfan, çekirge, bit, kurbağalar, kan, silinme (et-tamse), kendi çöllerindeki kuraklık ve ekinlerindeki eksilmedir.» (Zemahşerî'nin sözü) burada bitti. Buna göre «في», «مع» anlamında olur; çünkü o zaman el ve asa dokuzun dışında kalır. İbn Atıyye de böyle yapmıştır; yani «في تِسْع»i «أَلْقِ» ve «أَدْخِلْ»e bağlamış, ancak el ve asayı dokuzun cümlesinden saymıştır. Dedi ki: «Takdiri: Bunu sana hazırlarız ve dokuzun [cümlesi] içinde kolaylaştırırız.»
Zeccâc ise «في»yi «مِنْ» anlamında yapmıştır. Dedi ki: «"Benim için develerden on tane al, içinde iki aygır olsun" dediğin gibi; yani onlardan iki aygır.»
Onun sözü: {إلى فِرْعَوْنَ}: Bu, onu hâl yapmazsan «في تسعِ»in müteallik olduğu şeye müteallik olur. Hâl yaparsak mahzûfa müteallik kılarız; Ebü'l-Bekâ onu «فرعون'a gönderilmiş olarak» (مُرْسَلاً إلى فرعون) diye takdir etmiştir. Bunda nazar vardır; çünkü bu kayıtlı bir kevn'dir (kevn mukayyed) ve bu takdire Zeccâc ondan önce davranmıştır. Sanki ikisi de i'rabı değil anlamın tefsirini kastetmişlerdir. Ebü'l-Bekâ ayrıca onun «آيات»ın sıfatı olmasını da câiz görmüş ve «Firavun'a ulaşan» (واصلةً إلى فرعونَ) diye takdir etmiştir. Bunda da önceki geçen vardır.

His saying: {واستيقنتهآ}: This clause may be conjoined to the preceding clause. It may be a ḥāl from the agent of «جَحَدُوا», and this is stronger in blame. And istafʿala here has the meaning of tafaʿʿala, as in istaʿẓama and istakbara, meaning taʿaẓẓama and takabbara.
His saying: {ظُلْماً وَعُلُوّاً}: Both may be in the position of ḥāl, i.e. "wrongdoing and exalting themselves", or both may be objects of purpose, i.e. what drove that was wrongdoing and arrogance. ʿAbd Allāh, Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥa read «وعِليَّاً» with kasra on the ʿayn and the lām, turning the wāw into yāʾ. Its explanation has been covered at «عِتيَّا» in Maryam. It is also reported from al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb with ḍamma on the ʿayn as in «عِتيّا». It was also read «غُلُوَّاً» with the dotted ghayn, which is close to this meaning.
His saying: {كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ}: «كيف» is a fronted khabar and «عاقبةُ» its ism, the clause being in the accusative position by removal of the preposition, because it is suspended from «انْظُرْ» with the meaning "reflect".

Onun sözü: {وَأُوتِيَتْ}: «تَمْلِكُهم»e atfedilmiş olması câizdir. Mâzînin muzâriye atfı câiz olmuştur, çünkü muzâri onun anlamındadır; yani «مَلَكَتْهُمْ». «تَمْلِكُهم»in merfû zamirinden hâl olarak nasb mahallinde olması da câizdir; bunu câiz görene göre yanında «قد» gizlidir.
{مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ} sözü, akılla tahsis edilmiş âmm'dır; çünkü ona Süleyman'a verilen verilmemiştir.
Onun sözü: {وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ}: Bu cümlenin kendi başına bağımsız bir cümle olarak haber vermek için getirilmiş olması, «أُوتِيَتْ»e atfedilmiş olması ve «أُوتِيَتْ»in merfû zamirinden hâl olması câizdir. En güzeli, hâli câr ve mecrûr yapmak ve «عَرْشٌ»i onunla merfû kılmaktır. Bazıları «عَرْشٌ» üzerinde vakfeder ve onu na'tinden keser. Zemahşerî dedi ki: «Kıssacıların budalalarından bazıları {وَلَهَا عَرْشٌ} üzerinde vakfeder, sonra "عظيمٌ وَجَدْتُها" diye başlarlar; yani "Onu bulmam büyük bir iştir". Hüdhüdün onun arşını büyük bulmasından kaçmış, Allah'ın kitabının tahrif edilmesi gibi büyük bir iş içine düşmüştür.» Ben (Semîn) dedim: «النوكى», «أَنْوكِ»in çoğulu olarak ahmaklar demektir. Vakf konusunda zikrettiğini ed-Dânî Nâfi'den nakletmiş ve teyid etmiştir; Ebû Bekr b. el-Enbârî de, bunu bazı ilim ehline kadar çıkarmıştır; bu yüzden "kıssacıların budalaları" denmemelidir. Ed-Dânî bunu «عظيم»in mübtedâ, «وَجَدْتُها»nın haber olması üzere tahric etmiştir. Bu hatadır; mesûğ olmaksızın nekire ile nasıl başlanır ve onun hakkında, ondan bir râbıt bulunmayan bir cümleyle nasıl haber verilir? İ'rab, Zemahşerî'nin dediğidir: «عظيماً» mahzûf bir şeyin sıfatıdır, öne alınmış haberdir, [«وَجَدْتُها» ise sonraya bırakılmış mübtedâdır, yanında masdar harfi takdir edilir; yani: «Onu ve kavmini Allah Teâlâ'ya ibadet etmeyenler olarak bulmam büyük bir iştir».
[Mütercim notu: Kaynakta köşeli parantez burada açılmış, bir sonraki girdinin başında kapanmaktadır («هي التي بمعنى لَقِيْتُ] وأَصَبْتُ»); iki girdi bu yüzden kesintisiz okunmalıdır.]

His saying: {وَجَدتُّهَا}: This is the one meaning "I met" and "I came upon"; / so it takes one object, and «يَسْجُدون» is a ḥāl from its object and what is conjoined to it.
[Translator's note: the source text begins with a stray closing bracket "]" with no opening bracket; translated as the sense requires.]
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ}: Al-Kisāʾī read «ألا» lightened, and the others with shadda. As for al-Kisāʾī's reading, «ألا» in it is an alert and an opening particle, and «يا» after it is a vocative particle or also an alerting particle, as will come, and «اسْجُدوا» is an imperative verb. The proper writing, on this reading, would be «يا اسْجُدوا», but the Companions dropped the alif of «يا» and the hamzat al-waṣl of «اسْجُدوا» in writing, as both dropped in pronunciation, and joined the yāʾ to the sīn of «اسْجُدوا», so its form became «يَسْجُدوا» as you see. Thus the two readings coincided in pronunciation and writing and differed in analysis.
The grammarians differed about this «يا»: is it a particle of alerting, or of vocative with the one addressed omitted, its implied form being "O you, prostrate"? That was covered at His saying {ياليتني} [verse 73] in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. The preferred is that it is for alerting, so that it does not lead to much omission without anything remaining to indicate the omitted. Do you not see that the vocative clause itself is omitted; so if you claimed omission of the one addressed, the omission would be great and no governed element would remain to indicate its governor, unlike when you make it for alerting. But here we face the objection that before it is another alerting particle, namely «ألا». An excuse was made for that: that the two were combined for emphasis. And if they combined two operative particles for emphasis, as in his saying:
3559 - فَأَصْبَحْنَ لا يَسْألْنَنِي عَنْ بما به ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(So they became such that they ask me not about that which is in it…)
then non-operative ones are all the more fitting. Moreover they have combined two operative particles identical in wording and meaning, as in his saying:
3560 - فلا واللهِ لا يلفى لِما بي ... ولا لِلِما بهم أبداً دَواءُ
(No, by Allah, no remedy is found for what is in me, nor ever for what is in them.)
So this is more fitting. And the direct attachment of «يا» to an imperative verb, with «ألا» of opening before it, is frequent, as in his saying:
3561 - ألا يا اسْلَمِي ثُمَّ اسْلمي ثُمَّتَ اسْلَمي ... ثلاثَ تحيَّاتٍ وإنْ لَمْ تَكَلَّمي
(O be safe, then be safe, then again be safe: three greetings, even if you do not speak.)
and his saying:
3562 - ألا يا اسْلَمِي يا دارَ مَيَّ على البِلى ... ولا زالَ مُنْهَلاًّ بجَرْعائِكِ القَطْرُ
(O be safe, abode of Mayy, despite decay, and may rain ever pour on your sandy plain.)
and his saying:
3563 - ألا يا اسلمي ذاتَ الدَّماليجِ والعِقْدِ ... وذَاتَ اللِّثاثِ الجُمِّ والفاحِمِ الجَعْدِ
(O be safe, lady of the bracelets and necklace, lady of the abundant gums and the black curly hair.)
and his saying:
364 - ألا يا اسْلمي يا هندُ هندَ بني بدرٍ ... وإن كان حَيَّانا عِداً آخرَ الدهرِ
(O be safe, Hind, Hind of the Banū Badr, even if our two clans are enemies to the end of time.)
and his saying:
3565 - ألا يا اسْقِياني قبلَ حَبْلِ أبي بكرِ ... لعل منايانا قَرُبْنَ ولا نَدْري
(O give me drink before the rope of Abū Bakr; perhaps our deaths are near and we do not know.)
and his saying:
3566 - ألا يا اسْقِياني قبلَ غارةِ سِنْجالِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O give me drink before the raid of Sinjāl …)
and his saying:
3567 - فقالَتْ ألا يا اسْمَعْ أَعِظْكَ لخُطْبةٍ ... فقلتُ: سَمِعْنا فانْطِقي وأَصِيْبي
(She said, "O listen, I will admonish you with a speech." I said, "We are listening; speak and be right.")
And that has come even where «ألا» does not precede it, as in his saying:
3568 - يا دارَ هندٍ يا اسْلَمي ثُمَّ اسْلَمي ... بِسَمْسَِمٍ أو عَنْ يمين سَمْسَِمِ
(O abode of Hind, O be safe, then be safe, at Samsam or to the right of Samsam.)
You have known, then, that al-Kisāʾī's reading is strong because of the frequency of its occurrence in their language.
It has also been heard in prose; some have been heard saying: «ألا يا ارحموني» and «ألا يا تَصَدَّقوا علينا». As for the saying of another:
3569 - يا لعنةَ اللهِ والأقوامِ كلِّهمُ ... والصالحينَ على سَمْعانَ مِنْ جارِ
(O curse of Allah, and of all peoples and the righteous, upon Samʿān, as a neighbour!)
it is possible that «يا» is for the vocative with the one addressed omitted, and possible that it is for alerting, which is the more preferred for what has passed.
Know that for al-Kisāʾī, pausing at «يَهْتَدون» is a complete pause. He may pause on «ألا يا» together and begin «اسْجُدوا» with a hamza with ḍamma, and he may pause on «ألا» alone and on «يا» alone, because they are two separate particles. These two pauses are pauses of testing, not of choice, because they are two particles whose meaning is not complete except with what they are attached to; the readers did that only for examination and clarity. This, then, is the justification of al-Kisāʾī's reading, and the matter in it is easy.
As for the reading of the others, it needs close examination. There are many possibilities in it. The first: that the original of «ألاَّ» is «أَنْ لا», so «أنْ» is the particle governing the verb after it, and for that reason the nūn of the nominative dropped, and «لا» after it is a negative particle. And «أنْ» and what follows it are in the position of the object of «يَهْتَدون» by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to that they not / prostrate". And «لا» is redundant, like its redundancy in {لِّئَلاَّ يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الكتاب} [al-Ḥadīd: 29]. The second: that it is a badal from «أعمالَهم», with a parenthesis between them, the implied form being: "and Satan made the non-prostration to Allah attractive to them". The third: that it is a badal from «السبيل», also with «لا» redundant. The implied form is: "and he turned them away from prostration to Allah the Exalted". The fourth: that {أَلاَّ يَسْجُدُواْ} is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). There are two views about what it is attached to: the first, that it is attached to «زَيَّن», i.e. "he made it attractive to them so that they not prostrate"; the second, that it is attached to «صَدَّهم», i.e. "he turned them away so that they not prostrate". In «لا» then there are two views: the first, that it is not redundant, but negative in its sense of negation; the second, that it is redundant, the meaning being: "he made it attractive to them because of his expecting their prostration, or because of his fear of their prostration". Non-redundancy is more apparent.
The fifth: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. This mubtadaʾ is either implied as a pronoun referring to «أعمالَهم», the implied form being "it is that they not prostrate", so that «لا» is in its ordinary sense of negation; or implied as a pronoun referring to «السبيل», the implied form being "it is that they not prostrate", so that «لا» is redundant as previously stated, for the meaning to be sound.
On the four previous possibilities pausing at «يَهْتدون» is not allowed, because what follows it is either governed by it or by what precedes it, namely «زَيَّن» and «صَدَّ», or a badal of what precedes, from «أعمالَهم» or from «السبيل», as established and refined; unlike the fifth possibility, which is built on an implied mubtadaʾ, even if that pronoun is explained by what precedes it.
«ألاَّ» was written joined, not separated, so «أنْ» was not written separately from «لا». For that reason it is not allowed for these readers, in testing and examination, to pause on «أنْ» alone, because of its connection with «لا» in writing; rather they pause on «ألاَّ» as a whole. So said the readers. As for the grammarians, whenever they are asked about such a thing they pause, for clarity, at each word separately, out of the necessity of clarity, and its being written joined to «لا» does not prevent that. Then the readers' statement "it was written joined" has looseness and leniency, because the reality of this is that they would write the form of a nūn and join it to «لا», writing it «أَنْلا»; but since it was assimilated into what follows it in pronunciation and its sound went over to the sound of what follows it, they said that out of leniency.
Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: al-Zajjāj] based a ruling on the two readings: namely the obligation of the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwa) or its non-obligation. He made it obligatory with al-Kisāʾī's reading, as if because of the command in it, and did not make it obligatory in the reading of the others, for the absence of a command in it. But al-Zamakhsharī did not approve it of him, for he said: "If you ask: is the prostration of recitation obligatory in both readings, or in one of them? I say: it is obligatory in both, one of the two readings being a command to prostrate and the other a censure of the one who leaves it." So what al-Zajjāj mentioned, of the obligation of the prostration with the light form and not with the heavy, is not to be returned to.
I say: it is as if al-Zajjāj took the apparent sense of the command, and its apparent sense is obligation. Were we left with the verse alone, the prostration would be obligatory; but the Sunna indicated its recommendation rather than its obligation. Moreover we say: this is built on another consideration, namely whether this command is the speech of Allah the Exalted, or the speech of the hoopoe quoted from it. If it is the speech of Allah the Exalted, it is said: it entails obligation unless evidence comes to turn it from its apparent sense; and if it is the speech of the hoopoe, which is the apparent sense, there is, in its standing as evidence, a consideration that is not hidden.
Al-Aʿmash read «هَلاَّ» and «هَلا», turning the hamza into hāʾ, with shadda on «لا» and without it; and so it is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh. ʿAbd Allāh read «تَسْجُدون» with the tāʾ of address and the nūn of the nominative. It was also read so with yāʾ (third person). Whoever retains the nūn of the nominative, then «ألا» with shadda or without it is for urging (taḥḍīḍ); the lightened one may also be for offering (ʿarḍ), as in «ألا تَنْزِل عندنا نتحدَّث» ("Won't you stay with us so we may talk?"). In the version of ʿAbd Allāh also: «ألا هَلْ تَسْجدُون» in the second person.
His saying: {الذي يُخْرِجُ الخبء}: It may be in the genitive position as a naʿt of it, or a badal from it, or a bayān; or accusative / for praise; or nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Al-khab' is the maṣdar of «خَبَأْتُ الشَيءَ أخبَؤُه خَبْئاً», i.e. I concealed it; then it was applied to the thing concealed. Like it is {هذا خَلْقُ الله} [Luqmān: 11]. In the exegesis: the concealed in the heavens is the rain, and in the earth the plants. Al-khābiya (the jar) is from this, except that they kept to dropping the hamza in it, like al-bariyya and al-dhurriyya according to some. Ubayy and ʿĪsā read «الخَبَ», transferring the vowel of the hamza to the bāʾ and dropping the hamza, so it becomes like «رأيتُ الأَبَ». ʿAbd Allāh, ʿIkrima and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «الخبا» with a clear alif. Its justification: he turned the hamza into alif, so the bāʾ had to be vowelled; that is according to the dialect of those of the Arabs who, in pausing, replace the hamza with a letter homogeneous with its vowel, so he says «هذا الخَبُوْ», «رأيتُ الخَبا» and «مررت بالخَبِي», and then connected speech was treated as pausing.
In my view, when he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the quiescent letter before it, he did not drop it; rather he left it, so it became quiescent after a fatḥa and was turned according to the vowel of what precedes it; and this is an established dialect: they say «المَراة» and «الكَماة» with an alif in place of the hamza in this way.
Abū Ḥātim attacked this reading and said: "It is not allowed in Arabic, because if he drops the hamza he casts its vowel onto the bāʾ and says «الخَبَ»; and if he converts it he says «الخَبْيَ» with sukūn on the bāʾ and a yāʾ after it." Al-Mubarrad said: "Abū Ḥātim was below his peers in grammar and did not catch up with them, except that when he left their city he met no one more knowledgeable than he."
His saying: {فِي السماوات}: There are two views. The first: it is attached to «الخَبْءَ», i.e. "the hidden in the heavens". The second: it is attached to «يُخْرِجُ», with «في» having the meaning of «مِنْ», i.e. "He brings it out from the heavens". This is al-Farrāʾ's view.
His saying: {مَا تُخْفُونَ}: Al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read with tāʾ (second person) in both places, and the others with yāʾ (third person). The second person is evident in al-Kisāʾī's reading, because before it is the command to them to prostrate and the addressing of them with it. The third person in the reading of the others, besides Ḥafṣ, is also evident, because the third person pronouns precede, in His sayings «لهم», «أعمالهم», «صَدَّهم» and «فهمْ». As for Ḥafṣ's reading, its interpretation is that he moved on to addressing those present after completing the case of the people of Saba'. It may also be an iltifāt, on the basis that he put the absent in the place of the present and addressed him, turning to him.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The reading with the yāʾ of the third person gives that the verse is from the speech of the hoopoe, and with the tāʾ of address it gives that it is Allah's address to the community of Muḥammad ﷺ." It has already been covered that the apparent sense is that it is the speech of the hoopoe in every case. Likewise the disagreement over His saying {الله لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}: is it from the speech of the hoopoe, as a correction from it when it described the great throne of Bilqīs, or from the speech of Allah the Exalted, in reply to it in its describing her throne as great?

Onun sözü: {إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ}: Çoğunluk iki hemzeyi de kesre ile, isti'nâf (yeni cümle) olarak okumuştur; bu, kavminin sorusuna cevaptır. Sanki onlar «Mektup kimden? İçinde ne var?» demişler de o ikisine birden cevap vermiştir.

Abdullah [Mütercim notu: İbn Mes'ûd] «وإنَّه مِنْ سليمانَ» şeklinde, «إنه من سليمان»den önce atıf vâvı ilâvesiyle, {إني أُلْقِيَ إِلَيَّ} sözüne atfederek okumuştur. İkrime ve İbn Ebî Abele iki hemzeyi de fetha ile okumuştur. Bunu Zemahşerî ve başkaları açıkça belirtmiştir. Ebü'l-Bekâ ise «إنه من سليمان»de yalnızca kesreyi zikretmiş, ikincisi hakkında sanki susmuştur; çünkü o birincisine atıftır. Her ikisinde fethanın tahrîci hakkında birkaç vecih vardır: Birincisi, «كتاب»dan bedel-i iştimâl veya bedel-i kül mine'l-kül olmasıdır; sanki şöyle denmiştir: «Bana, onun Süleyman'dan olduğu ve şöyle şöyle olduğu bildirildi.» En sahih olan budur. İkincisi, «كريمٌ» ile merfû olmasıdır; bunu Ebü'l-Bekâ zikretmiştir ve güçlü değildir. Üçüncüsü, illet harfinin düşürülmesi üzerine olmasıdır. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: «Şunu da kastetmen câizdir: "Çünkü o Süleyman'dandır ve çünkü..."; sanki o, mektubun değerli oluşunu, Süleyman'dan olmasıyla ve başına Allah'ın isminin konmasıyla gerekçelendirmiştir.»

Mekkî şöyle demiştir: «Ferrâ, kelâmda ikisinde de fethayı câiz görmüştür»; sanki onun bunun bir kıraat olduğundan haberi olmamıştır.

Übeyy «أَنْ مِنْ سليمانَ، وأنْ بسمِ اللهِ» şeklinde, her ikisinde de nûnu sükûnlu okumuştur. Bunda iki vecih vardır; en zâhir olanı, bunun tefsîriyye «أنْ» olmasıdır, çünkü öncesinde «söz» mânâsında bir şey bulunmaktadır. İkincisi, bunun muhaffefe olması ve ismin mahzûf bulunmasıdır; bu ise Basralıların usûlüne uymaz, çünkü onun ismi ancak şe'n zamiri olabilir, şe'n zamiri de ancak iki rüknü açıkça belirtilmiş bir cümleyle tefsir edilir.

His saying: {أَنَاْ آتِيكَ}: it may be an imperfect verb, its pattern being «أفْعِلُ», like «أَضْرِبُ», the original being «أَأْتِيْك» with two hamzas, the second of which was changed into an alif. Or it may be an active participle, its pattern being «فاعِل», the alif being supernumerary and the hamza radical — the reverse of the first. Ḥamza read «آتِيْكَ» with imāla (inclination) in both places in this sura, with a disagreement transmitted from Khallād.

His saying: {طَرْفُكَ}: there are two aspects in it. The first: that it is the eyelid, by which the speed of the matter is expressed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the movement of your eyelids when you look, and it was put in the place of looking." The second: that it is in the sense of «المَطْروف», i.e. the thing you look at. The first is the apparent one, because «الطَّرْف» has been described as being "sent forth" in the saying [of the poet]:

3571 - وكنتَ متى أرسَلْتَ طرفَك رائداً ... لقلبِك يوماً أَتْعَبَتْكَ المناظِرُ
رأيتُ الذي لا كلُّه أنت قادِرٌ ... عليه ولا عَنْ بَعْضِه أنتَ صابرُ
(Whenever you send forth your glance one day as a scout for your heart, the sights weary you: you saw that which you are not able to bear in its entirety, nor are you patient to refrain from even part of it.)

His saying: {مُسْتَقِرّاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual. «عنده» is governed by it. It is not to be said: when an adverb (ẓarf) occurs as a ḥāl, what it is attached to must be omitted, so how is it mentioned here? — because «الاستقرار» here is not that unrestricted "being present"; rather, what is meant by it here is the fixed thing that does not / waver. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it the very governor of the adverb which ought to have been omitted, saying: "The governor of the adverb appears in His saying «مُسْتَقرًّا»; this is what is always implied with every adverb, and it comes here overt; there is nothing like it in the Book of Allah." What Abū al-Baqāʾ said is better. Besides, the unrestricted governor has appeared overtly in the saying [of the poet]:

3572 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فأنتَ لدى بُحْبُوْحَةِ الهَوْنِ كائنُ
(…for you are, in the midst of ease, existing.)

This was established thoroughly at the beginning of al-Fātiḥa, so be sure to turn to it.

His saying: {أَأَشْكُرُ}: it suspends «لِيَبْلُوَني», and «أم» is connected (muttaṣila); likewise His saying {نَنظُرْ أتهتدي أَمْ تَكُونُ مِنَ الذين لاَ يَهْتَدُونَ} [al-Naml: 41].

His saying: {وَمَن شَكَرَ} {وَمَن كَفَرَ}: «مَنْ» may be conditional, or a relative noun containing the sense of condition; for that reason the fāʾ entered the khabar (predicate). The apparent sense is that the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the second condition, or the khabar of the relative, is His saying {فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ}; and in that case there must be a pronoun referring to «مَنْ», its implied form being: "free of need of his thanks". It has also been said: the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then his disbelief is only against himself", because its counterpart — His saying {فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ} — indicates it.

His saying: {الصرح}: the disagreement has already been given about the adverbial noun occurring after «دخل»: is it accusative as a ẓarf (adverbial), this being anomalous with «دخل» specifically, as Sībawayh said; or is it a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), like «هَدَمْتُ البيتَ», as al-Akhfash said? «الصَّرْح» is a palace, or the courtyard of a house, or a pavement made of glass. Its origin is from «التصريح», which is uncovering. «كَذِبٌ صُراحٌ» means a lie that is evident and exposed; likewise «لُؤْمٌ صُراحٌ» (open baseness). «الصَّريح» (the explicit) is the counterpart of «الكناية» (the allusive), because it is evident while its opposite is concealed. It has also been said: «الصريح» is the pure, from their saying «لَبَنٌ صَريحٌ» (pure milk), "clear in its «صَراحة» and «صُرُوحة»".

Al-Rāghib said: "«الصَّرْح» is a lofty, ornamented building; it was so called in consideration of its being clear of / admixture, i.e. pure."

His saying: {سَاقَيْهَا}: the majority read it with a plain alif. Qunbul related it with a hamza from Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAlī judged it weak. Qunbul did the same in the plural of «ساق» in Ṣād and in al-Fatḥ, putting a hamza for its wāw; he read «بالسُّؤْقِ والأَعْناق» and «فاستوى على سُؤْقِه», with a hamza in place of the wāw. Another way is related from him: «السُّؤُوْق» and «سُؤُوْقة», with an added wāw after the hamza.

It is also related from him that he used to put a hamza in it in the singular, in His saying {يُكْشَفُ عَن سَأْقٍ} [al-Qalam: 42].

As for putting a hamza for the wāw, there are several aspects. The first: that an unvowelled wāw preceded by a ḍamma is turned into a hamza by some Arabs. This was established at the beginning of al-Baqara at «يُوْقنون», and I cited for it:

3574 - أَحَبُّ المُؤْقِدِين إليَّ موسى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The dearest of fire-kindlers to me is Mūsā…)

Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī used to put a hamza for every wāw in the Quran having this description. The second: that «ساق» is on the pattern «فَعَل», like «أَسَد», so it was given the plural «فُعُل», with ḍamma on the ʿayn, like «أُسُد»; and a wāw with ḍamma is changed into a hamza, as in «وُجوه» and «وُقِّتَتْ»; then after being made a hamza it was made unvowelled. The third: that the singular is heard with a hamza, as will be established, so its plural came on that pattern.

As for «سُؤُوْق», with a wāw after the hamza: «ساق» was given the plural «سُوُوق», with [two] wāws, and the first was given a hamza because of its ḍamma. This transmission is rare (gharīb) from Qunbul, and we have read with it, praise be to Allah.

As for «سَأْقَيْها», the justification of the hamza is one of several aspects: either the dialect of those who change the alif into a hamza — on which is the usage of al-ʿAjjāj in «العَأْلَم» and «الخَأْتَم»; he recited:

3575 - وخِنْدِفٌ هامَةُ هذا العَأْلَمِ ...
(And Khindif is the head of this world…)

— and this will also be established at «مِنْسَأَته» in Sabaʾ, if Allah the Exalted wills, and part of it was given in al-Fātiḥa; or by likening it to «رَأْس» and «كَأْس», just as they said «حَلأْت السَّويق», by analogy with «حَلأُتُه عن الماء», i.e. "I drove him away"; or by treating the singular and the dual like their plural, and the hamza has been established in their plural.

His saying: {مُّمَرَّدٌ}: i.e. made smooth. From it is «الأَمْرَد» (beardless youth), for the smoothness of his face from hair; «بَرِّيَّة مَرْدَاء» (a bare wilderness), for its being devoid of vegetation; and «رَمْلَةٌ مَرْداء», sand that grows nothing. «المارِد» among the devils is one who is stripped bare of good and divested of it. «مارِد» is a well-known fortress. Among the proverbs of al-Zabbāʾ: «تَمَرَّد مارِدٌ وعَزَّ الأَبْلَقُ» (Mārid rebelled and al-Ablaq proved impregnable); she said it about two fortresses whose conquest was denied her.

«القوارِيْر» is the plural of «قارُوْرة», which is transparent glass. «مِنْ قواريرَ» is a second ṣifa (adjective) of «صَرْحٌ».

His saying: {مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ}: attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is not attached to «أَسْلَمْتُ», because his submission preceded hers by a long time. This is a subtle aspect. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«مع» is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; as for when the ʿayn is unvowelled, there is no disagreement that it is a particle." I say: the discussion of that has already been given. Makkī said here something similar to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya said.

«تَطَيَّرْنا بك» şeklinde de okunmuştur; asıl budur, (diğerinde) idğam yapılmıştır. Bunun izahı daha önce geçmişti.

Onun sözü: {تُفْتَنُونَ}: Önceki zamire riayet edilerek muhatap sîgasıyla gelmiştir. Sonrasındakine riayet edilseydi gaip yâ'sıyla «يُفْتَنُون» denirdi; bu da câizdir, ancak racih değildir. «أنت رجلٌ تَفْعل» ve «يَفْعل» diye tâ ile ve yâ ile söylersin; «نحن قومٌ نقرأ» ve «يَقْرؤون» de denir.

Onun sözü: {قُلِ الحمد لِلَّهِ}: Çoğunluk, iki sâkinin karşılaşması sebebiyle «قُلِ»nin lâmını kesre ile okumuştur. Ebü's-Semmâl hafiflik için fetha ile okumuştur; {وَقُلِ الحمد للَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ} [Neml: 93] sözünde de böyledir. «سلامٌ» mübtedâdır; onunla başlamayı câiz kılan, bir dua olmasıdır.

Onun sözü: «أَمْ ما»: Bu «أم» muttasıl ve atıf edicidir, çünkü şartlarını tamamlamıştır. Takdir: «Hangisi daha hayırlıdır?» «خيرٌ», ya kâfirleri zorlamak ve hasmı ilzam etmek için bir tafdîldir, ya da tafdîl içermeyen bir sıfattır. «أَمْ ما»daki «ما», «الذي» mânâsındadır. Masdar olduğu da söylenmiştir; bu takdirde birincisinden bir muzâf hazfedilmiştir, yani: «Allah'ın tevhîdi mi daha hayırlıdır, yoksa onların şirki mi?»

Ebû Amr ve Âsım, öncesindeki sözüne hamlederek «أَمْ ما يُشْرِكون»u gaybet sîgasıyla okumuştur... [Mütercim notu: kaynak metin burada kesilmektedir.]

Onun sözü: {أَإِذَا}: İki istifhâm bir araya geldiğinde söz Ra'd sûresinde geçmiş ve tahkik edilmişti. «إذا»daki amil, «لَمُخْرَجُون»un delâlet ettiği mahzûf bir fiildir, takdiri: «Diriltilip çıkarılacağız». «مُخْرَجُون»un onda amel etmesi üç engel sebebiyle câiz değildir: istifhâm, «إنَّ» ve ibtidâ lâmı. «إنَّ»in haberinde ibtidâ lâmı konusunda ihtilaf vardır. Zemahşerî burada zekâ göstermiş ve tatlı bir ibare kullanarak şöyle demiştir: «Çünkü ism-i fâilin onda amel etmesinin önünde engeller (kaynakta: «عِقاباً») vardır: istifhâm hemzesi, "إنَّ" ve ibtidâ lâmı; bunlardan biri yeterliyken üçü bir araya gelince nasıl olur?» Ayrıca şöyle demiştir: «"Bu âyette "هذا"yı {نَحْنُ وَآبَآؤُنَا}den önce getirmiş, başka bir âyette {نَحْنُ وَآبَآؤُنَا}yı "هذا"dan önce getirmiştir!" dersen, derim ki: Öne alma, öne alınanın zikredilmekle kastedilen ve dayanılan olduğuna, sözün onun için sevk edildiğine delildir. İki âyetten birinde, kastedilenin dirilişin vukuu olduğuna, diğerinde ise bu bağlamda diriltilenin vukuuna delâlet eder.»

«آباؤُنا» [Mütercim notu: kaynak metinde «آباؤُها» yazılmıştır], «كان»in ismine atıftır. Cer ile yapılan ayırma, te'kîd ile yapılan ayırmanın yerini tutmuştur.

Onun sözü: {مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ}: «الحشر»e müteallik olması câizdir; o takdirde «مِنْ» başlangıç içindir. Ayrıca «فَوْجاً»dan hâl olmak üzere mahzûf bir şeye müteallik olması da câizdir; çünkü asılda onun sıfatı olması câizdir. «الفَوْج», «القوم» gibi cemaattir. Râgıb bunu kayıtlamış ve şöyle demiştir: «Geçip giden, acele eden cemaat.» Sanki asıl budur, sonra geçiş ve acele olmasa da mutlak olarak kullanılmıştır. Çoğulu «أفواجٌ» ve «فُؤُوج»dur. «مِمَّنْ يُكَذِّبُ» onun sıfatıdır. «مِن كلِّ» içindeki «مِنْ» tebʿîz (kısmî) içindir, «مِمَّن يُكَّذِّبُ» içindeki ise beyâniyyedir.

* İ'rab:
(الواو): isti'nâfiyye. (اللام): takdîr edilen bir kasem için kasem lâmı. (قد): tahkîk harfi. (علما): mansûb ikinci mef'ûlün bih. (الواو): atıf harfi. (لله): الحمد mübtedâsının mahzûf haberine müteallik. (الذي): mebnî ism-i mevsûl olup lafza-i celâlin sıfatı olarak cer mahallindedir. (على كثير): (فضّلنا)'ya müteallik. (من عباده): كثير'in sıfatına müteallik.
Takdîr edilen kasem cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayan isti'nâfiyye cümledir.

«فضّلنا ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; (الذي) mevsûlünün sılasıdır.
