And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ما يَمْلِكُونَ مِن قِطْمِيرٍ﴾: it is the thin wrapping of the date-stone. ”اَلنَّقِيرُ“ is the small pit on the back of the date-stone, and ”اَلْفَتِيلُ“ is the thread in the middle of the date-stone.
﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُونَ بِشِرْكِكُمْ﴾ [Fāṭir: 14]: the meaning is: "they will say: 'It was not us that you used to worship'", so they will disown your worship of them. ﴿وَلا يُنَبِّئُكَ مِثْلُ خَبِيرٍ﴾ [Fāṭir: 14]: that is Allah, because what Allah has informed of, of what will come to pass, He alone has knowledge of it; no one shares it with Him.

﴿وَإنْ تَدْعُ مُثْقَلَةٌ إلى حِمْلِها﴾: the meaning is: "if a soul heavily laden with sins calls to [have] its load — its sins — [carried], nothing of its sins will be carried". ﴿وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى﴾, that is: even if the one it calls upon were a near relative, such as the father, the son and whoever resembles these.
﴿إنَّما تُنْذِرُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهم بِالغَيْبِ وأقامُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾. The interpretation of “تُنْذِرُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهم” — and he is the Prophet ﷺ — is: "you warn all of creation", and the meaning here is that your warning benefits those who fear their Lord.

﴿وَما يَسْتَوِي الأعْمى والبَصِيرُ﴾ ﴿وَلا الظُّلُماتُ ولا النُّورُ﴾ [Fāṭir: 20] ﴿وَلا الظِّلُّ ولا الحَرُورُ﴾ [Fāṭir: 21]. This is a parable Allah has struck for the believers and the unbelievers. The meaning is: "the one blind to the truth — the unbeliever — is not equal to the one who sees the truth — the believer, who sees his right guidance — nor are darkness and light"; darkness is the errors and light is guidance. ”وَلا الظِّلُّ ولا الحَرُورُ“: the meaning is: "the people of truth, who are in a shade of the truth, are not equal to the people of falsehood, who are in scorching heat", that is, in constant heat, night and day. “اَلْحَرُورُ” is the blazing of heat and its scorching by day and by night, whereas the samūm (the hot wind) is only by day.
﴿وَما يَسْتَوِي الأحْياءُ ولا الأمْواتُ﴾: the living are the believers and the dead are the unbelievers; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿أمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أحْياءٍ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 21].

﴿وَمِنَ الجِبالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وحُمْرٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ ألْوانُها﴾. ”جُدَدٌ“ is the plural of ”جُدَّةٌ“, which is a stripe and a track. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎كَأنَّ سَراتَهُ وجُدَّةَ مَتْنِهِ ∗∗∗ كَنائِنُ يَجْرِي فَوْقَهُنَّ دَلِيصُ
(As though his back and the stripe along his spine were quivers over which a gleaming sheen flows.)
”جُدَّةَ مَتْنِهِ“ is the black stripe you see on the back of the wild ass; and every track is a jādda and a judda. ﴿وَغَرابِيبُ سُودٌ﴾, that is: and among the mountains are gharābīb, namely the ḥirār (lava fields): mountains with black rocks. ”اَلْغِرْبِيبُ“ is that which is intensely black.

﴿وَمِنَ النّاسِ والدَّوابِّ والأنْعامِ مُخْتَلِفٌ ألْوانُهُ كَذَلِكَ﴾. The meaning is: "among what We created is that whose colours vary; and among people, beasts and livestock likewise", that is, like the variation of fruits and mountains. ﴿إنَّما يَخْشى اللَّهَ مِن عِبادِهِ العُلَماءُ﴾, that is: whoever has knowledge of Allah, his fear of Him becomes intense. It has come in the exegesis: "Fear of Allah suffices as knowledge, and being deluded about Allah suffices as ignorance."
﴿يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ﴾, that is: it will never go bad and never be unprofitable.
﴿لِيُوَفِّيَهم أُجُورَهم ويَزِيدَهم مِن فَضْلِهِ إنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾: Forgiving of their sins, Appreciative of their good deeds.

And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ثُمَّ أوْرَثْنا الكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِن عِبادِنا﴾, up to His saying: ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها﴾ [Fāṭir: 33]. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may Allah have mercy on him — said, attributing it to the Prophet: «”سابِقُنا سابِقٌ، ومُقْتَصِدُنا ناجٍ، وظالِمُنا مَغْفُورٌ لَهُ“». The verse indicates that the believers are forgiven — for their moderate one and the one of them who wrongs himself «[Translator's note: the source prints «لِمُقْتَصِدِهِمُ الظّالِمِ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنهُمْ», which looks corrupt; «لِمُقْتَصِدِهِمْ والظّالِمِ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنهُمْ» is probably meant and is translated so.]» — after the soundness of belief. It has come in the exegesis that His saying ﴿فَمِنهم ظالِمٌ﴾ is the unbeliever; that is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; and it has been related from al-Ḥasan that it is the hypocrite. But the wording indicates what ʿUmar said from the Prophet ﷺ, and what most of the exegetes hold, because His saying ﴿ثُمَّ أوْرَثْنا الكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِن عِبادِنا فَمِنهم ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ indicates that these are all among the chosen ones. And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has said: ﴿قُلِ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وسَلامٌ عَلى عِبادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفى﴾ [al-Naml: 59].

﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ ولُؤْلُؤًا ولِباسُهم فِيها حَرِيرٌ﴾. There are two ways in it. One of them: ”يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ ومِن لُؤْلُؤٍ“; and ”وَلُؤْلُؤًا“ is permissible, in the sense of ”يُحَلَّوْنَ أساوِرَ“, because the meaning of ”مِن أساوِرَ“ is like the meaning of ”أساوِرَ“. The exegesis according to the genitive (khafḍ) is more common, in the sense: ”يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ ولُؤْلُؤٍ“; and it has come in the exegesis that this gold has the purity of pearls, just as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿قَوارِيرا﴾ [al-Insān: 15] ﴿قَوارِيرا مِن فِضَّةٍ﴾ [al-Insān: 16], that is: they are glass vessels, but their whiteness is like the whiteness of silver, and silver is their origin. It is also possible that it is ”يُحَلَّوْنَ مِن أساوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ“ and ”يُحَلَّوْنَ مِن لُؤْلُؤٍ“; and it is permissible in the sense of ”وَيُحَلَّوْنَ لُؤْلُؤًا“. ”أساوِرُ“ is the plural of ”إسْوِرَةٌ“, and ”أساوِرُ“ — its singular is siwār. ”اَلْأُسْوارُ“, from the asāwira of the Persians, is the one who is skilled at shooting arrows. The poet said:
؎وَوَتَّرَ الأساوِرُ القِياسا ∗∗∗ سَعْدِيَّةٌ تَنْتَزِعُ الأنْفاسا
(And the Persian archers strung the bows — Saʿdī bows that snatch away the breaths.)

﴿وَقالُوا الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أذْهَبَ عَنّا الحَزَنَ﴾. ”اَلْحُزْنُ“ is also permissible, like ”اَلرُّشْدُ“ and ”اَلرَّشَدُ“, and ”اَلْعُرْبُ“ and ”اَلْعَرَبُ“. The meaning of ”أذْهَبَ عَنّا الحَزَنَ“ is: He has removed from us everything that grieves — grief over livelihood, or grief over punishment, or grief over death; and Allah has removed every grief from the people of Paradise. [Translator's note: the printed word مَقاسٍ is rendered here as "livelihood" on the assumption that مَعاشٍ is intended; it may be a misprint.]

﴿الَّذِي أحَلَّنا دارَ المُقامَةِ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾: [المُقامَة is] like al-iqāma (staying); you say: ”أقَمْتُ بِالمَكانِ، إقامَةً، ومَقامَةً، ومُقامًا“ ("I stayed in the place"). That is: He has settled us in the abode of eternity out of His bounty, that is: that is by His favour, not by our deeds. ﴿لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ﴾, that is: fatigue. ﴿وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ﴾: ”اَللُّغُوبُ“ is exhaustion from fatigue. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: ”لَغُوبٌ“, with fatḥa on the lām, and the ḍamma is more common. The meaning of ”لَغُوبٌ“ is: something from which one becomes weary, that is: we do not burden ourselves with anything from which we become exhausted.

﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهم نارُ جَهَنَّمَ لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا﴾. ”فَيَمُوتُوا“ is accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn; it is the answer to the negation. The meaning is: "death will not be decreed for them so that they die". ﴿وَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهم مِن عَذابِها﴾, that is: the punishment of the Fire of Hell. ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي كُلَّ كَفُورٍ﴾, and [also read] ”يُجْزى كُلُّ كَفُورٍ“. There is a third way in it: ”كَذَلِكَ يَجْزِي كُلَّ كَفُورٍ“, that is: "thus does Allah recompense…". The meaning is: "like that recompense which We have mentioned". I do not know anyone who read it so — I mean ”يَجْزِي“ with the yāʾ and with its fatḥa.

﴿وَهم يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها﴾: they call for help: "Our Lord, bring us out!" The meaning is: "they say: Our Lord, bring us out, we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do"; the meaning is: "if You bring us out, we will do righteous deeds". So Allah rebuked them and said: ﴿أوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكم ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ﴾. Its meaning is: "Did We not give you the life-span in which whoever would remember could remember?!" It has come in the exegesis: "Allah has left no excuse to a servant whose life reaches sixty years", and it is said: "from sixty to seventy". It has also come in the exegesis that one of seventeen years is included in it, and it has been said: "forty". ﴿وَجاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ﴾: meaning the Prophet ﷺ; and it has been said: grey hair. The first view, that the Prophet ﷺ is the warner, is what most exegesis holds. And it has been said: "forty".

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ عالِمُ غَيْبِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾. The common reading is with the genitive (khafḍ). It is permissible [to say]: ”عالِمٌ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ“, in the sense of ”يَعْلَمُ“ ("He knows"); and ”عالِمٌ غَيْبَ“ in the sense of ”قَدْ عَلِمَ ذَلِكَ“ ("He has known that").

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكم خَلائِفَ في الأرْضِ﴾. ”خَلائِفَ“ is the plural of ”خَلِيفَةً“. The meaning is: "He made you a community that succeeded those before it, and saw and witnessed, in those who went before, what ought to be taken as a lesson". ﴿فَمَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ﴾: the meaning is: "upon him is the recompense of his disbelief". ﴿وَلا يَزِيدُ الكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إلا مَقْتًا﴾: "maqt is the most intense loathing".

﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ شُرَكاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "Say: Tell me about your partners."
﴿ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾: the meaning is: "On what ground have you assigned to them partnership with Allah? Is it for something they created of the earth?" ﴿أمْ لَهم شِرْكٌ في السَّماواتِ أمْ آتَيْناهم كِتابًا﴾, that is: or have We given them a Book supporting the partnership they claim? ﴿فَهم عَلى بَيِّنَتٍ مِنهُ﴾, and it is also read: ”بَيِّناتٍ“. ﴿بَلْ إنْ يَعِدُ الظّالِمُونَ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا إلا غُرُورًا﴾. ”اَلْغُرُورُ“ is the falsehoods that delude. The meaning of ”إنْ يَعِدُ“ is ”ما يَعِدُ“ ("they do not promise"), and ”بَعْضُهم“ is a badal (substitute) for ”اَلظّالِمِينَ“.

﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ أنْ تَزُولا﴾. The meaning of ”يُمْسِكُ“ is: He prevents the heavens and the earth from ceasing. When the Christians said: "The Messiah is the son of Allah", and the Jews said: "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah", the heavens were about to burst apart because of it, the mountains were about to cease, and the earth was about to split. Allah said: ﴿وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ ولَدًا﴾ [Maryam: 88] ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إدًّا﴾ [Maryam: 89] — the three verses — so Allah held them. He said ”اَلسَّماواتِ والأرْضَ“ [with the earth in the singular] because "the earth" indicates the earths. ﴿وَلَئِنْ زالَتا إنْ أمْسَكَهُما مِن أحَدٍ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾: this admits — and Allah knows best — two ways of answer. One of them: "their ceasing at the Resurrection"; Allah said: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 11]. And it may be said that [it says] ”زالَتا“ while they do not cease. As for His saying in this place: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيمًا غَفُورًا﴾, some people asked and said: why is there mention of forbearance and forgiveness in this place, when this is a place indicating power? The answer to this is that when He held the heavens and the earth at their saying "The Most Merciful has taken a son", [that was] forbearance: He did not hasten the punishment for them, and He held the heavens and the earth lest they cease because of the enormity of their fabrication.

﴿وَأقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أيْمانِهِمْ﴾: meaning the polytheists. They had sworn and done their utmost: ﴿لَئِنْ جاءَهم نَذِيرٌ لَيَكُونُنَّ أهْدى مِن إحْدى الأُمَمِ﴾, that is: than the Jews, the Christians and others. ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهم نَذِيرٌ﴾ — and he is Muḥammad ﷺ — ﴿ما زادَهم إلا نُفُورًا﴾: only in that they fled from the truth.

﴿اسْتِكْبارًا في الأرْضِ﴾. ”اِسْتِكْبارًا“ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "it increased them only in fleeing out of arrogance".
﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾, that is: the plotting of polytheism. ﴿وَلا يَحِيقُ﴾: [it does not] encompass. Ḥamza read: ”وَلا يَحِيقُ المَكْرُ السَّيِّئْ“, with a pause [i.e. a sukūn on the hamza]. According to the skilled grammarians this is a solecism (laḥn) and is not permissible; the like of it is permissible only in poetry, under metrical necessity. The poet said:
؎إذا اعْوَجَجْنَ قُلْتُ صاحِبْ قَوِّمِ
(When they [the camels] veer off course, I say: "Companion, set them straight!")
The original is ”يا صاحِبُ قَوِّمِ“, but he elided [the vowel] out of necessity; there was a ḍamma after a kasra, and a kasra after a kasra is felt to be heavy. They also recited:
؎فاليَوْمَ أشْرَبْ غَيْرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ ∗∗∗ إثْمًا مِنَ اللَّهِ ولا واغِلِ
(So today I drink, not burdening myself with a sin before Allah, nor as an uninvited intruder.)
These two verses have been recited by all the grammarians mentioned, and they all held that this is metrical necessity in poetry and that the like of it is not permissible in the Book of Allah. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] — may Allah have mercy on him — recited them to us as:
؎إذا اعْوَجَجْنَ قُلْتُ صاحٍ قَوِّمِ
(When they veer off course, I say: "Friend, set them straight!")
and this is excellent and perfect; and he recited to us:
؎فاليَوْمَ فاشْرَبْ غَيْرَ مُسْتَحْقِبٍ
(So today, drink, not burdening yourself…)
As for what is related from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ in his reading ”إلى بارِئْكم“, it is only that he slurs the kasra (ikhtilās), and does not give ”بارِئِكم“ a sukūn. This — I mean the sukūn of بارِئِكم — was only related from Abū ʿAmr by someone who does not master grammar as Sībawayh and al-Khalīl master it; Sībawayh related it with a slurred kasra, as though he reduced his voice at the kasra.
﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا سُنَّتَ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: its meaning is: "Do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away before them?!", and the meaning is: "Do they await anything but that there should descend upon them the like of the punishment that descended upon those before them?!"
﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾: the meaning is: "that anything of the affair of the heavens or of the affair of the earth could escape Him".

﴿وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النّاسَ بِما كَسَبُوا ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها مِن دابَّةٍ﴾. They said: He said ”عَلى ظَهْرِها“ ("upon its back") because the meaning makes it known that it is upon the back of the earth. The truth of this is that mention of the earth has already occurred, in His saying in the verse before this one, which immediately precedes it: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِن شَيْءٍ في السَّماواتِ ولا في الأرْضِ﴾ [Fāṭir: 44]; that is why ”عَلى ظَهْرِها“ came.
And His saying: ﴿ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها مِن دابَّةٍ﴾ — there are two views on it. It has been said: "any creature among humans and jinn and every being that reasons"; and it has come from Ibn Masʿūd: "The dung-beetle almost perishes in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam" — and this indicates generality. What has come [in the view] that humans and jinn are meant by it seems more likely — and Allah knows best.
End of the Sūra of "al-Malāʾika" (the Angels).

Bu da Allah Teâlâ'nın şu kavlidir: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ لاَ يُقْضَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُواْ﴾.
Muhammed b. Yezîd (Müberred) dedi ki: Adamlar dört türlüdür: cömert, cimri, müsrif ve orta yollu.
Cömert: Âhiret payını da dünya payını da tamamen âhiretine yöneltendir.
Cimri: Bunların hiçbirine hakkını vermeyendir.
Müsrif: İkisini de dünya için toplayandır.
Orta yollu (muktesıd): Her birine payını ulaştırandır; yani ameli ölçülüdür, (ibadette) aşırı gayret eden değildir.
[Mütercim notu: Metinde «ليس يمجتهد» yazılmıştır; «ليس بمجتهد» olmalıdır.]
Ebû İshak (Zeccâc) dedi ki: ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الحَزَنَ﴾ kavlinin anlamı: geçim kaygısını, azap korkusunu ve ölümü beklemeyi (giderdi) demektir.
Onun söylediklerinin hepsi tefsirde gelmiştir; bu (ifade) her türlü hüznü kapsayan geneldir.
«المُقامة» ile «المَقام» (ikamet yeri) aynıdır. «النَّصَب»: yorgunluktur.
«اللُّغُوب»: bitkinliktir; lâmın fethasıyla «اللَّغُوب» ise kendisinden dolayı bitkin düşülen şeydir.
Hasan ﴿لا يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُونَ﴾ şeklinde okudu.
Onun kıraatine göre anlam şudur: Onlara ölüm hükmedilmez ve ölmezler.

* İ'rab:
(الواو) isti'nâfiyyedir. (لهم) نار mübtedâsının mukaddem haberine müteallik. (لا) nefy harfidir. (عليهم) meçhul (يقضى) fiilinin nâib-i fâilidir. (الفاء) sebebiyye fâsıdır. (يموتوا) fâdan sonra gizli أن ile mansûb muzâridir. (لا) birincisi gibidir. (عنهم) meçhul يخفّف fiilinin nâib-i fâilidir [Dipnot: Nâib-i fâilin (من عذابها) olması ve (عنهم)'un (يخفّف)'e müteallik olması caizdir.]. (من عذابها) (يخفّف)'e müteallik..
Müevvel masdar (أن يموتوا ...), önceki nefiyden alınan bir masdara ma'tûf olarak ref' mahallindedir; yani: ليس ثمّة قضاء عليهم فموت آخر (onlar hakkında bir hüküm, dolayısıyla başka bir ölüm yoktur).
(كذلك) mef'ûl-i mutlak olan mahzûfa müteallik; âmili نجزي'dir..
«الذين كفروا....» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«كفروا ...» cümlesi (الذين) mevsûlünün sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«لهم نار ...» cümlesi (الذين) mübtedâsının haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«لا يقضى عليهم..» cümlesi ikinci haber olarak ref' mahallindedir [Dipnot: Veya (لهم)'daki zamirden hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir; âmili istikrârdır (الاستقرار).].
«يموتوا ...» cümlesi gizli harfî mevsûl (أن)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«لا يخفّف عنهم ...» cümlesi لا يقضى.. cümlesine ma'tûf olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«نجزي ...» cümlesi i'tirâziyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur..
(37) (الواو) atıf harfidir. (فيها) (يصطرخون)'a müteallik. (ربّنا) muzâf münâdâ olup mansûbdur; nidâ harfi hazfedilmiştir. (نعمل) talebin cevabı olarak meczûm muzâridir. (صالحا) masdarın yerine geçen (nâib) mef'ûl-i mutlaktır, zira onun sıfatıdır [Dipnot: Veya mansûb mef'ûlün bihtir.]. (غير) (صالحا)'nın sıfatıdır [Dipnot: Veya mef'ûl-i mutlak ya da mef'ûlün bih olan mahzûfun ikinci sıfatıdır.]. (الهمزة) inkârî istifhâm içindir. (الواو) atıf harfidir. (ما) «vakit» manasında nekre-i mevsûfedir; (نعمّركم)'a müteallik. (فيه) يتذكّر fiiline müteallik. (من) mevsûl olup يتذكّر'ın fâilidir. (الواو) atıf harfidir -veya hâliyyedir-. (الفاء) takdîrî bir şartın cevabına râbıtadır; ikincisi ta'lîliyyedir. (ما) nefy harfidir. (للظالمين) mukaddem habere müteallik. (نصير) lafzen mecrûr, mahallen merfû olup muahhar mübtedâdır.
«هم يصطرخون ...» cümlesi لا يخفّف عنهم cümlesine ma'tûf olarak ref' mahallindedir.
«يصطرخون ...» cümlesi (هم) mübtedâsının haberi olarak ref' mahallindedir.
Nidâ cümlesi «ربّنا..» takdîrî bir kavlin mekûlü'l-kavli olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«أخرجنا ...» cümlesi nidânın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«نعمل ...» cümlesi fâ ile birlikte gelmemiş, takdîrî bir şartın cevabı olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«كنّا نعمل ...» cümlesi (الذي) mevsûlünün sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«نعمل ...» cümlesi كنّا'nın haberi olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«نعمّركم..» cümlesi takdîrî mekûlü'l-kavle ma'tûf olarak nasb mahallindedir; yani onlara şöyle denir: ألم نمهلكم ونعمّركم ... (Size mühlet vermedik ve sizi yaşatmadık mı...)
«يتذكّر ...» cümlesi (ما)'nın sıfatı olarak nasb mahallindedir.
«تذكّر ...» cümlesi (من) mevsûlünün sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
«جاءكم النذير..» cümlesi نعمّركم cümlesine ma'tûf olarak nasb mahallindedir [Dipnot: Veya «قد» takdiriyle hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir.].
«ذوقوا ...» cümlesi takdîrî bir şartın cevabı olarak cezm mahallindedir; yani: إن كفرتم بالنذير فذوقوا (Uyarıcıyı inkâr ettiyseniz tadın).
«ما للظالمين من نصير..» cümlesi ta'lîliyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* Sarf:
(يصطرخون): Bunda iftiâl tâsının tâ'ya (ط) ibdâli vardır. Aslı يصترخون'dur; tâ (ت) sâddan sonra gelmiş ve kıyâsî bir şekilde tâ'ya (ط) kalbedilmiştir. Vezni يفتعلون'dur.

* Fevâid:
- غير:
غير: mana bakımından izâfete bağlı (mülâzım) bir isimdir; mana anlaşılır ve kendisinden önce ليس kelimesi gelirse lafız olarak izâfetten kesilmesi caizdir. (لا غير) sözü ise lahn ve hatadır. (قبضت عشرة ليس غيرها) (On tane aldım, başkası değil) denir; غير, haberin hazfi üzere merfû okunur, yani «مقبوضا»; ismin gizlenmesi üzere mansûb da okunur, yani (ليس المقبوض غيرها). (ليس غير) tenvinsiz fetha ile de -yine ismin gizlenmesi ve muzâfun ileyhin lafzen hazfedilip sübûtunun niyet edilmesi üzere- ve (ليس غير) tenvinsiz damme ile de söylenir.
«غير», müphemliğinin şiddeti sebebiyle izâfetle marife olmaz. Lafzen muzâf olan «غير» iki şekilde kullanılır:
Birincisi -ki asıl budur-: Nekrenin sıfatı olmasıdır; Allah Teâlâ'nın üzerinde durduğumuz âyetteki رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ kavlinde olduğu gibi; veya nekreye yakın bir marifenin sıfatı olmasıdır; Allah Teâlâ'nın صِراطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ. غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ kavlinde olduğu gibi. Çünkü cinsî marife nekreye yakındır ve غير iki zıt arasında yer aldığında müphemliği zayıflar.
İkincisi: İstisnâ olmasıdır; bu durumda (إلا)'dan sonra gelen ismin i'rabıyla i'rab edilir. Bundan başka bir yerde bunu ayrıntılı olarak ele aldık; oraya müracaat edilsin.

* Lügat:
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ): Onları örneksiz olarak yaratan. الفطر'ın aslı mutlak olarak yarmaktır; uzunlamasına yarmaktır da denmiştir; el-Muhtâr'da olduğu gibi babı نصر'dır. Mücâhid'den, o da İbn Abbâs'tan şöyle rivayet edilmiştir: «فاطر السموات والأرض'ın ne olduğunu bilmiyordum; nihayet iki bedevî bir kuyu hakkında bana davalaştılar; biri: أنا فطرتها, yani "onu ben başlattım ve ilk ben açtım" dedi.» Bazıları bu kökün farklı anlamlarını bir araya toplayarak şöyle demiştir:
الابتداء والابتداع فطر ... والصّدع والغمز وأما الفطر
فترك صوم بعض كمء فطر ... وما بدا من عنب في الشجر
(Başlamak, örneksiz yaratmak, yarmak ve sıkmak "فَطْر"dır; "فِطْر" ise orucu bırakmak, bir tür mantar ve ağaçta üzümden ilk görünen şeydir.)
(تُؤْفَكُونَ): Çevriliyorsunuz. Fethalı الأفك'den gelir ki o çevirmek demektir; «ما أفكك عن كذا», yani "seni ondan ne çevirdi?" denir. Kesralı الإفك'ten olduğu da söylenmiştir ki o yalan demektir. el-Muhtâr'da: «Fethalı الأفك, أفكه'nin masdarıdır; yani onu altüst etti ve bir şeyden çevirdi; babı ضرب'dır. Allah Teâlâ'nın «قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا» sözü de bundandır.»

* İ'rab:
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (الحمد) mübtedâdır; (لله) onun haberidir. (فاطر السموات) onun (Lafzatullah'ın) sıfatıdır; (الأرض) (السموات)'a atıftır. (الحمد)'deki "el" cins ve istiğrak ifade eder; yani hamd cinsi. (فاطر السموات)'taki izâfet mahzdır (gerçek izâfettir), çünkü (ism-i fâil) geçmiş zaman içindir.
(جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) (جاعل الملائكة) ikinci sıfattır; buradaki izâfet de mahzdır. Bazıları onu gayr-i mahz saymıştır, çünkü hâlin hikâyesidir; bu yüzden ism-i fâilin amel etmesi caiz olmuştur, zira o geçmiş zaman anlamında olduğunda amel etmez. Bu yüzden bazıları (رسلا)'yı gizli bir fiille mansûb kılmıştır. Kisâî ise onun her hâlükârda amel etmesini caiz görmüştür. (رسلا) (جاعل)'in ikinci mef'ûlüdür; (جاعل) "yaratan" anlamında olursa (رسلا) hâl-i mukaddere olur. (أولي أجنحة) (رسلا)'nın sıfatıdır (na't). (مثنى), (ثلاث) ve (رباع) (أجنحة)'nin sıfatlarıdır; vasıf olmaları ve tekrarlı olandan —yani "ikişer ikişer, üçer üçer, dörder dörder"den— udûl edilmiş olmaları sebebiyle gayr-i munsarif olmuşlardır. Bu sıfatlar hakkındaki söz Nisâ sûresinde geçmişti. Kâzerûnî ise hâşiyesinde onları (أجنحة)'den bedel olarak i'rab etmiştir.
(يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَلْقِ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) Öncesini pekiştiren isti'nâfî bir sözdür. (في الخلق) câr ve mecrûr olup (يزيد)'e mütealliktir; (ما) mef'ûlün bihtir; (يشاء) cümlesi sıladır. (إن) ve ismidir; (على كل شيء) câr ve mecrûr olup (قدير)'e mütealliktir; (قدير) (إن)'nin haberidir. Cümle ta'lîliyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.
(ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ رَحْمَةٍ فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها) (ما) cezmeden şart ismi olup (يفتح)'in öne alınmış mef'ûlün bihi olarak nasb mahallindedir. (يفتح) fiilü'ş-şarttır; (الله) fâildir; (للناس) câr ve mecrûr olup (يفتح)'e mütealliktir; (من رحمة) hâldir. Fâ, şartın cevabını bağlayan fâdır; (لا) cinsini nefyeden lâdır; (ممسك) onun ismi, (لها) haberidir; cümle şartın cevabı olarak cezm mahallindedir.
(وَما يُمْسِكْ فَلا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) Vav atıf harfidir; (ما) cezmeden şart ismi olup yine (يمسك)'in öne alınmış mef'ûlü olarak nasb mahallindedir. (يمسك) fiilü'ş-şarttır; fâ râbıtadır; (لا) cinsini nefyeden lâdır; (مرسل) onun ismi, (له) haberidir. Birincisinde, yani «فلا ممسك لها» sözünde, müennes kılma (ما)'nın manasına hamledilmiştir, çünkü kastedilen rahmettir; ikincisinde ise lafzına hamledilmiştir. (من بعده) hâldir; yani "onu tutmasından sonra". (هو) mübtedâ, (العزيز) birinci haber, (الحكيم) ikinci haberdir.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ) (يا) nidâ harfidir; (أي) nekre-i maksûde münâdâ olup damme üzere mebnîdir, nasb mahallindedir; hâ tenbîh içindir; (الناس) bedeldir. (اذكروا نعمة الله) emir fiil, fâil, mef'ûlün bih ve muzâfun ileyhtir. (عليكم) câr ve mecrûr olup (نعمة)'ye mütealliktir, çünkü o "nimet vermek" (in'âm) anlamındadır; eğer "verilen nimet" anlamında olursa câr ve mecrûr hâl olmak üzere mahzûf bir şeye müteallik olur.
(هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (هل) istifhâm harfidir; (من) zâid cer harfidir; (خالق) mübtedâ olup lafzen mecrûr, mahallen merfûdur. (غير الله), mahalle göre veya lafza göre (خالق)'in sıfatıdır, ya da istisnâ üzere mansûbdur; hepsiyle okunmuştur. (خالق)'in haberi mahzûftur, yani «لكم». (يرزقكم) cümlesinin hâl olarak nasb mahallinde, ya da mahalle göre (خالق)'in sıfatı olarak ref', ya da lafza göre (خالق)'in sıfatı olarak cer mahallinde olması caizdir; (خالق)'in haberi olması da caizdir. (من السماء) câr ve mecrûr olup (يرزقكم)'a mütealliktir; (الأرض) atıftır. Bu âyetin i'rabının devamı ve onun hakkında söylenenler Fevâid bahsinde gelecektir. İstifhâmın manası takrîr ve azarlamadır (tevbîh).
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ) İstifhâmdan anlaşılan nefyi pekiştirmek için sevk edilmiş isti'nâfî bir cümledir. «لا إله إلا الله»nin i'rabı daha önce ayrıntılı olarak geçmişti. (فأنى): fâ isti'nâfiyyedir; (أنى) istifhâm ismi olup hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir. (تؤفكون) meçhul muzâri fiildir; vav nâib-i fâildir.

* Fevâid:
1- «نزيد في الخلق ما نشاء»nın manası: [Mütercim notu: Başlık kaynakta «نزيد … نشاء» şeklindedir; âyetteki lafız «يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء»dır.]
Bu âyetler pek çok faydayı içermektedir. Bunların ilki, yaratılıştaki ziyadenin manasıdır. Bu hususta söylenenlerin en iyisinin, Zemahşerî'nin el-Keşşâf'ında zikrettiği olduğunu görüyoruz. O, âlimlerin bu hususta söylediklerini aktardıktan sonra şöyle demiştir: «Âyet mutlaktır; yaratılıştaki her ziyadeyi kapsar: Boy uzunluğu, suretin düzgünlüğü, organların tamlığı, yakalayıp tutmada kuvvet, akılda sağlamlık, görüşte isabet ve kuvvet, kalpte cesaret, nefiste cömertlik, dilde akıcılık, konuşmada incelik, işlerle uğraşırken güzel teenni ve vasfın kuşatamayacağı buna benzer şeyler.» Bu söz, kısalığı ve belâgatıyla birlikte câmi' ve mâni'dir; Allah'ın yaratıklarında gördüğün farklılık için de hoşnut edici bir açıklama içermektedir.
"Açmak" (fetih) fiilini, salıvermek ve göndermek için istiâre etmiştir; sanki nimet çeşitleri ve lütuf türleri —rızık, yağmur, sağlık, yurtlarda emniyet ve sayısı sayılamayan diğerleri gibi— kilitlerini Allah'tan başkasının açamadığı, sürgülenmiş kapılardır.
Rahmetin nekre getirilmesinde, —daha önce geçtiği gibi— nimet türlerinin onun katları içine girmesi için yaygınlığa ve mübhemliğe delalet eden bir yön vardır.
2- (هل من خالق)'ın i'rabı:
Bazıları (يرزقكم) cümlesinin (خالق)'in haberi olmasını men etmiştir; çünkü en sahih görüşe göre (هل), fiil ile haber verilen bir mübtedânın üzerine girmez.
3- «من»nin zâid olduğu yerler:
Başka bir yerde, cer harfi «من»nin, kendisinden önce nefy, nehiy veya istifhâm geldiğinde nekreden önce zâid olarak geldiğini söylemiştik. Burada şunu ekliyoruz: Bu, dokuz yerde kıyasîdir (muttarid):
1- Mübtedâda.
2- Fâilde.
3- Kâne'nin isminde.
4- Tek mef'ûle geçişli fiilin mef'ûlünde.
5- ظننت'in iki mef'ûlünden birincisinde.
6- علمت'in mef'ûllerinden birincisinde.
7- أعطيت'in iki mef'ûlünden birincisinde.
8- أعطيت'in iki mef'ûlünden ikincisinde.
9- Fâili zikredilmeyen fiilin (meçhulün) mef'ûlünde (nâib-i fâilde).

* Vocabulary:
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ): their Creator without a precedent. The root meaning of al-faṭr is splitting in general; it is also said to be splitting lengthwise, and its verb pattern is naṣara, as in al-Mukhtār. From Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "I did not know what fāṭir al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: 'I faṭartuhā', meaning I began it and originated it." Some have gathered the meanings of this root, despite their differences, saying:
الابتداء والابتداع فطر ... والصّدع والغمز وأما الفطر
فترك صوم بعض كمء فطر ... وما بدا من عنب في الشجر
(Beginning and originating are faṭr, as are cleaving and pressing; as for al-fiṭr, it is giving up the fast, like a mushroom, and what appears of grapes on the tree.)
(تُؤْفَكُونَ): you are turned away, from al-afk with fatḥa, which is turning away. One says:
"What turned you away (ma afakaka) from such and such?", i.e. what turned you away from it. It is also said to be from al-ifk with kasra, which is lying. In al-Mukhtār: "al-Afk with fatḥa is the maṣdar of afakahu, meaning he overturned him and turned him away from something, and its verb pattern is ḍaraba; from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا»."

* I'rab:
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ, (لله) is its khabar, and (فاطر السموات) is a naʿt of it. (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات). The (أل) in (الحمد) is generic and all-inclusive, i.e. the whole genus of praise. The annexation in (فاطر السموات) is a true annexation (muḥḍa) because it refers to the past. (جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) (جاعل الملائكة) is a second naʿt, and the annexation here too is a true one. Some regarded it as not true, because it narrates a state; hence it is sound for the active participle to govern, since it does not govern when it has the sense of the past. For this reason some made (رسلا) accusative by an implied verb. Al-Kisāʾī permitted its governing in every case. (رسلا) is the second object of (جاعل). If (جاعل) means "creator", then (رسلا) is an implied ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). (أولي أجنحة) is a naʿt of (رسلا). (مثنى وثلاث ورباع) are adjectives of (أجنحة), and they are diptotes because of being adjectives and because of deviation from repetition, i.e. two by two, three by three, four by four. The discussion of these adjectives was given earlier in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. Al-Kāzarūnī in his marginal commentary parsed them as a badal of (أجنحة). (يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَلْقِ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) A resumptive statement confirming what precedes. (في الخلق) is attached to (يزيد). (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi and the clause (يشاء) is a ṣila. (إن) with its ism; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); (قدير) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause is causal, with no grammatical position.
(ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ رَحْمَةٍ فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها) (ما) is a jussive conditional noun, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of (يفتح). (يفتح) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ and (الله) is the agent. (وللناس) is attached to (يفتح). (ومن رحمة) is a ḥāl. The fāʾ is the linking particle of the apodosis. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ممسك) is its ism and (لها) its khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive, the apodosis. (وَما يُمْسِكْ فَلا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is a jussive conditional noun, likewise in the position of accusative as a fronted object of (يمسك). (يمسك) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ. The fāʾ is the linking particle. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (مرسل) its ism and (له) its khabar. In His first statement (فلا ممسك لها) the feminine is carried according to the meaning of (ما), because what is meant is mercy; in the second it is carried according to the word. (ومن بعده) is a ḥāl, i.e. after His withholding. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) is the first khabar and (الحكيم) the second.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ) (يا) is a vocative particle. (أي) is the one addressed, an indefinite noun made definite by being intended, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. The hāʾ is for alerting, and (الناس) is a badal. (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb with its agent, a mafʿūl bihi and a muḍāf ilayhi. (عليكم) is attached to (نعمة) because it has the sense of "bestowing of favour" (al-inʿām); if it has the sense of "the thing bestowed", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl.
(هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (هل) is an interrogative particle. (من) is a redundant preposition. (خالق) is a mubtadaʾ, genitive in form and nominative in position. (غير الله) is a naʿt of (خالق) either according to the position or according to the form, or is accusative as an exception; all of these were read. The khabar of (خالق) is omitted, i.e. "for you". It is permissible for the clause (يرزقكم) to be accusative as a ḥāl, or nominative as a naʿt of (خالق) by position, or genitive as a naʿt of (خالق) by form, and it may also be a khabar of (خالق). (ومن السماء) is attached to (يرزقكم), and (الأرض) is conjoined. More on the i'rab of this verse and what was said about it will come in the section on benefits. The meaning of the question is affirmation and rebuke.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ) A resumptive clause given to establish the negation derived from the question. The i'rab of «لا إله إلا الله» has been given in detail before. (فأنى): the fāʾ is resumptive, and (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (تؤفكون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent.

* Benefits:
1- The meaning of «نزيد في الخلق ما نشاء»:
These verses contain many benefits. The first is the meaning of the addition in creation, and we see that the best of what has been said on it is what al-Zamakhsharī gave in his Kashshāf. After citing what the scholars said, he said: "The verse is unrestricted, and covers every addition in creation: height of stature, symmetry of form, completeness of the limbs, strength in seizing, soundness of intellect, excellence of judgment, boldness of heart, generosity of soul, fluency of tongue, eloquence in speech, good deliberation in handling affairs, and the like, which description cannot encompass." This statement, for all its brevity and eloquence, is comprehensive and exclusive, and contains a satisfying explanation of the differences you see among Allah's creatures.
And He used "opening" metaphorically for releasing and sending, as though they were locked doors that none but Allah opens, of all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, such as provision, rain, health, security in one's homeland, and other things beyond counting.
The indefiniteness of "mercy" indicates diffusion and vagueness, so that all kinds of blessings are included within it, as stated before.
2- The i'rab of «هل من خالق»:
Some prevented the clause (يرزقكم) from being a khabar of (خالق), because, according to the sounder view, (هل) does not enter upon a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is a verb.
3- Places where «من» is redundant:
We said elsewhere that the prepositional «من» is added before an indefinite noun when preceded by negation, prohibition or a question, and we add here that this is regular in nine positions:
1- At the beginning of a sentence.
2- In the agent.
3- In the ism of kāna.
4- In the object of a verb that takes one object.
5- In the first of the two objects of ظننت.
6- In the first of the objects of علمت.
7- In the first of the two objects of أعطيت.
8- In the second of the two objects of أعطيت.
9- In the object of a verb whose agent is not named (the passive).

* İ'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَناً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ) İki zümrenin âkıbetleri arasındaki, daha önce geçen farkı, o iki âkıbete götüren hâllerinin farklılığını açıklayarak pekiştirmek için sevk edilmiş isti'nâfî bir sözdür.
Hemze inkârî istifhâm içindir; fâ mahzûf bir şeye atfeder; benzerleri daha önce geçmişti. (من) ism-i mevsûl olup mübtedâ olarak ref' mahallindedir; haberi, sözün siyakının delalet ettiği mahzûf bir şeydir; takdir: «كمن هداه الله» (Allah'ın hidayet ettiği kimse gibi midir?). Bedreddin İbn Mâlik onu şart ismi olarak i'rab etmiştir; şartın cevabı mahzûf olup takdiri: «ذهبت نفسك عليهم حسرة» (Onlara hasret yüzünden canın gider). (زين) cümlesi (من)'in sılasıdır; (له) câr ve mecrûr olup (زين)'e mütealliktir; (سوء عمله) nâib-i fâildir. (فرآه): fâ atıf harfidir; (رآه) (زين)'e atıftır; hâ (رأى)'nın birinci mef'ûlü, (حسنا) ise (رأى)'nın ikinci mef'ûlüdür, çünkü (bu fiil) kalbîdir. Fâ, mevsûldeki şart manası sebebiyle râbıtadır. (إن) ve ismidir; (يضل) cümlesi onun haberidir; (من يشاء) (يضل)'in mef'ûlüdür; (ويهدي من يشاء) cümlesi (يضل من يشاء) cümlesine atıftır.
(فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَصْنَعُونَ) Fâ fasîha fâsıdır; (لا) nehiy lâsıdır; (تذهب) (لا) ile meczûm muzâri fiildir; (نفسك) fâildir. (عليهم) câr ve mecrûr olup (تذهب)'e mütealliktir; tıpkı «هلك عليه حبا» (ona olan sevgiden helak oldu) ve «مات عليه حزنا» (ona üzüntüden öldü) demen gibi. Onun (حسرات)'a müteallik olması caiz değildir, çünkü masdarın sılası ondan önce gelmez. (حسرات) mef'ûlün lieclihtir; mana: «Canını hasretler yüzünden helak etme» demektir. Müberred onun temyîz olduğunu söylemiştir. Zemahşerî de şöyle demiştir: «Hâl olması da caizdir; sanki hasretlenmenin aşırılığından (nefsin) tamamı hasretlere dönüşmüş gibidir; Cerîr'in dediği gibi:
مشق الهواجر لحمهن مع السرى ... حتى ذهبن كلا كلا وصدورا
(Öğle sıcakları, gece yürüyüşleriyle birlikte onların etlerini eritti; ta ki göğüsler ve sinelerden ibaret kalıp gittiler.)»
[Mütercim notu: Zemahşerî'den yapılan alıntının kapanış tırnağı kaynakta bulunmamaktadır.] (Şair) zayıflıkla dişi develeri vasfetmektedir. «فرس ممشوق», yani uzun ve zayıf at denir; «جارية ممشوقة القوام» (ince uzun boylu kız) da denir. الهاجرة sıcağın şiddetidir. Dammeyle السرى gece yürüyüşüdür. الكلكل ve الكلكال göğüstür. Yani şiddetli sıcaktan, üzerlerinde et olmayan sadece kemikler gibi oldular. Sinelerin (الصدور) göğüslere (الكلاكل) atfı açıklama (tefsir) içindir. Bu bahsin devamı Belâgat bahsinde gelecektir.
(إن), ismi ve haberidir; (بما يصنعون) câr ve mecrûr olup (عليم)'e mütealliktir.

* Belâgat:
«فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات» sözünde îgâl sanatı vardır. Bu, ihtiyat için önceki bir sözün tamamlayıcısı mesabesinde sayılan bir sözü getirmektir. Allah Teâlâ, ondan yüz çevirip ona muhalefet edenlerin, yüz çevirmeleriyle her sınırı aştıklarına ve aptallıkta ifrata gittiklerine, sapıklığa iyice daldıklarına dair Rasûl'ün hayatı üzerine birden fazla kez yemin etmiştir; tıpkı birden fazla yerde buyurduğu gibi: «لعمرك إنهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون». Yine: «ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر» ve «فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا» buyurmuştur.
Nefsin hasret ve üzüntüyle gitmesi, şairlerin çokça göz diktiği seçkin bir ifadedir. Eski bir şair şöyle demiştir:
فعلى إثرهم تساقط نفسي ... حسرات وذكرهم لي سقام
(Onların ardından canım hasretler halinde dökülüyor; onları anmak bana hastalıktır.)
Sevdiklerinin gidişinden sonra hüzün ona isabet edip nefsine yerleşince ve kanına hâkim olunca, canının birbirini izleyen hasretler halinde saçılıp bedeninden döküldüğünü hayal etmiştir. Nefsi hasretlerle karıştığı için hasretler kılmıştır; sanki o, onların ta kendisidir. Ya da (mana): Onlardan sonra hasretler ve hüzünler yüzünden (canı) dökülür. «وذكرهم», yani onları hatırlamak bana hastalıktır; (سقام) fethayla السقم gibi masdardır.
İbnü'r-Rûmî de bu nadide lafzı iktibas ederek, çocuklarının ortancası olan oğlu Muhammed'in mersiyesinde şöyle demiştir:
وظل على الأيدي تساقط نفسه ... ويذوي كما يذوي القضيب من الزند
(Kollar üzerinde canı dökülüp durdu; dal nasıl kuruyup solarsa öyle soldu.)
Hasta ancak küçük olduğunda kollar üzerinde taşınır. Oğlu Muhammed, dört ile beş yaş arasında iken kan kaybından ölmüştür.
Derim ki: Tarih şunu rivayet etmiştir: Bu âyet, Ebû Cehil b. Hişâm hakkında inmiştir; kötü ameli kendisine süslenip de onu doğru ya da güzel görünce sapıklık içinde şaşkınca dolaştı; «أطلق آمر النهي» [Mütercim notu: ibare kaynakta anlaşılmaz olup yazıldığı gibi "nehyi emredeni serbest bıraktı" diye çevrilmiştir] ve hevaya itaati benimsedi; öyle ki güzeli çirkin, çirkini güzel gördü; sanki (kalbinin) üzerini pas kaplamış, aklını, idrakini ve temyizini elinden almıştı. Ebû Nüvâs bu anlamın semasına göz dikerek şöyle demiştir:
اسقني حتى تراني ... حسنا عندي القبيح
(Bana içki sun ki beni, çirkin bana güzel görünür halde göresin.)
Şarap sakisine: "Bana içki sun ki sarhoş olayım da çirkin bana güzel görünsün" demektedir. (حسنا), (تراني)'nin ikinci mef'ûlüdür; (القبيح) ise sıfat-ı müşebbehe olduğu için (حسنا)'nın fâilidir.

* Vocabulary:
(بَلَدٍ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-balad is masculine or feminine", and al-balda is al-balad. Both al-balad and al-balda are applied to every place on the earth, whether inhabited or empty. In the Revelation: «إلى بلد ميت», that is, to a land with no vegetation or pasture, which is then brought forth by the rain and grazed by their livestock; so death was applied to the absence of vegetation and pasture, and life to their presence."
(الْكَلِمُ): a generic noun (ism jins), because it denotes the essence as such; it is not a plural, contrary to the author of al-Qāmūs and other grammarians, because its pronoun may be masculine whereas a plural tends to take the feminine; nor is it a collective noun (ism jamʿ), because it has a singular from its own wording, whereas the usual case with a collective noun is otherwise. Its singular is kalima, and kalima has three dialectal forms: kalima with fatḥa on the kāf and kasra on the lām, kilma with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the lām, and kalma with fatḥa on the kāf and sukūn on the lām.
(يَبُورُ): perishes and is ruined. One says bāra yabūru būran wa-bawāran: it perished. Al-sūq or al-silʿa bārat means it stagnated; bāra al-ʿamal means the work became void; bārat al-arḍ means the land was not sown; bawwara al-arḍ means he left it or made it barren; abārahu means he destroyed him; tabawwara nafsahu means he mourned for himself and wailed from destruction. Al-bāʾir is land that has lain fallow, and the plural is būr. One says ḥāʾir bāʾir, meaning one who obeys no guide and heads nowhere. Al-būr is also the corrupt, ruined one in whom there is no good; one says imraʾa būr and qawm būr. Al-būr of land is what has not been sown; al-bawār is destruction and ruin; and dār al-bawār is Hell.

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحاباً) (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) is its khabar. The clause (أرسل الرياح) is the ṣila of the relative noun, and (الرياح) is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is a conjunction. (تثير) is an imperfect verb; the secret of conjoining an imperfect to a past verb, and how it comes differing from what precedes and follows it, will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (سحابا) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَسُقْناهُ إِلى بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها كَذلِكَ النُّشُورُ) (فسقناه) is also a conjunction, in the manner of iltifāt (shift of person). (سقناه) is a verb with its agent and object. (وإلى بلد) is attached to (سقناه), and (ميت) is a naʿt. (فأحيينا به الأرض) is also a conjunction, and the adverbial phrase is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (كذلك) is a fronted khabar and (النشور) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the secret of this simile will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً) (من) is a jussive conditional noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (كان) is a defective past verb whose ism is a latent pronoun referring back to (ما) [Translator's note: the source prints "ما"; (من) is evidently meant], and the clause (يريد) is its khabar. (العزة) is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is the linking particle of the apodosis. (لله) is a fronted khabar and (العزة) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of jussive, the apodosis. It was sound for this clause to stand in place of the apodosis because it indicates it, since a thing is sought only from its possessor and owner. A parallel is your saying "whoever wants good advice, it is with the righteous", meaning "let him seek it with them", except that you put what indicates it in its place. The meaning of «فلله العزة جميعا» is that all might belongs exclusively to Allah. Others said: "(من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being 'let him give Him' (فليعطه); and His words «فلله العزة» are the reason for the omitted apodosis." Al-Bayḍāwī gave the omitted apodosis as "let him obey Him" (فليطعه). (لله) is a fronted khabar, (العزة) a postponed mubtadaʾ and (جميعا) a ḥāl. The conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar of (من).
(إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ) The clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (إليه) is attached to (يصعد). (يصعد الكلم) is an imperfect verb and its agent, and (الطيب) is a naʿt of (الكلم). (والعمل) is a mubtadaʾ; its being nominative by conjunction is also permissible. (الصالح) is a naʿt, and the clause (يرفعه) is the khabar of (العمل). The agent of (يرفعه) is a latent pronoun referring back to (العمل), i.e. the good deed raises the good word. It is also said that the agent is the pronoun of Allah, in which case the hāʾ refers back to (العمل). From Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ: "A word without deed is like tharīd without fat, a cloud without rain, and a bow without a string." (وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَكْرُ أُولئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ) A resumptive statement given to explain the state of the evil word and the bad deed, after explaining the state of the good word and the righteous deed and their people. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يمكرون) is the ṣila of (الذين). (السيئات) is a naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq, the implied form being "the evil plottings" (al-makarāt al-sayyiʾāt); it is not permissible to make it accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, because (مكر) is an intransitive verb. Al-makarāt, with fatḥas, is the plural of makra, with sukūn on the kāf, which is a single instance of makr, meaning scheme and deception. Some said it is permissible to give (يمكرون السيئات) the meaning of (يكسبون السيئات) ("they earn evil deeds"), in which case it may be accusative as a mafʿūl bihi. (مكر) is a mubtadaʾ and (أولئك) is a muḍāf ilayhi. The demonstrative was placed where the pronoun would be, to signal that they are distinguished by evil and corruption from all other wrongdoers, i.e. they and no others. (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), with no grammatical position, and the clause (يبور) is the khabar of (مكر). It is also possible that (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبور) its khabar, the nominal clause being the khabar of (مكر). There is disagreement about the occurrence of the separating pronoun before a khabar: some prevented it and others allowed it, and we incline to permissibility.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift):
In His words «والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلخ» there are two shifts. The first is in reporting the past with an imperfect: He said «فتثير» in the imperfect, while what precedes and follows it is past, to narrate a past state and to bring that fine picture before the mind, indicating the perfection of power and wisdom. This is done with every action that has a kind of distinction or specificity, such as a state that is strange or that concerns the addressee, and the like, as Taʾabbaṭa Sharrā said:
فمن ينكر وجود الغول إني ... أخبر عن يقين بل عيان
(Whoever denies the existence of the ghoul, I report from certainty, indeed from eyewitness,)
بأني قد لقيت الغول تهوي ... بسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان
(That I met the ghoul rushing down on a plain like a sheet, level and wide,)
فأضربها بلا دهش فخرت ... صريعا لليدين وللجران
(And I struck her without dismay and she fell, prostrate on her hands and her neck.)
Al-ghūl is the female of the devils; al-ʿiyān is seeing with the eye; al-hawī is descending, and what is meant is speed of running; al-sahb, with fatḥa, is open space level and distant at its edges; al-ṣaḥīfa is the book; al-ṣaḥṣaḥān, with fatḥa, is level ground; and al-jirān, like kitāb, is the front of the neck bone from the throat to the upper chest, with plurals jurun and ajrina. He says: whoever denies the existence of the ghoul has lied, for I report from certainty; or the meaning: O you who deny the existence of the ghoul, I report a report arising from certainty, which is what rests on decisive proof, let alone eyewitness with the eye.
In this style is what came in the report of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām at the battle of Badr. He said: "I met ʿUbayda ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a horse, in full armour so that nothing was seen of him but his eyes, and he was saying: 'I am Abū Dhāt al-Kuʾūs.' I had a short spear in my hand and I thrust (fa-aṭʿunu) with it into his eye, and he fell, and I trod (waʾaṭaʾu) with my foot on his cheek until the spear came out bent." His words «فأطعن بها في عينه وأطأ برجلي» are turned from the past wording to the imperfect, to portray to the listener the scene in which he did what he did of daring and boldness in killing that armoured horseman. Do you not see that he first said "I met ʿUbayda" in the past, and then said "and I thrust with it into his eye"? Had he conjoined his speech to its beginning, he would have said "so I thrust (faṭaʿantu) with it into his eye".
The second shift is in His words: «فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا إلخ». Had it followed the pattern of the discourse, He would have said "so he drove ... and he revived", but He turned from the third-person wording to the first-person wording, which is more fitting for specification and indicates it more strongly. He expressed with two pasts after the imperfect to indicate certainty of occurrence.
2- Simile:
In His words «كذلك النشور» there is a simile mursal (with the particle stated), because the particle is present; that is, as the reviving of dead land, so is the resurrection of the dead, in the soundness of its being within power or in the manner of the reviving.
3- Figurative attribution (majāz isnādī):
In His words «إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه» there is figurative usage in the predicate and in the attribution. Ascent is figurative for knowledge, because ascent is a quality of bodies, and the word is known; so the verb was attributed to the object.

* Vocabulary:
(فُراتٌ): extremely sweet. In al-Qāmūs: "farata al-māʾ, like karuma, furūtatan: it was sweet."
(أُجاجٌ): extremely salty. In al-Qāmūs: "ajja al-māʾ ujūjan, with ḍamma, ya'ujju like yasmaʿu, yaḍribu and yanṣuru, when its saltiness is intense." You say hajīr ujāj of the sun, in which there is majāj, which is the saliva of the sun; and māʾ ujāj burns with its saltiness.
(قِطْمِيرٍ): al-qiṭmīr is the wrapping of the date stone, which is the thin skin wound around it; it is also said to be the speck on its back. It is known that the date stone has four things which are used as proverbs for smallness: al-fatīl, which is what is in the cleft of the stone; al-qiṭmīr, which is the wrapping; al-naqīr, which is what is on its back; and al-thufrūq, which is between the cap and the stone. Al-Jawharī said: "It is said to be the white speck on the back of the stone from which the palm grows."

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمْ أَزْواجاً) A resumptive statement given to bring another confirmation or another proof of the soundness of resurrection and revival. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (خلقكم) is its khabar. (ومن تراب) is attached to (خلقكم). (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay. (ومن نطفة) is conjoined to (من تراب). (ثم جعلكم أزواجا) is conjoined to (خلقكم من تراب), and (أزواجا) is the second object of (جعل), i.e. kinds, males and females.
(وَما تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنْثى وَلا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (تحمل) is an imperfect verb, nominative. (من) is a redundant preposition and (أنثى) is genitive through (من) in form and nominative in position as the agent. (ولا تضع) is conjoined to (وما تحمل). (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (بعلمه) [Translator's note: the source misprints "وبعمله"] is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. known to Him. «[Translator's note: the printed text has a stray "ز" before the next sentence.]» (وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (يعمر) is a passive imperfect verb. (من) is a redundant preposition and (معمر) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (ولا ينقص) is conjoined to (وما يعمر). (من —) is attached to (ينقص) [Translator's note: the source breaks off here, "ومن - متعلقان"; (من عمره) is evidently meant]. (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (في كتاب) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning of this indulgent expression will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (إن ذلك على الله يسير) (إن) with its ism; (على الله) is attached to (يسير); (يسير) is the khabar of (إن). In al-Miṣbāḥ: "yasura al-shayʾ, like qaruba, means it was little, so it is yasīr al-amr; yaysiru yusran, of the pattern taʿiba, and yasura yusran, of the pattern qaruba, so it is yasīr, that is, easy; Allah made it easy (yassarahu) and it became easy (tayassara), and istaysara has the same meaning."
(وما يستوى البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج) A resumptive statement given to coin a parable for the believer and the disbeliever. (ما) is negative. (يستوي) is an imperfect verb, nominative. (البحران) is the agent, nominative, its sign of nominative being the alif, being a dual. (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (عذب) is a khabar and (فرات) is a second khabar or a naʿt. (سائغ شرابه): (سائغ) may be a third naʿt, with (شرابه) as agent of (سائغ) because it is an assimilated adjective, i.e. its drink goes down easily. It is also possible that (سائغ) is a fronted khabar and (شرابه) a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second naʿt. The clause (هذا عذب إلخ) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (البحران). (وهذا ملح أجاج) is conjoined to (عذب فرات). More elaboration on this parable will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(ومن كل تأكلون لحماً طرياً وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها) The wāw is either a conjunction, the clause then serving as a completion of the parable, or resumptive, the clause then being a resumptive digression (istiṭrād). The detail of each of the two meanings will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (ومن كل) is attached to (تأكلون), and (منهما) is a naʿt of the omitted noun after (كل), i.e. each one of them. (تأكلون) is an imperfect verb with its agent, and (لحما) is a mafʿūl bihi; (طريا) is a naʿt. (وتستخرجون) is conjoined to (تأكلون), and (حلية) is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause (تلبسونها) is a naʿt of (حلية). «[Translator's note: the printed text here reads "لحماًََ مفعول به ولحماً مفعول به" with a repeated phrase and "تلبسوننا نعت لحية"; these are evident misprints for (لحما) and (حلية)/(تلبسونها) and are rendered according to their evident sense.]»
(وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون) The wāw is a conjunction. (ترى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, implied "you", and (الفلك) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فيه) is attached to (مواخر), a ḥāl, since the seeing is visual. The lām in (لتبتغوا) is causal, and (تبتغوا) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مواخر). (ومن فضله) is attached to (تبتغوا). (لعل) with its ism, and the clause (تشكرون) is its khabar.
(يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل) [Translator's note: the source prints the verse corrupted as "يولج الليل في النهار في اليل"] You may take it as resumptive, and you may take it as in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (خلقكم), i.e. Allah the Exalted. (الليل) is a mafʿūl bihi of (يولج), and (في النهار) is attached to (يولج). (ويولج النهار في الليل) is conjoined to the clause before it. (وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى) The wāw is a conjunction; the secret of the difference between the two conjoined elements will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (سخر) is a verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring back to Allah, and (الشمس) is a mafʿūl bihi. (والقمر) is conjoined to (الشمس). (كل) is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. each one of them, and the clause (يجري) is the khabar. (لأجل) is attached to (يجري), and (مسمى) is a naʿt of (أجل). (ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك) (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, and three khabars are given for it: (الله), (ربكم), and the clause (له الملك). (له) is a fronted khabar and (الملك) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قمطير) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ, the clause (تدعون) is a ṣila, and (من دونه) is a ḥāl. (ما) is negative, (يملكون) is an imperfect verb with its agent, and the clause (ما يملكون) is the khabar of (الذين). (من) is a redundant preposition and (قطمير) [Translator's note: the source misprints "قمطير"] is genitive in form, accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi.
(إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم) A resumptive statement given to confirm the preceding content. (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (تدعوهم) is a verb, and the wāw is the agent. «[Translator's note: the source calls (تدعوهم) a past verb ("فعل ماض"); it is in fact an imperfect verb, jussive.]» (ما) is negative. (استجابوا) is a verb with its agent, and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition. (ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم) The adverbial is attached to (يكفرون), and (بشرككم) is attached to (يكفرون). The kāf is annexed to the maṣdar, as a maṣdar annexed to its agent, i.e. they will disown you and your worship of them. (ولا ينبئك مثل خبير) The better view is that the address is general, i.e. O listener, whoever you may be. (لا) is negative, (ينبئك) is an imperfect verb with the kāf as its object, and (مثل خبير) is its agent, i.e. one who knows the inner reality of things.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indulgent speech (al-kalām al-mutasāmiḥ):
In His words «وما يعمر من معمر إلخ» there is the art of indulgent speech, in which the speaker trusts the understanding and taste of his listeners, because it will not be confused for them and the grasping of its implications and the comprehension of its aims will not elude them. The apparent wording suggests that the two conjoined elements alternate upon every person and that lengthening of life and its opposite succeed each other upon him, which is impossible in itself; but it is among the self-evident matters grasped at first glance. The common speech of people is on this model; they say: "He does not reward a servant or punish him except justly", and "I did not enjoy a land or dislike it except that my stay in it was short." [Translator's note: the source prints the corrupt "ثورايي"; al-Zamakhsharī's wording "ثوائي" (my stay) is meant] Al-Zamakhsharī says there is also another interpretation, namely that no human's life is lengthened or shortened except in a Book, and its form is that it is written on the Tablet: "If so-and-so performs the pilgrimage, his life is forty years; if he performs the pilgrimage and fights, his life is sixty years." If both are combined and he reaches sixty, he has been granted a long life; if only one is done and he does not pass forty, then some of his life, whose limit is sixty, has been reduced.
2- Parable (al-tamthīl):
In His words «وما يستوي البحران إلخ» — some call it the extended metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya) — it is a construction used in other than its original place because of a relation of similarity, in which neither the thing likened nor the particle of likening is mentioned. An example that clarifies it is their saying: "You are striking cold iron." He likened the state of one who persists in obtaining something that cannot be achieved to the state of one who strikes cold iron, on the basis that each is work behind which no result is hoped. There is no mention of the thing likened nor of the particle of likening in this construction, so it is an extended metaphor, because it is a construction used for other than what it was set for, and the similarity between the figurative and the literal meanings is evident. This type is frequent in current proverbs, prose and verse, such as their saying: "If you were a wind, you have met a hurricane", said to one who lords it over you, or to a strong person who falls upon one stronger and fiercer than he; yet the addressee was not a wind and did not meet a hurricane.
ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī has a delightful passage on tamthīl, which we summarise as follows. He said: "Can it be doubted that it works the work of magic, so that what lies between East and West is shortened?" And he said: "It shows you, for the meanings represented in the imagination, likenesses in matching persons; it makes the mute speak for you and gives you eloquence from the inarticulate; it shows you life in the inanimate and shows you the reconciliation of opposites, and makes the distant thing near."
In Asrār al-Balāgha ʿAbd al-Qāhir cited a splendid poetic example. He said: "Consider likewise the verse of Abū Tammām:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
(When Allah wills to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He gives it the tongue of an envier.)
taken apart from the verse that follows it, although the verse is clear in meaning; then follow it with the next verse, which is:
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(Were it not for the fire's blazing in what it neighbours, the sweet fragrance of aloes-wood would not be known.)
And see whether the meaning displayed the full beauty of its dress and revealed the hidden part of its loveliness and adornment, and deserved all its precedence, except through the last verse and the tamthīl and imagery in it."
Not every simile, however, turns into a metaphor, as the preceding discussion might suggest; this is allowed only when the likeness between the two things is one whose grasp is near and easy of reach, and there is in the situation an indication of it, so that the addressee, when the name is applied to him freely, can know what you meant. If there is no way to know the intended likeness except after mentioning the sentences by which the parable is tied, metaphor does not enter it, because when the likeness is obscure it is not permitted to take the name by force and transfer it to what is its proper bearer without a witness accompanying you that points to the likeness. ʿAbd al-Qāhir illustrated this with a verse by al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī. He said: "If you tried to turn the poet's words:
فإنك كالليل الذي هو مدركي ... وإن خلت أن المنتأى عنك واسع
(For you are like the night that will overtake me, even if I thought the place of refuge from you was wide)
into a metaphor, and treat the night as you treat the lion in your saying 'I saw a lion', you would find no way for it in speech, because you would be left with one of two things: either you omit the qualification and confine yourself to mentioning the night alone, saying 'if I flee, the night shades me', which is absurd [Translator's note: the source prints "محاول"; "محال" is meant], since there is nothing in the night to indicate the point the poet intended, that he will not escape him however far he flees, because of the breadth of his dominion and the length of his reach; or, if you do not omit the qualification, you find that the way of metaphor in it leads to strain; for were you to say 'if I flee from you I find a night that overtakes me, though I thought the place of refuge [source: "المتنادي", i.e. "المنتأى"] was wide and the flight far', you would say what natures do not accept, because custom has not applied it to the one praised in this way."
Let us return to the verse we are discussing. Allah gave the believer and the disbeliever the parable of the two seas, and then favoured the salty sea over the disbeliever in that it shares with the sweet in benefits, from fish, pearls, and the running of ships with what benefits people, whereas the disbeliever is devoid of benefit. This is in the manner of His words the Exalted: «ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة» and then He said: «وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله». It is also said that the believer and the disbeliever, though they share some qualities such as courage and generosity, are not equal in the greatest distinguishing feature, because one of them remains on his original nature.
«[Translator's note: the source quotes 2:74 as «ثم قسمت قلوبكم…», «لما يتفجر من الأنهار» and «وان لما يهبط»; these are misprints for the text of the Qur'an and are given here in the standard form.]»
3- Digression (al-istiṭrād):
Since digression has been mentioned, we say that it was referred to earlier in this book and here we add to its exposition. It is that a poet or writer builds much speech upon speech of another kind, interrupts it while it is his real aim, apart from all that preceded, and returns to his first speech. Most of what comes is by way of simile. In the verse there is a digression to the mention of the two seas, the salty and the sweet, and the bounty and gift attached to them: from each of them you eat fresh meat, which is fish, and extract ornaments to wear: the ring is placed on the finger, the bracelet on the wrist, the necklace on the neck and the anklet on the leg. And you see the ships in each of them mawākhir, that is, cleaving the water as they run through it. One says makharat al-safīna al-māʾ, and clouds are called banāt makhr because they cleave (tamkhuru) the air; and al-safn, from which safīna is derived, is close to al-makhr, because it scrapes the water as though peeling it, as it cleaves it.

* Vocabulary:
(حملها): al-ḥiml with kasra is what is carried; the plural is aḥmāl and ḥumūla. Al-ḥiml is also the singular of al-ḥumūl, which are the howdahs or the camels carrying the howdahs. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-ḥiml with kasra is what is carried on the back and the like; the plural is aḥmāl and ḥumūl. I carried (ḥamaltu) the goods, ḥamlan, of the pattern ḍaraba, so I am ḥāmil; and the feminine is ḥāmila with tāʾ because it is a shared adjective." And in al-Mukhtār: "Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-ḥaml with fatḥa is what is in the belly or on the top of a tree, and al-ḥiml with kasra is what is on a back or a head. Al-Azharī said: this is the correct view and it is the saying of al-Aṣmaʿī. He said: a woman is ḥāmil or ḥāmila when she is pregnant. Whoever says ḥāmil says: this is an adjective that applies only to females; and whoever says ḥāmila builds it on 'she carried (ḥamalat), so she is ḥāmila'. Ibn Durayd mentioned that for the fruit-load of a tree there are two forms, with fatḥa and with kasra." Some scholar has composed a rule for this wondrous root, saying:
؎ ما كان في بطن فذاك حَمْلُ ∗∗∗ وإن على ظهر ورأس حِمْلُ
(What is in a belly is ḥaml; and what is on a back or a head is ḥiml.)
؎ والكفلاء والديات حُمْلُ ∗∗∗ جمع حِمال وحميل فادر
(And guarantors and blood-money payments are ḥuml, plural of ḥimāl and ḥamīl; so know it.)
؎ كثير حَمْل اسمه الحَمّال ∗∗∗ وحامل الديات والحِمّال
(One who carries much is called al-ḥammāl, as is one who bears blood-money payments, and al-ḥimmāl.)
؎ مصدر حمّلتك والحُمّال ∗∗∗ جمع لحامل لأي وِقر
(The verbal noun of "I burdened you (ḥammaltuka)"; and al-ḥummāl is a plural of ḥāmil for any load.)

* I'rab:
(يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء الى الله): (يا أيها الناس): its parsing has been given many times. (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الفقراء) is the khabar (predicate). (الى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (الفقراء), because it is the plural of faqīr, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
(والله هو الغني الحميد): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (الغني الحميد) is the khabar of inna (as the text has it) for the mubtadaʾ or for (هو); and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الله).
(إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأتي بخلق جديد): (إن) is conditional; (يشأ) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (يذهبكم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and its consequence; (ويأت) is conjoined to (يذهبكم); (بخلق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يأت); (جديد) is an adjective (naʿt).
(وما ذلك على الله بعزيز): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; (ذلك) is the subject (ism) of mā; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عزيز); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition; (عزيز) is genitive in form and accusative in position, being the khabar of mā.
(ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى): (لا) is negative; (تزر) is an imperfect verb; (وازرة) is the fāʿil (agent), or it is an adjective of an omitted agent, the implied form being "a bearing soul (nafs wāzira)"; (وزر) is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi); (أخرى) is a muḍāf ilayhi. The meaning of this speech will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وإن تدع مثقلة الى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى): (إن) is conditional; (تدع) is the protasis; (مثقلة) is an adjective of an omitted agent, i.e. "a burdened soul"; (الى حملها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تدع); the direct object is omitted because it is known; (لا) is negative; (يحمل) is passive and is the apodosis; (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (شيء); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb and its subject (ism) is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "the one called upon (al-madʿū)"; (ذا قربى) is its khabar, meaning "possessor of kinship (qarāba)".
(إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقامو الصلاة): (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (تنذر) is an imperfect verb and its agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "you (anta)"; (الذين) is the direct object; the clause (يخشون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ربهم) is a direct object; (بالغيب) is a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. they fear their Lord while absent from His punishment, or they fear His punishment while it is absent from them; (وأقاموا الصلاة) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object.
(ومن تزكى يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير): the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and it is permissible that it be resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; (تزكى) is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis; the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (يتزكى) is an imperfect verb and its agent is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he"; (لنفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتزكى), as a qualification of it; (إلى الله) is a fronted khabar and (المصير) is a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1 - In His saying «أنتم الفقراء الى الله» there is the definite article on (الفقراء). The secret in it is exaggeration of their poverty: as if, because of the intensity of their neediness, they are the ones branded with "the poor", and the neediness of others, compared with their poverty, is not counted as neediness; or as if they have reached the utmost of need and the furthest limit of want, the very genus of the poor. This is among the marvels of the science of bayān.
2 - In His saying «ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى» there is paronomasia of derivation (jinās al-ishtiqāq) among (تزر), (وازرة) and (وزر). Al-wizr, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, is sin, and al-wizr is also a weight; hence it is said wazara yazir, of the pattern waʿada, when one carried a sin. Here a question arises: how does this statement agree with His saying, the Exalted: «وليحملن أثقالاً مع أثقالهم»? The answer is that this verse concerns those who go astray and lead others astray: they carry the burdens of their own misguidance and the burdens of their misleading of others. As for the verse before us, it is restricted to those who carry the sins and burdens of themselves. On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās: the father meets his son, and the two say to him, "O my son, carry for us some of our sins." He says, "I cannot; what is upon me is enough for me."

* Vocabulary:
(نَصَبٌ): fatigue. In al-Qāmūs: "naṣiba, like fariḥa: he was worn out." And in al-Mukhtār: "naṣiba: he tired, and its pattern is ṭariba."
(لُغُوبٌ): exhaustion from fatigue. In al-Qāmūs: "laghiba, laghaban and laghūban, like manaʿa, samiʿa and karuma: he was exhausted with the severest exhaustion." And in al-Mukhtār: "Al-lughūb, with two ḍammas, is fatigue and exhaustion; its pattern is dakhala; and laghiba with kasra, laghūban, is a weak dialectal form." The apparent sense of what appears in the lexicons is that the two agree in meaning, but al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between them with a fine distinction. He said: "If you say, what is the difference between al-naṣab and al-lughūb? I say: al-naṣab is the fatigue and hardship that befalls the one who is exerting himself on a matter and engaged in it, while al-lughūb is the languor that overtakes him because of the exertion. So al-naṣab is the hardship and strain itself, and al-lughūb is its result and what arises from it of weariness and slackness."

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا): (ثم) is a conjunction of order with delay; (أورثنا الكتاب) is a verb, an agent and a second direct object. The second object was put first only with the aim of honouring and exalting the Book, and its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric. (الذين) is the first object, and the clause (اصطفينا) is the ṣila of (الذين); (من عبادنا) is a ḥāl.
(فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سابِقٌ بِالْخَيْراتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ is one of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), because He divided His servants to whom He gave the Book as inheritance, as will come. (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (ظالم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (لنفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ظالم); these are the first division. (ومنهم مقتصد) is conjoined to what precedes, and they are the second division; (ومنهم سابق بالخيرات) is also conjoined, and they are the third division; (بإذن الله) is a ḥāl or is attached to (سابق). The detail of that will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation; (الفضل الكبير) is the khabar of (هو), and the sentence is the khabar of (ذلك); or (الفضل الكبير) is the khabar of (ذلك).
(جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها): (جنات عدن) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يدخلونها) is the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a badal (substitute) from (الفضل), and there is no obstacle; but al-Zamakhsharī slipped through this parsing into establishing his Muʿtazilite creed, as will come in the section on Benefits, for its curiosity.
(يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤاً وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ): the sentence is a second khabar. Its parsing has already been given in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, where it occurred in this very wording, so renew your acquaintance with it. It is strange that al-Zamakhsharī, who parsed (لؤلؤا) as accusative by an omitted verb in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, i.e. "and they will be given", parsed it here as conjoined to the position of (من أساور), saying: "(ولؤلؤا) is conjoined to the position of (من أساور), and (من) enters for partitiveness, i.e. they are adorned with some bracelets of gold." (ولباسهم) is a mubtadaʾ, (فيها) is a ḥāl, and (حرير) is the khabar.
(وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (قالوا) is a past verb by which the imperfect is meant, and the turn to the past is to indicate certainty (taḥqīq); (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) is the khabar; (الذي) is an adjective (naʿt); the clause (أذهب عنا) is the ṣila; (الحزن) is the direct object of (أذهب), which became transitive by the hamza; (عنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أذهب).
(إِنَّ رَبَّنا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ): (إن) and its subject; the shifted lām; (غفور) is the first khabar of (إن) and (شكور) the second.
(الَّذِي أَحَلَّنا دارَ الْمُقامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): a badal from the preceding (الذي); the clause (أحلنا) is the ṣila, and it is a past verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; (دار المقامة) is a second direct object, i.e. "He lodged us in the abode of residence"; (من فضله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أحلنا), and (من) is for beginning or for justification.
(لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ): the clause (لا يمسنا) is a ḥāl from the first object of (أحلنا), and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from the second object, the first being preferable; (يمسنا) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يمسنا); (نصب) is the agent; and (ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب) is conjoined to what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1 - In His saying «ثم أحدثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا» [Translator's note: the source prints «أحدثنا» (we brought into being) where the verse reads «أورثنا» (we made inherit), as parsed above] there is a metaphor of the implicit, derivative kind (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): the giving of the Book to them, without toil or fatigue in its reaching them, is likened to the bequeathing to an heir.
2 - In this verse there is also the art of "joining with division" (al-jamʿ maʿa al-taqsīm), which is for the speaker to join two or more things in one ruling and then divide what he joined, or to divide first and then join. The first is like the verse mentioned and His saying, the Exalted: «يوم تأتي لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد» to the end of the verse.

* Benefits:
1 - The order according to the stations of people:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was the wrongdoer put first, then the moderate, then the foremost? I say: to announce the great number of the transgressors and their predominance, and that the moderate are few in relation to them, and the foremost are fewer than few." Al-Khāzin made this meaning clear in a fuller wording, saying: "If you say: why was the wrongdoer put first, then the moderate, then the foremost? I say: it is said that He ordered them in this order according to the stations of people, because the conditions of people are three: disobedience, heedlessness and repentance. When a man disobeys he enters the sphere of the wrongdoers; when he repents he enters the number of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are many, he enters the ranks of the foremost."
2 - Between the Muʿtazila and Ahl al-Sunna:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did you make «جنات عدن» a badal from «الفضل الكبير»? I say: because the pointing to «الفضل» is to the foremost in good deeds, which is the cause of the Gardens and of obtaining reward, so He put the cause in the place of the effect.
