(أَشَهِدُوا خَلْقَهُمْ سَتُكْتَبُ شَهادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْئَلُونَ) The sīn is a particle of futurity (its secret will come in the section on Rhetoric); «تكتب» is a passive imperfect verb; «شهادتهم» is the deputy agent; «يسألون» is conjoined to «ستكتب».

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of futurity: He only turned toward the future [Translator's note: the source reads «ضجّ إلى الاستقبال»; «جنح» ("turned toward") is probably meant], bringing the sīn that indicates it, so that the speech would contain the meaning of ample time for repentance, and so as to build hope on appealing for its acceptance before what they said is recorded; in keeping with what they believed about preferring males over females and ascribing the worse of the two parts, namely females, to Allah. In this is the utmost declaration of foolishness of their opinions, for they wronged our second half by ascribing evil and deficiency of intellect to it, then wronged their Creator by ascribing this part, which is evil, to Him. It is related of one of the Arabs that his wife gave birth to a girl, so he abandoned the house in which the woman was, and she said:
ما لأبي حمزة لا يأتينا ... يظل في البيت الذي يلينا
غضبان أن لا نلد البنينا ... ليس لنا من أمرنا ماشينا
وإنما نأخذ ما أعطينا ... حكمة ربي ذي الجلال فينا
(What is wrong with Abū Ḥamza that he does not come to us, but stays in the house next to ours, angry that we do not bear sons? We have no say in our affair as we wish; we only take what we are given, the wisdom of my Lord, Possessor of Majesty, concerning us.)

* Lügat:
(يَخْرُصُونَ): el-Misbâh'ta şöyle denir: «"خرص الكافر خرصا", "قتل" bâbından: kâfir yalan söyledi; o "خارص"tir.» el-Kâmûs ve et-Tâc'da: «الخرّاص: çok yalan söyleyen.» Kelimenin fâ ve ayn harfi olarak hâ (خ) ve râ (ر) için şaşırtıcı bir sır vardır: Bu ikisi aşağılık, pislik ve kötü bir iz bırakma anlamlarına delâlet eder. «خرئ خرءا وخراءة وخروءا»: dışkıladı, pisledi. Şöyle denir:
«خرئت بينهم الضبع», yani aralarına düşmanlık girdi. «المخراة» ve «المخرأة»: içinde dışkılanan yer; çoğulu «مخارئ»dir. «خرب البيت», «عمر»un (bayındır oldu) zıddıdır (ev harap oldu). «خرب الرجل»: adamın kulağı yarık veya delik oldu; o «أخرب», kadın «خرباء»dır. «خربش الكتاب أو العمل»: yazıyı veya işi bozdu; bu, avâm dilinin fasîh olanlarındandır. «خربص» de malı alıp götürmek anlamındadır; bu da fasîh bir avâm sözüdür. «خرت الأذن»: kulağı deldi. «خرّت الأرض»: yeri iyice tanıdı ve yolları ona gizli kalmadı; çünkü onun her yanında gezmiş ve köşe bucağında dolaşmıştır. «الخرثاء», kadının çirkin görülen sıfatlarındandır: Böğürleri iri, eti sarkık kadındır. «الخرتي» (hânın ötresiyle): eşyanın en kötüsü ve döküntüsüdür; «خرتي الكلام», sözün hayırsız olanıdır. «خرج»: ortaya çıktı; bilinen bir kelimedir. «الخراج الولّاج» (şeddeli): çok girip çıkan. «الخراج» (hâ üç harekeyle okunur): haraç, vergi; aslı, yerin ürününden ve maldan çıkandır. «الخُراج» (hânın ötresiyle): çıban gibi bedende çıkan her şey. «الخارجي»: sultana ve cemaate muhalefet eden kimse; Hâricîler (الخوارج) adı buradan verilmiştir; onlar büyük İslâm fırkalarından yedi fırkadır. «خرخر النائم»: uyuyan horladı. «الخريدة»: delinmemiş inci. «الخرور» (yere kapanma, düşme) bilinir; sahibi için bunda bir zillet vardır. «الخرازة» (dikicilik) hakir görülen bir meslektir. «أخرسه الله» (Allah onu dilsiz etti) bilinir. «أطعموا النفساء خرستها»: lohusaya «خرسة»sını yedirdiler; bu, ona mahsus yemektir; «خرّست فتخرّست» denir. Şair şöyle demiştir:
فلله عينا من رأى مثل مقبسي ... إذا النفساء أصبحت لم تخرّس
(Lohusaya lohusa yemeği verilemediği [kıtlık] zamanda, benim ateş aldığım [cömert] kimse gibisini gören gözlere Allah aşkına [ne güzel!].)
«رماه الله بخرساء»: Allah onu bir «خرساء» ile vurdu; bu, büyük belâdır. Ahtal şöyle demiştir:
وكم أنقذتني من جرور حبالكم ... وخرساء لو يرمى بها الفيل تلبّدا
(Uzun iplerinizden [tuzaklarınızdan] ve fil ona atılsa yere yapışacağı nice büyük belâdan beni kurtardı.)
Bunun aslı engerek yılanıdır. Antere şöyle demiştir:
عليهم كل محكمة دلاص ... كأن قتيرها أعيان خرس
(Üzerlerinde sağlam örülmüş, parlak zırhlar vardır; perçin başları sanki engereklerin gözleridir.)
«Üzerinde, incelik ve berraklıkta yılanın "خرشاء"sı gibi bir gömlek gördüm»; bu, yılanın gömleğidir (kavı) [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «سلحها» geçmektedir; «سلخها» olmalıdır.]. «Göğsünden çirkin "خراشيّ" atıyor»; bunlar balgam ve sümüktür. «خرط الورق»: yaprağı ağaçtan çekip soydu. «وسمه على الخرطوم»: onu burnundan damgaladı, yani onu zelil etti. «هم خراطيم القوم»: onlar kavmin ileri gelenleridir. «خرطوم الشراب»: «السلامة»dır [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «وشرب الخرطوم: السلامة» geçmektedir; doğrusu muhtemelen «خرطوم الشراب: السلافة» (şarabın ilk sızan halisi) olmalıdır; açıklama da buna uygundur.], çünkü o ilk sıkılan kısımdır. Ahtal şöyle demiştir: جادت بها من ذوات القار مترعة ... كلفاء ينحتّ عن خرطومها المدر
(Onu, katranlı küplerden ağzına kadar dolu, ağzından [mühür] çamuru dökülen koyu renkli bir küp cömertçe verdi.)
«Dalda "خرع" vardır», yani yumuşaklık ve gevşeklik; bu yüzden fâhişe kadına «الخريع» denmiştir. Şair şöyle demiştir:
يزيد جمال الدّل منها رزانة ... وحلم إذا خفّ النساء الخرائع
(Gevşek kadınlar hafiflik gösterdiğinde, onun ağırbaşlılığı ve hilmi, nazının güzelliğini artırır.)
«O, hint yağı ağacı (الخروع) gibi gevşektir.» «خرف الثمار»: meyveleri topladı; «أخرفي لنا يا جارية» (Ey cariye, bize meyve topla). «خرق الثوب وخرّقه»: elbisenin yırtığını genişletti; «انخرق» ve «تخرّق» (yırtıldı); «اتسع الخرق على الراقع» (yırtık yamayanın gücünü aştı). «شاة خرقاء»: kulağı delik koyun. «خرق في عمله»: işinde beceriksiz oldu; «فيه خرق» (onda beceriksizlik var); erkeğe «أخرق», kadına «خرقاء» denir. «خرم الشيء»: onu deldi. «اخترمهم الدهر وتخرّمهم»: zaman onları yok etti. Ebû Züeyb el-Hüzelî şöyle demiştir:
سبقوا هوى وأعنقوا لهواهم ... فتخرّموا ولكل جنب مصرع
(Arzumla [benden] önce gittiler ve ölümlerine koştular; derken yok oldular; her yan için bir düşüş yeri vardır.)
Bu, şerefli dilimizin şaşılacak şeylerindendir.
(أُمَّةٍ): Yönelinen ve kastedilen yol; hemzesi kesreyle de okunur.

* İ'rab:
(وَقالُوا لَوْ شاءَ الرَّحْمنُ ما عَبَدْناهُمْ): Onların küfür türlerinden başka bir türü beyan için getirilmiş isti'nâfî bir sözdür. «قالوا» fiil ve fâildir; «لو» şartiyyedir; «شاء الرحمن» fiil ve fâildir; mef'ûlün bih mahzûftur; daha önce geçtiği gibi meşîet fiilinden sonra onun hazfi çoktur; yani: Meleklere ibadet edilmemesini dileseydi onlara ibadet etmezdik. «ما» nâfiyedir; «عبدناهم» fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; cümlenin i'rabdan mahalli yoktur, çünkü «لو»nun cevabında vâki olmuştur. (ما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ): «ما» nâfiyedir; «لهم» öne alınmış haberdir; «بذلك» hâldir, çünkü aslında sıfat idi. «من» zâid cer harfidir; «علم» geriye bırakılmış mübtedâdır. Haberinin isminden önce gelmesini caiz görenlerin görüşüne göre «ما»yı Hicâziyye kılman da caizdir. «إن» nâfiyedir; «هم» mübtedâdır; «إلا» hasr edatıdır; «يخرّصون» merfû muzâri fiildir. (أَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ كِتاباً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ فَهُمْ بِهِ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ):
«أم», «أشهدوا خلقهم» sözündeki istifhâma denk (muâdil) olan atıf harfidir; dolayısıyla muttasıladır. Bazıları ise «أم»in, inkârî istifhâm hemzesi anlamında munkatıa olduğunu söylemiştir; sanki onların aklî delilini nefyettikten sonra, sözden vazgeçerek naklî delillerini nefyetmeye geçmiştir. eş-Şihâb el-Hafâcî, «شهدوا» sözünden uzak olduğu için bu vechi tercih etmiştir. (بَلْ قالُوا إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ): «بل» atıf ve idrâb harfidir; «قالوا» fiil ve fâildir; «إن» ve ismi; «وجدنا آباءنا» cümlesi onun haberidir; «إن», ismi ve haberinden oluşan cümle onların sözünün mekûlü'l-kavlidir. «على أمة», «وجدنا»nın ikinci mef'ûlü mevziindedir. (وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ): Vâv atıf harfidir; «إن» ve ismi; «على آثارهم» (câr ve mecrûr) «مهتدون»a mütealliktir; «مهتدون» onun haberidir. «على آثارهم»ın haber olduğu, yani «ماشون» (yürüyenler) anlamında olduğu ve «مهتدون»un ikinci haber olduğu da söylenmiştir; belki daha uygun olanı budur. (وَكَذلِكَ ما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ): Vâv atıf harfidir; «كذلك» mahzûf bir masdarın sıfatıdır; bunun benzerleri daha önce geçti. «ما» nâfiyedir; «أرسلنا» fiil ve fâildir; «من قبلك» (câr ve mecrûr) «أرسلنا»ya mütealliktir; «في قرية» (câr ve mecrûr) mahzûf bir hâle mütealliktir; «من» zâid cer harfidir; «نذير» lafzen mecrûr, «أرسلنا»nın mef'ûlü olmak üzere mahallen mansûbtur. (إِلَّا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُقْتَدُونَ): «إلا» hasr edatıdır; istisnâ, hâllerin en genelindendir. «قال مترفوها» fiil ve fâildir; sonrasının i'rabı daha önce geçti. (قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آباءَكُمْ): «قال» mâzî fiildir; fâili müstetir zamir olup takdiri «هو»dur. Hemze istifhâm içindir; vâv hâliyyedir. Takdir: «أتقتدون بآبائكم ولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم من الضلالة» (Babalarınızı üzerinde bulduğunuz sapıklıktan daha doğru olanı size getirmiş olsam bile mi babalarınıza uyacaksınız?). «لو» şartiyyedir; «جئتكم» fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; «بأهدى» (câr ve mecrûr) «جئتكم»e mütealliktir; tafdîlin sırrı Belâgat bölümünde gelecektir. «مما» (câr ve mecrûr) «أهدى»ye mütealliktir; «وجدتم» cümlesi sıladır; «عليه» (câr ve mecrûr) «وجدتم»e mütealliktir. (قالُوا إِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ): «قالوا» fiil ve fâildir; «إن» ve ismi; «بما» (câr ve mecrûr) «كافرون»a mütealliktir; «أرسلتم» cümlesi ism-i mevsûlün sılasıdır; «به» (câr ve mecrûr) «أرسلتم»e mütealliktir; «كافرون», «إنّا»nın haberidir. (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ): Fâ atıf harfidir; «انتقمنا» fiil ve fâildir; «منهم» (câr ve mecrûr) «انتقمنا»ya mütealliktir. «فانظر»: fâ atıf harfidir; «انظر» emir fiildir, fâili müstetir olup takdiri «أنت»tir. «كيف» istifhâm ismi olup «كان»ın öne alınmış haberi olarak nasb mahallindedir; «كان» nâkıs mâzî fiildir; «عاقبة المكذبين» onun geriye bırakılmış ismidir.

* Belâgat:
«قال أو لو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنّا بما أرسلتم به كافرون» sözünde «ilcâ» sanatı vardır. Bu, konuşanın hasmına, onu kendi nefsinin hakikatini ve kalbinin içinde gizlediğini itiraf etmeye mecbur bırakacak bir sözle ansızın karşılık vermesidir. Âyette, babalarının üzerinde bulunduğu şeyde de bir hidayet olmasını gerektiren tafdîl (ism-i tafdîl) ile ifade edilmesi, ancak onları, gizledikleri niyetlerinin hakikatini itiraf etmeye mecbur bırakmak içindir. Sanki onlarla en uzak sınırlara kadar iner ve onlara en son noktalara kadar dizgin salıverir; tâ ki sonunda, sözde nasihatin fayda vermediği ve hüccet getirmenin onu yumuşatmakta işe yaramadığı inatlarını itiraf etsinler.

* Vocabulary:
(يَخْرُصُونَ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "kharaṣa al-kāfir kharṣan, from the pattern of qatala: he lied, so he is a khāriṣ." And in al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: "al-kharrāṣ: the liar." The letters khāʾ and rāʾ as the first and second radicals of the word have a wonderful secret: they indicate abasement, filth, and the production of a bad effect. Thus: khariʾa khaʾan, kharāʾatan, khurūʾan: he defecated and had loose bowels. One says:
خرئت بينهم الضبع
that is, enmity entered among them. Al-mikhrāt and al-mikhraʾa: the place where one defecates; plural makhāriʾ. Kharaba al-bayt: the opposite of ʿamara (to be inhabited/built up). Kharaba al-rajul: the man became split-eared or pierced-eared, so he is akhrab and she is kharbāʾ. Kharbasha al-kitāb or al-ʿamal: he spoiled it; it is of the eloquent colloquial. Kharbaṣa also, meaning he took the money and went off with it, is likewise eloquent colloquial. Kharata al-udhun: he pierced the ear; and kharrata al-arḍ: he knew the land and its paths were not hidden from him, because he had gone through its regions and wandered in its sides. Al-kharthāʾ is among the attributes of the ugly woman: she is broad in the flanks and slack in flesh. Al-kharthī (with ḍamma on the khāʾ) is the worst of goods and their refuse, and kharthī al-kalām is what has no good in it. Kharaja: he emerged, which is well known. Al-kharrāj al-wallāj (with shadda) is one who goes out and in often. Al-kharāj (with the khāʾ vowelled in three ways) is tribute, and its origin is what comes out of the yield of the land and of wealth. Al-khurāj (with ḍamma on the khāʾ) is anything that comes out on the body, like an abscess. Al-khārijī is one who rebels against the ruler and the community, and from it the Khawārij were named, who are seven sects among the major Islamic sects. Kharkhara al-nāʾim: the sleeper snored. Al-kharīda is the pearl that has not been pierced. Al-khurūr (falling down) is well known, and there is abasement in it for the one who does it. Al-kharāza (cobbling) is a menial trade. Akhrasahu Allāh (Allah struck him dumb) is well known. "Feed the woman in childbed her kharsa" is her particular food, and she has been given kharas and so takharrasat. He said:
فلله عينا من رأى مثل مقبسي ... إذا النفساء أصبحت لم تخرّس
(By Allah, what eyes have seen the like of my fire-brand, when the woman in childbed has not been given her kharsa food.)
And "Allah struck him with a kharsāʾ", which is a calamity. Al-Akhṭal said:
وكم أنقذتني من جرور حبالكم ... وخرساء لو يرمى بها الفيل تلبّدا
(How often have you saved me from the dragging of your ropes, and from a kharsāʾ which, were an elephant struck with it, would cower down.)
Its original sense is the viper. ʿAntara said:
عليهم كل محكمة دلاص ... كأن قتيرها أعيان خرس
(Upon them is every well-wrought, smooth coat of mail, its rivet-heads like the eyes of vipers.)
And "I saw him wearing a shirt like the kharshāʾ of the snake", in thinness and clarity, which is its slough [Translator's note: the source reads «سلحها»; «سلخها» is evidently meant]; and "he brings up from his chest foul kharāshī", which is phlegm and mucus. Kharaṭa al-waraq: he stripped the leaf from the tree by pulling at it. Wasamahu ʿalā al-khurṭūm: he humbled him; and "they are the kharāṭīm of the people" (their leaders); and "shurb al-khurṭūm" is safety, because it is the first that is pressed out. Al-Akhṭal said:
جادت بها من ذوات القار مترعة ... كلفاء ينحتّ عن خرطومها المدر
(She poured it for us, from the pitch-lined jars, full, dark-brown, the clay seal scraping away from its spout.)
In the stick there is khariʿ, that is softness and slackness, and from it the dissolute woman is called al-kharīʿ. He said:
يزيد جمال الدّل منها رزانة ... وحلم إذا خفّ النساء الخرائع
(Her coquetry's beauty is increased by her gravity and forbearance, when the loose women are light.)
It is limp like the castor-plant (khirwaʿ). Kharafa al-thimār: he gathered the fruit; "akhrifī lanā, O girl" (gather for us). Kharaqa al-thawb and kharraqahu: he widened its tear, and it became torn and ragged, and "the tear grew too large for the mender"; a kharqāʾ sheep is one whose ear is pierced; kharaqa fī ʿamalihi: he was clumsy in his work, and in him is khurq, and he is akhraq and she is kharqāʾ. Kharama al-shayʾ: he pierced it; and "ikhtaramahum al-dahr" and "takharramahum": time cut them down. Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī said:
سبقوا هوى وأعنقوا لهواهم ... فتخرّموا ولكل جنب مصرع
(They outstripped my desire and hastened to their own; then they were cut down, and every side has its place of falling.)
And this is among the marvels of our noble language.
(أُمَّةٍ) A path (ṭarīqa) that is followed and aimed at; its hamza can also be read with kasra (imma).

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا لَوْ شاءَ الرَّحْمنُ ما عَبَدْناهُمْ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain another kind of their disbelief. «قالوا» is verb and agent; «لو» is conditional; «شاء الرحمن» is verb and agent, and the direct object is omitted (its omission is frequent after the verb of will, as has already preceded), i.e. "had He willed that the angels not be worshipped, we would not have worshipped them"; «ما» is negative; «عبدناهم» is verb, agent and direct object; the clause has no position because it occurs as the apodosis of «لو». (ما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ) «ما» is negative; «لهم» is a preposed khabar; «بذلك» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective; «من» is a redundant preposition and «علم» is a postposed mubtadaʾ. You may also make «ما» a Ḥijāzī «mā», according to the view of those who allow the preposing of its khabar before its noun. «إن» is negative; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «يخرصون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative. (أَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ كِتاباً مِنْ قَبْلِهِ فَهُمْ بِهِ مُسْتَمْسِكُونَ) «أم» is a conjunction equivalent to the interrogative in His words «أشهدوا خلقهم», so it is the connected type. Some said «أم» is disconnected, meaning the hamza of rhetorical interrogation, as if, after denying their rational argument, He turned from the speech to deny their transmitted argument; al-Shihāb al-Khafājī preferred this view because it avoids the awkwardness with «شهدوا». (بَلْ قالُوا إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ) «بل» is a conjunction and particle of turning away (iḍrāb); «قالوا» is verb and agent; «إن» and its noun, and the clause «وجدنا آباءنا» is its khabar; the clause of «إن», its noun and its khabar is the quoted speech of their saying; «على أمة» is in the position of the second object of «وجدنا». (وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; «على آثارهم» is attached to «مهتدون» and «مهتدون» is its khabar. It has also been said that «على آثارهم» is the khabar, i.e. "walking", and «مهتدون» a second khabar, which is perhaps preferable. (وَكَذلِكَ ما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِنْ نَذِيرٍ) The waw is a conjunction; «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and parallels of it have already preceded; «ما» is negative; «أرسلنا» is verb and agent; «من قبلك» is attached to «أرسلنا»; «في قرية» is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «من» is a redundant preposition and «نذير» is genitive in form and accusative in position as the direct object of «أرسلنا». (إِلَّا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها إِنَّا وَجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وَإِنَّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُقْتَدُونَ) «إلا» is a particle of restriction, and the exception is from the most general of circumstances; «قال مترفوها» is verb and agent, and the i'rab of what follows has preceded. (قالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِأَهْدى مِمَّا وَجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آباءَكُمْ) «قال» is a past verb and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو); the hamza is interrogative and the waw circumstantial; the implied form is "Will you follow your fathers even if I bring you what is better guided than that upon which you found your fathers of misguidance?"; «لو» is conditional; «جئتكم» is verb, agent and direct object; «بأهدى» is attached to «جئتكم» (the secret of the comparative will come in the section on Rhetoric); «مما» is attached to «أهدى»; the clause «وجدتم» is the ṣila; «عليه» is attached to «وجدتم». (قالُوا إِنَّا بِما أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كافِرُونَ) «قالوا» is verb and agent; «إن» and its noun; «بما» is attached to «كافرون»; the clause «أرسلتم» is the ṣila of the relative; «به» is attached to «أرسلتم»; «كافرون» is the khabar of «إنّا». (فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «انتقمنا» is verb and agent; «منهم» is attached to «انتقمنا»; «فانظر»: the fāʾ is a conjunction and «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative, a preposed khabar of «كان»; «كان» is a defective past verb and «عاقبة المكذبين» is its postposed noun.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «قال أو لو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم قالوا إنّا بما أرسلتم به كافرون» there is the art of compulsion (al-iljāʾ), which is that the speaker takes his adversary by surprise with what compels him to admit the reality of his soul and the inner secret of his heart. The expression in the verse with the comparative, which implies that what their fathers were upon contained some guidance, was only to compel them to admit the reality of their intentions, which they hide, as though He descended with them to the furthest limits and gave them rein to the utmost extents, so that they would in the end confess their obstinacy, with which no counsel in speech avails, and in subduing which bringing proof is of no use.

* Vocabulary:
(بَراءٌ) With fatḥa on the bāʾ, an alif, and a hamza after the rāʾ. It is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has taken the place of an adjective, and for that reason masculine and feminine, singular, dual and plural are the same in it. In al-Mukhtār: "tabarraʾa min kadhā, so he is barāʾ min-hu, with fatḥa and elongation; it is not put in the dual or the plural because it is a maṣdar like samāʿ." In al-Qāmūs: "anā barāʾ minhu: it is not put in the dual or plural, nor made feminine; that is, barī'." 
(عَقِبِهِ) His offspring. In al-Qāmūs: "al-ʿaqib: running after running; and the child, and the child of the child, like al-ʿaqib on the pattern of katif."
(سُخْرِيًّا) With ḍamma on the sīn, relating to sukhra, which is work without pay. In al-Qāmūs: "sakhkharahu, like manaʿahu, sukhriyyan with kasra, and also with ḍamma: he charged him with what he did not want and overpowered him." Its explanation has already preceded. It is unlikely to be from sukhriyya in the sense of mockery and derision, contrary to the one who said it is from sukhriyya meaning mockery, i.e. so that the rich mocks the poor.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَراءٌ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ) The waw is resumptive and the speech is resumptive, introduced to remind the Arabs of the state of their remote forefather. The adverbial is attached to an omitted «اذكر» ("remember"); the clause «قال إبراهيم» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «لأبيه» is attached to «قال»; «قومه» is conjoined to «أبيه»; the clause «إنني برآء» is in the position of accusative, the quoted speech; «مما» is attached to «براء»; the clause «تعبدون» is the ṣila of «ما». [Translator's note: the source writes «برآء» here in the quotation of the verse and «براء» in the vocabulary section; the verse itself reads «براء».] (إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ) «إلا» is a particle of exception and «الذي» is the excepted; the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), as if He had said "but the One Who created me, for He will guide me". It is also possible that the exception is connected, on the basis that they used to associate idols with Allah. Al-Zamakhsharī and others allowed «إلا» to be an adjective meaning «غير», on the basis that «ما» in «ما تعبدون» is descriptive (mawṣūfa), the implied form being "I am free of gods you worship other than the One Who created me", which is parallel to His words the Exalted «لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا». Abū Ḥayyān preferred a disconnected exception, since they did not worship Allah alongside their idols. [Translator's note: the source prints «يسركون»; «يشركون» ("associate") is meant.] The clause «فطرني» is the ṣila of the relative; the fāʾ is causal; «إن» and its noun, and the clause «سيهدين» is its khabar; the sīn is for emphasis, not for futurity, that is, "He will continue my guidance", since He the Exalted is his guide in the future and the present; the direct object is omitted, i.e. «سيهديني», to preserve the verse-ending (fāṣila). (وَجَعَلَها كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «جعلها» is a verb, a latent agent pronoun and a first direct object, and the pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm; «كلمة» is the second direct object; «باقية» is an adjective; «في عقبه» is attached to «باقية»; «لعلهم»: «لعل» and its noun, and the clause «يرجعون» is its khabar. What is meant by "the abiding word" will come in the section on Benefits. (بَلْ مَتَّعْتُ هؤُلاءِ وَآباءَهُمْ حَتَّى جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ وَرَسُولٌ مُبِينٌ) «بل» is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb) and conjunction; the iḍrāb is from an omitted element which must be supposed for the speech to run on, the implied form being: "and he made it an abiding word among his descendants, by enjoining it upon them, hoping that the polytheists would return to it; but what he hoped did not come about; rather I gave these people, who are related to Ibrāhīm, enjoyment, and did not treat them with punishment, and I deferred their appointed terms." «هؤلاء» is a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of accusative as a direct object; «آباءهم» is conjoined to «هؤلاء» or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); «حتى» is a particle of end-point and of genitive; the secret of the end-point of the enjoyment will come in the section on Rhetoric. «جاءهم الحق» is a verb, a preposed direct object and a postposed agent; «رسول» is conjoined to «الحق»; «مبين» is an adjective of «رسول». (وَلَمَّا جاءَهُمُ الْحَقُّ قالُوا هذا سِحْرٌ وَإِنَّا بِهِ كافِرُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; «لما» is a connective or a temporal particle; «جاءهم الحق» is a verb, a preposed direct object and a postposed agent; the clause «قالوا» has no position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ and «سحر» its khabar, and the clause is the quoted speech; «إنّا»: «إن» and its noun; «به» is attached to «كافرون», and «كافرون» is the khabar of «إنّا». (وَقالُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَ هذَا الْقُرْآنُ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنَ الْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ) The waw is a conjunction on the preceding speech; «قالوا» is verb and agent; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning "why not" (hallā); «نزل» is a passive past verb; «هذا» is a demonstrative, deputy agent; «القرآن» is a badal; «على رجل» is attached to «نزل»; «من القريتين» is an adjective of «رجل»; «عظيم» is a second adjective of «رجل». More about the two will come in the section on Benefits. (أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ) The hamza is for rhetorical interrogation, charging them with ignorance and deeming their minds weak; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يقسمون» is the khabar; «رحمة ربك» is the object of «يقسمون». «رحمة ربك» is written in the muṣḥaf with the open tāʾ (tāʾ maftūḥa), the details of which will come in the section on Benefits. (نَحْنُ قَسَمْنا بَيْنَهُمْ مَعِيشَتَهُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «قسمنا» is the khabar; «بينهم» is an adverbial attached to «قسمنا»; «معيشتهم» is a direct object; «في الحياة الدنيا» is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَرَفَعْنا بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ لِيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً سُخْرِيًّا) The waw is a conjunction; «رفعنا» is verb and agent; «بعضهم» is a direct object; «فوق بعض» is an adverbial attached to «رفعنا»; «درجات» is a tamyīz; the lām is causal, and it has been said that it is the lām of outcome (ṣayrūra or ʿāqiba); «يتخذ» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an optionally implied «أن» after the lām; «بعضهم» is the agent; «بعضا» is the first direct object and «سخريا» is the second direct object. What follows from this is what al-Khāzin set out when he said: "He means that if we had made them equal in all circumstances, no one would serve anyone, and none of them would be made to labour for another, and in that case it would lead to the ruin of the world and the corruption of the state of this life." (وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ) The waw is a conjunction or circumstantial; «رحمة ربك» is a mubtadaʾ and «خير» its khabar; «مما» is attached to «يجمعون»; the clause «يجمعون» is the ṣila of «ما».

* Rhetoric:
In the coming of the iḍrāb in His words the Exalted «بل متّعت هؤلاء» (the verse), and in making the end-point of the enjoyment the coming of the truth, there is a wonderful point. The aim of the iḍrāb is not to refute the preceding speech but to emphasise and continue, to show that they were preoccupied from the truth that had come to them, since there is no relation between the coming of the truth and the enjoyment. The meaning is that they were preoccupied from thanking the Bestower: instead of submitting to the truth, taking up its means, devoting themselves to it and seeking out its bounties, they brought something worse than the heedlessness they were in.

* Benefits:
1- What is meant by the abiding word among the descendants of Ibrāhīm, blessings of Allah be upon him, is the word of tawḥīd (divine oneness) which he spoke, namely his words: «إنني برآء مما تعبدون إلا الذي فطرني».
2- What is meant by the two towns is Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif, and the two men are al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī in Mecca and ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī from al-Ṭāʾif, because the noble man with them, according to their silly beliefs, was the one who had much wealth and standing, and Muḥammad was not like that, so the message was not fitting for him.
3- The tāʾ is written open in His words «ورحمة ربك» in the muṣḥaf, as it is written in al-Aʿrāf, al-Rūm, Hūd and al-Baqara.

* Vocabulary:
(سُقُفاً) In al-Qāmūs: "al-saqf of the house, like al-saqīf; the plural is suqūf, and also suqf with two ḍammas." From al-Farrāʾ: it is the plural of saqīfa. It has also been read «سقوفا» as a plural on the pattern fuʿūl, like kaʿb, kuʿūb.
(وَمَعارِجَ) Plural of miʿraj, with fatḥa or kasra on the mīm. The stairs by which one ascends are called maʿārij because walking on them is like the walking of the lame (aʿraj).
(وَزُخْرُفاً) Al-zukhruf is gold and adornment. Ibn Zayd said: it is what people keep in their houses of furnishings and furniture. Al-Ḥasan said: engravings; its origin is adornment. One says zakhrafat al-dār, that is, I adorned it, and tazakhrafa fulān, that is, he adorned himself. The lexicons give many meanings of al-zukhruf, among them gold, the beauty of a thing, and "zukhruf al-kalām" meaning its gilded falsehoods, and "zukhruf al-arḍ" meaning the colours of its plants [Translator's note: the source reads «بناتها»; «نباتها» is meant]; the plural is zakhārif.
(يَعْشُ) In al-Qāmūs: "al-ʿashā, shortened: poor sight at night and by day; and blindness is ʿashā like raḍiya and daʿā." And in al-Mukhtār: "ʿashā ʿanhu: he turned away from it; its pattern is that of ʿadā, and from it comes His words the Exalted «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن»." I say: some interpreted it in the verse as weakness of sight. Abū al-Haytham and al-Azharī said: ʿashawtu ilā kadhā means I aimed at it, and ʿashawtu ʿan kadhā means I turned away from it, so a distinction is made between ilā and ʿan, like "iltu ilayhi" and "iltu ʿanhu".
(نُقَيِّضْ) We cause and we decree. One says qayyaḍa Allāhu lahu kadhā: He decreed it for him; and qayyaḍa Allāhu fulānan li-fulān: He brought him to him.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْلا أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً) The waw is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of prevention due to existence; «أن» and what follows it, in the interpretation of a maṣdar, is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; «الناس» is the noun of «يكون»; «أمة» is its khabar; «واحدة» is an adjective. The meaning of their being one community is their agreeing upon one matter, and what is meant here is disbelief, by the indication of the apodosis, as will come. (لَجَعَلْنا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَمَعارِجَ عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ) The lām is the connective of the apodosis; «جعلنا» is verb and agent; «لمن» is in the position of the second object; the clause «يكفر» is the ṣila of «من»; «بالرحمن» is attached to «يكفر»; «لبيوتهم» is a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «لمن يكفر» with the preposition repeated; «سقفا» is the first object of «جعلنا»; «من فضة» is an adjective of «سقفا»; «معارج» is conjoined to «سقفا»; «عليها» is attached to «يظهرون»; «يظهرون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the clause is an adjective of «معارج». (وَلِبُيُوتِهِمْ أَبْواباً وَسُرُراً عَلَيْها يَتَّكِؤُنَ) Conjoined to what precedes. The word «البيوت» is repeated for greater confirmation. You may also suppose an omitted verb to govern «أبوابا» and «سررا» in the accusative, so that it would be a conjunction of clauses. (وَزُخْرُفاً وَإِنْ كُلُّ ذلِكَ لَمَّا مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) «وزخرفا» is also conjoined to «سررا», or is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and we made for them gold ornament". Al-Zamakhsharī conjoined it to the position of «من فضة», as if He had said "a roof of silver and gold", that is, some of them thus and some thus. The waw is a conjunction; «إن» is negative; «كل ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ; «لما» with shadda means «إلا»; «متاع الحياة الدنيا» is the khabar. It has also been read with «لما» lightened, in which case «إن» is the lightened form of the heavy «إن», without operation, the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and «ما» is redundant. (وَالْآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ) The waw is circumstantial; «الآخرة» is a mubtadaʾ; «عند ربك» is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; «للمتقين» is attached to an omitted element that is the khabar of «الآخرة». In this is a full confirmation that the truly great is the great in the Hereafter, not in this world. (وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطاناً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ) A resumptive speech, introduced to narrate the outcome of those who turn away from the remembrance of Allah. It has also been said that it is connected to His words at the beginning of the surah «أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا». «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «يعش» is the protasis; «عن ذكر الرحمن» is attached to «يعش»; «نقيض» is the apodosis; the two clauses of protasis and consequence are the khabar of «من»; «له» is attached to «نقيض»; «شيطانا» is the direct object of «نقيض»; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «له» is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «قرين» and was placed before it; «قرين» is the khabar. (وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَصُدُّونَهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ) The waw is a conjunction; «إن» and its noun; the shifted lām; the clause «يصدّونهم» is the khabar of «إن»; «عن السبيل» is attached to «يصدّونهم». (وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ) The waw is circumstantial or a conjunction; «يحسبون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; «أن», its noun and its khabar stand in the place of the two objects of «يحسبون». The secret of the plural will come in the section on Rhetoric. (حَتَّى إِذا جاءَنا قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ) «حتى» is a particle of end-point and of genitive; «إذا» is an adverbial of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause «جاءنا» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the agent of «جاءنا» refers to the one who turns away (al-ʿāshī) taken from the preceding «يعش»; the clause «قال» has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «يا» is a particle of alerting or of vocative, and the one addressed is omitted and apparent, its implied form being apparent; «ليت» is a particle of wishing and of accusative; «بيني» is an adverbial attached to an omitted preposed khabar of it; «بينك» is conjoined to «بيني»; «بعد المشرقين» is the postposed noun of «ليت» [Translator's note: the source reads «اسم ليست»; «اسم ليت» is meant]. The meaning of «المشرقين» will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَبِئْسَ الْقَرِينُ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «بئس» is a past verb, jāzim [Translator's note: the source reads «جازم»; «جامد» (non-conjugating) is meant], to form blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm); «القرين» is the agent of «بئس»; the specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "you" (أنت). (وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ إِذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ فِي الْعَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to set out what will be said to them in the Hereafter; «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; «ينفعكم» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by «لن»; «اليوم» is an adverbial attached to «ينفعكم»; «إذ» is an adverbial for past time, a badal from «اليوم». It is not to be said that «إذ» is for the past and «اليوم» for the present so the badal is not permissible, because this world and the Hereafter are connected and are equal in the judgement and knowledge of Allah, so that «إذ» is as if it were future and «اليوم» as if it were past. Ibn Jinnī said, in his questioning of Abū ʿAlī: "I went back to it several times, and the last that came from him was that this world and the Hereafter are connected, and they are equal in the judgement and knowledge of Allah." The clause «ظلمتم» is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; «أن» and what follows it, in the interpretation of a maṣdar, is the agent of «ينفعكم», i.e. "your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you, as sharing in the calamities of this world benefits, where the afflicted one finds consolation in the like of his own". It has also been said that the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "your wishing" (تمنّيكم), which is indicated by His words «يا ليت بيني وبينه», i.e. "your wishing for distance will not benefit you". The reading «إنكم» with kasra supports the implied agent, since it is then resumptive and gives a causal meaning; as for the reading with fatḥa, «أن» and what follows it are in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "because you"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ينفعكم»; «في العذاب» is attached to «مشتركون»; «مشتركون» is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
1- The indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition: in His words «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن نقيض له شيطانا» (the verse) there is a wonderful point, namely that an indefinite noun occurring in the context of a condition gives generality, and for that reason the pronoun refers back to it in the plural in His words «وإنهم ليصدّونهم»; the second is the waw in His words «ويحسبون» and the third is the hāʾ in His words «إنهم». [Translator's note: the source lists "the second" and "the third" but the first item is not stated in the text as printed; presumably the plural pronoun in «ليصدّونهم» is the first.]
Ibn Abī Ḥātim related, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-Makhzūmī, that Quraysh said: "Assign to every man among the companions of Muḥammad a man who will seize him." So they assigned Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh to Abū Bakr, and he came to him while he was among the people, and Abū Bakr said: "To what do you call me?" He said: "I call you to the worship of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā." Abū Bakr said: "And what is al-Lāt?" He said: "The sons of Allah." He said: "And what is al-ʿUzzā?" He said: "The daughters of Allah." Abū Bakr said: "Then who is their mother?" Ṭalḥa fell silent and did not answer him, and said to his companions: "Answer the man," but the people fell silent. Then Ṭalḥa said: "Rise, O Abū Bakr: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah." Then Allah sent down: «ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن» (the verse).
2- In this verse there is also the art of tankīt (the pointed choice), which is that the speaker aims at mentioning one thing rather than another that would fill its place, for the sake of a point in what is mentioned that favours its coming over anything else. Someone may ask: for what point did He depart from the literal word and not say "whoever turns away (yuʿriḍ) from the remembrance of the Merciful", and instead borrowed the word ʿashā (dim-sightedness) for misguidance? We say: the point is that the metaphorical word fulfils the intended meaning, unlike the literal word, for turning away is of two kinds: a turning away after which return is hoped, because the one turning away is able to return, and that is the turning away of the believer who holds the best belief, to whom there occur pleasures that absorb his thought and occupy his heart and mind with that pleasure, or its opposite, or other worldly matters, so he turns away from remembrance in that state; the companionship of Satan in that case is not permanent, because it is possible for him to return to Allah the Glorified and repent of it, and turn to the remembrance he had turned away from, whose way he knew of old and to whose path he was guided and in which he was brought up, or because of a divine solicitude required by an eternal precedent that draws him to it; and a turning away of misguidance from the path of right guidance and the way of good, such that even if we supposed that he wanted to turn to the good, the precedent of misguidance and wretchedness that has overcome him would prevent him. What is meant by turning away in the verse is the turning away of misguidance, not the turning away of heedlessness, so it is beyond doubt that the borrowing of ʿashā for misguidance is fitting in it. This is the turning-away one for whom the companionship of Satan is decreed wherever he is and wherever he may be; thus the place of the point is made clear that favoured the departure from the literal word to the metaphorical word.
3- Taghlīb (predominance): in His words «بعد المشرقين» is the art of taghlīb, which is common in their speech: they let one thing predominate over what belongs to another, by applying its name to the other and using the dual on this consideration, because of affinity and mixture between them. An example of taghlīb for affinity is their saying al-abawayn (the two fathers) for the father and the mother, and from it comes His words the Exalted «ولأبويه لكل واحد منهما السدس»; and al-mashriqayn (the two easts) and al-maghribayn (the two wests) and al-khāfiqayn (the two horizons), which is the place of khufūq, i.e. setting, from khafaqa al-najm, i.e. it set; and al-qamarayn (the two moons) for the sun and the moon. Abū al-Ṭayyib said:
نشرت ثلاث ذوائب من شعرها ... في ليلة فأرت ليالي أربعا
واستقبلت قمر السما بوجهها ... فأرتني القمرين في وقت معا
(She let loose three locks of her hair in one night, so she showed me four nights; and she faced the moon of the sky with her face, so she showed me the two moons at one time.)
that is, the sun, which is her face, and the moon of the sky. The two moons in common usage are the sun and the moon. It is also said that among such instances is al-Farazdaq's saying:
أخذنا بآفاق السماء عليكم ... لنا قمراها والنجوم الطوالع
(We have seized the horizons of the sky against you; ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
and it has been said that he meant only Muḥammad and al-Khalīl (Ibrāhīm), peace and blessings be upon both, because his lineage relates to them. They also say al-ʿUmarayn for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; and it is said that what is meant are ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, in which case there is no taghlīb. As for the first, there is taghlīb in it: they let the lighter name predominate, and it is said, because of the length of his life. They also say al-ʿAjjājayn for Ruʾba and al-ʿAjjāj, and al-marwatayn for al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa. An example of taghlīb for mixture is His words the Exalted: «فمنهم من يمشي على بطنه ومنهم من يمشي على رجلين ومنهم من يمشي على أربع», for the mixture is attained in the preceding generality in His words «كل دابة», which He then detailed afterwards, and in "those who walk on two legs" in the expression of the detail, for it includes human beings and birds. And His words the Exalted: «اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم والذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون», because «لعل» is attached to «خلقكم», not to «اعبدوا», lest it follow that a thing be explained by itself, i.e. "worship for the sake of piety (taqwā)", while taqwā is worship. They also let the masculine predominate over the feminine, so that she was counted among them in His words the Exalted: «وكانت من القانتين», that is, Maryam, and she was counted among the males, in that she was treated as one of them by the expression with a word that is specific to males in its original usage; and had there been no predominance He would have said «من القانتات».

* Benefits:
This world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever. In the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Tirmidhī: "From Abū Hurayra, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever.'" And from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If this world weighed with Allah the wing of a gnat, He would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it."

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا إِلى فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَائِهِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain an objection that Pharaoh raised against Moses, just as Quraysh raised the objection of poverty against Muhammad ﷺ. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of affirmation; أرسلنا is a verb and agent; موسى is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); بآياتنا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the bāʾ being the bāʾ of accompaniment; إلى فرعون are both attached (mutaʿalliq) to أرسلنا; and ملئه is conjoined to فرعون. (فَقالَ إِنِّي رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إني is inna and its noun; رسول رب العالمين is its predicate (khabar); and the clause of inna and what follows it is the content of what was said. (فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ بِآياتِنا إِذا هُمْ مِنْها يَضْحَكُونَ) The fāʾ is conjoined to something implied, that is, "so they asked him for signs proving his truthfulness"; لما is a temporal adverbial or a connective; جاءهم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بآياتنا are both attached to جاءهم; and إذا is the particle of surprise. You may take it as an adverbial governed by the verb of surprise which is the apodosis of لما, and you may take it as a particle. What follows is the text of Abū Ḥayyān's statement on this matter. He said: «Al-Zamakhsharī said: If you ask, how is it permissible for لما to be answered by the إذا of surprise? I say: because the verb of surprise is implied with it, and it is what governs the accusative in its position, as if it were said: "when he came to them with Our signs, they were surprised [and] «وقد ضحكهم»" [Translator's note: the source reads «فاجئوا وقد ضحكهم»; the Kashshāf has «وقت ضحكهم» ("at the time of their laughing")]. End of quotation. We know of no grammarian who held what this man held, namely that the إذا of surprise is put in the accusative by an implied verb whose implied form is "he surprised"; rather the views about it are three: either it is a particle, and so needs no governor; or an adverb of place; or an adverb of time. If a predicate is mentioned after the noun that follows it, it (إذا) is accusative as an adverbial, and the governor in it is that predicate, as in خرجت فإذا زيد قائم, whose implied form is "I went out, and in the place where I went out Zayd was standing" or "and at the time I went out Zayd was standing". If nothing is mentioned after the noun, or an accusative noun is mentioned as a ḥāl, then إذا is the predicate of the subject (mubtadaʾ). If the noun is a body, and we say it is an adverb of place, the matter is clear, as in خرجت فإذا الأسد, that is, "and in the presence was the lion", or فإذا الأسد رابضا ("and there was the lion, crouching"). If we say it is an adverb of time, then there is an omitted muḍāf (the first term of a genitive construct), so that time is not predicated of a body, as in خرجت فإذا الأسد, that is, "and at the time was the lion's presence". As for what al-Zamakhsharī claims, the implying of a verb of surprise, it has not been uttered, not even in a single place. Then the surprise he claims is not indicated by the meaning as coming from the preceding speech; rather the meaning indicates that the surprise comes from the speech in which إذا occurs. You say خرجت فإذا الأسد and the meaning is "and the lion surprised me", not "and I surprised the lion".» We have already given the discussion of the إذا of surprise. هم is a subject (mubtadaʾ); منها are both attached to يضحكون; and the clause يضحكون is their predicate. (وَما نُرِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ إِلَّا هِيَ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ أُخْتِها) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; نريهم is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; من is a redundant preposition; آية is the second direct object of نريهم; إلا is a particle of restriction; هي is a subject; أكبر is the predicate; من أختها are both attached to أكبر; and the clause is an adjective of آية. More discussion of this saying will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (وَأَخَذْناهُمْ بِالْعَذابِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أخذناهم is a verb, an agent and a direct object; بالعذاب are both attached to أخذناهم; and لعل with its noun and its predicate. (وَقالُوا: يا أَيُّهَا السَّاحِرُ ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ إِنَّنا لَمُهْتَدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and an agent; يا أيها is a vocative, whose i'rab has already been given; الساحر is a substitute (badal) for أي or an adjective of it; ادع is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the weak letter; لنا are both attached to ادع; ربك is a direct object; بما are both attached to ادع; ما may be a relative noun or a maṣdar (verbal-noun) particle, and the clause عهد is a ṣila (relative clause) or is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ; عندك is an adverbial attached to عهد; and إن with its noun, and لمهتدون is its predicate, with the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). (فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمُ الْعَذابَ إِذا هُمْ يَنْكُثُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element, that is, "so Moses prayed, and when We removed"; لما is a connective or temporal; كشفنا is a verb and an agent; عنهم are both attached to كشفنا; العذاب is a direct object; إذا is the particle of surprise, which has been discussed in detail; هم is a subject; and the clause ينكثون is its predicate. (وَنادى فِرْعَوْنُ فِي قَوْمِهِ قالَ يا قَوْمِ أَلَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وَهذِهِ الْأَنْهارُ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِي أَفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ) The wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; نادى فرعون is a verb and an agent; في قومه are both attached to نادى (the secret of this calling and of the containment will come in the chapter on rhetoric); قال is a past verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "he", and the clause is explicative; يا قوم is a vocative, a muḍāf to the omitted first-person yāʾ.
The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation; ليس is a defective, inert past verb; لي is its fronted predicate; and ملك مصر is its postponed noun. This wāw is either circumstantial, in which case the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl, or a conjunction, in which case هذه is conjoined to ملك مصر; on the first view هذه is a subject, الأنهار is a substitute, the clause تجري is the predicate, and من تحتي are both attached to تجري. أفلا: the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied element, لا is negative, and تبصرون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn. (أَمْ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْ هذَا الَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينٌ) أم is a conjunction; it is munqaṭiʿa (disjunctive), taken to mean بل together with the hamza, that is, "rather, I am better"; so it is disjunctive in expression but connected (muttaṣila) in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Suyūṭī said: this أم is connected, because the meaning is "Do you not see, or do you see?", except that he put the words "I am better" in the place of "you see", because if they said to him "You are better", they would be seeing people in his view; and this is a case of setting the cause in the place of the effect. Abū Ḥayyān objected to al-Zamakhsharī that the correlate (muʿādil) is not omitted after أم unless the word لا follows it, as in أتقول أم لا, that is, "or do you not say?"; as for omitting it without لا, as here, it is not permitted, although the omission of أم and the correlate has occurred, though rarely, and among it is the poet's verse:
دعاني إليها القلب إني لأمره ... سميع فما أدري أرشد طلابها
(The heart called me to her; I am obedient to its command, so I do not know whether seeking her is right.) He means "or error".
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «أم here is disjunctive in expression because a sentence occurs after it, and in meaning it is connected and correlative, since the meaning is "I am better than him, or not".» More of this discussion will come in the section on benefits. أنا is a subject; خير is the predicate; من هذا are both attached to خير; الذي is a substitute for the demonstrative; هو is a subject; مهين is the predicate; and the clause is the ṣila of الذي. (وَلا يَكادُ يُبِينُ) You may take the wāw as a conjunction, so that the clause is conjoined to the ṣila of the relative noun; you may take it as resumptive, so that the clause also has no grammatical position; and they permitted that it be circumstantial. لا is negative; يكاد is a defective imperfect verb, one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba); its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; and the clause يبين is the predicate of يكاد, that is, "make his speech clear". (فَلَوْلا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَسْوِرَةٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لولا is a particle of urging, meaning هلّا ("why not"); ألقي is a passive past verb; عليه are both attached to ألقي; أسورة is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil), the plural of سوار ("bracelet"); and من ذهب is an adjective of أسورة. (أَوْ جاءَ مَعَهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ)
أو is a conjunction; جاء is a past verb; معه is an adverbial attached to جاء; الملائكة is the agent; and مقترنين is a ḥāl, that is, "following one another, testifying to his truthfulness". (فَاسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطاعُوهُ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; استخف is a past verb, meaning "he incited", and in al-Mukhtār: «استفزه الخوف: استخفه» ("fear incited him: it made him light"), and in al-Miṣbāḥ: «واستخف قومه: حملهم على الخفّة والجهل» ("he made his people light: he drove them to levity and ignorance"); قومه is a direct object. فأطاعوه: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أطاعوه is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; إن with its noun; the clause كانوا is its predicate; the clause of inna is causal and has no grammatical position; قوما is the predicate of كانوا; and فاسقين is an adjective. (فَلَمَّا آسَفُونا انْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is temporal, adverbial, or a connective; آسفونا is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, derived by the hamza from أسف when he is angry, so it made it transitive by the hamza; the meaning is "when they did what warrants the exercise of forbearance and rouses indignation" [Translator's note: the source reads «ما يوجب دالة الحلم»; the wording is unclear and is rendered according to context]. The clause انتقمنا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to لما; منهم are both attached to انتقمنا; فأغرقناهم is conjoined to انتقمنا; and أجمعين is an emphasis (tawkīd) for the hāʾ. (فَجَعَلْناهُمْ سَلَفاً وَمَثَلًا لِلْآخِرِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; جعلناهم is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; سلفا is the second direct object, that is, "predecessors, going ahead to the punishment so that others may take a lesson from them"; مثلا is conjoined to سلفا; and للآخرين is an adjective of مثلا.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «وما نريهم من آية إلا هي أكبر من أختها» there is a comprehensive and exclusive statement, meaning that they are described as great, hardly differing in it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Such is the custom with things that meet in excellence and whose ranks differ in it by only a slight difference: people's opinions differ over which is better, so some prefer this one and some that one. On this people built their speech, saying: "Have you seen men, some of whom are better than others?" Sometimes the opinions of a single man differ about them, so at one time he prefers this one and at another that one. To it belongs the verse from the Ḥamāsa:
من تلق منهم تقل لاقيت سيدهم ... مثل النجوم التي يسري بها الساري
(Whomever of them you meet you say, "I have met their chief", like the stars by which the night traveller is guided.)
The woman of Anmār compared the perfect ones (الكلمة) among her sons [Translator's note: the source reads «الكلمة»; «الكملة» is meant] with one another, then, when she saw their ranks close together with little difference, said: "May I lose them, if I know which of them is better! They are like a ring of metal, in which one does not know where its two ends are."» So the description by "greatness" is figurative (majāz), and it is relative to those who look at them.
2- Figurative language also: in His saying «ونادى فرعون في قومه» there is a majāz mursal (loose metonymy) whose relation is locality, for he made his people the place of his calling and its site. The meaning is that he commanded the calling in their gatherings and places, just as what is meant by "he called among them" is that the calling is attributed to him, like your saying "the emir cut off the thief" when he commanded that he be cut off.

* Benefits:
أم also: We presented in the chapter on i'rab a glimpse of أم and mentioned in earlier places of this book weighty discussions about it. Here we quote the delightful chapter that the author of al-Mughnī devoted to it, with a useful comment on it. Ibn Hishām said: «The omission of the connected أم and of what is conjoined to it has been heard, as in the saying of the Hudhalī: دعاني أيها القلب إني لأمره ... سميع فما أدري أرشد طلابها
(The heart called me; I am obedient to its command, so I do not know whether seeking her is right.)
Its implied form is "or error". So they said, and there is a discussion of it, as already mentioned (that is, in the section on the single alif, that the hamza here is like هل and so needs no correlate). Some permitted the omission of what is conjoined to it without it, and said, regarding the saying of the Exalted «أفلا تبصرون أم», that the pause is here and that the implied form is "or do you see?", then he begins "I am better". This is false, since the omission of a conjoined element without its conjunction has never been heard; the conjoined element is rather the sentence "I am better". The aspect of equivalence between it and the preceding sentence is that the original is "or do you see?", then the nominal sentence was set in the place of the verbal one, and the cause in the place of the effect, because if they said to him "You are better", they would be seeing people in his view; and this is the meaning of Sībawayh's speech. If you ask: they say أتفعل هذا أم لا, and the original is "or you do not do it?", I say: the omission occurred only after لا and did not occur after the conjunction; and the particles of response often have sentences omitted after them and stand in expression in the place of those sentences, so it is as though the sentence were mentioned here owing to the presence of what makes it unnecessary.»
Sībawayh's wording in al-Kitāb: «This is the chapter of the disjunctive أم, and it is your saying: أعمرو عندك أم عندك زيد. This is not on a par with أيّهما عندك ("which of them is with you?"); do you not see that if you said أيّهما عندك it would not be sound except by repetition and emphasis? What shows you that the latter is cut off from the former is the man's saying «إنها لا بل» then saying «أم شاء» [Translator's note: the source reads «إنها لا بل»; Sībawayh's known example is «إنها لإبل أم شاء», "It is camels, or sheep?"]; so just as أم comes here after a statement, disjunctive, so it comes after an interrogative. That is because when he said أعمرو عندك he supposed that he was with him, then a like supposition overtook him about Zayd after his speech had been completed. Then he said: and like that: وهذه الأنهار تجري من تحتي أفلا تبصرون أم أنا خير, as if Pharaoh had said "Do you not see, or are you seeing?" So his saying "or am I better" is on a par with "or are you seeing", because had they said "You are better than he", it would have been on a par with their saying "We are seeing". So likewise "or am I better" is on a par with "or are you seeing".» Sībawayh thus ruled that أم is disjunctive.

* İ'rab:
(وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ): Müste'nef (yeni başlayan) bir sözdür; onların inatlarının ve kibirlenmede ileri gitmelerinin başka bir türünü beyan için sevk edilmiştir. «لما»: zarfiyye-hîniyye veya râbıta (bağlayıcı) edattır. «ضرب»: meçhul, mâzî fiildir. «ابن مريم»: nâib-i fâildir. «مثلا»: ikinci mef'ûlün bihtir; çünkü «ضرب» fiili «جعل» manasını tazammun etmiştir (içine almıştır). Hâl olarak i'rab edilmesi de caizdir; yani «kendisiyle misal verilen olarak zikredildi» demektir. «إذا»: fücâiyye (ansızınlık bildiren) edattır; onunla ilgili söz daha önce geçti. «قومك»: mübtedâdır. «منه»: câr ve mecrûr; «يصدون»e müteallik. «يصدون» cümlesi «قومك»in haberidir. Bu kelime sâd'ın kesresiyle (يَصِدُّونَ) okunur; yani işittikleri şeyden dolayı sevinç, neşe ve gülüşmeyle onlardan bir gürültü ve velvele yükselir. Kıssa «Fevâid» bölümünde gelecektir. «يصدون» kelimesi zamme ile (يَصُدُّونَ) de okunmuştur; bu «الصدود»dan, yani yüz çevirmekten gelir. Bunların iki lügat (iki ayrı söyleyiş) olduğu da söylenmiştir.
(وَقالُوا أَآلِهَتُنا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ): Vâv atıf harfidir. «قالوا»: fiil ve fâil. Hemze istifhâm içindir. «آلهتنا»: mübtedâ; «خير»: haber. «أم»: atıf harfidir ve muttasıladır. «هو»: «آلهتنا»ya ma'tûftur.
(ما ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًا بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ): «ما»: nefy harfidir. «ضربوه»: fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih. «لك»: câr ve mecrûr; «ضربوه»ya müteallik. «إلا»: hasr edatıdır. «جدلا»: mef'ûlün lieclihtir; yani hakkı ortaya koymak için değil, cedel, münakaşa ve inat uğruna demektir. Hâl yerinde bir masdar olması da caizdir; yani «ancak mücadele edenler olarak». «بل»: idrâb harfidir. «هم»: mübtedâ; «قوم»: haber; «خصمون»: «قوم»un sıfatıdır.
(إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلًا لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): «إن»: nefy harfidir. «هو»: mübtedâ. «إلا»: hasr edatı. «عبد»: «هو»nun haberi. «أنعمنا» cümlesi «عبد»in sıfatıdır. «عليه»: câr ve mecrûr; «أنعمنا»ya müteallik. «جعلناه»: «أنعمنا»ya ma'tûftur. «مثلا»: «جعلناه»nın ikinci mef'ûlün bihidir. «لبني إسرائيل»: «مثلا»nın sıfatıdır.
(وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ مَلائِكَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ): Vâv atıf harfidir. «لو»: şart edatıdır. «نشاء»: merfû muzâri fiil; fâili müstetir olup takdiri «نحن»dir. Lâm, «لولا»nın cevabında vâki olan lâmdır [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta böyle «لولا» yazılmıştır; âyetteki edat «لو»dur.]. «جعلنا»: fiil ve fâil. «منكم»: eğer «جعلنا» «صيّرنا» (kıldık) manasında ise ikinci mef'ûl yerindedir; eğer «خلقنا» (yarattık) manasında ise câr ve mecrûr «جعلنا»ya müteallik olur. «في الأرض»: câr ve mecrûr; «يخلفون»a müteallik. «يخلفون» cümlesi «ملائكة»nin sıfatıdır. Bazı nahivciler şöyle demiştir: «من» bedel (yerine) manası içindir; yani «sizin yerinize melekler kılardık». Bundan olmak üzere Allah Teâlâ'nın «أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة» kavlini de saymıştır; yani «âhiretin yerine». Şairin şu sözü de böyledir:
أخذوا المخاض من الفصيل غلبة ... ظلما ويكتب للأمير أقالا
(Zorbalıkla ve zulmen yavru deve yerine gebe develeri aldılar; emîr için de «أقالا» yazılıyor.) [Mütercim notu: Sondaki «أقالا» kelimesi kaynakta böyle basılmıştır ve anlamı belirsizdir; «أفيلا» (genç deve) kastedilmiş olabilir.]
Yani «yavru devenin yerine». Daha evlâ olanı ise —i'rabda zikrettiğimiz gibi— bunun teb'îz (kısmîlik) için olmasıdır. [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «في الإعراض» yazılmıştır; «في الإعراب» kastedilmiş olmalıdır.]
(وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِها): Vâv atıf harfidir. «إن» ve ismi; lâm müzahlaka lâmıdır. «علم»: «إنه»nin haberidir. «للساعة»: «علم»in sıfatıdır; yani kendisiyle (kıyametin yaklaştığı) bilinen alâmetlerinden bir alâmettir; alâmete, onunla bilgi hâsıl olduğu için «علم» denmiştir. Fâ fasîha fâsıdır. «لا»: nehiy edatıdır. «تمترن»: nehiy «لا»sı ile meczûm muzâri fiil olup cezm alâmeti nûnun hazfidir; iki sâkinin buluşması sebebiyle hazfedilen vâv fâildir; şeddeli nûn ağır te'kîd nûnudur. «المرية»: şüphe demektir.
(وَاتَّبِعُونِ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ): Vâv atıf harfidir. «اتبعوني»: nûnun hazfi üzere mebnî emir fiil; vâv fâildir; nûn vikâye nûnudur; Mushaf'ın yazım usulüne uyularak hatta (yazıda) hazfedilen yâ mef'ûlün bihtir. «هذا»: mübtedâ; «صراط»: haber; «مستقيم»: sıfat.
(وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ): Vâv atıf harfidir. «لا»: nehiy edatıdır. «يصدنكم»: ağır te'kîd nûnuna bitiştiği için fetha üzere mebnî muzâri fiildir ve «لا» sebebiyle cezm mahallindedir. Kâf mef'ûlün bihtir. «الشيطان»: fâildir. «إنه لكم عدو مبين» cümlesi ta'lîliyyedir (sebep bildirir); i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* Fevâid:
Bu âyet —«ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدّون»— hakkında tarihçilerin rivayet ettiği hoş kıssalardan biri şudur: Rivayet ettiklerine göre Resûlullah (s.a.v.) Kureyş'e «إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم» (Siz ve Allah'tan başka taptıklarınız cehennemin yakıtısınız) âyetini okuyunca, buna son derece içerlediler. Abdullah b. ez-Ziba'râ: «Ey Muhammed! Bu sadece bize ve ilâhlarımıza mı mahsus, yoksa bütün ümmetlere mi?» dedi. O (a.s.): «O, size ve bütün ümmetleredir» buyurdu. (İbnü'z-Ziba'râ) dedi ki: «Kâbe'nin Rabbine yemin olsun ki seni hücceten yendim! Hristiyanlar Mesîh'e, Yahudiler Üzeyr'e, Benû Melîh de meleklere tapmıyorlar mı? Eğer bunlar cehennemde ise, biz de kendimizin ve ilâhlarımızın onlarla beraber olmasına razıyız.» Bunun üzerine sevindiler, güldüler ve sesleri yükseldi. İşte Allah Teâlâ'nın «إذا قومك منه يصدون» kavli budur. Allah Teâlâ onların bu inatçı karşı koyuşlarını, bununla ancak putları kastettiğini, peygamberleri ve melekleri kastetmediğini bildirerek çürüttü. Ancak İbnü'z-Ziba'râ, Resûlullah'ın sözünün lafzının umum (genellik) ihtimali taşıdığını görünce —bununla sadece onların putlarının kastedildiğini bildiği hâlde— hileye bir yol buldu ve sözün manasını kılı kırk yaran bir inat ve münakaşa yoluyla şümul ve kuşatıcılığa çevirdi. Resûlullah ona cevap vermekten vakarla kaçındı; nihayet Rabbi onun adına «إن الذين سبقت لهم منّا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون» (Kendileri için tarafımızdan güzellik takdir edilmiş olanlar ise oradan uzaklaştırılmışlardır) kavliyle cevap verdi ve bununla âyetin putlara mahsus olduğuna delâlet etti. Kıssanın özeti budur. Şuna da dikkat çekmek gerekir: Abdullah b. ez-Ziba'râ meşhur bir sahâbî ve tanınmış bir şairdir; Müslüman olmuş ve Müslümanlığı güzel olmuştur. Bu kıssa, sahih olduğu takdirde, onun Müslüman olmasından önceydi. «الزبعرى» kelimesi zâ'nın kesresi, bâ'nın fethası, ayn'ın sükûnu, fethalı râ ve elif-i maksûre iledir; lügatte manası «huyu kötü» demektir.

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلًا إِذا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain another kind of their obstinacy and persistence in stubborn arrogance. لما is temporal or a connective; ضرب is a passive past verb; ابن مريم is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); and مثلا is a second direct object, because ضرب has been given the sense of جعل ("made"); it may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "he was mentioned as an example". إذا is the particle of surprise, discussed above; قومك is a subject (mubtadaʾ); منه are both attached to يصدون; and the clause يصدون is the predicate of قومك. It is read with kasra on the ṣād, that is, a clamour and uproar rose from them out of joy, delight and laughter at what they heard (the story will come in the section on benefits). It was also read يصدون with ḍamma, from ṣudūd, meaning turning away; and it is said that they are two dialects. (وَقالُوا أَآلِهَتُنا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هُوَ) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and an agent; the hamza is for interrogation; آلهتنا is a subject; خير is the predicate; أم is a conjunction and is connected (muttaṣila); and هو is conjoined to آلهتنا. (ما ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلًا بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ خَصِمُونَ) ما is negative; ضربوه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; لك are both attached to ضربوه; إلا is a particle of restriction; جدلا is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), that is, for the sake of disputation, wrangling and obstinacy, not to show the truth; it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "not disputing"; بل is a particle of rectification; هم is a subject; قوم is the predicate; and خصمون is an adjective of قوم. (إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنا عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلًا لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) إن is negative; هو is a subject; إلا is a particle of restriction; عبد is the predicate of هو; the clause أنعمنا is an adjective of عبد; عليه are both attached to أنعمنا; جعلناه is conjoined to أنعمنا; مثلا is the second direct object of جعلناه; and لبني إسرائيل is an adjective of مثلا. (وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ مَلائِكَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لو is conditional; نشاء is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its agent latent, its implied form being "We"; the lām occurs in the answer of لولا «[Translator's note: the source reads «لولا» where «لو» is evidently meant]»; جعلنا is a verb and an agent; منكم is in the position of the second direct object if جعلنا means "We made", and if it means "We created", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلنا; في الأرض are both attached to يخلفون; and the clause يخلفون is an adjective of ملائكة. Some grammarians said: «من is for substitution, that is, "We would have made angels in your place", and they counted among that the saying of the Exalted «أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة», that is, in place of the hereafter, and the poet's verse:
أخذوا المخاض من الفصيل غلبة ... ظلما ويكتب للأمير أقالا
(They took the pregnant she-camels in place of the weanling by force, unjustly, and «أقالا» is written for the emir.) [Translator's note: the final word «أقالا» is printed so in the source and its sense is unclear; «أفيلا» (a young camel) may be meant.]
that is, in place of the weanling. But it is better that it is partitive, as we mentioned in the i'rab.» «[Translator's note: the source reads «في الإعراض» (in the turning away) where «في الإعراب» (in the i'rab) is evidently meant, and the opening quotation mark before «من تكون للبدل» is never closed in the source.]» (وَإِنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسَّاعَةِ فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِها) The wāw is a conjunction; إن with its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); علم is the predicate of إنه; and للساعة is an adjective of علم, that is, a condition (sharṭ) among its portents by which it is known, so the portent was named "knowledge" because knowledge is obtained through it. The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference (al-faṣīḥa); لا is prohibitive; تمترن is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. المرية means doubt. (وَاتَّبِعُونِ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; اتبعوني is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; the nūn is the protective nūn; the yāʾ, omitted in writing to follow the practice of the codex, is a direct object; هذا is a subject; صراط is the predicate; and مستقيم is an adjective. (وَلا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; يصدنكم is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of the jussive by لا; the kāf is a direct object; الشيطان is the agent; and the clause إنه لكم عدو مبين is causal and has no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
Among the delightful stories that historians relate concerning this verse «ولما ضرب ابن مريم مثلا إذا قومك منه يصدّون»: they mention that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to Quraysh «إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم» ("you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell"), they were intensely resentful of that, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: "O Muḥammad, is this for us and our gods in particular, or for all the nations?" He, peace be upon him, said: "It is for you and for all the nations." He said: "By the Lord of the Kaʿba, I have bested you! Do the Christians not worship the Messiah, and the Jews worship ʿUzayr, and the Banū Mulayḥ worship the angels? If these are in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be with them." So they rejoiced and laughed and their voices rose, and that is the saying of the Exalted: «إذا قومك منه يصدون». Allah refuted their stubbornness, saying that He meant only the idols by it and did not mean the prophets and the angels. But when Ibn al-Zibaʿrā saw that the words of the Messenger of Allah could, in their wording, bear a general sense, while he knew that what was meant was their idols and nothing else, he found a loophole for a trick, so he turned its meaning to inclusiveness and comprehensiveness by way of quibbling and obstinacy. The Messenger of Allah held himself in dignified restraint from answering him, until his Lord answered for him with His saying: «إن الذين سبقت لهم منّا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون» ("Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it"), thereby showing that the verse is specific to the idols. This is the gist of the story. It must be noted that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā was a well-known Companion and a famous poet; he accepted Islam and his Islam was good, and this story, supposing it sound, was before his conversion. Al-Zibaʿrā, with kasra on the zāy, fatḥa on the bāʾ, sukūn on the ʿayn and a fatḥa on the rāʾ with a short alif, means in the language "the ill-natured".

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَ عِيسى بِالْبَيِّناتِ قالَ: قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِالْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain the intransigence of the Children of Israel. لما is a connective or temporal; جاء عيسى is a past verb and an agent; بالبينات are both attached to جاء; the clause قال has no grammatical position; and the clause قد جئتكم بالحكمة is the content of what was said. ولأبين: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of causation; أبين is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن, optionally so, after the lām of causation; and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to بالحكمة. The wording of al-Shihāb: «His saying ولأبين لكم is attached to an implied element, that is, "and I have come to you in order to make clear"; the conjunction was not left out so that it might attach to what precedes it, to signal concern for the reason, so that it was made as though it were a speech by itself.» لكم are both attached to أبين; بعض الذي is a direct object of أبين; the clause تختلفون is a ṣila (relative clause); and فيه are both attached to تختلفون. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) You may take the fāʾ as a conjunction, so that the speech is conjoined to what precedes it as a completion of the speech of ʿĪsā, and you may take it as resumptive, so that the speech is a fresh speech from Allah, pointing to the way of obedience and its clear highway. اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; أطيعون is conjoined to فاتقوا, and the yāʾ, omitted to observe the writing of the codex, is a direct object. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) The clause is an explanation of the preceding «وأطيعون»; إن with its noun; هو is a subject; ربي is the predicate; the clause is the predicate of inna; ربكم is conjoined to ربي; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference (al-faṣīḥa); اعبدوه is a verb, an agent and a direct object; هذا is a subject; صراط is the predicate; and مستقيم is an adjective. (فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; اختلف الأحزاب is a verb and an agent; and من بينهم is a ḥāl from الأحزاب. (فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ويل is a subject, and it has already been said that it is a word of punishment, and that is why it is permissible to begin with it; للذين is its predicate; and من عذاب يوم أليم is a second predicate or a ḥāl, that is, "being of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection".

* Vocabulary:
(أَبْرَمُوا) They made firm. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «abramtu al-ʿaqd ibrāman: I made the contract firm, and it became firm (inbarama); and abramtu al-shayʾ: I planned the thing.» One says abrama al-ḥabl when he has twisted it tightly, and what is meant is the second twisting; as for the first, it is called saḥl. In al-Qāmūs: al-saḥl is a cloth whose yarn is not twisted tight, like al-saḥīl. Zuhayr said, praising Harim ibn Sinān and al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAwf:
يمينا لنعم السيدان وجدتما ... على كل حال من سحيل ومبرم
(I swear, you two were found excellent chiefs in every condition, whether loosely or tightly twisted.)

* I'rab:
(أَمْ أَبْرَمُوا أَمْراً فَإِنَّا مُبْرِمُونَ) A resumptive speech, introduced to direct blame at the polytheists for what came from them. أم is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) with the meaning of بل, so بل is for rectification and for moving from the rebuke of the people of the Fire and the account of their state to the account of the offence of these polytheists; the hamza is for denial; أبرموا is a past verb and an agent; أمرا is a direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction; and إن with its noun and predicate. (أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ؟) أم has been discussed already; يحسبون is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is the agent; أن and what follows it fill the place of the two objects of تحسبون; the clause لا نسمع is the predicate of أنّا; سرهم is the object of نسمع; and نجواهم is conjoined to سرهم. (بَلى وَرُسُلُنا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ) بلى is a particle of response, that is, "We do hear that"; the wāw is circumstantial; رسلنا is a subject; لديهم is an adverbial attached to يكتبون; and the clause يكتبون is the predicate of رسلنا, and the sentence is circumstantial. (قُلْ إِنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمنِ وَلَدٌ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الْعابِدِينَ) قل is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and the sentence is resumptive, introduced to refute their claims, mentioned at the beginning of the sura, that Allah has a child from among the angels; إن is conditional; كان is a defective past verb; للرحمن is its fronted predicate; ولد is its postponed noun; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أنا is a subject; and أول العابدين is the predicate. The meaning of making worship depend on the existence of a child will come in the section on benefits. (سُبْحانَ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ) سبحان is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; رب السموات والأرض is its muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); رب العرش is a substitute (badal) for the first رب; عما are both attached to سبحان; and the clause يصفون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا حَتَّى يُلاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference; ذرهم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; يخوضوا is the answer to a request, and for that reason it is jussive; يلعبوا is conjoined to يخوضوا; حتى is a particle of limit and governing the genitive; يلاقوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى, and the wāw is the agent; يومهم is a direct object; الذي is an adjective; the clause يوعدون is a ṣila; and يوعدون is a passive imperfect, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّماءِ إِلهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلهٌ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ) The wāw is resumptive; هو is a subject; الذي is its predicate; في السماء are both attached to إله, because it has the meaning "one who is worshipped". Al-Zamakhsharī gave as an example of it their saying "he is Ḥātim of Ṭayy, Ḥātim among Taghlib", on the implication of the meaning of "the generous one" for which he is famous, as if you said "he is generous in Ṭayy, generous among Taghlib". إله is the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being "He", and the sentence is the ṣila of الذي; وفي الأرض إله is conjoined to His saying في السماء إله; هو is a subject; and الحكيم العليم are two predicates.
