(وَتَبارَكَ الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما) The wāw is a conjunction; تبارك is a past verb; الذي is its agent; له is a fronted predicate; ملك السموات is a postponed subject; the sentence is a ṣila; ما is conjoined to السموات والأرض; and the adverbial is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. (وَعِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; عنده is an adverbial attached to an omitted fronted predicate; علم الساعة is a postponed subject; إليه are both attached to ترجعون; and ترجعون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَلا يَمْلِكُ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ الشَّفاعَةَ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يملك is an imperfect verb; الذين is its agent; the clause يدعون is the ṣila of the relative noun; من دونه are both attached to يدعون; and الشفاعة is the object of يملك. (إِلَّا مَنْ شَهِدَ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ) إلا is a particle of restriction; من is excepted from الذين, and this is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the meaning is: and their gods, meaning by them the idols and the images, do not possess intercession, as they claimed that they are their intercessors with Allah; but whoever bears witness to the truth, which is the oneness of Allah, and knows what he bears witness to, is the one who possesses intercession. The exception may be connected (muttaṣil), since the excepted-from would be omitted, as if He had said "and those whom they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession for anyone except for those who bear witness to the truth", so it is an exception from the omitted object, in line with the poet's saying:
نجا سالم والنفس منه بشدقه ... ولم ينج إلا جفن سيف ومئزر
(Sālim escaped with his life in his jaws, and nothing escaped but a sword-sheath and a loincloth.)
So it is an exception from those interceded for. The clause شهد بالحق is the ṣila of من; وهم: the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; هم is a subject; and the clause يعلمون is the predicate. (وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ فَأَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the one that prepares for the oath; إن is conditional; سألتهم is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a subject; the clause خلقهم is the predicate of من; the interrogative clause, suspended, is in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of سألتهم; ليقولن: the lām is the answer to the oath, and the answer to the condition is omitted according to the well-known rule, namely when an oath and a condition coincide; يقولن is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the retention of the nūn, omitted because of the succession of similar letters, and the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; and الله is the agent of an omitted verb indicated by the relative of the interrogative, the implied form being "Allah created us", because the conditional proposition calls for neither occurrence nor non-occurrence. The evidence that the nominative is an agent of an omitted verb and not a subject is that it has come when there is no omission, as in His saying the Exalted mentioned above «ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولن خلقهنّ العزيز العليم»; although this argument may be countered by a like one, so it is said: the evidence that it is a subject is that it has come like that, as in His saying the Exalted «قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر» up to His saying «قل الله ينجيكم منها». And what is said, that it was fronted to give the sense of specification, is disallowed, because the agent may not be fronted before its governor according to the sounder view. It is best to say that the verbal argument in this chapter is more frequent, so it is better to carry it over onto that. Ibn Hishām said: «Some of them say, regarding ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله, that the name of Allah, glory be to Him the Exalted, is a subject or an agent, that is, «الله خلقهم» or «خلقهم الله»; the correct view is to carry it on the second, on the evidence of ولئن سألتهم من خلق السموات والأرض ليقولنّ خلقهنّ العزيز الحكيم.» Al-Damāmīnī, the commentator of al-Mughnī [Translator's note: the source has «شارع المغني»; «شارح المغني» is meant.], took him to task, saying: «This is contradicted by His saying the Exalted: قل من ينجيكم من ظلمات البر والبحر تدعونه, until he said: قل الله ينجيكم منها ومن كل كرب.» Al-Shumunnī in turn took him to task, saying: «I say: it does not contradict it, because the discussion concerns only the particular answer whose basis is creation, not every answer.»
The fāʾ is a conjunction; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف ("how"), in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and يؤفكون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the deputy agent. (وَقِيلِهِ يا رَبِّ إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ) The wāw is for the oath; قيله, that is, his saying, is genitive by the wāw of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; and the answer is either omitted, that is, "I shall surely do to them what I wish", or mentioned, and it is His saying إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون, as if it were said "and I swear by his saying: O my Lord". It is also said that it is conjoined to الساعة, but that is far-fetched. It was read in the accusative. Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī said: «Its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) of its implied verb. It is said that the accusative is by conjunction to سرهم ونجواهم. It is said that it is by conjunction to the position of الساعة, as if it were said "He knows the Hour and his saying". It was read in the nominative as a subject, with what follows it as the predicate, or the predicate is omitted, its implied form being "and his saying is heard" or "accepted".» إن with its noun and predicate; and the clause لا يؤمنون is an adjective. (فَاصْفَحْ عَنْهُمْ وَقُلْ سَلامٌ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent inference; اصفح is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; عنهم are both attached to اصفح; قل is conjoined to فاصفح; سلام is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is peace"; the fāʾ in فسوف is a conjunction; سوف is a particle of postponement; يعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; and the direct object is omitted for magnification, that is, "the outcome of their affair".

* Benefits:
We promised you the discussion of making worship depend on the existence of a child. A long dispute has arisen among the exegetes and the theologians about it, especially between the Sunnis and the Muʿtazila. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in his brilliant style, the following: «قل إن كان للرحمن ولد: and if that is sound and established by a valid proof that you bring and a clear argument that you put forward, then I am the first to venerate that child and the first of you to obey and submit to him, just as a man venerates the king's son out of veneration for his father. This is speech that comes by way of supposition and illustration for a purpose, which is exaggeration in denying a child and elaborating on it, so that the speaker leaves no doubt except that it dissolves, while reporting of himself his firm footing in the matter of tawḥīd. That is because He made worship depend on the existence of a child, which is impossible in itself, so what depends on it is impossible like it. In the form of affirming existence and worship, it is in meaning a denial of both, in the most eloquent and strongest manner.» Then he put forward a mockery of the Sunnis and gave rein to his tongue, offending against the Divine Essence, when he said: «And its like is for the ʿadlī (Muʿtazilī) to say to the Jabrī (determinist): "If Allah is the creator of disbelief in hearts and punishes for it with everlasting punishment, then I am the first to say He is a devil and not a god." So the meaning of this speech, and what its style and composition were set for, is the denial that Allah the Exalted is the creator of disbelief, and His exaltedness and sanctification above that, but by way of exaggeration in it in the manner we mentioned, with a pointing to the ugliness of the doctrine and the error of the one who holds it, a decisive testimony of its impossibility, a declaration from himself of his disavowal of it, and the utmost aversion and repugnance at committing it.»
Abū Ḥayyān drew attention to al-Zamakhsharī's offence, saying after quoting what we quoted from al-Zamakhsharī's words: «Then he mentioned words for which he deserves discipline, even the sword; I have kept my book free of mentioning them.» This is not a refutation, as you see, but a meeting of abuse with abuse and of excess with excess.
Imam Nāṣir al-Dīn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Munayyir al-Iskandarī al-Mālikī, judge of Alexandria, who died in the year 683 AH, replied to al-Zamakhsharī with a good reply, in which he followed the path of sound criticism. He said: «He has dared greatly and plunged into perdition in his illustration with the saying of the one he called an ʿadlī, "If Allah is the creator of disbelief in hearts and punishes for it, then I am the first of those who say He is a devil and not a god." Let such a person be requited for that by the saying of someone who says: it has been established by reason and by Revelation that He, the Exalted, is the creator of that in hearts as He created faith, in fulfilment of the requirement of the proof of reason indicating that there is no creator but Allah, and in affirmation of the content of His saying the Exalted «هل من خالق غير الله» and His saying «الله خالق كل شيء». If this premise is established by reason and by transmission, it follows that his ear should be rubbed and his neck shackled, for he deviates in matters of Allah with a deviation that none of His disbelieving servants preceded him in, and which no rebellious one of the wicked insurgents dared.» Up to the end of this reply, which was not free of abuse and insults either.
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: «People have strained in order to bring it out of this noble style, full of fine points and benefits that independently affirm tawḥīd in its most eloquent aspects. So it was said: "If the Merciful has a child, as you claim, then I am the first of the worshippers who affirm Allah's oneness and who deny their statement by ascribing a child to Him." And it was said: "If the Merciful has a child, I am the first of those who are disdainful (ānifīn) of His having a child", from ʿabida yaʿbadu when his nose swells (ashtadda anfuhu), so he is ʿabid and ʿābid.» And it was said: it is the negative إن, that is, "The Merciful has no child, and I am the first to say so, and to worship and affirm His oneness." Abū Ḥayyān refuted all these aspects at a length that the scope of this book cannot accommodate.
The wording of al-Shawkānī: «That is, if He has a child according to your statement and your claim, then I am the first to worship Allah alone, because whoever worships Allah alone has repelled the idea that He has a child. So said Ibn Qutayba. Al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī said: the meaning is "the Merciful has no child", and His saying فأنا أول العابدين is the beginning of a new statement. And it is said the meaning is:
"Say, O Muḥammad: if it is proved that Allah has a child, then I am the first to worship this child whose existence you claim, but it is impossible that He has a child." In it is a denial of a child in the most eloquent manner, the most complete expression and the finest style, and this is the apparent sense of the Qur'anic composition. Of this kind is His saying the Exalted: «وإنّا وإياكم لعلى هدى أو في ضلال مبين»; and like this is a man's saying to one he is debating: "If what you say is proved by evidence, then I am the first to believe it and say it." So إن is conditional. This is what we chose, and Ibn Jarīr and others preferred it. There are other sayings that we passed over, because they belong to strained and artificial interpretation, and it is not fitting for the noble Qur'an to bring them or hint at them, since the Qur'an does not bring the rare or the anomalous of the language.»

﴿وقيله يا رب﴾: Vâv kasem içindir. ﴿قيله﴾, yani ﴿قوله﴾, kasem vâvı ile mecrûrdur; câr ve mecrûr, takdiri «أقسم» olan mahzûf bir fiile mütealliktir. Cevap ya mahzûftur, yani: «لأفعلن بهم ما أريد»; ya da zikredilmiştir, o da onun şu sözüdür: ﴿إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون﴾; sanki «وأُقسم بقيله يا رب» denmiştir. ﴿إن﴾: nâsih harf. ﴿هؤلاء﴾: inne'nin ismi. ﴿قوم﴾: inne'nin haberi. ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ cümlesi «قوم»ün sıfatıdır (na't).

﴿وقيله يا رب﴾: the wāw is for the oath; «قيله», i.e. ﴿قوله﴾ (his saying), is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» (I swear); the answer [of the oath] is either omitted, i.e. «لأفعلن بهم ما أريد» (I shall surely do with them what I will), or stated, namely his saying ﴿إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون﴾: as though it were said: «وأُقسم بقيله يا رب» (and I swear by his saying "O my Lord"); «إن»: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); «هؤلاء»: the noun of «إن»; «قوم»: the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم».

Müellifin sözü: {رَهْواً}: «تَرَكَ» «صَيَّر» (kıldı) anlamında olduğu takdirde ikinci mef'ûl olması câizdir; o anlamda olmadığı takdirde hâl olması câizdir. «الرَّهْو»un «durgunluk» olduğu söylenmiştir; buna göre mânâ «onu durgun bırak»tır. «رَهَا يَرْهُوا رَهْواً» denir. «Atlar sakin sakin geldi» (جاءَتِ الخيلُ رَهْواً) sözü de bundandır. Nâbiğa şöyle demiştir:
4014 - والخيلَ تَمْزَعُ رَهْواً في أَعِنَّتِها ... كالطيرِ تَنْجُوْ مِنَ الشُّؤْبوب ذي البَرَدِ
(Atlar dizginlerinde sakin sakin koşuyor; dolu yağan yağmur bulutundan kurtulan kuşlar gibi.)
«رَهَا يَرْهُو» yürüyüşünde yumuşak davrandı demektir. Kutâmî şöyle demiştir:
4015 - يَمْشِيْنَ رَهْواً فلا الأَعْجازُ خاذِلَةٌ ... ولا الصدورُ على الأعجازِ تَتَّكِلُ
(Sakin sakin yürürler; ne sağrılar geri kalır ne de göğüsler sağrılara yaslanır.)
Ebû Ubeyde'den: «رَهْواً» yani «onu, bıraktığın gibi aralıklarla açık bırak».
Tefsirde şöyle geçer: Deniz Mûsâ için yarılıp o çıkınca, Firavun'un arkasından gelmesinden korktu ve denize vurmak istedi ki eski haline dönsün de onlar kendisine yetişemesin. Bunun üzerine denizi aralıklı bırakması emredildi. Kelimenin aslı şu sözden gelir: / «رَها الرجلُ يَرْهُو رَهْواً»; adam iki bacağının arasını açtı. «الرَّهْو» ve «الرَّهْوَة», yüksek ve alçak olup içinde (su) toplanan yerdir; dolayısıyla zıt anlamlı kelimelerdendir (ezdâd). «الرَّهْوَة» ayrıca edep yerinin geniş olduğu kadındır. «الرَّهْو» bir kuş olup turna (الكُرْكِيّ) olduğu söylenir. {كَمْ تَرَكُواْ مِن جَنَّاتٍ} benzeri üzerine söz, Şuarâ sûresinde geçmişti.

Müellifin sözü: {كالمهل}: ikinci bir haber olması câizdir; ayrıca mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olması da câizdir, yani «o, «المُهْل» gibidir». «طعام الأثيم»den hâl olması ise câiz değildir. Ebü'l-Bekâ şöyle demiştir: «Çünkü o durumda amil yoktur.» Bunda bir bakış vardır (itiraz edilebilir); zira hâl olması câizdir ve onda amil teşbih mânâsıdır, «Zeyd senin kardeşindir, cesur olarak» demen gibi.
«الأَثيم» mübalağa sıfatıdır. «الأَثُوم» da denir, «الصَّبور» ve «الشَّكور» gibi. «المُهْل»: zeytinyağının tortusu olduğu söylenmiştir. Katran tortusu olduğu söylenmiştir. Eritilmiş altın ya da gümüş olduğu söylenmiştir. Bu ikisinden ve anlamca onlara benzeyen, dövülerek şekil verilen her şeyden — demir, bakır ve kurşun gibi — eritilmiş olan olduğu da söylenmiştir. «المَهْل», fetha ile, ağırbaşlılık ve yumuşaklıktır. {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين} [et-Târık: 17] da bundandır. Hasan «كالمَهْل»i yalnızca mîm'in fethasıyla okumuştur; bu, zammeli «المُهْل»de bir lehçedir.
Müellifin sözü: «يَغْلي»: İbn Kesîr ve Hafs, alttan iki noktalı yâ ile okumuştur. Fâil, «طعام»a dönen bir zamirdir. Ebü'l-Bekâ onun «الزَّقُّوم»a dönmesini de câiz görmüştür. «المُهْل»in kendisine döndüğü de söylenmiştir; bu durumda «يَغْلي», câr ve mecrûrdaki müstetir zamirden hâldir; yani «erimiş madene benzeyerek kaynayan». «المُهْل»in kendisinden hâl olması da câizdir. Ebü'l-Bekâ onun mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olmasını da câiz görmüştür; yani «o kaynar», yani Zakkûm ya da yiyecek. Diğerleri üstten iki noktalı tâ ile «تَغْلي» okumuşlardır; fâil ağacın zamiridir ve cümle ikinci haberdir, bir görüşe göre hâldir, ya da mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberidir; yani «o kaynar».

His saying: {كالمهل}: it may be a second khabar, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is like the muhl." It is not permitted to be a ḥāl from «طعام الأثيم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because there is then no operator." There is something to consider here, because it is permissible for it to be a ḥāl, with the operator in it being the sense of comparison, as in your saying "Zayd is your brother, courageous."
الأَثيم is an intensive adjective. One also says الأَثُوم, like الصَّبور and الشَّكور. As for المُهْل: it is said to be the dregs of oil. It is said to be the sediment of tar. It is said to be what is melted of gold or silver. And it is said to be what is melted of them and of everything similar among the malleable metals, such as iron, copper and lead. المَهْل with fatḥa means calm and gentleness. From it comes {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين} [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. al-Ḥasan read «كالمَهْل» with fatḥa on the mīm only, which is a dialectal form of المُهْل with ḍamma.
His saying: «يَغْلي»: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read it with yāʾ (below). The agent is a pronoun referring back to the food (ṭaʿām). Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to refer to the zaqqūm. It is said it refers to the muhl itself, and «يَغْلي» is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition-phrase, i.e. "resembling the muhl, boiling." It may be a ḥāl from the muhl itself. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils," meaning the zaqqūm or the food. The rest read «تَغْلي» with tāʾ (above), the agent being a pronoun for the tree; the clause is then a second khabar, or a ḥāl according to one opinion, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it boils."

Müellifin sözü: {فَضْلاً}: bu, mef'ûlün lieclihtir; Mekkî'nin «'يَدْعُون' in amel ettiği bir masdardır» demekle kastettiği de budur. Amilin «ووَقاهم» olduğu da söylenmiştir. «آمِنين» olduğu da söylenmiştir; bu ancak mef'ûlün lieclih oluşuna göre görünür. Bununla birlikte masdar olması da câizdir; çünkü «يَدْعُون» ve sonrası lütufta bulunma (tefaddul) bâbındandır; dolayısıyla amiliyle mânâda örtüşen bir masdardır. Ebü'l-Bekâ ise bunu takdir edilen bir fiille mansub kılmıştır; yani «bununla lütufta bulunduk, lütuf olarak», yani «tefaddul olarak».

* I'rab:
(كم) declarative (khabariyya), an allusive noun of number (kināya al-ʿadad), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من جنّات) tamyīz (specification); (فيها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فاكهين).
The clause «تركوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كانوا فيها فاكهين» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of نعمة.
28- (كذلك) attached to the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus [Note: Or attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), governed by the verb تركوا or by an omitted verb, its implied form being "أهلكناهم" or "أخرجناهم".. In that case the clause أورثناها is conjoined to the implied clause.]; (الواو) conjunction; (قوما) an accusative second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «(الأمر) كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «أورثناها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause.
29- (الفاء) conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (عليهم) attached to (بكت); (ما) "sufficing" (kāfiya) [Translator's note: so in the source; نافية "negative" is evidently meant.] in both places.
The clause «ما بكت عليهم السماء» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أورثناها.
The clause «ما كانوا منظرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to أورثناها.

* Morphology:
(29) بكت: it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, the lām of the word and the tāʾ of the feminine.. its pattern is فعت.

* Rhetoric:
Imaginative representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ».
For the state of their death, because of its severity and magnitude, is likened to the state of one over whom the sky and the great celestial bodies weep. It is also said: it is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya), in that the sky and the earth are likened to a human being and weeping is attributed to them.
When an eminent man died, the Arabs would say, in magnifying his death: the sky and the earth wept over him, the wind wept for him, and the like. The poet said, lamenting the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz:
الشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة ... تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا
(The sun has risen, not eclipsed; the stars of the night and the moon weep over you.)

* Benefits:
- In this verse occurs (كم) al-khabariyya (the declarative كم). We have spoken in detail about the interrogative كم and the declarative كم in Sūrat al-Zukhruf, verse (6), so refer back to it.

* I'rab:
(في مقام) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of إنّ; (في جنّات) a badal (substitute) of مقام with the preposition repeated; (من سندس) attached to (يلبسون).
The clause «إنّ المتّقين في مقام ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يلبسون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (إنّ).].
54- (كذلك) attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: the matter is thus; (الواو) conjunction; (بحور) attached to (زوّجناهم).
The clause «الأمر كذلك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «زوّجناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause يلبسون.
55- (فيها) attached to (يدعون); (بكلّ) attached to (يدعون) by its being made to carry the meaning of يرغبون "they desire" (taḍmīn); (آمنين) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يدعون.
The clause «يدعون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the third-person pronoun in (زوّجناهم).
56- 57- (لا) negative; (فيها) attached to (يذوقون); (إلّا) for exception; (الموتة) excepted, accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: Some said the exception is connected (muttaṣil), the interpretation being: the believer, at his death in this world, is as though in his place in Paradise, because of what he is given of it or because of what he becomes certain of regarding its bliss (Ḥāshiyat al-Jamal).]; (الواو) conjunction; (فضلا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it coincides with it in derivation, i.e. as a favour [Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) governed by وقاهم or يدعون.]; (من ربّك) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (فضلا); (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl).
The clause «لا يذوقون ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the fāʿil in (يدعون) or of the pronoun in (آمنين).
The clause «وقاهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause زوّجناهم, taking account of the iltifāt (shift of person).
The clause «ذلك ... الفوز» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(54) حور: plural of حوراء, feminine of أحور, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from حور يحور of the fariḥa class, i.e. the black of the eye became intense and its white became intense; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
Implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ».
أمين is from الأمن (security), which is the opposite of betrayal [Translator's note: the source says الأمن; الأمانة (trustworthiness) is evidently meant]; the place is described by it by way of metaphor, as though a fearful place betrays its occupant because of the hardships he meets in it.

* Vocabulary:
(فَتَنَّا): "We tried and tested", that is, We dealt with them as one who tests does, wishing to know the reality of a thing. That test consisted in increasing their provision and giving them power in the land, whereupon they became corrupt, persisted in error, and rode the back of misguidance.
(رَهْواً): al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "There are two views on rahw. The first is that it means 'calm'. al-Aʿshā said:
يمشين رهوا فلا الأعجاز خاذلة ... ولا الصدور على الأعجاز تتكل
(They walk calmly: neither do the hindquarters lag behind, nor do the forequarters lean upon the hindquarters.)
that is, a calm walk, at ease. When Moses crossed the sea he wanted to strike it with his staff so that it would close up, just as he had struck it and it had parted; so he was commanded to leave it calm, at ease, fixed in its state, with the water standing upright and the road dry, neither striking it with his staff nor changing anything of it, so that the Copts might enter it, and when they were inside, Allah would close it over them. The second view is that rahw is a wide gap. It is related of one of the Arabs that he saw a camel with a wide gap between its humps and said: 'Glory be to Allah, a rahw between two humps!', that is, leave it as it is, parted." So in origin it is a verbal noun of rahā yarhū rahwan, like ʿadā yaʿdū ʿadwan, either in the sense of "became calm" or in the sense of "parted and opened up". In al-Mukhtār: "rahā between his legs means he opened them wide, and its class is that of ʿadā; and rahā al-baḥr means the sea became calm, also of the class of ʿadā."
(فاكِهِينَ): "of good cheer", or "possessors of fruit", like "possessor of milk" (labin) and "possessor of dates" (tāmir). This form has already occurred. The wording of al-Qāmūs is: "al-fākiha is all fruit; al-fākihānī is its seller; and, on the pattern of khajil (fakih), it means one who eats it; al-fākih is its owner; fakkahahum tafkīhan means he gave them a delicacy of it; the noun is al-fukayha, and al-fukāha with ḍamma; and fakiha, like fariḥa, fakahan, so he is fakih or fākih: good of spirit, laughing, or one who talks with his companions and makes them laugh."

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَجاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to begin setting forth examples for them from the peoples who came before them. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; فتنا is a past verb and agent; قبلهم is an adverbial attached to فتنا; قوم فرعون is the direct object. وجاءهم: the wāw is a conjunction; جاءهم is a past verb with a fronted direct object; رسول is the agent; كريم is an adjective.
(أَنْ أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ): أن may be explicative, because the coming of messengers contains the sense of speech; it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it with what follows is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to جاءهم; and it may be the lightened form of the heavy أنّ, its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with the clause أدّوا إليّ as its predicate. عباد الله is a vocative, a genitive construct from which the vocative particle has been omitted, so that "servants of Allah" would mean the Copts. al-Zamakhsharī preferred that عباد الله be a direct object, and that they are the Children of Israel, the meaning being "hand them over to me and send them with me". This is supported by what occurs in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: «فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنّا رسول رب العالمين أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل». إن and its noun; ولكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; رسول is the predicate of إنّي; أمين is an adjective.
(وَأَنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; وأن is conjoined to the first أن, and the same possibilities apply to it as to the first; لا is prohibitive; تعلو is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn; على الله is attached to تعلوا; إن and its noun, with the clause آتيكم as its predicate; بسلطان is attached to آتيكم; مبين is an adjective. The clause gives the reason for the prohibition and has no grammatical position.
(وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ): the wāw is a conjunction on بربي; إن and its noun, with the clause عذت as its predicate; بربي is attached to عذت; وربكم is conjoined to بربي; أن and what follows is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to عذت, that is, "from your stoning me"; the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the direct object of ترجمون.
(وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي فَاعْتَزِلُونِ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; تؤمنوا is the protasis; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; the clause اعتزلون is in the position of jussive as apodosis. The clause is joined with the fāʾ necessarily because it is a request (ṭalab). The yāʾ is likewise not written, because this is one of the "added" verses (āyāt al-zawāʾid).
(فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to an implied element which al-Jalāl implied by his words "so they did not leave him alone"; دعا ربه is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; أنّ and what follows is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "that these..."; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دعا; أن with its noun and predicate; مجرمون is an adjective of قوم.
(فَأَسْرِ بِعِبادِي لَيْلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa), which occurs as the answer to an implied condition, as if He had said: "If the matter is as you say, then travel by night"; بعبادي is attached to أسر; ليلا is an adverb of time, also attached to أسر; إن with its noun and predicate; the clause gives the reason for the command to travel by night (al-isrāʾ), which is travelling at night.
(وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْواً إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ مُغْرَقُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; اترك is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; رهوا is a ḥāl or a second direct object of اترك; إن with its noun and predicate; the clause gives the reason for the command to leave it.
(كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ): the speech is linked to an implied element which is indispensable for the coherence of the discourse; the implied form is "so Moses was reassured by that, and their drowning was completed". كم is the predicative (khabariyya) kam, in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object of تركوا; من جنات وعيون is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
(وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ): conjoined to جنات وعيون. By "noble station" (al-maqām al-karīm) are meant their crowded assemblies which they used to hold, and their pleasant gatherings in which they used to congregate.
(وَنَعْمَةٍ كانُوا فِيها فاكِهِينَ): also conjoined; it is an instance of conjoining the general to the particular, because "bounty" (niʿma) does not include everything mentioned before, nor other things not mentioned. The clause كانوا is an adjective of نعمة; فيها is attached to فاكهين; فاكهين is the predicate of كانوا.
(كَذلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْناها قَوْماً آخَرِينَ): كذلك is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is thus". al-Zamakhsharī said: "The kāf is accusative, meaning 'in the manner of that expulsion We expelled them from it'", so in his view it is in the position of absolute object. Abu al-Baqāʾ said (it means) "an abandoning like that", making it an adjective of the omitted "abandoning". The wāw is a conjunction; أورثناها is a verb, agent and direct object, the clause being conjoined to كم تركوا; قوما is a second direct object; آخرين is an adjective of قوما.
(فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ وَما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to the implied clause "they were drowned"; بكت عليهم السماء والأرض is a verb and agent; ما is negative; وكانوا منظرين is kāna with its noun and predicate.

* Rhetoric:
The meaning of "the heaven and the earth wept for them": in His words «فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض» there is an implicit imaginative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya takhyīliyya). The heaven and the earth are likened to one of whom concern can properly be expected; then the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi), namely the one of whom concern can properly be expected, is omitted, and one of its attributes, weeping, is borrowed for it. The meaning is that they did no righteous deed that would be cut off by their destruction so that the earth would weep for its cessation, nor did any such righteous deed ascend to the heaven so that it would weep after their destruction. Some made it a free metaphor (majāz mursal) for concern at the perishing of the one who perishes, the relation being causal: the effect is mentioned and the cause intended, since that concern is a cause which ordinarily leads to remaining.
Abū Ḥayyān said: «فما بكت عليهم السماء والأرض» is a metaphor expressing contempt for their affair, and that nothing changed at their destruction. In magnification it is said: "the heaven and the earth wept for him", "the wind wept for him", "the sun was darkened for him". Zayd ibn Mufazziʿ said [Translator's note: the source has «زيد بن مفزع»; the known poet is Zayd ibn Mufarrigh]:
الريح تبكي شجوها ... والبرق يلمع في غمامه
(The wind weeps for its sorrow, while the lightning flashes in its cloud.)
And Jarir said:
فالشمس طالعة ليست بكاسفة ... تبكي عليك نجوم الليل والقمرا
(The sun is rising, yet it is not eclipsed; the stars of the night and the moon weep for you.)
We cannot avoid taking up Jarir's verse for explanation and parsing, for it has occupied the critics greatly. It belongs to a poem in which he laments ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and before it come:
نعى النعاة أمير المؤمنين لنا ... يا خير من حج بيت الله واعتمرا
(The announcers of death announced to us the Commander of the Faithful: O best of those who made pilgrimage and ʿumra to the House of Allah!)
حملت أمرا عظيما فاضطلعت به ... وقمت فيه بأمر الله يا عمرا
(You bore a great charge and were equal to it, and you carried it out by the command of Allah, O ʿUmar!)
Then: فالشمس طالعة (the verse). His words يا خير are a quotation of the announcers' speech, that is, "saying: O best..."; it is also possible that it is the poet's own speech, in which case it contains an iltifāt (shift of address). al-Naʿy is the proclamation of a death. The "great charge" is the caliphate with its hardships and burdens, which he likens to a tangible load that is carried, by way of the implicit metaphor, the "bearing" being the imaginative element of the metaphor. "The command of Allah" is His law. On this verse there are several opinions. Among them: that it contains a transposition (taqdīm and taʾkhīr), and that نجوم الليل and القمر are accusative by كاسفة and not by تبكي, its arrangement being "the sun is not eclipsing the stars of the night nor the moon; it weeps for you". If it is not eclipsing the other heavenly bodies, it is not shining, so it is black and dark, and all the time is night; and this is the utmost that exaggeration in elegies can reach, and among the finest that has been said in lamentation. طالعة is the predicate of الشمس; وليست بكاسفة is a second predicate; تبكي عليك is a ḥāl or a third predicate; نجوم الليل is the object of كاسفة, that is, the sun does not eclipse the stars of the night, because it has been obliterated and its light is feeble from the abundance of its weeping, so it cannot prevent the stars from appearing. It is also possible that نجوم الليل is the object of تبكي, that is, "she surpasses the stars of the night in weeping for you". It is said that its narration is thus a mistake, and that the narration is "the sun is eclipsed, not rising", that is, it will never rise from then on; the most likely view is that نجوم الليل is the object of تبكي. It is also said to be an adverbial of it, i.e. "for the duration of the stars of the night", etc. And it is said that نجوم is nominative as agent and القمر an object of accompaniment. The accusative of عمر is problematic, because it is a single proper noun and should have been indeclinable on ḍamma. There are several explanations. Among them: that he meant "O ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb" or "O ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz", the addressed genitive construct being accusative, and then he cut off the annexation because the metre ended. Among them: that he meant "yā ʿUmarā" as a lament (nudba) and dropped the final hāʾ, as was said of His words, Exalted: «يا أسفا على يوسف». Other things have been said, on which discussion would be long and unprofitable.

* Vocabulary:
(تُبَّعٍ): he is Tubbaʿ al-Ḥimyarī, who marched with armies, built al-Ḥīra and built Samarqand (or, it is said, destroyed it). He was a believer while his people were disbelievers, and for that reason Allah censured them and not him. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: "The apparent sense is that Tubbaʿ is a well-known person, and that a comparison of merit was made between his people and the people of the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, although the word tubbaʿ is applied to every one who ruled the Arabs, just as kisrā is applied to whoever ruled the Persians and qayṣar to whoever ruled the Romans. It is said that his name was Asʿad al-Ḥimyarī and that his kunya was Abū Karib. Abu Ḥātim al-Riyāshī mentioned that he believed in the Prophet ﷺ nine hundred years before he was sent. It is related that when he believed, in Medina, he wrote a letter and composed verse. As for the verse, it is:
شهدت على أحمد أنه ... رسول من الله باري النسم
(I bear witness concerning Aḥmad that he is a messenger from Allah, the Creator of souls;)
فلو مدّ عمري إلى عمره ... لكنت وزيرا له وابن عمّ
(and if my life were extended to his lifetime, I would be a minister to him and a cousin.)
As for the letter, Ibn Isḥāq and others related that in it was: 'To proceed: I have believed in you and in your Book which has been sent down to you, and I am upon your religion and your sunna. I have believed in your Lord and the Lord of everything, and in all that has come from your Lord of the laws of Islam. If I reach you, then excellent and blessed; and if I do not reach you, intercede for me and do not forget me on the Day of Resurrection, for I am of your earliest community and I followed you before your coming; I am upon your creed and the creed of your father Abraham, peace be upon him.' Then he sealed the letter and engraved on it 'To Allah belongs the command before and after', and wrote its address: 'To Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah, the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger, the Seal of the Prophets and the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, ﷺ, from Tubbaʿ the First.' It is said that the letter and the verse were with Abū Ayyūb Khālid ibn Zayd and remained with him until the Prophet ﷺ was sent. They used to inherit it, elder from elder, until they handed it to the Prophet ﷺ. A group said that by Tubbaʿ is not meant a single man; what is meant are the kings of Yemen, who were called the Tabābiʿa. al-Jawharī said: 'The Tabābiʿa are the kings of Yemen; and al-tubbaʿ is the shade; and al-tubbaʿ is the shade; and al-tubbaʿ is a kind of bird [Translator's note: the source repeats «والتبع الظل» twice].' And the wording of al-Zamakhsharī: 'The kings of Yemen were called the Tabābiʿa because they follow (yatbaʿūn), just as they were called the Aqyāl because they take the midday rest (yataqayyalūn).'" And in Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: al-taqyīl is drinking at midday. The shade is called tubbaʿ because it follows the sun.
Now there were seventy Tubbaʿs among them. al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr al-Anṣārī said: لنا من بني قحطان سبعون تبعا ... أطاعت لنا بالخرج منّا الأعاجم
(Of the sons of Qaḥṭān we have seventy Tubbaʿs; the non-Arabs obeyed us, paying us tribute.)
ومنّا سراة الناس هود وصالح ... وذو الكفل منّا والملوك الأعاظم
(And of us are the noblest of men, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ; and Dhū al-Kifl is of us, and the mighty kings.)
It is also said they were eighty, which the verse did not allow him to say. The details of their reports are scattered through the bellies of the long history books, so let whoever is tempted to read enjoyable legends and their wondrous stories turn to them.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ نَجَّيْنا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْمُهِينِ): a resumptive sentence, introduced to console the Prophet ﷺ for what he was enduring from Quraysh and to cool his heart with the assurance that Allah is able to rescue him and his followers from their harm, as He rescued the Children of Israel from the Copts, a matter which, outwardly, seemed remote from happening.
The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; نجينا is a verb and agent; بني إسرائيل is the direct object; من العذاب is attached to نجينا; المهين is an adjective of العذاب.
(مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ كانَ عالِياً مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ): من فرعون is a substitute for «من العذاب» with repetition of the preposition, as though he himself were a humiliating torment, because of the torment and humiliation they suffered from him. It is also said that it is attached to an omitted ḥāl of العذاب, that is, "being from, or issuing from, Pharaoh". إن and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; عاليا is its predicate; من المسرفين is a second predicate of كان. The clause of إن and what follows has no position, because it is explanatory of the reason.
(وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ عَلى عِلْمٍ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of certainty; اخترناهم is a verb, agent and direct object; على علم is attached to an omitted ḥāl; على here means "with", that is, "with Our knowledge that they would deviate and commit lapses"; على العالمين is attached to اخترناهم, or (it is so) because of the many prophets among them.
(وَآتَيْناهُمْ مِنَ الْآياتِ ما فِيهِ بَلؤُا مُبِينٌ): conjoined to what precedes; آتيناهم is a verb, agent and object; من الآيات is a fronted ḥāl; ما is a second direct object of آتيناهم; فيه is a fronted predicate; بلاء is a postponed subject; مبين is an adjective of بلاء; and the sentence is the ṣila of the relative.
(إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ): إن and its noun; the shifted lām; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the clause is the predicate of إن. The clause «إن هؤلاء» is resumptive, introduced to speak of Quraysh after the digression about the Children of Israel.
(إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولى وَما نَحْنُ بِمُنْشَرِينَ): إن is negative; هي is the subject; إلا is a particle of restriction; موتتنا is the predicate of هي; الأولى is an adjective. The meaning of "the first death" will come in the section of Benefits. The wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Hijazi negative; نحن is its noun; بمنشرين: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and منشرين is its predicate, accusative in position and genitive in form.
(فَأْتُوا بِآبائِنا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you are truthful in what you say, then hasten for us the revival of those of our fathers who have died, so that it stands as proof for what you promise of the rising of the Hour and the resurrection of the dead".
(أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ أَهْلَكْناهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ): the hamza is of rebuking interrogation; هم is the subject and خير the predicate; أم is a conjunction; قوم تبع is conjoined to هم; الذين is conjoined to قوم تبع; من قبلهم is attached to an omitted ṣila of الذين; the clause أهلكناهم is a ḥāl of the conjoined and the one conjoined to, or resumptive with no position; إن and its noun, with the clause كانوا مجرمين as its predicate. By superiority (khayriyya) is meant excellence in strength and power in this world. The clause «إنهم كانوا مجرمين» is explanatory and has no position, since it gives the reason for their destruction.

* Benefits:
The meaning of "the first death" (al-mawta al-ūlā) is this. When they were promised, after the life of this world, two further states, the first of them death and the other the life of resurrection, they affirmed the first state, which is death, and denied what comes after it. They called it "first" although they believed that nothing comes after it, because they set their denial on the footing of the affirmation, and so made it "first" in accordance with what had been said to them. This is preferable to taking "the first death" as the one preceding the life of this world, for two reasons. The first: they would not believe in restricting themselves to that death, since they affirm the death that follows the life of this world; and to take the direct restriction to death in their speech as referring to an attribute that is mentioned, and not to the death they actually witness, is a departure from the apparent sense without need. The second: the death that precedes the life of this world is not expressed by mawta, for mawta is of the form fiʿla, which suggests renewal and occurrence, whereas the death preceding the life of this world is a continuing state not preceded by a life that it came upon; besides, in the remainder of the sūra is His word, Exalted: «لا يذوقون فيها الموت إلا الموتة الأولى», and what is meant by "the first death" here is only the death that follows the life of this world.

* Lügat:
(مَوْلًى): el-Muhtâr'da şöyle denir: «المولى: azat eden (veya azatlı), amcaoğlu, yardımcı, komşu ve antlaşmalı müttefik.»
(شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ): Bu konudaki söz Sâffât sûresinde geçti; oraya dön.
(المهل): Gümüş ve demir gibi madenlerin cevherlerini toplayan bir isimdir; bakırın erimiş olanı, ince (akıcı) katran, ince yağ, zehir, irin veya özellikle ölünün kanlı irini, ekmekten dökülen kül de (böyle adlandırılır). Mîm'in zammesiyledir; mîm'in fethasını da caiz görmüşlerdir; çünkü onda az kullanılan bir lügat işitmişlerdir. «المهل» fetha ile ise ağır davranma ve yumuşaklık demektir.
(الْحَمِيمِ): Çok sıcak su.
(فَاعْتِلُوهُ): Yani onu sertlik ve kabalıkla sürükleyin. «العتل», adamın yakasından tutulup hapse veya ölüme sürüklenmesidir. «العتل» —kaba, katı kimse— de buradan gelir. el-Muhtâr'da şöyle denir: «عتل الرجل: adamı şiddetle çekti; babı ضرب ve نصر'dir.» Dolayısıyla ücretle yük taşıyan kimseye «العتّال» (hamal) denmesi doğrudur, onda hiçbir kusur yoktur; mesleğe de «العتالة» denir.

* İ'rab:
(وَما خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما لاعِبِينَ): Müste'nef bir sözdür; haşrin doğruluğunu ve vukuunu delillendirmek için sevk edilmiştir. Sözün ahenkli olması ve iki ucunun birleşmesi için onu öncesine atfetmen de mümkündür. «ما»: nefy harfi. «خلقنا السموات»: fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih. «ما»: «السموات والأرض»e ma'tûftur. «بينهما»: zarf; «ما»nın sılası olan mahzûf bir şeye müteallik. «لاعبين»: fâilden hâldir.
(ما خَلَقْناهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): Cümle öncesini tefsir edicidir. «ما»: nefy harfi. «خلقناهما»: fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bih. «إلا»: hasr edatı. «بالحق»: hâldir; yani akıllı kimse için bunda bir burhan olsun diye, bunda hak üzere olarak. Vâv hâliyyedir. «لكن»: istidrâk için fiile benzeyen harftir; «أكثرهم»: ismi; «لا يعلمون» cümlesi haberidir.
(إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ): «إن» ve ismi; «ميقاتهم»: haberi. «أجمعين»: zamirin te'kîdidir; yani bütün insanlar için.
(يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئاً وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ): «يوم»ün «يوم الفصل»den bedel olması da, «الفصل»in delâlet ettiği şeyin zarfı olması da caizdir; yani «hiçbir yakının fayda vermeyeceği gün aralarında ayırım yapılır». Bizzat «الفصل»e müteallik olmaz; çünkü ondan haber verilmiştir (haber verildikten sonra ma'mûl alamaz). «لا يغني» cümlesi, zarfın ona izâfe edilmesiyle cer mahallindedir. «مولى»: fâil. «عن مولى»: câr ve mecrûr; «يغني»ye müteallik. «شيئا»: mef'ûlün bih veya mef'ûl-i mutlaktır; yani «ondan azıcık bir şey». Vâv atıf harfidir. «لا»: nefy harfi. «هم»: mübtedâ; «ينصرون» cümlesi haberdir; bu fiil meçhuldür, vâv nâib-i fâildir.
(إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ): «إلا»: hasr edatı. «من», «ينصرون»daki vâv'dan bedel olarak ref' mahallindedir; yani «Allah'ın rahmet ettiğinden başkası azaptan korunmaz». Kisâî'nin görüşüne göre istisnâ üzere mansûb olup munkatı' olması da caizdir; yani «Fakat Allah'ın rahmet ettiği kimselere, kendisi hakkında mahlûkattan kendilerine fayda verecek birine muhtaç olacakları bir şey isabet etmez». Yahut muttasıl olur; takdiri: «Hiçbir yakın bir yakına fayda vermez; ancak müminler müstesna; onlara şefaat için izin verilir, onlar da birbirlerine şefaat ederler.» «رحم الله» cümlesi mevsûlün sılasıdır.
(إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ): «إن» ve ismi; «هو»: mübtedâ veya fasıl zamiri; «العزيز الرحيم»: «إن»nin veya «هو»nun iki haberidir; cümle «إن»nin haberidir.
(إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزَّقُّومِ طَعامُ الْأَثِيمِ): «إن» ve ismi; «الزقوم»: muzâfun ileyh; «طعام الأثيم»: haberidir.
(كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي فِي الْبُطُونِ كَغَلْيِ الْحَمِيمِ): «كالمهل»: «إن»nin ikinci haberidir. «يغلي» cümlesi «الزقوم»dan veya «طعام الأثيم»den hâldir. Muzâfun ileyhten hâl gelmesi bahsi daha önce geçti; çünkü o, muzâfın bir parçası gibidir. «في البطون»: câr ve mecrûr; «يغلي»ye müteallik. Kâf ve mecrûru mahzûf bir masdarın na'tıdır; yani «kaynar suyun kaynaması gibi bir kaynamayla kaynar».
(خُذُوهُ فَاعْتِلُوهُ إِلى سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ): «خذوه»: nûnun hazfi üzere mebnî emir fiil; vâv fâili, hâ mef'ûlüdür. Emir zebanilere yöneliktir; dolayısıyla cümle mahzûf bir kavlin mekûlüdür. «فاعتلوه»: «خذوه»ya ma'tûftur. «إلى سواء الجحيم»: câr ve mecrûr; «اعتلوه»ya müteallik; yani cehennemin ortasına.
(ثُمَّ صُبُّوا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ الْحَمِيمِ): «ثم»: terâhî ile tertip bildiren atıf harfi. «صبّوا»: emir fiil ve fâil. «فوق رأسه»: zarf; «صبّوا»ya müteallik. «عذاب الجحيم»: mef'ûlün bihtir [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «عذاب الجحيم» yazılmıştır; âyette «من عذاب الحميم»dir.].
(ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ): Cümle mahzûf bir kavlin mekûlüdür; yani «Ona "Tat!" denir». «ذق»: emir fiil; fâili müstetir olup takdiri «أنت»tir. «إن» ve ismi; «أنت»: mübtedâ veya fasıl zamiri; «العزيز الكريم»: «إن»nin veya «أنت»in iki haberidir. «إنك…» cümlesi ta'lîliyyedir. Bu ta'lîlin sırrı «Belâgat» bölümünde gelecektir.
(إِنَّ هذا ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَمْتَرُونَ): «إن» ve ismi; «ما»: haberi. «كنتم» cümlesi sıladır. «به»: câr ve mecrûr; «تمترون»a müteallik. «تمترون» cümlesi «كنتم»in haberidir.

* Belâgat:
1- «ثم صبّوا فوق رأسه من عذاب الحميم» kavlinde mekniyye-tahyîliyye istiâre vardır: Azabı sıvı bir şeye benzetmiş, sonra ona «dökme» ile tahyîl yapmıştır.
2- «ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم» kavlinde tehekküm (alay) sanatı vardır. Daha önce geçtiği üzere bu, söyleyenin kendisine söylenen kimseyi hafife alması ve onunla alay etmesi için, korkutma yerinde müjde lafzını, tehdit yerinde va'd lafzını getirmekten ibarettir. Bunun örnekleri yerlerinde geçmiştir; Allah Teâlâ'nın Nisâ sûresindeki «بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما» kavli gibi. Bu, kendisiyle alay edilen kimseyi daha çok öfkelendirir ve ona daha çok acı verir.

* Vocabulary:
(السندس): it is the fine kind of brocade (dībāj), and al-istabraq is the coarse kind of it; it is an Arabicized form of «استير» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Persian original is usually cited as «استبر» (istabr)]. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how is it permissible for a non-Arabic word to occur in the clear Arabic Qur'an? I say: when it is Arabicized it ceases to be non-Arabic, because Arabicization means making it Arabic by modifying it, changing it from its pattern and treating it according to the aspects of i'rab." There is another question raised by the heretic Ibn al-Rāwandī: how did Allah promise the people of Paradise the wearing of istabraq, which is coarse brocade, when with the rich of this world it is a defect and a deficiency? The answer is that the coarse brocade of Paradise is not equal to the coarse brocade of this world, so that it should be faulted, just as the sundus of Paradise, which is the fine brocade, is not equal to the sundus of this world. Abu al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī, in Risālat al-Ghufrān, dealt with Ibn al-Rāwandī at length, in mockery and ridicule.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ): إن and its noun; في مقام is its predicate; أمين is an adjective of مقام.
(فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ) [Translator's note: in the source the beginning of this verse is garbled and runs into the previous sentence as «لمقامِ ي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ)»]: the preposition and its genitive noun are a substitute for «في مقام», with repetition of the preposition.
(يَلْبَسُونَ مِنْ سُندُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ): the sentence is either a second predicate of إن or a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun; من سندس is attached to يلبسون; متقابلين is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يلبسون. In this ḥāl is a beautiful description of the gatherings of the people of Paradise: none of them looks at the back of another's neck, since their couches turn round with them.
(كَذلِكَ وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ): كذلك is the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, "the matter is thus"; this sentence is parenthetical between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined, brought for confirmation. وزوجناهم is conjoined to يلبسون; it is a past verb, agent and direct object; بحور is attached to زوجناهم; عين is an adjective of حور. An unusual description of the ḥūr ʿīn will come in the section of Benefits.
(يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ): the sentence is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in زوجناهم; يدعون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw its agent; فيها is a ḥāl; بكل is attached to يدعون, that is, "they ask for it to be brought to them"; آمنين is a ḥāl, that is, "not fearing the consequence of eating it".
(لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولى): the sentence is a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمنين; لا is negative; يذوقون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; فيها is a ḥāl; الموت is the direct object; إلا is a particle of exception; الموتة is excepted from الموت as a disconnected exception; الأولى is an adjective. More will be said on the parsing of this exception in the section of Benefits.
(وَوَقاهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ): the wāw is a conjunction; وقاهم is a past verb with a latent agent referring to Allah; عذاب الجحيم is a second direct object.
(فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكَ ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): فضلا is an absolute object of an omitted verb; it is also said to be an object of purpose, but the first is closer, because it is a maṣdar agreeing with its governing verb in meaning, that is, "We bestowed that as a favour"; من ربك is an adjective of فضلا; ذلك is the subject; هو is a pronoun of separation; الفوز is the predicate; العظيم is an adjective of الفوز. It is also possible that هو is a second subject and الفوز its predicate, the sentence being the predicate of the demonstrative.
(فَإِنَّما يَسَّرْناهُ بِلِسانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (a particle that prevents the governing action of إن). We have made it eloquent because the verse is the summation (fadhlaka, a concluding digest) of the sūra, for it has made explicit something implied. يسرناه is a verb, agent and direct object; بلسانك is attached to يسرناه; لعل and its noun, with the clause يتذكرون as its predicate.
(فَارْتَقِبْ إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ): the fāʾ is again the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if they do not take heed and do not believe in it, then wait"; ارتقب is an imperative whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you", and its object is omitted, its implied form being "their destruction"; the clause «إنهم مرتقبون» is explanatory of the command to wait; إن with its noun and predicate; the object of مرتقبون is also omitted, its implied form being "your destruction".

* Benefits:
1- A problematic exception: al-Shihāb al-Samīn said: "His words «إلا الموتة الأولى» have several aspects. The first is that it is a disconnected exception, i.e. 'but they have already tasted the first death'. The second is that it is connected, and they interpreted it as meaning that the believer at his death in this world is in the position of being in Paradise, because of his seeing what is given him of it or because of his certainty of its bliss. The third is that illā means siwā ('other than'); al-Ṭabarī transmitted this and weakened it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: its weakening is not sound, rather its being in the sense of siwā is straightforward and consistent. The fourth is that illā means baʿda ('after'); al-Ṭabarī chose it and the majority rejected it, because the coming of illā in the sense of baʿda is not established. al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say, how was the first death, tasted before entering Paradise, excepted from the negated death that is tasted in it? I say: it was intended to say 'they will never taste death in it', so his words «إلا الموتة الأولى» were put in the place of that, because a death that has passed is impossible to taste in the future; so this belongs to the category of suspension upon the impossible, as if it were said: 'If the first death could be tasted in the future, then they would taste it in Paradise.'" I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned and al-Samīn transmitted is built on الموتة being a substitute, according to the method of the substitute in which a substitute from a different genus is permitted. As for the method of the Hijazis, الموتة is accusative as a disconnected exception. The secret of the Tamimi dialect is the construction of the intended negation in a manner that leaves the hearer no hope of affirmation, so they say "there is no one in it except a donkey" in the sense of "if the donkey is among the people, then there is someone in it", thus suspending the affirmation upon something necessarily impossible by means of the negation.
2- The ḥūr ʿīn: We promised you the transmission of an unusual description of the ḥūr ʿīn taken from the noble hadith. Before we cite what we chose of the hadiths on this subject, we say: al-ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrāʾ, which, as in al-Qāmūs and elsewhere, derives from al-ḥawar with fatḥa, which is that the whiteness of the eye is intensely white and its blackness intensely black, its pupil is round, its eyelids are fine, and what surrounds it is white. al-ʿīn is the plural of ʿaynāʾ, like ḥamrāʾ; so ʿīn was originally with ḍamma on the ghayn [Translator's note: so in the source, «الغين»; the letter ʿayn is meant], on the pattern of qufl, but it was given kasra so that the yāʾ would be sound; that is, wide-eyed. What follows is the text of the hadith we chose for this description:
"On the authority of ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about this verse: «يوم نحشر المتقين إلى الرحمن وفدا» to its end. He said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, the delegation (wafd) is only riders. The Prophet ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves they will be met with white she-camels which have wings, upon which are saddles of gold; the straps of their sandals are shining light, and each step of them is as far as the eye can see. They will reach the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby upon plates of gold, and a tree at the gate of Paradise from whose root two springs flow. When they drink from one of them, the freshness of bliss flows into their faces, and when they perform ablution from the other, their hair will never be dishevelled. They will strike the ring with the plate; if only you could hear the ringing of the ring, O ʿAlī! Then it reaches each ḥawrāʾ that her husband has arrived; she is lightened by haste and sends her steward, who opens the door for him, and he says (and if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had not made him know himself, he would fall prostrate before him, from the light and splendour he sees): I am your steward who has been entrusted with your affair. He follows him, treading in his footsteps, and comes to his wife; she is lightened by haste and comes out of the tent, embraces him and says: You are my beloved and I am your beloved; I am the contented, so I shall never be angry; I am the blissful, so I shall never be in want; I am the immortal, so I shall never depart. Then he enters a house from its foundation to its roof one hundred thousand cubits, built upon stones of pearl and ruby, in layers of red, layers of green and layers of yellow, no layer resembling its fellow. He comes to the couch, and upon it is a bed, and on the bed seventy mattresses, on each mattress seventy wives, each wife wearing seventy garments, the marrow of her shin visible from beneath the garments. He fulfils his union with them in the span of one night. Beneath them flow running rivers: rivers of water not stagnant, pure, with no turbidity; rivers of purified honey which did not come from the bellies of bees; rivers of wine, a delight to the drinkers, which men did not press with their feet; and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, which did not come from the bellies of cattle. When they desire food, white birds come to them and raise their wings, and they eat from their sides of whatever colours they wish; then they fly off and go away. And in it are hanging fruits: when they desire them, the branch inclines toward them and they eat of whatever fruits they wish, standing if they wish or reclining if they wish. That is His saying «وجنى الجنتين دان», and before them are servants like pearls." Ibn Abi al-Dunyā related it in the Book of the Description of Paradise, from al-Ḥārith. We content ourselves with this hadith, sufficing with it in place of many hadiths in this sense, which will come in their places, if Allah wills.

Müellifin sözü: {وَإِذَا عَلِمَ}: Çoğunluk ayn'ı fetha, lâm'ı kesre ile hafif ve malûm okumuştur. Katâde ve Matar el-Verrâk «عُلِّم» diye meçhul ve şeddeli okumuşlardır.
Müellifin sözü: «اتَّخَذها»: Müennes zamirde iki vecih vardır. Birincisi: «آياتِنا»ya dönmesi. İkincisi: müzekker olmasına rağmen «شيئاً»ye dönmesi; çünkü o, âyet anlamındadır. Ebü'l-Atâhiye'nin şu sözü gibi:
4030 - نفْسي بشيءٍ من الدنيا مُعَلَّقَةٌ ... اللَّهُ والقائمُ المهدِيُّ يَقْضِيها
(Nefsim dünyadan bir şeye bağlanmıştır; onu Allah ve Kâim Mehdî yerine getirir.)
Çünkü o «شيء» ile «Utbe» denilen bir cariyeyi kastetmiştir.
Müellifin sözü: «أولئك»: «كلِّ أَفَّاكٍ» anlamına işarettir; önce lafzına hamledilip müfred getirilmiş, sonra mânâsına hamledilip çoğul yapılmıştır; {كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ} [el-Mü'minûn: 53] gibi.
Müellifin sözü: {وَلاَ مَا اتخذوا}: «ما كَسَبوا»ya atıftır. İkisindeki «ما» ya masdariyyedir ya da «الذي» anlamındadır; yani «kazançları da edinmeleri de fayda vermez» ya da «kazandıkları şey de edindikleri şey de».

Müellifin sözü: {على شَرِيعَةٍ}: Bu, «جَعَلْناك»ın ikinci mef'ûlüdür. Şerîa aslında insanların nehirlerdeki sulardan su içmeye geldikleri yerdir. O yere şerîa denir. Çoğulu şerâi'dir. Şair şöyle demiştir:
4033 - وفي الشَّرائِع مِنْ جَيْلانَ مُقْتَنِصٌ ... رَثُّ الثيابِ خَفِيُّ الشخصِ مُنْسَرِبُ
(Ceylân'ın su başlarında, giysisi eski, kendisi gizli, sinsice dolaşan bir avcı vardır.)
Bu kelime dine ödünç alınmıştır; çünkü kullar, nefislerinin kendisiyle hayat bulduğu şeye gelirler.

His saying: {أَمْ حَسِبَ}: «أم» is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), so it is implied as "rather" and the interrogative hamza, or as "rather" alone, or as the hamza alone. The verification of this has been given.
His saying: {كالذين آمَنُواْ}: it is the second object of the "making," i.e. "that We make them be like those who believed," i.e. they do not reckon that. It was mentioned in Sūrat al-Ḥajj that the two companions (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «سواءً» here accusative, and the others nominative, and I promised to discuss it here. So I say, and with Allah is success: as for the accusative reading, there are three aspects to it. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «كالذين آمنوا», and the second object of the making is «كالذين آمنوا», i.e. "Did they reckon that We would make them like them in a state of equality of their life and death? It is not so." The second: «سواءً» is the second object of the making, and «كالذين» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "We will not make them, while being like them, equal"; and its meaning is not that. The third: «سواءً» is a second object of «حَسِب».
Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to this aspect, and I think it a mistake, as will become clear to you. He said: "It is also read accusative. There are two aspects: the first, it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the kāf, i.e. 'We make them like the believers in this state.' The second: it is a second object of «حَسِب», with the kāf a ḥāl, and the equality of their life and death has entered into the reckoning; and on this aspect their life and their death are nominative through «سواء», because it has gained strength by its reliance." End quotation. He has thus stated explicitly that it is a second object of the reckoning. This is not correct at all, because «حَسِبَ» and its sisters, when the doubled «أنَّ», or the lightened «أَنْ», or the subjunctive «أَنْ» occurs after them, stand in for two objects; and here the subjunctive «أنْ» occurs after the reckoning, so it stands in for the two objects; so how could «سواءً» be a second object of «حَسِب»?
If you say: what I have said is the opinion of the majority, Sībawayh and others, but others, like al-Akhfash, claim that it stands in for one; and given this, it is possible that Abū l-Baqāʾ followed this school, so he parsed «أَنْ نجعلَهم» as a first object and «سواءً» as a second object.
The answer: al-Akhfash stated explicitly that the second object is then omitted. And even if we concede that it is not omitted, it is prevented from another aspect: «محياهُم ومماتُهم» are made nominative by it, because it has the sense of "equal," as stated earlier, and there is no pronoun returning from its nominative to the first object; rather it makes nominative something foreign to the first object. This is like: "I reckoned your standing equal, your going and its absence."
As for whoever reads it nominative, his reading admits two aspects: the first, that «سواءٌ» is a fronted khabar and «مَحْياهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ/ and the second, that «سواء» is the mubtadaʾ and «مَحْياهم» its khabar.
So they parsed it. There is something to consider in this, mentioned in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, namely that it is indefinite with nothing to justify it, and whenever a definite and an indefinite meet, one makes the indefinite the khabar, not the mubtadaʾ. Then in this clause there are three aspects. The first: it is resumptive. The second: it is a badal for the kāf that falls as second object. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because a clause may fall as a second object, it is in the ruling of the single word. Do you not see that if you said: 'that We make them equal, their life and their death,' it would be sound, as you say: 'I thought Zayd, his father is departing.'" The Shaykh said: "This, I mean substituting a clause for a single word, was permitted by Ibn Jinnī and Ibn Mālik, and prohibited by Ibn al-ʿIlj," then he mentioned from him much speech in establishing that, then said: "And what appears is that it is not permitted," meaning what al-Zamakhsharī allowed. He said: "Because it has the sense of 'transforming,' and it is not permitted to say 'I made Zayd, his father is standing,' since transformation is a transition from one entity to another, or from a description in the entity to another description in it. And that clause that falls after the object of the implied «صَيَّرْت», as a second object, contains no transition of what we mentioned, so it is not permitted." I say: and one may say: rather, there is in it a transition from a description in the entity to a description in it, because the grammarians stated explicitly that a clause may fall as an adjective and as a ḥāl, as in: "I passed by a man whose father is standing," and "Zayd came, his father standing." So what they judged to be adjectival and circumstantial may fall within the scope of transformation, since there is no difference between one description and another in this respect.
The third: the clause is a ḥāl, the implied form being: "Or do the disbelievers reckon that We will make them like the believers in a state of equality of their life and death? They are not so; rather they are divided." This is the apparent view according to the Shaykh. On the last two aspects the clause falls within the scope of the reckoning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, for he said: "This speech requires that the wording of the verse is a statement, and it appears that His saying {سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ} falls within the denounced, evil reckoning; and this is a good possibility, and the first is fine." End quotation. He did not explain how it enters the reckoning, and the manner is one of the last two aspects: either badal or ḥāl, as you have learned.
al-Aʿmash read «سواءً» accusative with «مَحْياهم ومَماتَهم» also accusative. As for «سواءً», it is a second object or a ḥāl, as stated earlier. As for the accusative of «مَحْياهم ومماتَهم», there are two aspects: the first, that they are two adverbs of time, accusative as a badal for the object of «نَجْعَلَهم», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), with «سواءً» in that case being the second object. The implied form: "that We make their life and their death equal." The second: they are accusative as adverbs of time, and the operator is either the making or «سواء». The implied form: "that We make them equal at these two times," or "make them equal at these two times."
al-Zamakhsharī said, implying this aspect: "Whoever reads it accusative makes «مَحْياهم ومماتَهم» two adverbs, like 'the arrival of the pilgrim' and 'the setting of the star.'"
The Shaykh said: "His example of 'the setting of the star' is not good, because «خُفوق» is a maṣdar not on the pattern maf ʿal, so in truth it involves an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'the time of setting,' unlike «مَحْيا», «مَمات» and «مَقْدَم», which are set down as shared among three meanings: maṣdar, time and place. When they are used as maṣdar, that is by original setting, not by omitting a muḍāf like «خُفوق»; for there must be an omitted muḍāf for it, as it is set down as a maṣdar." This is a minor matter, because he only meant that this word occurs with time intended by it. Whether it is by origin or by derivation does not harm.
The pronoun in «مَحْياهم ومماتُهم» may refer back to both groups, meaning: the life and death of the believers are equal with Allah in honour, and the life and death of the wrongdoers are equal in disgrace with Him; so he folded the speech, relying on the listener's mind and understanding. It may also refer back to the wrongdoers only: He reports that their state in the two times is equal.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«مَماتَهم» is also read accusative, i.e. 'in their life and their death.' The operator is «نَجْعل» or «سواء». It is also said it is an adverb." I say: his saying "it is also said" is the first view exactly.
His saying: {سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ}: its parsing has been given. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said here: "«ما» is a maṣdar particle, i.e. 'evil is their judgement.'"

* İ'rab:
(أم): «بل» anlamında munkatıa olup inkâr hemzesi anlamını taşır. (كالذين): mahzûf ikinci mef'ûlün bihe müteallik..
Müevvel masdar (أن نجعلهم ...) nasb mahallinde olup حسب fiilinin iki mef'ûlünün yerini tutmuştur.
(سواء): mübtedâ (محياهم)'nın öne alınmış haberi, merfû. (ساء): zem için mâzî fiil. (ما): masdar harfi.. Mahsûs (el-mahsûs bi'z-zem) takdîrîdir, yani «hükümleri».
Müevvel masdar (ما يحكمون) ref' mahallinde olup ساء fiilinin fâilidir. «حسب الذين ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «اجترحوا ...» cümlesi ism-i mevsûl (الذين)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «نجعلهم ...» cümlesi harf-i mevsûl (أن)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «آمنوا ...» cümlesi ikinci ism-i mevsûl (الذين)'in sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «عملوا ...» cümlesi آمنوا cümlesine ma'tûf olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «سواء محياهم ...» cümlesi, takdîr edilen ikinci mef'ûlden bedel olarak nasb mahallindedir [Dipnot: Âyetin anlamı: Onları âhirette mü'minler gibi mutlu kılmamızı, dünyadaki yaşayışlarına denk saydılar mı?.. Cümlenin açıklayıcı bir isti'nâf olup i'rabdan mahalli olmaması da caizdir.]. «ساء ما يحكمون ...» cümlesi isti'nâfiyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur. «يحكمون» cümlesi harf-i mevsûl (ما)'nın sılası olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur.

* İ'rab:
(حم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ): Sûrelerin başlangıçları hakkındaki söz geçti; oraya dönerek hatırını tazele. «تنزيل الكتاب»: mübtedâ; «من الله»: onun haberi; «العزيز الحكيم»: «الله»ın iki na'tıdır. «تنزيل»in mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberi olarak i'rab edilmesi ve «من الله»ın ona müteallik olması da caizdir.
(إِنَّ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآياتٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): «إن»: fiile benzeyen harf. «في السموات»: mukaddem haber. Lâm te'kîd içindir. «آيات»: «أن»nin ismi [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «اسم أن» şeklinde yazılmıştır; «إنّ»nin ismi kastedilmiştir.]. «للمؤمنين»: «آيات»ın sıfatıdır.
(وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَما يَبُثُّ مِنْ دابَّةٍ آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ وَما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ رِزْقٍ فَأَحْيا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ آياتٌ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ): Vâv atıf harfidir. «في خلقكم»: mukaddem haber. Vâv atıf harfidir. «ما»: ism-i mevsûl olup «خلقكم»e ma'tûftur. «يبث» cümlesi sıladır. «من دابة»: câr ve mecrûr; «يبث»e veya mahzûf bir hâle müteallik; yani «onu bir canlıdan olmak üzere yayar». «آيات»: muahhar mübtedâ; «لقوم»: «آيات»ın sıfatı; «يوقنون» cümlesi «قوم»un sıfatıdır. «اختلاف» de «خلقكم»e ma'tûftur; mahzûf bir mukaddem habere müteallik olması bakımından onun yerine konulmuştur. «ما»: «اختلاف»a ma'tûftur. «أنزل الله»: fiil ve fâil; cümle «ما»nın sılasıdır. «من رزق»: hâldir veya «أنزل»e mütealliktir. «فأحيا»: «أنزل»e ma'tûftur. «به»: câr ve mecrûr; «أحيا»ya müteallik. «الأرض»: mef'ûlün bih. «تصريف الرياح»: «اختلاف»a ma'tûftur. «آيات»: muahhar mübtedâ; «لقوم»: sıfat; «يعقلون» cümlesi «قوم»un sıfatıdır. Burada Zemahşerî'nin ibaresini aktarmak faydalıdır; zira o bu iki âyetteki kıraatleri eksiksiz ele almıştır. Şöyle der: «"آيات لقوم يوقنون" nasb ve ref' ile okunmuştur; "إن زيدا في الدار وعمرا في السوق" veya "وعمرو في السوق" demen gibi. "آيات لقوم يعقلون" kavline gelince, ister nasbet ister ref' et, bu iki âmil üzerine atıftandır. Nasbettiğinde iki âmil «إن» ve «في»dir; vâv bu ikisinin yerine konmuş, «اختلاف الليل والنهار»da cer, «آيات»ta nasb amelini yapmıştır. Ref' ettiğinde ise iki âmil ibtidâ (mübtedâ olma) ve «في»dir; (vâv) «آيات»ta ref', «اختلاف»ta cer amelini yapmıştır. İbn Mes'ûd "وفي اختلاف الليل والنهار" diye okumuştur. Eğer: İki âmil üzerine atıf, Ahfeş'in mezhebine göre isabetlidir, onda söz götürür bir şey yoktur; Sîbeveyh ise bunu reddetmiştir; onun görüşüne göre âyetin tahrîci (izahı) nasıldır? dersen, derim ki: Onun görüşüne göre bunda iki vecih vardır: Birincisi: Gizli bir «في» takdiri üzere olmasıdır; bunu güzel kılan, ondan önceki iki âyette onun zikrinin geçmiş olmasıdır; İbn Mes'ûd'un kıraati de bunu destekler. İkincisi: «آيات»ın, mecrûr bitirildikten sonra ihtisas üzere mansûb olup öncesine ma'tûf olması veya tekrar (te'kîd) üzere olmasıdır; ref'i ise gizli bir «هي» iledir. "واختلاف الليل والنهار" ref' ile de okunmuştur.»
(تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ): «تلك»: mübtedâ; «آيات الله»: haber; «نتلوها» cümlesi hâliyyedir. «آيات الله»nın ism-i işaretten bedel olması ve «نتلوها» cümlesinin haber olması da caizdir. «عليك»: câr ve mecrûr; «نتلوها»ya müteallik. «بالحق»: hâldir; yani hakla mülâbis (hakka bürünmüş) olarak.
(فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وَآياتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ): Fâ atıf harfidir. «بأي»: câr ve mecrûr; «يؤمنون»a müteallik. İstifhâm inkârîdir, manası nefiydir; yani «iman etmezler». «حديث»: «أي»ye muzâfun ileyhtir [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «مضاف لأي» (أيّ'ye izâfe edilmiş) şeklindedir.]. «بعد الله»: zarf; «الحديث»in na'tı olan mahzûf bir şeye müteallik. «يؤمنون»: merfû muzâri fiil.

* Belâgat:
«إن في السموات» kavlinden «يعقلون» kavline kadar olan kısımda «tahyîr» sanatı vardır. Bu, şairin veya kâtibin, çeşitli kafiyelerle bitirilmesi caiz olan beyitler veya cümleler getirip bunlardan diğerlerine tercih ettiği bir kafiyeyi seçmesidir. Âyetlerdeki belâğat, birinci âyetin fâsılasının «للمؤمنين» olmasını gerektirir; çünkü Allah Sübhânehû «السموات والأرض» diyerek âlemi bütünüyle zikretmiştir; âlemde bulunan, onu icat edenin kadîr, alîm ve hakîm olduğuna delâlet eden âyetleri bilmek de (bunun içindedir). Mamuldeki âyetlerin, (yapıcının) bu sıfatlarla muttasıf olduğuna delil olabilmesi için önce Sâni'i (Yaratıcı'yı) tasdik etmek gerekir; tasdik ise imandır. Allah Teâlâ'nın ikinci âyetteki «لقوم يوقنون» kavli de böyledir; çünkü insanın yaratılışı, hayvanların yaratılışının tedbiri ve bunlar üzerinde tefekkür, kişinin ilk inancında yakînini artıran şeylerdendir. Aynı şekilde âlemin cüziyyâtını —gece ile gündüzün birbirini takip etmesi, rızkın gökten indirilmesi, ölümünden sonra yerin diriltilmesi ve rüzgârların yönlendirilmesi— bilmek, aklın olgunluğunu gerektirir; ta ki külli âlemin seçme hürriyetine sahip bir Sâni'i olduğuna dair burhan kâim olduktan sonra, bu cüziyyâtı yapanın külli âlemi yapan olduğu bilinsin. Bu yüzden belâğat, üçüncü âyetin fâsılasının «لقوم يعقلون» olmasını gerektirmiştir. Her ne kadar hepsinde akla ihtiyaç duyulsa da, burada onun zikredilmesi mana bakımından birincisinden daha sağlamdır.

* İ'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ): «ويل»: mübtedâdır; bu bir azap kelimesidir; bu yüzden onunla ibtidâ caiz olmuştur. «لكل أفّاك»: onun haberidir. «أثيم»: na'ttır. Bu ikisi (أفّاك ve أثيم) yalan ve günah için mübalağa sıfatlarıdır.
(يَسْمَعُ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ): «يسمع» cümlesi «أفّاك أثيم»in sıfatıdır veya ikisindeki zamirden hâldir; onu müste'nef kılman da mümkündür. «يسمع آيات الله»: muzâri fiil, müstetir fâil ve mef'ûlün bih. «تتلى عليه» cümlesi «آيات الله»dan hâldir. «عليه»: câr ve mecrûr; «تتلى»ya müteallik.
(ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِراً كَأَنْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْها): «ثم»: tertip ve terâhî için atıf harfi. «يصرّ»: «يسمع»e ma'tûf muzâri fiil. Zemahşerî dedi ki: «Bunun aslı, erkek yaban eşeğinin dişi yaban eşeği sürüsü üzerine "ısrar etmesi"dir; o da kulaklarını dikip toplayarak (صارّا أذنيه) onlara yönelip saldırmasıdır.» Ben derim ki: es-Sıhâh'ta şöyle denir: «صرّ الفرس أذنيه: at kulaklarını başına doğru topladı (dikti). (Fiilin mef'ûlünü) zikretmedikleri zaman elif ile "أصرّ الفرس" derler.» «مستكبرا»: «يصرّ»ın fâilinden hâldir. «كأن»: ağır (şeddeli) olandan muhaffefedir; ismi şe'n zamiridir; «لم يسمعها» cümlesi haberidir; cümle ikinci hâldir; yani «işitmeyen kimse gibi olduğu hâlde ısrar eder».
(وَإِذا عَلِمَ مِنْ آياتِنا شَيْئاً اتَّخَذَها هُزُواً): Vâv atıf harfidir. «إذا»: şart manasını tazammun eden istikbal zarfıdır. «علم» cümlesi, zarfın ona izâfe edilmesiyle cer mahallindedir. «من آياتنا»: câr ve mecrûr; «علم»e veya mahzûf bir hâle müteallik; çünkü aslında «شيئا»nın sıfatı idi. «شيئا»: mef'ûlün bih. «اتخذها» cümlesinin i'rabdan mahalli yoktur; çünkü cezmetmeyen şartın cevabıdır. Hâ «اتخذ»ın birinci mef'ûlü, «هزوا» ikinci mef'ûlüdür.
(أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): İsm-i işaret mübtedâdır. «لهم»: mukaddem haber; «عذاب»: muahhar mübtedâ; «مهين»: «عذاب»ın sıfatı; cümle «أولئك»in haberidir. «أولئك» cümlesi müste'neftir.
