2- And He made رواسي شامخات and ماء فراتا indefinite to convey partition, because in the sky there are mountains — Allah the Exalted said: «وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد» — and in it there is much sweet water; indeed it is its source and its outflow.
3- In His saying: «انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب، لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب» there is a curious art among the arts of rhetoric, which the ancients named «al-ʿunwān» (the title/index). Reference to it has preceded in this book: it consists in the speaker taking up a purpose of his — description, boasting, praise, reproach, satire or other such arts — and then, with the aim of completing it, bringing examples of words that serve as a title for earlier reports and past stories. And there is a very great kind of it, which is what serves as a title for the sciences: that words are mentioned in the speech which serve as keys to sciences and entrances to them. This verse we are dealing with is among the truest proofs of that, for His saying «ظل ذي ثلاث شعب» is a title for the science attributed to Euclid, a Greek philosopher who composed a book on astronomy, geometry and arithmetic, which al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf al-Kūfī translated into Arabic. He taught geometry in Alexandria in the days of Ptolemy and laid down the principles of plane geometry; he also has the book of the Elements, which Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī commented upon; and he died in the year 283. [Translator's note: translated as written; it is unclear in the source to whom the death date refers, and the details are compressed.] For the triangular figure is the first of figures and their basis, and from it the rest of the figures are composed; and it is a figure which, when set up in the sun, however it is set up and on whichever of its sides, has no shade, because of the sharpness of the vertices of its angles. So Allah, Glorified is He, commanded these people of Hell to go off to the shade of this figure in mockery and derision of them.
4- Simile (tashbīh): He, Glorified is He, likened the sparks to the palace in its hugeness and size, and likened them secondly to yellow camels in form, colour, multitude, succession and speed of movement. We quote here a curious passage of al-Zamakhsharī and then comment on it briefly. He said in al-Kashshāf: «They were likened to palaces and then to camels to make the simile clear; do you not see that they liken camels to al-afdān and al-majādil?» — i.e. palaces, the plural of fadan and mijdal, both meaning palace, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. Then he said: «And جمالات was read with ḍamma, which are the thick ropes (qulūs) of bridges; and it is said the ropes of sea ships, the singular being jumāla» — and al-qulūs is the plural of qals, a thick rope among the ropes of ships. Then he said: «And it is said: صفر, intending the genus; and it is said: صفر means black ones tending to yellowness. And in the poetry of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān the Khārijite:
دعتهم بأعلى صوتها ورمتهم ... بمثل الجمال الصفر نزاعة للشوى
(It called them with its loudest voice and pelted them with the like of yellow camels, stripping away the scalps.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكل شرارة كطراف
(Red, its locks shining in the darkness, it throws every spark like a leather tent.)
So he likened it to the ṭirāf, which is a tent of leather, in hugeness and redness. It is as though, out of his malice, he intended to go beyond the simile of the Qur'an; and in his conceit at the illusion of surpassing it that he was tempted into, he placed at the beginning of his verse his word «حمراء» as a preparation for it, a proclamation of it, and an alerting of the listeners to its place. But he was blind — may Allah join for him the blindness of both abodes — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «كأنه جمالات صفر», for that is equivalent to saying «like a red tent». Moreover, in the simile with the qaṣr, which is the fortress, there is a likening from two aspects: hugeness and height in the air; and in the simile with jumālāt, which are the ropes, there is a likening from three aspects: hugeness, length and yellowness. So may Allah render far his strangeness in his ṭirāf, and the cheeks he puffed out in finding it so original.»
And the author of Nasmat al-Saḥar mentioned, concerning al-Zamakhsharī at His saying, the Exalted:
«إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر», that he mentioned the verse of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ describing the fire of hospitality, from the qaṣīda rhyming in fāʾ in which he elegized the Naqīb Abū Aḥmad al-Mūsawī, father of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī and al-Murtaḍā, namely:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكلّ شرارة كطراف
and he became heated against him and said that he intended and aimed to go beyond the simile of the Mighty Qur'an with the palace. He said: «And I do not know whence he got that he aimed to go beyond the simile of the Qur'an, for it is known that the palace is greater than the ṭirāf, which is a tent of red leather used by the nomadic Turks and the wealthy among the Arabs; but al-Zamakhsharī, despite his merit, was very sharp of temper.»
I say: al-Zamakhsharī — may Allah have mercy on him — picks quarrels with Abū al-ʿAlāʾ in many places, and he is, as we see in his criticism of al-Maʿarrī's beautiful verse, clearly biased and partial. We are accustomed to al-Zamakhsharī attacking the opponents of the Muʿtazila, and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ was not one of them; but al-Zamakhsharī was a man of letters who had read al-Maʿarrī's epistles and took note of [Translator's note: the source has «ووطن»; presumably «وفطن» is meant] his stance toward the grammarians, so his dislike drove him to provoke him.
This grammatical feud did harm to Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, for the grammarians neglected his poetry and very rarely took it up with commentary, citation or criticism; they gave attention to the poetry of Abū Tammām and al-Mutanabbī for their free handling of the language and of grammatical styles, and there was in Abū al-ʿAlāʾ's poetry what would tempt them to study it, but they turned away from it. Al-Maʿarrī's criticism of the grammarians has passed in this book, so renew your acquaintance with it.
As for likening camels to al-afdān, which are palaces, it is very frequent in their poetry. ʿAntara said:
فوقفت فيها ناقتي فكأنها ... فدن لأقضي حاجة المتلوم
(I halted my she-camel there, and she was like a castle, so that I might fulfil the need of one who lingers.)
And al-Maʿarrī was captivated by the description of camels and tried to follow in their footsteps, but he went extremely far into strangeness in that, as in his saying, from a qaṣīda of his in Saqṭ al-Zand addressing the keeper of the House of Knowledge in Baghdad:
وحرف كدال تحت ميم ولم يكن ... براء يؤم الرسم غيره النقط
(And a lean she-camel like a dāl beneath a mīm, and there was no "rāʾ" heading for the trace that the drops had altered.)
The ḥarf is the she-camel, and the dāl is a likening of it; the mīm is the bent-over rider, from the angle of simile, not of lexical explanation; the rāʾī is one who strikes the lung, from raʾāhu when he hits his lung; the rasm is the trace of the abodes, and al-nuqaṭ is rain. We have digressed to this only to set out al-Maʿarrī's strangeness, in criticism of which al-Zamakhsharī did not go beyond the truth.

﴿إنَّهم كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ حِسابًا﴾: Yani dirilişe ve hesaba çekileceklerine iman etmezler ve hesabın sevabını umarlar.
[Mütercim notu: Kaynak metinde «ويرجون» (ve umarlar) yazılıdır; bağlama göre «ولا يرجون» (ve ummazlar) beklenir. Metin yazıldığı gibi çevrilmiştir.]

﴿وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذّابًا﴾: Bu, kıraatin en yaygın olanıdır. Hafif olarak «كِذابًا» şeklinde de okunmuştur. Şeddeli ﴿كِذّابًا﴾ daha yaygındır; o, «فَعَّلْتُ» (babının) masdarlarında «فِعالٌ»dan daha güzeldir. Şair şöyle demiştir:
لَقَدْ طالَ ما رَيَّثَتْنِي عَنْ صَحابَتِي ∗∗∗ وعَنْ حِوَجٍ قَضّاؤُها مِن شِفائِيا
(Beni arkadaşlarımdan ve görülmesi bana şifa olan ihtiyaçlarımdan ne uzun zaman alıkoydu!)
(Bu «قَضاؤُها»), «قَضَيْتُ قَضاءً»dandır. Hafif «كِذابًا»nın benzeri de şairin şu sözüdür:
فَصَدَقْتُها وكَذَّبْتُها ∗∗∗ والمَرْءُ يَنْفَعُهُ كِذابُهْ
(Ona doğru da söyledim, yalan da söyledim; kişiye bazen yalanı da fayda verir.)

Ve Allah celle ve azze'nin ﴿وَكَأْسًا دِهاقًا﴾ sözü: Yani (önceki) âyetin takdiri «لا يَرْجُونَ ثَوابَ حِسابٍ» (hesabın sevabını ummazlar) şeklindedir; orada mahzûf bir muzâf vardır.
Ebû İshâk dedi ki: «اَلْكَأْسُ»: İçinde içecek bulunan her kap «كأس»tır; içinde içecek bulunmadığında «كأس» değildir. Sofra (المائدة) da böyledir: «الأخونة»dan (yemek sofralarından) üzerinde yemek bulunan her biri «مائدة»dır. «دِهاقًا»nın anlamı: dolu demektir. Tefsirde onun saf olduğu da gelmiştir. Şair şöyle demiştir:
يَلَذُّهُ بِكَأْسِهِ الدِّهاقُ
(Dolu kadehiyle ona lezzet verir.)
﴿إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا﴾ Gözetleyen (رَاصِدَة) veya hazırlayıp gözeten (مُرْصِدَة).

His saying: {دِهَاقاً}: an adjective of «كأس». Al-dihāq means full, filled to the brim. It was said: it is taken from dahaqahu, that is, "he pressed it and tightened it with his hand", as if it filled the hand and so was compressed. The poet said:
4477 - لأَنْتِ إلى الفؤادِ أحَبُّ قُرْباً ... من الصَّادي إلى الكأسِ الدهاق
(You are dearer to the heart in nearness than the cup filled to the brim is to the thirsty man.)
It was said: al-dihāq means successive, one following another. And [the poet] recited:
4478 - أتانا عامِرٌ يَبْغي قِراناً ... فأتْرَعْنا له كأساً دِهاقا
(ʿĀmir came to us seeking hospitality, so we filled for him a cup to the brim.)

Allah Teâlâ'nın {يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ} sözü: Kendisinden önceki «يَومَ»den bedel olması da, «عذاباً» ile mansûb olması da câizdir; yani «azap o günde vuku bulacaktır». Ebü'l-Bekā onun «قريباً»nın na'ti olmasını câiz görmüştür; eğer onu «عذاباً»nın na'ti kabul etseydi daha evlâ olurdu.
Kurrânın çoğunluğu «المَرْءُ»nun mîmini fethayla okumuştur; bu yüksek (âliye) olanıdır. İbn Ebû İshâk ise onu dammeyle okumuştur; bu bir lehçedir: fâ'ü'l-fiili lâmü'l-fiile tâbi kılarlar. Ebû Hâtim bu kıraati hatalı saymıştır; bu doğru değildir, çünkü lehçe olarak sabittir.
Allah Teâlâ'nın {مَا قَدَّمَتْ} sözü: «يَنْظُرُ»yu (amelden) ta'lîk eden istifhâmiyye olması câizdir; bu, onun «bakmak (nazar)» anlamından olması esasınadır; bu durumda cümle, cer harfinin düşürülmesiyle nasb mahallinde olur. Mef'ûlün bih olan ism-i mevsûl olması da câizdir; bu durumda «nazar» beklemek anlamındadır; yani «Ellerinin önden gönderdiği şeyi bekler.»
Kurrânın çoğunluğu «كنتُ»un tâsını «تُراباً»daki (tâya) idğam etmezler. Dediler ki: Çünkü fâil hazfedilmez; idğam da hazfe benzer.
«ويقولُ الكافرُ» sözünde, onun (kâfirliğine) şahitlik olmak üzere zamirin yerine zâhir (isim) konmuştur.

* Vocabulary:
(سُباتاً) Rest for your bodies. In al-Mukhtār: «al-subāt is sleep, and its origin is rest; from it is His saying, the Exalted: وجعلنا نومكم سباتا; and its pattern is naṣara.» In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«al-subāt, with ḍamma, like ghurāb: heavy sleep, and its origin is rest. From it one says sabata, yasbutu, of the pattern of qatala; and subita, in the passive: he fainted, and also: he died.» Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «سباتا: death; and al-masbūt is the dead, from al-sabt, which is cutting, because he is cut off from movement; and sleep is one of the two takings of the soul (al-tawaffiyayn); and it is on the pattern of the names of diseases.» As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said: «al-subāt is a known illness in which silence overcomes a person excessively until it becomes fatal.»
(الْمُعْصِراتِ) al-muʿṣir: al-Farrāʾ said: the clouds that bring rain but have not yet gathered, like the girl who is muʿṣir, who is about to menstruate but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Qutayba said something similar. And Abū al-Najm al-ʿIjlī said:
تمشي الهوينى مائلا خمارها ... قد أعصرت أو قد دنا إعصارها
(She walks gently, her veil leaning; she has come of age, or her coming of age has drawn near.)
And ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
فكان مجني دون من كنت أتقي ... ثلاث شخوص كاعبان ومعصر
(My shield against those I feared was three figures: two full-breasted maidens and a girl come of age.)
(ثَجَّاجاً) al-thajj: pouring down with abundance and force. In the ḥadīth: «The deed most beloved to Allah is al-ʿajj and al-thajj»; al-ʿajj is raising the voice in the talbiya and al-thajj is shedding the blood of the sacrificial animals. One says: the water thajja by itself, i.e. it poured down; and I thajajtuhu, i.e. I poured it, thajjan and thujūjan; so it is intransitive and transitive. [Translator's note: the opening quotation mark before «أحب العمل» is not closed in the source.] In al-Mukhtār: «The water and the blood thajja: flowed, and its pattern is radda; and a thajjāj rain, i.e. pouring down greatly. And al-thajj is also the flowing of the blood of sacrificial animals, and it is intransitive; you say from it: the blood thajja, yathijju (with kasra), thajjan (with fatḥa). I say: al-Azharī transmitted the like of this from Abū ʿUbayda.»
(أَلْفافاً) Intertwined. In al-Asās: «He wrapped (laffa) the garment and other things, and wrapped the thing in his garment, and laffafahu; and he wrapped his head in his clothes, and iltaffa in his clothes, and talaffafa; and the plants became intertwined (iltaffa), and in the land there are talāfīf of herbage; and جنات ألفافا: intertwined; and in it there is a thicket (lafaf) of trees. Al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
ولقد عرتني منك جدوى أنبتت ... خضرا إلى لفف من الأشجار
(A gift from you came to me that made green things grow, up to a thicket of trees.)
And a man is alaff and a woman laffāʾ; she laffat, talaffu, lafafan, which is the closeness of the thighs from fatness; it is a defect in a man and a praise in a woman. Naṣr ibn Sayyār, ruler of Khurāsān, said:
ولو كنت القتيل وكان حيّا ... تشمّر لا ألفّ ولا سؤوم
(Had I been the slain and he alive, he would have girded himself, neither heavy-thighed nor weary.)
And he said, describing women:
عراض القطا ملتفة ربلاتها ... وما اللفّ أفخاذا بتاركة عقلا»
(Broad of rump, their inner thighs fleshy; and the full-thighed ones do not leave a mind (intact).)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «ألفافا: intertwined; it has no singular, and it is said the singular is liff, with kasra on the lām», so it would be like sirr and asrār. And it is said it is the plural of lafīf — al-Kisāʾī said that — and similar are sharīf and ashrāf, shahīd and ashhād.

* I'rab:
(عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ، عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ، الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ) عن is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun, genitive (majrūr) by عن. It has preceded that the alif of interrogative ما is mostly omitted when a preposition enters upon it. And عمّا was read with the alif retained, and it has preceded that this is permissible by poetic necessity or in a small portion of speech; on this is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit:
على ما قام يشتمني لئيم ... كخنزير تمرغ في رماد
(For what reason did a base man rise to revile me, like a swine rolling in ashes?)
What appears is that عمّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتساءلون, and the interrogative is for magnifying the matter, as if He said: about what thing are they asking one another? Similar is the like of the saying «Zayd — what is Zayd!»: you have made him, because he has no peer, as though he were something hidden from you, so you ask about his kind and examine his essence and substance; you say: what is the ghoul, and what is the ʿanqāʾ? meaning: what thing among things is this? Then it was stripped down to express magnification, until it occurred in the speech of Allah the Exalted, from whom nothing hidden is hidden. وعن النبإ العظيم is a resumed statement presented to clarify that thing, so it is attached to an omitted verb indicated by يتساءلون; it is not a complement of يتساءلون because عمّ is its complement; i.e. they are asking one another about the great news; so it is a grammatical ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). الذي is a second naʿt (adjective) of النبإ; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); فيه is attached to مختلفون, and مختلفون is the khabar (predicate) of هم, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي. (كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ) A deterrent and threat to those asking in mockery; it contains the sense of threat and menace: the deterrence with the word كلا and the threat with the word سيعلمون. The object of سيعلمون is omitted, its implied form being «what will befall them». ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay, and كلا سيعلمون is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of the preceding clause, and the intervention of the conjunction does no harm. The grammarians insist that it can only be a conjunction, even if it conveys emphasis; and it can be answered that there is a noticeable difference, namely that the second threat is more severe than the first; by this consideration it became different from what precedes it, and therefore it was conjoined with ثم. (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهاداً وَالْجِبالَ أَوْتاداً) A resumed statement presented to set out His power, Glorified is He, to resurrect and to bring proofs of it; He mentioned nine of them. The point in them is that if He is able to do these things, then by plain intuition He is able to resurrect. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), i.e. «We made the earth a resting place». لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; الأرض is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and مهادا the second direct object, because جعل means transformation (taṣyīr). It may also mean creation, so that مهادا is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). والجبال أوتادا is conjoined to الأرض مهادا. (وَخَلَقْناكُمْ أَزْواجاً) Conjoined to what preceded. خلقناكم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; أزواجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of the same kind and resembling one another, males and females. (وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكُمْ سُباتاً) Also conjoined. جعلنا is a past verb and its agent; نومكم is the first object of جعلنا and سباتا the second object of جعلنا. (وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً) Also conjoined, and the clause is like the one before it in parsing. (وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهارَ مَعاشاً) Also conjoined, and it too is like the one before it. معاشا is a mīm-maṣdar meaning livelihood, and here it has occurred as an adverb of time, i.e. a time of livelihood. (وَبَنَيْنا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعاً شِداداً)
Also conjoined. بنينا is a past verb and its agent; فوقكم is an adverb attached to بنينا; سبعا is the direct object, i.e. seven heavens; and شدادا is an adjective. (وَجَعَلْنا سِراجاً وَهَّاجاً) Also conjoined. سراجا is the object of جعلنا and وهاجا an adjective; جعل here means creation. (وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ ماءً ثَجَّاجاً) Also conjoined. أنزلنا is a verb and its agent; من المعصرات is attached to أنزلنا; ماء is the direct object and ثجاجا an adjective. (لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَباتاً) The lām is the lām of causation; نخرج is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and it is also attached to أنزلنا. به is attached to نخرج; حبا is the object of نخرج, and نباتا is conjoined to حبا. (وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفافاً) Conjoined to حبا, and the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; ألفافا is an adjective of جنان [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has جنات], i.e. intertwined orchards.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وجعلنا الليل لباسا» there is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh). The point of resemblance is covering, because each of the garment and the night covers the one who wears it; i.e. it conceals you from eyes when you want to save yourselves from an enemy pursuing you, or as a night raid on him when you want to inflict a blow on him far from eyes, or it helps you hide what you do not wish anyone to see. Abū al-Ṭayyib (al-Mutanabbī) glanced at this lofty heaven, as is his custom, and said:
وكم لظلام الليل عندك من يد ... تخبر أن المانوية تكذب
(How many a favour has the darkness of night done for you, showing that the Manichaeans lie!)
وقال رد الأعداء تسري إليهم ... وزارك فيه ذو الدلال المحجب
(It guarded you against the enemies' ruin as you marched by night to them, and in it the coy, veiled beloved visited you.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is printed garbled in the source; the gloss follows its evident sense.]
The Manichaeans (al-Mānawiyya) are named after Mani, founder of the Manichaean doctrine of two principles in existence, a principle of good and a principle of evil: light and darkness. Mani entered into Persian painting, arranged Chinese painting and drew angels and devils, and he died in 276 CE. The explanation of the Manichaean question is that they said: you find in the world much good and much evil, and one being cannot be both good and evil; so each of good and evil has an independent agent. They said the agent of good is light and the agent of evil is darkness, and they believed that the two are eternal bodies, sentient, hearing and seeing — and all of that is manifestly false.
Abū al-Ṭayyib also said, clinging to the fringes of this lofty eloquence:
أزورهم وسواد الليل يشفع لي ... وأنثني وبياض الصبح يغري
(I visit them while the blackness of night intercedes for me, and I turn back while the whiteness of dawn incites.) [Translator's note: the verse ends with «يغري» in the source; the known form of the line is «يغري بي» ("incites against me"); the source is left as written and the Arabic is translated as it stands.]
And Ibn Zaydūn said:
سرّان في خاطر الظلماء يكتمان ... حتى يكاد لسان الصبح يغشينا
(Two secrets kept hidden in the mind of the darkness, until the tongue of dawn almost reveals us.) [Translator's note: the source has «يكتمان» and «يغشينا»; the known form of the line is «يكتمنا» and «يفشينا» ("keep us hidden" / "reveals us"). The Arabic is left as written, and the gloss follows the known form.]

Allah Teâlâ'nın {فَإِذَا هُم} kavli: Burada müfâcee (ansızınlık) ve tesebbüb (sebeplilik) açıktır. «السَّاهرة» hakkında yeryüzü ve çöl olduğu söylenmiştir; içinde vuku bulan şeyle, yani korku sebebiyle uykusuz kalmakla (السَّهَر) vasfedilmiştir. Serap içinde aktığı için (böyle denildiği) de söylenmiştir; bu, «عَيْنٌ ساهرَةٌ» (akan pınar) sözlerindendir. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: «السَّاهرة: düz, beyaz yerdir; böyle isimlendirilmiştir, çünkü serap onda akar; bu, "عينٌ ساهِرَةٌ" yani suyu akan pınar sözlerindendir; bunun zıddına "نائمة" (uyuyan) denir. Eş'as b. Kays şöyle demiştir:
4486 - وساهِرَةٍ يُضْحِي السَّرابُ مُجَلِّلاً ... لأَقْطارِها قد جُبْتُها مُتَلَثِّما
(Kuşluk vakti serabın her yanını örttüğü nice düz beyaz çölü yüzümü peçeyle örterek aştım.)
Yahut (böyle isimlendirilmiştir), çünkü orada yaşayan helak korkusundan uyumaz.» (Zemahşerî'nin sözü) bitti. Ümeyye de şöyle demiştir:
4487 - وفيها لَحْمُ ساهِرَةٍ وبَحْرٍ ... وما فاهوا لهمْ فيها مُقيمُ
(Orada kara ve deniz [hayvanlarının] eti vardır; ağızlarıyla diledikleri şey orada onlar için daimîdir.)
«sâhire bir arzın hayvanının eti»ni kastediyor. Ebû Kebîr el-Hüzelî de şöyle demiştir:
4488 - يَرْتَدْنَ ساهِرَةً كأنَّ جَميمَها ... وعَمِيْمَها أسْدافُ ليلٍ مُظْلِمٍ
(Öyle bir düzlükte otlarlar ki, oranın kısa ve uzun gür bitkileri karanlık gecenin koyu siyahlıkları gibidir.)
Râğıb şöyle demiştir: «O yeryüzüdür. Kıyamet arzı olduğu da söylenmiştir. Hakikati, üzerine çokça basılan yerdir; sanki bundan dolayı uykusuz kalmıştır. Bu, şairin şu sözü gibi bir şeye işarettir:
4489 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَحَرَّكَ يَقْظانُ الترابِ ونائِمُهْ
(… toprağın uyanık olanı da uyuyanı da kımıldadı.)
"الأَسْهَران": burunda bulunan iki damardır.» (Râğıb'ın sözü) bitti. «السَّاهُوْر»: Ayın tutulduğunda içine girdiği kılıfıdır. (Şair) şöyle demiştir:
4490 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أو شُقَّةٌ أُخْرِجَتْ مِنْ بَطْنِ ساهُوْرِ
(… yahut sâhûrun içinden çıkarılmış bir parça [ay].)
Yani bu kadın ayın bir parçası mesabesindedir. Ümeyye de şöyle demiştir:
4491 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قَمَرٌ وساهُوْرٌ يُسَلُّ ويُغْمَدُ
(… bir ay ve [onun] kılıfı; [ay ondan] çekilip çıkarılır ve içine sokulur.)

* İ'rab:
(الهمزة) tevbîhî (azarlama bildiren) istifhâm içindir. (خلقا) mansûb temyîzdir. (السماء) atıf harfiyle mübtedâ olan (أنتم) zamirine ma'tûftur. (بناها)'nın fâili, Allah'a dönen bir zamirdir; bu, siyaktan anlaşılmıştır ...
«أنتم أشدّ ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayan isti'nâfiyye cümledir.
«بناها ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayan beyânî isti'nâftır.
«رفع ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayan başka bir beyânî isti'nâftır.
«سوّاها ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayıp رفع cümlesine ma'tûftur.
«أغطش ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayıp رفع cümlesine ma'tûftur.
«أخرج ...» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayıp رفع cümlesine ma'tûftur.

* Sarf:
(أشدّ): sülâsî شدّ fiilinden ism-i tafdîldir; vezni أفعل'dir; ayn'ı ve lâmı aynı harftir.
(خلقا): sülâsî خلق fiilinin masdarıdır; vezni fetha ve sükûnla فعل'dir.
(سمكها): سمك'in masdarıdır, yani kalınlaştı ve yoğunlaştı. Vezni fetha ve sükûnla فعل'dir.
(سوّاها): Kalb yoluyla i'lâl vardır; kıyası (بناها) gibidir: kelimenin lâmı olan yâ, fethadan sonra harekeli olunca elife kalbedilmiştir.
(ضحاها): güneş ile öğle arasındaki vaktin adıdır; vezni damme ve fethayla فعل'dir. Ayrıca bkz. A'râf sûresi (98). âyet.

* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of rebuke. (خلقا) a tamyīz, accusative. (السماء) conjoined to the pronoun mubtadaʾ (أنتم) by the conjunction, and the fāʿil of (بناها) is a pronoun referring to Allah, understood from the context ...
Clause: «أنتم أشدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «بناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «رفع ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أغطش ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.
And the clause: «أخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause رفع.

* Morphology:
(أشدّ): an elative from the triliteral شدّ; its wazn is أفعل, and its ʿayn and lām are of one letter.
(خلقا): a maṣdar of the triliteral خلق; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سمكها): a maṣdar of سمك, i.e. "became thick and dense".. its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(سوّاها): it contains an iʿlāl by substitution, whose analogy is like (بناها): the yāʾ – the lām of the word – was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(ضحاها): a name for the time between the sun and noon; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa..
And see verse (98) of al-Aʿrāf.

* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction of ramification (tafrīʿ). (أمّا) a non-jussive-governing conditional particle. (من) a relative in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "is punished". (الفاء) the second is causal. (هي) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl)..
Clause: «من طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: in verse (34) of the sūra, which is composed of the condition, its verb and its apodosis].
And the clause: «طغى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «آثر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause طغى.
And the clause: «إنّ الجحيم ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar.
40- 41 (الواو) is a conjunction in both places. (أمّا من خاف ... ) like أمّا من طغى [Note: in verse (37) of this sūra]. (عن الهوى) attached to (نهى). (الفاء) causal. (إنّ الجنّة هي المأوى) like إنّ الجحيم هي المأوى [Note: in the preceding verse (39)].
And the clause: «من خاف ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من طغى.
And the clause: «نهى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خاف, the ṣila of من.
And the clause: «إنّ الجنّة ... المأوى» has no grammatical position; it is a reason for the omitted khabar..
And the apodosis is implied, indicated by the khabar, namely: "he enters Paradise".

* Morphology:
(37) طغى: it contains an iʿlāl by substitution; its original is طغي, its maṣdar طغيان; the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(آثر): the madda is composed of two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second sākin (أأثر); its wazn is أفعل, its imperfect يؤثر like أكرم يكرم.
(39) المأوى: a noun of place from the triliteral أوى; its wazn is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; it is a lafīf maqrūn.

* Rhetoric:
The art of muqābala (antithetical correspondence): in these noble verses, where several antitheses (ṭibāq) occur; and the multiplicity of ṭibāq, as is well known in the science of rhetoric, is called muqābala.

Sūrat ʿAbasa
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾: «أنْ» is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "because the blind man came to him." These verses and those after them, up to His saying ﴿فَأنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 10], were revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. He had come to the Prophet ﷺ while the Prophet was calling one of the nobles of Quraysh to Islam, hoping that others would embrace Islam through his embracing it; so he, upon him be peace, was occupied with calling him and did not turn to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm. So Allah commanded him not to let preoccupation with anyone else keep him from turning to any one of the Muslims, and said: ﴿عَبَسَ وتَوَلّى﴾ ﴿أنْ جاءَهُ الأعْمى﴾ ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكّى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 3] ﴿أوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى﴾ [ʿAbasa: 4]. It is also read «فَتَنْفَعُهُ الذِّكْرى». Whoever reads it in the accusative does so as the answer to «لَعَلَّ», and whoever reads it in the nominative does so by conjunction with «يَزَّكّى».

﴿أنّا صَبَبْنا الماءَ صَبًّا﴾: «إنّا صببنا» şeklinde de okunur. «إنّا» okuyan, ibtidâ ve isti'nâf (yeni cümle) olarak okumuştur. «أنّا» okuyan ise «الطعام»dan bedel olarak okumuştur; bu durumda «إنّا» cer mahallinde olur; anlam: «İnsan, bizim suyu bolca döktüğümüze baksın.»
[Mütercim notu: Kaynak metinde son cümlede «إنّا» yazılıdır; oysa söz konusu kıraat «أنّا»'dır. Metin yazıldığı gibi çevrilmiştir.]

His saying: {تصدى}: The two readings, with and without doubling, have preceded / for it. Its meaning is: you present yourself [to him]. One says taṣaddā, i.e. presented himself. Its origin is taṣaddada, from al-ṣadad, which is what faces you and is in front of you; one of the identical letters was replaced by a weak letter, as in taẓannaytu and qaṣṣaytu aẓfārī, and:
4498 - تَقَضِّيَ البازِيْ. . . . . . . . . ...
(… like the swooping of the falcon …)
The poet said:
4499 - تَصَدَّى لِوَضَّاحٍ كأنَّ جَبينَه ... سِراجُ الدُّجى تُجْبَى إليه الأساوِرُ
(He presented himself to a radiant one whose brow is like the lamp of darkness, to whom bracelets are brought as tribute.)
It was also said: it is from al-ṣadā, which is the sound heard in empty places and hard bodies. It was also said: from al-ṣadā, which is thirst. The meaning is presenting oneself, and one has to strain for that if we say its origin is from sound or thirst.
Abū Jaʿfar read «تُصَدَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the ṣād undoubled, i.e. your presenting yourself urges you on towards his Islam «[Translator's note: so in the text]». One says taṣaddī al-rajul and taṣdiyatuhu. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been read «تُصَدَّى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, i.e. you are made to present yourself; its meaning is: something calls you to present yourself to him, out of eagerness and keenness for his Islam."

His saying: {مَآ أَمَرَهُ}: «ما» is a relative noun. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the sense of «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. what He commanded him with." I say: this is questionable, in that he supplied the returning pronoun as governed by a preposition that does not govern the relative noun: «ولا أمره به» [Translator's note: so in the text; the wording is unclear]. If you say: «أمرَ» takes it as object by deletion of the preposition, so I supply it as not governed by a preposition—I say: if you supply it as not governed by a preposition, you must supply it either attached or detached, and both are problematic, for the reason I set out at the beginning of al-Baqara at His saying {وَممَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ} [al-Baqara: 3].

* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive [Note: or connecting the apodosis of an omitted conditional] , (اللام) is the lām of command, (إلى طعامه) attached to (ينظر), (صبّا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا صببنا..) is in the position of a genitive, a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) for طعامه.
Clause: «لينظر الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or it is the apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e.: if you wish to know the power of Allah and His management, then let the human being look ... [Translator's note: the source reads «أردتهم»; «أردتم» is evidently intended.]] .
And the clause: «صببنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
26-32 (ثمّ) is a conjunction, and likewise (الفاء) and (الواو) in the four places; (شقّا) is an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq; (فيها) is attached to (أنبتنا); (حدائق) is denied tanwīn because it is of the form of the "furthest limit of plurals" (a diptote); (متاعا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. "He gave you enjoyment with that, as an enjoyment" [Note: see (33) of Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt.] , (لكم) is attached to (متاعا), and likewise (لأنعامكم) ..
And the clause: «شققنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause صببنا.
And the clause: «أنبتنا ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause شققنا.

* Morphology:
(25) صبّا: a samāʿī (heard, non-rule-based) maṣdar of the triliteral صبّ, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn); its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
(26) شقّا: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral شقّ, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn); its ʿayn and lām are the same letter.
(28) قضبا: a noun for fresh, tender herbage, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).
(30) غلبا: a noun for thick, densely entwined trees, on the pattern فعل (with ḍamma then sukūn).
(31) أبّا: a noun for dry herbage, and it is said to be chaff (straw), on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn).

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His saying, the Exalted, «ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا» .
Attributing it to His pronoun is a figure of speech, of the kind of attribution to the cause, even though Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is in reality the Originator; the attribution of an act is literally to the one by whom it is carried out, not to the one from whom it issues as an act of origination.

* Lügat:
(تَصَدَّى): Aslı «tetasaddâ»dır, yani ona yönelerek kendini ona arz ediyorsun (ilgileniyorsun) demektir. «el-Musâdât» karşı koyma (muâraza) demektir. «Tasaddâ», yani kendini arz etti, yöneldi denir. Aslı «tasaddada»dır; «sadad» kökündendir ki sana doğru gelen ve karşında duran şey demektir; benzer harflerden biri illet harfine çevrilmiştir (ibdâl). «Sadâ» kökünden olduğu da söylenmiştir; o, boş yerlerde ve sert cisimlerde işitilen sestir (yankı). «Sadâ» kökünden olduğu, bunun da susuzluk demek olduğu da söylenmiştir. Mana, (her durumda) kendini arz etme (yönelme) üzeredir.

* İ'rab:
(عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى، أَنْ جاءَهُ الْأَعْمى): «عبس» ve «تولى» fetha üzere mebnî iki mâzî fiildir; fâilleri takdiri «hüve» olan müstetir zamirdir. Bu iki yerde ve bunlardan sonraki üçüncü bir yerde (gâib sîgasıyla) gelinmesi ancak Hz. Peygamber'i (s.a.v.) yüceltmek ve ona lütufta bulunmak içindir; çünkü hitap tâsı ile yüz yüze konuşmada ve karşılaşmada (bulunan sertlik) gizli değildir. «أن جاءه» mef'ûlün lieclih olarak nasb mahallindedir; onu nasb eden ya «عبس» ya da «تولى»dir. «جاءه» mâzî fiil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; «الأعمى» fâildir. Daha uygun olanı şöyle denmesidir: «أن» ve ondan sonrası, cer harfinin düşürülmesiyle (nez'u'l-hâfıd) mansûb bir masdar te'vilindedir; câr ve mecrûr «عبس»e mütealliktir. Çünkü gelmek kalp fiillerinden değildir; böylece mef'ûlün lieclihin nasb şartlarından biri «ihtalle» [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «فاحتل» yazılıdır; kastedilen «فاختلّ» (bozuldu, eksik kaldı) olmalıdır.] olmuştur.
(وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى): Vav atıf harfidir. «ما» ref' mahallinde mübtedâ olan istifhâm ismidir; «يدريك» cümlesi haberdir. Kâf, «يدري»nin birinci mef'ûlü yerindedir; terecci (ümit) cümlesi ise ikinci mef'ûlü yerindedir. «لعله»: lealle ve ismidir; «يزّكّى», yani temizlenir cümlesi leallenin haberidir. «يدريك»in ikinci mef'ûlünün mahzûf ve takdir edilmiş olduğu da söylenmiştir; takdir: "Onun durumunu ve halinin akıbetini sana ne bildirir?" şeklindedir; ﴿لعله يزكى﴾ cümlesi de ibtidâiyye (yeni başlayan) cümledir. «أو» atıf harfidir; «يذكر» «يزّكّى» üzerine ma'tûftur. Fâ, sebebiyet fâsıdır. «تنفعه», sebebiyet fâsından sonra gizli «en» ile mansûb muzâri fiildir; he mef'ûlün bih, «الذكرى» fâildir. «فتنفعُه» ref' ile de okunmuştur; buna göre fâ atıf harfidir ve merfû «تنفعه» ﴿أو يذكر﴾ üzerine ma'tûftur.
(أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنى فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى وَما عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى): «أما» şart ve tafsîl harfidir. «من» mübtedâ olan ism-i mevsûldür; «استغنى» cümlesi i'rabdan mahalli olmayan sıladır. Fâ râbıtadır. «أنت» ref' mahallinde mübtedâ olan bariz, ayrı zamirdir. «له» (câr ve mecrûr) «تصدى»ye mütealliktir; «تصدى» cümlesi «أنت»in haberidir; isim cümlesi de «من»in haberidir. Vav hâliyyedir; «ما» nâfiyedir; «عليك» öne alınmış haberdir; «أن» ve etki alanındaki şey sona bırakılmış mübtedâdır. Yani: Onun İslâm ile arınmamasında senin için bir sakınca yoktur. Ebû Hayyân, «ما»nın inkâr için istifhâm olmasını tercih etmiştir; buna göre o mübtedâ olur, «عليك» onun haberidir; «ألا يزكى» cer harfinin düşürülmesiyle mansûbdur; câr ve mecrûr, «عليك»in müteallik olduğu şeye, yani istikrâra mütealliktir. Cümle «تصدى»deki zamirden hâldir.
(وَأَمَّا مَنْ جاءَكَ يَسْعى، وَهُوَ يَخْشى فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى): Vav atıf harfidir. «أما» şart ve tafsîl harfidir. «من» ref' mahallinde mübtedâ olan ism-i mevsûldür; «جاءك» cümlesinin i'rabdan mahalli yoktur, çünkü «من»in sılasıdır. «يسعى» cümlesi «جاءك»in fâilinden hâldir. Vav hâliyyedir; «هو» mübtedâ, «يخشى» cümlesi haberdir; cümle «يسعى»nin fâilinden hâldir; dolayısıyla bu, iç içe (mütedâhil) hâldir. Fâ, «أما»nın cevabını bağlayan râbıtadır. «أنت» mübtedâdır; «عنه» (câr ve mecrûr) «تلهى»ye mütealliktir. «تلهى», yani «tetelehhâ», merfû muzâri fiildir; fâili takdiri «ente» olan müstetirdir; cümle haberdir. ﴿أنت عنه تلهى﴾ cümlesi «من»in haberidir. Yani: Meşgul oluyorsun. Yani bu, «lehiye bi-kezâ yelhâ», yani onunla meşgul oldu fiilindendir; hiçbir şekilde «lehv» (eğlence) kökünden değildir. Çünkü Hz. Peygamber'in zamirine isnad edilmiştir; eğlence kökünden bir fiilin ona nispet edilmesi onun yüce makamına yakışmaz. Meşgul olmak ise böyle değildir; zira onun bazı zamanlarda ondan sadır olması caizdir. el-Kâmûs'ta şöyle denir: «"Lehâ lehven": oynadı — «iltehâ» gibi; bu onu oyaladı (elhâhu). «Radiye» gibi "lehiye bihî": onu sevdi; "(lehiye) anhu": ondan avundu, gafil oldu ve onu anmayı bıraktı. «Deâ» gibi "lehâ", «lehiyyen» ve «lehyânen» (masdarlarıyla) ve «telehhâ» da (gelir).»
(كَلَّا إِنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ): «كلا», her insanı kendisinden dolayı itap edilen şeyin benzerini işlemekten men eden ve sakındıran (red' ve zecr) harftir. Rivayet edildiğine göre Hz. Peygamber (s.a.v.) bundan sonra hiçbir fakirin yüzüne asla surat asmadı ve hiçbir zengine (ilgiyle) yönelmedi. Inne ve ismi; «تذكرة» inne'nin haberidir; zamir öğüde veya sûreye aittir. Fâ i'tirâziyyedir. «من» mübtedâ olan cezmeden şart ismidir. «شاء» fiilü'ş-şart olarak cezm mahallinde mâzî fiildir; fâili «hüve»dir; mef'ûlü mahzûftur, yani öğüt almayı (dilerse). «ذكره»: mâzî fiil, müstetir fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; o, cevâbü'ş-şart olarak cezm mahallindedir. Cümle i'rabdan mahalli olmayan i'tirâziyye cümledir.
(فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ كِرامٍ بَرَرَةٍ): «في صحف» «إنها»nın ikinci haberidir. «مكرمة» ve ondan sonrakiler «صحف»in sıfatıdır (na't). «بأيدي» de sıfattır ya da mahzûf bir mübtedânın haberidir. «سفرة» muzâfun ileyhtir; ondan sonrakiler sıfattır. «es-Sefere», «sâfir»in çoğuludur; o da kâtip (yazıcı) demektir; «kâtib» ve «ketebe» de onun gibidir. "Sefertü beyne'l-kavmi esfiru sifâraten": aralarını düzelttim (elçilik ettim). el-Muhtâr'da şöyle denir: «"Sefera'l-kitâbe": onu yazdı; bâbı «daraba»dır.»
(قُتِلَ الْإِنْسانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ): Cümle i'rabdan mahalli olmayan dua (beddua) cümlesidir. «قتل»in manası lanet edildi ve azap edildi demektir. «الإنسان» nâib-i fâildir. «ما», «şey» manasında tam nekredir,
ref' mahallinde mübtedâdır. «أكفر» mâzî fiildir; fâili vücûben müstetir olup takdiri «hüve»dir — «yalnızca burada» —; he mef'ûlün bihtir. (Araplar) "Kâtelehullâhu mâ ehbesehû" (Allah onu kahretsin, ne kadar habistir!) ve "Ahzâhullâhu mâ azlemehû" (Allah onu rezil etsin, ne kadar zalimdir!) demişlerdir. Mana şudur: İnsanın, bundan sonra zikrettiğimiz her şeye rağmen inkâr etmesine şaşın. «ما»nın mübtedâ olan istifhâm, «أكفره» cümlesinin de haber olduğu söylenmiştir; yani "Onu küfre çağıran şey nedir?" demektir; bu, azarlama istifhâmıdır. Buna gerek yoktur; çünkü bu, onun küfründeki aşırılığından dolayı bir taaccübdür (hayret ifadesidir). Taaccüb mahlûklara nispetledir; zira Allah Teâlâ hakkında muhaldir. Yani o, hakkında "Ne kadar da kâfir!" denilen kimselerdendir. Zemahşerî'nin beğenilen bir ibaresi vardır; şöyle demiştir: «﴿ما أكفره﴾, onun nimete nankörlükteki aşırılığından dolayı bir taaccübdür. İki ucunun birbirine yakınlığıyla beraber bundan daha sert, dokunuşu daha haşin, öfkeye daha çok delalet eden ve kötülemede daha uzun mesafe kat eden; metninin kısalığıyla beraber kınamayı daha çok toplayan bir üslup göremezsin.» [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «للأئمة» (imamlar için) yazılıdır; Zemahşerî'nin ibaresinde muhtemelen «للائمة» (kınama için) olmalıdır; çeviri bu okumaya göre yapılmıştır.]

* Fevâid:
Tarih şunu rivayet eder: Abdullah b. Ümmü Mektûm b. Şüreyh b. Mâlik b. Rebîa el-Fihrî, Âmir b. Lüey oğullarındandır. Ümmü Mektûm babasının annesidir; adı Âtike bint Âmir el-Mahzûmî'dir. O, Hatice bint Huveylid'in teyzesinin oğludur. Nevevî'nin Müslim (şerhi)nde bulunana göre ise Ümmü Mektûm'un oğlunun adı Abdullah b. Amr'dır; Ümmü Mektûm Amr'ın karısıdır, dolayısıyla Abdullah'ın annesidir. Adının Amr, babasının adının da Zâid olduğu [Mütercim notu: kaynakta «زائد» yazılıdır; bir ad olarak anlaşılmış, belki «Zâide» kastedilmiştir] da söylenmiştir. (İbn Ümmü Mektûm,) yanında Kureyş'in ileri gelenleri — Rebîa'nın iki oğlu Utbe ve Şeybe, Ebû Cehil b. Hişâm, Abbâs b. Abdülmuttalib, Ümeyye b. Halef ve Velîd b. Muğîre — bulunduğu sırada ona (Hz. Peygamber'e) geldi. (Hz. Peygamber) onları İslâm'a davet ediyordu; konuştuğu bu şereflilerin İslâm'a girmesini, böylece İslâm'ın onlarla desteklenmesini, onların Müslüman olmasıyla taraftarlarının da Müslüman olmasını ve böylece Allah Teâlâ'nın kelimesinin yücelmesini umuyordu. (İbn Ümmü Mektûm): "Ey Allah'ın Resûlü! Bana (Kur'an) okut ve Allah Teâlâ'nın sana öğrettiklerinden bana öğret" dedi ve bunu tekrarladı; onun o kavimle meşgul olduğunu bilmiyordu. Resûlullah (s.a.v.) onun sözünü kesmesinden hoşlanmadı, yüzünü ekşitti ve ondan yüz çevirdi; bunun üzerine (bu ayetler) indi. Bundan sonra Resûlullah (s.a.v.) ona ikram eder, onu gördüğünde "Rabbimin kendisi hakkında beni itap ettiği kimseye merhaba!" der ve ona "Bir ihtiyacın var mı?" diye sorardı. Onu iki defa Medine'de yerine vekil bıraktı. Kurtubî şöyle demiştir: «Bunların hepsi müfessirlerin hatasıdır; çünkü Ümeyye ve Velîd Mekke'de idiler, İbn Ümmü Mektûm ise Medine'de idi; onlarla birlikte hazır bulunmadı. O ikisi kâfir olarak öldüler; biri hicretten önce, diğeri Bedir'de. Ümeyye asla Medine'ye gitmedi; (İbn Ümmü Mektûm) ne tek başına ne de bir başkasıyla birlikte onunla beraber bulunmadı.» Ebû Hayyân ise şöyle demiştir:
«Hata Kurtubî'dendir. İbn Ümmü Mektûm'un onlarla birlikte bulunmasını nasıl nefyeder? Bu ondan bir vehimdir. Hepsi Kureyş'tendir; İbn Ümmü Mektûm da orada (Mekke'de) idi ve sûre icma ile tamamen Mekkî'dir. "İbn Ümmü Mektûm Medine'de idi" nasıl der? O önce Mekke'de idi, sonra Medine'ye hicret etti. Bu ayet indiği sırada hepsi Mekke'de idiler.» Bazılarının benimsediği başka bir rivayet daha vardır: Surat asmakla kendisinden söz edilen Hz. Peygamber (s.a.v.) değil, Ümeyyeoğulları'ndan bir adamdır; İbn Ümmü Mektûm geldiğinde surat asan odur. Çünkü eş-Şerîf el-Murtazâ'nın dediği gibi, surat asmak, (dinine) muhalif düşmanlara karşı bile onun (s.a.v.) sıfatlarından değildir; doğru yolu arayan müminlere karşı ise hiç değildir. Okuyucu bütün bunları uzun eserlerde görebilir; dilerse onlara başvursun.

* Vocabulary:
(تَصَدَّى) its origin is تتصدى, i.e. you expose yourself by turning toward him; المصاداة is opposing. One says تصدى, i.e. he exposed himself; its origin is تصدد from الصدد, which is what faces you and comes to be opposite you, so one of the identical letters was replaced by a weak letter. It is also said to be from الصدى, the sound heard in empty places and hard bodies; and it is said to be from الصدى, which is thirst; the meaning is exposing oneself.

* I'rab:
(عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّى، أَنْ جاءَهُ الْأَعْمى) عبس and تولى are two past verbs, indeclinable on fatḥa, and their agent is latent, the implied form being "he". It was only brought in these two places, and in a third after them, [in the third person] out of reverence for him, peace be upon him, and gentleness toward him, since in face-to-face address with the tāʾ of the addressee there is something not hidden. [Translator's note: the source sentence is elliptical; the words «in the third person» are supplied to complete the sense, as the source does not state what was brought.] أن جاءه is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is either عبس or تولى; جاءه is a past verb and a direct object, and الأعمى the agent. It is better to say that أن and what follows are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to عبس, because coming is not among the verbs of the heart, so one of the conditions for the accusative of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is defective. (وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّى أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنْفَعَهُ الذِّكْرى) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يدريك is the khabar; the kāf is in the position of the first object of يدري and the clause of hope is in the position of the second object. لعله: لعل with its noun, and the clause يزكى, i.e. purifies himself, is the khabar of لعل; it is also said that the second object of يدريك is omitted, implied, the implied form being "what informs you of his affair and the outcome of his state", and the clause لعله يزكى is inceptive. أو is a conjunction; يذكر is conjoined to يزكى; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation; تنفعه is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation, the hāʾ a direct object, and الذكرى the agent. It was also read فتنفعه with nominative, the fāʾ being a conjunction and تنفعه in the nominative conjoined to أو يذكر. (أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنى فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى وَما عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّى) أما is a particle of condition and detail; من is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause استغنى is a ṣila with no position; the fāʾ is the connecting one; أنت is an overt detached pronoun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; له: attached to تصدى; the clause تصدى is the khabar of أنت, and the nominal clause is the khabar of من. The wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; عليك is a fronted khabar; and أن and what is in its scope is a postponed mubtadaʾ, i.e. "there is no blame upon you in his not purifying himself through Islam". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that ما be interrogative of denial, in which case it is a mubtadaʾ and عليك its khabar, and ألا يزكى is accusative by removal of the preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun attached to what عليك is attached to, i.e. "settling"; and the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in تصدى. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ جاءَكَ يَسْعى، وَهُوَ يَخْشى فَأَنْتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّى) The wāw is a conjunction; أما is a particle of condition and detail; من is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause جاءك has no position because it is a ṣila of من; the clause يسعى is a ḥāl from the agent of جاءك; the wāw is circumstantial; هو is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يخشى its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of يسعى, hence a nested ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). The fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis of أما; أنت is a mubtadaʾ; عنه: attached to تلهى; تلهى, i.e. تتلهى, is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent latent, the implied form being "you", and the clause is a khabar; and the clause أنت عنه تلهى is the khabar of من, i.e. "you busy yourself", i.e. it is from لهي بكذا يلهى, meaning to busy oneself with it, and it has nothing to do with اللهو (play), because it is attributed to the pronoun of the Prophet, and it is not fitting to his noble station that the act of play be attributed to him, unlike busying oneself, which may occur from him at times. In al-Qāmūs: «لها لهوا: he played, like التهى; and that ألهاه; and لهي به, like riḍiya: he loved it; and لهي عنه: he forgot, was heedless and left mention of him; and لها, like daʿā, لهيا and لهيانا, and تلهى». (كَلَّا إِنَّها تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَنْ شاءَ ذَكَرَهُ) كلا is a particle of rebuke and deterrence for every person from committing the like of what was blamed. It is reported that, peace be upon him, he never again frowned in the face of a poor man or exposed himself to a rich one. إن with its noun, and تذكرة is the khabar of إن; the pronoun refers to the admonition or the sūra. The fāʾ is parenthetical; من is a conditional noun that jussives, a mubtadaʾ; شاء is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and its agent is "he", and the object is omitted, i.e. being admonished; ذكره is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object, and it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the clause is parenthetical, with no position. (فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ كِرامٍ بَرَرَةٍ) في صحف is a second khabar of إنها; مكرمة and what follows are adjectives of صحف; بأيدي is also an adjective, or a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; سفرة is a muḍāf ilayhi and what follows are adjectives. السفرة is the plural of سافر, the scribe, like كاتب and كتبة; "سفرت between the people, أسفر, سفارة": I reconciled them. In al-Mukhtār: «سفر the book: he wrote it, of the pattern ḍaraba». (قُتِلَ الْإِنْسانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ) The clause is an invocation (duʿāʾ'iyya), with no position; the meaning of قتل is cursed and tormented; الإنسان is a deputy agent; ما is an indefinite complete noun meaning "something", in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أكفر is a past verb whose agent is obligatorily latent, the implied form being "he" ("here in particular"), and the hāʾ is a direct object. They said "May Allah fight him, how vile he is" and "Allah disgrace him, how unjust he is". The meaning is "wonder at man's disbelief, despite everything we have mentioned after this". It is also said that ما is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause أكفره its khabar, i.e. "what thing called him to disbelief?", a question of reproach, but there is no need for this, because it is wonder at his excess in his disbelief, wonder being in relation to creatures, since it is impossible in the case of Allah the Exalted, i.e. he is one of whom "how disbelieving he is!" is said. al-Zamakhsharī has a fine statement: «"ما أكفره" is wonder at his excess in ingratitude for blessings. You will see no style harsher than it, rougher to the touch, more indicative of wrath, further-reaching in blame despite the closeness of its two ends, or more gathering for the imams on the brevity of its body.»

* Benefits:
History relates that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm ibn Sharīḥ ibn Mālik ibn Rabīʿa al-Fihrī, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy (Umm Maktūm being his father's mother, whose name was ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir al-Makhzūmī, and he was the son of the maternal aunt of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid). In al-Nawawī's commentary on Muslim, it is that Ibn Umm Maktūm's name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, and Umm Maktūm was the wife of ʿAmr, so she is the mother of ʿAbd Allāh; it is also said that his name was ʿAmr and his father's name is Zāʾid [Translator's note: the source prints «زائد», which is taken here as a name (perhaps Zāʾida); it is not read as the adjective "additional"]. He came to him while with him were the chiefs of Quraysh, ʿUtba and Shayba, sons of Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, Umayya ibn Khalaf and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, and he was calling them to Islam, hoping that those nobles whom he was addressing would accept Islam, so that Islam would be strengthened through them and their followers would become Muslim with their becoming Muslim, and the word of Allah the Exalted would be raised. So he said: "O Messenger of Allah, recite to me and teach me from what Allah the Exalted taught you", and he repeated that, not knowing of his being occupied with the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked his interrupting his speech, and frowned and turned away from him; so (the verses) were revealed. After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to honour him and say when he saw him: "Welcome to him on whose account my Lord rebuked me", and say to him: "Do you have any need?"; and he appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice. al-Qurṭubī said: «All of this is a mistake of the commentators, because Umayya and al-Walīd were in Mecca and Ibn Umm Maktūm was in Medina, he did not attend with the two of them, and they died disbelievers, one before the Hijra and the other at Badr; Umayya never made for Medina nor was he present with him alone or with anyone.» Abū Ḥayyān said: «The mistake is al-Qurṭubī's; how can he deny Ibn Umm Maktūm's attending with them? It is a delusion on his part; they were all of Quraysh, and Ibn Umm Maktūm was there, and the sūra is entirely Meccan by consensus. How can he say "and Ibn Umm Maktūm was in Medina"? He was first in Mecca, then emigrated to Medina, and they were all in Mecca at the time this verse was revealed.» There is another report some have followed, which is that the one spoken of as frowning is not the Prophet ﷺ but a man of Banū Umayya, who frowned when Ibn Umm Maktūm came, because frowning, as al-Sharīf al-Murtaḍā says, is not among his, ﷺ, attributes even toward hostile enemies, let alone believers seeking guidance. The reader will find all this in the longer works; let him return to them if he wishes.

Allah'ın sözü: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ ﴿الجَوارِ الكُنَّسِ﴾. "اَلْخُنَّسُ", "خانِسٌ"in cemidir; "اَلْجَوارِي", "جَرى، يَجْرِي"den gelen "جارِيَةٌ"nin cemidir. "اَلْخُنَّسُ", "خانِسٌ" ve "خانِسَةٌ"nin cemidir; "اَلْكُنَّسُ" da aynı şekilde "كانِسٌ" ve "كانِسَةٌ"nin cemidir. Anlam: "Yemin ederim"dir; "لا" ise te'kîd edicidir (müekkide). Buradaki "اَلْخُنَّسُ" ile -tefsirlerin çoğuna göre- yıldızlar kastedilir; çünkü onlar "تَخْنِسُ" yani gizlenir; zira ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ [et-Tekvîr: 17] ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ [et-Tekvîr: 18] ayetlerinin anlamı… Yıldızlar hakkında "اَلْخُنَّسُ" ve "اَلْكُنَّسُ"un anlamı şudur: Onlar akıp giderek doğarlar; aynı şekilde "تَخْنِسُ" yani kaybolurlar; aynı şekilde "تَكْنُسُ" yani inlerine girerler, yani kayboldukları yerlerde gizlenirler. Denildi ki: Buradaki "اَلْخُنَّسُ" ile yaban sığırları ve yaban ceylanları kastedilir. "خُنَّسٌ"ün anlamı: "خانِسٌ"in cemidir; ceylanlar خُنَّس'tır, sığırlar خُنَّس'tır. "اَلْخَنْسُ" burnun kısa olması ve ağızdan geride kalmasıdır. Eğer (bu kelime) sığırlar ya da ceylanlar için olursa, "اَلْكُنَّسُ"un anlamı: "Kinâsa giren" demektir; كِناس ise ağaç dallarından bir daldır.
[Mütercim notu: Kaynak metinde «çünkü ... ayetlerinin anlamı» ile başlayan cümle tamamlanmadan kesilmektedir; metin yazıldığı gibi çevrilmiştir.]

﴿الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ﴾ they are the five stars: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury. تَخْنُسُ, with ḍamma on the nūn, i.e. they go back along their course, behind them: while we see the star at the end of a zodiacal sign, it turns back towards its beginning; and تَكْنِسُ, with kasra on the nūn, they enter their lairs (كِنَاسِهَا), i.e. disappear in the places where they disappear.

His saying: {بالخنس}: the plural of khānis; al-khunūs is withdrawing. One says khanasa from the people and inkhanasa. In the ḥadīth: "So I inkhanastu", i.e. I slipped away and hid. Al-khanas is the receding of the nose from the lip with the tip slightly raised; one says an akhnas man and a khansāʾ woman; from it is al-Khansāʾ the poetess. Al-khunnas in the Qur'an: it was said they are seven stars: the sun and moon (al-qamarān), Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, Mars and Mercury. Al-kunnas are those entering al-kinās, which is the lair of wild animals. Al-jawārī is the plural of jāriya. It was also said: they are the wild cows, because this is their description. It was also said: the gazelles; they said: because snub-nosedness (al-khanas) is found in them.

{بِضَنِينٍ} kavli: İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr ve Kisâî «zâ» (ظ) ile okumuştur; «itham edilen» manasındadır; «ittiham etti» manasındaki «ظنَّ» fiilindendir ve tek mef'ûle müteaddî olur. Manasının «tebliğ hususunda gücü zayıf olan» olduğu da söylenmiştir; «بئرٌ ظَنُوْنٌ», yani «suyu az kuyu» sözlerinden. Abdullah'ın (İbn Mes'ûd'un) Mushaf'ında da böyledir. Diğerleri ise «dâd» (ض) ile okumuştur; mana: «Rabbi tarafından kendisine gelen şeyi esirgeyen cimri». Ancak Taberî, dâdın bütün Mushafların hattı olduğunu nakletmiştir; geçen sebepten dolayı durum böyle değildir. Resûlullah (s.a.v.) onunla okurdu. [Mütercim notu: Metinde hangi harfin kastedildiği belirtilmemiştir.] Bu, iki harf arasında ayrım yapmanın gerekliliğine delildir; bilinmesinin güçlüğü sebebiyle birinin diğerinin yerine kullanılması hâlinde caiz olacağını söyleyenlerin aksine. Zemahşerî bunu söyleyenleri şiddetle kınamış, bazı mahreçleri ve bazı sıfatları zikretmiştir; burada bunu uzatmak uygun düşmez. «على الغيب», «ظَنِين»e veya «بضَنِين»e mütealliktir.

* Vocabulary:
(بِالْخُنَّسِ) الخنس: all the stars, or only the planets among them, or some of them; from الخنس, which is going back, because they go back in their course behind them. The verb is خنس يخنس, of the pattern دخل. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "الخنس are all the stars, because they recede (تخنس) at setting and because they are hidden by day; and it is said: they are the planets among them, to the exclusion of the fixed stars." Al-Farrāʾ said on the saying of the Exalted فلا أقسم بالخنس الجواري الكنس that they are the five stars: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury, because they recede in their course and withdraw (تكنس) as gazelles withdraw into their lairs. الخنس is also the shelter of gazelles, and the gazelles themselves, and wild cows.
(الْكُنَّسِ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "كناس الظبي, with kasra, is the gazelle's dwelling; كنس الظبي كنوسا, of the pattern نزل: it entered its lair; تكنس الظبي: it went out of sight and hid in its lair; تكنس الرجل: he entered the tent; تكنست المرأة: she entered the litter (al-hawdaj)."
(عَسْعَسَ) it advanced with its darkness, or retreated. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
حتى إذا الصبح لها تنفسا ... وانجاب عنها ليلها وعسعسا
(Until, when the morning breathed for her, and her night was rent away from her and departed.)

* I'rab:
(فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ، الْجَوارِ الْكُنَّسِ، وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا عَسْعَسَ، وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا تَنَفَّسَ) The fāʾ is resumptive. The discussion of (لا) has preceded, so refresh your memory of it. (أقسم) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā". (بالخنس) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أقسم). (الجواري) is a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute), and (الكنس) is a naʿt of (الجواري). (والليل): the wāw is also for the oath; (الليل) is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". (إذا) is an adverb attached to the verb of oath, and the clause (عسعس) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (والصبح إذا تنفس) is conjoined to the preceding clause. We did not conjoin (الليل) to (الخنس) only because the wāw is the beginning of [a new] oath.
If it is said: "Then you have contradicted Sībawayh, for he does not regard the wāw that follows an oath as the beginning of an oath, but as a conjunction; and you have made the first wāw, which follows an oath, the beginning of an oath?" We say: Sībawayh spoke only about the wāw [of oath]; as for the verse, the first oath in it is with the bāʾ and the verb, so we made the wāw after that an oath and a follower; and that is more eloquent, as though He swore by two different things.
If it is said: "Indeed, Sībawayh spoke only about the wāw that follows an oath; so what is the difference between a wāw that follows an oath made with the wāw and a wāw that follows an oath made with the bāʾ, when they are nothing but the same? For each of them is an instrument for it, and the tāʾ indicates the bāʾ, so their rule is one." We say: they are not the same. When the oath begins with the wāw and is followed by another wāw, making the other an oath involves a distasteful repetition, since the instrument is one. That is not so in the verse, since the instrument differs, so the [distasteful] effect of repetition is then avoided. Do you not see that if the oath began with the wāw and was then followed by an oath with the bāʾ, it would be necessary to make them two independent oaths? So likewise if this order were reversed. Moreover, if what prevented Sībawayh from making the second wāw an independent oath was that the apodosis comes as a single one and that the first wāw would need something omitted, while conjunction makes the assumption of an omitted element unnecessary — then this does not necessarily extend to the bāʾ, because it is the root of the oath, especially with the verb of oath stated explicitly and then emphasized by the addition of (لا); for in all of that together there is what makes it unnecessary to give it its own stated apodosis. That is not so with the wāw, for its standing in the oath is weak in comparison with the bāʾ. So it does not follow from the omission of an apodosis whose indication is firmly established that an apodosis less clear than it may be omitted.
We close the discussion of this question with an excellent subtle point: I restricted the raising of the question to the second wāw, in His saying (والليل إذا عسعس), and not the third, because it does not apply to it. Do you not see that if you made it a conjunction you would not be committed to conjoining onto two governors, because you would make it stand in for the bāʾ and make (إذا) in it accusative directly by the verb, since no adverb preceded in the verb's clause onto which (إذا) could be conjoined? It then becomes like your saying مررت بزيد وعمرو اليوم (I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr today): (اليوم) is accusative directly by the verb, and it is understood from the example that your passing by Zayd is unrestricted, not qualified by an adverb, and that only your passing by ʿAmr in particular is qualified by (اليوم). But it matches the verse; for the adverb in it, even though the verb governs it directly, qualifies the oath by the night, not the oath by الخنس.
(إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of the oath. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (قول) is its khabar (predicate), (رسول) is muḍāf ilayhi, and (كريم) is a naʿt. What is meant by it will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ مُطاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ) (ذي قوة) is a second adjective of (رسول). (عند ذي العرش) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (مسكين) [Translator's note: so in the source; read مكين], because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed first it became accusative as a ḥāl. (مكين) is a third adjective and (مطاع) a fourth adjective. (ثم) is an adverb meaning "there", attached to (مطاع). (أمين) is a fifth adjective.
(وَما صاحِبُكُمْ بِمَجْنُونٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to (إنه لقول رسول كريم). (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative ما, (صاحبكم) is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (مجنون) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of (ما).
(وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ) conjoined to His saying (إنه لقول …), so it falls within the scope of what is sworn [Translator's note: the source has في حيز المقسم به (the scope of that by which the oath is made); the sense required is المقسم عليه (that upon which the oath is made, i.e. the answer to the oath); translated as written]. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, (قد) is a particle of realization, (رآه) is a past verb with a latent fāʿil, (بالأفق) is attached to (رآه), and (المبين) is a naʿt of (الأفق).
(وَما هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ) also conjoined. (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative ما and (هو) its noun; (على الغيب) is attached to (ضنين); the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and (ضنين) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of (ما). (على) means the bāʾ, i.e. he does not withhold it from you but informs you of it. It was also read بظنين, with the dotted ẓāʾ, i.e. suspected. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "الظنة, with kasra, is suspicion; it is a noun from ظننته, of the pattern قتل, when you suspected him; so he is ظنين, a faʿīl in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl). Among the Seven [readings]: وما هو على الغيب بظنين, i.e. suspected." Also in al-Miṣbāḥ: "ضن بالشيء يضنّ, of the pattern تعب, ضنا and ضنّة with kasra and ضنانة with fatḥa: he was miserly, so he is miserly; and the pattern ضرب is a dialectal variant of it."
(وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطانٍ رَجِيمٍ) also conjoined; it is a negation of their saying that it is soothsaying and sorcery.
(فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction. (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, vague rather than specific, attached to (تذهبون). (تذهبون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil; i.e. which road are you taking?
(إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ لِمَنْ شاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ) (إن) is negative, (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (ذكر) is the khabar. (للعالمين) is attached to (ذكر) or is a naʿt of it. (لمن) is a badal from His saying (للعالمين), with repetition of the governor, which is the lām. The clause (شاء) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من); (منكم) is a ḥāl; and (أن) with what is in its scope is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (شاء).
(وَما تَشاؤُنَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, (ما) is negative, (تشاءون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is its fāʿil, and (إلا) is a particle of restriction. (أن) and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تشاءون). (الله) is the fāʿil, and (رب العالمين) is a badal or naʿt of (الله). Al-Bayḍāwī preferred making the interpreted maṣdar accusative as an adverb (ẓarfiyya); his wording: "And you do not will uprightness, O you who will it, except that Allah wills — i.e. except at the time that Allah wills your willing; so to Him belongs the favour, and the right is upon you for your uprightness."

* Benefits:
The exegetes differed. A great multitude of them held that what is meant by the noble messenger here, down to the last of the attributes, is Muḥammad ﷺ; if the matter is so, that is Allah's customary favour upon His Prophet. A great multitude of them also held that what is meant by it is Jibrīl, upon him be peace. Disagreement has arisen over the relative merit of the angels and the messengers. The well-known position of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī is to prefer the messengers, and the doctrine of the Muʿtazila is to prefer the angels. However, those who differed agreed that it is not permissible to prefer either of the two exalted groups in a way that implies disparaging a specific one of the angels or a specific one of the messengers, because even though preference is established, specifying [the one surpassed] is hurtful to the one surpassed. On this the skilled scholars interpreted his saying ﷺ: "Do not prefer me over Yūnus ibn Mattā," i.e. do not specify one surpassed in particular; for preference in general is established by the consensus of the Muslims, i.e. the preference of the Prophet ﷺ over all the prophets together. Ibn Fāris, may Allah have mercy on him, used to clarify this with an example, saying: if you said in the presence of a group of jurists, "So-and-so is the best of the people of his age," the group would bear this preference, even though it entails their inclusion among those surpassed; but if you specified one of them and said, "So-and-so is better than you," the hurt would quickly reach some of you.
Al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī said: "It has been used as evidence for the superiority of Jibrīl over Muḥammad, upon both of them be blessing and peace, since He enumerated the excellences of Jibrīl and limited Himself to denying madness of him ﷺ. That is weak, since what is intended by it is to refute their saying 'it is only a human being who teaches him' and 'has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?', not to enumerate their merits and weigh them against each other."
As for al-Karkhī, he said: "Then, if you look closely, you will realize that applying those attributes to Jibrīl in this setting is an insertion (idmāj) of the glorification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he reached such standing and loftiness of rank with the Lord of the Throne that the envoy between Him and him was made one like this angel, brought near, obeyed and trustworthy. So the statement of these attributes, with respect to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is an elevation of rank for him, just like the statement 'with the Lord of the Throne' with respect to the elevation of the rank of Jibrīl, upon him be peace."
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he produced something which perhaps Jibrīl, Allah's blessings be upon him, would not have been pleased with, a shortcoming in the right of the bearer of good news and the warner, by saying: "This suffices you as evidence of the standing of Jibrīl, upon him be peace, and his superiority over the angels, and of the difference from the rank of the best of humans, Muḥammad ﷺ, if you weigh the two mentions when He paired them, and compare His saying: إنه لقول رسول كريم، ذي قوة عند ذي العرش مكين، مطاع ثم أمين with His saying: وما صاحبكم بمجنون."
Ibn al-Munayyir, as is his habit, refuted al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "Then the discussion returns to the verse, after granting that Jibrīl is meant and after we entrust to Allah [the reckoning for] his specifying the Prophet ﷺ and counting him the one surpassed. We say: no attribute is mentioned in it but the Prophet ﷺ has its like. The first of them is رسول كريم; He said with respect to him ﷺ at the end of Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa: إنه لقول رسول كريم. It has also been said that Jibrīl is meant there, but His saying وما هو بقول شاعر rejects that, and al-Zamakhsharī agreed with that earlier. So this is the first of the attributes [Translator's note: the source has الفوت, apparently for النعوت] and the greatest of them. As for His saying ذي قوة, it is not the point of dispute, since there is no contention that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, has superiority in bodily strength; whoever uproots cities with a feather of his wing — there is no disputing the superiority of his strength over the strength of humans; this has been said in explaining His saying ذو مرة فاستوى. As for His saying عند ذي العرش مكين مطاع ثم أمين, the obedience of the angels has also been established [Translator's note: the source prints نبتت for ثبتت] for our Prophet ﷺ. It has come that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, said to the Prophet: 'Allah conveys greetings of peace to you, and He has ordered the angel of the mountains to obey you,' when Quraysh harmed him; so the angel greeted him and said: 'If you order me to bring the two mountains (al-Akhshabān) together upon them, I will do it'; but the Prophet ﷺ was patient and sought the reward. The greatest and noblest of that is his Praised Station in the Great Intercession, on the day when no one goes before him, when Allah the Exalted will say to him: 'Raise your head; speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' As for أمين, he said: 'By Allah, I am trustworthy on earth and trustworthy in heaven.' And sufficient for you is His saying وما هو على الغيب بظنين: if you read it with the ẓāʾ, its meaning is that he ﷺ is trustworthy over the unseen and not suspected; and if you read it with the ḍād, it goes back to generosity. So how can one argue for preference by means of attributes shared equally by the superior and the surpassed?"

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «والليل إذا عسعس والصبح إذا تنفس» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). He likened the night to a person who advances and retreats, then omitted the thing compared to [Translator's note: the source says المشبه (the thing compared), though in an implicit metaphor it is the المشبه به that is omitted] and took one of its attributes, namely the word عسعس, i.e. it advanced and retreated. Likewise He likened the morning to a living being that breathes, omitted [the thing compared to], and brought one of its attributes, namely breathing, i.e. the exit of breath from the interior. Or it may be said that He likened the night to a distressed, grieving person who is confined so that he does not move; when he breathes, he finds his relief. Here, when the morning rises, it is as though it has been entirely freed from grief, so that was expressed by breathing.
2- In His saying «فلا أقسم بالخنس الجوار الكنس» there is the device of al-iltizām (self-imposed constraint), for the nūn is kept before the sīn.

﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ sözü. "يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ" şeklinde de okunmuştur. Ref' ile okuyan, "اليوم"in "يَوْمُ الدِّينِ" sözünün sıfatı olması esasına göre okumuştur. Takdir edilen "هُوَ" ile merfû olması da caizdir; bu durumda mâna "هُوَ يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا" (O, hiçbir nefsin bir nefis için hiçbir şeye malik olmadığı gündür) olur. "لا تَمْلِكُ" sözüne izâfe edilmesi sebebiyle fetha üzere mebnî olup ref' mahallinde olması da caizdir; çünkü mütemekkin olmayana izâfe edilen şey, ref' veya cer mahallinde olsa bile bazen fetha üzere mebnî kılınır. Şairin şöyle dediği gibi:
لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Meyveli dallarda bir güvercinin ötmesinden başka hiçbir şey ondan içmeye engel olmadı.)
"غير"i "أنْ نَطَقَتْ"e izâfe etmiş ve onu fetha üzere mebnî kılmıştır. Onun nasbının, zikredilen bu şeylerin mânası üzere olması da caizdir; (bu durumda) ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ olur [Mütercim notu: Kaynak metin burada eksik kesilmektedir.].

(وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ): İbn Ebû Talha, İbn Abbâs'tan rivayet etti; şöyle dedi: "بحثرت" (altı üstüne getirildi) diyor. Ferrâ bunu, yerin altı üstüne getirilip içindeki hazineleri ve ölüleri dışarı attığı şeklinde te'vil etmiş ve «تلقي الأرض أفلاذ كبدها» (Yer ciğerinin parçalarını dışarı atacak) hadisini delil getirmiştir. Ebû Ca'fer dedi ki: Bu bir hatâdır. Kur'ân'da "وإذا الأرض" yoktur; burada özellikle kabirler (söz konusu)dur. «وتلقي أفلاذ كبدها» hadisinin ahir zamanda olduğu ve kıyamet günü olmadığı hususunda ilim ehli arasında ihtilaf yoktur.
[Mütercim notu: Kaynakta ikinci alıntıda «أفلا كبدها» yazılmıştır; «أفلاذ» yanlış basımıdır.]

Ferrâ, Medine ehlinden bazılarından «بل يكذبون» nakletmiş ve onu reddetmiştir; çünkü ondan sonra [Mütercim notu: kaynak metin burada kesilmiştir; devamı bir sonraki girdidedir: «وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ», muhatap sîgasıyla]
Hasan b. Vâkıd dedi ki: Yani «معتد» (haddi aşan) kendi sözünde, «أثيم» (günahkâr) ise Rabbinin katındadır.

Al-Ḥasan ibn Wāqid said: i.e. a transgressor in his speech, a sinner in the sight of his Lord. [Translator's note: the known transmitter of this name is al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid; the source reads «الحسن بن واقد».]

﴿خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ﴾: Mübtedâ ve haberidir. Bu, insanların çoğunun kıraatidir. Kisâî ise —Ebû Ubeyd'in ondan rivayet ettiğine göre— «خاتمه مسك» şeklinde okumuş ve bu kıraatin Ali b. Ebî Tâlib'in (Allah ondan razı olsun) kıraati olduğunu ileri sürmüştür. İsmâîl b. İshâk ise bunu Ali b. Ebî Tâlib'den (Allah ondan razı olsun) bilen hiç kimseyi bulamadığını zikretmiştir. İbrâhîm b. Mûsâ'ya, Muhammed b. el-Cehm'den, o Yahyâ b. Ziyâd'dan, o Muhammed b. el-Fadl'dan, o Atâ b. es-Sâib'den, o Ebû Abdurrahmân es-Sülemî'den, o da Ali b. Ebî Tâlib'den (Allah ondan razı olsun) onun «خاتمه مسك» şeklinde okuduğu okunmuştur. Ebû Ca'fer der ki: (خاتمه ile) ختامه aynı anlamdadır; ancak «ختام» masdardır, «خاتم» ise ism-i fâildir. İnsanlar ve onlara benzeyenler hakkında Arapların sözlerinin çoğu «هو خاتمهم» şeklindedir; nitekim Allah celle ve azze ﴿وَلكِنْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ [el-Ahzâb: 40] buyurmuştur; aynı şekilde «خاتم» denir. İnsanlar dışındakiler için ise «ختام» kullanılır; nitekim şair şöyle demiştir: [el-Kâmil] 552-
أغلي السّباء بكلّ أدكن عاتق ... أو جونة قدحت وفضّ ختامها
(Her koyu renkli, eski şarap tulumu ya da kepçeyle alınıp mührü açılan her siyah küp için şaraba yüksek fiyat öderim.)
﴿وَفِي ذلِكَ فَلْيَتَنافَسِ الْمُتَنافِسُونَ﴾: Yani hırsla istesin ve talep etsin. Bunun aslı «نفست عليه بالشيء» sözündendir, yani "o şeyin ona değil bana ait olmasını istedim". İştikakı «النّفس»tendir; yani nefsin sevindiği ve meylettiği şey.

His saying: {أَلا يَظُنُّ}: The apparent view is that it is the «ألا» of urging (taḥḍīḍ): He urged them to that, and «الظنّ» then means certainty. It was also said: it is the negating «لا» into which the interrogative hamza has entered. [Translator's note: the text reads «هل لا النافية»; «هل» is evidently a misprint.]

His saying: {مِن رَّحِيقٍ}: al-raḥīq is the drink in which there is no adulteration; it has also been said: the finest wine. Ḥassān said:
4517 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... بَرَدى يُصَفِّقُ بالرَّحيقِ السَّلْسَلِ
(… [the water of the river Baradā] is blended with pure wine that flows easily down the throat.) [Translator's note: The first hemistich of the verse is not given in the source.]

* Vocabulary:
(لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) التطفيف: short-changing in measure and weight, because what is withheld is something slight (طفيف) and paltry. طفف المكيال: he diminished the measure slightly. Al-Zajjāj said: "The one who diminishes the measure and the balance was called مطفف only because he hardly steals from the measure and the balance anything but a small, slight amount."
(اكْتالُوا) Al-Farrāʾ said: one says اكتلت على الناس: I took full measure from them; and اكتلت منهم: I took what was due from them; so على has the meaning of من.
(سِجِّينٍ) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: Allah has reported of the record of the wicked that it is in سجين, and has explained سجين as a written record, so it is as though it were said: their record is in a written record — what does that mean? I say: سجين is a comprehensive book; it is the register of evil, in which Allah has recorded the deeds of the devils and the deeds of the disbelievers and the corrupt among jinn and humans. It is a written record, inscribed and clearly written, or marked, so that whoever sees it knows there is no good in it. So the meaning is that what is written of the deeds of the wicked is established in that register.
