It was named سجين, a faʿīl from السجن, which is imprisonment and constriction, because it is a cause of imprisonment and constriction in Hell," until he says: "If you say: what is سجين — is it an adjective or a noun? I say: rather, it is a proper noun transferred from an adjective, like حاتم, and it is triptote, because there is only one cause [of diptosis] in it, namely definiteness."
Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "As for سجين, the majority said it is a faʿīl from السجن, like سكير; or in place of ساجن, so it came as an intensive form; on this view سجين is an adjective of an omitted place. Ibn Muqbil said:
ورفقة يضربون البيض ضاحية ... ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجينا
(And a band of companions striking the helmets in broad daylight, with a lasting, severe blow which the heroes enjoined one another.)"
Then he cited what al-Zamakhsharī said, and said: "They differed over سجين, if it is a place, in a confused disagreement whose mention we have omitted. The apparent sense is that سجين is a book, and that is why كتاب مرقوم was made a badal (substitute) from it. ʿIkrima said: سجين is an expression for loss and abasement, as you say 'So-and-so has reached rock bottom' when he has become utterly inert. Some lexicographers said: the nūn of سجين is a substitute for a lām, and it is from السجل (the register). It is thus summarized from their statements that the nūn of سجين is either radical or a substitute for a lām; if it is radical, its derivation is from السجن."
The author of al-Qāmūs cited under the root سجن the following text: "And [سجين], like سكين: the lasting, the severe; a place in which is the record of the wicked; a valley in Hell — may Allah the Exalted protect us from it; or a rock in the seventh earth."
(مَرْقُومٌ) written, inscribed. The basic meaning of الرقم is writing; and from it is the poet's saying:
سأرقم في الماء القراح إليكم ... على بعدكم إن كان للماء راقم
(I shall write to you on clear water, despite your distance, if water has anyone who can write on it.)

* I'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what licenses beginning with it is its being an imprecation; and (للمطففين) is its khabar (predicate). Had it been accusative, that would have been permissible. It has been said: "The preferred form for ويل and its like, when it is not in a genitive construct, is the nominative, and the accusative is permissible; if it is in a construct or made definite, the preferred form is the accusative, as in ويلكم لا تغترّوا."
(الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ) (الذين) is an adjective of (المطففين). (إذا) is an adverb for future time containing the meaning of condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its implied form being "they took from them". The clause (اكتالوا) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (على الناس) is attached to (اكتالوا); it has also been said that it is attached to (يستوفون), the object having been placed before the verb only to convey specificity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Since their taking measure was a taking of measure that harmed [people] and in which they were imposed upon, على was substituted in place of من to indicate that. It may also be attached to يستوفون, the object being placed before the verb to convey specificity, i.e. they take full measure from people in particular; as for themselves, they take full measure for them." Ibn Hishām made «على» mean «من», agreeing in that with al-Zamakhsharī. The clause (يستوفون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the omitted apodosis, i.e. they took from them, taking full measure.
(وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction. (إذا) is an adverb for future time attached to the omitted apodosis, its implied form being "they took full measure for it". The clause (كالوهم) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (كالوهم) is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ [i.e. هم] is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. they measured the food out for them. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم) and parsed in parallel with it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "The pronoun in كالوهم أو وزنوهم is an accusative pronoun referring to الناس, and there are two views on it: that what is meant is كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined directly, as he said:
ولقد جنيتك أكمؤا وعساقلا ... ولقد نهيتك عن نبات الأوبر
(I gathered truffles and ʿasāqil for you, and I forbade you the daughters of Awbar.)"
جنى is transitive only to one object, and to the second by means of the lām; so the original is جنيت لك, with the preposition omitted and the pronoun joined directly; or it was made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of انجتك [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently a corruption of a verb such as أجنيتك or أنلتك] and so made transitive to both. الأكمؤ is the plural of كمء, like أفلس; it is the singular of الكمأة, which is a large kind of plant called "the fat of the earth"; it was called كمأة because of its being known by it. العساقل is the plural of عسقول, like عصفور; its due form was عساقيل, but the yāʾ was dropped for the metre. It has been said that it is the plural of عسقل, which is a small, good, white kind of it. بنات أوبر are a poor, black, downy kind of it, as though it had fur on it; it has been said that it is a species resembling colocasia or turnip. بنات أوبر is the plural of ابن أوبر, because it is a proper name for something non-rational, and the al in it is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Mubarrad said: it is a generic noun. The verse is of the type of allegory (tamthīl) for the state of one who was urged towards the good but turned aside to the bad, then came back regretting its outcome. We return to what we are about, and say: among examples of what is accusative by removal of the preposition is their saying الحريص يصيدك لا الجواد ("the eager one catches for you, not the generous one"), the original being يصيد لك. What has been said, that هم is a nominative pronoun emphasizing the wāw in (كالوهم), is a mistake. (أو) is a conjunction, and (وزنوهم) is conjoined to (كالوهم); the same is said in its parsing as was said about (كالوهم), i.e. وزنوا لهم. Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "كال and وزن are among the verbs made transitive by a preposition; so you say كلت لك and وزنت لك, and the lām may be omitted, as in your saying نصحت لك and نصحتك, شكرت لك and شكرتك. The pronoun is an accusative pronoun, i.e. كالوا لهم ووزنوا لهم, with the preposition omitted and the verb joined by itself; and the object, which is what is measured or weighed, is omitted." The clause (يخسرون) is a ḥāl from the omitted apodosis.
(أَلا يَظُنُّ أُولئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, (لا) is negative, and (يظن) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ). الظن here means certainty, i.e. are those not certain? Had they been certain, they would not have diminished the measure and the weight. (أولئك) is the fāʿil, the reference being to those who give short measure. (أنّ) with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of (يظن). (أنّ) and its noun; (مبعوثون) is its khabar; and (ليوم) is attached to (مبعوثون), or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and it is indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa only because of its annexation to the verb [Translator's note: this remark evidently refers to the alternative of (يوم يقوم) being in the nominative position yet ending in fatḥa; it is so placed in the source]. (عظيم) is a naʿt (adjective). (يوم) is a badal from (ليوم), following it in position; its position is accusative by the mentioned (مبعوثون) or by an implied verb like it, because the badal is on the intention of repeating the governor. The clause (يقوم الناس) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and (لرب العالمين) is attached to (يقوم). It is reported of Ibn ʿUmrān [Translator's note: so in the source; the report is known of Ibn ʿUmar] that he recited this sūra, and when he reached His saying يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين he wept aloud and was unable to recite what came after it. It is reported of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān that a Bedouin said to him: "You have heard what Allah said about those who give short measure" — by that he meant: the one who gives short measure has had this tremendous threat, which you have heard, directed at him; so what do you think of yourself, when you take the wealth of the Muslims without measure or weight?
(كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتابَ الفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ وَما أَدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ) (كلا) is a rebuke and restraint for them from giving short measure and from heedlessness of the Reckoning and the Resurrection. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (في سجين) is the khabar of (إنّ). (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar. (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ, and (سجين) is the khabar; the nominal clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of (أدراك). (كتاب) is a badal from (سجين), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a written record"; and (مرقوم) is an adjective of (كتاب). If (سجين) is considered the name of a place, then the khabar reading is preferable, or one assumes an annexed noun omitted before (سجين), so as to ward off the objection: سجين is the name of a place, so how can it be explained as a written record?
(وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ) (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ, as has preceded; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to (ويل); (للمكذبين) is the khabar; (الذين) is a naʿt of (المكذبين); the clause (يكذبون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين); and (بيوم الدين) is attached to (يكذبون).
(وَما يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ) The wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) is negative; (يكذب) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (به) is attached to (يكذب); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (كل معتد أثيم) is the fāʿil of (يكذب).
(إِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِ آياتُنا قالَ أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to its apodosis, which is (قال). The clause (تتلى) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (عليه) is attached to (تتلى); and (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تتلى). The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (إذا). (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. هي. It has preceded that الأساطير is the plural of أسطورة or أساطرة [Translator's note: so in the source; usually given as إسطارة], with kasra, which is a tale written down long ago.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «الذين إذا اكتالوا على الناس يستوفون وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون» there is antithesis (muqābala), which came in the finest and most orderly way: i.e. when the measuring is on the part of others, they take it in full, and when the measuring is on their own part in particular, they make it deficient, whether they carry it out themselves or not. The pronoun does not indicate carrying out personally, nor does it hint at that. What shows you that the pronoun does not convey carrying out the act personally is that you may say: "The rulers are the ones who carry out the prescribed punishments, not the common people," and you do not mean that they carry it out themselves; its meaning is only that doing that is on their part in particular. It has been said that the people of Medina were merchants who gave short measure, and their sales were al-munābadha [Translator's note: the source prints المنابزة, for المنابذة], al-mulāmasa and al-mukhāṭara. So it was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and recited it to them and said: "Five for five." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break the covenant but Allah sets their enemy over them; they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed but poverty spreads among them; indecency does not appear among them but death spreads among them; they do not give short measure but they are denied vegetation and seized with years of famine; and they do not withhold the zakāt but rain is held back from them." It has also been said that it was revealed about a man known as Abū Juhayna who had two ṣāʿ-measures: he measured out with one and took measure with the other, i.e. he took with one and gave with the other.

* Vocabulary:
(رانَ): it overcame, encompassed and covered, as clouds cover the sky. In al-Mukhtār: "al-rayn is the seal and the filth. One says rāna dhanbuhu ʿalā qalbihi (his sin overlaid his heart), of the pattern bāʿa (rāna yarīnu); and rayūnan also means it overcame." Abū ʿUbayda said: "Whatever overcomes you has rāna bika, rānaka and rāna ʿalayka. A man is rīna when he falls into something he cannot get out of and has no power over." Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "﴿رانَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: it mounted them as rust mounts, and overcame them. That is, he persists in major sins and keeps postponing repentance until his heart is sealed, so that it neither accepts good nor inclines to it. On the authority of al-Ḥasan: it is sin upon sin until the heart turns black. One says rāna ʿalayhi al-dhanb and ghāna ʿalayhi, rayn and ghayn; and al-dhayn [Translator's note: the source prints الذين; in context read الغين, al-ghayn] is cloud. One says rāna fīhi al-nawm (sleep settled deep in him), and rānat bihi al-khamr (wine carried him away)." I say: rāna is of the yāʾ-type and the wāw-type; here it is of the yāʾ-type. One says rāna yarīnu raynan and rayūnan, said of a thing, such a person, "upon him" and "with him": it overcame him. You say rāna hawāhu ʿalā qalbihi, i.e. his desire overcame it; rānat nafsuhu: his soul became foul and clouded over; rāna al-mawt ʿalayhi and bihi: death took him away; rīna bihi: he fell into what he cannot get out of and has no strength for, and died, and fell into distress; arāna, irānatan, of a people: their cattle perished, so they are murīnūn. Al-rān is a shoe like the khuff but longer. Al-rayna is wine, because it overcomes the intellect.
As for the wāw-type, one says rāna yarūnu raunan (of the pattern dakhala) of a matter: it became severe; rānat al-layla: its terror or gloom became severe. Al-raun (with a doubled, damma-vowelled rāʾ) is hardship, plural ruʾūn; rawnat al-shayʾ (with damma) is its greater part and its severity. One says "may Allah remove from you the rawna of this matter," i.e. its severity and gloom. Al-arūnān means the hard thing. One says al-arūnān and al-arūnānī for what is severe in anything: heat, cold, uproar, shouting, grief and joy; its feminine is arūnāna and arūnāniyya.
(عِلِّيُّونَ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ʿIlliyyūn is a proper name for the register of good in which is recorded everything that the angels and the righteous of the two weighty races (jinn and mankind) have done. It is transferred from the plural of ʿilliyy, a faʿīl form from al-ʿulūw (height), like sijjīn from al-sijn. It was so named either because it is the cause of ascent to the highest degrees in Paradise, or because it is raised up in the seventh heaven where the cherubim dwell, in honour and veneration of it." Abū Ḥayyān's wording: ʿilliyyūn is a plural whose singular is ʿilliyy, derived from al-ʿulūw, being an intensive form; this was said by Yūnus and Ibn Jinnī. Abū al-Fatḥ said: the proper form would be ʿilliyya, as they call the upper room ʿilliyya; when the tāʾ was dropped they compensated for it with the plural in wāw and nūn. It was also said that it is a description of the angels, which is why it is pluralised with wāw and nūn. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a noun set down on the plural pattern, with no singular from its own wording, like ʿishrīn and thalāthīn; when the Arabs form a plural that has no singular pattern and no dual, they use wāw and nūn for both masculine and feminine. Al-Zajjāj said: this noun is declined like the plural: "this is Qinnasrūn" and "I saw Qinnasrīn." Ibn Hishām said in the discussion of what is attached to the sound masculine plural: "The fourth is what is used as a name from these plurals and what is attached to it, such as ʿilliyyūn," that is, it is attached to this plural and is used as a name for the highest part of Paradise. Al-Rāghib said: it was said to be the name of the noblest of the gardens, just as sijjīn is the noblest of the fires; and it was said that in reality it is the name of its inhabitants, which is closer to Arabic since this plural is specific to rational beings and the singular is ʿilliyy; its meaning is that the righteous are among these.

* I'rab:
(كَلَّا بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ): كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproof to the sinful transgressor against that false statement, and a denial of him in it; بل is a conjunction and particle of rejection (iḍrāb); رانَ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ is attached to رانَ; ما is the agent (fāʿil); the clause كانُوا is a clause with no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; كان and its subject, and the clause يَكْسِبُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. (كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ): كلا is likewise a particle of rebuke and reproof against the earning that has overlaid their hearts; إن and its noun; عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ is attached to مَحْجُوبُونَ; يَوْمَئِذٍ is an adverbial (ẓarf) annexed to its like, also attached to مَحْجُوبُونَ; مَحْجُوبُونَ is the predicate of إن; the tanwīn in إذ is a compensation for a clause whose implied form is "on the day when the people rise". The meaning of "veiled" will come under the section on Rhetoric. (ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصالُوا الْجَحِيمِ): ثم is a conjunction denoting distance in rank, for burning in Hell is worse than humiliation and deprivation of mercy and honour; إن and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); صالُوا الْجَحِيمِ is the predicate of إن. (ثُمَّ يُقالُ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ): ثم is a conjunction denoting sequence and distance as well; يُقالُ is an imperfect passive verb, and the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِي its khabar; the clause كُنْتُمْ is a ṣila; كان and its subject; بِهِ is attached to تُكَذِّبُونَ, and the clause تُكَذِّبُونَ is the predicate of كُنْتُمْ. (كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتابَ الْأَبْرارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ وَما أَدْراكَ ما عِلِّيُّونَ): كلا is an emphasis of the rebuke and of the obligation to desist; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; فِي عِلِّيِّينَ is its predicate, and the sign of the genitive in عِلِّيِّينَ is the yāʾ in place of the kasra because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause أَدْراكَ is its khabar; ما is an interrogative noun for magnification and exaltation, mubtadaʾ, and عِلِّيُّونَ is the khabar, its sign of nominative being the wāw in place of the damma because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; the clause suspended by the interrogative fills the place of the second object of أَدْراكَ. (كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ): كِتابٌ is a badal of عِلِّيُّونَ, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, which is preferable; مَرْقُومٌ is an adjective (naʿt) of كِتابٌ, and the clause يَشْهَدُهُ is a second naʿt; the hāʾ is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) and الْمُقَرَّبُونَ is the agent. (إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to begin on the merits of their conditions; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; فِي نَعِيمٍ is its predicate; عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ is attached to يَنْظُرُونَ, and the clause يَنْظُرُونَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the predicate of إن, or is resumptive. What is meant by الأرائك is the couches in the canopies, and al-ḥijāl, as al-Jawharī says, is the plural of ḥijla (with vowelled letters), whose singular is ḥijāl al-ʿarūs, a chamber adorned with cloths and beds. Al-Shihāb said: al-ḥajla (with two fatḥas) is a square chamber of fine cloths hung over the bed, called in common usage al-nāmūsiyya, i.e. the curtain. (تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to notify the one addressed to turn to them and contemplate the traces of bliss on their faces. It was also read in the passive, in which case نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ is the deputy agent; فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ is attached to تَعْرِفُ, and نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ is the direct object. (يُسْقَوْنَ مِنْ رَحِيقٍ مَخْتُومٍ خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ وَفِي ذلِكَ فَلْيَتَنافَسِ الْمُتَنافِسُونَ): يُسْقَوْنَ is an imperfect passive verb, the wāw is the deputy agent; مِنْ رَحِيقٍ is attached to يُسْقَوْنَ; مَخْتُومٍ is a naʿt, that is, wine pure of every impurity or adulteration; خِتامُهُ مِسْكٌ is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, the clause being a second naʿt of رَحِيقٍ. The apparent sense is that the rahīq is sealed to ensure cleanliness and a musky fragrance, as he explains afterwards. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "al-khitām is the clay with which one seals," and Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd said likewise: its vessel is sealed with musk instead of clay. He said:
كأن مشعشعا من خمر بصرى ... نمته البحت مشدود الختام
(As if it were a diluted wine of Buṣrā, pure ones bred it, its seal fastened.)
The wāw is a conjunction; فِي ذلِكَ is attached to the phrase فَلْيَتَنافَسِ; the fāʾ is a conjunction for added emphasis; the lām is the lām of command; يَتَنافَسِ is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām; الْمُتَنافِسُونَ is the agent. In al-Mukhtār: "nafusa al-shayʾ (of the pattern ẓarufa): it became desirable; nāfasa fī al-shayʾ, munāfasatan and nifāsan (with kasra), when he desired it in a spirit of rivalry in generosity; tanāfasū fīhi: they desired it." (وَمِزاجُهُ مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; مِزاجُهُ is a mubtadaʾ and مِنْ تَسْنِيمٍ its khabar. It is a proper name of a specific spring, named al-tasnīm, which is the maṣdar of sannamahu, "he raised it", because it comes to them from above; as reported, it flows through the air, and they drink it pure, those brought near, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. It was also said that it was named al-tasnīm because it is the highest drink in Paradise. عَيْناً is accusative as praise by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I praise"; al-Zajjāj said: it is accusative as a ḥāl from تَسْنِيمٍ since it is described as a proper name. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said that tasnīm is a maṣdar and it is what puts عَيْناً in the accusative." Al-Akhfash said: "they are given to drink a spring."
The clause يَشْرَبُ is a naʿt of عَيْناً, and بِها is attached to يَشْرَبُ, i.e. "from it", on the view that the implication (taḍmīn) lies in the particle; or the implication lies in the verb, i.e. he delights in it; الْمُقَرَّبُونَ is the agent of يَشْرَبُ. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ): a resumptive utterance, introduced to console the believers and strengthen their hearts with what has been prepared for the righteous in Paradise. إن and its noun; the clause أَجْرَمُوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; the clause كانُوا is the predicate of إن; كان and its subject; مِنَ الَّذِينَ is attached to يَضْحَكُونَ, and the clause يَضْحَكُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. The polytheists of Mecca, such as Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil and their followers, used to laugh at ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl and others of the poor believers and mock them. It was also said that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, came with a group of believers and the hypocrites mocked them, laughed and winked at one another, then returned to their companions and said, "Today we saw the bald one," and laughed at him. (وَإِذا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغامَزُونَ وَإِذَا انْقَلَبُوا إِلى أَهْلِهِمُ انْقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverbial containing the sense of a condition, attached to يَتَغامَزُونَ; the clause مَرُّوا بِهِمْ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause يَتَغامَزُونَ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. إذا is again a future adverbial; the clause انْقَلَبُوا is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; إِلى أَهْلِهِمُ is attached to انْقَلَبُوا; the clause انْقَلَبُوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; فَكِهِينَ is a ḥāl, i.e. delighted with themselves. It was also read فاكِهِينَ, i.e. rejoicing and luxuriating. (وَإِذا رَأَوْهُمْ قالُوا إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَضالُّونَ): the wāw is likewise a conjunction; إذا is a future adverbial; the clause رَأَوْهُمْ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; the clause قالُوا has no grammatical position. The nominative pronoun refers to the believers and the accusative to the sinners, i.e. when the believers see the sinners they ascribe error to them; the reverse is permissible. إن with its noun and predicate; the clause is the content of what they said. (وَما أُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حافِظِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in قالُوا; ما is negative; أُرْسِلُوا is a passive past verb, the wāw being the deputy agent; عَلَيْهِمْ is attached to حافِظِينَ, and حافِظِينَ is a ḥāl. (فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction of consequence; الْيَوْمَ is an adverbial attached to يَضْحَكُونَ; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آمَنُوا is a ṣila; مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ is likewise attached to يَضْحَكُونَ; the clause يَضْحَكُونَ is the khabar of الَّذِينَ; عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ is attached to يَنْظُرُونَ; the clause يَنْظُرُونَ is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يَضْحَكُونَ, i.e. they laugh while looking at them and at the abasement and humiliation they are in. (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ): the clause is the content of an omitted saying, i.e. "they say: has it been requited..." They also allowed that the clause be suspended by the interrogative, in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. ثُوِّبَ is a passive past verb and الْكُفَّارُ is the deputy agent; ثُوِّبَ here means requital, i.e. "have they been rewarded," or it is from thāba meaning "to return," because thawāb is what returns to a person in return for his deed. ما is in the position of an accusative, a second direct object; the clause كانُوا is the ṣila of ما, and the clause يَفْعَلُونَ is the predicate of كانُوا. Aws said:
سأجزيك أو يجزيك عنّي مثوب ... وحسبك أن يثني عليك وتحمدي
(I shall repay you, or one who rewards will repay you on my behalf; and it suffices you that you be praised and commended.)

* Rhetoric:
In the words «كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ» there is a representation (tamthīl) of the contempt and humiliation shown them, for permission to enter upon people of high rank and lofty station is given only to the honoured ones brought near to them, and only the lowly, marked by baseness, contemptibility and smallness, are barred from them. Abū Tammām gazed at the sky of this meaning when he justified al-Muʿtaṣim's withdrawal from his subjects:
ليس الحجاب بمقص عنك لي أملا ... إن السماء ترجى حين تحتجب
(The veil does not remove from you any hope of mine; the sky is hoped for even when it is veiled.)

{وَإِذَا قُرِىءَ} kavli: Şarttır; «لا يَسْجُدون» da onun cevabıdır. Bu şart cümlesi de, kendisinden öncekine atfen nesak yoluyla, hâl olarak nasb mahallindedir; yani: «فمالهم إذا قُرىء عليهم القرآن لا يَسْجُدون؟» (Onlara ne oluyor ki, kendilerine Kur'an okunduğunda secde etmiyorlar?).

* Vocabulary:
(وَأَذِنَتْ): it listened to His command. One says "adhintu laka," i.e. I listened to your speech. In the Ḥadīth: "Allah has not listened to anything as He listens to a prophet chanting the Qur'an melodiously." The poet said:
صم إذا سمعوا خيرا ذكرت به ... وإن ذكرت بسوء عندهم أذنوا
(Deaf, when they hear the good with which I am mentioned; but if I am mentioned with evil in their presence, they listen.)
In al-Mukhtār: "adhina lahu: he listened; its pattern is ṭariba, and from it the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وَحُقَّتْ﴾." One says adhina yaʾdhanu adhanan ilayhi and lahu: he listened to it admiringly, or generally; and of the smell of food, he desired it. Adhina bi-l-shayʾ (like samiʿa), idhnan (with kasra, or with vowelling) and adhānan and adhānatan: he knew of it; fa-ʾdhanū bi-ḥarb means "be aware of war." Ādhanahu al-amr and bihi: he informed him. Adhdhana tāʾdhīnan: he made much announcement. Of a person: he rubbed his ear and turned him back from drinking, so he did not give him to drink; of a sandal and the like: he made an ear for it. "He did it with my idhn and adhīn," i.e. with my knowledge. Adhina lahu fī al-shayʾ (like samiʿa), idhnan (with kasra) and adhīnan: he permitted it to him. Istaʾdhanahu: he asked his permission... and so on to the end of this wondrous root.
(كادِحٌ): striving in your work. Al-kadḥ is the exertion of the soul in work and toil in it until it leaves a mark on it, from kadaḥa jildahu, when he scratched it. In al-Mukhtār: "al-kadḥ is work, effort, toil and earning, and it is also scratching, the pattern of all of it being qaṭaʿa. And the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿إِنَّكَ كادِحٌ إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ mean striving; wa-bi-wajhihi kudūḥ means scratches; huwa yakdaḥu li-ʿiyālihi wa-yaktadiḥu: he earns." Among the curiosities of the kāf and dāl is that when they occur as the first and middle letters of a word, they indicate exertion, perseverance and effect. One says "so-and-so is kadūd": he drives himself in work and wearies himself. By figurative usage: kadda lisānahu bi-l-kalām and qalbahu bi-l-fikr; kaddat al-dawābb al-arḍ bi-l-ḥawāfir, and it is al-kadīd; and kardtu raʾsī wa-jildī bi-l-aẓfār when I scratched it with insistent scratching. From this is the saying of Kuthayyir:
غنيت فلم أرددكم عن بغيّة ... وجعت فلم أكددكم بالأصابع
(I was self-sufficient and did not turn you away from any desire, and I was hungry and did not drive you with my fingers.)
that is, I did not press you with requests. A well from which water is not reached except with exertion is called kadūd; likewise a she-camel kadūd and a man kadūd: his milk and his good are not obtained except after hardship. Ibn Hubayra used to say: "Kuddūnī, for I am mukidd," that is, ask me, for I give upon request. Kadira al-māʾ, on the authority of Ibn al-Aʿrābī, has the three forms; māʾ akdar and kadir is plainly turbid. By figurative usage: kadira ʿaynuhu and takaddara; "take what is clear and leave what is turbid"; kadira ʿalayya fulān, and he is kadir al-fuʾād toward me. He said:
وإني لمشتاق إلى ظل صاحب ... يرق ويصفو إن كدرت عليه
(I long for the shade of a companion who softens and grows clear when I am clouded toward him.)
And "he has a kuds of food" and akdās. Al-Mutalammis said:
لم تدر بصرى بما آليت من قسم ... ولا دمشق إذا ديس الكداديس
(Buṣrā did not know of the oath I swore, nor Damascus when the heaps were trodden.)
He meant al-akdās, and it is a collective noun. Kadasa al-ṭaʿām fa-takaddasa: heaping up food, and what is in it of weight and effort is not hidden. Kadamahu: he bit him with the edge of the mouth, and ḥimār mukaddam means bitten. And "he is dhū kudna and ʿabāla," meaning thickness and heaviness, and from this is al-kawdan, the Turkish pack-horse. Akdā al-ḥāfir: the hoof reached al-kudya, the hardness of the ground, which stopped it, like their saying ajbala al-ḥāfir. By figurative usage akdā al-rajul: he failed and did not obtain his need; and "so-and-so is mukidd, his wealth does not grow"... and so on to the end of what came from this root.
(ثُبُوراً): al-thubūr is destruction. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "thabara Allāh al-kāfir thubūran (of the pattern qaʿada): He destroyed him; and thabara huwa thubūran: he perished; it is both transitive and intransitive."
(يَحُورَ): to return. Al-Rāghib said: al-ḥawr is hesitation in a matter, and from it "we seek refuge in Allah from al-ḥawr after al-kawr," that is, from hesitation in a matter after having proceeded in it; muḥāwarat al-kalām is exchanging it back and forth; and al-ḥawr is the wood on which the pulley runs because it goes back and forth upon it. In al-Mukhtār: "ḥāra: he returned, and its pattern is qāla and dakhala"; the maṣdar is on the pattern qawl and dukhūl; one says ḥawran, ḥuʾūran, maḥāran and maḥāratan. Further, ḥāra comes in the sense of ṣāra (became), taking a nominative noun and an accusative predicate.

* I'rab:
(إِذَا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وَحُقَّتْ): إذا is an adverbial for future time; السَّماءُ is the agent of an omitted verb that what follows explains, the implied form being "when the sky splits, it splits," because conditional إذا is specifically entered before verbal clauses, and whatever comes in this form and the like is interpreted to preserve the rule of specificity, as was discussed in detail in Sūrat al-Takwīr. The clause انْشَقَّتْ is explicative, with no grammatical position; the omitted clause انْشَقَّتْ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. The apodosis of إذا is omitted; it was omitted to alert that it is something description cannot encompass, or so that the imagination may go every way. It was also said that its apodosis is what is indicated by فَمُلاقِيهِ, i.e. when the sky splits, man meets his toil. It was also said it has no apodosis, being accusative as the object of an omitted "mention" (udhkur), and so it is not conditional. The wāw is a conjunction; أَذِنَتْ is a past verb; لِرَبِّها is attached to أَذِنَتْ, i.e. it listened to Him; وحُقَّتْ is a passive past verb. Know that the agent in this construction is Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah made that due upon it, that is, its hearing and obedience; one says "he is fit (ḥaqīq) for such" and "he is entitled to it." The meaning is "it was fitting for it to do that." So the agent is omitted, namely Allah the Exalted, and the direct object is its hearing and obedience, which is not mentioned; the attribution in the verse is to the sky itself, so it needs an implied element, the implied form being "and it was made due," i.e. its hearing and obedience was made due, that is, Allah the Exalted made it due upon it, obligated it and bound it to it. This is the apparent sense. Al-Bayḍāwī allowed that the deputy agent be the pronoun of the sky latent in the verb, without implying anything; his words: "wa-ḥuqqat means 'it was made worthy of listening and submission.'" (وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ، وَأَلْقَتْ ما فِيها وَتَخَلَّتْ وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّها وَحُقَّتْ): a conjunction to what precedes, similar to it in its i'rab. (يا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسانُ إِنَّكَ كادِحٌ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَدْحاً فَمُلاقِيهِ): يا is a vocative particle; أَيُّ is an indefinite particular noun addressed, indeclinable on damma in the position of an accusative; the hāʾ is for alerting; الْإِنْسانُ is a badal; إن and its noun; كادِحٌ is its predicate; إِلى رَبِّكَ is attached to كادِحٌ. "إلى" here has the meaning of limit, i.e. the limit of your toil in good and evil ends in meeting your Lord, which is death. كَدْحاً is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); the fāʾ is a conjunction; مُلاقِيهِ is conjoined to كادِحٌ, and it may be the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so you are meeting it"; on the first view it is a conjoining of a single word to a single word, on the second a conjoining of clauses. (فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; أما is a particle of condition and detailing; مَنْ is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause أُوتِيَ is a ṣila with no position, and the deputy agent is a latent pronoun referring to مَنْ; كِتابَهُ is a second direct object; بِيَمِينِهِ is attached to أُوتِيَ. (فَسَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ حِساباً يَسِيراً): the fāʾ links to the apodosis of أما; سَوْفَ is a particle of futurity; يُحاسَبُ is an imperfect passive verb whose deputy agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; حِساباً is an absolute object and يَسِيراً is a naʿt of حِساباً. (وَيَنْقَلِبُ إِلى أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً): the wāw is a conjunction; يَنْقَلِبُ is an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; إِلى أَهْلِهِ is attached to يَنْقَلِبُ; مَسْرُوراً is a ḥāl; and the clause سَوْفَ يُحاسَبُ is the khabar of مَنْ. (وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ وَراءَ ظَهْرِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوا ثُبُوراً): a conjunction to the preceding clause, similar to it in i'rab. وَراءَ ظَهْرِهِ is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. he is given his book in his left hand from behind his back; the fāʾ links; the clause سَوْفَ يَدْعُوا ثُبُوراً is the khabar of مَنْ, and ثُبُوراً is the object of يَدْعُوا, i.e. he calls out for his destruction saying "yā thubūrāh," because calling on what is not rational is meant as a wish; so the "call" (duʿāʾ) here means a request by vocative. (وَيَصْلى سَعِيراً): conjoined to يَدْعُوا, and سَعِيراً is the object of يَصْلى. (إِنَّهُ كانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُوراً): a reason for what he meets; إن and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; فِي أَهْلِهِ is a ḥāl and مَسْرُوراً is the predicate of كان. (إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ يَحُورَ): a second reason; إن and its noun; the clause ظَنَّ is its predicate; ظن here means knowledge and certainty; أن is the lightened form of the heavy أن and its noun is the pronoun of the situation (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; يَحُورَ is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by لن; the clause لَنْ يَحُورَ is the predicate of أن, and أن with what is within its scope fills the place of the two objects of ظَنَّ. (بَلى إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كانَ بِهِ بَصِيراً): بَلى is a particle of reply affirming what follows a negation; إن and its noun; the clause كان is its predicate; بِهِ is attached to بَصِيراً and بَصِيراً is the predicate of كان; the clause of إن with what is within its scope is the response to an implied oath, or a reason for the affirmation of what follows لن that بَلى conveys.

* Rhetoric:
1- In «وأذنت لربها وحقّت» there is a metaphor with the likened-to omitted (istiʿāra makniyya): the state of the sky in its submission to the effect of Allah the Exalted's power, when He wished it to split, is likened to the submission of an obedient listener to a command; then the likened-to is omitted and the word for listening and hearing, used for its goal, is borrowed.
2- In «وألقت ما فيها وتخلت» there is a metaphor with the likened-to omitted (istiʿāra makniyya): the state of the earth is likened to that of a pregnant woman who casts out what is in her belly under hardship and terror; then the likened-to is omitted and the word for casting out is borrowed.

* Vocabulary:
(الشفق): Al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-shafaq is the redness seen in the west after the sun has set; with its disappearance the time of Maghrib ends and the time of ʿatama (the Ishāʾ prayer) begins, according to the generality of scholars, except what is reported from Abū Ḥanīfa in one of two narrations, that it is the whiteness; Asad ibn ʿAmr reported that he retracted it. It was named shafaq because of its fineness (riqqa); from it comes al-shafaqa for a person, which is tenderness of heart toward him." Al-Rāghib said: "al-shafaq is the mingling of the light of day with the blackness of night at sunset; and ishfāq is solicitude mixed with fear, because the one who feels it (mushfiq) loves the one he feels it for (mushfaq ʿalayhi) and fears what may befall him; when it is made transitive with min, the sense of fear in it is more evident, and when with ʿalā, the sense of solicitude is more evident." Al-Samīn said: "al-shafaq is of two kinds, the red shafaq and the white shafaq; al-shafaq and al-shafaqa are two nouns for ishfāq." Abū Ḥayyān said: "al-shafaq is the redness after the setting of the sun, when the time of the last night prayer comes; it was said that its root is from the fineness of a thing; one says shayʾ mushfiq, i.e. it does not hold together because of its fineness, and from it ashfaqa ʿalayhi, his heart softened; al-shafaqa is the noun from al-ishfāq, and so too al-shafaq. The poet said:
تهوى حياتي وأهوى موتها شفقا ... والموت أكرم نزال على الحرم
(She wishes my life and I wish her death out of solicitude; and death is the most generous guest to the women's quarters.)"
The wording of al-Qāmūs: "al-shafaq (vowelled) is the redness on the horizon from sunset to the last night prayer, or to near it, or to near the darkness"; and this is the sound view. From it is the poet's saying:
قم يا غلام أعنّي غير مرتبك ... على الزمان بكأس حشوها شفق
(Rise, boy, and help me, unflustered, against time with a cup whose filling is shafaq.)
(وَسَقَ): he gathered and joined. One says wasaqahu fa-inshaqqa wa-istawsaqa [Translator's note: so in the source (فانشق); presumably فاتسق, i.e. so it was gathered and became gathered]; its parallel in the occurrence of iftaʿala and istafʿala as reflexives is ittasaʿa and istawsaʿa. In al-Qāmūs: "wasaqahu yasiquhu (of the pattern ḍaraba): he gathered it and carried it; and from it ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ وَما وَسَقَ﴾."
(اتَّسَقَ): it gathered and became even on the night of the fourteenth. Al-Farrāʾ said: "it is its fullness and evenness on the nights of the full moon," and it is iftaʿala from al-wasq, which is joining and gathering, as above; and "so-and-so's affair is muttasiq," i.e. gathered upon what pleases.

* I'rab:
(فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ وَاللَّيْلِ وَما وَسَقَ وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقاً عَنْ طَبَقٍ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa), because it stands in the apodosis of a preceding condition, i.e. "if you have known this," or "if you are certain of the return by resurrection, then I do not swear." The discussion of لا أُقْسِمُ has already preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. بِالشَّفَقِ is attached to أُقْسِمُ; اللَّيْلِ is conjoined to الشَّفَقِ and the wāw is a conjunction; ما may be a relative noun, or an indefinite described noun, or a maṣdar particle. If it is relative or indefinite described, the returning pronoun of the ṣila or description is omitted, i.e. "wasaqahu," "gathered it." The meaning is the gathering of what had been dispersed by day of the kinds of creatures and species of beings, for each of them returns at night to its shelter. الْقَمَرِ is likewise conjoined; إذا is an adverbial void of the sense of condition, attached to the verb of oath, i.e. the time of its fullness and evenness; the lām is the response to the oath; لَتَرْكَبُنَّ is an imperfect verb in the nominative by the presence of the nūn, which is dropped on account of the succession of similar letters, as it is one of the five verbs, and the omitted wāw, dropped through the meeting of two quiescents, is the agent, and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; طَبَقاً is a ḥāl or a direct object; and عَنْ طَبَقٍ, i.e. a community of people, is an adjective of طَبَقاً, i.e. a class passing beyond a class. On طَبَقاً being a direct object, there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "you will surely ride the ways, or the path, of class after class." Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "If you say, what is the position of عَنْ طَبَقٍ? I say: accusative as an adjective of طَبَقاً, i.e. a class passing beyond a class, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in لَتَرْكَبُنَّ, i.e. you will ride a class, passing beyond a class (or 'passing' or 'passed') according to the reading." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It was read latarkabanna addressing the human being in ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسانُ﴾; latarkabunna with damma addressing the genus, because the address is to the genus; latarkabinna with kasra addressing the soul; and layarkabanna with yāʾ, 'the human being will surely ride.' Al-ṭabaq is what corresponds to another; one says 'this is not ṭabaq to that,' i.e. it does not correspond to it, and from it the cover is called al-ṭabaq, and iṭbāq al-tharā is what is layered of it; then the state corresponding to another was called ṭabaq, and from it the words of the Mighty and Majestic ﴿طَبَقاً عَنْ طَبَقٍ﴾, i.e. state after state, each corresponding to its sister in severity and terror. It may also be the plural of ṭabaqa, which is a rank, from their saying 'he is on ranks'; from it ṭabaq al-ẓahr for the vertebrae, the singular being ṭabaqa, in the sense 'you will ride states after states which are ranks of severity, some higher than others, namely death and what follows of the stations of the Resurrection and its terrors.'" I say: among the uses of al-ṭabaq in the sense of a community is the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
وأنت لما ولدت أشرقت الأر ... ض وضاءت بنورك الأفق
تنقل من صالب إلى رحم ... إذا مضى عالم بدا طبق
(When you were born the earth shone, and the horizon was lit by your light. You are moved from loin to womb; when one age passes, another community appears.)
(فَما لَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; ما is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ; لَهُمْ is the khabar; the clause لا يُؤْمِنُونَ is a ḥāl. (وَإِذا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنُ لا يَسْجُدُونَ): the clause is conjoined to the preceding circumstantial clause; إذا is a future adverbial containing the sense of a condition; the clause قُرِئَ is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; الْقُرْآنُ is the deputy agent; the clause لا يَسْجُدُونَ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُكَذِّبُونَ): بل is a particle of transitional rejection; الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause كَفَرُوا has no position because it is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; the clause يُكَذِّبُونَ is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يُوعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ and أَعْلَمُ its khabar; بِما is attached to أَعْلَمُ; the clause يُوعُونَ has no position because it is the ṣila of ما, i.e. what they hold in their hearts of denial. (فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; بِعَذابٍ is attached to بَشِّرْهُمْ and أَلِيمٍ is a naʿt. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ): إلا is a particle of exception, and the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), meaning "but" (lākin); الَّذِينَ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آمَنُوا is a ṣila; وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ is conjoined to the ṣila, within its scope; لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar and أَجْرٌ a deferred mubtadaʾ; غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ is a naʿt, i.e. not cut off nor diminished; and the nominal clause is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. It is also permissible for the exception to be connected (muttasil), in which case الَّذِينَ is the excepted.

* Rhetoric:
In «والليل وما وسق والقمر إذا اتسق» there is the art of iltizām, or luzūm mā lā yalzam (the obligation of what is not obligatory), which some call iʿnāt. It has been alluded to before: that the poet in his verse and the prose-writer in his prose binds himself to one letter or two or more before the rhyme letter, as far as he is able, on condition that there be no strain. We said that Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī has a dīwān in which he bound himself to what is not obligatory. As for the verse, the nūn is observed before the qāf [Translator's note: so in the source (النون); in وسق / اتسق the letter before the qāf is the sīn].

Allah Teâlâ'nın {مَّحْفُوظٍ} sözü: Nâfi' «قرآن»ın na'ti olarak ref'le, diğerleri «لوحٍ»un na'ti olarak cerle okumuşlardır. Kurrânın çoğunluğu lâmın fethasıyla okumuştur; İbnü's-Semeyfa' ve İbn Ya'mer ise dammesiyle okumuşlardır. Zemahşerî şöyle demiştir: «Yedinci göğün üstündeki "اللوحَ"u kastediyor; onda "اللوحُ", şeytanların ona ulaşmasından korunmuş olarak bulunur.» [Mütercim notu: Arapça metin böyledir; ibare muğlaktır.] Ebü'l-Fadl şöyle demiştir: «"اللُّوح": havadır.» Zemahşerî'nin tefsiri anlama daha yakındır; İbn Hâleveyh'in kastettiği de odur.

* Vocabulary:
(الْبُرُوجِ): the plural of burj, which is originally the corner, fortress, castle, and any lofty building of round or square form, whether standing alone or part of a great structure. Burj is also one of the towers of the sky, which according to the lexicographers are twelve: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces. The root of the composition is for appearing, that is, the original meaning of burj is the manifest thing, from tabarruj; then in common usage it became in reality the lofty castle because of its visibility; and what rises of a city's wall is also called burj.
(الْأُخْدُودِ): singular; its plural is akhādīd. Al-khadd (with fatḥa on the khāʾ) has the meaning of al-ukhdūd, and its plural is khudūd; it is a cleft in the earth, or an elongated pit in it, and it is pluralised akhādīd. Al-akhādīd are also the marks of beating with a whip, and from it the akhādīd of the well ropes in the well, which is the effect of their dragging in it. One says of an old man, "he has taken on furrows (qad takhaddada)," meaning his skin has contracted.

* I'rab:
(وَالسَّماءِ ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ وَشاهِدٍ وَمَشْهُودٍ): the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; السَّماءِ is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear"; ذاتِ الْبُرُوجِ is a naʿt of السَّماءِ; الْيَوْمِ الْمَوْعُودِ is conjoined to السَّماءِ, or is an oath in itself, and what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection; other things were said, so refer to the longer works. شاهِدٍ and مَشْهُودٍ are likewise conjoined, and what is meant by it is Muḥammad ﷺ; other things were also said. The response to the oath is omitted, and there is disagreement about it. It was said that it is indicated by the words قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ, as if it were said, "I swear by these things that they are cursed as the people of the ditch were cursed." It was also said that its beginning is omitted and the implied form is "laqad qutila"; this omission was needed because the well-known view among the grammarians is that a positive, inflecting past verb whose object has not been fronted, when it occurs as the response to an oath, necessarily takes the lām, and it is not permissible to limit oneself to one of them (lām and qad) except when the speech is long; so the implied form is "laqad qutila," and the clause is therefore declarative, not an imprecation. (قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ النَّارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ): قُتِلَ is a passive past verb and أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ is the deputy agent; النَّارِ is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from الْأُخْدُودِ, because the ditch contains the fire; a pronoun must be implied in the badal of inclusion, the implied form being "the fire in it"; ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ is a naʿt of النَّارِ. There is disagreement about the link, for they stipulated that the badal of inclusion be attached to a pronoun referring to the substituted-for, as they stipulated that in the badal of part from whole, to link the part to its whole. It was said that the link is omitted, attached to something other than the badal, i.e. "the fire in it," and this is the view of the Basrans. It was also said that nothing is implied and the origin is "its fire," and then the definite article stands in for the pronoun, and this is the view of the Kufans. (إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْها قُعُودٌ وَهُمْ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ): إذ is an adverbial for past time, attached to قُتِلَ, i.e. they were cursed when they were burnt by the fire while sitting over it in a place overlooking it from the edges of the ditch; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; عَلَيْها is attached to قُعُودٌ; قُعُودٌ is the plural of qāʿid, the khabar of هُمْ; and the clause is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ; عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ is attached to شُهُودٌ; and شُهُودٌ is their khabar, i.e. on the Day of Resurrection they will bear witness to what they did to the believers. It was also said that ʿalā means "with," and shuhūd means presence, so the meaning is that "they were present at the torment inflicted on the believers, not softening toward them because of the hardness of their hearts"; this construction is more in keeping with the arrangement of the Qur'an, and Abū Nuwās followed it when he said:
أنت على ما بك من قدرة ... فلست مثل الفضل بالواجد
(For all the power you have, you are not like al-Faḍl in finding means.) «[Translator's note: the sense of this verse as given in the source is obscure; the gloss is tentative.]»
In that case it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. at the time of their doing it to the believers. (وَما نَقَمُوا مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; ما is negative; نَقَمُوا is a past verb with its agent; مِنْهُمْ is attached to نَقَمُوا; إلا is a particle of restriction; أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of an accusative, the object of نَقَمُوا, i.e. they found no fault with them and denied nothing but faith. More elaboration of this meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric. They expressed it with the imperfect in يُؤْمِنُوا although faith had occurred in them in the past, because their torturing them and denying them was not for the past faith but for its permanence, firmly rooted in their breasts, as if it were said, "except their continuing in their faith." بِاللَّهِ is attached to يُؤْمِنُوا; الْعَزِيزِ الْحَمِيدِ are two adjectives of اللَّهِ; He mentioned the attributes by which He deserves to be worshipped and believed in by every creature, among them might (ʿizza) and the bestowing of favour for which He deserves praise [Translator's note: the source prints والأنعام (cattle); read as والإنعام, bestowing favour]. (الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): الَّذِي is a third naʿt; لَهُ is a fronted khabar and مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ a deferred mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause has no position because it is a ṣila; اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ and شَهِيدٌ its khabar; عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ is attached to شَهِيدٌ.

* Rhetoric:
In «وما نقموا منهم إلا أن يؤمنوا بالله العزيز الحميد» there is the art of emphasising praise by what resembles blame (tawkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm), which was alluded to in Sūrat al-Māʾida. It is that a praise attribute be excepted from a negated blame attribute, or that a praise attribute be affirmed for something and then an exception particle follows, followed by another praise attribute. Of the first kind is the verse of al-Nābigha in praise of the Ghassānids:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أنّ سيوفهم ... بهنّ فلول من قرع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them except that their swords are notched from striking the battalions.)
and the saying of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt, who borrowed the Qur'anic wording and gazed at the sky of its eloquence:
ما نقموا من أمية إلا ... أنهم يحملون إن غضبوا
(They found no fault with Umayya except that they "bear down" (yaḥmilūn) when they are angry.) [Translator's note: the source has يحملون; the well-known transmission of the verse is يحلمون, "they show forbearance".]
and from it the saying of Ibn Nubāta al-Miṣrī:
ولا عيب فيه غير أني قصدته ... فأنستني الأيام أهلا وموطنا
(There is no fault in him except that I made for him, and the days made me forget family and homeland.)
and the saying of al-Maʿarrī:
تعدّ ذنوبي عند قوم كثيرة ... ولا ذنب لي إلا العلا والفضائل
(My sins are counted many among some people, yet I have no sin except loftiness and virtues.)
As for the second kind, it is rare in poetry, and from it is the saying of one of them:
ما فيك من الجمال سوى ... أنك من أقبح القبيحات
(There is nothing of beauty in you except that you are among the ugliest of the ugly.)

﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of inna.
﴿فتنوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿المؤمنين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿والمؤمنات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and al-muʾmināt is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-muʾminīn, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra [Translator's note: so in the source; as it is conjoined to an accusative mafʿūl bihi, "accusative by the kasra" would be expected].
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation and jussive.
﴿يتوبوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil.
﴿فلهم﴾: the fāʾ is connective (ṣila); lahum: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿عذاب﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿جهنم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and feminine.
﴿ولهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; lahum: the lām is a preposition and hum is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar.
﴿عذاب﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿الحريق﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿إن الذين فتنوا المؤمنين والمؤمنات﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿فَتَنُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position [Translator's note: the word «صلة» appears to have dropped out of the source here; the sense is supplied]; the clause ﴿لم يتوبوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿فتنوا﴾; ﴿لهم عذاب جهنم﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna; and ﴿لهم عذاب الحريق﴾ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause ﴿لهم عذاب جهنم﴾.

﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿بطش﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿لشديد﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and shadīd is the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause ﴿إن بطش ربك لشديد﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or it is the answer to the oath at the beginning of the sūra.

Kavli: {والطارق}: الطارق aslında «طَرَقَ يَطْرُقُ طُروقاً», yani geceleyin geldi (fiilinden) ism-i fâildir. (Şair) şöyle demiştir:
4539 - فمِثْلَكِ حُبْلى قد طَرَقْتُ ومُرْضِعاً ... فألهَيْتُها عن ذي تمائمَ مُحْوِلِ
(Senin gibi nice hamile ve emzikli kadına geceleyin vardım da onu muskalı, bir yaşındaki çocuğundan alıkoydum.)
Aslı vurmaktandır. «الطارقُ بالحصى», onunla vuran (çakıl atan) kimsedir. (Şair) şöyle demiştir:
4540 - لعَمْرُكَ ما تَدْري الضواربُ بالحصى ... ولا زاجراتُ الطيرِ ما اللَّهُ صانعُ
(Canına yemin olsun, çakıl atan (fal bakan) kadınlar da, kuşları ürküterek fal bakanlar da Allah'ın ne yapacağını bilmezler.)
Sonra anlam genişletilmiş ve geceleyin gelen herkese «طارِقٌ» denmiştir.

Kavli: {والترآئب}: «تَريبة»nin çoğuludur; bu, göğüs kemiklerinden gerdanlığın yeridir. Çünkü çocuk ikisinin (erkek ve kadının) suyundan yaratılmıştır; erkeğin suyu sulbündedir, kadınınki de göğüs kemiklerindedir. {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ} [el-İnsân: 2] kavlinin manası budur. Şair şöyle demiştir:
4540 - مُهَفْهَفَةٌ بيضاءُ غيرُ مُفاضَةٍ ... تَرائِبُها مَصْقُولةٌ كالسَّجَنْجَلِ
(İnce belli, beyaz, karnı sarkık olmayan; göğsünün kemikleri ayna gibi cilalı.)
Ve şöyle demiştir:
4541 - والزَّعْفَرانُ على ترائبِها ... شَرِقَتْ به اللَّبَّاتُ والنَّحْرُ
(Göğsünün üst kısmında safran; gerdanlık yerleri ve boğazı onunla boyanmış.)
Ebû Ubeyde şöyle demiştir: «التَّريبة'nin çoğulu تريب'dir.» (Şair) şöyle demiştir:
4542 - ومِنْ ذَهَبٍ يَذُوْبُ على تَرِيْبٍ ... كلَوْنِ العاجِ ليس بذي غُضونِ
(Fildişi renginde, buruşuksuz bir göğüs üzerinde eriyen altından [süs]…)
«الترائب»in köprücük kemikleri olduğu da söylenmiştir. Erkeğin sulbün altındaki kaburgaları olduğu da söylenmiştir. İki omuz ile göğüs arası olduğu da söylenmiştir. İbn Abbâs'tan: Bunlar kişinin uçlarıdır; elleri, ayakları ve gözleri. Kalbin özü olduğu da söylenmiştir. İbn Atiyye şöyle demiştir: «Bu görüşlerde lügat hususunda keyfî hüküm vardır.»

Cumhur «يَخْرُج»u ma'lûm olarak okumuştur. İbn Ebî Able ve İbn Miksem ise meçhul olarak okumuştur. Yine o [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «وقرأ أيضاً» denmiş, kimin kastedildiği açıkça belirtilmemiştir.] ve Mekke ehli «الصُّلُب»ü sâd ve lâmın dammesiyle, Yemânî ise ikisinin fethasıyla okumuştur. Accâc'ın şu sözü buna göredir:
4543 - في صَلَبٍ مِثْلِ العِنانِ المُؤْدَمِ
(Derisi tabaklanmış dizgin gibi [sağlam] bir bel (صَلَب) içinde…)
Bunun lügatleri en-Nisâ sûresinde geçmişti. En garibi «صالِب»dir; şu söz gibi:
4544 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . مِنْ صالِبٍ إلى رَحِمٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(…sulbden rahme…) [Mütercim notu: Beyit kaynakta eksik verilmiştir.]

* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of command. (ممّ) is attached to (خلق); (ما) is interrogative, and its alif is dropped because a preposition precedes it. (من ماء) is attached to the second (خلق). (من بين) is attached to (يخرج).
Clause: «لينظر الإنسان» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «خلق (الأولى) » is in the position of accusative as the direct object of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, by implying a preposition.
And the clause: «خلق (الثانية) » has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive).
And the clause: «يخرج ... » is in the position of genitive as an naʿt (adjective) of ماء «[Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ماء, because it has been specified by the qualification.]».

* Morphology:
(6) دافق: an active participle from the triliteral دفق; its wazn is فاعل «[Note: in the verse it is a majāz ʿaqlī (rational figurative usage) meaning "poured" (مدفوق), or it is used in the sense of attribution, i.e. "possessing outpouring".]».
(7) الصلب: a noun meaning the back; its wazn is فعل (with ḍamma and sukūn); its plural is أصلاب, on the wazn أفعال.
(الترائب) plural of تريبة, a noun for the chest, or its ribs, or its flesh and blood; its wazn is فعلية like صحيفة, and the plural is فعائل. It contains the change of yāʾ into hamza because it comes after a silent alif; the original is ترايب.

* Rhetoric:
Ṭibāq (antithesis): in His words, the Exalted, «مِنْ بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ وَالتَّرائِبِ».
He set the bone of the back against the bone of the chest, putting the first in the singular and the latter in the plural, because a woman's chest is her تريبة, so one says of a woman "ترائب", meaning the تريبة and what is around it and surrounds it.
Or it is said that the Exalted meant: "He brings forth from between the backbones and the chests," and was content with the singular in place of the plural, as the Exalted said «أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كانَتا رَتْقاً فَفَتَقْناهُما» without saying "the earths".

Kavli: {الأعلى}: «ربِّك»in sıfatı olarak mecrûr olması, «اسم»in sıfatı olarak da mansûb olması câizdir. Ancak bu, «الذي»nin «ربِّك»in sıfatı olmasına engel olur; bilakis onun «اسم»in na'ti kılınması ya da maktû' (ayrılmış) olması gerekir; tâ ki sıfat ile mevsûf arasına başkasının sıfatıyla fasıl girmesi gerekmesin. Zira terkip, «جاءني غلامُ هندٍ العاقلُ الحسنةِ» ("Bana Hind'in kölesi, akıllı olan, güzel olan (müennes) geldi") sözün gibi olur; bunda «العاقل», «هند» ile onun sıfatı arasını ayırır. İsmin müsemmâya izâfesi hakkındaki söz daha önce geçmişti.

* Vocabulary:
(غُثاءً) In the Qāmūs: "al-ghuthāʾ, like ghurāb and like zinnār: rubbish, foam, and the perished, worn-out leaves of trees." It also says: "al-qamsh is the plural of qumāsh, which is the scraps of things on the face of the earth, so that the dregs of people are called qumāsh, and 'he gave me nothing but qumāsh', i.e. the poorest thing he found." In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ghuthāʾ al-sayl is what the flood carries; ghathā al-wādī, ghuthūwan (of the pattern qaʿada), means the valley became full of ghuthāʾ; and ghathat nafsuhu, taghthā, ghathyan (of the pattern ramā) and ghathayānan is its turbulence, so that one is nearly sick, from a mixture flowing into the mouth of the stomach."
(أَحْوى) al-aḥwā is of the pattern afʿal from al-ḥuwwa, which is a blackness tending to greenness; it is also said that al-aḥwā is greenness with blackness upon it; al-aḥwā is also the gazelle, because it has two lines on its back; one says "a man aḥwā" and "a woman ḥawwāʾ", and its plural is ḥuwwun, like aḥmar and ḥumr. In the Qāmūs: "al-ḥuwwa, with ḍamma, is blackness toward greenness, or redness toward blackness; ḥawiya, like raḍiya, ḥawan." Ibn Jinnī said: al-ḥuwwa is a redness tending to blackness that occurs in the lip, and the Arabs find that desirable. Dhū l-Rumma said:
لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس ... وفي اللّثات وفي أنيابها شنب
صفراء في نعج بيضاء في دعج ... كأنها فضة قد مسّها ذهب
(A dark-lipped girl, in whose lips is a dark ruddiness, a deep red, and in her gums and in her teeth a cool sweetness; yellow-tinged in her fair whiteness, white against the dark of her eyes, as if she were silver that gold has touched.)
And Abū ʿUbayda recited, also from Dhū l-Rumma, about the pasture that is aḥwā:
حوّاء قرحاء أشراطيّة وكفت ... فيها الذهاب وحفتها البراعيم
(A dark-green, white-blazed pasture of the Ashrāṭ star, on which the light rains dripped, and the buds surrounded it.)
al-qarḥāʾ is the white one; one says "qarḥa" of a blaze (ghurra); ashrāṭiyya means rained on by the star-setting of the two Sharaṭān; al-dhihāb, with kasra on the dhāl, is light rain; and al-barāʿīm is the plural of burʿūma, which is the flower before it opens, and it is also called the kamm, the plural being aknām.

* I'rab:
(سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى) سبّح is an imperative verb, meaning "declare transcendent", and has been treated before; its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and اسم ربك is its direct object. Al-Jalāl made it an interpolated word, on the model of Labīd's saying:
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما ... ومن يبك حولا كاملا فقد اعتذر
(Until the year, then the name of peace be upon you both; and whoever weeps a full year has made his excuse.)
There is no need for this strained reading, since declaring transcendent may fall upon the name, i.e. declare the name of your Lord transcendent above being used to name an idol or image, so that it is called "lord" or "god". And الأعلى is an adjective of ربك; Ibn Hishām allowed it to be an adjective of اسم. (الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى) الذي is a second adjective of the Lord; the clause خلق is the ṣila (relative clause), and the object of خلق is omitted, i.e. "everything"; the فاء is a conjunction, and سوّى is conjoined to خلق. What is meant by "proportioning" is that He created what He willed in the most complete and perfect manner, according to an order described as firm and masterly, free of blemishes and defects. (وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدى) This too is conjoined, in sequence, to what preceded. (وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أَحْوى)
This too is conjoined to what precedes it; the clause أخرج is the ṣila of الذي, and المرعى is the direct object; فجعله is conjoined to أخرج, the هاء is the first direct object, غثاء is the second direct object, and أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. But a difficulty arises, since al-ghuthāʾ is the dry matter while al-ḥuwwa is a lasting greenness, so the two contradict each other. It is therefore preferable to parse أحوى as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى, i.e. "He brought it forth aḥwā, black from the intensity of greenness, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought it out of the pasture black from the intensity of greenness and abundant watering, and then made it ghuthāʾ after its ḥuwwa." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As for His saying, the Exalted, أحوى, it is said that it is an adjective of غثاء, and it is said that it is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture green and then turned it into ghuthāʾ, so he put part of the ṣila first." Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent sense is that أحوى is an adjective of غثاء. Ibn ʿAbbās said the meaning is: He made it dark ghuthāʾ, i.e. black, because when ghuthāʾ ages and rain strikes it, it blackens and rots and becomes aḥwā. It is also said that أحوى is a ḥāl from المرعى, i.e. He brought forth the pasture aḥwā, i.e. black from the intensity of its greenness and freshness through abundant watering; and the postposing of أحوى is good for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil). He said:
وغيث من الوسمي حوّ تلاعه ... تبطنته بشيظم صلّتان
(And a rain from the wasmī season, whose hollows are dark-green, I entered it on a long-legged, lean, swift horse.)"
Ibn Khālawayh said in his book "I'rab of Thirty Surahs of the Noble Qur'an": "فجعله غثاء أحوى means that Allah made the pasture aḥwā, and al-aḥwā is intensely green, tending to black because of abundant watering, and then He turned it into ghuthāʾ after it dried; so the meaning involves a fronting and postponing." Ibn Hishām said in his book al-Mughnī, in mentioning the aspects from which an objection may enter against the one who parses: "The fourteenth is the saying of some about أحوى that it is an adjective of غثاء. This is not correct without qualification; it is so only if aḥwā is interpreted as black from dryness and withering. But if it is interpreted as black from the intensity of greenness through abundant watering, as مُدْهَامَّتَانِ was interpreted, then making it an adjective of غثاء is like making قيما an adjective of عوجا; rather it must be a ḥāl from المرعى, postposed to match the verse-endings." By my life, he has settled the dispute in what he laid down. (سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى) The سين is a particle of futurity; نقرئك is an imperfect verb, nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; the فاء is a conjunction; لا is negative; and تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative. The wording of Abū l-Suʿūd: "سنقرئك فلا تنسى is an exposition of Allah the Exalted's special guidance of His Messenger ﷺ following the exposition of His general guidance of all His creatures, namely his, peace be upon him, guidance to receive the revelation, to memorize the Qur'an, and his guidance of all people. The سين is either for emphasis or because what is meant is making him recite what Allah revealed to him at that time and what would be revealed to him afterwards, so it is a promise that the revelation will continue within the promise of making him recite, i.e. We shall make you recite what We reveal to you, and what follows, through the tongue of Jibrīl, or We shall make you a reciter by inspiring recitation, so you will not forget at all, from the «قسوة» of memorization [Translator's note: the source reads «قسوة» (hardness); probably «قوة» (strength) is meant] and mastery, even though you are unlettered, not knowing what writing or reading is; so that is another sign for you, besides what lies within what you recite of the clear signs, in respect of inimitability and of informing about the unseen." The فاء is a conjunction and لا is negative: Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet that he would not forget. تنسى is an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative sign being the implied ḍamma on the alif. It is also said that لا is prohibitive and تنسى is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its jussive sign being the dropping of the weak letter, and then the alif was brought as a support for the fatḥa of the sīn so as to agree with the verse-endings, as in His saying السبيلا. Abū Ḥayyān did well when he condemned this view; he said: "This is a weak statement; the sense of the verse is utterly clear, and they have been far-fetched in understanding it." (إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ إِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ وَما يَخْفى) إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is the object of تنسى; the exception is vacated (mufarragh) from the most general of objects; the clause شاء الله is the ṣila of ما; and the clause إن and what is within its scope is a justification of what precedes; إن and its noun; the clause يعلم is its predicate; and الجهر is a direct object;
the واو is a conjunction and ما is a relative noun conjoined to الجهر; the clause يخفى is its ṣila. Al-Samīn said: "It is not permissible for it to be maṣdar-forming, lest the verb be left without an agent; were it not for that, its being maṣdar-forming would be better, so that an interpreted maṣdar would be conjoined to a plain maṣdar like it." (وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرى فَذَكِّرْ إِنْ نَفَعَتِ الذِّكْرى) The واو is a conjunction; ونيسرك is conjoined to سنقرئك; it is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the كاف is a direct object; and ولليسرى are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to نيسرك, i.e. to the tolerant Islamic law. The فاء is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you know that you are among those who receive perfecting outpourings through Our guidance and success, then remind"; إن is conditional; نفعت is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and الذكرى is the agent. In إن there is a sense of regarding it as improbable, as though he were sure they would not incline to guidance and would persist in riding the back of excess. The apodosis (jawāb) of إن is omitted, indicated by what precedes. Al-Zamakhsharī has a subtle question and a subtler answer. He said: "If you say: the Messenger ﷺ was commanded to remind whether the reminder benefits or not, so what is the meaning of making benefit a condition? I say: it has two aspects. One is that the Messenger of Allah had already exhausted his effort in reminding them, and they only increased in insolence and tyranny from the increase of reminding, and the Prophet ﷺ was burning with regret and anguish and increasing in grief and eagerness over reminding them; so it was said to him: 'You are not a compeller over them' — so remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My threat, and turn away from them and say 'Peace', and remind if the reminder benefits, and that is after the argument has been established by repeated reminding. The second is that it is conditional in form, but its meaning is a censure of those who remind, a report of their state, a regarding as improbable that the reminder will affect them, and a recording against them that their hearts are sealed, as you say to the preacher, 'Enrage the tax-collectors, if they listen to you,' intending by this condition to regard that as improbable and that it will never be." As for Ibn Khālawayh, after citing the view we cited he said: "Others say: إن means قد, i.e. remind, for the reminder has benefited; but that is very remote, and supposition and speculation do not befit the style of the Qur'an." As for Abū Ḥayyān, he said:
"The apparent sense is that his command to remind is conditional on the reminder's benefit, and this condition was brought only as a rebuke to Quraysh, i.e. if the reminder benefits these tyrannical, obstinate ones, and its meaning is the improbability of their benefiting from the reminder. It is as the poet said:
لقد أسمعت لو ناديت حيّا ... ولكن لا حياة لمن تنادي
(You have made yourself heard, had you called one alive; but there is no life in him whom you call.)
Al-Farrāʾ, al-Naḥḥās, al-Zahrāwī and al-Jurjānī said: its meaning is 'and if it does not benefit', so he limited himself to the one alternative because it indicates the other." (سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَنْ يَخْشى، وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى، الَّذِي يَصْلَى النَّارَ الْكُبْرى، ثُمَّ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها وَلا يَحْيى) The سين is a particle of futurity; يذكر is an imperfect verb, nominative; من is a relative noun, the agent; the clause يخشى is a ṣila with no grammatical position; ويتجنبها is conjoined to سيذكّر; the هاء is a direct object and the pronoun refers back to الذكرى; and الأشقى is the agent. Ibn Khālawayh said: "One says 'Zayd is al-ashqā' and 'the woman is al-shaqyā', like al-aʿlā and al-ʿulyā, and one says: 'al-ashqā spoke to al-shaqyā', 'the two ashqayn spoke to the two shaqyayn', 'the ashqūn spoke to the ashqayn', and 'the shaqiyyāt spoke to the shaqiyyāt'." الذي is an adjective of الأشقى; the clause يصلّى has no position because it is the ṣila of الذي; the agent of يصلّى is a latent pronoun referring to الأشقى; النار is a direct object and الكبرى is an adjective of النار; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; لا is negative; يموت is an imperfect verb, nominative; وفيها are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يموت; and ولا يحيا is conjoined to لا يموت. The meaning of the delay is that wavering between life and death is more terrible than burning, so it is delayed from it in degrees of severity: "he who dies is at rest"; but these are neither dead, that they might rest, nor alive, that they might find a breath from the punishment. (قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ تَزَكَّى وَذَكَرَ اسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّى) قد is a particle of affirmation; أفلح is a past verb; من is the agent; the clause تزكى, i.e. purified himself, has no position because it is the ṣila of من; وذكر is conjoined to تزكى; واسم ربه is a direct object; and فصلّى is conjoined to ذكر. (بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقى) It is an iḍrāb (turning away) from an implied statement to which the speech leads, the implied form being: "you do not do what is for the good of your affair, rather you prefer"; تؤثرون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the واو is the agent; الحياة is a direct object and الدنيا is an adjective of الحياة. What is meant by preferring the life of this world is inclining to it, being deceived by its adornments, and seeking out its milk-flows. The واو is a ḥāl-wāw; الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); خير is the khabar (predicate); and أبقى is conjoined to خير; so in it are the pleasures of this world and what the mind cannot conceive of increase upon them, and it has besides that the attribute of permanence and eternity. (إِنَّ هذا لَفِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولى صُحُفِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى) إن is a particle resembling the verb; هذا is its noun, the demonstrative referring to the success of him who purified himself and the words that followed; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); في الصحف is the predicate of إن; الأولى is an adjective of الصحف; and صحف إبراهيم وموسى is a badal (substitute) for الصحف.

* Benefits:
A glimpse of the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā:
In al-Khāzin the following is reported: From Abū Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mosque has a greeting." I said: "And what is its greeting, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Two rakʿas that you pray." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah revealed to you anything of what was in the scrolls of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā?" He said: "O Abū Dharr, recite: قد أفلح من تزكّى وذكر اسم ربه فصلّى بل تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا والآخرة خير وأبقى إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Mūsā?"
