İkinci cevap şudur: Bu söz Resûl (s.a.v.) tarafından şart kalıbında söylenmiştir; sanki şöyle demiştir: 'عَلَيْكَ بِذَاتِ الْبَيْنِ تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكَ' —sana emrettiğimi yapmazsan elin toprak olsun!— Bu güzeldir; Sa'leb ve Müberred'in tercihi de budur.» [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta ikinci cevapta «بذات البين» yazılmıştır; hadisin önceki zikri gereği doğrusu «بذات الدين» olmalıdır.]
(مُؤْصَدَةٌ): Üzeri kapatılmış. Hemzeli (okunuşu) Hafs, Ebû Amr ve Hamza'nın kıraatidir; sâkin vâv ile (مُوصَدَة) ise diğerlerinin kıraatidir. Bunlar iki lügattir; kapıyı kapadığında ve üzerini örttüğünde «أَصَدْتُ الْبَابَ», «آصَدْتُهُ» ve «أَوْصَدْتُهُ» denir. Hemzelinin anlamının «üzeri örtülü», hemzesizin anlamının «kapalı» olduğu da söylenmiştir; el-Kâmûs ikisi arasında fark gözetmemiştir.

* İ'rab:
(لا أُقْسِمُ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ): «لا أُقْسِمُ»un i'rabı ve (لا'nın) zâide olduğu görüşü daha önce çok defa geçti; onu (oradan) tazele. «بِهذَا» (câr ve mecrûr) «أُقْسِمُ»e mütealliktir; «الْبَلَدِ», «هذَا»dan bedeldir. Vâv hâliyye veya i'tirâziyyedir; «أَنْتَ» mübtedâ, «حِلٌّ» haberdir; «بِهذَا» «حِلٌّ»e mütealliktir; «الْبَلَدِ» bedeldir. Zemahşerî vâvın i'tirâziyye, cümlenin de ara cümle (mu'teraza) olmasını tercih etmiştir; Ebû Hayyân ise bunu reddetmiştir. Aşağıda Zemahşerî'nin ifadesi ile Ebû Hayyân'ın reddiyesi verilmektedir.
Zemahşerî şöyle dedi: «Allah Sübhânehû, insanın meşakkatlere ve sıkıntılara katlanmaya gömülmüş olarak yaratıldığına dair Beled-i Haram'a ve ondan sonrakine yemin etmiş; kasem ile üzerine yemin edilen şey arasına ‹وأنت حلّ بهذا البلد› sözünü ara söz olarak koymuştur. Yani: Katlanılan meşakkatlerden biri de şudur ki senin gibi biri, hürmetinin büyüklüğüne rağmen, Harem dışında avın helâl sayılması gibi bu Beled-i Haram'da (kanı) helâl sayılmaktadır.» (Sözünü) şuraya kadar sürdürür: «Ya da Resûlullah'ı (s.a.v.), insanın sıkıntılara katlanmaktan hâlî olmadığına dair onun beldesine yemin ederek teselli etmiş; tesellinin tamamlanması ve onu ferahlatmak için de ara söz olarak ona Mekke'nin fethini vaat etmiş ve ‹وأنت حل بهذا البلد› buyurmuştur; yani: Sen gelecekte orada helâl kılınmış olacaksın; orada öldürme ve esir almadan dilediğini yapacaksın.» (Sözünü) şuraya kadar sürdürür: «Eğer ‹وأنت حلّ› sözünün istikbal anlamında olmasının benzeri nerede? dersen, derim ki: Allah Azze ve Celle'nin ‹إنك ميت وإنهم ميّتون› sözüdür. Bunun benzeri kulların sözünde de yaygındır: İkram ve bağışta bulunacağını vaat ettiğin kimseye 'Sen ikram edilmiş, bağışlanmışsın' dersin. Bu, Arapların sözünde daha da yaygındır; çünkü gelecekteki hâller O'nun katında hazır ve müşahede edilen (hâller) gibidir. [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «في كلام العرب» yazılmıştır; «عنده» (O'nun katında) zamiri ve el-Keşşâf'ın metni dikkate alındığında doğrusu «في كلام الله» (Allah'ın sözünde) olmalıdır.] Onun istikbal için olduğuna ve hâl ile tefsir edilmesinin muhal olduğuna kesin bir delil olarak şu sana yeter: Sûre ittifakla Mekkîdir; nüzûlü vaktinden hicret ne kadar uzaktır! Ya fetih nasıl olsun?»
Ebû Hayyân ise şöyle dedi: «Onun cümleyi i'tirâziyye olarak yorumlaması zorunlu değildir. Biz önce onun hâl cümlesi olduğunu zikretmiş ve konumunun güzelliğini, yani kendisiyle yemin edilen şeyin (المقسم به) yüceliğini ifade ettiğini açıklamıştık. Bu, hâl-i mukārinedir; ne mukaddere ne de mahkiyyedir; dolayısıyla gelecekten haber verme kabîlinden değildir. Onun sorusu ve cevabına gelince, bunu nahiv ilmiyle en küçük ilgisi olan kimse sormaz; çünkü haber, gelecekteki şeylerle de olabilir. İsm-i fâil ve onun yerine geçen şeyin, isnad edildiği veya onunla vasıflandırıldığı hâlde hâle hamledilmesi zorunlu değildir; bilakis bazen mâzî, bazen hâl, bazen de istikbal için olur. Bu, nahiv ilminin ilk ilkelerindendir. Onun ‹Kesin bir delil olarak şu sana yeter…› sözüne gelince, bu bir şey değildir; çünkü biz ‹وأنت حل›i, nüzûlü vaktinde Mekke'de esir alma ve öldürmeden yaptığın şeyin sana helâl olacağı şeklinde yorumlamadık ki (ikisi) birbiriyle çelişsin; aksine onu, özellikle orada ikamet ediyor olması şeklinde yorumladık; o da nüzûl vaktinde zorunlu olarak orada ikamet ediyordu. Ayrıca onun, (sûrenin) Mekke'de indiğine dair ittifak naklettiği şey de doğru değildir; bu konuda bir topluluktan ihtilaf nakledilmektedir.»
Bu tartışmayı ancak şunun için getirdik: Tartışanların delillerinin kuvveti, yaklaşık olarak bütün müfessirleri bu anlaşmazlıkta «hayâ»ya (الحياء) bağlı kalmaya sevk etmiştir; bu yüzden biz de tercihte bulunmak istemedik. [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «التزام الحياء» yazılmıştır; bağlam gereği doğrusu muhtemelen «التزام الحياد» (tarafsız kalmak) olmalıdır.] Bununla beraber Kerhî, Zemahşerî'nin görüşünü desteklemiş ve şöyle demiştir: «Allah, insanı meşakkat içinde yarattığına dair Beled-i Haram'a yemin etmiş; tesellinin tamamlanması için de ikisinin arasına, ona Mekke'nin fethini vaat etmesini ara söz olarak koymuştur; çünkü ‹وأنت حلّ› buyurmuştur; yani gelecekte orada (helâl kılınmış olacaksın); öldürme ve esir almadan dilediğini yapacaksın.» Celâl de tefsirinde Zemahşerî'yi destekleyerek şöyle demiştir: «Cümle, üzerine yemin edilen ile kasem arasında ara sözdür (i'tirâz).» Semîn ise onun sözünü getirip ardından şöyle demiştir: «Hâliyye olduğu ve ‹لا›nın nefy için olduğu da söylenmiştir; yani: Sen bu beldede ikamet ediyorken, kadrinin büyüklüğü sebebiyle ona yemin etmem; yani yemin edilmeye ondan daha lâyık olan sen varken hiçbir şeye yemin etmem.» İbn Hâleveyh de Ebû Hayyân'ı desteklemiştir.
(وَوالِدٍ وَما وَلَدَ): Önceki kasem üzerine ma'tûftur. «والِد» ile kastedilen Âdem'dir; «ما», «والِدٍ» üzerine ma'tûftur; «وَلَدَ» cümlesi sıladır; yani onun zürriyeti. Bundan daha güzeli Ebû Hayyân'ın söylediğidir: «Zâhir olan, ‹ووالد وما ولد› sözüyle belirli birinin kastedilmediği, aksine her babaya şâmil olduğudur.» Zemahşerî ise başka bir görüşe meyletmiş ve şöyle demiştir: «Eğer ‹والد وما ولد› ile kastedilen nedir? dersen, derim ki: Resûlullah (s.a.v.) ve onun doğurduklarıdır (zürriyetidir). (Allah) onun doğduğu yer, babası İbrâhim'in Harem'i ve babası İsmâil'in (aleyhimesselâm) yetiştiği yer olan beldesine, onun doğurduklarına ve kendisine yemin etmiştir. Eğer neden nekre getirildi? dersen, derim ki: Övgü ve hayreti tek başına ifade eden müphemlik içindir. Eğer ‹ومن ولد› denseydi ya? dersen, derim ki: Bunda, Allah'ın ‹والله أعلم بما وضعت› sözündeki (anlam) vardır; yani şanı şaşılacak bir doğurulan (kastedilmiştir).» Ferrâ ise şöyle dedi: «ما» insanlar içindir; tıpkı «ما طاب لكم» sözü gibi, «وما خلق الذكر والأنثى», yani «erkeği ve dişiyi yaratan O'dur» (sözü gibi).
(لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ فِي كَبَدٍ): Cümle kasemin cevabıdır. Lâm cevapta gelen (lâm)dır; «قَدْ» tahkîk harfidir; «خَلَقْنَا» fiil ve fâildir; «الْإِنْسانَ» mef'ûlün bihtir; içindeki «أل» cins içindir, çünkü insan cinsini kastetmiştir. «فِي كَبَدٍ» (câr ve mecrûr), «الْإِنْسانَ»dan hâl olmak üzere mahzûf bir şeye mütealliktir; yani meşakkatlere katlanan, ayakları üzerinde dik duran, toplumunun inşasında rolünü yerine getiren (olarak); yemeğini ağzıyla alan hayvan gibi değil.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ): Hemze inkâr ve tevbîh içindir. «يَحْسَبُ» merfû muzâri fiildir; fâili insana veya Resûlullah'ın (s.a.v.) kendilerinden çektiğini çektiği Kureyş ileri gelenlerinden bazısına dönen müstetir zamirdir. «أَنْ», ağırından hafifletilmiştir; ismi zamîru'ş-şe'ndir. «لَنْ» nefy, nasb ve istikbal harfidir; «يَقْدِرَ» «لَنْ» ile mansûb muzâri fiildir; «عَلَيْهِ» (câr ve mecrûr) «يَقْدِرَ»e mütealliktir; «أَحَدٌ» «يَقْدِرَ»in fâilidir.
Şaşılacak şeydir ki İbn Hâleveyh aynen şöyle der: «‹أَنْ› nasb eden harftir, ‹لَنْ› nasb harfidir; ‹يَقْدِرَ› ‹لَنْ› ile mansûbtur. Araplar amel eden iki harfi bir araya getirdiklerinde birini ilga ederler.» İşte bu, ardından başka saçma söz olmayan bir saçmalıktır; bu, nahivcilerin söz konusu ayeti şâhit getirmeleri hususundaki icmâını açıkça çiğnemektir. Çünkü fethalı «أَنَّ» hafifletildiğinde ismin zamîru'ş-şe'n olması şart koşulur; (ismin) zikredilmesi ancak şiir zarureti hâlinde işitilmiştir; Amr Zü'l-Kelb'in kız kardeşi Cenûb'un şu sözü gibi:
وقد علم الضيف والمرملون ... إذا اغبرّ أفق وهبت شمالا
بأنك ربيع وغيث مريع ... وأنك هناك تكون الثمالا
(Kısa anlamı: Ufuk tozla kaplandığında ve kuzey rüzgârı estiğinde misafir de azığı tükenmiş olanlar da bilir ki sen bir bahar ve bereketli bir yağmursun; o zaman (herkesin) sığınağı sen olursun.)
Burada (أَنْ'in) ismi zikredilmiş bir zamir olarak gelmiştir ve şe'n için değildir. Haberine gelince, onun cümle olması gerekir. Sonra cümle isim cümlesi ise veya fiili câmid ya da dua olan bir fiil cümlesi ise bir fâsıla (ayırıcı) gerekmez. İsim cümlesine örnek: «وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين»; fiili câmid olan fiil cümlesine örnek: «وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى»; fiili dua olan fiil cümlesine örnek: «والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها». Bunların dışındakilerde fâsıla «يحب». [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «ويحب» yazılmıştır; doğrusu «ويجب» (gerekir) olmalıdır; buna göre anlam: «Bunların dışındakilerde fâsıla gerekir».] (Bu fâsıla), «أَنَّهُ»den hazfettikleri şeye —ki o iki nûndan biri ile isimdir— bedel olsun diye veya masdariyye «أَنْ» ile karışmasın diyedir. Fâsıla ya «قَدْ» iledir —çünkü o mâzîyi hâle yaklaştırır—; «ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا» gibi; ya tenfîs (سَ / سَوْفَ) iledir; «علم أن سيكون» gibi; ya da «لا», «لَنْ» veya «لَمْ» ile nefiy iledir. «لَنْ»in örneği: «أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد».
Eğer «Onlar, ilim fiilinden sonra (أَنْ'in) muhaffefe olmasını vâcib görmüşlerdir; zan fiilinden sonra ise hem muhaffefe hem masdariyye olmasını caiz görmüşlerdir» denirse, derim ki: Kur'ân üslûbu, aynı anlamda iki âmilin araya sokulmasından ve bizim bunlardan birini ilga etmek zorunda kalmamızdan ne kadar yücedir! Bu, Kur'ân-ı Azîm'in üslûbunun kendisinden yüce olduğu bir şeydir.
(يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَداً): Cümle hâliyye veya isti'nâfiyyedir. Söz, övünme ve böbürlenme yoluyladır. «أَهْلَكْتُ» cümlesi mekūlü'l-kavldir (sözün mef'ûlüdür); «مالًا» mef'ûlün bihtir; «لُبَداً» sıfattır.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ): İstifhâm yine inkâr ve tevbîh içindir; i'rabı da öncekinin i'rabı gibidir.
(أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ وَلِساناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ): Hemze takrîrî istifhâm içindir. «لَمْ» nefy, kalb ve cezm harfidir; «نَجْعَلْ» «لَمْ» ile meczûm muzâri fiildir. «لَهُ» (câr ve mecrûr) «نَجْعَلْ»e mütealliktir; çünkü o «نَخْلُقُ» (yaratırız) anlamındadır. «عَيْنَيْنِ» mef'ûlün bihtir; «لِساناً» ve «شَفَتَيْنِ», «عَيْنَيْنِ» üzerine ma'tûftur. «الشَّفَة» lâmı mahzûf (bir kelime)dir; aslı «شَفَهَة»dir; delili tasğîrinin «شُفَيْهَة», cemiinin «شِفَاه» olmasıdır. Benzeri «سَنَة»dir. «شِفَاه» şeklindeki kırık cemi ile yetinildiği için elif ve tâ ile cemilenmez. «هَدَيْناهُ»: mâzî fiil, fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir; «النَّجْدَيْنِ» ikinci mef'ûlün bihtir veya daha önce geçtiği gibi nez'u'l-hâfıd (cer harfinin kaldırılması) ile mansûbtur.
(فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ): Fâ atıf harfidir; «لا» nefy harfidir; bu, Ebû Ubeyde, Ferrâ ve Zeccâc'ın görüşüdür. Sanki şöyle demiştir:
«Ona organları bağışladık ve ona yolu gösterdik; fakat o hiçbir hayır işlemedi», yani (sarp yokuşu) aşmadı. Ferrâ ve Zeccâc şöyle demişlerdir: «لا»yı bir kere zikretmiştir; Araplar ise mâzî fiil ile «لا»yı hemen hemen hiç tek kullanmazlar, onu tekrarlarlar; Allah Teâlâ'nın «فلا صدق ولا صلّى» sözünde olduğu gibi. (Burada) onu tek kullanması, sözün sonunun onun anlamına delâlet etmesi sebebiyledir. Böylece ileride gelecek «ثُمَّ كانَ…» sözünün tekrarın yerini tutması caizdir; sanki «(sarp yokuşu) aşmadı ve iman etmedi» demiştir. Bunun dua yerine geçtiği de söylenmiştir; «لَا نَجَا وَلَا سَلِمَ» (kurtulmasın ve selamet bulmasın) sözü gibi; (yani) hiçbir hayır yapmaması için onun aleyhine bir bedduadır.
Zemahşerî ise Ferrâ, Zeccâc ve Ebû Ubeyde'nin görüşünü «تنحل» ettikten sonra şöyle dedi [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «بعد أن تنحل مقالة» yazılmıştır; okuma şüphelidir, muhtemelen «انتحل» (sahiplendi, benimsedi) kastedilmiştir.]: «(لا) anlam bakımından tekrarlanmış ‹لا› demektir; çünkü ‹فلا اقتحم العقبة›nin anlamı ‹فلا فكّ رقبة ولا أطعم مسكينا›dır. Görmez misin ki sarp yokuşu aşmayı bununla tefsir etmiştir.» Bu ise onun için ancak «فكّ»i mâzî fiil olarak okuyanların kıraatine göre tamam olur. Bununla birlikte okuduğumuz en garip şey, Şeyh Celâl'in «لا»nın «هَلَّا» anlamında, yani tahdîd (teşvik) harfi olduğu sözüdür. Celâl, Ebû Zeyd'in bir rivayetine dayanmıştır; fakat biz yanında hemze olmaksızın tek başına «لا»nın tahdîd için olduğunu işitmedik.
İbn Hişâm'ın el-Muğnî'deki ifadesi şöyledir: «Allah Sübhânehû ve Teâlâ'nın:
‹فلا اقتحم العقبة› sözüne gelince, buradaki ‹لا› anlamca tekrarlanmıştır; çünkü anlam ‹فلا فكّ رقبة ولا أطعم مسكينا›dır; zira bu, sarp yokuşun tefsiridir. Bunu Zemahşerî söylemiştir. Zeccâc ise şöyle demiştir:
Bu ancak ‹ثم كان من الذين آمنوا› ona ma'tûf olduğu ve nefyin içine girdiği için caiz olmuştur; sanki ‹فلا اقتحم ولا آمن› denmiştir. Eğer bu sahih olsaydı ‹لا أكل زيد وشرب› demek de caiz olurdu. Bazıları ‹لا›nın duâiyye olduğunu, onun aleyhine hiçbir hayır yapmaması için dua edildiğini söylemiştir. Bir başkası da tahdîd (için) olduğunu, aslının ‹فَأَلَّا اقْتَحَمَ› olduğunu, sonra hemzenin hazfedildiğini söylemiştir; bu ise zayıftır.»
Bu görüşler gözden geçirildiğinde, onu (لا'yı) duâiyye kılmanın en racih ve Kur'ân-ı Kerîm'in üslûbuna en uygun (görüş) olduğu ortaya çıkar. Demâmînî şöyle demiştir: «Bu, güzelliği açık, üzerinde hiçbir toz bulunmayan bir vecihtir; onu diğer görüşlerden önce zikretmek daha evlâ idi.»
«اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ»: mâzî fiil, takdiri «هُوَ» —yani (o sözü) söyleyen kimse— olan müstetir fâil ve mef'ûlün bihtir. Sarp yokuşu aşmanın anlamına dair daha fazlası Belâgat bölümünde gelecektir. Vâv i'tirâziyyedir; «ما» ref' mahallinde istifhâm ismi olup mübtedâdır; «أَدْراكَ» cümlesi «ما»nın haberidir. (İkinci) «ما» istifhâm ismi olup mübtedâ, «الْعَقَبَةُ» haberdir. İstifhâm ile muallak kılınan isim cümlesi nasb mahallindedir ve «أَدْراكَ»nin ikinci mef'ûlünün yerini tutmuştur. Cümle, sarp yokuşu açıklamak için araya sokulmuş ve müphemlik anlamını pekiştiren bir ara cümledir. Tefsir (açıklama) şöyledir: «وما أدراك ما العقبة» sözü, o sarp yokuşun ta kendisidir; çünkü elif-lâm ile ma'rife yapılan (kelime) tekrar edildiğinde ikincisi birincisinin aynısı olur.
(فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ): «فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ» gizli bir mübtedânın haberidir, yani «هُوَ فَكٌّ»; takdir şöyledir: «Sarp yokuşu aşmak nedir? O, köle azat etmek veya (açlık gününde) yedirmektir…» Bu muzâfı (اقتحام'ı) takdir etmeye, açıklanan (müfesser) ile açıklayan (müfessir) birbirine uygun olsun diye ihtiyaç duyulmuştur. Görmez misin ki sîn kesreli müfessir masdardır, sîn fethalı müfesser —ki o «الْعَقَبَة»dır— masdar değildir. Eğer muzâf takdir edilmeseydi, masdar olan «فَكّ» bir aynı (somut bir şeyi), yani «الْعَقَبَة»yı açıklamış olurdu.
«فَكَّ رَقَبَةً» şeklinde, mâzî fiil olarak da okunmuştur; fâili «هُوَ»dur, «رَقَبَةً» mef'ûldür; bu durumda fiil cümlesi, «لا» ile nefyedilmiş «اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ» sözünden bedeldir; sanki «فلا فكّ رقبة ولا أطعم» denmiştir. Bu da Zemahşerî'nin gittiği görüşü destekler.
«أَوْ إِطْعامٌ», birinci kıraate göre «فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ» üzerine ma'tûftur. «فِي يَوْمٍ» (câr ve mecrûr) «إِطْعامٌ»a mütealliktir; «ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ», «يَوْمٍ» için sıfattır. «يَتِيماً», nasb (amelinin) şartlarını tamamlamış bir masdar olarak «إِطْعامٌ»ın mef'ûlüdür; veya (diğer) kıraate göre «أَطْعَمَ»in mef'ûlüdür. «ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ», «يَتِيماً» için sıfattır. «أَوْ» atıf harfidir; «مِسْكِيناً», «يَتِيماً» üzerine ma'tûftur; «ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ», «مِسْكِيناً» için sıfattır.
(ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ): «ثُمَّ», rütbede terâhî (uzaklık) ifade eden atıf harfidir; çünkü iman asıldır ve önce gelendir; hiçbir amel onsuz tamam olmaz. «كانَ» nâkıs mâzî fiildir; ismi ona dönen müstetir zamirdir; «مِنَ الَّذِينَ» haberidir. «آمَنُوا» cümlesi sıladır; «تَواصَوْا» sılaya ma'tûftur ve onun kapsamına dahildir. «بِالصَّبْرِ» (câr ve mecrûr) «تَواصَوْا»ya mütealliktir. «وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ» de ma'tûftur.
(أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هُمْ أَصْحابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ): «أُولئِكَ» mübtedâ, «أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ» haberdir. «الَّذِينَ» mübtedâdır; «كَفَرُوا» cümlesi sıladır; «بِآياتِنا» (câr ve mecrûr) «كَفَرُوا»ya mütealliktir. «هُمْ» mübtedâ, «أَصْحابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ» onun haberidir; cümle «الَّذِينَ»nin haberidir. İfade kalıplarının farklılığına dair değerli bir bahis Belâgat bölümünde gelecektir. «عَلَيْهِمْ» mukaddem haber, «نارٌ» muahhar mübtedâ, «مُؤْصَدَةٌ» «نارٌ» için sıfattır; cümle ikinci haberdir; onu isti'nâfiyye kılman da caizdir.

* Belâgat:
1- «وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ» sözünde istiâre-i tasrîhiyye vardır: «النَّجْدَيْنِ»i hayır ve şer için istiâre etmiş; müşebbeh olan hayır ve şerri hazfetmiş, müşebbehün bihi bırakmıştır. Eğer «Hayrın, yolun yüksek kısmı olan necde benzetilmesinde bir sakınca yoktur, çünkü açıktır; fakat şer böyle değildir, çünkü o fıtratın zirvesinden bayağılığın çukuruna bir iniş ve gerilemedir» dersen, deriz ki: (Allah) ikisini ya tağlîb yoluyla bir araya getirmiştir ya da hayal gücünün onda bir yükseliş, bir gerileme ve bir alçalma olduğunu vehmetmesi yoluyla. Bu, sözün en beliğ ve en hayranlık uyandıranlarındandır.
2- «فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ» sözünde, müşebbehe uygun düşen şeyin zikredilmesiyle istiârenin terşîhi vardır; örnekleri daha önce geçmiştir. Burada şunu ekliyoruz: Terşîhin temeli, teşbihin unutulmuş gibi gösterilmesidir; «تقوّله» iddia ve mübalağadır. [Mütercim notu: Kaynakta «وتقوّله الادّعاء» yazılmıştır; okuma şüphelidir, muhtemelen «وقِوامُه الادّعاء» (dayanağı iddia ve mübalağadır) kastedilmiştir. Ayrıca terşîh, istiare literatüründe müşebbehün bihe uygun olanın zikridir; metinde «müşebbehe» denmesi de şüphelidir.] Bu yüzden terşîh tecrîdden daha beliğdir. (Tecrîd), müşebbehün bihe değil de müşebbehe uygun düşen şeyin zikredilmesidir; çünkü onda teşbihin itirafı vardır. (Terşîhte) öyle ki mekânî yüceliğe benzetilen kadir yüceliği üzerine, mekânî yücelik üzerine bina edilen şey bina edilir; tıpkı Ebû Temmâm'ın şu sözünde olduğu gibi:
ويصعد حتى يظن الجهول ... بأن له حاجة في السماء
(Kısa anlamı: O öyle yükselir ki cahil kişi onun gökte bir işi olduğunu sanır.)
Yükselmeyi kadrin yüceliği için istiâre etmiş, sonra onun üzerine mekânın yüceliği üzerine bina edilen şeyi bina etmiştir. Eğer maksadı teşbihi unutmuş gibi görünmek ve onu inkârda ısrar edip onu gökte yükselen biri kılmak olmasaydı, bu sözün bir vechi olmazdı. Sonra onlar bu unutmuş gibi görünmeyi, teşbihi açıkça söyleyip aslı itiraf ettikleri hâlde de yaparlar; o hâlde istiârede olduğu gibi aslı inkâr edip bunda ısrar edildiğinde (bunu yapmaları) evleviyetle (daha uygundur). Abbâs b. Ahnef'in şu sözü gibi:
هي الشمس مسكنها في السماء ... فعزّ الفؤاد عزاء طويلا
فلن تستطيع إليها الطلوع ... ولن تستطيع إليك النزولا
(Kısa anlamı: O, meskeni gökte olan güneştir; kalbini uzun bir sabırla teselli et; sen ona yükselemezsin, o da sana inemez.)
Gizli değildir ki bu unutmuş gibi görünme, aslın itirafıyla birlikte gerçekleşmiştir; o da «هي الشمس» sözündeki «هي»dir; çünkü o sevgiliye râcidir. Bu açıktır. Bazılarının vehmettiği gibi onu zamîru'l-kıssa kılmak ise tekellüftür.
Mücerred istiâre örneklerinden biri de şairin şu sözüdür:
فإن يهلك فكل عمود قوم ... من الدنيا إلى هلك يصير
(Kısa anlamı: Eğer o helâk olursa (şaşılmaz); zira dünyada her kavmin direği (reisi) helâke varır.)
«عمود» sözünde istiâre-i tasrîhiyye-i asliyye vardır: Kavmin reisini, her ikisinin de taşıması (yük taşıması) ortak noktasıyla direğe benzetmiştir; karine «يهلك»tir. «إلى هلك يصير» sözünde ise tecrîd vardır. Terşîh, tecrîd ile bir araya gelebilir; çünkü teşbihin bazı sıfatlarda unutulmuş gibi gösterilip bazılarında gösterilmemesi caizdir. Bunun örneklerinden biri Ebu't-Tayyib'in şu sözüdür:
سقاك وحيّانا بك الله إنما ... على العيس نور والخدور كمائمه
(Kısa anlamı: Allah seni sulasın ve seninle bizi yaşatsın! Develerin üzerindekiler ancak çiçeklerdir; hevdeçler de onların tomurcuk kabuklarıdır.)
«النَّوْر» çiçek veya onun beyazıdır; burada onunla kadınlar kastedilmiştir; ortak nokta güzelliktir. Dolayısıyla istiâre tasrîhiyye-i asliyyedir. Hevdeçlerin (الخدور) zikredilmesinde tecrîd, tomurcuk kabuklarının (الكمائم) zikredilmesinde terşîh vardır. Bu durumda istiâreye «mutlaka» denir.
3- «أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هُمْ أَصْحابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ» sözünde ifadede farklılık yapılmıştır: Mü'minlere, onları ikram etmek için ve onların Allah Teâlâ'nın katında, O'nun ikram makamında hazır olduklarını, O'nun önünde oturanlar mesabesinde bulunduklarını —iş, onlara parmakla işaret etmekten öteye geçmeyecek şekildedir— (belirtmek için) işaret etmiştir. Sonra uzaklığa delâlet eden işaret lafzını kullanmış ve «هؤلاء» dememiştir; bu da onların O'nun katındaki menzilelerinin yüksekliğini (uzaklığını) ve O'nun yakınlığı ve iltifatı şerefine nail olduklarını bildirmek içindir. Kâfirleri ise gâib zamiriyle zikretmiştir; bu, onların O'nun tecellileri makamından ve feyizlerinin nurlarından uzak (gâib) olduklarına ve en zayıf bir bağla bile O'na nispet edilmeye lâyık olmadıklarına işarettir. Bu, şaşılacak şeylerin en şaşırtıcısıdır; onu iyi düşün.

* Vocabulary:
(الْبَلَدِ) In al-Qāmūs: "(البلد) and (البلدة) is Mecca, may Allah the Exalted honour it, and every tract of land that is enclosed, whether inhabited or desolate, and the soil; (البلد) is also the grave, the cemetery, the house, the trace, and the ostrich's nest-hollow" and so on, until he says: "(بلد بالمكان بلودا) means he stayed and kept to it, or took it as a town."
(حِلٌّ) One says (حلّ) and (حلال), and (حرم) and (حرام), in one meaning. (حلّ في المكان) means he alighted in it; (يحل), with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, (حلولا), so he is (حال) and the place is (محلول فيه). More of its meaning will come in the section on I'rab.
(كَبَدٍ) Toil and hardship; he endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the next. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "(الكبد), with two fatḥas, is hardship, from (المكابدة) of a thing, which is bearing the hardships of doing it." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī is: "Its origin is from (كبد الرجل) (كبد), of the pattern ṭariba, so he is (أكبد), when his liver pains him and swells; then it was extended until it was used for every weariness and hardship, and from it (المكابدة) was derived, just as it was said (كبته الله) in the sense of 'He destroyed him', whose origin is (كبده), i.e. He struck his liver. Labīd said, lamenting his brother Arbad:
يا عين هلّا بكيت اربد إذ ... قمنا وقام الخصوم في كبد
(O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad when we rose, and the adversaries rose in distress?)
that is, in the severity of the affair and the difficulty of the matter." Now among the strange features of the letters kāf and bāʾ is that when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word they indicate hardness, hardship and subjugation. One says (كببته في الهوّة) "I threw him into the pit", and (كبكبته), and (كببته), and likewise when someone is thrown from the top of a mountain or a wall; the horseman (يكبّ) the wild beasts, and they (يكبون العشار). He said:
يكبّون العشار لمن أتاهم ... إذا لم تسكت المائة الوليدا
(They slaughter the pregnant she-camels for whoever comes to them, when the hundred does not quiet the newborn.)
Among the figurative uses: (أكبّ على عمله), and he is (مكب عليه), meaning devoted to it, never leaving it. Labīd said: "The bending of the Hālikī over his hands, bent over (مكبّا), examining the notches of the arrowheads." (كبت الله عدوّك) means Allah subdued your enemy and destroyed him; and you say: "May your adversary never cease to be (مكبوتا) and your enemy (مكبوتا)." (كبح فرسه) means he pulled its rein until its head stood erect; for this reason it was also said: "(في كبد) means upright, not made to walk on all fours taking things with his mouth, nor on his belly, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted, honoured the children of Adam with things of which this is one." Another Bedouin said: "What is it with the falcon, that it loves the hare as it does not love the (خرب)?" He said: "Because it (يكبح) its moustache and turns it back", that is, it strikes its moustache with its droppings and soils it. (كبر الأمر) and (خطب كبير), and (كبر علي ذلك) means it was hard on you: (كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه). (كبر الرجل في قدر) and (كبر في سنّه), and (شيخ كبير) and (ذو كبر وكبر); and the condition of (الكبرة) and (المكبرة) is advanced age and the hardship and effort it entails. He said:
عجوز عليها كبرة في ملاحة ... أقاتلتي يا للرجال عجوز
(An old woman, on whom is age along with charm; will she kill me, O men, an old woman?)
(كبس الحفرة) means he filled it in; (كبس رأسه في جيب قميصه) means he put it into it; and he is (عابس كابس); and the nightmare (الكابوس) fell upon him. (انتطحت الكباش) the rams butted each other; (كبش كتيبة) is the leader of a battalion, and they are (كباش الكتائب). He said:
وإنّا لمما نضرب الكبش ضربة ... على رأسه تلقي اللسان من الفم
(We are of those who strike the ram a blow on its head that throws the tongue out of the mouth.)
(فلان مكلّب مكبل) means a man bound with (الكلب), which is rawhide strap, shackled with (الكبل), which is the fetter; (كبلت الأسير) and (كبّلته) and (اكتبلته); and on his shanks are (كبل) and (كبول). Jarīr said:
ومكتبلا في القدّ ليس بنازع ... له من مراس القدّ رجلا ولا يدا
(Shackled in the strap, not freeing from the grip of the strap either a foot or a hand of his.)
And (كبا لوجهه) "he fell on his face". You say: "the sharp edge turns back and fortune stumbles", and so on to the end of this wonderful material in our beloved language.
(لُبَداً) Abundant, heaped one upon another, and its depletion is not feared because of its quantity; (وما له سبد ولا لبد) is also said, and this is what is meant here. (لبد) was also the last of the vultures of Luqmān. It is said that ʿĀd sent him to the Sanctuary to pray for rain for them; when they were destroyed, Luqmān was given the choice between the survival of seven droppings of dun gazelles on a rugged mountain that no rain touches, or the survival of seven vultures, each time one vulture died another succeeding it. He chose the vultures, and the last of them was Lubad; when it died, Luqmān died. That was in the time of al-Ḥārith al-Rāʾish, one of the kings of Yemen. The poets mentioned him; al-Nābigha said:
أضحت خلاء وأضحى أهلها احتملوا ... أخنى عليها الذي أخنى على لبد
(She became empty and her people departed; what destroyed Lubad destroyed her.)
(النَّجْدَيْنِ) The two ways, meaning the way of good and the way of evil. (النجد) is a road on a height. It was also said that they are the two breasts; this is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAlī, because they are like the two ways for the life of the child and his sustenance. (النجد) is height, its plural (نجود); from it Najd was named, for its elevation above the low-lying Tihāma. In al-Qāmūs: "(النجد) is what rises above the land, its plural (أنجد), (أنجاد), (نجاد), (نجود), and (نجد), and the plural of (النجود) is (أنجدة); it is the clear raised road and whatever is the opposite of (الغور), that is Tihāma; its jīm is also given ḍamma; masculine; its upper part is Tihāma and Yemen, its lower part Iraq and Syria, and its beginning from the side of the Hijaz is Dhāt ʿIrq. It is also what a house is furnished with, of rugs, bedding and cushions, the plural being (نجود) and (نجاد); the skilled guide; and a place with no trees" until he says "and the breast."
(الْعَقَبَةَ) The hard road in a mountain. (اقتحامها) is passing through it. More on this discussion will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(مَسْغَبَةٍ) A mīm-prefixed verbal noun from (سغب يسغب سغبا), of the pattern fariḥa: he was hungry. In al-Qāmūs: "(سغب), like (فرح) and (نصر), (سغبا) and (سغبا) and (سغابة) and (سغوبة) and (مسغبة) means he was hungry, so he is (ساغب), (سغبان) and (سغب), and she is (سغبى), plural (سغاب). (السغب) is also thirst, but it is not in use."
(مَتْرَبَةٍ) In al-Mukhtār: "(ترب الشيء) means dust touched it, of the pattern ṭariba; from it (ترب الرجل) means he became poor, as if he clung to the dust. (تربت يداه) is a curse upon him, meaning may he gain no good. (تربه تتريبا فتترّب) means he smeared it with dust and it became smeared; (أتربه) means he put dust on it. In the ḥadīth: 'Put dust on the writing, for it is more apt to succeed in the need.' (أترب الرجل) means he became rich, as if he came to have wealth as much as the dust. (المتربة) is destitution and poverty, and (مسكين ذو متربة) means one who clings to the dust." Ibn Khālawayh said:
"Abū ʿAbd Allāh Niftawayh informed us from Thaʿlab, who said: One says (ترب الرجل) when he became poor and (أترب) when he became rich, and its meaning is that his wealth became like dust in quantity. If someone asks:
'If the matter is as you claim, then what is the point of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saying to the man who consulted him about marriage: "Take the one with religion, (تربت يداك)", when the Prophet does not curse any of the believers?' there are answers to that, and two of them are preferred. The first is that he, peace be upon him, intended a supplication that is not meant to take effect, like their saying to a man when praising him: 'May Allah fight him, how poetic he is', and 'May Allah disgrace him, how learned he is'. The poet said, speaking of a woman he loved, and he is Jamīl Buthayna:
رمى الله في عيني بثينة بالقذى ... وفي الغر من أنيابها بالقوادح
وفي وجهها الصافي المليح بقتمة ... وفي قلبها القاسي بودّ مماتح
(May Allah cast a mote in the eyes of Buthayna and decay in her bright teeth, and a dimness in her clear, fair face, and in her hard heart a love that draws out [his life].)
The second answer is that this speech came from the Messenger ﷺ in the manner of a condition, as if he had said: 'Take the one with religion, (تربت يداك) if you do not do what I have commanded you.' This is fine, and it is the choice of Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad."
(مُؤْصَدَةٌ) Closed over, with hamza, which is the reading of Ḥafṣ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza; and with a silent wāw, which is the reading of the rest. They are two dialects. One says (أصدت الباب), (آصدته) and (أوصدته) when you shut it and closed it. It was also said that the meaning of the hamzated form is "closed over" and the meaning of the non-hamzated is "locked"; al-Qāmūs did not distinguish between them.

* I'rab:
(لا أُقْسِمُ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ وَأَنْتَ حِلٌّ بِهذَا الْبَلَدِ)
The i'rab of (لا أقسم) and the view that (لا) is redundant have often preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. (بهذا) is attached to (أقسم), and (البلد) is a badal for (هذا). The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or parenthetical. (أنت) is mubtadaʾ, (حلّ) is the khabar, (بهذا) is attached to (حل), and (البلد) is a badal. al-Zamakhsharī preferred that the wāw be parenthetical and the clause an interjected one, and Abū Ḥayyān rejected him. What follows is the wording of al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān's rejection.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "He, Glory be to Him, swore by the Sacred Land and what follows on the point that man was created immersed in the toil of hardships and trials, and interjected between the oath and what is sworn upon His saying: (وأنت حلّ بهذا البلد), meaning: among the hardships is that one like you, despite the greatness of your sanctity, is treated as lawful in this Sacred Land, as game is treated as lawful outside the Sanctuary" until he says: "Or he consoled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by swearing by his city, to the effect that man is never free from enduring hardships, and he interjected by promising him the conquest of Mecca, to complete the consolation and relief for him, so He said: (وأنت حل بهذا البلد), meaning: you will be free in it in the future, doing in it what you wish of killing and capture" until he says: "If you say: where is a parallel to His saying (وأنت حلّ) in the sense of the future? I say: His saying, Mighty and Majestic, (إنك ميت وإنهم ميّتون); and the like of it is wide-spread in the speech of people: you say to one whom you promise honour and gifts: 'You are honoured, given gifts', and it is wider still in the speech of the Arabs, because future states are, in their view, like those present and witnessed. And sufficient as a decisive proof that it is for the future, and that interpreting it as present is impossible, is that the sūra is by agreement Meccan, so how far is the Hijra from the time of its revelation, let alone the conquest?"
Abū Ḥayyān said: "Taking the clause as parenthetical is not necessary. We mentioned at the outset that it is a circumstantial clause and showed the fineness of its place, which is to convey the magnification of that by which the oath is sworn; and it is a concurrent ḥāl, neither anticipated nor narrated, so it is not an announcement of the future. As for his question and answer, this is not something that would be asked by anyone with the slightest connection to the science of grammar, because announcement may be about future things, and the active participle and what takes its course, when predicated or used as an attribute, need not be taken as present, but may be for the past at times, for the present at others and for the future at others; and this is among the first principles of grammar. As for his saying 'sufficient as a decisive proof…' etc., it is nothing, because we did not take (وأنت حل) to mean that it becomes lawful to you what you do in Mecca of capture and killing at the time of its revelation in Mecca, such that they would conflict; rather we took it to mean that he resides there in particular, and at the time of revelation he was necessarily residing there. Also, what he relates of agreement that it was revealed in Mecca is not correct, and disagreement over it is sometimes reported from some people."
We have cited this debate only because the strength of argument on both sides moved all the commentators, roughly speaking, to maintain modesty in this dispute; therefore we too did not wish to give a preference. However, al-Karkhī supported al-Zamakhsharī's view, saying: "Allah swore by the Sacred Land that He created man in hardship, and interjected between them by promising him the conquest of Mecca, to complete the consolation, in His saying (وأنت حلّ), i.e. in it in the future, doing what you wish of killing and capture." Likewise al-Jalāl in his commentary supported al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "The clause is an interjection between the oath and what is sworn upon." al-Samīn followed him, citing his words and saying: "It was also said that it is circumstantial and (لا) is negative, i.e. 'I do not swear by this land while you are residing in it, because of the greatness of your worth', that is, 'I do not swear by anything, while you are more entitled to be sworn by than it.'" Ibn Khālawayh supported Abū Ḥayyān.
(وَوالِدٍ وَما وَلَدَ)
Conjoined to the preceding oath. What is meant by (الوالد) is Adam; (ما) is conjoined to (والد), and the clause (ولد) is the ṣila, i.e. his offspring. Better than that is what Abū Ḥayyān said: "The apparent sense is that His saying (ووالد وما ولد) does not intend a particular one but applies to every father." As for al-Zamakhsharī, he leaned towards another opinion, saying: "If you ask: what is meant by (والد وما ولد)? I say: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his offspring. He swore by his city, which is his birthplace, the sanctuary of his father Ibrāhīm and the place where his [other] father Ismāʿīl grew up, peace be upon them both, and by those whom he begot and by him. If you ask: why was it indefinite? I say: for the vagueness that stands alone in praise and wonder. If you ask: why was it not said (ومن ولد)? I say: in it is what is in His saying: (والله أعلم بما وضعت), meaning something placed, wondrous in its matter." al-Farrāʾ said: (ما) is for people, like His saying (ما طاب لكم), and (وما خلق الذكر والأنثى), while He is the Creator of the male and the female.
(لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ فِي كَبَدٍ)
The clause is the answer to the oath; the lām occurs in the answer; (قد) is a particle of certainty; (خلقنا) is a verb and an agent; (الإنسان) is a direct object, and the (أل) in it is generic, since He meant the genus of man; (في كبد), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to an omitted ḥāl from (الإنسان), i.e. enduring hardships, standing upright on his two feet, performing his role in building his society, not like the animal that takes its food with its mouth.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَنْ يَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ)
The hamza is for denial and rebuke. (يحسب) is an imperfect nominative verb whose agent is latent, returning to man, or to some of the chiefs of Quraysh from whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ endured what he endured. (أن) is the lightened form of (أنّ), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and future; (يقدر) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by (لن); (عليه), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (يقدر); and (أحد) is the agent of (يقدر).
It is strange that Ibn Khālawayh says what is literally: "(أن) is an accusative particle, (لن) is an accusative particle, and (يقدر) is accusative by (لن); and when the Arabs combine two operating particles, they cancel one of them." This is nonsense beyond which there is no nonsense, a flagrant breach of the consensus of the grammarians, who cite this very verse. For it is a condition that when the opened (أنّ) is lightened, its noun is a pronoun of the matter, and its mention has been heard only in poetic necessity, as in the saying of Janūb, sister of ʿAmr Dhū al-Kalb:
وقد علم الضيف والمرملون ... إذا اغبرّ أفق وهبت شمالا
بأنك ربيع وغيث مريع ... وأنك هناك تكون الثمالا
(The guest and the destitute know, when the horizon turns dusty and the north wind blows, that you are spring and fertile rain, and that you, there, are the refuge.)
Here its noun came as a mentioned pronoun, not of the matter. As for its khabar, it must be a clause; then if the clause is nominal, or verbal with a verb that is inert or one of supplication, no separator is needed. The nominal: (وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين). The verbal whose verb is inert: (وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى). The verbal whose verb is supplication: (والخامسة أن غضب الله عليها). In other cases a separator is obligatory, to be a compensation for what they dropped from (أنّه), namely one of the two nūns and the noun, or so that it is not confused with the maṣdar (أن). The separation is by (قد), because it brings the past close to the present, as in (ونعلم أن قد صدقتنا); or by a particle of futurity, as in (علم أن سيكون); or by a negative with (لا), (لن) or (لم). An example with (لن) is (أيحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد). If it is said: "They have made it obligatory that it be the lightened one after a verb of knowing, but after a verb of thinking they have permitted it to be either lightened or maṣdar", I say: how lofty is the style of the Qur'an above thrusting in two operators of one meaning and our being forced to cancel one of them; this is something above which the style of the Great Qur'an stands.
(يَقُولُ أَهْلَكْتُ مالًا لُبَداً)
The clause is circumstantial or resumptive. The saying is by way of boasting and pride. The clause (أهلكت) is the content of the saying; (مالا) is a direct object; and (لبدا) is an adjective.
(أَيَحْسَبُ أَنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ)
The question is for denial and rebuke as well, and its i'rab is like that of the preceding one.
(أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ وَلِساناً وَشَفَتَيْنِ وَهَدَيْناهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ)
The hamza is for an affirmative question; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and the jussive; (نجعل) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم); (له), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (نجعل), because it is in the sense of (نخلق); (عينين) is a direct object; (ولسانا وشفتين) are conjoined to (عينين). (الشفة) has an omitted lām; the original is (شفهة), by the evidence of its diminutive (شفيهة) and its plural (شفاه); its parallel is (سنة). It is not pluralised with alif and tāʾ, being independent of that by its broken plural (شفاه). (هديناه) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (النجدين) is a second direct object, or accusative by removal of the preposition, as preceded.
(فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْعَقَبَةُ)
The fāʾ is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj, as if He had said: "We granted him the limbs and guided him to the path, yet he did no good, i.e. he did not (اقتحم)." al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: (لا) was mentioned only once, whereas the Arabs hardly use (لا) alone with the past verb without repeating it, as in His saying (فلا صدق ولا صلّى); He used it alone only because the end of the speech indicates its meaning, so it is possible that His coming saying (ثم كان…) etc. stands in place of the repetition, as if He had said "he did not enter the steep path and did not believe". It was also said that it follows the course of supplication, as in His saying (لا نجا ولا سلم), a supplication against him that he do no good. al-Zamakhsharī, after faulting the statement of al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿUbayda, said: "It is in the sense of (لا) repeated in meaning, because the meaning of (فلا اقتحم العقبة) is 'he neither freed a neck nor fed a poor man'; do you not see that He explained the entering of the steep path in this way?" This works for him only on the reading of one who read (فكّ) as a past verb. Yet the strangest thing we have read is the statement of Shaykh al-Jalāl that (لا) is in the sense of (هلّا), i.e. a particle of urging; al-Jalāl relied on a report from Abū Zayd, but we have never heard that (لا) alone is for urging without the hamza with it. The wording of Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī: "As for the saying of the Exalted, Glory be to Him: (فلا اقتحم العقبة), (لا) in it is repeated in meaning, because the meaning is 'he neither freed a neck nor fed a poor man', for that is the explanation of the steep path; so said al-Zamakhsharī. al-Zajjāj said: it is permissible only because (ثم كان من الذين آمنوا) is conjoined to it and enters into the negation, as if it were said: 'he neither entered nor believed'. If this were sound, it would be permissible to say (لا أكل زيد وشرب). Some said (لا) is supplicatory, a supplication against him that he do no good. Another said: it is urging, the original being (فألّا اقتحم), then the hamza was dropped; and this is weak." From reviewing these opinions it becomes clear that taking it as supplicatory is the more preferable and more fitting to the style of the Noble Qur'an. al-Damāmīnī said: "This is a view of evident fineness with no dust upon it, so it would have been better to put it before the other opinions." (اقتحم العقبة): a past verb, a latent agent, its implied form being "he", i.e. the speaker, and a direct object. More on the meaning of entering the steep path will come in the section on Rhetoric. The wāw is parenthetical. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar of (ما). (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and (العقبة) its khabar; the nominal clause, suspended by the interrogative, is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second object of (أدراك). The clause is parenthetical, thrust in to make the steep path plain and to confirm the sense of vagueness and explanation: for His saying (وما أدراك ما العقبة) is the very same steep path, because a word defined by alif-lām, when repeated, the second is the same as the first.
(فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ أَوْ إِطْعامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ أَوْ مِسْكِيناً ذا مَتْرَبَةٍ)
(فكّ رقبة) is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the freeing", the implied form being "what is the entering of the steep path? It is the freeing of a neck, or feeding…" etc. This implied muḍāf was needed only so that the explained and the explanation correspond. Do you not see that the explanation (المفسِّر), with kasra on the sīn, is a verbal noun, while the explained (المفسَّر), with fatḥa on the sīn, which is the steep path, is not a verbal noun? Had the muḍāf not been implied, the verbal noun (فكّ) would be explaining the entity (العقبة). It was also read (فكّ رقبة) with (فكّ) as a past verb whose agent is "he" and (رقبة) its object; the verbal clause is then a badal for His saying (اقتحم العقبة) negated by (لا), as if it were said: "he neither freed a neck nor fed", and this supports the view of al-Zamakhsharī. (أو إطعام) is conjoined to (فكّ رقبة) on the first reading; (في يوم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (إطعام); (ذي مسغبة) is an adjective of (يوم); (يتيما) is the object of (إطعام) as a verbal noun that has met the conditions for governing the accusative, or the object of (أطعم) on the other reading; (ذا مقربة) is an adjective of (يتيما); (أو) is a conjunction; (مسكينا) is conjoined to (يتيما); and (ذا متربة) is an adjective of (مسكينا).
(ثُمَّ كانَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَواصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ وَتَواصَوْا بِالْمَرْحَمَةِ)
(ثم) is a conjunction conveying distance in rank, because faith is the foundation and the first, and no deed is complete without it. (كان) is a defective past verb, its noun is latent, returning to him; (من الذين) is its khabar; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (وتواصوا) is conjoined to the ṣila and falls within its scope; (بالصبر), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (تواصوا); and (وتواصوا بالمرحمة) is also conjoined.
(أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْمَيْمَنَةِ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِنا هُمْ أَصْحابُ الْمَشْأَمَةِ عَلَيْهِمْ نارٌ مُؤْصَدَةٌ)
(أولئك) is mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب الميمنة) is the khabar. (الذين) is mubtadaʾ, the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila, and (بآياتنا), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (كفروا). (هم) is mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب المشأمة) is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of (الذين). A valuable discussion of the difference in forms of expression will come in the section on Rhetoric. (عليهم) is a fronted khabar, (نار) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and (مؤصدة) is an adjective of (نار); the clause is a second khabar, and you may make it resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying (وهديناه النجدين) there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He borrowed (النجدين) for good and evil, omitted the thing likened, which is good and evil, and retained the thing to which it is likened. If you say: the likening of good to the height, which is the raised part of the road, is beyond dispute because it is apparent, unlike evil, which is a descent and a falling from the peak of the natural disposition to the depths of vulgarity, we say: He joined them either by way of preponderance, or on the imagination's fancy that in it are ascent, falling back and descent; and this is among the most eloquent and most marvellous of speech.
2- In His saying (فلا اقتحم العقبة) there is a ranking embellishment (tarshīḥ) of the metaphor, by mentioning what suits the thing likened to. Examples of it have passed, and we add here that the basis of tarshīḥ is to pretend to forget the likening, and its sayings are claim and exaggeration. For this reason tarshīḥ is more eloquent than tajrīd, which is mentioning what suits the thing likened, without the thing likened to, because in it is an admission of the likening, such that what is built on spatial height is built on loftiness of rank likened to spatial height, as Abū Tammām said:
ويصعد حتى يظن الجهول ... بأن له حاجة في السماء
(He ascends until the ignorant think he has a need in the sky.)
He borrowed ascent for loftiness of rank, then built upon it what is built on height of place. Were it not that his aim was to forget the likening and insist on denying it, making him ascend in the sky, this speech would have no point. Furthermore, they do this forgetting even with an explicit statement of the likening and admission of the origin; so with denial of the origin and insistence on it, as in the metaphor, it is all the more fitting, as in the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Aḥnaf:
هي الشمس مسكنها في السماء ... فعزّ الفؤاد عزاء طويلا
فلن تستطيع إليها الطلوع ... ولن تستطيع إليك النزولا
(She is the sun, whose dwelling is in the sky; so console the heart with a long consolation. You will never be able to rise to her, and she will never be able to descend to you.)
It is not hidden that this forgetting occurred along with admission of the origin, namely (هي) in his saying (هي الشمس), because it returns to the beloved, and this is plain; and making it the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), as some imagined, is a strain.
Among the examples of the bare metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-mujarrada) is also the saying of the poet:
فإن يهلك فكل عمود قوم ... من الدنيا إلى هلك يصير
(If he perishes, then every pillar of a people from this world goes to perdition.)
In his saying (عمود) there is an original explicit metaphor: he likened the chief of the people to a pillar, on the ground that both bear a load; the indicator is (يهلك); and in (إلى هلك يصير) there is tajrīd. Tarshīḥ and tajrīd may also be combined, since it is permissible to forget the likening in some attributes and not in others. An example is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
سقاك وحيّانا بك الله إنما ... على العيس نور والخدور كمائمه
(May Allah give you drink and greet us through you; for upon the camels is a blossom, and the howdahs are its calyxes.)
(النور) is the flower, or the white of it, and what is meant by it here is women, the common ground being beauty; the metaphor is an original explicit one; in the mention of the howdahs there is tajrīd and in the mention of the calyxes there is tarshīḥ; and such a metaphor is then called absolute (muṭlaqa).
3- In His saying (أولئك أصحاب الميمنة والذين كفروا هم أصحاب المشأمة) the expression was varied. He pointed to the believers as an honour to them and to show that they are present with Him, the Exalted, in the station of His generosity, as if sitting before Him, the matter amounting to no more than pointing at them with the finger; then He used the word of pointing that indicates distance, and did not say (هؤلاء), announcing the remoteness of their rank with Him and their attaining the honour of favour and nearness to Him. As for the disbelievers, He mentioned them with the pronoun of the absent third person, pointing to the fact that they are absent from the station of His manifestations and the splendours of His outpourings, and that they do not deserve to have a relation to Him even through the feeblest of ties. This is among the greatest of wonders, so ponder it.

﴿وأنت﴾: vâv hâliyye ya da i'tirâziyye; «أنت» merfû mübtedâ.
﴿حل﴾: merfû haber.
﴿بهذا﴾: câr ve mecrûr, ﴿حل﴾e müteallik.
﴿البلد﴾: ﴿هذا﴾dan bedel-i mutâbık (tam bedel), mecrûr. Cümle i'tirâziyye olup i'rabdan mahalli yoktur, ya da hâliyyedir. Takdir: لا أقسم بهذا البلد وأنت حالٌّ (Hayır, sen bu beldede iken bu beldeye yemin ederim), yani bu beldede konaklayan iken. Şöyle de denmiştir: Anlam, لا أقسم به وأنت مُستحَلّ فيه (Hayır, sana (eziyet etmek) helal sayılırken ona yemin ederim) demektir, yani sana eziyet etmek helal sayılırken.

﴿فلا﴾: fâ atıf harfi; «لا» nefy ya da dua bildiren harf.
﴿اقتحم﴾: mâzî fiil; fâili müstetir zamir olup takdiri «هو»dur.
﴿العقبة﴾: mansûb mef'ûlün bih.

﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is an interrogative noun, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو), and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of «ما».
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ.
﴿العقبة﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause ﴿ما العقبة﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. The clause ﴿وما أدراك...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿العقبة﴾ in the previous ayah.

* Vocabulary:
(وَضُحاها) al-Qurṭubī said: "(الضحى) is feminine. One says (ارتفعت الضحى) 'the forenoon rose', above (الضحو); it is also treated as masculine. Whoever treats it as feminine takes it to be the plural of (ضحوة); whoever treats it as masculine takes it to be a noun of the pattern fuʿal, like (صرد)." Ibn Khālawayh said: "(الضحى) is a shortened noun like (هدى). (الضحى) is feminine, and its diminutive is (ضحية); but the better course is to say (ضحيّ) in its diminutive without the hāʾ, so that its diminutive does not resemble the diminutive of (ضحوة). (الضحى) is the face of the day. One says (ليلة اضحيان) when the moon in it is bright from its beginning to its end. (أضحى النهار) means the day rose. One says (ضحي فلان للشمس يضحى) when he came out to the sun and appeared. Allah the Exalted said: (وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى). Ibn ʿUmar saw a man saying the talbiya in a hidden voice and said to him: (أضح لمن لبّيت له), that is, make it evident. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيضحى وأيما بالعشيّ فيخصر
(She saw a man who, whenever the sun met him, would come out into the open, and who in the evening would be chilled.)"
And in al-Qāmūs: "(الضّحو) and (الضحوة) and (الضّحية), like (عشيّة), is the rising of the day; (الضحى) is a little after it; it is treated as masculine and its diminutive is (ضحيّ) without a hāʾ; (الضحاء), with a long vowel, is when midday draws near; with ḍamma and shortened, [it is the same]; (أتيتك ضحوة وضحى) 'I came to you in the forenoon'; (أضحى) means he entered it, and he made a thing appear; (ضاحاه) means he came to him in it."
(جَلَّاها) He made it appear and uncovered it.
(طَحاها) He spread it out, because what appears of it to the beholder is like a carpet, so this does not conflict with its being spherical. In al-Mukhtār: "(طحاه) means he spread it out, like (دحاه), and its pattern is (عدا)." And in al-Qāmūs: "(طحا يطحو) means he went far away and perished, and he threw a man on his face. (الطحا) is the level stretch of land. (طحى), like (سعى), means he spread out, and was spread out, and lay down, and went away in the land. (طحا به قلبه) means his heart carried him off into every matter."
(دَسَّاها) (التدسية) is diminishing and concealing through immorality. The origin of (دسى) is (دسس), as was said of (تقضض) that it became (تقضى), and as was said (قصيت أظفاري), whose origin is (قصصت أظفاري).
(فَدَمْدَمَ) He closed the punishment over them for their sin and destroyed them. al-Farrāʾ said: "The reality of (الدمدمة) is the doubling and repeating of punishment. One says (دمدمت على الشيء) when you covered it over." In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "(دمدمت الشيء) is when you made it stick to the ground; (دمدم الله عليهم) means Allah destroyed them; one says (دمدمت على الميت التراب) meaning I levelled it over him." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "(دمدم) means he became angry, and (الدمدمة) is speech that alarms a man." In al-Qāmūs: "(دمم الأرض) means he levelled it; (دمم فلانا) means he punished him with a complete punishment; and (دمم القوم) means he destroyed them, like (دهدم) and (دمدم عليهم)."
(عُقْباها) Its consequence and its outcome. In al-Qāmūs: "(أعقبه الله بطاعته) means He rewarded him, and (العقبى) is the recompense of a matter."

* I'rab:
(وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحاها وَالْقَمَرِ إِذا تَلاها)
The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (الشمس) is genitive through the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (وضحاها) is conjoined to (الشمس); (والقمر) is likewise conjoined. (إذا) is for mere time, attached to the omitted verb of the oath. An objection has been raised that the verb of the oath is a performative (inshāʾ) whose time is the present, so it cannot govern (إذا), since that is for the future, and a difference of time between the governing word and the governed is necessarily impossible. It was answered that it is permissible to swear now by the rising of a star in the future, so the oath is in the present and the rising in the future; and it is permissible to swear by a future thing, as you say "I swear by Allah, when the sun rises", where the oath becomes binding at the sun's rising. The verb of the oath is of the present only when it does not depend on a condition. We have set this out usefully and fully in the discussion of Sūrat al-Takwīr. The clause (تلاها) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it.
(وَالنَّهارِ إِذا جَلَّاها وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشاها)
The two clauses are strung onto what preceded and parallel it in i'rab.
(وَالسَّماءِ وَما بَناها وَالْأَرْضِ وَما طَحاها)
Likewise conjoined. (ما) in the three clauses is either maṣdar or in the sense of (من), and in any case it is conjoined to the noun before it, or the interpreted maṣdar formed from it and the verb is conjoined to it. al-Zamakhsharī rejected its being maṣdar.
(وَنَفْسٍ وَما سَوَّاها)
Likewise strung onto what preceded. The indefiniteness in (نفس) is meant for the genus, as though He had said "and any one of the souls".
(فَأَلْهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْواها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (ألهمها) is a past verb with a latent agent and a direct object; (فجورها) is a second direct object; and (وتقواها) is conjoined to (فجورها). They differed over the meaning of inspiration (ilhām). Ibn Jubayr said: "He made it incumbent upon it." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He made it known to it." Ibn Zayd said: "He made it clear to it." al-Zajjāj said: "He granted it success towards piety, and 'He inspired it with its immorality' means He forsook it." It was also said: He made it known to it and gave it a power with which both the acquisition of immorality and the acquisition of piety are possible. al-Zamakhsharī said:
"The meaning of inspiring immorality and piety is making it understand and comprehend that one of them is good and the other ugly, and enabling it to choose whichever of them it wishes." In this is an allusion to the doctrine of the Muʿtazila, who hold rational good and evil (al-taḥsīn wa-l-taqbīḥ al-ʿaqliyyān), that is, that good and evil are perceived by reason. The Sunnis, however, hold legal (revealed) good and evil, that is, that good and evil are perceived only through revelation, because they return to the legal rulings, without discarding the role of reason in perceiving the legal rulings; and in their view the knowledge of every legal ruling requires two premises: a rational one, which leads to the creed, and a revealed one built upon it, which indicates the specific ruling.
As for inspiration (al-ilhām) in the language, it is the casting of something into the mind. al-Rāghib said: "It is specific to what comes from the side of the Exalted and the side of the Highest Assembly. The Exalted said: (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها), so it is known that it is not specific to good but includes evil as well." In technical usage it is the casting of a meaning into the heart by way of outpouring without acquisition, so it is specific to good, since "outpouring" is not applied to evil, for which "whispering" (waswasa) is used.
(قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاها وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسَّاها)
The clause is the answer to the oath, and the lām was omitted because of the length of the speech. It was also said that the answer is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected". al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its implied form is 'Allah will surely destroy them', meaning the people of Mecca, for their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as He destroyed Thamūd because they denied Ṣāliḥ. As for (قد أفلح), it is speech following His saying (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها) by way of digression, and is not part of the answer to the oath at all." (قد) is a particle of certainty; (أفلح) is a past verb; (من) is a relative noun, the agent; the clause (زكّاها) is the ṣila; and the agent of (زكاها) is a pronoun returning to (من). It was also said that it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "he has succeeded whom Allah the Exalted has purified through obedience". (وقد خاب من دسّاها) is conjoined to the preceding clause and parallel to it.
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْواها إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقاها)
A resumptive statement, delivered to confirm what was mentioned about the success of the one who purified his soul, or whom Allah purified, and the failure of the one who corrupted his soul, or whom Allah corrupted. (كذبت ثمود): a past verb and an agent; (بطغواها), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (كذبت). The meaning of the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of their transgression". In al-Kashshāf he made it for seeking aid, figuratively, as in your saying "I wrote with the pen", meaning: they did the denying by means of their transgression. Both (الطغوى) and (الطغيان) are verbal nouns, but the expression with (الطغوى) was chosen because it better resembles the ends of the verses. In al-Mukhtār: "(طغى يطغى), with fatḥa on the ghayn in both, and (يطغو), (طغيانا) and (طغوانا), mean he exceeded the limit; (طغي), with kasra, is the same; and (الطغوى), with fatḥa, is like (الطغيان)." As for al-Zamakhsharī, he said: "(الطغوى) is from (الطغيان). They distinguished between the noun and the adjective in the pattern fuʿlā from the roots ending in yāʾ, by turning the yāʾ into wāw in the noun and leaving it unchanged in the adjective, and so they said (امرأة خزيا) and (صديا)." (إذ) is an adverb for the time past, attached to (كذبت) or to (الطغوى); the clause (انبعث) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it; and (أشقاها) is the agent of (انبعث). What is meant by it is Qudār ibn Sālif, with ḍamma on the qāf, who is made a proverb for ill omen, so it is said "more ill-omened than Qudār"; he was nicknamed "the red one of Thamūd". It is also permissible that they were a group, and the singular is because the elative, when annexed, is the same for singular and plural, masculine and feminine. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh, in which he made a strange confusion, is: "If the masculine is (أشقى), then the woman is (شقواء), because it is of the wāw-class, as in His saying: (ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا) and (شقاوتنا). The (ها) is genitive by annexation. The plural of (أشقى) is (شقو), like (حمر) and (صفر); if you form a sound plural you say (أشقون) in the masculine and (شقواوات) in the feminine, like (حمراوات)." Ibn Hishām said in reply: "His saying 'if the masculine is (أشقى) the feminine is (شقواء) and the plural (شقو)' is not good, as he did not distinguish between the afʿal that is an adjective of an indefinite noun and the afʿal that follows the course of nouns and is an adjective of an indefinite noun only with (من), being either annexed or accompanied by (أل). The feminine in this case is (الشقيا), and the masculine plural is (الأشقون), and (الأشاقي) is permissible by analogy, just as you say (الأكبر), (الأكبرون) and (الأكابر); and the feminine plural is (الشّقى) and (الشقييات), just as you say (الكبرى), (الكبر) and (الكبريات)."
(فَقالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ناقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْياها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال) is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; (لهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (قال); (رسول الله) is the agent; and (ناقة الله) is accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "leave off hamstringing her and beware of her drinking". A discussion of the warning will come in the section on Benefits. (وسقياها) is conjoined to (ناقة الله), i.e. "and her drinking".
(فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوها فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاها وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (كذبوه) is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (فعقروها) is conjoined to (فكذبوه), i.e. Qudār struck her on her legs and brought her down, and they slaughtered her and divided her meat among themselves. (فدمدم) is likewise conjoined; (عليهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (دمدم); (ربهم) is the agent; and (بذنبهم) is also attached to (دمدم), the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "because of their sin". (فسوّاها) is conjoined to (دمدم). The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; (يخاف عقباها) is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object. We made the wāw a conjunction only to suit the reading with the fāʾ, which is also one of the Seven; although the parsers and the commentators say that the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; among those who said it is a conjunction is Ibn Khālawayh.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying (ولا يخاف عقباها) there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), on the view that the pronoun in (يخاف) refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is the apparent sense: that He, Glory be to Him, does not fear its consequence, as kings fear the consequence of their deeds. The purpose of the metaphor is to humiliate and abase them. It is also permissible that the pronoun return to the Messenger, i.e. that he does not fear the consequence of his warning them, and the metaphor remains. al-Suddī, Muqātil, al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿAlī said: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl and the pronoun in (يخاف) returns to (أشقاها), i.e. he rose up to hamstring her while not fearing the outcome of his act, because of his disbelief and transgression. (العقبى) is the end of a thing and what comes of matters in its wake. In this there is some remoteness [Translator's note: the source reads (يعد); in context the correct reading must be (بُعْد), "remoteness, weakness"], because of the length of the interval between the ḥāl and its owner.

* Benefits:
The warning (al-taḥdhīr): it is the putting of a noun in the accusative by an omitted verb that conveys alerting and warning, the verb being implied as suits the situation, such as "beware", "keep away", "avoid", "guard against", "protect yourself" and the like. The warning is:
1- Sometimes with the word (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (إياك والكذب): (إياك) is an overt detached pronoun in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "keep away" or "guard against" or "beware"; and (الكذب) is conjoined to (إياك), or is a direct object of an omitted verb as well, as before. You may also make the wāw one of accompaniment and (الكذب) a mafʿūl maʿahu.
2- Sometimes without (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (نفسك والشر) and (الأسد الأسد); their i'rab is as before.
3- Sometimes with the word (إياه) and (إياي) and their derivatives, when conjoined to the one warned, as in his saying:
فلا تصحب أخا الجهل ... وإياك وإياه
(So do not keep company with the ignorant man, and beware of yourself and him.)
The governing verb in a warning is necessarily omitted in three places:
1- That the thing warned with is (إياك) itself and its derivatives.
2- That there is a conjunction.
3- That there is repetition, as in your saying: (الأسد الأسد).
It is strange that al-Nasafī mentioned in his commentary that the saying of the Exalted (ناقة الله وسقياها) is an incitement (ighrāʾ). There is no doubt of its problematic nature on the apparent reading, because incitement does not apply to it on the apparent reading; what applies to it is only the warning.

﴿والقمر﴾: Bu da ﴿الشمس﴾'e atıftır, mecrûrdur.
﴿إذا﴾: Gelecek zaman için olan zarftır, nasb mahallindedir; mahzûf kasem fiiline mütealliktir.
﴿تلاها﴾: Mâzî fiil ve müstetir fâildir; zamir mef'ûlün bihtir. ﴿تلاها﴾ cümlesi zarfın ona izâfesiyle cer mahallindedir.

(فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى): (مَنْ), Basralılara göre ibtidâ ile ref' mahallindedir; Kûfelilere göre ise ona dönen hâ (zamir) ile (merfûdur). Hüseyn b. Vâkıd: "Zekâtını veren ve Rabbinden korkan kimse" demiştir. "وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى"nın anlamı hakkında söylenenlerin en güzellerinden biri, Muhammed b. Ca'fer b. Hafs b. Râşid'e, Yûsuf b. Mûsâ'dan, o da İbn Uleyye'den naklen okunan şu rivayettir: (İbn Uleyye) dedi ki: Bize Dâvûd b. Ebû Hind, İkrime'den, o da İbn Abbas'tan haber verdi: "وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى" (âyetinde) dedi ki: «بالحلف». [Mütercim notu: Metinde «بالحلف» yazılıdır; rivayet «بالخَلَف» olarak bilinir, yani Allah'ın harcananın yerine bedel vermesi.] Bu, düzgün bir isnaddır ve sözün siyakına uygun bir anlamdır.

Dahhâk "فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى" (10) hakkında "Ateş (cehennem)" demiştir. Eğer "Kolaylaştırma ancak hayır için olur; zorluk için nasıl gelmiştir?" denirse, cevap şudur: Bu, "فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ" [Âl-i İmrân: 21] âyeti gibidir; yani «ما يا قوم لهم» sözünü müjde makamına koy. [Mütercim notu: Metinde «ما يا قوم لهم» yazılıdır; «ما يقوم لهم» yerine bozulmuş görünmektedir; anlam: onlara (verilecek) şeyi müjde makamına koy.] Sîbeveyh şu (mısraı) okumuştur: [Vâfir]
571- تحيّة بينهم ضرب وجيع
(Aralarındaki selamlaşma acıtan bir darbedir.)
Bu, Basralıların görüşüdür. Ferrâ'nın görüşü ise şudur: Hayır ve şer bir araya geldiğinde, hayır için müjdeleme kullanılınca şer için de onun benzerinin kullanılması caizdir.

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى وَالنَّهارِ إِذا تَجَلَّى وَما خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى)
The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (والليل) is genitive through the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear". (إذا) is an adverb of mere time, free of any conditional sense, attached to the verb of the oath; the discussion of it has already preceded. The clause (يغشى) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it. (والنهار إذا تجلى) is conjoined to the preceding clause. (وما خلق): (ما) is either maṣdar (verbal noun) or relative, conjoined to what preceded. (إن سعيكم لشتى) is the answer to the oath: He, Glory be to Him, swore that the deeds of His servants are (شتى), the plural of (شتيت). Whatever is diverse and mutually different is called (شتى) because of the distance between its parts; (الشتات) is separation. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "(شتّ) (شتّا), of the pattern of ḍaraba, when it is scattered; the noun is (الشتات); and (شيء شتيت), of the pattern of (كريم), is something scattered; (قوم شتى), of the pattern fuʿlā, are people scattered; (جاءوا أشتاتا) is the same; and (شتان ما بينهما) means 'how far apart they are'." (إن) and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (شتى) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن).
(فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرى)
The fāʾ is resumptive, and (أما) is a particle of condition and elaboration. (من) is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (أعطى) is the ṣila (relative clause). (واتقى) is conjoined to (أعطى); (وصدّق بالحسنى) is likewise conjoined. (فسنيسّره): the fāʾ is the connector of the apodosis, the sīn is for futurity, and (نيسّره) is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object. (لليسرى) and the preposition are attached to (نيسّره).
(وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنى وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنى فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرى)
Conjoined to what preceded, parallel to it in its i'rab.
(وَما يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مالُهُ إِذا تَرَدَّى)
The wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative. It is also permissible for it to be interrogative, in the sense of denial, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of (يغني), i.e. "what kind of benefit will it benefit?". Some parse it as a fronted direct object, with the implied sense "what thing will it avail?". (يغني) is an imperfect nominative verb; (عنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يغني); (ماله) is the agent. (إذا) is an adverb of mere time attached to (يغني), and the clause (تردى) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it.
Ibn Khālawayh has a fine discussion of (تردى). He said: "(تردّى) is a past verb, and its verbal noun is (تردّى يتردّى تردّيا), so he is (متردّ); from it comes the saying of the Exalted (والمتردية والنطيحة). One says: (تردّى) into a well, or into a chasm, or into a perdition, when he fell into it. And one says: (ردي زيد يردى ردى) when he perished, and (أرداه الله يرديه إرداء). And one says: (ردى الفرس يردي رديانا). al-Aṣmaʿī said: I asked Muntajiʿ ibn Nabhān about the (رديان) of the horse, and he said: it is its running between its (آريّه) and its (متمعّكه). [Translator's note: the source reads (بن آريّه), "ibn āriyyihi"; in context it should be (بين آريّه), "between its āriy"; the name of the narrator is also written (منتجع بن بنهان) in the source, whereas the known name is Muntajiʿ ibn Nabhān. Translated according to the corrected sense.] The (آري) is the (آخيّة), that is, the manger; and the (متمعّك) is the place in which it rolls. The (آري) is of the pattern fāʿūl, so named because it holds the animal back; one says (تأريت بالمكان) when you stayed in it and were held back in it." al-Mubarrad said: "Two things are said about it: one, 'when he falls into the Fire'; the other, 'when he dies'; and is it a form of the pattern tafaʿʿala derived from (الردى)?"
(إِنَّ عَلَيْنا لَلْهُدى)
A resumptive statement, delivered to inform them that it rests upon Him, Glory be to Him, by the requirement of His wisdom, to make clear the guidance as distinct from error. (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (علينا) is its fronted khabar (predicate); the lām is for emphasis; and (الهدى) is the postponed noun of (إن).
(وَإِنَّ لَنا لَلْآخِرَةَ وَالْأُولى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and what follows it is conjoined to what preceded, parallel to it in i'rab.
(فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ ناراً تَلَظَّى)
The fāʾ is conjoined to something implied, i.e. "whoever seeks this world and the next from other than their true Owner, who is Allah, has missed the way and strayed from the right path". (أنذرتكم) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; (نارا) is a second direct object; and the clause (تلظى) is an adjective of (نارا). (تلظى) is an imperfect verb, the original being (تتلظى). The wording of Ibn Khālawayh is excellent, and it is: "(تلظى) is an imperfect verb, the original being (تتلظى), and Ibn Masʿūd indeed read it so. Ibn Kathīr read:
(نارا تّلظى) with the assimilation of the tāʾ, meaning (نارا تتلظى). Had (تلظى) been a past verb, it would have been said (تلظت), because (النار) is feminine. The verbal noun is (تلظّت تتلظى تلظّيا), so she is (متلظية). Among the names of Hell are said to be Saqar, Jahannam, al-Jaḥīm and Lazā; we seek refuge in Allah from it. These names are definite and are diptotes, because of feminine gender and definiteness."
(لا يَصْلاها إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى)
(لا) is negative; (يصلاها) is an imperfect nominative verb, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الأشقى) is the agent of (يصلاها).
(الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى)
(الذي) is an adjective of (الأشقى); the clause (كذب) has no grammatical position, because it is a ṣila; and (تولى) is conjoined to (كذب), falling within the scope of the ṣila.
(وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى الَّذِي يُؤْتِي مالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and the sīn is a particle of the future, brought for emphasis. (يجنبها) is an imperfect nominative verb with a direct object; (الأتقى) is the agent; (الذي) is an adjective; the clause (يؤتي) is a ṣila; (ماله) is a direct object; and (يتزكى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent. The clause is either a badal (substitute) for (يؤتي), in which case it has no grammatical position, since it falls within the scope of the ṣila of (الذي); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (يؤتي), i.e. "purifying himself by it in the sight of Allah".
(وَما لِأَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزى إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلى)
The wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is negative. (لأحد), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عنده) is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (من) is a redundant preposition of the genitive, and (نعمة) is genitive by (من) in form, nominative in position, as mubtadaʾ. (إلا) is a particle of exception in the sense of (لكن) ("but"), and (ابتغاء) is excepted from a different class, for it is a disconnected exception, because seeking the face of his Lord is not of the class of favour; that is: "no one has with him any favour, except the seeking of the face of his Lord". It is better to parse (ابتغاء) as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because the meaning is: he gives his wealth only for the seeking of the face of his Lord, not in recompense for a favour. (ابتغاء) was also read in the nominative, on the dialect of one who says (ما في الدار أحد إلا حمار) ("there is no one in the house but a donkey"), and then it is a badal for the position of (من نعمة). He said:
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس
(Many a land in which there is no companion, except the gazelles and except the white camels.)
And Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim said:
أضحت خلاء قفارا لا أنيس بها ... إلا الجآذر والظلمان تختلف
(She became empty, a wasteland, with no companion in her, except the gazelle-calves and the ostriches, going back and forth.)
The detail of this rule will come in the section on Benefits.
(وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضى)
The wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the answer of an implied oath, i.e. "By Allah, he will surely be satisfied". (سوف) is a particle of the future, and (يرضى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is "he", referring to Abū Bakr, about whom the verse was revealed when he bought Bilāl, who was being tortured for his faith, from his master Umayya ibn Khalaf, and freed him. The disbelievers said: "He only did that because of some favour Bilāl had done him."

* Benefits:
When the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), which is where the excepted is not part of that from which it is excepted, on condition that what precedes (إلا) indicates what is excepted: if it is not possible to direct the governing word onto the excepted, the accusative is obligatory for the excepted, by agreement, as in (ما زاد هذا المال إلا ما نقص): (ما) is maṣdar and (نقص) is its ṣila, and their position is accusative as an exception. It is not permissible to make it nominative as a badal from the agent, because the governing word cannot be directed onto it, since one does not say (زاد النقص). Likewise (ما نفع زيد إلا ما ضرّ), since one does not say (ما نفع الضرّ). But if it is possible to direct the governing word onto the excepted, as in (ما قام القوم إلا حمارا), since it is sound to say (قام حمار), then the Hijazis make the accusative obligatory, because badal is not truly sound there, as the excepted is not of the class of that from which it is excepted; and on this is the reading of the Seven: (ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن). Tamīm prefer it (the accusative) and permit following (the badal), and they read (إلا اتباع الظن) in the nominative as a badal for (العلم) with regard to its position. From this is the saying of Jarān al-ʿAwd ʿĀmir ibn al-Ḥārith:
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس
(Many a land in which there is no companion, except the gazelles and except the white camels.)
He made (اليعافير) and (العيس) a badal for (الأنيس); the second (إلا) is a confirmation of the first. (اليعافير) is the plural of (يعفور), which is the calf of the wild cow; and (العيس), with kasra on the ʿayn, is the plural of (عيساء), like (البيض) the plural of (بيضاء); they are white camels whose whiteness is mixed with some reddishness. Sībawayh mentioned two explanations for the nominative: one, that they construed it according to the meaning, since the intended thing is the excepted: one who says (ما في الدار أحد إلا حمار) means "there is in the house only a donkey", and the mention of (أحد) became a confirmation, to make known that there is no human there; then what he intended by mentioning the donkey was made a badal for (أحد). The second explanation is that he made the donkey the "person" of the house, that is, the one who takes the place of a human in the house.
Ibn Yaʿīsh said: "Of the disconnected exception is the saying of the Exalted: (وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى). The Banū Tamīm read it in the nominative, and make seeking the face of Him, Glory be to Him, a favour of theirs with Him."
